speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: Take care of yourself. The price of kolto tanks has jumped through the roof.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: The Selkath put a bunch of export restrictions in place for kolto. It's hurting everybody.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I hear that Manaan is no longer shipping kolto. The Selkath must be trying to drive prices up.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: If you have kolto tanks, use them sparingly. I can't find them cheap anywhere.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I'm sure I saw some holo-footage of you on the Manaan swoop track, what you doing here?

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: Did you win a regional swoop championship on Manaan or something? I recognize your face.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I heard about your Manaan win. I'm surprised the Tatooine track was able to attract a racer of your ability.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: Motta swears he can get professional racers to come to Tatooine. If the Manaan Sector Champion is here, I guess he was right.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I hear Czerka is closing their Kashyyyk operation. Nobody seems to know why.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: Czerka is claiming that their operation on Kashyyyk has become to costly to maintain. Sounds like a cover-up to me.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: No more supplies have been ordered for the Czerka outposts on Kashyyyk. Doesn't sound like "economic restructuring" to me.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: A private trader told me about the bloodshed on Kashyyyk. Seems like Czerka wants to forget it was ever there.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: A trader I know says there was some trouble on Korriban. I didn't want to hear about it. That's where the Sith Academy is.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: If you're doing any private shipping, stay away from Korriban. Sounds like the Sith can't even get along with themselves.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: Word is Korriban is a dangerous place to visit right now. Something about the Sith at the Academy.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I heard the Sith were fighting amongst themselves on Korriban. Course, they're always fighting someone.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: I still haven't heard a final figure of how many people died on Taris.

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: You never know what the Sith will do. Look at Taris; was there any reason for what happened there?

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: The Republic is too complacent. If they let Taris fall, do you think they care what happens out here?

speaker: Anchorhead Tradesman
text: With Taris gone, I wonder who the Sith will turn on next.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: Move along, spacer.
comment: These guards need to go hostile when the player has helped Freyyr.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: You want to arrange a purchase, go talk to the director in his office.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: This assignment is the worst in the galaxy.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: Czerka Corporation should burn down some trees. Make room for some swoop races.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: Keep walking. This ain't no holiday port of call.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: If you've business with Czerka Corporation, take it to the director's office.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: Take a walk, spacer. You don't look like a big buyer to me.

speaker: Czerka Patrol Guard
text: Watch yourself. We don't need anyone agitating the locals.

speaker: Elora
text: I was told that you're a friend of Jolee Bindo... and that Jolee has returned to the sector. Please, I must speak to him. It's very urgent!
comment: if jolee is not in the party, first time talked to

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Elora
text: My name is Elora. My husband Sunry and Jolee are old friends. Now Sunry needs Jolee's help.

speaker: Player
text: I shall tell Jolee immediately.

speaker: Elora
text: Please, I beg you to bring Jolee to speak to me about my husband. Sunry's life depends on it!
comment: if jolee is not in party, subsequent conversations

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I can help your husband.

speaker: Elora
text: Someone is out to destroy my husband. I... I don't know who I can trust. I don't know you. But Jolee - he was always a true friend to Sunry.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you need to speak to Jolee?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this.

speaker: Elora
text: Jolee! It *is* you! I... need your help.
comment: jolee is in party, first time conversation with him in party

speaker: Jolee
text: Elora? Of all the people... How did you even know I'd left Kashyyyk?

speaker: Elora
text: I didn't. Nobody knew where you were, not even Sunry! But I heard the Selkath mention you and your friends. The Force has brought you to help us!

speaker: Jolee
text: Why? Whatever could be the matter, my dear?

speaker: Elora
text: It's horrible, Jolee! Sunry has been arrested! The Sith have accused him of murder!

speaker: Jolee
text: Murder? But how...

speaker: Elora
text: It's all a mistake, Jolee! Sunry isn't a murderer - someone is trying to frame him.

speaker: Jolee
text: Calm down, Elora. Where's Sunry now?

speaker: Elora
text: Sunry's being held at the Selkath courts. They won't let anyone in to see him. Please, go to the courts, talk to the Judges. Maybe the Selkath will listen to you.
comment: subsequent conversations with jolee in the party, player not appointed arbiter

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't worry, Elora. We'll get to the bottom of this and help Sunry... somehow.

speaker: Elora
text: I hear you have been appointed as Arbiter in Sunry's trial. My husband is innocent - please don't let him go to jail for a crime he didn't commit!

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me anything about Sunry?

speaker: Elora
text: Sunry is... he's a cripple. There's no way he could have overpowered this Sith woman like they claim.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's true... I'd forgotten about that. Let's not forget that he would have had to have been considerably older than the Sith woman.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying someone your age couldn't overpower a woman?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. I'm a Jedi... and one who was living alone in the Shadowlands until recently. That keeps you in shape, damn it! We're talking about Sunry, here.

speaker: Elora
text: And there's no way he would do something so dishonorable as hit her from behind. Sunry's a decorated war hero! He's a hero of the Republic!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry, Elora. I'll save him.

speaker: Elora
text: Find the real evidence, that's all I ask. The real evidence will prove Sunry didn't do this.

speaker: Player
text: Your husband might not be so innocent, Elora.

speaker: Elora
text: This is all a plot to discredit the Republic! Sunry is a victim of a Sith frame up!

speaker: Jolee
text: It's possible. I haven't seen Sunry since I crashed on Kashyyyk... a man can change a lot in that time. The man I knew could never have done this crime, however.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Was Sunry having an affair?

speaker: Elora
text: [Success] Of... of course not! He... he... *sob*

speaker: Elora
text: Yes... *sob* ...yes, he was having an affair. He was seeing that... that Sith woman.

speaker: Elora
text: After all these years we've been together he just... just dropped me like that. Not publicly, oh no, but inside that's what it feels like.

speaker: Elora
text: He started seeing Elassa last year. I... I had my suspicions for a while, but he was careless. Pretty soon everyone knew.

speaker: Elora
text: But... but... even though I'm sure that harlot was only using him, I know he couldn't have killed her. He came and confessed to the affair to me. He said he was going there to break it off - to end it.

speaker: Elora
text: Maybe the Sith woman attacked him and he had to defend himself?

speaker: Elora
text: But even though he cheated on me, inside he's still the man I loved... love... He is too kind and gentle to have killed her in cold blood.

speaker: Player
text: He is a soldier, though.

speaker: Elora
text: That was a long time ago, in a war far, far away. He's changed now... settled down. Just please, prove his innocence.

speaker: Player
text: He has killed many Sith before.

speaker: Elora
text: [Failure] What?? Don't insult us both! Sunry is... Sunry is a just and honorable man. How dare you accuse him... us, of such a thing!

speaker: Jolee
text: Now, now, Elora. We're not here to pass judgment, my dear. We do need to know everything if we're to help, yes?

speaker: Bastila
text: Madam. I would remind you that I am a Jedi. Now, then... was he having an affair?

speaker: Elora
text: Find proof to set him free instead of bringing these baseless accusations against us.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Sunry and Elassa.

speaker: Player
text: I have this recording showing Sunry killing Elassa.

speaker: Elora
text: Lies! It... it must be! I knew the Sith would never let a Republic hero get away... You must find Sunry innocent!

speaker: Gate Guard
text: A horrible fate for poor Hendar... I warned him not to leave the safety of the village.
comment: first time talked to and Hendar dead Dialog Mission Statement: Usually the gate guard will open the gate whenever the player wants to enter or leave the village, this is done through dialog. After 2 rounds he will automatically close the gate. The first time the player approaches the gate from the interior of the village a conversation between the gatekeeper (OutcastMan045) and Hesther (OutcastWom043) will ensue as Hendar (OutcastMan046) runs for the gate with a Rakghoul in pursuit. The player can offer to help Hendar and the gatekeeper will open the gate, or he can simply sit and watch as hendar is killed (4 rounds after Hendar reaches the gate if the player does not intervene, or instantly if the player refuses to open the gate). If the player saves Hendar, he and Hesther thank the player and wander off. If Hendar dies, Hesther wanders off and reviles the player. Exit points in conversation: Exit stream 1: If the player approaches the guard for the first time and is outside the gates this will mark the guard as talked to and open the gates then close them after 2 rounds. Exit stream 2: Player has promised to save Hendar, guard opens gate. Player has 4 rounds to go through the gate or Rakghoul kills Hendar then runs off. Exit stream 3: If player talks to guard while Hendar is being attacked and chooses to let him die. Depending on the path the player can get a dark side hit. Exit stream 4: If player asks guard to open gate. Gate is opened then closed after 6 seconds. Exit stream 5: Player just says goodbye. Nothing happens.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: But I couldn't open the gate... not while the rakghouls were so close. I had to protect the village.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: But enough of this grim talk... we must focus on the positive if we are to survive down here. How can I help you, up-worlder?

speaker: Player
text: Open the gate for me.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: I will open the gate for you, up-worlder, but you've got to be quick. In a few seconds I must close and lock it again for the safety of the village.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Gate Guard
text: I am Trewin, from the Outcast village. It's my job to guard the gates and see they are locked to protect us from the rakghouls.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Heh. I just guard the gates. Gendar is the leader of the village, up-worlder. You should speak to him if you have any questions.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Goodbye, up-worlder.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Thank you for saving Hendar. You are braver than I, up-worlder. Maybe we Outcasts have lived too long in selfish fear.
comment: first time talked to since Hendar lived

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Perhaps we can learn a lesson from your brave actions. Hmph. But enough of my ramblings... is there something you need, up-worlder?

speaker: Gate Guard
text: You're not from the village. In fact, you look like you're from the up-world!
comment: first time spoken to, player on far side of gate

speaker: Gate Guard
text: I don't know why you'd come down here to our village, but I guess I can let you in. There don't seem to be any rakghouls nearby.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Hurry, up-worlder. I can only leave the gate open for a few seconds. I can't risk letting the rakghouls in!

speaker: Gate Guard
text: I can't open the gate... not while the rakghouls are so near.

speaker: Player
text: Open the gate... I will kill the rakghouls.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: You would risk your life for a stranger? You are brave... or foolish.

speaker: Player
text: You're right, it's too dangerous. Leave the gate closed.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: *Sigh* A horrible fate for poor Hendar. I warned him not to leave the safety of the village.

speaker: Player
text: Keep the gate closed. I'm not risking my life here.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: The gate is open. If you're going through you have to hurry, up-worlder, before I have to close it again.

speaker: Gate Guard
text: Yes, up-worlder? Is there something you need?

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: So do we have a deal?
comment: scripted encounter when player first approaches the recruiter

speaker: Echani Mercenary
text: That's an awful lot of money... is there something you're not telling me?

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: Don't be so suspicious. The Republic is generous, we pay our mercenaries well.

speaker: Echani Mercenary
text: Makes sense, I guess. Alright, I'm in. When do I start?

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: Just show up at the Republic Embassy tomorrow and speak to our Representative there. I'm sure he'll have some task he wants you to start on right away.

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: Do you mind? I'm in the middle of a Republic recruiting drive right now. I need to hire these mercenaries before they sign up with the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you hiring mercenaries?

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: In case you hadn't noticed, there's a war on. If we don't hire these mercs, the Sith will. Now excuse me, I have to continue my recruitments.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you could hire me?

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: I don't know if you've got what we're looking for... Jedi aren't generally suited to mercenary work. If you want, talk to Roland Wann at the Republic Embassy and see if he can find anything for you.

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: It's north of here, then east past the first courtyard. It's just off the north end of the second courtyard. You can't miss it.

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: Now if you'll excuse me, I have to continue my recruitments.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Republic Negotiator
text: Good. The longer I spend talking to you, the less time I have to talk to the mercs.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: The second tomb on the left within the valley is the tomb of Naga Sadow. It is off-limits to all students, unless they are in the company of Master Uthar.
comment: if selected by the player, player is part of the Sith

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Beware of the tuk'ata. They are a pack beast that have their nests in one of the tombs. We fight them off as best we can.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: There is an old Sith hermit that has been haunting this area, we understand. Watch out for him.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: A dangerous assassin droid has barricaded itself within the tomb of Marka Ragnos, the first one on the left. Be wary.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Watch out for the tuk'ata. They will charge you on sight. Run back to the excavation area and we can protect you.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Any artifacts found should be brought to the attention of Master Uthar immediately.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: I am not here to get you out of trouble if you do something stupid, student. Enter the tombs at your own risk.

speaker: Bastila
text: I will stay here in this chamber and use my Battle Meditation to aid the Republic fleet. I am their only hope of destroying the Star Forge and ending the Sith menace.
comment: After converted, but Malak not dead and player speaks to her

speaker: Bastila
text: You must go and face Malak, but you have to hurry. Once I turn the battle in the Republic's favor we won't have much time to escape the Star Forge before it is destroyed.

speaker: Bastila
text: Good luck, my love... and may the Force be with you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Good luck... and may the Force be with you.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Star Forge is under assault from the entire Republic fleet! If I don't use my Battle Meditation to turn the tide, Admiral Dodonna's capital ships will destroy the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: I have to stay here in the command center so that I can best use my Battle Meditation against our enemy. If I don't the Star Forge will be lost!

speaker: Bastila
text: You must go to face Malak without me. Find him, kill him and reclaim the title of Dark Lord of the Sith!

speaker: Bastila
text: Revan - I knew you'd come for me.

speaker: Player
text: I'm <FullName> now, Bastila. Revan is no more.

speaker: Bastila
text: Sadly, I know this is true. Had you reclaimed the power of your previous identity I would be your apprentice, not Malak's. But you rejected the dark side.

speaker: Bastila
text: Now you must pay the price. Here on the Star Forge the power of the dark side is at its strongest. This time you will not defeat me!

speaker: Player
text: I'll never give up on you, Bastila. I know you can still be saved.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are wasting your time. I have seen the Jedi for what they are: weak and afraid. The Sith are the true Masters of the Force. You have forgotten that lesson, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: You can't escape, Bastila! Wherever you run I'll hunt you down!

speaker: Bastila
text: I have no doubt of that. I was no match for you in the Temple, but when I fled I knew you would follow me here.

speaker: Bastila
text: I see now why Malak followed you. Even though you are only a shell of your former self, you are still a formidable opponent.
comment: Second dialog (init after 100 points of damage dealt)

speaker: Bastila
text: I can't even imagine the power you must have wielded when you were the Dark Lord. You were a fool to give it all up and follow the light side.

speaker: Player
text: I am as strong in the light as I ever was following the dark side.

speaker: Bastila
text: The dark side has made me stronger than I ever was before! I have a greater command of the Force than all but the most powerful Jedi Masters.

speaker: Bastila
text: As Malak teaches me the greatest secrets of the Sith, I will unlock more of my potential. Eventually there will be no limit to what I can accomplish with the Force!

speaker: Player
text: Malak will never let you become that powerful. He will kill you first.

speaker: Bastila
text: Have you forgotten the ways of the Sith already, Revan? Eventually I will challenge my Master. If I am worthy he will die by my hand and I will become the new Sith Master.

speaker: Bastila
text: Then I will take on my own apprentice and the cycle will begin again. This is the way of the Sith, it is how we assure our leaders are always the strongest and most worthy!

speaker: Player
text: You're dooming yourself to an endless cycle of death and betrayal.

speaker: Bastila
text: No, Revan, it is you who are doomed!

speaker: Player
text: I won't let that happen! I'll kill you first!

speaker: Bastila
text: No, Revan. You are the one who will die here!

speaker: Player
text: You will accomplish death and destruction with the dark side, nothing else.

speaker: Bastila
text: Jedi propaganda. The dark side is only a tool, and Malak will train me in its use. Eventually I will surpass my Master and challenge him. If I am worthy he will die by my hand.

speaker: Player
text: You've been consumed by the dark side, Bastila. Can't you see it's destroying you?

speaker: Player
text: I'm still strong enough to defeat you, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: Then it's time for you to prove it!

speaker: Bastila
text: You are growing weary, I can sense it! Your strength falters, the light side is failing you while the power of the Star Forge re-energizes me! Soon this will all be over!
comment: Third dialog (init after second 100 points of damage dealt)

speaker: Player
text: I have not faltered, Bastila. You have been misled by the dark side.

speaker: Bastila
text: The dark side will always triumph over the light! Malak has assured me of victory! You can't defeat me here on the Star Forge! YOU CAN'T!

speaker: Player
text: Then strike me down, Bastila. I won't defend myself.

speaker: Bastila
text: What type of trick is this?

speaker: Player
text: Remember what you once were, Bastila. A Jedi would never strike down a defenseless opponent.

speaker: Bastila
text: I am a Sith apprentice now. You place too much faith in what I used to be... and for that you shall pay!

speaker: Player
text: You are not evil, Bastila. You will not strike down a defenseless opponent.

speaker: Player
text: We meant something to each other, once. I don't believe you will strike me down.

speaker: Player
text: Your emotions get the better of you, Bastila. Remember the Jedi code.

speaker: Bastila
text: You dare spew those Jedi lies in my face? You will die screaming, Revan!

speaker: Player
text: You are the one growing weak, Bastila. I hear the desperation in your voice!

speaker: Bastila
text: No, this is not possible! You have rejected the dark side, you are a weak and pathetic servant of the light! How can you still stand against me? Why can't I defeat you?
comment: Fourth dialog (init when dropped to 1 hit point)

speaker: Player
text: Now you see the dark side is not stronger than the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, I see you speak the truth. I am no match for you. Please, for the sake of what we once shared, do not make me suffer. End my life quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: I could never kill you, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: What other choice do you have? I have fallen to the dark side, I am the apprentice to the Dark Lord himself. You cannot let me live.

speaker: Player
text: You can reject the dark side, Bastila. Return to the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: No... I'm not strong enough. There is too much anger inside me now. Too much hatred and fear. I can no longer find peace in the Force.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Use our bond, then. Take your strength from me.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] You... always had more strength than I did. I told you that. I felt so... helpless before your destiny.

speaker: Bastila
text: You were Revan and I couldn't tell you... it was agonizing! Even worse when I began to... feel closer to you. I despised myself for it.

speaker: Bastila
text: And even now I... feel your strength. It... does help me. Thank you, I think I can face the end, now. If you are the one to end it for me.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I love you, Bastila. I can't abandon you, ever.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] You... love me? Heh. I... there was a time I yearned for and yet dreaded to hear those words. I loved you, too, but I could never... face who you were.

speaker: Bastila
text: Malak knew how I felt. Any part of the light that was within me would be extinguished when I killed you.

speaker: Bastila
text: But what good is love? It cannot save me from the sea of blackness I am drowning in. I have betrayed everything I ever believed in! How can I atone for that?

speaker: Player
text: Help us defeat the Sith, Bastila. This will atone for what you have done.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, I... could join you in your battle against the Dark Lord. That alone would not make up for all I have done, yet... it would be a step in the right direction.

speaker: Bastila
text: But how would you be able to trust me? How do you know I wouldn't turn on you when you faced Darth Malak? How do you know the dark side wouldn't make me betray you again?

speaker: Player
text: I trust you enough to leave myself open to your attack, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: You play a dangerous game. Are you certain you wish to take this risk? I could end your life and gain Malak's favor with a single stroke of my lightsaber.

speaker: Player
text: You won't, Bastila. Because I love you and I believe in you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are brave... and some would say foolish. But you are also right. The dark side has not wholly consumed me. I cannot raise my blade against you.
comment: Player has high enough conversion score from dialog

speaker: Bastila
text: You will go on to defeat Malak, of this I have little doubt. You will have gone from being the Sith Lord, himself, to the savior of our galaxy.

speaker: Bastila
text: And... and you said you loved me. This may not be the best time to say it, but...

speaker: Bastila
text: I love you, too. With all my heart.

speaker: Player
text: You aren't afraid to love anymore?

speaker: Bastila
text: After this? No, nothing could make me feel safer than to be loved by you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You should go. Malak awaits. This isn't over, yet... for any of us.

speaker: Bastila
text: I should stay here, though. If we face Malak I am afraid his dark presence will overwhelm me. It would not be wise to expose myself to such temptation.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila, I want you at my side when I face the Dark Lord.

speaker: Bastila
text: I'm sorry, but the risk is too great. I am not wholly free of the dark side's shadow. Not yet. But you are more than a match for the Dark Lord. I understand that now.

speaker: Player
text: You could use your Battle Meditation to aid the Republic fleet.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, that would be for the best. You don't need me to defeat Malak, anyway. Now I understand that a true Jedi is a match for any Sith. Even the Dark Lord himself.

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I must know something, first, before that happens. I must ask you something.

speaker: Bastila
text: Will there be a place for me in your future? Do you... do you love me?

speaker: Player
text: I do love you, Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I love you, Bastila, but after everything that's happened...

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. Thank you for your honesty. It's probably for the best that it goes no further. You saved me and I will always be grateful.

speaker: Player
text: No. I'm sorry, Bastila, but I don't love you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are brave... and foolish. The dark side has wholly consumed me, and you will suffer for failing to see that!

speaker: Player
text: You won't, Bastila. I know you still serve the light side.

speaker: Player
text: You're right. I suppose I can't trust you, after all.

speaker: Bastila
text: A wise decision. You cannot trust me, and you cannot bring yourself to execute me. I see now there is only one way this can end. The time for words is done! Defend yourself!

speaker: Player
text: You're right. Don't worry, you won't feel a thing.

speaker: Bastila
text: Do it. Quickly...

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure] There is nothing in my heart but the blackness of the dark side! I am sick of your preaching, Revan!

speaker: Bastila
text: I ask you for an honorable death, but you are too weak to even grant me that! No more words! This must end with blood!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Look into your heart, Bastila, and you will find the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] I... I know a flicker of the light still burns within me. Malak felt it too. He knew it could only be extinguished if I killed you.

speaker: Bastila
text: But what good is a single flicker of light against the sea of darkness I am drowning in? I can never atone for my betrayal.

speaker: Player
text: I was redeemed, Bastila. You can be, too.

speaker: Bastila
text: You were a special case. The Council had no other choice. They needed you alive so they could discover the location of the Star Forge. It was an act of desperation.

speaker: Bastila
text: It was my responsibility to watch over you, to make sure you did not slip back into your evil ways. I was supposed to protect you from the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: You did protect me, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: But at what cost? In protecting you, I fell to the dark side myself. Is that the price of a Jedi's redemption? Must another of the Order fall to save me?

speaker: Bastila
text: I cannot allow that to happen. Please, this is too painful. Strike me down. End this now, quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: You can't protect someone from the dark side. Each individual must choose their own path.

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I suppose you are right. Yet the path I have chosen is that of the dark side. I don't see any way I could atone for what I have done. I deserve to die.

speaker: Player
text: You did more than protect me, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: It's true I possess... feelings for you. But was it only an illusion brought about by our bond? And what was the cost?

speaker: Bastila
text: Please... this is too painful. End it now, quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: I was the Dark Lord, Bastila, and the Jedi Council let me live.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure!] No! That bond is what took me down this path to begin with! It poisoned me... I hated myself for loving you and now I have betrayed everything!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Turn to the Jedi code, Bastila. It can help you.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] I doubt mere words can help me now, but to appease you I will recite them:

speaker: Bastila
text: There is no emotion: there is peace. There is no ignorance: there is knowledge. There is no passion: there is serenity. There is no chaos: there is harmony...

speaker: Bastila
text: Strange, but even now I find comfort in these words. I... suppose old habits die hard.

speaker: Bastila
text: There is no death: there is the Force. Thank you, Revan. I am ready to face my fate now.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure] The Jedi code is nothing but words, the babblings of senile old Masters! The code cannot help me now!

speaker: Player
text: There's no need for me to kill you, Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I am stronger than you could ever be, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: You can't win, Bastila. Now you must die!

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: You there! Up-worlder! Anyone using this elevator has to pay the toll!

speaker: OutcastMan042
text: Yeah, this is our elevator! If you use it, you've got to give us something!

speaker: Carth
text: I don't believe this planet! Even the beggars are trying to shake us down.

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: Five credits! That's what it costs to use our elevator! Five credits!

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? What are you doing here in the Undercity?

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: We are the Outcasts, banished and reviled by those who dwell above!

speaker: OutcastMan042
text: Here in the filth and darkness we claw out a wretched existence, scavenging and begging just to survive long enough to see another wretched day.

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: This is our village. We live here in the undercity. You have to pay us five credits for using our elevator.

speaker: Player
text: You poor wretches. Here's 20 credits to buy some food and clothing.

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: Credits, my brother! We have credits! Now we can buy food and medicine!

speaker: OutcastMan042
text: Hush, or the others will hear us! They'll want our credits! We have to hide them!

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Go on, you two! Get out of here! I'm sorry about that... those two beggars give everyone in the village a bad name! We aren't all like that, you know. Most of us are good people.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm sure you are, miss. It's just too bad your little welcoming committee is there to give people a bad first impression.

speaker: Player
text: My name's <FullName>. Who are you?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: My name is Shaleena... you're from the up-world, aren't you? I've... I've never seen it. I was born here in the Undercity. Is it as nice as they say up there?

speaker: Player
text: The surface is a beautiful place.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: I've never been to the surface, but sometimes I think I can see it in my dreams. The sun, the sky, the stars... it all sounds so... so... so wonderful.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Gendar, the leader of our village, tells me I should spend more time trying to improve things down here and less time dreaming about something I can never have. Maybe he's right.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: You probably think I'm a fool, having dreams of a place I've never even seen. But when I was little, Rukil used to tell me stories of what it was like up there.

speaker: Player
text: Rukil? Who's that?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Rukil's the oldest man in the village. The kids call him Rukil Wrinkle-Skin, but he's a kind man. He used to tell me the greatest stories when I was a little girl.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: I still like to listen to his tales about the Promised Land, even though I know they're just legends. But it helps to make the Undercity seem less... less dark, somehow.

speaker: Player
text: The Promised Land? What's that?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: It's... it's just a story to make little children smile. Rukil believes in it, though. Sometimes I can almost believe it myself, but then I look around and I see the ugly truth.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: *sigh* I guess we have to make the best of what we have though. If you really want to learn more about the promised land you should speak to Rukil.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find Rukil?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: He's wandering around somewhere on the south side of the village. He doesn't move too far... it's hard on his bones. He's over 100 years old!

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: The children laugh at him and people think he's crazy because of his stories about the Promised Land, but he's really just a kind old man.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: You'd probably get more information from Gendar, the village leader. Or maybe Rukil. But I'll tell you whatever I can.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find Gendar?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: He'll be somewhere in the village. I couldn't say where for sure. He's always busy, doing whatever he can to make the lives of the other villagers easier.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Oh... okay. Well, if you ever need anything, or if you just feel like talking, come back and see me. I hardly ever get a chance to speak to someone from the up-world.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the escape pods that crashed into the Undercity?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: I don't know anything about that, but maybe Gendar could help you. Sorry... is there anything else you need?

speaker: Player
text: Have any other up-worlders come through here recently?

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: There were quite a few people from the surface marching through the village, but none of them bothered to talk to me. Gendar might know more about them.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about this village.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Well, I was born here for starters. My parents were Outcasts, banished to the Undercity for some crime or other... they never really liked to talk about it.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Everyone here is an Outcast... or the descendant of one. It's tough down here, but we survive. I guess it's easier for me, since I've never known anything different.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Some of the people have given up all hope; they've become bitter and depressed. But most of us are good people... despite what our ancestors may have done.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Gendar could probably tell you more. Or maybe Rukil. You could talk to them if you want.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Of course... I'm sorry. You're probably here for something important, right? You probably want to speak to Gendar. He's the leader of our village.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: But if you... if you have time later, maybe you could come back and speak to me again. I don't get much chance to talk with people from the surface.

speaker: Player
text: It's nothing special.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: Not to you, I suppose. But you're probably used to its beauty by now.

speaker: Player
text: It's better than this festering slime pit.

speaker: outcastshaleena
text: I... I suppose our world doesn't look like much to you. It's dark and cold and lonely down here - but this is the only world I've ever known.

speaker: Player
text: What do you want?

speaker: Player
text: Okay, here's five credits.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have any credits on me.

speaker: OutcastMan042
text: We are not fools... we know all who come from the up-world are rich! Please, is 5 credits so much to ask?

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: Please, have pity on us. We have nothing. All we ask is a few credits to make our lives easier.

speaker: Player
text: Get out of here you filthy beggars, or I'll use my blaster to end your suffering permanently!

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: Run, my brother! Flee this one's wrath!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! You get nothing from me!

speaker: OutcastMan042
text: Have you no heart? Have you no compassion?

speaker: OutcastMan041
text: Come, my brother - let us go. We will get nothing from this selfish up-worlder!

speaker: Player
text: This is a public elevator! I'm not paying any toll!

text: No. But thanks for letting your guard down.

speaker: Thalia May
text: You... you tricked us! You just wanted to get closer!! Quick, get them!!

speaker: Player
text: Not yet, but I'm working on it.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Alright. We'll keep waiting, then. Watch out for that beast... it's dangerous.

speaker: Player
text: It's clear. You're free to go.

speaker: Thalia May
text: It... it's clear? We can go?

speaker: Thalia May
text: Thank you. This... I wasn't expecting help from anyone in the academy. I guess we aren't the only ones who don't... agree with everything.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Maybe... maybe the Jedi will accept us. I've seen how evil the dark side is. Maybe I could try.

speaker: Thalia May
text: At any rate, thank you again. You've saved our lives.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Hold it right there, whoever you are! We... we're not going back to the academy! We'll kill you rather than go back!

speaker: Player
text: Go back? What are you talking about?

speaker: Thalia May
text: You mean you aren't here to kill us or bring us back? I find that hard to believe. The only way into these caves is through the academy. You must be a Sith.

speaker: Thalia May
text: So what is it, then? If you're not here to kill us or bring us back, why are you here? Speak up!

speaker: Player
text: Okay, you got me. I'm here to kill you after all.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Open fire! Get them! Get them!!

speaker: Player
text: Slow down and tell me what you're doing here.

speaker: Thalia May
text: So you don't know about us? I don't know if I'm ready to believe that or not, but I'll play along for the moment.

speaker: Thalia May
text: My name is Thalia May. The others here and myself refused to murder a bunch of people on a whim from Master Uthar... so here we are.

speaker: Thalia May
text: We thought that becoming a Sith was what we always wanted, but that wasn't true. Now all we want is to get out of here. Fair enough?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I can help you.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Help us? Why should I believe that this isn't some kind of trick?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Give me a chance and I'll prove it to you.

speaker: Thalia May
text: [Success] You want to help us? Alright... I can think of a way. We're stuck in these caves, obviously, or we would have been long gone.

speaker: Thalia May
text: There's a passage to the surface through the caves, but we're blocked by some kind of large creature. We can't defeat it.

speaker: Thalia May
text: If you could kill it and clear up the passageway for us, we could escape. That would be help enough. Can you do that?

speaker: Player
text: I can try.

speaker: Thalia May
text: I'll believe that when I see it... but if you could, we would be... grateful.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. Get yourselves out.

speaker: Thalia May
text: I figured as much. Get out of here, then. Go on! We have enough to worry about with the shyrack!

speaker: Player
text: The passage is already clear.
comment: if the passageway has been cleared

speaker: Thalia May
text: [Failure] No! I know what Sith like you want from us! You're not bringing our heads to Master Uthar so he can pat you on the back!

speaker: Thalia May
text: They're here to kill us! Get them!! Get them!!

speaker: Player
text: Fine. You've worn out my patience. Time to die.

speaker: Player
text: Fair enough. I'll leave you be.

speaker: Thalia May
text: Then get out of here! Now! Or we'll open fire!!

speaker: Player
text: Sorry. Time for you to die.

speaker: Player
text: You're... the renegade students? The ones who ran away?

speaker: Thalia May
text: So you have heard about us. Yes, we ran away before Master Uthar could execute us. Is that so hard to believe?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not here to bring you back.

speaker: Player
text: I guess we'll do this the hard way, then.

speaker: Player
text: Alright, I'll leave you be.

speaker: Thalia May
text: You came back again? Why?! I told you we're not going back to the academy, so go away!!

speaker: Wookiee Rebel

speaker: Wookiee Rebel
text: You are the only outsider that will survive us! We swear it!

speaker: Wookiee Rebel
text: Kashyyyk will be ours once more!

speaker: Wookiee Rebel

speaker: Wookiee Rebel

speaker: Wookiee Rebel

speaker: Wookiee Rebel

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Your precious Republic's days are numbered! It won't be long until Malak turns his armada loose on Coruscant itself!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Save your empty threats, Sith scum! Malak isn't stupid enough to attack the Core worlds - not with the entire Republic fleet waiting for him!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You're a fool! When the Sith descend on Coruscant, our numbers will block out the sun itself! The galactic senators will collapse trembling in fear, and beg for mercy at Malak's feet!

speaker: Republic Soldier

text: Do you know who I am, worm?

speaker: Player

speaker: Sith Soldier

speaker: Player
text: I'll kill you!

speaker: Player
text: Don't laugh!

speaker: Player
text: Yes... Yes I am.

speaker: Player

speaker: Rodian
text: I must go to the office of the Czerka company. That is where business is transacted.

speaker: Rodian
text: This planet is controlled by the Sith. They are the supreme law here, and I suggest you be wary of them.

speaker: Rodian
text: I have only recently come to this planet, myself. My apologies if I cannot help you.

speaker: Rodian
text: Many sentients come to this planet to attempt to enter the Sith academy. I understand most die in the process. How unfortunate.

speaker: Rodian
text: There is a building called the cantina which is a place of recreation.

speaker: Rodian
text: Taris has been destroyed. This portends ill for the future, sentient.

speaker: Rodian
text: If you are wise, you will avoid the Sith on this planet, sentient. They do as they wish and many are killed without regret.

speaker: Rodian
text: I must be on my way, sentient. My ship leaves very soon.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer

text: This planet is the worst assignment to have with a kolto shortage coming up.

text: Bring those Selkath here see if they think we need kolto. They'd start shipping it out quick, I bet.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: If we don't get another shipment of kolto, we'll have to start using local herbs for healing. Then we'll hurt *and* stink.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: Are you... no, there's no way a swoop champion is on Kashyyyk. No way.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: Is your ship equipped to get the major planetary broadcasts? I heard the Manaan races were pretty good.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: I heard some rookie took the big prize at the Manaan swoop races. I guess anyone can win now that Taris is gone.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: You look a lot like the winner of the Manaan races. I bet that opens door for you.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: I don't mind being on a backwater planet when I hear about the trouble places like Korriban get.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: I heard something about trouble with Sith on Korriban, but as long as no cities are being destroyed, they can do what they like.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: Have you been by Korriban recently? The Sith there aren't planning on taking their trouble off-world, are they?

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: We get the occasional private trader from Korriban through here, but not recently. I wonder what's up.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: Have you heard where the Sith might be headed next? I don't even know why they targetted Taris.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: All those people on Taris dead. First I heard the whole planet was gone, but even just the city is sad.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: I guess I should be grateful I'm on Kashyyyk. I could have been posted to Taris.

speaker: Czerka Liaison Officer
text: It took ten days for news of Taris to reach me. They don't tell us anything.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Let the record show that the trial of Sunry vs. the Ahto City Authority has commenced. Presiding are judges Shelkar...

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Jhosa...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Naleshekan...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Kota...

speaker: Judge Duula
text: and Duula.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This trial is to determine the culpability of Sunry in the death of the Sith Elassa.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Representing Sunry in his defense is a member of the Jedi Order. Do you have any opening statements?

speaker: Player
text: Sunry is guilty of the murder. He has confessed to me.

speaker: Sunry
text: No! You traitor!

speaker: Elora
text: Sunry! No!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Your client is guilty, Arbiter? Are you sure you wish to enter this plea?

speaker: Player
text: I do.

speaker: Sunry
text: No! I object! I am the victim of a conspiracy here!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Is this true Arbiter? Your client does not seem to agree with your assertations.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The position of Arbiter is to defend your client. Therefore, inspite of your personal feelings, you must do so to the best of your ability.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This trial will proceed on schedule.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Acting as a prosecutor for the Ahto City Authority is an impartial observer from the Sith Empire.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: It is an honor to see justice served.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: And I will see Sunry is executed for the crime he has committed.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Do not be too overzealous in pressing your commission, Sith!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The first matter of business is the presentation of a sworn testimony by the proprietor - Ignus - of the hotel where the murder occurred. What is the testimony you wish to give us?

speaker: Ignus
text: The man I saw leaving - Sunry - left before I heard the blaster shot.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Impossible!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Know your place, Sith!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This is serious evidence indeed. The court will keep this in mind near the top of the list of pertinent facts.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We will now begin by calling forth the witnesses to the crime and taking their testimony.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: After each witness has given their testimony and you have cross-examined them, you may ask the presiding judges for their opinions on the current state of the case. This is a special privilege given by Manaan law only to the defendant, so use it wisely.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: The first witness is Firith. The prosecution will question the witness first.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: You are Firith Me, the well-known Pazaak player. I wonder if we can trust the word of a gambler as reliable testimony...

speaker: Player
text: Objection, your Honors!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Objection sustained. Ask the witness your questions and do it promply.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Of course, your Honor.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Firith: what did you see the night of the murder?

speaker: Firith Me
text: I came out into the hallway after hearing the blaster shot and saw Sunry over there limping down the hall out of the building.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Heh. A very obvious point, your Honors. The accused was seen leaving the scene of the crime after the blaster that killed Elassa was fired.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: A very pertinent point, prosecutor.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It is now the defense's turn to cross-examine the witness.

speaker: Player
text: I have no additional questions.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Very well. Would you like to use this opportunity to poll the judges?

speaker: Player
text: Yes.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: I think that Sunry, perhaps, could have been the culprit.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: I think that Sunry was perfectly capable of committing this crime.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: It seems to me that the evidence is weighted against Sunry.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Despite his honorable past, Sunry would seem to have done something deplorable.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Sunry is obviously guilty of killing the Sith woman.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Since the defense has no further questions, we will call out the second witness: the Rodian Gluupor.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The prosecution may question the witness.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Gluupor the Rodian, you were staying in the hotel the night of the murder and saw Sunry leaving Elassa's room didn't you?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Yes, Gluupor see Sunry running down hallway, and when Gluupor look in room, Sith woman dead on floor.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: This is clear then: that Sunry left the room with the Sith Elassa already dead behind him.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Perhaps, Sith, perhaps. It is the turn of the defense to question the witness now.

speaker: Player
text: Did you see Sunry kill Elassa?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor... Gluupor not see Sunry really hurt Sith... But Gluupor did see Sunry leaving room with dead Sith in it!

speaker: Gluupor
text: But... Gluupor not see him really kill Sith...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: An important distinction Arbiter.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Do you wish to ask the witness anything else?

speaker: Player
text: Isn't the medal at the crime scene too obvious a clue?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor not know. Why anyone leave things in someone else's room?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor just think these things happen. It is just... odd...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Yes. Odd indeed.

speaker: Player
text: Do you really think a cripple could have hurt Elassa?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Sunry seems like strong man, but he is hurt, too.

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor not think that man like that would stand up to a Sith. Not at all. But Sunry still run fast after.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: We know full well the extend of Sunry's injuries, Arbiter!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: But the fact still remains.

speaker: Player
text: Did you plant the medal on Elassa?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor... Gluupor...

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Don't do it, Gluupor...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The prosecution will be silent!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: What is it you wish to say Gluupor?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor... Gluupor paid by Sith to plant that medal.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Lies! Slander! I object!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You are certain of this Gluupor?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor certain...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This new evidence puts the entire case in a new light.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Perhaps I was wrong, after all, in my thoughts about Sunry.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I cannot tell yet if Sunry killed Elassa, but I am confident it will be proven.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I do not believe Sunry, as a well-standing Republic citizen, could have committed this crime.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I just do not have enough information to judge this case yet.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Sunry did not have the capacity to commit these murders... I think.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I cannot make my decision on what I have yet seen.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Sunry perhaps was not the killer.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: I am unsure as yet as to whether Sunry was the actual murderer.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: I think that Sunry could not have committed this crime.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: I do not have enough information to make an informed decision.

speaker: Player
text: No.

speaker: Player
text: Did you actually see the murder happen?

speaker: Firith Me
text: You mean actually see him kill her with my own eyes? Well... no... But I don't think there could have been anyone else there.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Your point is well-taken Arbiter.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Do you have additional questions?

speaker: Player
text: Was the medal left at the crime scene not a little too obvious?

speaker: Firith Me
text: I think it may have been. I mean, you'd have to pretty stupid to leave something that important lying around, wouldn't you?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: This argument has merit.

speaker: Player
text: How could Sunry have harmed her if he was a cripple?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Well he was moving pretty fast running away... but yeah, I mean, how could he kill a Sith warrior in combat? I don't know for sure...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Do not think less of Sunry because of his handicap. He is fully capable.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Can't you see that the man can hardly walk, let alone fight Elassa?

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: That is enough for now. We will deliberate on this later in private.

speaker: Player
text: Elassa is a Dark Jedi, isn't she?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Yes, from what I could tell. She carried a lightsaber around under that cloak of hers.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Objection! That doesn't prove she was a Jedi!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: No, this piece of evidence is very important. It establishes the character of Elassa and perhaps her intent in dealing with Sunry.

speaker: Player
text: Do not undermine the witness!

speaker: Ignus
text: The man I saw leaving - Sunry - probably left after I heard the blaster shot.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: The guilt of the accused is apparent even this early in the trial.

speaker: Player
text: I have reconsidered.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Honesty is an attribute essential to the position of Arbiter, as is impartiality. It would not be advised for you to abuse either of these.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Do not mock us, Jedi!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Enough! This case will proceed on schedule.

speaker: Player
text: Sunry is guilty of the murder. I have this recording as proof.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: A recording? Let this new evidence be entered in the records.

text: Ah... this new evidence is most convincing.

text: Yes. Yes it seems to be.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This court hereby finds Sunry guilty of the murder of the Sith Elassa.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: In accordance with Selkath law the proscribed punishment for murder is death.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The verdict has been delivered and this trial is now over.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Do not think that we Selkath, the pinnacle of evolution, can be swayed by such means!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: If you attempt such manipulations again, Sunry will be found guilty, and you will summarily be put to death! We do not tolerate intrusions upon the justice of our courts!

speaker: Player
text: I will find Sunry innocent.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: That remains to be seen.

speaker: Player
text: I have no comments at this time.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: If the defense has no more questions, the court will call out Elora, Sunry's wife.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: You Elora, are Sunry's lawful wife. Your husband was a hero in the last war between the Sith Empire and the Republic.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: He was crippled in that war. Do you not believe he'd blame the Sith for his injury?

text: Yes, I guess he would.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: And there you have motive! Sunry seeks revenge on the Sith for what they did him and killed Elassa.

speaker: Player

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: It seems painfully obvious that he killed her to keep quiet about the affair.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Be silent! You have already questioned the witness, prosecutor.

speaker: Elora
text: He had been seeing her for some time, I think. *sniff* But he said he was going to change!

speaker: Elora
text: He had gone there that night to end it! We talked the night before and he had promised!

speaker: Elora
text: But now things have become so very complicated...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: That is very enlightening evidence. It will influence our deliberation considerably.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Do you have any more questions, Arbiter?

speaker: Player
text: Sunry was a cripple. Could he have killed Elassa?

speaker: Elora
text: He was a good man, but his injuries pained him terribly. But he always held on. Always persevered.

speaker: Elora
text: I don't think he could have beaten her or anything like that... but a blaster? I just don't know...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Sunry seems fully capable to me. But it seems unlikely that he would choose to do such a thing.

speaker: Player
text: Sunry was a Republic war hero, wasn't he?

speaker: Elora
text: Yes. He fought against the Sith in the last war. He fought bravely and was even awarded the Hero's Cross!

speaker: Elora
text: I don't know how much that means to the Sith or to your Selkath, your Honors, but in the Republic it is awarded only to the bravest, most valorous, most honorable men.

speaker: Elora
text: The kind of man who earns that medal would not kill someone in cold blood!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Your husband earned a medal because he excelled at killing Sith. It relates directly.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Do not let personal opinions sway your judgment of the law!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Does the prosecution have any remaining witnesses to call forth?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I wish to call forth Sunry himself, your Honors.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Very well.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Are you a war hero, Mr. Sunry? You fought in wars against the Sith Empire, correct?

speaker: Sunry
text: Yeah, that's right. I don't regret it either. The Republic needs its heroes.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Indeed... Would you say that you dislike the Sith? Even... hate them?

speaker: Sunry
text: Of course I hate them! Trying to take over the galaxy every chance they get! Killing millions of innocents!

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Pure politics. Were you in Elassa's room on the night of the murder?

speaker: Sunry
text: Well, yes I... I was...

speaker: Sunry
text: I had been having an affair with Elassa on my wife, yes... But I realized how wrong I had been and I was going there to end it!

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: You were having an affair with a Sith! You wanted to end it quickly and quietly, so you killed her from behind and tried to flee!

speaker: Sunry
text: No, I...

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I think we can see the answer clear enough, Mr. Sunry!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Do not interrupt the accused!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: In fact, I think you've said quite enough already, prosecutor.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Do you have any question to ask the accused, Arbiter?

speaker: Player
text: Elassa was a Sith spy, wasn't she?

speaker: Sunry
text: Of course she was! Why would a young, beautiful Sith woman get with an old cripple like me?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: You are not helping yourself, Sunry. You only give reason why you might kill her.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: He merely states facts. The incompetence of the murder indicates that her occupation was not the motive for the killing.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: The fact remains: Elassa was a Sith and likely a spy as well.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Is there anything else you wish to ask the accused?

speaker: Player
text: How could Elassa have got ahold of your medal?

speaker: Sunry
text: I don't know. The medal had gone missing some time ago. I never found out what happened to it.

speaker: Sunry
text: It's possible the Sith had stolen it and had it planted on the body...

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Supposition, your Honors!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: True, but it does have merit and deserves consideration.

speaker: Player
text: You were going there to end the affair. Would the Sith object?

speaker: Sunry
text: Yes I think they would. They wouldn't want to lose one of their sources - even though I didn't give them anything!

speaker: Sunry
text: They... they might have killed her for her failure... or they might have thought she'd turn against them or something like that.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: The Sith Empire is not the barbaric institution you portray it to be!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Be silent, prosecutor. This is a valuable point, that lends some credence to your defense, Arbiter.

speaker: Sunry
text: I knew she was a Sith, and she would be trying to pump me - for information, of course - so I... I just simply turned the tables.

speaker: Sunry
text: I was working on her, trying to turn her over to the Republic's side. Trying to turn her into a double agent. But that's kind of ruined now that she's been murdered.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: An obviously false story! I have proof here, in the form of data recording, that proves you were, in fact, having an affair with Elassa!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Let this new evidence be entered in the court records.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: So be it.

speaker: Sunry
text: I... I... What's the use now... I had been having an affair with Elassa, it's true. But I had realized my mistake and was going there to end it! But I did not kill her!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The witnesses have all been called forward and questioned by both prosecution and defense. The prosecution will now present, in closing, its summary of the pertinent facts of this case.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I think the facts in this case are very straight forward: Sunry was having an affair with Elassa. He sought to end it, and the simplest, quickest method given his hatred of the Sith was to simply kill her.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: *Ahem* Witnesses saw Sunry fleeing the scene, and material evidence places him there at the time of the murder as well.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I am confident that any informed observation of the facts will lead the judges - your Honors - to this very conclusion.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Indeed. And your closing statements, Arbiter?

speaker: Player
text: No one actually witnessed the murder.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Truth.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: That doesn't mean a thing! He was there, running from the room!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: If you speak out of turn again, you will be forcibly ejected from the court! The Arbiter speaks a valid fact.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Is there another point you would make?

speaker: Player
text: Sunry was a cripple and couldn't have killed her.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: A cripple can be just as capable as any other man. And Sunry more than most.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: You overrate this man!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Perhaps. Are there any other arguments, Arbiter?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are obviously evil and set this up.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Objection!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The Arbiter is allowed an opinion as well as you, prosecutor.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: No matter how erroneous...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Or truthful.

speaker: Player
text: Sunry was ending the affair, so the Sith killed her.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: The Sith would not leave the medal of her killer clutched in her hand!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Your time for arguments has passed, and you would do well to remember that!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The Arbiter's argument does bring up a valid point.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Is there anything else you would state?

speaker: Player
text: Elassa was a spy and the Sith are framing Sunry.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I find that highly unlikely, Arbiter. The Sith have no need of such deception. The facts speak clear.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: But the Sith have been known for violence, deception, and murder before.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: That is also true. Is there another point you would make?

speaker: Player
text: My arguments are complete.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Then the court will now deliberate amongst ourselves.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This court hereby finds Sunry innocent of the murder of the Sith Elassa.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: In addition, this court finds the Sith Empire guilty of conspiracy and obstruction of justice.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Your Honors! No!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Silence!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: The Sith Empire is hereby forced to subsidize a portion of Republic purchases on Manaan for a period of the next solar year.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The verdict has been delivered and this trial is now over.

speaker: Mission
text: Yes! Score one for the good guys!

speaker: Carth
text: I knew you wouldn't let the Republic down!

speaker: Juhani
text: Well done. You showed wisdom worthy of a Jedi Master during this trial.

speaker: Cand
text: I guess you got the result you wanted, but I still think this was a big waste of time. We Mandalorians prefer to settle things with a nice, quick trial by combat.

speaker: Elora
text: Sunry... I'm so glad...

speaker: Sunry
text: Elora...

text: We have done all we could for you, old friend.

text: Thank you for saving me. I don't know how I can repay you. Elora and I are going to leave here and get as far away from all this as soon as we can.

speaker: Sunry
text: I - and the Republic - will not forget what you've done for us. Thank you.

speaker: Sunry
text: Thank you, Jolee! I... I don't know what I would have done if you hadn't shown up!

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't thank me, thank your Arbiter. I was glad to help.

speaker: Sith Student
text: It's really strange. Nobody seems to know where Master Uthar or Yuthura Ban have disappeared to. Some of the sensitives are claiming they're dead.

text: Rumor has it that something has happened to Master Uthar and Yuthura Ban. Do you know anything?

speaker: Sith Student
text: I heard that Yuthura Ban was dead. I suppose that means Master Uthar will be taking a new apprentice, soon.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Did you hear? Yuthura is dead. Master Uthar said so. I bet she got too impatient and failed to assassinate him. Idiot.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Master Yuthura has taken over the academy. Everyone's talking about it! I guess she finally got rid of Uthar, somehow.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Have you heard? Yuthura... I mean Master Yuthura has taken over the academy! Well done, I say!

speaker: Sith Student
text: You aren't even a full Sith. Don't bother me.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Get out of my way. I don't have time to deal with hopefuls.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Come back when you've taken your final test. If you survive it.

speaker: Sith Student
text: If Master Uthar gives you an order, you'd better follow it. There were some students who disobeyed him and now they're hiding out on the surface somewhere.

speaker: Sith Student
text: There are some students in hiding that refused to follow an order. Master Uthar wants them found and dead... and is offering a reward for it, too!

speaker: Sith Student
text: Just be careful if you go into the valley. I hear there's a hermit living in the hills that kidnaps students.

text: The former master of the academy, Jorak Uln, is supposedly hiding out in the hills on the surface as some kind of mad hermit.

text: Word is that one of our experimental droids went mad and escaped and is hiding in the ruins. I wonder why we don't just gather up and destroy it?

speaker: Sith Student
text: One of my friends went to find that crazy droid that's hiding in the ruins in the valley. He hasn't come back, yet.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Ha! It's great to be on the winning side, isn't it? We've been crushing the Republic at every battle so far!

speaker: Sith Student
text: The latest reports say the Republic is on the run. Before long the Sith will be ruling the entire galaxy.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Darth Malak is one of the greatest Sith leaders ever. I hope he comes back to the academy before I leave.

speaker: Sith Student
text: It is my most fervent hope to serve under Darth Malak once my training is complete. Don't you feel the same?

speaker: Sith Student
text: Rumor around the academy is that you had something to do with those rebel students being caught, finally. They got what they deserved, I say.

speaker: Sith Student
text: I was told that you actually met the old master of the academy, Jorak. Is the hermit as mad as they say?

speaker: Sith Student
text: The buzz is that you took care of that crazy droid out in the ruins. That's pretty impressive.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: You are the great warrior now, it seems. You came before and defeated us, and now do so again.

speaker: Player
text: What of it?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: If you are as great as you appear to be, then perhaps you can help us as well.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: There have been many attacks on the island recently by blue- and red-armored warriors against our scouts.

speaker: Player
text: Mandalorians!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: If that is your name for them, then yes.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I was given the task of rooting out their forces, but as you can see, I have failed... Failed both the One, who gave me the command, and the dozen warriors who accompanied me... and did not return.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: If you are a great warrior, then you may yet be able to destroy them where I have failed. Surely you have powers beyond my ken, and those would undoubtedly prove critical.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I help you?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: You came to the One seeking entrance to the Temple of the Ancients, did you not?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: These killers have made their base of sorts near the entrance to the Temple itself. Our scouts can no longer travel safely in that area, and any passage by you towards the Elders' compound would be in danger as well.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Your own best interests lie in their deaths... and...

speaker: Player
text: And?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: There have been many wrecks that have crashed onto this world... Many of the items from these vessels may be of some use to you. If you bring me back the head of their leader, I could show you one of the better caches...

speaker: Player
text: Why don't I just take that information?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I am an old and bitter warrior. My injuries are many and I have just come back from a fearsome battle... a slaughter. Even a light hit could kill me, so don't threaten me with violence!

speaker: Player
text: I don't need anything from you!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Whether you believe you do or not, there is no way into the Temple without our assistance. Bring his head to me, and both our causes will be helped.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you need his head?

speaker: Warleader Garn

speaker: Player
text: Very well, I'll do it.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Good. I can see that you are a true friend to our people.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I will be waiting here for you when you return.

speaker: Player
text: I've already killed the Mandalorians.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I assure you, I can give a reward, I... You... you what?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Th... thank you for what you have done! The souls of my warriors can rest at peace now.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: And with his head, I can gain his strength so that we may overcome his people in the future.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: And now, for the reward I promised...

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I found these while searching among the wreckage. I don't know what they do, but I hid them here quite some time ago. They are yours now.

speaker: Player
text: I still see no reason to help you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't really feel like.

speaker: Player
text: OK, I'll find those Mandalorians.

speaker: Player
text: I know the beings you are talking about.

speaker: Player
text: ... And? So?

speaker: Player
text: What do you want?

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I kicked your backsides pretty good.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: You have earned the gratitude of our people for eliminating the killers who lurked by the Temple of the Ancients.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Now the souls of my warriors can rest in peace. Thank you, Revan.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: You have returned. Have you managed to slay the aliens who massacred my warriors?

speaker: Player
text: They are dead. Here is their leader's head.

speaker: Player
text: No, I have not.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Return to me when you have the head of their leader, and I shall show you where some items I have scavenged are.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have to do your dirty work!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: If you do not slay them, then you will never gain entrance to the Temple anyway. They make their camp there, and you think they will let you pass?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: When you do get the head of their leader, I will be waiting here.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Mandalorians?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: They appear from the shadows, seeming to blend in and out of thin air. They gather near the obelisk at the far side of the field, attacking any who approach.

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Perhaps they worship it, and kill us as sacrifices... but they haven't eaten any of the bodies... They hold us in contempt!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: My blood burns at their insult! The souls of the dead howl in anger!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: You must go there and kill them so that my warriors will be avenged... Only then will I give you the reward I have promised you.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned something about salvage?

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: I will only show you where it is once you've brought me the head of their leader!

speaker: Warleader Garn
text: Threaten me all you want, but until then, I will show you nothing! The souls of my warriors rest uneasy knowing they still live...

speaker: Player

text: I want to ask you some questions.

text: Not right now.

speaker: Jolan Aphett
text: Here, take this. My old Pazaak mentor Daoy gave them to me when I started playing. Maybe they'll do you more good than they have me.

speaker: Player
text: Is this the best place for racing?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: Perhaps not, but it will do for now. Professional racers like myself travel wherever the purses are highest.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: It's no secret that one of the most popular tracks was lost with Taris. Other promoters will need time to organize.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: In the meantime, we will race at the smaller venues. This is almost a recreational stop for me.

speaker: Player
text: If this track is so small, why bother?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: You lose the skills if you don't use them. I could race on any open road, but competition gives the push to get better.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: Besides, if my presence lends a little prestige to the track, maybe we'll get some new racers out of it.

speaker: Player
text: How long have you been at this?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: A few years, but I raced under a different name when I was young. My early career was not very spectacular.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you change your racing name?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: It wasn't that big of a deal. I made the jump from one league to another and wanted to shed some baggage.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: Don't waste much thought on it. It was purely a personal matter that has no bearing today.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the other racers?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: There are some promising newcomers here. Garm tries hard and I wish him well, but Nico is the one to watch.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: It's invigorating to watch him discover his skills. I hope he manages to remember why he took up the sport.

speaker: Player
text: What makes you say that?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: The race is not just about speed. It is a business, and we are the product. He must market himself carefully.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think about that?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: It is a necessary side to the sport. We must make someone money, or there would be no circuit.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my first questions.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something. Who knows this planet best?

speaker: Zoriis Bafka

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: Some of the hunters in Fazza's lodge seem like they would know more than I would, but that wouldn't take much.

speaker: Player
text: I have to leave. Goodbye.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: Racer's luck be with you.

speaker: Player
text: Your petty hobbies are of no interest to me.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka
text: All right. Merely making conversation. I'm not looking for a fight.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] A fight? You are nothing to me. Leave.

speaker: Zoriis Bafka

text: You know what? Sometimes you're nothing but a bully!
