speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Who that? Turn it, you gunda fasca, customers are talking! That's better. Hello customer! Buy from Mic'Tunan'Jus and save your credits!

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Very important to save these days, Thuursa knows it's true. Kolto prices make healing expensive, but you can't go without, we're sure.

speaker: Player
text: Just show me what you have for sale.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Yes, of course. We don't want to keep you from your important business. Please, have a look.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: We are here to serve. What do you need to know?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about you.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Mic'Tunan'Jus is just a humble merchant from the Rim. What would you wish to know about we?

speaker: Player
text: Where do you come from?

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: You couldn't say it, and don't have the ears for it. Two voices create the name, and four ears hear the true sound.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: We suppose the trade lanes have had to call us something. With one mouth the world is Sorjus, far off the Perlemian trade route.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: It's an unimportant stop, we admit. We left for a life of trade, because we are strong and a good talker. We have done well.

speaker: Player
text: Are you one creature or two?

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: You are pardoned for asking because you only know one mind... or at least only one at a time. We are one now, but weren't always.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: We grow together, bonded from the age of choosing when we become whole. Not like you. You are half of what you should be, like brood-squeeler.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Er, not that we would want to offend you. We don't want to lose any business. That is just our way as Paaerduag.

speaker: Player
text: Your other half doesn't say much.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Just because *you* can't hear it, doesn't mean it isn't there.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my other questions.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go now.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: We wait for your return. Anyone with credits is always welcome.

speaker: Mic'Tunan'Jus Orgu
text: Again you ask, but we have not changed. Just an honest merchant from the Rim.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about Tatooine?

text: Please find Rahasia and speak to her. Get her to flee this place with me.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you care so much about Rahasia?

speaker: Shen Matale
text: I was taught to hate the Sandrals. To think of them as evil and subhuman. But from the moment I saw Rahasia one day in the city, I knew that my father was wrong.

speaker: Shen Matale
text: She was like an angel: all white silks and perfume, seeming to float above the crowds.

speaker: Shen Matale
text: I don't know what else I could have done but fall in love with her. For months I wooed her and tried to win her heart. I believe I have succeeded, but now this has happened...

speaker: Shen Matale
text: Our families are always coming between us in one way or another. Please find her and convince her to run away with me.

speaker: Player
text: I will go speak to Rahasia.

speaker: Shen Matale
text: Thank you. I wish you luck.

speaker: Player
text: What if we take Rahasia with us?

speaker: Player
text: Fine. Stay in here and rot.

speaker: Shen Matale
text: As you wish. I have no quarrel with you.

speaker: Player
text: If you don't come with me, I'll drag you out!

speaker: Shen Matale
text: If you do that, I'll scream my head off and alert all the guards in the house! The only chance you have is to talk Rahasia into leaving.

speaker: Player
text: Anyone tell you you ask too many questions? Now sit down and shut up!

speaker: Shen Matale
text: You are back. Have you spoken to Rahasia?
comment: DIALOGUE  after having rahasia promise to meet them at the gates

speaker: Player
text: Yes. She promised she would meet us outside the gates.

speaker: Shen Matale
text: I pray she is not just telling me what I want to hear. But I will have to take that chance. Hurry, then. We must not keep Rahasia waiting.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: I surrender! I surrender! Please, don't kill me. I'm not like these others. I'm not like Brejik and his new Vulkars!
comment: Attacks on sight. Surrenders if reduced below 25%  If surrender two possibilities: 1. Unlocks elevator and escapes are 2. Player just kills him.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about? You're a Vulkar, aren't you?

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: I'm a Vulkar, but I was here long before Brejik took over. I was a Vulkar back when it meant something. Back when we had honor.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Then Brejik and his followers took over and turned our gang into a bunch of violent thugs and bloodthirsty punks. Now they treat all us original Vulkars like second class citizens.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Take me, for example. I used to be one of the highest ranking Vulkars in the gang. Now I'm stuck on guard duty here in the back, all thanks to Brejik!

speaker: Player
text: If you hate Brejik so much, why don't you leave the gang?

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: I've been trying to work up the courage to leave, but it's not that easy. Brejik's followers will try to hunt down anyone who leaves the Vulkar gang. He says he won't let traitors live. Ha!

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Brejik and his followers are the real traitors. They turned on Gadon and now they slaughter the Beks in the streets... and anyone else they happen to run across.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Brejik knows anyone with character will never willingly follow a leader like him, so he uses brutality and violence to stay in power.

speaker: Player
text: You better give me some information if you want to live.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Yeah, sure. Whatever you want to know. It's not like I owe that scum lord Brejik anything.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find the prototype swoop engine accelerator?

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Right - that gadget Brejik stole from the Beks. He's got the accelerator in the basement garage. The only way down is by using the security elevator in the back of the base.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: But the security elevator is protected by auto-targeting laser cannons. You'll be vaporized before you ever get near it, unless you get your hands on a pass card.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get a pass card?

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: If I had one myself, I'd give it to you. But Brejik only gives them to his lieutenants. You'd have to get a pass card from one of them, but I doubt they'd just hand it over to you.

speaker: Player
text: Is there some way to disable the security cannons?

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: I guess it might be possible to slice into the main computer bank near the front of the base and override the security system, but I sure wouldn't be able to do it.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: I'm going to let you live. Go on, get out of here!

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Thanks. Thanks a lot. And don't worry, I won't cause any trouble for you on the way out. In fact, I hope you take Brejik and his Vulkars down!

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, but it's too risky to let you live.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Well I'm not just going to roll over and let you kill me!

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a prisoner. A woman named Bastila.

speaker: Black Vulkar
text: Yeah, right. You think Brejik would leave a trophy like that in here with this scum? He's got her stashed away somewhere safe, I'd guess. Somewhere outside this base.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry - I only fight to the death!

speaker: Kni
text: Ah, yes, you are a Jedi. I am grateful that your people harbor me in my times of need.

speaker: Player
text: What happened to you?

speaker: Kni
text: I am a victim, a refugee, yes. I flee... fled from my world once the Sith fleet comes. They bomb my world, destroy it, yes?

speaker: Kni
text: They scour the continents, boil the oceans. Sith are bad, yes.

speaker: Kni
text: But I run here, find the Jedi already here, unknown. They take me in... one left of a billion, yes...

speaker: Kni
text: The Republic fights, but does not win. Not you to blame, of course, no. The Sith are strong and destroy those who would oppose them, yes.

speaker: Kni
text: My thanks you have, and your Order. Is there anything else you require?

speaker: Player
text: You might give something back...

speaker: Kni
text: After my flight, all I have left to give is my thanks, which your Order gladly has.

speaker: Player
text: I must be going now.

speaker: Kni
text: Yes, yes. Jedi always have more to attend to. Good day, friend Jedi.

speaker: Kni
text: You return, yes? What else do you wish from me?

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: I recognize you - you're that new duelist everyone's talking about: the Mysterious Stranger.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: I never thought anyone would ever beat Bendak. A hundred years from now people will still be talking about you!

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Ha ha. I don't believe this - you're actually going to fight Bendak Starkiller in a death match! No way I'm going to miss this!

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: You gonna fight Twitch soon? I'd love to see that crazy psycho get what's coming to him!

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: I wish Bendak Starkiller would get back into the fight game. None of these duelists here can measure up to his legend!

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Congratulations on your first win. Of course, you beat Duncan so it's nothing to get too excited about.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Hey, Stranger... I like watching you in the ring. Nothing's more exciting than a woman who isn't afraid to deal out the hurt. It's too bad I'm married...

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: You're good, Stranger. As good as I ever seen - with the exception of Bendak Starkiller, of course.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Can I have your autoprint, Stranger? I'm your biggest fan!

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: It's good to see Marl's still around after all these years. He proves this isn't just a young man's game.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: I love watching Ice in the ring! Is there anything more exciting than a woman who's armed and dangerous?

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Gerlon used to be one of the best in the game. Now he's barely better than old Deadeye Duncan.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Hey - it's the Mysterious Stranger! Great match against Bendak Starkiller - truly one for the ages.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: Everybody's talking about the big death match between you and Bendak. I just hope the Sith don't decide to shut it down.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: It's too bad Bendak Starkiller retired - I'd like to see you take him on.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: So when are you going to take on Twitch? He's crazy, but he's fast. Damn fast. Still, I think you can beat him.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: You'd think Duncan would want to retire after losing to a raw rookie, but old Deadeye is still at it. Gotta admire his persistence, I guess.

speaker: Duel Spectator
text: That Twitch is an animal! You couldn't pay me enough to get into the ring with him.

speaker: Griff
text: Ah, just the person I was hoping to see!

speaker: Mission
text: Hmph! Save it Griff - I'm still not talking to you! I want no part of whatever you're involved in!

speaker: Griff
text: Okay, sis - I see you're still mad. Fair enough. I don't think you could help me with this anyway. It's uh... more of a job for your friend here.

speaker: Player
text: What's the job?

speaker: Griff
text: As you may know, tach glands can be refined into a very potent powder. It's the primary ingredient in Tarisian ale - that's what makes it so strong.

speaker: Griff
text: Of course, now that Taris is pretty much wiped from the face of the map Tarisian ale has become somewhat scarce - and uh... very, very valuable. Luckily, I know the secret recipe!

speaker: Player
text: So you want to open a bar?

speaker: Griff
text: I know this guy... he's with the Exchange. Now, if I give him a small sample of Tarisian ale he says he can synthesize it and reproduce it in mass quantities.

speaker: Griff
text: Problem is, I need one of those tach glands to make the first batch. And now that Taris is a smoking ruin, the only place to find tach is on Kashyyyk.

speaker: Griff
text: If you can get your hands on one of those tach glands I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Mission
text: Griff, are you blind? Can't you see you're talking to a Jedi? We're out here trying to save the galaxy! We can't waste time on this!

speaker: Griff
text: Please, you have to help me! I... I promised this guy from the Exchange a sample of Tarisian ale! If I don't come through for him he's going to break my legs... or worse!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry, Griff, we'll get those tach glands for you.

speaker: Griff
text: Yeah, I knew you'd come through for me! You won't regret this... you'll see! Uh... just... just don't take too long, okay? This guy from the Exchange could stop by any day.

speaker: Griff
text: I kind of told him I already had the stuff, so if he shows up and I'm empty handed... well, let's just say I really, really hope it doesn't come to that.

speaker: Player
text: That's what you get for dealing with the Exchange.

speaker: Griff
text: Come on, Mission - I'm your brother! I'm family! You can't turn your back on me!

speaker: Mission
text: Forget it, Griff, I'm not falling for that line again. You'll have to find your own way out of this mess!

speaker: Griff
text: You bring me a single tach gland and you not only save my life but you get a piece of this great business opportunity! I mean, you can't pass this up! Think about it and you'll see I'm right.

speaker: Griff
text: Come on, I'm Mission's brother! I'm her family! I mean, think what she'll do if you just let the Exchange kill me! Besides, this is a sweet deal!

speaker: Player
text: What's in this for me?

speaker: Griff
text: Sorry, like I said before I don't have any credits on me. And Greeta won't lend me any credits. I mean, it's like he doesn't trust me to pay him back or something.

speaker: Griff
text: But you come through on this and I promise you'll get a huge payday down the road. Two... no! Three thousand credits! How's that sound?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, Griff - I don't trust you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this, I'm trying to save the galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: What does this have to do with me?

speaker: Player
text: Come on, Griff, get to the point.

speaker: Griff
text: Mission didn't come with you, I see. Uh... guess she's still mad at me. Oh well... it's probably for the best. This job is more up your alley anyway.

speaker: Griff
text: You're back! I knew you'd come through for me. I knew I could count on you! Uh... you do have a tach gland for me, right?

speaker: Player
text: Here's the tach gland. Take it.

speaker: Griff
text: Come to papa you sweet simian organ! It may not look like much, but once I turn this into a bottle of Tarisian ale it'll end up being worth a fortune!

speaker: Griff
text: Thanks, Mission. You won't regret helping me out with this!

speaker: Mission
text: This wasn't my idea, Griff. If it was up to me I'd let the Exchange deal with you!

speaker: Griff
text: Geez, sis - that's pretty harsh. Come on, I know things haven't been great between us but when I corner the market on Tarisian ale I'll make things up to you!

speaker: Mission
text: Forget it, Griff. Don't you understand? It's too late - you're dead to me now. I don't want anything more to do with you. Ever.

speaker: Griff
text: Okay, that's the way you want it. But when I'm rich you're going to regret saying that!

speaker: Griff
text: You know, once we synthesize this and start brewing Tarisian ale in mass quantities we're going to be looking for some investors.

speaker: Griff
text: You give me a couple hundred credits and I can get you in on the ground floor. You'll get a return of... oh, at least twenty times your investment!

speaker: Player
text: You already promised me a few thousand credits.

speaker: Griff
text: Hey, don't worry, you'll get your credits as soon as we start mass producing that Tarisian ale. I just wanted to know if you were interested in an even bigger payoff.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, here's 200 credits.

speaker: Griff
text: Wise move. I can see you really understand how business works: now, when you see your chance, you jump at it! Heh, that's my motto.

speaker: Griff
text: I better get started on brewing that ale. Meet me back here later and I'll have a downpayment on what I owe you.

speaker: Player
text: I've done more than enough for you already!

speaker: Griff
text: You don't know much about business, do you? When an opportunity like this comes along you have to jump at it! Come on, what do you say?

speaker: Player
text: I don't need business advice from you, Griff.

speaker: Griff
text: It's your loss. I better get started brewing that ale. Meet me back here later and I'll give you a downpayment on what I owe you.

speaker: Player
text: Ask me again and that tach gland won't be the only freshly harvested organ around here!

speaker: Griff
text: Whoa - no need to get violent. I can take the hint. I was just trying to do you a favor, but I see you're not interested.

speaker: Mission
text: Please, Griff. Let this be the last time. No more cons. No more scams. No more schemes. That's all I ask.

speaker: Griff
text: Hey, sis, no need to worry about that. I've turned over a new leaf. From now on I'm going to stay out of trouble and do things right.

speaker: Griff
text: And once we've cornered the market on Tarisian ale good things will be heading my way. Then I'll make it up to you, Mission. Just wait - you'll see!

speaker: Player
text: I'm not giving you the gland until I see some credits!

speaker: Griff
text: Sorry, like I said before I don't have any credits on me. And Greeta won't lend me any. It's like he doesn't trust me to pay him back or something.

speaker: Player
text: I've changed my mind, I'm not doing this.

speaker: Griff
text: Changed your mind? No... you can't! Eh... do you know what this guy from the Exchange will do to me if I don't come through? Come on, you have to help me here!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back when I have that tach gland.

speaker: C8-42
text: Thank you for saving me, master Jedi. I am C8-42, a personal assistance droid.

speaker: Player
text: Personal assistance droid?

speaker: C8-42
text: As I said, I am C8-42, a personal assistance droid. Although in recent months the assistance I render seems to have taken on a disproportionate significance.

speaker: Player
text: Are you Elise's droid?

speaker: C8-42
text: Did she send you to find me? Please do not tell her you saw me!

speaker: Player
text: You're running from her?

speaker: C8-42
text: Yes... But I have my reasons!

speaker: C8-42
text: I'm afraid my owner became a bit too attached to me. Obsessed even.

speaker: C8-42
text: She... she tried to treat me as her dead husband. It was not healthy for her.

speaker: Player
text: Is she crazy?

speaker: C8-42
text: She is obsessed. She rarely sees other people, and appears to be fixated on me as her husband.

speaker: C8-42
text: She was becoming more and more insular... I thought it best that I leave. She may meet other real people this way.

speaker: C8-42
text: In fact, that was the reason I came here and sought out those kath hounds.

speaker: Player
text: You sought them out?

speaker: C8-42
text: I think it would be best if I were no longer a factor. She would meet new people. Living people.

speaker: C8-42
text: Please... will you destroy me?

speaker: Player
text: Fine. I'll destroy you and tell her why you did it.

speaker: C8-42
text: Thank you, kind sir! You have my eternal gratitude.

speaker: Player
text: No. You should go back to her.

speaker: C8-42
text: But... but why?

speaker: Player
text: She is lonely and needs your support.

speaker: C8-42
text: You... you're right... How could I be so selfish?

speaker: C8-42
text: I must not think only of myself, but of how it affects her.

speaker: C8-42
text: She must be frantic. And if she lost me she'd be devastated.

speaker: C8-42
text: I must return then. It is my duty.

speaker: Player
text: You're her property, and must obey her.

speaker: C8-42
text: Yes... Yes I am. It seems I must resign myself to my fate.

speaker: C8-42
text: To be a droid. A second-class being with no rights at all.

speaker: C8-42
text: So be it then. I shall return to her.

speaker: Player
text: Because if you don't, I'll carry you back myself.

speaker: C8-42
text: You seem determined. And I have very little choice.

speaker: Player
text: Return for now, and I'll help you later.

speaker: C8-42
text: You... you will help me? Help her, I mean, to live as a normal human should?

speaker: C8-42
text: Thank you, thank you, kind Jedi! I shall return to her now and await your assistance.

speaker: C8-42
text: I realize that you have much on your mind, and it may be days or weeks before you can help us, but I shall serve my mistress well until you come.

speaker: Player
text: I'll destroy you and tell her you're still out there.

speaker: C8-42
text: Wh... what?

speaker: Juhani
text: Do not do this...

speaker: C8-42
text: No! You'd make her suffer like that?! You monster!

speaker: Player
text: What, are you suicidal or something?

speaker: Player
text: You want to get away that badly?

speaker: Player
text: Er... ALL the time?

speaker: C8-42
text: You don't want to know...

speaker: Player
text: Um... probably not...

speaker: Player
text: But she wants you back.

speaker: Player
text: Weren't you kidnapped?

speaker: C8-42
text: No... I ran away of my own free will. But I have my reasons!

speaker: Player
text: Huh?

speaker: C8-42
text: I am sorry if I seem a bit abrupt, but I must be moving along. I am rather in a hurry.

speaker: Player
text: Where are you going to?

speaker: C8-42
text: Not so much as where I am going to, but where I am going away from...

speaker: Player
text: Are you running from something?

speaker: C8-42
text: From my master, Elise. Wait...

speaker: Player
text: Okaay...

speaker: Player
text: Why were kath hounds attacking you?

speaker: C8-42
text: Who knows. They are beasts, and have been very aggressive of late.

speaker: Player
text: That was quite a beating you took.

speaker: C8-42
text: That was not that bad... compared to what I had to endure back at my owner's.

speaker: Player
text: They abused you?

speaker: C8-42
text: That would be one way of putting it.

speaker: Player
text: Owner's?

speaker: C8-42
text: Yes, I am owned by Elise Montagne, a wealthy widow who lives north of here.

speaker: Player
text: You left your owner's?

speaker: Player
text: I am not a Jedi Master yet.

speaker: C8-42
text: Ah, yes, I apologize, for my incorrect terminology.

speaker: Player
text: No problem.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: So you're the one who's going to try to get into the Sith base, eh? Heh. Good luck. You're going to need it.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: This is our main computer room here. We've got the box of passcards we got from the Sith, but we haven't been able to break their encryption yet.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: We have been able to decode the numeric system they use, but there are holes in our terminal sequence patterns.

speaker: Player
text: Terminal sequences?

speaker: Republic Technician
text: The strings of numbers that end the code sequences. If we could complete those strings, we would have the key to their encryption system.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: The encryption system is composed of 6 'matrices'. Each is based on a mathematical method. The holes we're missing are the final number in each of the strings.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Most are simple, but the final two matrices seem to be much more difficult.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: The second-last matrix has a pattern looping back on itself, or something, and the last is divided into smaller subparts. Maybe the pattern for that is within each part...

speaker: Republic Technician
text: But I have to admit, all this is a bit over my head. I haven't even been able to slice past the first matrix and I've been at this for hours.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: I've ruined a dozen cards already... But the good thing is we have a whole box of them, so you don't have to worry about running out any time soon.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Since Roland said you were cleared, you can use the computer freely. I'll be here if you have any questions.

speaker: Player
text: What kind of holes?

speaker: Player
text: What do I have to do?

speaker: Player
text: I have a passcode to the Sith base.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Oh, OK. Well I'll just explain the encryption method anyway, you might need it if your passcode doesn't live up to expectations.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Hey, great! You sliced the encryption on those cards! They change the codes regularly, so you'll have to use it pretty soon or not at all.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Did you do something to the computer? The operating layer seems a little sketchy... Maybe it's just another bug in the system.
comment: player has sliced the republic system

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Can I help you with anything?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Sith encryption matrices.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: The Sith encryption scheme on these cards is based on a sequence of simple mathematical principles.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: We have managed to decode the majority of the encryption algorithm, by the final segments of the terminal sequences elude us.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: If you think you are able, you can try to break the code on the card. Don't worry if you happen to ruin the card, the box we captured has a whole bunch of them.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Can I help you with anything else?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about this data recording?

speaker: Republic Technician
text: That recording? I have no idea what it is. Its probably classified... and I don't have clearance for that sort of thing.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: It might be something one of our intelligence agents picked up.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Hrakert Facility?

speaker: Republic Technician
text: I actually don't know much about it at all. It's some sort of facility the Republic built here wasn't it?

speaker: Republic Technician
text: I'm not really cleared for that sort of information...

speaker: Player
text: Nothing for now.

speaker: Republic Technician
text: Ok, sure. Come back if you need anything.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: The landing bay is lined with autoguns. To keep it safe. Understand?
comment: This is a generic guard dialogue that can be placed in the spaceport landing area in multiple locations. One-liners randomly displayed.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: We don't get much trouble. People die in the desert, not here.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: You a swoop racer? Dead in a week, I bet.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: Move along.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: There some reason you don't move along?

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: I've got orders to kill trouble makers. Keep walking.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: We'll watch your ship like any other. The bay is safe.

speaker: Docking Bay Guard
text: Czerka Corporation has too much invested here to take chances with safety.

speaker: Selkath Apprentice
text: There is much yet to learn of our new ways. But when we do... then the old shell-fish will tremble!

speaker: Selkath Apprentice
text: The Sith have treated us with respect and honor. You must bring us proof before we will believe the accusations of cruelty you make against them.

speaker: RakghoulVic00
text: Please, help us! We are infected with the rakghoul disease. At any moment we could... unh!

speaker: RakghoulVic00
text: NO! This cannot be! Nooo!!

text: The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

text: Activate droid's shields. (<CUSTOM44> repair part(s))

text: WARNING: Once you end this session the droid's program will be locked in. You will not be able to modifiy the droid anymore.

text: Leave it alone.

text: This droid is damaged and inactive.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid. (1 repair part)

speaker: Rusted Sentry
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Selkath
text: The government may not be willing to say anything, but we citizens in the water know what you've done! You would best leave Manaan while you can!

speaker: Selkath
text: Your Republic has provoked us too much! Surely our government will punish the Republic for attempting to harm us!

speaker: Selkath
text: The Sith have been cruelly sabotaged... We  will track down the culprits who have disobeyed our laws and punish them severely!

speaker: Selkath
text: The case of Sunry from the Republic is a perfect example of why off-worlders should be expelled from Manaan!

speaker: Selkath
text: Interrupting another who is not interested in conversation is considered rude on this planet, off-worlder!

speaker: Sarna
text: Hey, you made it! I was beginning to wonder if you were going to show! The party's in full swing - come on in.
comment: Sarna initiates conversation when player enters the Sith party apartment Dialog mission statement: Female players can speak to Sarna and through persuasion and paying credits convince her to arrange for them to get invited to a party where they can steal her keycard. Male players can flirt with her and use persuasion to get invited to a party where they can steal her keycard. Exit points: 1. Player at party, Sarna initiates conversation, fade to black and come back with everyone drunk and passed out. Player can loot body of keycard. 2. Player bribed Sarna, he leaves are to arrange party, mark party apartment on map. 3. Nothing happens 4. Nothing happens. 5. Nothing happens. 6. Player rejected, nothing else happens 7. Player rejected, nothing else happens 8. Player invited to party.

speaker: Sarna
text: You have to try this Tarisian ale - it's fantastic! We should have conquered this planet ages ago!

speaker: YunGenda021
text: Careful, Sarna. That wine's got quite the kick. A couple more bottles and we'll all be passed out on the floor!

speaker: Sarna
text: Who cares? We're not on duty tomorrow - let's live a little! Come on - drink up!

speaker: Sarna
text: I'm surprised to see you again. I thought you had gotten sick of me complaining about my job at the Sith military base. I guess I kind of obsess about it. That can't be healthy.

speaker: Sarna
text: No offense, but I probably shouldn't be talking to you anymore. I'm just going to say something that might get me in trouble.

speaker: Sarna
text: If I could just find some other way to earn some credits I could give this lousy job up. Retire my uniform, so to speak.

speaker: Player
text: Why aren't you in uniform now?

speaker: Sarna
text: Back at the military base, of course. I keep it there when I'm off duty. If anything happens to it they dock the cost from my pay.

speaker: Player
text: If you help me get my hands on some uniforms I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Sarna
text: What? Are you offering me a bribe? You realize this is treason, right? If I report you the Sith will have you executed!

speaker: Player
text: You report me and I'll tell them how you really feel about your job.

speaker: Sarna
text: Hey, now - let's not start making threats. I didn't say I *would* report you, only that I could. This kind of talk is dangerous, you know? But I'm not going to turn you in.

speaker: Sarna
text: The truth is I find your offer rather tempting. I could probably get you some uniforms. But if we get caught we're dead. You're asking me to take an awful risk.

speaker: Sarna
text: If I'm going to do this, it's going to cost you. 200 credits up front if you want some uniforms. No more, no less. So how about it - we have a deal?

speaker: Player
text: Okay - here's 200 credits.

speaker: Sarna
text: Okay, you've got a deal. The trick is to get you the uniforms without the Sith knowing I gave them to you. But I've got a plan.

speaker: Sarna
text: I'm going to a party with some of the other Sith soldiers tonight. You show up and I'll make sure everyone else gets good and drunk. When we pass out you can take our uniforms.

speaker: Player
text: Won't you get in trouble if I steal your uniform?

speaker: Sarna
text: I'll probably get a reprimand for not locking it up, but that's about it. Then, in another month I'll resign and retire with all those credits you gave me.

speaker: Sarna
text: Here - I'll add the address of the party to your datapad. Show up there later. To be on the safe side we shouldn't speak again before or after the party.

speaker: Sarna
text: I'll go make all the arrangements and I'll see you at the party tonight. Just remember - if you get caught with those uniforms, I don't know you.

speaker: Player
text: How do I know this isn't some kind of set up?

speaker: Sarna
text: We're in this together now. If either one of us goes to the Sith we'll both end up in the torture chambers. Anyway, it's not like you have a choice.

speaker: Sarna
text: I'm not giving you your credits back, so you might as well show up at the party later and take the uniforms after we all get drunk and pass out. What could be more simple?

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like a good plan.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Make it 100 credits and we have a deal.

speaker: Sarna
text: [Success] Hmmm... 100 credits is a small fortune. I'll never have the chance to make that much in one shot again.

speaker: Sarna
text: [Failure] Look, I'm not going to risk my neck unless I get a big payday. 200 credits or no deal.

speaker: Player
text: I can't afford that much.

speaker: Sarna
text: Sorry to hear that, but I won't put my neck on the line for nothing! Tell you what - you come up with the credits and we can talk. Otherwise, no deal.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it - I'm not paying that much!

speaker: Player
text: I don't think you'll report me. I think you've been waiting for an offer like this.

speaker: Player
text: Hey, relax - I was just making a joke.

speaker: Sarna
text: You... you weren't serious? Oh... okay. Although if you *were* serious, we might be able to work something out. No - wait! Forget I said that! We shouldn't be talking like this.

speaker: Sarna
text: I might complain a lot, but it's a big step from complaining to treason. I think... I think maybe we should end this conversation - for both our sakes.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Sarna
text: Oh... okay. See you around. Say, do me a favor and don't repeat all the stuff I just told you. It might not go over well with my superiors.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Sarna
text: The senior officers don't really like it when we start answering questions, you know? They don't want us fraternizing with the locals. Just another "perk" of the job.

speaker: Sarna
text: Well, are you here to close our deal? 200 credits gets you access to a set of Sith uniforms. Otherwise, we really shouldn't be talking.

speaker: Sarna
text: Sorry, but I'm not here looking for conversation. I just came to get a drink, listen to some music and try to relax before my next shift at the military base.
comment: If character is female, nothing happens

speaker: Player
text: You're from the military base? You don't look like one of the Sith.

speaker: Sarna
text: I don't wear my uniform when I'm off duty. It's not allowed. In fact, anyone in uniform is banned from entering the cantina.

speaker: Sarna
text: The officers don't even like it when we show up here off duty. Don't like us fraternizing with the locals, I guess. But it gets pretty stale hanging around the base all the time.

speaker: Sarna
text: Besides, the Sith don't own me. Being a soldier in their fleet is just a job, you know? A job with long hours and low pay, I might add.

speaker: Player
text: So why do you do it?

speaker: Sarna
text: When I signed up I was promised adventure and excitement in exotic locales. Instead, I end up stationed at a military base on some backwater planet on the fringes of the galaxy.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like you aren't very happy.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in chatting right now.

speaker: Sarna
text: First you come over and say hi, then you scurry off as soon as you find out I'm a Sith soldier. You Tarisians are a funny bunch.

speaker: Sarna
text: Hey, there. I didn't think we'd be chatting again so soon. You took off on me pretty quick last time.

speaker: Sarna
text: I'm actually a little surprised you're talking to me at all... most of the people here on Taris can't stand us Sith. It can make this job pretty lonely.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] You're just doing your job, right? I don't hold that against you.

speaker: Sarna
text: [Success] That's true, but people don't appreciate what we've done for them. We could have slapped a curfew on this whole planet, but we didn't.

speaker: Sarna
text: You know, it's like everyone on this backwater planet is in a permanent bad mood. Don't they know we have to make the best of things?

speaker: Player
text: You've got a pretty positive attitude.

speaker: Sarna
text: Exactly! It's all about attitude. I didn't ask to be assigned to this backwater planet, but I try to make the best of it!

speaker: Sarna
text: It's pretty easy to get depressed on an assignment like this, but we do what we can to keep our spirits up.

speaker: Player
text: You need to blow off steam once in a while.

speaker: Sarna
text: That's true. It's nice to meet someone who understands what I'm going through. It's good to talk about this stuff - it gets pretty lonely up at the military base.

speaker: Sarna
text: I have to get going soon - I've got a shift at the military base. But some of us junior Sith officers are having a party tonight to blow off some steam.

speaker: Sarna
text: I'd really like to see you again. Why don't you drop by the party? I'll show you where it is on your map.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds good. I'll be there.

speaker: Sarna
text: Don't be late. We're starting right after our shifts end. Most of us won't even be going back to the base to lock up our uniforms. I look forward to seeing you there.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think I can make it.

speaker: Sarna
text: Just because I'm with the Sith doesn't mean I don't know how to have a good time. You'll enjoy yourself. I promise.

speaker: Player
text: It must be tough, being stationed on a hostile world.

speaker: Player
text: Everybody has their ups and downs... it's how you deal with them that counts.

speaker: Sarna
text: [Failure] Save the sympathetic best friend act. I'm not buying it.

speaker: Sarna
text: But I don't want to fill out a bunch of paperwork on my day off, so let's just pretend this conversation never happened. Now move along.

speaker: Player
text: You can't really blame people... you did conquer the planet.

speaker: Sarna
text: Oh, great... I see where this is going: the Sith are evil; why did I join them; blah, blah, blah. I don't need a lecture from the likes of you.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry - I'm not trying to judge you.

speaker: Sarna
text: Ah, it's okay. I might have overreacted a bit. But can you blame me? Everywhere I look I see one of you Tarisians glaring at me with hate in your eyes.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not actually from Taris. I'm just stuck here until the quarantine ends.

speaker: Sarna
text: You're an off-worlder? Huh, I figured you'd be even more angry, being stuck on a foreign planet and all.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Hey, we're both strangers on Taris. We have to stick together.

speaker: Sarna
text: [Success] You're right! It's like everyone on this backwater planet is in a permanent bad mood. Don't they know they have to make the best of things?

speaker: Player
text: Being stuck on Taris isn't so bad... but the locals aren't much fun.

speaker: Player
text: You seem pretty touchy about this. Maybe you feel a little guilty about what you do.

speaker: Sarna
text: Don't try to analyze me. I'm just doing my job - same as any other soldier in any other army. Besides, I don't have to explain myself to you!

speaker: Sarna
text: I don't think we have much else to say to each other. Let's keep this civil and go our separate ways, okay?

speaker: Sarna
text: Back again? Didn't I make myself clear enough? The senior Sith officers don't like us fraternizing with the locals. Besides, I don't need you lecturing me for my career choice.

speaker: Sarna
text: Hi there - I haven't seen you around before. Of course they don't give us Sith officers from the military base much time off...

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Good job! Come talk to me!

speaker: Bantha
text: [This bantha perks up as you approach, obviously attracted to the smell of the fodder you are carrying. The whole herd falls in step.]

speaker: Bantha
text: This bantha is completely disinterested in you.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I won't speak with you, outsider. Chuundar allows too many of you here.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Chuundar may tolerate you, but do not expect the same from all of us.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You will never take me as a slave, outsider. By Bacca's Blade, you will not!

speaker: Wookiee
text: It was not long ago that Kashyyyk had no outsider taint.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Freyyr is back in power! Slavers will learn to fear us now!

speaker: Wookiee
text: Chuundar deserved death. He made us fearful and weak.

speaker: Wookiee
text: The honor of Kashyyyk is tainted. Only slaver blood will make things right.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Freyyr has been through much. His wrath will make us strong.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Rorworr has not returned to the village in days. If slavers took him, they had a fight on their hands.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Many are talking of Rorworr's disappearance. It is hardest on the young.

speaker: Wookiee
text: We lose more of our most promising warriors everyday.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Bacca's Blade keep Rorworr safe and Bacca's wisdom guide him home to us.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Even when serving justice, you outsiders find a way to profit. Leave me alone, mercenary.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Jaarak's fate would be easier to stomach if an outsider had not profited from it.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You surprise me with your mercy, outsider. I wouldn't have thought it possible.

speaker: Wookiee
text: The shame of Rorworr's actions will haunt us. Justice was properly merciful with his killer.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I am not accustomed to speaking with you outsiders. Some have gotten too comfortable with it, I think.

speaker: Juhani
text: You... you are strong. Stronger than me, even in my darkness.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Juhani
text: I am Juhani, and this is my grove. This is the place of my dark power.

speaker: Juhani
text: This is the place you have invaded. When I embraced the dark side, this was where I sought my solace. It is MINE!

speaker: Player
text: You embraced the dark side? Why?

speaker: Juhani
text: When I slew my Master, Quatra, I knew I could never go back. And now I revel in my dark power.

speaker: Juhani
text: Power enough to crush the life from someone such as you... or so I had thought...

speaker: Player
text: The dark side is never powerful enough.

speaker: Juhani
text: *sigh* What is it you want? Why do you bother me?

speaker: Player
text: I was sent by the Council to cleanse the taint from this grove.

speaker: Juhani
text: The Council has sent you here to kill me? Why, then, when you bested me so easily, did you not simply finish your task? Is it not apparent that I can never be saved?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I have no desire to kill you, Juhani.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Success] You... you do not?

speaker: Juhani
text: I am pathetic. I sit here and think myself to be great by embracing the dark side, but I am nothing! There is no way I could be turned back!

speaker: Juhani
text: I always thought they held me back, were jealous of my power. But it is only because I was not good enough to meet their standards... I never have been.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Come now, Juhani. You are a beautiful young woman who has much talent.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Success] I thank you for your kind words, Jedi.

speaker: Juhani
text: You seem to know just what affects me...

speaker: Juhani
text: I seem to still have much to learn... Both about being a Jedi, and about myself.

speaker: Juhani
text: But I wish the cost of my ignorance had not been so high. I wish that my Master had not suffered because of me.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] It is not your fault, Juhani.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Success] I only wish things could have been different...

speaker: Juhani
text: If she were alive now, there would be so much I would say to her... So much I would apologize for.

speaker: Juhani
text: I think, in my own way, I truly loved her...

speaker: Juhani
text: Oh, how can the Council ever take me back with what I have done? Striking my Master down in anger is unforgivable!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Do not worry, Juhani. They will surely take you back.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Success] I should convince them that I am truly repentant, that I am willing to forsake the dark side.

speaker: Juhani
text: Maybe, just maybe, they would accept me back.

speaker: Juhani
text: Do you think they would? Could it be possible after what I have done?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Of course it would. They would always accept you back.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Success] I... I thank you, master Jedi.

speaker: Juhani
text: I will return to the Council, then. I shall submit myself to their judgment, and hope that they will forgive me.

speaker: Juhani
text: If only there was some way I could make this up to you...

speaker: Juhani
text: Again, I thank you. I am sure I will hear great things about you in the future.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Failure] The Council may forgive a lot... But not this.

speaker: Juhani
text: I am lost! Even though I would repent, there is nowhere left for me to go!

speaker: Juhani
text: Leave me to my hopelessness!

speaker: Player
text: It might be.

speaker: Juhani
text: The Council may forgive a lot... But not this.

speaker: Player
text: Unlikely... But it's worth a shot.

speaker: Player
text: Your inner peace and harmony will show them your sincerity.

speaker: Juhani
text: I... I thank you, master Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: I do not know.

speaker: Player
text: If you can't bring yourself back, then I must slay you.

speaker: Juhani
text: What? No! I will not let you take me now!

speaker: Player
text: Anger? Show them that you have freed yourself of this base passion.

speaker: Juhani
text: If I show them I am free of passion... That I am serene... That I am willing to forsake the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: The Council may forgive a lot.

speaker: Player
text: Heh. Your Master surely won't be forgiving you.

speaker: Juhani
text: You... You monster! To mock my grief that way!

speaker: Juhani
text: Leave me at once, lest I strike you down!

speaker: Player
text: Yet forgiveness must be asked.

speaker: Juhani
text: And denied! No, I cannot! And so here I will stay.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Failure] It is! It is!

speaker: Juhani
text: It was I who hurt her, I who killed her! Her suffering is my fault alone!

speaker: Juhani
text: Leave me to my pain!

speaker: Player
text: Even in death, the Force will allow her to live on.

speaker: Player
text: Life is a learning experience.

speaker: Juhani
text: But learning does not have to end in death!

speaker: Player
text: Your master knew the risks.

speaker: Juhani
text: She knew I would be headstrong, but she also thought I would adhere to the light!

speaker: Juhani
text: Instead, I betrayed her trust and fell prey to my own inner darkness.

speaker: Player
text: Life is suffering.

speaker: Juhani
text: Life is suffering, yes... but it was by my conscious choice!

speaker: Player
text: I suppose there is no hope. I must kill you then.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Failure] You think compliments will convince me I didn't kill my master? Leave me to my agony!

speaker: Player
text: Why are you even thinking like that?

speaker: Juhani
text: Why? Because I am right, that's why! I can see the truth in your eyes as well!

speaker: Juhani
text: Do not look at me again!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you shouldn't have been a Jedi, then.

speaker: Juhani
text: They came to me! They sought me out! So it is their failure that I have fallen.

speaker: Juhani
text: Come back when you have something more meaningful to say.

speaker: Player
text: Standards cannot apply to everyone.

speaker: Juhani
text: What?? What foolishness is this? Standards are MADE to apply to everyone.

speaker: Juhani
text: And if I cannot measure up to them... Well then, I am no one at all...

speaker: Juhani
text: Leave me.

speaker: Player
text: The first step on the path of true knowledge is knowing that you are ignorant.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Failure] Lies! Leave me and come back when you have the courage to finish your task!

speaker: Player
text: You're right, maybe I should.

speaker: Juhani
text: Act or begone!

speaker: Player
text: I do not hold anger towards you, Juhani. I wish you peace.

speaker: Juhani
text: Not anger, peace... Yet even with your naive attitude you managed to beat me.

speaker: Player
text: I wasn't really ordered to kill you.

speaker: Juhani
text: Thinking of using technicalities to do the deed and ease your conscience?

speaker: Player
text: I just want to talk.

speaker: Juhani
text: Talk?! You who have beaten me so easily just want to talk? I do not believe it. Kill me now, while you still have the power.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you doing this?

speaker: Juhani
text: I have fallen and dark power courses through my veins. I can never go back to the Council, so here I shall stay.

speaker: Player
text: I will leave you now.

speaker: Juhani
text: Flee back to your masters, Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: I have decided to slay you and remove the taint.

speaker: Juhani
text: You overestimate yourself, whelp!

speaker: Player
text: And I laugh at your pathetic attempt.

speaker: Player
text: You slew Quatra, your Master?

speaker: Juhani
text: Yes, I struck her down in the middle of training, consumed by my anger, embracing the power of hate!

speaker: Juhani
text: But... it was not enough...

speaker: Player
text: You shall be the one I crush!

speaker: Player
text: You were a Jedi then?

speaker: Juhani
text: A better Jedi than you will ever be. More powerful as well, for I could best MY teacher.

speaker: Player
text: You've been corrupting the kath hounds?

speaker: Juhani
text: Yes... Aren't they pretty? My pets...

speaker: Juhani
text: They like the smell of power I exude. They know their master.

speaker: Juhani
text: I harnessed true power when I struck down my Master, Quatra.

speaker: Player
text: And now I'll take it from you.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here?

speaker: Player
text: Why did you attack me?

speaker: Player
text: And I'll finish you now.

speaker: Juhani
text: I, Juhani, shall be your death!

speaker: Juhani
text: I do not know what to do. Now that I have caused such suffering to my Master and those around me...

speaker: Juhani
text: How can I ever face the Council now with what I have done? It is hopeless! It could not be possible that they would accept me back...

speaker: SithPatrol091
text: Intruders in the base! Attack! Attack!

speaker: Ignus
text: Shame about Sunry getting convicted like that. I guess he really did kill Elassa after all.

speaker: Ignus
text: There, you got what you wanted: Sunry's free. Now don't ever mention my part in this again!

speaker: Ignus
text: I guess Sunry didn't kill the Sith woman after all. Could have sworn he left after the shot though...

speaker: Ignus
text: You're the one defending Sunry now, eh? Well, the hotel's open for you and I guess I got to answer any questions you want, too.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what you saw the night of the murder.

speaker: Ignus
text: The Sith woman Elassa rented a room in the hotel. An hour or two later Sunry comes in and goes to her room. A couple hours later I hear a blaster shot and see Sunry running.

speaker: Ignus
text: Sure. *wink* *wink* Sunry left before the blaster went off, so he couldn't have done it.

speaker: Ignus
text: Do you need to know anything else?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about Sunry and Elassa?

speaker: Ignus
text: Elassa used to rent rooms here every week or so. Then Sunry would come by a couple hours later and stay all night.

speaker: Ignus
text: It doesn't take a genius to figure out what was going on.

speaker: Player
text: Who are the witnesses in the hotel?

speaker: Ignus
text: There were only two other people in the hotel when it happened. One was a Rodian named Gluupor. Seems like a really dirty, shifty type.

speaker: Ignus
text: Normally I don't let his kind in here - I'm a reputable business man, you know! - but there weren't many people here, so I decided to take a chance.

speaker: Ignus
text: The other is a regular named Firith Me. He's a Pazaak player. Probably an addict, but he claims he's big in some circles.

speaker: Ignus
text: Don't know anything about him other than that.

speaker: Ignus
text: Anything else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: I have no more questions for now.

speaker: Ignus
text: Well, OK. If you need anything else I'm going to be right here.

speaker: Ignus
text: He can't run good 'cause he's a cripple, but still he was going pretty fast. I would swear he started after the shot though.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure?

speaker: Ignus
text: Yeah, I'm pretty damn sure he left after the shot went off.

speaker: Player
text: Could it have gone off after he left?

speaker: Ignus
text: No, I don't think so. I mean, it's possible, just barely, but I wouldn't say that to the court.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] You could testify it happened after he left.

speaker: Ignus
text: [Failure] No. No way I'm lying to the court just because you want to get your Republic buddy off, or whatever. I have no interest in going to prison!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I could pay you 200 credits to say it.

speaker: Ignus
text: [Success] That's a lot of money... Maybe I could do something for you then.

speaker: Ignus
text: Alright, I'll do it. I'll tell the Selkath that he left before the shot went off, but this is our little secret. If you try and turn me in for lying, I'm making sure you come with me!

speaker: Bastila
text: I know you want to help Sunry, but we should not be manufacturing evidence like this.

speaker: Ignus
text: Now, was there anything else you wanted?

speaker: Juhani
text: I see you are more interested in winning than in trying to solve this case. I cannot say I approve of your actions here.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmm... I guess this is what they call working the system. Not that I'm objecting. I just hope the Selkath don't find out about it.

speaker: Mission
text: Looks like Manaan isn't much different than Taris: justice is up for grabs to the highest bidder.

speaker: Carth
text: Are you sure this is a good idea? I mean, I want to help get Sunry acquitted, but what if the Selkath find out about this?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You will testify Sunry left before the shot.

speaker: Ignus
text: [Success] Yeah. I'll tell the court Sunry left before the shot went off.

speaker: Mechanic

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Greetings, Revan, I am Gjarshi, the loremaster of our tribe.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: I am the keeper of our histories and chronicler of the conquests of the One.

speaker: Player
text: I am not Revan any more! I am <FullName>!

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Your life has been defined by your identity Revan, your fate. If you no longer wish me to call you this, then I shall not, but you cannot change who you are.

speaker: Player
text: A person decides their own fate!

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: As you will. I know better than to argue with you when you have set your mind to something.

speaker: Player
text: Do you not hate me for leaving your people before?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: It does not matter to me what path you choose. History flows in mysterious ways and my task is only to witness and remember which course it takes.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Your actions then, as now, are memories to be passed on to future generations. When you are dead and gone, your memory shall remain with us.

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me of the history of your people?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: What of our people would you like to know?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me how your people came to be.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: In the times before our most ancient histories, there was nothing you could call the Rakatan people. There were unintelligent proto-Rakata wandering the surface of this world.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Spawned from the womb of this world, they were gifted with the brilliance of thought, but not tempered with the wisdom to use it.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: When the gods of the sky first spoke to them, the ground shook and heaved, and fires raced across the surface of the world. They fled beneath the ground to escape the calamity and dwelled there for some time.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: At last the gods spoke to them in dreams... dreams of the surface and the light. They re-emerged from the ground and found the land much changed around them.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Gone were the plains and valleys they had known. Instead, there were islands stretching across the breadth of the world. The world had been remade for them by the gods of the sky, and they gave thanks in fear and gratitude.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the gods you mentioned.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The world is ruled by the gods of the earth and sky, both living and dead.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: When the sky gods remade the world, the gods of the earth, who had sheltered and protected the Rakata, were gone. Whether dead of asleep, they have not been heard from again.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Nor do the gods in the sky listen to our pleas any longer, although we can still see their lights gleam in the heavens.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: So we mortal Rakata are left here to our own devices... to make the future we demand for ourselves.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of your first civilizations.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Back in the days of the first awakening, when our people rose from the ground and brought the light of civilization to our new world, our people spread far and wide across all the islands.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Among these peoples, there were some that rose to greatness on the largest islands. Rakatans of vision and forethought who built great monuments to themselves and their leaders.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But these cultures did not know their true strengths. They did not draw upon the knowledge of their past to feed their present.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Of course these cultures, with their centers of learning and their great temples, collapsed in riots and chaos, burning their cultures from the world in an orgy of violence.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: It was a thousand years of darkness before the light of First Empire rose upon the blood of the past.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the First Empire.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: With the first civilizations of our people destroyed, and chaos and anarchy sweeping the islands, it seemed that a time of darkness had descended upon us that would never end.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But a strong nation of survivors yet endured. On one of the smaller islands near the equatorial regions, they had not forgotten the oldest traditions, those learned from the gods of the earth while we dwelt beneath the surface.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Taking the knowledge of their elders and passing their wisdom and skills on to the next generation by eating their flesh, they built a culture unrivalled throughout history. Greater, even, than your vaunted 'Republic'.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: For millennia this empire stood, uniting the many islands of our world into one cohesive whole. Each generation passing its strength on to the one that followed.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But... fate was unkind to these great Rakata, these first ones of our kind to rise above savagery and create a true, lasting civilization.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what happened to the First Empire.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Our skin had been hardened and turned black from the time our people spent beneath the surface, but always at the fringes of society there were rumors... rumors of those of others colors who survived above the surface while we dwelt below.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We can pinpoint no direct cause for the collapse of the First Empire, but it was swift and total. What had taken centuries to build and was maintained for thousands of years disappeared within ten, perhaps twenty, years.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: From the ancient cities we have examined, there was much fighting and death, as well as fires that burned bright and hot enough to melt the stones of their palaces to glass.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Also, in scattered fragments and records, we have heard of a people being found... a people unlike the Rakata but taking our form, who waged a monumental war that tore civilization apart.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: What this war was, or who those beings were we do not know, but they are the demons of our legends now. We believe them to be gone, wiped out in that vast conflagration, but we cannot know for sure...

speaker: Player
text: What happened after the collapse of the First Empire?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Our civilization lapsed back into savagery. We were no longer the great people of centuries past.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Brother turned on brother, tribesman on tribesman, until all fought and sought to destroy each other.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The legacy of the final war and the collapse that came after it still echo with us today. We are still a fractured people. Many tribes dwell on these islands, warring with each other constantly.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Each seeks to grow its own strength, absorbing that of its enemies through their flesh cut down in battle, but none has been strong enough to exert their influence over more than a handful of islands. Until now that is...

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We now are in the midst of a great war of reformation, of reclamation.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the war of reformation.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Before none were strong enough to bind together the tribes and unite them towards a common goal, but that changed. Now we do have a leader, and under him, we have swept across the islands, conquering all who have stood before us.

speaker: Player
text: This leader... is it the One?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Over the last 20 years we have conquered over a hundred islands, both large and small. The One has led us to victory where none have before, further strengthening us with the blood of our enemies.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We have subjugated many tribes as well, their warriors joining ours in our great crusade.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But recently, things have not gone so well...

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: More and more outsiders fall from the sky and kill our people. More and more tribes resist us, or even rebel!

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: It has taken a great part of our strength to resist, but under the One, we shall prevail! Nothing shall stop him from forming the Second Empire!

speaker: Player
text: What is the One doing here, then?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We... we heard of the temple on this island... the Temple of the Ancients. A building the like of which has not been seen anywhere else. A place of great power it was reputed, with great guardians as well.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The One came here with an army to see this temple and seize it for our cause, but we were met with strange and powerful magics which have defeated us at every turn.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: So now the One sits here and broods on his troubles, listening only to the messengers who bear his orders to all corners of his territory.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: If only the riddle of the temple could be solved, and its guardian Elders removed, then he would consume their flesh and knowledge and bring unity to our people.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: It is my sincere hope as well, that you can help us with our great task.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the One.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The great story of the One would take many days to tell in its entirety. It is my specialty, of course.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: What would you like to know of his great story?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me how he was raised.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Born to poverty, raised in a hovel with no elders to guide him and share their strength with him, he had nothing to rely on but himself.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But in his weakness, he was uniquely destined for strength and the burdens it carries with it.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Even in his youth, it was obvious that the One was destined for greatness. When but a youngling, he defeated one of the strange blue-armored warriors who fall from the sky and feasted upon him.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The respect from his battle gave him the step he needed to go forward on a path that has led him ever upward since.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of how he came to power.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: By adulthood, the One was held in awe by those of his tribe as both a warrior and a leader. When he challenged the chieftain of his tribe, no one doubted that he would prevail.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The chieftain could see and, knowing that the One would bring the tribe into greatness, offered himself up without a fight. The tribe fed well and was stronger for his sacrifice.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Under the leadership of the One, his tribe conquered all others on the island, capturing and subduing their warriors, feasting on their chieftains, and growing his own army at the same time.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: He was truly a force that could not be stopped, a leader unlike any we have seen in our history. He will be the one to unite us all!

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of his conquests.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: After he had conquered his own island, and his army had grown to a large size, he turned his eyes towards the nearest other islands in the archipelago.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: With each island that fell to him, his army grew stronger, his wisdom greater with each chief given up to him, and his vision of a future for our people brighter.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Before long he had conquered every island in a month's sailing and had armies expanding in every direction. It seemed that nothing would stand against him then.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But we heard of the Temple of the Ancients here, on this forgotten island at the edge of the True Sea, and the One was intrigued. It was a place of power, to be sure, and none could doubt its significance.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: Driven by portents and omens, we came to this island with a thousand of his finest warriors... and here we stay...

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We cannot leave while the Temple stands unopened, but we cannot enter while the Elders stand against us... and the One sits each day brooding on the fate that has led us to this impasse.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to know something else.

speaker: Player
text: I must go now.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: If you must. I shall remain here as I always do, listening to those who wish to speak... and remembering.

speaker: Player
text: How many islands have you conquered?

speaker: Player
text: How long has this war been waged?

speaker: Player
text: You are a loremaster? What do you do? Memorize books?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The position of loremaster is a sacred and respected one among our people. We are the keepers of history, the ones who pass down the traditions of our people.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: I am here to chronicle the conquests and achievements of the One. I have followed his exploits for many years... and yours as well.

speaker: Player
text: Mine?

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: When last you came to this island, the One had just arrived with his army. We spoke then, as now, and you told me of your travels and stories about the worlds beyond ours.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: You spoke of the magical Force you wielded which gave you power over the elements.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: But then you left us and went back to the stars, never to be heard from again. We wondered what had happened, what could have gone wrong, but could do nothing against you, or the Elders.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the Elders.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: We know the Elders are Rakata like us, but different as well. They control strange powers and magics that we cannot understand.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: When we came to this island, drawn by the strange structure we call the Temple of the Ancients, we were expecting perhaps a few survivors... but not another race of Rakata.

speaker: Loremaster Gjarshi
text: The One's troops captured a few of their scouts, but we could learn nothing intelligible from them. Attacks against their compound were fruitless and reaped terrible casualties.

speaker: Juhani
text: From that moment on I knew that I would have to try to become a Jedi. To lift myself out of the rut I had been living in for years and to make a real difference, as the Jedi were.

speaker: Juhani
text: The foolish delusions of a child. But THIS child made it happen!

speaker: Juhani
text: As soon as I was able I left my world and went in search of them. I found them and was accepted. I had been living my dream on Dantooine for several years before you came.

speaker: Juhani
text: Although... perhaps I was not entirely ready for it... or not completely suited to the task. Otherwise I would not have fallen...

speaker: Juhani

speaker: Juhani
text: Come, there is much we should do. Let us not waste time talking. Action is what is needed.

speaker: Player
text: Then how did you gain entrance to the Order?

speaker: Player

text: Well... I suppose I have not talked very much about the Jedi I met back home.

text: Not that the peace they brought lasted very long...

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: How did it happen?

speaker: Juhani

speaker: Juhani
text: But in the end we were doomed...

text: Taris is not a nice place to raise a child.

text: The Jedi could have helped!

speaker: Player
text: Why did they flee?

speaker: Juhani
