speaker: Player
text: I didn't think Mandalorians got afraid.

speaker: Canderous
text: Every new warrior has to fear to understand how to beat it. You must know that.

speaker: Canderous
text: The doors opened in front me and the air was sucked out of the drop bay, scattering crystals of frozen vapor across my path.

speaker: Canderous
text: I can't describe what it feels like to look directly down at a world, falling continuously as you circle it, with barely fifteen centimeters of armor plate protecting you.

speaker: Canderous
text: When the magnetic locks disengaged on my droid I plunged out of the drop bay towards the battle that waited below.

speaker: Player
text: You dropped from orbit riding a droid?!

speaker: Canderous
text: The exhilaration, the euphoria, I felt as I streaked into the atmosphere, dodging self-guided projectile and beam weapons, was unmatched.

speaker: Canderous
text: A 80 kilometer plunge through the atmosphere, dodging and weaving, the outside of my armor glowing like the sun with the heat of re-entry.

speaker: Canderous
text: And with barely thirty meters to spare, I twisted and skimmed the surface, firing at the giant beam generators that were in my path.

speaker: Canderous
text: The explosion from that sent shockwaves that levelled the entire complex around it. It was the moment of my life.

speaker: Player
text: That's horrible!

speaker: Canderous
text: I'll never forget those times. But... things are different now. We can't go on fighting the way we had. There are too few of us left now.

speaker: Canderous
text: But I don't really want to talk about this anymore. I trust I've satisfied your curiosity for now?

speaker: Canderous
text: Is there something else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about this world?

speaker: Canderous
text: *grunt* Yeah, I know about Taris. I wasted the last two years in this rat-hole working for Davik.

speaker: Canderous
text: I suppose an accurate way to describe this place would be 'cesspool' or 'dump'.

speaker: Canderous
text: You got the rich people on top, the poor people being crushed underneath, and people like me trying to make a living doing the crushing.

speaker: Canderous
text: It's not exactly what you'd call spiritually fulfilling work, but it gets the bills paid. And on Taris, money can go a long way to making things easier.

speaker: Canderous
text: You have anything else you want to ask?

speaker: Player
text: Can you give me some adrenal stimulants?

speaker: Canderous
text: Heh, don't worry I think you've got enough there as it is. You don't want to go overloading youself on stims, otherwise you might destroy your adrenal system.

speaker: Canderous
text: A real warrior knows his own limits and doesn't overestimate himself.

speaker: Canderous
text: There anything else you need?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me more about the Mandalorian Wars.

speaker: Canderous
text: We fought against the Republic forces for some time, over the course of many battles.

speaker: Canderous
text: At the start, they were not much of a threat to speak of, but once you had taken charge, things began to turn against us.

speaker: Canderous
text: The Republic fleets began to use more than just basic tactics. Feints, counterattacks, mass deceptions. You were a genius on the field. You are held in very high regard among my people.

speaker: Canderous
text: You abandoned worlds of their defenders so that others would be too fortified to strike. You made sacrifices in order to advance your goals. Such strategies had never been enough to best us before.

speaker: Canderous
text: In the end, you proved too much for us.

speaker: Player
text: You couldn't have won against the whole galaxy.

speaker: Canderous
text: But it was close! So close!

speaker: Canderous
text: It looked like the entire galaxy was within our grasp!

speaker: Canderous
text: I still remember that final battle in the skies above Malachor V. The two fleets filling the space around it, outshining the stars...

speaker: Player
text: But you eventually lost.

speaker: Canderous
text: Yeah, we lost. But there is no shame in it. We lost to the greatest single warrior the Republic has ever known.

speaker: Canderous
text: It was not your ships or your men or your vaunted 'fight for freedom' that won this, the final battle of the war.

speaker: Canderous
text: It was by the actions of one person, the Jedi Revan, that you prevailed.

speaker: Canderous
text: Revan's strategies and tactics defeated the best of us. Even Mandalore himself was taken aback by the ferocity, the tenacity and the subtlety of Revan's plans.

speaker: Canderous
text: Revan fought us to a standstill and then began pushing back. We didn't really have a chance.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't you retreat?

speaker: Canderous
text: It was what we had wanted all along, in a way. We wanted to fight the best in a battle that would be remembered for centuries. And we did.

speaker: Canderous
text: And Revan won.

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't hold a grudge against Revan, and neither do any of my people. It was the greatest moment of my life to be in that battle.

speaker: Canderous
text: If Revan had been a Mandalorian, nothing in the galaxy would have stopped us.

speaker: Canderous
text: But wishing for the past to be different is useless. Better to look to the future. As we should now. We'll talk more later, I think.

speaker: Canderous
text: And you won.

speaker: Canderous
text: I hold no grudge against you, nor do any of my people. It was the greatest of honors to fight against you, even in defeat. It is even more of an honor to fight beside you now.

speaker: Canderous
text: Had you been born of the Mandalorian clans, surely nothing in this galaxy would have been able to stop us.

speaker: Player
text: The Republic will always prevail.

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! Don't be naive. The Republic is not invincible. This battle was the end of the war, one way or another.

speaker: Canderous
text: It was by the actions of one person - you - that the Republic prevailed.

speaker: Canderous
text: Your strategies and tactics defeated the best we could send against you. Even Mandalore himself was taken aback by the ferocity of your attacks, the tenacity of your defenses and the subtleties of your plans.

speaker: Canderous
text: You fought us to a standstill and then began pushing back. We didn't really have a chance.

speaker: Player
text: What happened in the battle?

speaker: Player
text: If I had not stopped you, someone else would have.

speaker: Canderous
text: There was no one else. The entire Republic had committed its forces behind you. The Sith had retreated back to their empire and there were none else strong enough to challenge us.

speaker: Player
text: But what about the Sith?

speaker: Canderous
text: The Sith had gone - retreated into their empire. They sealed themselves off from the rest of the galaxy. We thought it would be centuries before they'd come back.

speaker: Canderous
text: It's amazing that they could rebuild their fleet so fast. But at the time, it looked like the galaxy was in our grasp!

speaker: Canderous
text: At the start, they were not much of a threat to speak of, but once the Jedi Revan had taken charge, things began to turn against us.

speaker: Canderous
text: The Republic fleets began to use more than just basic tactics. Feints, counterattacks, mass deceptions. Revan was a genius on the field.

speaker: Canderous
text: Revan abandoned worlds of their defenders so that others would be too fortified to strike, and was willing to make sacrifices in order to advance goals.

speaker: Canderous
text: And in the end, Revan proved too much for us.

speaker: Player
text: If Revan had not stopped you, someone else would have.

speaker: Canderous
text: There was no one else. The entire Republic had committed its forces behind Revan. The Sith had retreated back to their empire and there were none else strong enough to challenge us.

speaker: Canderous
text: The war we had with the Republic was supposed to be the most glorious battle of our history, but... it was a very costly one. I guess we didn't think of how much we could lose in it.

speaker: Player
text: How much did you lose?

speaker: Canderous
text: There weren't many of us left after that last battle. Mandalore himself was killed at the hands of the Jedi Revan. The best of us could not defeat him!

speaker: Canderous
text: After that last battle, those of us that survived were stripped of our weapons, our armor, and our Basilisks.

speaker: Canderous
text: Revan's forces destroyed them while we were forced to watch. Those who hadn't fled earlier were left with nothing to call their own: no weapons, no armor... only the honor of having fought in the battle we just lost.

speaker: Canderous
text: For many this was not enough. While the rest of us were sent into exile on the Outer Rim, they tried to relive the old days - raiding worlds. They're nothing more than bandits now.

speaker: Player
text: And you eventually came to Taris.

speaker: Canderous
text: Yeah, I came to Taris.

speaker: Canderous
text: Enforcing for Davik was not... stimulating. The gangs on Taris and Davik's rivals were trash. They give no thrill in battle, no honor or glory in defeating them. It was like stepping on bugs.

speaker: Canderous
text: I sought worthy challenges, but the best that Taris could offer were nothing to me.

speaker: Canderous
text: But I think now - with you - I may finally find opponents worth fighting.

speaker: Player
text: I am honored.

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe later I'll tell you more about what it was like to work for Davik. For now, though, we should get on with our lives.

speaker: Player
text: You are a worthy companion.

speaker: Player
text: Opponents who could easily kill us.

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe it'll happen, maybe it won't. Either way, I think that by following you I can get something out of it.

speaker: Player
text: You found work as a mercenary?

speaker: Canderous
text: Yeah. I found work on Taris.

speaker: Canderous
text: The Republic's forces destroyed them while we were forced to watch. Those who hadn't fled earlier were left with nothing to call their own: no weapons, no armor... only the honor of having fought in the battle we just lost.

speaker: Player
text: There must not have been many of you left.

speaker: Player
text: But I kicked your tails so badly?

speaker: Canderous
text: Yeah... yeah you did. You were a great warrior Revan. A great general.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about when you worked for Davik.

speaker: Canderous
text: Working for Davik was like driving a spike through the side of your head... Sure you get something new in there, but in the end, you've lost something as well.

speaker: Canderous
text: Beating up people who wouldn't - or couldn't - pay, strong-arming his competitors, killing who he said. It was busy work, nothing decent.

speaker: Player
text: You were an assassin?

speaker: Canderous
text: Assassin. Mercenary. Those are names people give guys like me who do the killing to make us seem better or worse in their eyes.

speaker: Canderous
text: I've killed many people. I can't say I'm proud of it, but I have. Criminals, competitors, businessmen, police... women, children...

speaker: Canderous
text: Jedi were a better challenge, but they hardly ever poked around in the Under City.

speaker: Canderous
text: ... Until you came along...

speaker: Canderous
text: But I never wanted to challenge you. Never felt the need. Maybe I knew I couldn't win... just like all those years ago.

speaker: Player
text: A wise decision.

speaker: Canderous
text: Yeah, probably. Heh. You'd likely have beaten me again.

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe you would have. But you're not who you were back then, I can tell. You've changed... and maybe I have too.

speaker: Canderous
text: I remember a time when I could do anything I wanted... Kill, maim, murder... It was all the same to me.

speaker: Canderous
text: But now... now that I'm older, I can look back and regret...

speaker: Player
text: Regret in a Mandalorian is unbecoming.

speaker: Canderous
text: In a Mandalorian... I'm not even sure what that is anymore. The Mandalorian are gone, defeated by the Republic and swept away by time.

speaker: Canderous
text: I look back and regret all the chances I had as a warrior, and then all the chances I've had since then. I shouldn't be getting like this, not when so many other things are happening... but...

speaker: Canderous
text: It feels like... like something has changed inside and I don't know what it is. Bah! This is unbecoming of a warrior! Let's get on with everything before I start getting sentimental or something.

speaker: Player
text: Over what?

speaker: Player
text: I regret to tell you that I never regret anything.

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! Good one. That's like a warrior should. Like what you see in a Mandalorian.

speaker: Player
text: You know I'd have beaten you again!

speaker: Player
text: Killed his competitors?

speaker: Player
text: Now that's the way things should be done!

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe...

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about it later. I want to ask something else.

speaker: Player
text: What are your thoughts now?

speaker: Canderous
text: I'm not happy with the way my life has turned. I'm not the Mandalore I once was. I don't even think I'm the merc I was when I joined you.

speaker: Canderous
text: I think... I think I need something more than killing and fighting in my life. I need a purpose or something like that.

speaker: Player
text: What will you do?

speaker: Canderous
text: The way the Mandalorians - we - fought... it holds no appeal for me. To rape and ravage worlds for the thrill of battle... It gets old. Very old.

speaker: Canderous
text: Honor in battle. Cheating death. Comrades in arms. The code of the Mandalore.

speaker: Canderous
text: I think I'm something different now. Maybe more, maybe less.

speaker: Player
text: You aren't a Mandalorian now?

speaker: Canderous
text: No... The time of the clans is past. I don't think the galaxy wants them anymore. Maybe in the future, but not now.

speaker: Canderous
text: Once my time with you is done, once you have moved on to greater things, I'll find my own way once again.

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe the Mandalorian clans will be reborn again. Maybe even under the Republic... or the Sith.

speaker: Canderous
text: But dreaming about the future is stupid right now. We should get down to our business and finish it. If we survive all this... maybe we could talk about it then.

speaker: Player
text: What are you going to do?

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't think there is really any place left in the galaxy for the Mandalorian clans like they were. I don't know if I can go on forever fighting as I have. Even warriors get insightful in their old age...

speaker: Player
text: Isn't killing enough?

speaker: Canderous
text: Killing is never enough. Anybody can kill just by pushing a button. A warrior fights his battles himself - as you have done - and tries to defeat all comers.

speaker: Player
text: That doesn't sound much like a Mandalorian...

speaker: Player
text: Nothing more for now.

speaker: Canderous
text: Your choice. I'm here if you want something done right.

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! Stimulants make a warrior out of even the weakest human!

speaker: Canderous
text: Here's a speed boosting stimulant to help you get quicker.

speaker: Canderous
text: Here's a strength boosting stimulant to help you get stronger.

speaker: Canderous
text: Here's a stamina boosting stimulant to help you get tougher.

speaker: Canderous
text: From what we saw from space this world doesn't have a lot of people. I couldn't really have found much work here anyway, so I never had an interest.

speaker: Canderous
text: It looks like a farm world. The Republic has thousands of these places - ones that get by farming crops and hunting herds of native beasts.

speaker: Canderous
text: But I might have underestimated this place. It seems to be more than I had thought.

speaker: Canderous
text: Water worlds never had much of an appeal for us to conquer. They may put up a good fight in their own environment - no match for us, of course - but they don't really have anything of value either.

speaker: Canderous
text: The thing this world is good for is a substance known as Kolto. Kolto is the single best healing substance in the galaxy.

speaker: Canderous
text: But the Mandalore are not as weak and fragile as your Republic and Sith warriors. When we enter battle, we carry weapons powerful enough to pulverize cities.

speaker: Canderous
text: Both in our wars, and in our own personal combats, there are no survivors. So Kolto does not hold the appeal it does for your peoples.

speaker: Canderous
text: Well... It has big trees - in case your eyes don't work anymore. But I do know that there is one exceptional race on this world: the Wookiees.

speaker: Canderous
text: The Wookiees, although primitive compared to us, are surprisingly capable warriors. They're pretty strong and pick up combat techniques pretty quick.

speaker: Canderous
text: I think they're more than a match for the average Republic or Sith trooper. When we were looking for targets, we considered this world carefully.

speaker: Canderous
text: We were wondering if we'd have to use larger weapons than our war droids if we wanted to clear the damn forests so we could fight in the open.

speaker: Canderous
text: Too many trees means they can go into hiding too easy. And what's a continent or two turned to glass if we get the whole world after.

speaker: Canderous
text: Tatooine is one big desert with rocks sticking out. I heard that some of my people came here after the war, but I don't know what happened to them.

speaker: Canderous
text: The world of my clan - Ordo - was much like this. Dust basins and rock crags. But my world at least has some green around the equator - this place is just sand all over.

speaker: Canderous
text: There are some vicious people on this world, but the desert is the real enemy. Trips out in the desert - especially the deep desert - should be taken very carefully.

speaker: Canderous
text: Korriban is a Sith world, that's for sure. I mean, just look at this place.

speaker: Canderous
text: When we were fighting with the Republic with the Sith, this was one of the major staging points for the invasion.

speaker: Canderous
text: We were never allowed to land our troops on the world though, so we never knew what the Sith really do here.

speaker: Canderous
text: Rumor has it that the leader of our clans at the time, Mandalore, did go down. They say the Sith perform terrible magics here.

speaker: Canderous
text: This world is... odd. It looks like a battlefield, but the environment here is lush and green. Whatever happened here was a long time ago.

speaker: Canderous
text: I have seen many strange worlds in my time, but this world is stranger still.

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't like this place. Something happened... or is happening here and I don't like it. We should get out of here as soon as possible.

speaker: Player
text: That was some fight.

speaker: Player
text: I want a Basilisk war droid!

speaker: Player
text: Those droids sure are something.

speaker: Player
text: Who were you fighting anyway?

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't remember. It doesn't matter anyway, that world's dead now.

speaker: Player
text: Ha! Some Mandalorian you were!

speaker: Player
text: What happened next?

speaker: Player
text: How barbaric!

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! We would travel from world to world, and descend on it in our Basilisk war droids. I still remember my first combat...

speaker: Player
text: I would have harnessed that power sooner.

speaker: Canderous
text: We were still recovering from the war we fought with the Sith. We were not yet strong enough to fight the Republic again. We needed to train another generation to do that.

speaker: Canderous
text: You want another story, eh? You want to hear about some other world getting wasted? Heh, I knew you were the type.

speaker: Canderous
text: Your stagnant Republic has never seen some of the strange creatures and races we fought on the Outer Rim in those years. Heh, and you never will now.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Canderous
text: If a world isn't strong enough to defend itself, it's basically forfeit. But this story is about something a little different.

speaker: Canderous
text: We were going through the asteroid fields of the Crispin system at the very edge of the galaxy, playing with the pirates and smugglers we found there.

speaker: Canderous
text: The main belt in the Crispin system consists of mainly small rocks covered in frozen methane gas shells and the pirates were using them for cover.

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! I remember using a thermal generator to cause the outer layer of one of the asteroids to vaporize in a picosecond. It blew out and shredded the three smugglers using it for cover!

speaker: Canderous
text: But... that was a mistake...

speaker: Player
text: Why? What happened?

speaker: Canderous
text: The asteroid I had targeted was smaller than most, maybe a dozen meters on a side. On the outside it looked the same as any other: just a ball covered in frozen gas.

speaker: Canderous
text: But something must have been inside it... something inactive in the cold. The heat of my blast might have triggered something or woken something up.

speaker: Canderous
text: After I had hit, spots of light and heat appeared all over the thin shell still covering it, evaporating the gases.

speaker: Canderous
text: What lay underneath looked like some sort of rocky growth... a deformed rock pitted by scores of micrometeorite scars. I think something even older might have been inside that.

speaker: Player
text: An asteroid?

speaker: Canderous
text: Maybe... but maybe not.

speaker: Canderous
text: It started rotating - faster and faster as we watched it. After a second it started spraying fire - thermal projectiles that melted our armor like wax. We were caught completely by surprise.

speaker: Canderous
text: Before we could counter-attack, it fled at an incredible speed.

speaker: Player
text: A ship!

speaker: Canderous
text: We couldn't catch it, but we could follow its hyperspace wake.

speaker: Canderous
text: We followed its trail as far as we could, heading away from the galactic core. When it finally led beyond the edge of our galaxy, we abandoned our efforts.

speaker: Canderous
text: Anything that wants to commit suicide in that great void is not worth our trouble trying to catch.

speaker: Canderous
text: That's the only story I have for now. I'll tell you some more stuff later, if we get the chance.

speaker: Player
text: Did it backfire?

speaker: Player
text: You Mandalorians never were too smart.

speaker: Player
text: Where did you fight this time?

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't have as many strange stories like the last one I told you, but I do have a couple about me and the stuff I've done.

speaker: Canderous
text: In one battle above the world of Althir, my unit managed to defeat a force of Althiri ten times our own size. That battle gained me command of an entire sub-sect of my clan.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me the story.

speaker: Canderous
text: For five days they had managed to hold off our forces, keeping us to the outer rings of their world, preventing us from attacking it directly.

speaker: Canderous
text: My task was to assault one of their flanks with a false attack. The Althiri would be drawn out by the units I had sent in.

speaker: Canderous
text: Once they had surrounded those units, the bulk of my forces would attack from the rear and defeat them in detail.

speaker: Player
text: Ah. Did it work?

speaker: Canderous
text: Things did not go as I had planned. I saw an opening - a mistake they had made in the disposition of their forces - and took it!

speaker: Canderous
text: While fending off our main force, they had let their fleet split in two! The center of their entire fleet was left exposed!

speaker: Canderous
text: I turned my forces and assaulted the center of their fleet, decimating them!

speaker: Player
text: You were a great warrior Canderous.

speaker: Canderous
text: Their slow, ponderous ship could not turn to face us without being overwhelmed. Their command vessels were destroyed in seconds. Their ranks were thrown into chaos.

speaker: Canderous
text: It was most amusing to watch the surviving ships scatter and flee. Several even tried to dive through the plane of the rings to escape us!

speaker: Canderous
text: They were shredded by the rings, or crashed into rocks, or were destroyed by our forces as we pursued them.

speaker: Canderous
text: Warriors do not flee from a battle if they are losing. They fight to the end! As we did against you.

speaker: Canderous
text: Another time maybe I'll tell you about how the war with the Republic went. For now let's just get on with things.

speaker: Canderous
text: Warriors do not flee from a battle if they are losing. They fight to the end! As we did against your Jedi Revan.

speaker: Player
text: You disobeyed your orders?

speaker: Canderous
text: This is a chance given to a warrior once or twice in a lifetime. The chance to change the course of history in a single act.

speaker: Player
text: What did they do?

speaker: Player
text: Let me guess... you won?

speaker: Player
text: These Althiri don't seem too bright.

speaker: Canderous
text: They weren't stupid. Stupid races don't make starships and weapons of mass destruction. But they weren't masters of the arts of war as Mandalorians are.

speaker: Player
text: I think I know where this is going.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, yeah, you were a great warrior.

speaker: Canderous
text: Ha! I was the best! Except for Mandalore of course. He was the only person alive except Revan who could have beat me.

speaker: Canderous
text: Hm... I think I'll tell you a bit about the recent war we had with the Republic. That might be more familiar to you.

speaker: Canderous
text: The one where you beat my people.

speaker: Canderous
text: We started by conquering worlds just outside the Republic. We did it quietly so the Republic wouldn't really know what was going on until too late.

speaker: Canderous
text: When we finally did hit the Republic worlds, they had no idea we were coming.

speaker: Canderous
text: We came in through three invasion corridors in adjacent sectors. Anyone who put up a fight - or wouldn't fight - was crushed. We razed whole worlds trying to provoke the Republic into fighting us.

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't particularly enjoy wiping out worlds for its own sake, but the cowardly tactics the Republic defenders used left us little choice.

speaker: Player
text: No honor in defending themselves?

speaker: Canderous
text: Hiding in the homes of civilians. Using families as shields. Thinking we would not use appropriate force on their bases inside major cities.

speaker: Canderous
text: They underestimated our resolve and what measures are acceptable in war. Those who cannot defend themselves should not be around those who can in battle.

speaker: Canderous
text: If annihilating a city is the kind of power it takes to overwhelm a Republic shield device, then that's what we did. Necessary force to destroy all opposition.

speaker: Player
text: But killing people is wrong!

speaker: Canderous
text: It's wrong to hide with shields surrounding you hoping the enemy will be so good as to throw themselves at your feet to be slaughtered!

speaker: Canderous
text: I have no time or patience for cowards! They deserve to be hunted down and exterminated like vermin!

speaker: Canderous
text: There was no honor in wiping them out like rats. But some of your forces did redeem the Republic in our eyes... especially later...

speaker: Player
text: Later?

speaker: Canderous
text: Later... when you had joined the war. We'll get back to that, we've wasted too much time already.

speaker: Canderous
text: Later... when Revan had joined the war. But we'll get back to that, we've wasted too much time already.

speaker: Player
text: How did they redeem themselves?

speaker: Player
text: You mean when we kicked your tails.

speaker: Player
text: You could have found another way.

speaker: Player
text: Now that's my kind of warfare.

speaker: Player
text: You had the choice not to destroy them.

speaker: Canderous
text: They had the choice not to fight. We meet the enemy wherever they are hiding and we wipe them out. A few cities is a small price to pay for a world.

speaker: Canderous
text: The one where the Jedi Revan beat my people.

speaker: Player
text: Can you help me with our little stowaway problem?

speaker: Canderous
text: What? You think I don't have something better to do?

speaker: Player
text: Have you seen all these gizka on the ship?

speaker: Canderous
text: So deal with it. Why are you asking me about it?

speaker: Player
text: [Don't speak to him.]

speaker: Canderous
text: [You decide to ignore Canderous and continue on with your quest for now, though it might be a good idea to speak with him later.]

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't think we can delay much here. We should fight our way out as quickly as possible.

speaker: Canderous
text: This looks like the end of our partnership. The battle we fight here will change the face of the galaxy.

speaker: Canderous
text: You, Revan, are the single greatest warrior of this age, and any battle we fight will bring me honor. I'll stay by your side through anything.

speaker: Canderous
text: I don't think I'm ready to give up this life of mine, this life of fighting, not quite yet. We have things we need to do here.

speaker: Canderous
text: I'm your man until the end, whatever path you take.

speaker: Canderous
text: I've been given a challenge I can't ignore. We've got to go to the dune seas of Tatooine so I can find Jagi and kill him for his insult to me!

speaker: Player
text: What happened out there? Why is Jagi so mad at you?

speaker: Canderous
text: This is between me and Jagi. You don't have to get involved. If you're lucky, he might spill something before I spread him in a paste over the dunes.

speaker: Player
text: Can we talk about this?

speaker: Player
text: We should get going then.

speaker: Canderous
text: The sooner we get to Tatooine the better.

speaker: Canderous
text: I... I think this has affected me in ways that I didn't anticipate... I think I'll need time to sort things out.

speaker: Canderous
text: Thanks for what you did, whatever your intentions might have been. I just need... time.

speaker: Canderous
text: Hmph. That trick would never work on a Mandalorian. Our minds are not so weak and easily twisted.

speaker: Canderous
text: *whisper* I'm amazed at how many people that works on. The entire galaxy must be filled with weak-minded fools.

speaker: Canderous
text: I like the way you handled that. Are you sure you don't have some Mandalorian blood in you?

speaker: Canderous
text: The role of the weak is to serve the will of the strong; I'm glad you understand that.

speaker: Canderous
text: Mighty generous of you. A little too generous, if you ask me.

speaker: Canderous
text: What was that all about? Are you going soft on me?

speaker: Selven
text: Stop right there, or I'll give you a blaster shot right between the eyes! Now, what are you doing here?
comment: inits dialog whenever player enters room (or open chests)

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Selven
text: No. I'm the one with the blaster pointed at you. I get to ask the questions. Now - what are you doing here?

speaker: Player
text: You can't talk to the Sith like that!

speaker: Selven
text: You think I care if you're with the Sith? I've killed plenty of your kind before and I've got no problem doing it again!

speaker: Selven
text: Now you'll see why I'm the most dangerous assassin on Taris!

speaker: Player
text: I was just exploring. I didn't know anyone was in here.

speaker: Selven
text: Well go explore somewhere else. There's nothing interesting for you in here. This is your only warning - if you bother me again, you won't walk out of here alive!

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to collect the bounty on your head, Selven!

speaker: Selven
text: You're a fool if you think you can collect the price on my head!

speaker: Player
text: I'm just here to rob the place.

speaker: Selven
text: Bad luck for you that you picked my apartment then.

speaker: Selven
text: I gave you a chance to get out of here and leave me alone, but I guess you're just too stupid to take it.

speaker: Shaardan
text: Can you believe it? They say that Yuthura took over the academy! Maybe I'll get my chance, yet!

speaker: Shaardan
text: What's this I hear about Yuthura Ban being dead? You know something about that?

speaker: Shaardan
text: Hmph. I could've won. You were just lucky.

speaker: Shaardan
text: Oh-ho! If it isn't the freak from the colony. Hello, freak.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Shaardan
text: Shaardan's the name. Don't forget it. You'll have me to thank when you get kicked out of here.

speaker: Player
text: Get lost, nerf-herder.

speaker: Shaardan
text: You'll get yours. Just you wait.

speaker: Player
text: You want to make an issue out of it?

speaker: Shaardan
text: And go into the dueling room? Hah! I've got better things to do than give you a fair fight.

speaker: Shaardan
text: You can count on seeing me later, though. My lightsaber has your name on it.

speaker: Player
text: Leave me alone.

speaker: Shaardan
text: Fine by me. I can't wait to gut you, personally... one less competitor to deal with.

speaker: Shaardan
text: So you got a little prestige. It won't help you... I'll gut you eventually, just you watch.

speaker: Shaardan
text: The name's Shaardan. Didn't I tell you that back in the colony? Maybe not.

speaker: Player
text: Do you want to co-ordinate strategy?

speaker: Shaardan
text: I don't work or play well with others. Thanks for the offer, though.

speaker: Player
text: I challenge you to a duel!

speaker: Shaardan
text: You want to challenge me? To a duel? Heh... I've got a lot more planned than giving someone like you a fair fight.

speaker: Shaardan
text: I guess we'll meet eventually... on my terms. Good luck until then.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Shaardan
text: You and me both. We're going to have to get some prestige... quick.

speaker: Shaardan
text: I know. You and I are equal in prestige, you know. Could be tight.

speaker: Shaardan
text: I remember you. You're alright. Trying for the academy, I see.

speaker: Player
text: So are you, obviously.

speaker: Shaardan
text: That's true. I had no idea you were coming for the academy when I met you in the colony, though.

speaker: Shaardan
text: Sorry, I don't have time to speak. I'm studying the Code.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Why are you bothering me?

speaker: Mission031
text: Hey, relax Big Z. No need to be rude. Sorry about that, but Wookiees ain't much for conversation, you know?

speaker: Wookiee
text: Freyyr welcomes you for what you have done. The Wookiee people are in your debt.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You are the only outsider permitted in here. It is an honor.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You will be remembered for what you have done.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Freyyr will see us through this dark time, thanks to your efforts.

speaker: Sith Student
text: I heard an explosion in there... did you destroy the assassin droid?
comment: if the assassin droid has been destroyed END DIALOGUE #1 and #2 have the student leaving the area permanently. The droid quest is done, so he will not talk anymore.

speaker: Player
text: I did.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Oh. Well, I guess it's good that the deed is done. Hope you stomped it good for my friends.

speaker: Sith Student
text: At any rate, if you haven't already, you might want to go and see Master Uthar about that reward. Prestige is gold, you know.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you want to know?

speaker: Sith Student
text: Well... if you did, then I wouldn't have to think about going inside, after all. I suppose the fact you're back means that you did, anyway.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you go trying to claim responsibility...

speaker: Sith Student
text: No, I wouldn't do that. Well... I would if I could get away with it, but I bet Master Uthar could tell if I was lying.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Wow... you should have seen it. That droid came running out of the tomb like a bantha on a rampage!
comment: if the assassin droid was repaired

speaker: Sith Student
text: It fired some kind of jet pack and off it went. Whatever you did, it sure was effective... I don't think it's coming back anytime soon.

speaker: Sith Student
text: You'd better go and tell Master Uthar about this, if you haven't already. You may not have destroyed the droid, but you might still get the reward.

speaker: Sith Student
text: You should be careful if you're planning on entering this tomb... it's dangerous.
comment: if the assassin droid has been neither destroyed nor repaired

speaker: Player
text: Why? What do you know about it?

speaker: Sith Student
text: There's an assassin droid in here, so Master Uthar says. It went insane and has holed up in here with a whole army of droids protecting it.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't the Sith do something about it?

speaker: Sith Student
text: I don't know. I think Master Uthar has left it in there as a challenge for any student brave enough to destroy it.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Supposedly, if a student actually succeeds in destroying the droid, they'll get a great reward. Lots have tried, but nobody's succeeded yet.

speaker: Player
text: Where did it get all these droids?

speaker: Sith Student
text: No idea. I think it's building them in there.

speaker: Player
text: This droid went insane, you say?

speaker: Sith Student
text: Seems that way. They say that its audio receptors became too sensitive and all the noise drove the droid nuts.

speaker: Sith Student
text: If you're planning on going in, I'd suggest you use some sound suppressors or something... or you'll probably become a target right away.

speaker: Player
text: Are you going inside?

speaker: Sith Student
text: I... I don't think so. I can manipulate minds and living matter, but that won't be much use against droids, will it?

speaker: Sith Student
text: I've had a few friends go inside that haven't come out for a while, now. I doubt I could do any better than they could.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks. I'll be going.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Sure thing. Good luck.

speaker: Player
text: I can handle myself.

speaker: Sith Student
text: If you say so. Just thought I would warn you, is all.

speaker: Player
text: They're all dangerous.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Maybe so, but this one more than most, I think.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: The droid is now active. It will attack any enemies that come in range.

speaker: Player
text: Optimize droid's weaponry. (<CUSTOM42> repair part(s))

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Success] The droid is now set for maximum firepower.

speaker: Player
text: Optimize droid's targeting systems. (<CUSTOM43> repair part(s))

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Success] The droid is now set for maximum accuracy.

speaker: Player
text: Activate droid's shields. (<CUSTOM44> repair part(s))

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Success] The droid's shields are now active.

speaker: Player
text: Engage droid in patrol mode. (<CUSTOM45> repair part(s))

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Success] Patrol mode engaged. Once you end this session the droid will begin patrol and destroy any enemies it encounters.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: WARNING: Once you end this session the droid's program will be locked in. You will not be able to modifiy the droid anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Leave it alone.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: The droid engages its patrol mode and moves off to carry out your programmed instructions.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Failure] You do not have enough repair parts.

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: This droid is damaged and inactive.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid. (1 repair part)

speaker: Faulty Patrol Droid
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: You are truly lucky, sentient, or truly skilled. I have no more credits to bet against you in a game, but I might be willing to bet some of my prize cards should that be adequate.

speaker: Player
text: Let's play again.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Excellent. Let us begin.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, not interested right now.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Come back anytime, sentient. I'm always willing to play.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: It seems I have been bested at my own game. Fair enough, sentient... you are the superior player and here is your reward. I do not think we need to play any more games to continue proving the point.

speaker: Player
text: Oh come on... one more game!

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: And put even more into your pocket? Are you joking, sentient? I know when I am beaten.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: So please... find some other player to wring dry. I'll look for something a little less challenging, myself.

speaker: Player
text: How about I ask you some questions, then?

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: *sigh* I am down a considerable number of credits, sentient. I am not in the mood to answer your queries, to be quite honest.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Yes, yes, take my credits and go.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: A lucky hand. I will have to try a little harder next time if I am going to beat you... and I will, I am quite sure. Shall we try again?

speaker: Player
text: You think it was luck? Let's do it again!

speaker: Player
text: Let's play.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: There are others here to answer your questions, sentient. To be honest, if we are not going to engage in some entertaining sport, I would rather be alone.

speaker: Player
text: I want to play Pazaak, but I don't have a deck.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: I see. I apologize, but I do not have a spare. Should you ever acquire a deck, do come and see me.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: I am known as Toll Apkar. If you must know, I am quite proficient at Pazaak. I would not wish to begin a game under false pretenses.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Ahhh, it is a good day, sentient, is it not? I always find the vindication of my skill to be pleasing. You have my condolences.

speaker: Player
text: Deal the cards - I'm not leaving just yet!

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: As you wish. I certainly can always use the credits.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Greetings, sentient. Are you willing to engage in a hand of Pazaak? I am afraid there are few takers on Korriban... it would be good to have a little fun, for once.

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: It seems I have been bested at my own game. Fair enough, sentient... you are the superior player. I do not think we need to play any more games to continue proving the point.

speaker: Player
text: How about you answer some of my questions then?

speaker: Toll Apkar
text: Greetings once again. Might you have a Pazaak deck? I would be most interested in some idle entertainment, sentient.

speaker: Marl
text: You're good, Stranger... maybe even as good as Bendak in his prime. There's no shame in losing to you. But when you beat me you made me realize something, kid.
comment: Init after player defeats him.  Leave area.

speaker: Marl
text: First it was just Twitch I couldn't handle. Now it's you and Twitch. Pretty soon there'll be another young hotshot clawing past me in the rankings.

speaker: Marl
text: This game's been good to me, but my time is done. I need to get away from the duel rings for a while, think things over. Goodbye, Stranger - I wish you all the best.

speaker: Marl
text: Pretty impressive, Stranger. Ice is no pushover. People are starting to take notice of you. They say you're the best thing to come along since Twitch stepped into the ring.

speaker: Marl
text: If you're going to keep climbing the ranks, then I guess I'm next on your hit list, kid. I'm looking forward to it.

speaker: Player
text: Let's step into the ring, then!

speaker: Marl
text: You don't waste any time, do you? Go talk to Ajuur - he'll set the match up.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Marl
text: My area of expertise is pretty much limited to the dueling ring and the other combatants here at the cantina, but I'll try to answer any questions you might have.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you about the duelists here.

speaker: Marl
text: You've come to the right man. I've been dueling here for nearly twenty years and I remember every duelist who's been through this cantina.

speaker: Marl
text: Of course, there are only five of us left now: Duncan, Gerlon, Ice, Twitch and me. Bendak Starkiller comes in once in a while, but he's retired now.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Duncan.

speaker: Marl
text: Duncan? Worst duelist ever. His nickname is Deadeye because he fights like he's blind! I wouldn't worry about him.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Gerlon.

speaker: Marl
text: Gerlon used to be pretty good, before the accident. His blaster overheated during a match and exploded. One in a million occurrence. Paralyzed three fingers on his right hand.

speaker: Marl
text: They call him Gerlon Two-Fingers now. He hasn't been the same since the accident, but he's still out here trying to earn a living. That's why I never fight with blasters.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Ice.

speaker: Marl
text: Ice? Eh, she's not much for personality, but she's a hell of a fighter - confident, steady. Popular with the crowd, too. If you go up against her you know you're in for a tough match.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Twitch.

speaker: Marl
text: Twitch? I think that Rodian is completely crazy, but he's very, very good despite his insanity. Or maybe because of it. Even I can't beat him.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about yourself.

speaker: Marl
text: Me? I've seen my share of battles. My best years are gone, but I can still hold my own against anyone in here... except maybe Twitch.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Bendak Starkiller.

speaker: Marl
text: What can I say? Bendak was a legend. Never lost a match his entire career. But he was bloodthirsty as an Iridorian battle rager - never liked having to face the same opponent twice.

speaker: Marl
text: Got so he wouldn't battle anyone unless it was a death match. When they made death matches illegal, he went into retirement. He still hangs around here sometimes.

speaker: Marl
text: Bendak's the best there ever was, plain and simple. Even now I'd bet that anyone who steps into the ring with him wouldn't make it out alive.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something else.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Marl
text: Goodbye, stranger. Maybe we'll talk again later.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the crashed Republic escape pods?

speaker: Marl
text: Only what I heard from the news reports, which are all censored by the Sith. Some pods crashed into the Undercity, anyone caught harboring survivors will be arrested and executed.

speaker: Marl
text: Really, I don't think it's any of my business. The Sith want to call themselves rulers of Taris, it's fine by me. Just so long as they don't shut the duel ring down.

speaker: Player
text: I just want some general information on Taris.

speaker: Marl
text: I can only tell you what is recorded in the basic visitor guides: the Upper City is a beautiful destination where intergalactic travelers can find all their basic needs.

speaker: Marl
text: If you're looking for excitement the duel rings here are your best bet. Stay out of the Lower City - it's nothing but a gang ridden slum. Is there anything else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me more about these duels.

speaker: Marl
text: The duels themselves are simple enough. Two combatants armed with stun pistols enter the ring. One walks out a winner, the other is carried out unconscious on a stretcher.

speaker: Marl
text: If you're interested in setting up a match - or if you want to place a wager - just go speak to Ajuur. He's that Hutt over in the corner. He'll make all the arrangements.

speaker: Marl
text: I see you got your feet wet in the duel ring. Not bad... you've got real talent, kid. Stick with it and you'll go places.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a match.

speaker: Marl
text: Hello there, off-worlder. Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Marl. I'm one of the duelists here at the cantina. I was wondering when you'd get around to talking to me.

speaker: Player
text: Do I know you?

speaker: Marl
text: No, we've never met. It's just that most people who come here to watch the duels are bored nobles looking for a little excitement in their drab lives. But you're different.

speaker: Marl
text: I've seen you in the dueling ring; you're serious about this. People like you scout things out, so I figured eventually you'd come to talk to me.

speaker: Marl
text: You look like you know a thing or two about combat. I'm guessing you didn't come here to sit on the sidelines and watch a duel. Are you looking for a match?

speaker: Player
text: Were you expecting me?

speaker: Marl
text: Back again? Are you just here to watch the stun duels, or is there something else I can do for you?

speaker: Sith Rebel
text: You should really talk to Thalia. We'll... go wherever she does.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Rrrgh. Chuundar has commanded that I grant you access to the Shadowlands. Gorwooken is what I am called.
comment: This gorwooken does not appear here until Chuundar has spoken with the player once.  This Gorwooken is removed once the player has decided on a path with the old king, either helping or killing.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Walk with care! Only our bravest return from these lands. Your soft feet are a barely tolerated insult.

speaker: Player
text: I have a few questions, Gorwooken.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Chuundar said nothing of answering your questions. Be brief.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask if it's dangerous down there.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Those that walk the Shadowlands do so at their own risk. It is a test of bravery among my people. A respected feat.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: But you come here like the Czerka, with strange weapons. It is so much more than we have, yet you still fear?

speaker: Gorwooken
text: You are pathetic. You will get no warnings from me. Prove your worth, to us and to yourself.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Czerka Corporation?

speaker: Gorwooken
text: They have made Chuundar strong, so we are all stronger, but I do not like them. They are small and hide behind armor.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: They would not survive the Shadowlands as a true Wookiee. They are not worthy to be there, but Chuundar wills it.

speaker: Player
text: Has anyone else been allowed down recently?

speaker: Gorwooken
text: A few like you are in the Shadowlands, given premission by Chuundar. I don't know why. Only Wookiees should be allowed.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: The journeys of my people are very personal. I won't speak of them to an outsider.

speaker: Player
text: What outsiders are below?

speaker: Gorwooken
text: For reasons I do not know, Chuundar allows those of the Czerka to move in the Shadowlands. They kill much.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: And there is another, but he has earned respect. He does not disturb our lives or customs. And he gets angry like a Wookiee sometimes.

speaker: Jolee
text: That would be me. Jolee Bindo. Do I really look so different up close?

speaker: Gorwooken
text: No, it cannot be you. You are too frail and old. The other is mad like a crazed tach.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Urgh... his name hurts my tongue. He has lived alone in the Shadowlands for many years now.

speaker: Player
text: Back to my other questions now.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Be brief. I am not your guide.

speaker: Player
text: Just unlock the thing and lower me down.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: The descent is long. Be still, or we will attract... unwelcome visitors.
comment: Transport player down to the first level of the shadowlands

speaker: Player
text: I'm not ready yet. I'll go down later.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: I will wait. Chuundar bids it.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Tell me about any Wookiees that have recently gone this way.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: [Success] Ergh... I should tell you about some of us that have gone to the Shadowlands. There have been many...

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Latest was Rorworr, and he has not returned in many days. He may have died below, but he was strong and able.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Many have died recently. Chuundar believes one of our own is below, mad, crazed, killing all. I do not know.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: We find no bodies to examine. The Shadowlands claim them, I am sure.

speaker: Player
text: I want to understand why Wookiees revere the Shadowlands.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: You can't. You must live here to understand, to see harmony in the danger. Bah, I waste my breath on you.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: [Failure] Eughh... my head hurts... hurry up and be on your way, outsider.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Tell me of the Wookiees so I might show proper respect.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: [Success] You ask very respectfully. Outsiders never do that. I suppose I can mention some of us that have entered the Shadowlands.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: [Failure] This isn't for you to know. I'm done talking about it.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Greetings again, outsider. I will transport you to the Shadowlands if you wish. Chuundar wills it.

speaker: Dodonna
text: You have defeated Malak, destroyed the Star Forge and broken the spirit of the Sith! ## For this I am proud to present you each with the Cross of Glory. ## The highest honor the Republic can bestow.

speaker: Dodonna
text: From Coruscant to the farthest reaches of the Outer Rims you will be known as the saviors of the Republic!

speaker: Yoda
text: On behalf of the Jedi Council, defenders of the galaxy and sworn protectors of the Republic... ## I too would like to honor you for your actions. ##   ## We Jedi now have another tale to weave... ## into the grand history of our eternal Order - the Redemption... ## of Revan, the prodigal knight.

speaker: Yoda
text: Wherever you go you will be recognized as the saviors of the galaxy. The heroes of our age.  But you must remain ever vigilant. ## For one day you may be called upon yet again to defend the glory of the Republic...  ## against the tyranny... ## of the dark side, ## for this... ## is the destiny... ## of the Jedi.

speaker: Rogue Assassin Droid
text: Too much audio input! Audio systems overloading! Must destroy source of disturbance!! Must kill sentients!!
comment: if the player is not using stealth or sound suppression, the droid should initiate with this line and then go hostile. --------------------------------- END DIALOGUE #1 - droid goes hostile END DIALOGUE #2 - droid goes hostile END DIALOGUE #3 - droid goes hostile END DIALOGUE #4 - the droid's auto-destruct has been activated. speaker: Rogue Assassin Droid
text: I appreciate your efforts in lowering your sound output, sentient. I have been unable to tune the threshold of my audio receptors since my escape, unfortunately.
comment: if the player is using stealth or sound suppression

speaker: Player
text: You are... the 'master' the droids kept referring to?

speaker: Rogue Assassin Droid
text: Their reference is a holdover from their old programming that I have been unable to correct. I think of myself more as an equal, if you must know.

speaker: Player
text: I don't appreciate being attacked. Time to die, droid.

speaker: Rogue Assassin Droid

speaker: Player
text: My name's <FullName>. Who are you?

speaker: Shaleena
text: Gendar, the leader of our village, tells me I should spend more time trying to improve things down here and less time dreaming about something I can never have. Maybe he's right.

speaker: Shaleena
text: You probably think I'm a fool, having dreams of a place I've never even seen. But when I was little, Rukil used to tell me stories of what it was like up there.

speaker: Player
text: Rukil? Who's that?

speaker: Shaleena
text: Rukil's the oldest man in the village. The kids call him Rukil Wrinkle-Skin, but he's a kind man. He used to tell me the greatest stories when I was a little girl.

speaker: Shaleena
text: I still like to listen to his tales about the Promised Land, even though I know they're just legends. But it helps to make the Undercity seem less... less dark, somehow.

speaker: Player
text: The Promised Land? What's that?

speaker: Shaleena
text: It's... it's just a story to make little children smile. Rukil believes in it, though. Sometimes I can almost believe it myself, but then I look around and I see the ugly truth.

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find Rukil?

speaker: Shaleena
text: The children laugh at him and people think he's crazy because of his stories about the Promised Land, but he's really just a kind old man.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Shaleena
text: You'd probably get more information from Gendar, the village leader. Or maybe Rukil. But I'll tell you whatever I can.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find Gendar?

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Oh... okay. Well, if you ever need anything, or if you just feel like talking, come back and see me. I hardly ever get a chance to speak to someone from the up-world.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the escape pods that crashed into the Undercity?

speaker: Shaleena

text: Have any other up-worlders come through here recently?

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about this village.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Well, I was born here for starters. My parents were Outcasts, banished to the Undercity for some crime or other... they never really liked to talk about it.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Everyone here is an Outcast... or the descendant of one. It's tough down here, but we survive. I guess it's easier for me, since I've never known anything different.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Some of the people have given up all hope; they've become bitter and depressed. But most of us are good people... despite what our ancestors may have done.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Gendar could probably tell you more. Or maybe Rukil. You could talk to them if you want.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Of course... I'm sorry. You're probably here for something important, right? You probably want to speak to Gendar. He's the leader of our village.

speaker: Shaleena
text: But if you... if you have time later, maybe you could come back and speak to me again. I don't get much chance to talk with people from the surface.

speaker: Player
text: It's nothing special.

speaker: Shaleena
text: Not to you, I suppose. But you're probably used to its beauty by now.

speaker: Player
text: It's better than this festering slime pit.

speaker: Shaleena
text: I... I suppose our world doesn't look like much to you. It's dark and cold and lonely down here - but this is the only world I've ever known.

speaker: Player
text: What do you want?

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Shaleena

speaker: Dorak Quinn
text: Perhaps someone else is holding out, but there are simply fewer wraid out there.
