text: Woorwill gets the rest. He is the closest to family that Rorworr had left. The others were lost to slavers.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Here, take it. I thank you for your help. Now please, just go.
comment: Give a bit of credits but less than if Jaarak was still alive.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything going on?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: A few details to work out following Jaarak's death, but nothing that need concern you.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye then.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Goodbye, outsider. Goodbye.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Well, I must say that you are the first outsider that I have been glad to know. You have surprised me.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Perhaps some of you are capable of honor after all. You are deserving of your reward.

speaker: Player
text: My reward? What reward?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Did I not explain? As the person that discovered the crime, you were also affected by it.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: You would've been given a portion of Jaarak's possessions, but he was innocent. Rorworr, however, was not.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Rorworr was wealthy. His family was taken by slavers, leaving him everything. You get one third of this.
comment: give player reward. More than if Jaarak had died

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Woorwill receives the rest, if he wishes. He is still upset, but he is young. He will recover.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you if anything is happening now?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Nothing that you can help with. Rorworr's crime is causing a bit of a stir, but it will pass in time.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Some of us will be disappointed in him, but we have other enemies to worry about.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye to you.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Goodbye. Bacca guide you.

speaker: Jolee
text: There was pain no matter how this ended. Perhaps this is for the best.

speaker: Mission
text: Big Z says honor was everything to his people. I... guess he's right.

speaker: Bastila
text: This isn't justice, it doesn't seem right! But... what else could we do?

speaker: Cand
text: At least he's going to die like a warrior.

speaker: Player
text: No, I won't let this happen.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Explain yourself, outsider. If you have information that will affect this trial, I must know it.

speaker: Jaarak
text: Don't listen to these outsider lies... please. Woorwill, don't listen.

speaker: Player
text: Rorworr dealt with slavers. The datapad I found on his corpse proves it.

speaker: Woorwill
text: But... no. No! That's not... that can't be. Jaarak? It can't be...

speaker: Jaarak
text: I'm sorry, Woorwill. I didn't want you to know. So much is against us... you need someone to look up to.

speaker: Jaarak
text: I couldn't let him betray you... betray everyone. Outsiders are enough of a threat by themselves; we don't need traitors of our own.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: See how this Wookiee truly understands honor? Do you see how important we consider these things, <FirstName>?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Well... as Holder of the Laws, I declare Jaarak innocent. I... will see to your release.
comment: Fade to black. Jaarak back at his house. Woorwil back in his house.

speaker: Jolee
text: A painful end, but perhaps it is the right thing to do. We shall see.

speaker: Mission
text: How awful. Big Z always said how important honor was to his people. It's everything.

speaker: Bastila
text: How sad. It feels like the right thing to do, but... to destroy a hero...

speaker: Player
text: Kill him then. Jaarak must *pay* for his crime.

speaker: Player
text: Kill him. I found nothing to justify the murder.

speaker: Woorwill
text: Nothing? There was no reason? You just killed him? Why! There has to be a reason why!

speaker: Jaarak
text: I'm sorry, Woorwill... I can't give a reason. It was between me and Rorworr, and neither of us will talk.

speaker: Player
text: No, Jaarak should live. Rorwill dealt with the slavers.

speaker: Player
text: Wait. Go back to the part where I get paid if he's guilty.

speaker: Cand
text: Yeah, let's keep the focus on what's important. If there's profit to be made here, we don't want to miss out.

speaker: Bastila
text: You mustn't let greed rule your decision here. Justice must be served.

speaker: Juhani
text: Greed will lead you down the dark side if you are not careful. You must not seek material gain at the expense of the ideals the Jedi hold dear.

speaker: Player
text: Is there no alternative to death as punishment?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: If there were circumstances that led to the attack, perhaps we could consider another punishment. It all depends on what was behind it.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: My life debt won't let me speak for you, <FirstName>, but you know Jaraak had justification. Will you tell them?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: This is a failure of honor. It is very serious. Were there any mitigating factors we need to be aware of?

speaker: Jolee
text: I urge you caution. This may seem like the right path to follow... but you do not know these people as I do.

speaker: Carth
text: Good thinking. Jaarak doesn't strike me as the type to murder for no reason.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me something. What's the penalty for murder?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: That would depend on the circumstances. We rarely have such crimes here. Wookiee honor does not allow it.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: When we have had a murder, the punishment was usually death. There is rarely any justification that would dictate otherwise.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: I'm sorry. Like most of the village, I've been preoccupied by these troubled times. I don't really want to speak with you.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Well, not unless you can tell me where young Rorworr is. Do you keep track of slaves taken?

speaker: Player
text: I am no slaver.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: I have no way of knowing one way or another. You'll excuse me if I don't take you at your word.

speaker: Player
text: When did Rorworr go missing?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: It could be ten days or more. He was planning a hunt, and nobody seems to know when he was leaving.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: He is now overdue. I don't know where to start. It is strange...

speaker: Player
text: Why do you think it is strange?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: I don't believe he was taken by slavers. Their slave transports haven't been seen around here.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: If it wasn't slavers, perhaps he fell in the Shadowlands... but he knew them well.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: I would search for him, but I don't know where to start. My days of hunting the lower forest are behind me.

speaker: Player
text: I could look for him.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: You could. I've never had an offer of help from an outsider. I'll reserve my judgment for when I see results.

speaker: Player
text: Would there be a reward for finding him?

speaker: Worrroznor
text: That would need to be determined. Wookiee justice rewards honor and honesty. You outsiders are a little lacking...

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Farewell then. Bacca keep you well.

speaker: Worrroznor
text: Greetings again, outsider. Please, if you have business here, make it brief.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Since you have been designated Arbiter in the Sunry case, I shall answer questions that you might have.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of Sunry?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Sunry is a former Republic officer who is highly regarded by your people. He is admired by your people here on Manaan, and even seems to maintain some sort of relations with them still.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: If he is as capable as some of the Republic citizens still believe him to be, he is certainly capable of actions that would result in this murder.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Is there anything else you wish to ask in relation to this case?

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything suspicious about this case?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Well I have often wondered, if Sunry were so innocent, why was he seen fleeing the scene of the crime?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Why would he have been running if he had not committed the crime himself, or was at least aware of what had occurred?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: This case seems fairly simple and obvious to me. You Republic types stick together, however, and I assume you will go to lengths to defend him.

speaker: Carth
text: The Republic believes in justice, as do you. We just want Sunry to be fairly treated, that's all.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: What else do you want to ask?

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Republic and the Sith Empire?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Both empires are at fault for this current conflict. The Republic in the past for laying the foundations upon which the Sith Empire grew. And the Sith now, obviously, for starting the war.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: But no matter the wrongs that had been done in the past, the Sith now have no cause for renewing hostilities. It almost seems as if they just want to conquer everything!

speaker: Bastila
text: 'Almost seems'? They do wish to conquer everything, and will not stop at Manaan. Why the Selkath believe themselves invulnerable I have no idea.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: I believe the Republic has every right to defend itself and drive the Sith back where they came from.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Unfortunately for them... and perhaps for us... they do not seem to be doing too good a job of it.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Was there anything else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: I have no more questions for now.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Return if you have pertinent details about the case to discuss.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Only those on legitimate business should consult the judges personally.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Since your case is done, you should refrain from abusing your past familiarity.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: For additional inquiries, Judge Shelkar is available for consultation.

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [Though you can't seem to understand him, the Sand People chieftain's tone is obvious. He clearly despises all outsiders.]
comment: This is the Chieftain of the Sand People. The player cannot understand him Translation by HK-47 works as follows: 1. Player asks HK-47 to say something 2. HK-47 says an [Unitelligible] line to Chieftain. 3. HK-47 translates the answer back to the player like at the UN, with the Sand Person speaking in the background and HK-47 translating as he says it.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: I can translate with some guarantee of accuracy that he is demanding to know why he should let us survive this encounter, master.
comment: HK-47 speaks with the Sand People chieftain talking behind him, as though HK-47 is translating as the Sand People Chieftain talks.

speaker: Player
text: Tell him we want a peaceful solution.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: [Unintelligible]
comment: This line requires that HK-47 say something short in Sand People dialect

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: He claims he has no reason to believe you, master. Your kind have tainted this land with machines and uncaring ignorant feet.
comment: HK-47 speaks with the Sand People chieftain talking behind him, as though HK-47 is translating as the Sand People Chieftain talks.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: He requires proof of good faith. We must make a contribution to his people that shows we are not a threat. Shall I blast him now, master?
comment: HK-47 speaks with the Sand People chieftain talking behind him, as though HK-47 is translating as the Sand People Chieftain talks.

speaker: Player
text: Offer him 100 credits to stop the attacks.

speaker: Player
text: Ask what it is that he wants.

speaker: Player
text: Tell him that I have questions first.

speaker: Player
text: See if he's holding the Jawas Iziz was looking for.

speaker: Player
text: This has gone far enough. Attack him.

speaker: HK47
text: Agreement: That is probably the most efficient course of action. This will be enjoyable.

speaker: Player
text: Tell him to surrender or face death.

speaker: HK47
text: Protocol: While I enjoy the prospect, master, are you certain that is wise? He will not react favorably.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, ask if he's open to a peaceful solution.

speaker: Player
text: You have my orders. Do as I say!

speaker: Player
text: Why are you able to speak with the Sand People when I can't?

speaker: HK47
text: Extrapolation: I understand that you are Force Sensitive, master, but I lack sufficient knowledge to make an accurate assumption.

speaker: HK47
text: Hypothesis: Perhaps your ability does not take the place of actual language study when the subject is out of the ordinary.

speaker: HK47
text: Or perhaps the Sand People confuse your ability because they actively refuse to communicate with most outsiders. I have no data on this, sadly.

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [His words are lost on you. Without HK-47 translating you have no hope of settling this situation peacefully. Sand People close around you.]

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [The Sand People Chieftain seems grateful to you, or at least less inclined to smash your head open like a pocky grub seed.]

speaker: HK47
text: Query: What do you wish to ask of him, master?

speaker: Player
text: Ask about the Star Map.
comment: player has not already acquired the Star Map

speaker: Player
text: Ask about captives.
comment: (player has talked to the captive jawas. Player has not yet asked the chieftain to release them) OR (player has not talked to the captive jawas, but HAS talked to Iziz about them. Player has not yet asked the chieftain to release them (global)) OR (player has talked to the captive Griff) OR (player has not talked to the captive Griff, but HAS talked to the person that said he was captured by Sand People.)

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: We must be more specific, master. They capture many organics.

speaker: Player
text: Ask about setting the captive Jawas free.
comment: player has talked to the captive jawas. Player has not yet asked the chieftain to release them

speaker: Player
text: Ask if he knows about the Jawas Iziz told us about.
comment: player has not talked to the captive jawas, but HAS talked to Iziz about them. Player has not yet asked the chieftain to release them (global)

speaker: Player
text: Ask about getting Griff set free.
comment: player has talked to the captive Griff

speaker: Player
text: Ask if he knows about Mission's brother Griff.
comment: player has not talked to the captive Griff, but HAS talked to the person that said he was captured by Sand People.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my other questions.

speaker: HK47
text: Protocol: We should not keep him long. It is an insult to take too much of his time. Unless the plan is to blast him when you are done, of course.

speaker: Player
text: I want information on Sand People culture.

speaker: HK47
text: Protocol: This will be a very sensitive topic, master. You will want to be careful with your questions or risk offending him. Not that that is much of a worry.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me the history of your clan.

speaker: Player
text: Why are they so hostile to outsiders?

speaker: Player
text: Tell him farewell for now.

speaker: Player
text: I've no further use for him. Kill him.

speaker: HK47
text: Agreement: My thoughts exactly, master. One dead organic meatbag, coming up.

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [You can't understand him without HK-47 present, and you can tell that speaking to him in outsider tongue would be a grave insult.]

speaker: Player
text: I have questions for you, Chieftain.

speaker: Player
text: [Leave quietly]

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [The Sand People Chieftain ignores you.]

speaker: Sand People Chieftain
text: [If you can read anything of the Sand People chieftain's emotions, it seems that he is surprised that you have returned.]

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: He did not expect us to return, master. He wonders if we have brought the moisture vaporators.
comment: HK-47 speaks with the Sand People chieftain talking behind him, as though HK-47 is translating as the Sand People Chieftain talks.

speaker: Player
text: Tell him that we have his vaporators.

speaker: Player
text: Tell him the deal is off unless the attacks stop.

speaker: Mandalorian Commander
text: You have interrupted our hunt, interloper. The inhabitants of this world could do little against us, but you appear to be a threat.
comment: This is a mandalorian that launches dialogue after the player destroys one of their speeder bikes (therefore rendering him visible).

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Your butchery will stop here!!

speaker: Mandalorian Commander
text: Has something happened to put fire in your people? Are you no longer slaves? It doesn't matter. You will die like the others!

speaker: Mandalorian Commander
text: You are nothing! Your people are sheep! I fear no slave! Especially willing ones!

speaker: Cand
text: More than a threat enough for you!

speaker: Mandalorian Commander
text: Another Mandalore, is it? Will you draw arms against those you would serve? We'll see who lives this day!

speaker: Mandalorian Commander
text: Our training here will continue... without your interference.
comment: He attacks with four other invisible Mandalorians. Destroying speeder bikes renders them visible.

speaker: Bith Musician
text: [This musician is too busy playing to pay any attention to you.]

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: What are you doing back here? You finally find the guts to meet me in a death match?
comment: Player rejected death match offer Dialog Mission Statement: Player can speak to Bendak. Bendak will brag about his reputation. If Bendka Bounty plot is active player can try to take Bendak in. All this will be in vain if the player has not beaten Twitch (current champion) in the dueling ring. Exit points:  1. Player leaves bendak, no scripting involved. 2. Player has beaten Twitch and accepts Bendak's challenge. Bendak will exit through the door to the duel ring and destroy himself and set his duel status to "pending". After two days the status of "pending" will change and the player will be able to fight Bendak in the duel ring by speaking to the duel organizer.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to collect the bounty on your head, Bendak!

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: So you're the one doing Zax's dirty work. Well I've got some bad news for you, little bounty hunter. There's no way you're bringing me in.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: This cantina is wired with a top level security grid. You pull a weapon on me and the auto-fire turrets will fry you before you can even pull the trigger.

speaker: Player
text: So you'll just hide in here like a coward?

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Why would I ever want to leave here? I've got food and drinks, a place to stay - and everybody treats me with the respect I've earned for my dueling career.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: But if you're set on collecting that bounty I'll make you a deal. I kind of miss the fight game; my hand is itching for the feel of a blaster in my grip.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: I've seen you in the duel ring. You're just good enough to spark my interest, so I'll agree to face you in a death match. You win, you get to collect that bounty for killing me.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it - I'm not interested in a death match.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Hmmm... never figured you for a coward. You ever get the guts to fight me come on back and we can set the match up. Otherwise we've got nothing to talk about.

speaker: Player
text: You're on, Bendak! Name the time and place!

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Finally - fresh meat! Ajuur will set it all up; go talk to him. It will take some time to arrange, so no point sticking around here until then. I'll be back when it's time for you to die!

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: If you can prove yourself in the ring by beating all these other so-called duelists, I'll agree to face you in a death match. You win, you get to collect that bounty for killing me.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back as soon as I beat all these other duelists.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Good luck with that, kid... you're going to need it. HA-HA-HA!

speaker: Carth
text: You sure you want to get involved in this? Seems a bit pointless to me. Up to you.

speaker: Player
text: You have to leave sometime, Bendak!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Off with you then. I'm done with this conversation anyway.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Since I'm not going to answer them, you'd just be wasting your breath. So move along before people see us talking and think I'm signing autoprints today. I don't want to be mobbed.

speaker: Player
text: Autoprints? What are you talking about?

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: People are always bugging me for my autoprint. Comes with the territory. You survive over 100 death matches and people tend to see you as something of a legend.

speaker: Player
text: You don't look so tough. Maybe you'll take me on.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: I'm retired now. Once death matches became illegal I just got bored with the game. I've got no interest in using stun blasters! There was nobody left to challenge me, anyway.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: But I saw you in the ring against Twitch. You've got enough talent to make me consider coming out of retirement for one last death match - unless you're afraid to face me.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: I've been watching these new kids in the ring, but I haven't found anyone worth my notice so far. Still, if someone could beat all these other pretenders I might give them a shot.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: I've seen you in the dueling ring, but you haven't impressed me. Now, if you could beat all these other pretenders... that might get my attention.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: What, you don't recognize me? I'm Bendak Starkiller, the most famous blaster-slinger on Taris. Over 100 duels without a loss - every one of them a death match!

speaker: Player
text: How come you don't hang around with the other duelists?

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: I've been watching you in the dueling ring. Not bad for an amateur. I'm tempted to come out of retirement and show you what it's like to do battle against a real champion.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: But I only fight in death matches, and not too many people are willing to step into the ring knowing they won't ever come out. How 'bout you, Stranger? You think you got what it takes?

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Back again? You're starting to bore me. I don't come here to talk - I come to watch the duels and see if there's anyone worthy of stepping into the ring with me.
comment: Second meeting (Bendak bragged) player not beaten Twitch

speaker: Player
text: I'll step into the ring with you Bendak!

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Sorry, I don't waste my time with no-names. You have to prove yourself before you get a shot at me. I'm the real deal, kid - 100 death matches without a loss!

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: But if you can knock off all these other pretenders in the duel ring, I might consider coming out of retirement to face you in one last death match.

speaker: Bendak Starkiller
text: Leave me alone... I'm not giving out any autoprints to my fans today.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Kolto production seems to have dropped off a LOT, recently. The Selkath have been eyeing us funny, too...

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: The Sith Embassy has gone silent... and they aren't explaining. I hope it was something bad!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Good thing Sunry got free! The Sith who tried to pin the murder on him would probably have made him disappear in prison.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: I can't believe those Selkath found Sunry guilty. The Sith must have bribed them or something... So much for neutrality!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Greetings, Master Jedi. I hope you have a pleasant stay here on Manaan. If you have any questions or needs, please direct them to our envoy Roland Wann at our Embassy.

speaker: Twi'lek Dancer
text: You may be a big celebrity and all, but I'm trying to earn a living here!

speaker: Twi'lek Dancer
text: Don't bother me while I'm working... I get paid to dance, not to talk.

speaker: Rakata
text: With the knowledge of the Red Rakata the One will lead us to dominance over all the other tribes of the world!

speaker: Rakata
text: As a reward for slaying our hated enemy you may search our cache for whatever parts you need to repair your ship, Revan.

speaker: Rakata
text: The One is studying the secrets of the Red Rakata. In time he will use them to unlock the knowledge trapped within the Temple of the Ancients!

speaker: Rakata
text: The One has decreed that you may claim any piece you wish from the treasures we have collected from the ships that fell from the sky, Revan.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Speak with Chorrawl if you must speak at all. He knows your jagged language best.
comment: Selected This conversation is shared between the four wookies that are hunting katarn in the area between the village and the basket to the shadowlands. They are standing amidst some dead Katarn A fifth wookie has more involved dialogue

text: I hear you managed to return Juhani to the Order. Congratulations.

speaker: Nemo
text: I regret not being able to tell you more, but some things you must see with your own eyes.

speaker: Nemo
text: Is there something I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: I have been given a task by the Council...

speaker: Nemo
text: Indeed. What is it you would like from me?

speaker: Player
text: I want to know about the Jedi Code.

speaker: Nemo
text: The Code is a way of life, not a strict set of laws. It would be wise for you to reflect on them, rather than rote memorization.

speaker: Nemo
text: But still you must learn.

speaker: Nemo
text: There is no emotion; there is peace. There is no ignorance; there is knowledge. There is no passion; there is serenity. There is no chaos; there is peace. There is no death; there is the Force.

speaker: Nemo
text: Live by these precepts and you will not fail, young apprentice.

speaker: Nemo
text: Is there something else I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: I have a question about Dantooine.

speaker: Nemo
text: Very well, what is it you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find a store?

speaker: Nemo
text: Ah, you can find two stores here at the Enclave. Aratech has opened both a general supply store and a droid facility and I think you will find their products quite good.

speaker: Nemo
text: The supply store is run by a Twi'lek name Crattis Yurkal. A talkative being with a big chip on his shoulder, but generous despite that.

speaker: Nemo
text: The droid repair facility is managed by Karal Kaar. A bit brusque, perhaps, but a good being nonetheless. We have shared many a game of Pazaak in the small hours of the morning.

speaker: Player
text: I've heard people mention Mandalorians.

speaker: Nemo
text: Mandalorian raiders, yes. They have been preying on the settlers in the surrounding farms. Stealing food, money, weapons... Jon was hit really hard recently... He lost his daughter.

speaker: Cand
text: You Republics are too weak. You should protect what you want to keep, otherwise someone stronger will take it.

text: If you want prestige, however, you'll find that hermit, as everyone calls him... you'll find Jorak and either kill him or bring back anything he's been writing. Uthar would like that.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Now begone. I have better things to do than chat with lost hopefuls.

speaker: Player
text: The hermit hiding in the hills?

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Pfah. He is much more than a simple hermit 'hiding in the hills', as you say. We are talking about the former master of the academy.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: If you've already been told about him, there's little more I can tell you. With luck, perhaps he'll kidnap you and you will get a chance to see him for yourself, eh?

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: May the Force serve you well.

speaker: Player
text: Yes. Can you help me?

speaker: Player
text: No. I don't need any help.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Hah! I doubt that. Have it your way, however, off you go.

speaker: Deesra
text: Padawan, a word, if I may. There are many rumors about your most recent meeting with the Jedi Council. There is talk that they are sending you on a mission to help us against Malak and the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: How do you know the Council gave me a mission?

speaker: Deesra
text: I saw you going into the Council chambers. You were in there for some time. I naturally assumed the Council had given you a task to perform.

speaker: Deesra
text: Please understand that I am not asking you to reveal anything that could endanger the Order or the Republic. Whatever task the Council has given you is for your ears, not mine.

speaker: Deesra
text: I only wanted to wish you well, and to warn you to be careful. There are many evils out there, many dangers. The Sith are not the only minions of the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: What could be more dangerous than the Sith?

speaker: Deesra
text: Master Dorak has been training me to succeed him as Chronicler here in the Academy. In my studies I have come across tales of creatures that are born of the dark side, monsters of pure evil.

speaker: Deesra
text: The worst of these abominations is the terentatek, a beast that feeds on the blood of those who are strong in the Force. Over the centuries, many Jedi have fallen to their ravenous hunger.

speaker: Player
text: What makes this creature so dangerous?

speaker: Deesra
text: The terentatek is a predator, and we Jedi are its prey. They are incredibly strong, with a primal cunning. And they have an in-born resistance to the Force.

speaker: Deesra
text: There are some who believe the terentatek is a monster bred by the ancient Sith, and spread throughout the galaxy to destroy the Jedi.

speaker: Deesra
text: Fortunately, the terentatek is quite rare. They only dwell in the most dangerous and darkest of places. In fact, one has not been seen in nearly forty years.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like they're extinct.

speaker: Deesra
text: This is not the first time the terentatek have vanished for long periods of time. Many believe they can lay dormant for years, only to rise and hunt when the power of the dark side waxes full.

speaker: Deesra
text: I fear Malak's rise may have woken these creatures from their dormant state. Once the Sith are beaten, I would not be surprised if the Council organized another Great Hunt to try and exterminate them.

speaker: Player
text: The Great Hunt? What's that?

speaker: Deesra
text: The Great Hunt was organized by the Jedi Council shortly after the war against Exar Kun. Jedi were scattered throughout the galaxy, helping to rebuild from the devastation.

speaker: Deesra
text: Many Jedi vanished during this period, disappearing from a variety of worlds without warning. We did not know they had been slain until their mutilated bodies began to be discovered.

speaker: Deesra
text: The Council investigated, and discovered the terentatek were behind the killings. It was decided the galaxy had to be purged of these insatiable monsters - though the cost proved high.

speaker: Player
text: So the Jedi just killed these creatures?

speaker: Deesra
text: The terentatek are an abomination, they are ruthless engines of death and destruction. The Council had no choice but to destroy them, for the greater good of the galaxy.

speaker: Deesra
text: Many Jedi banded together and journeyed to the planets that were suspected of harboring the terentatek. The Great Hunt did not rest until all the creatures had been slain - or almost all.

speaker: Deesra
text: There were still rumors of terentatek on the planet of Korriban, a dark world some believe to be the birthplace of the Sith. That is where Exar Kun was corrupted during the first Sith War.

speaker: Deesra
text: They never went to Korriban. The Council, fearing more Jedi might fall to the dark side, declared the Great Hunt was officially over... though three Jedi were appointed to continue the work.

speaker: Player
text: The work of killing the terentatek, you mean.

speaker: Deesra
text: The Jedi chosen to continue the hunt on their own were Duron Qel-Droma, Guun Han Saresh and Shaela Nur. These three shared a powerful bond, and each of them was devoted to the light.

speaker: Deesra
text: The Council felt that together they would be able to defeat any terentatek they found. And by supporting each other they could resist the temptations of Korriban and the lure of the dark side.

speaker: Deesra
text: But none of the three survived. Their Master felt them become one with the Force when they left this world. He believed they were slain by one of the monsters they sought.

speaker: Deesra
text: The Council felt it was too dangerous to send anyone else in search of their remains, so their exact fate is not known. But let their deaths serve as a warning to you, Padawan.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the three Jedi lost after the Great Hunt.

speaker: Deesra
text: There is not much I can tell you other than their names: Duron Qel-Droma, Guun Han Saresh and Shaela Nur. They disappeared nearly forty years ago, long before my time at the Academy.

speaker: Deesra
text: The Council is certain they are dead; their Master sensed them leaving this world to become one with the Force. More than this, I cannot say.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Great Hunt you mentioned before.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Deesra
text: If you have questions you should speak with Master Dorak. He is the Chronicler of the Academy here on Dantooine, and is far more knowledgeable than I.

speaker: Player
text: I am looking for crystals to alter my lightsaber.

speaker: Deesra
text: There are caves here on Dantooine that hold the rare crystals we use in our lightsabers. But if you wish to go there, you must be careful. The caves are a place of great danger.

speaker: Deesra
text: Good luck with your continued training. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Deesra
text: Then may the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks for the warning. I'll be careful.

speaker: Deesra
text: A final warning as you go, Padawan: do not underestimate the terentatek. If you do, you may suffer the same fate as those who disappeared after the Great Hunt.

speaker: Player
text: I can't waste time listening to your fables!

speaker: Player
text: Why? What was so special about those three?

speaker: Player
text: Cost? What cost?

speaker: Player
text: Then why are you worried about them now?

speaker: Player
text: It's hard to believe an animal could pose a threat to a Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you telling me this?

speaker: Deesra
text: You have completed your initial training in a fraction of the normal time. The Force is very strong with you. I'm afraid you might become a target for these creatures.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Player
text: I can look after myself.

speaker: Deesra
text: Yes, your skill and prowess are already well known throughout this Academy. But even you would be wise to heed my warnings.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think the Council would want me to speak openly of this mission.

speaker: Player
text: My discussions with the Council are none of your business!

speaker: Deesra
text: Welcome to the Jedi enclave on Dantooine. I do not believe we know each other. My name is Deesra Luur Jada. You may call me Deesra.

speaker: Deesra
text: I have not heard of any new apprentices being accepted for training recently. What brings you to this place, if I may ask?

speaker: Player
text: I came here with Bastila.

speaker: Deesra
text: Yes, of course. I should have known. I have only heard a little of how she escaped the destruction of Taris. Tell me, did she save you from that planet as well?

speaker: Player
text: She didn't save me. We worked together to escape Taris.

speaker: Deesra
text: Oh, I see. Well, I meant no offense of course. In any case, it is good to have her back here on Dantooine again. We were afraid Malak had captured her.

speaker: Deesra
text: I hope you enjoy your time here on Dantooine. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: Get your story straight: I'm the one who saved her!

speaker: Player
text: My business here is my own.

speaker: Deesra
text: Oh... I see. Very well, I have no wish to make you uncomfortable. I suppose I shall just wish you a good day, then.

speaker: Deesra
text: You must be the new apprentice Master Zhar is training. I hear you are progressing at an astonishing rate. How are you finding your lessons?

speaker: Player
text: It's difficult, but worthwhile.

speaker: Deesra
text: The lessons we learn at the feet of our Masters teach us to use the Force for good. They show us the power of the light side, and protect us from the dark.

speaker: Player
text: The Masters are bringing me along too slowly. They're holding me back.

speaker: Deesra
text: Patience, apprentice. The Force is a great gift, but it also brings us a heavy burden.

speaker: Player
text: I am still learning the Jedi Code.

speaker: Deesra
text: Of course. Learning the Code is an essential part of our training, for there is great wisdom in its words. Allow me to help you with this, apprentice.

speaker: Deesra
text: There is no emotion; there is peace. There is no ignorance; there is knowledge. There is no passion; there is serenity. There is no chaos; there is harmony. There is no death; there is the Force.

speaker: Deesra
text: Take heed of these words, apprentice. They contain a deeper truth than it first appears.

speaker: Deesra
text: I hear that Master Zhar feels you are now ready to become a full fledged memer of our Order. Congratulations, apprentice. Or should I say Padawan?

speaker: Deesra
text: It brings me great joy to see another who has joined our Order, particularly in these trying times. The path of the light is a difficult one to walk, and many have fallen into the darkness.

speaker: Deesra
text: But I am certain you will not be one of those. So, Padawan - what can I do for you?

speaker: Deesra
text: Greetings, apprentice. How goes your training? I hear you are progressing at an astonishing rate.

speaker: Deesra
text: Yes, Padawan? Is there something I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: I just came to tell you that I've killed a terentatek

speaker: Deesra
text: Then the galaxy is a better place for it. Every one of these creatures is an abomination that must be exterminated. You have done well, Padawan.

speaker: Deesra
text: But do not let your success blind you to the dangers of these monsters. A Jedi must never become complacent when facing one of the terentatek, as you well know.

speaker: Deesra
text: Is there anything else I can do for you, Padawan?

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Hello there. You're heading out to the desert? You're a hunter right? You must be if you've been allowed to leave Anchorhead.

text: When you see Tanis, and I know you know him, tell him his wife hopes he enjoys the anniversary gift.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you think I would know him?

speaker: Marlena Venn

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Well, he can do what he wants. He'll get what he deserves. I bought my own license just so I could see that he did.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: I'm sure you do. Like I said, when you see him, tell him his wife Marlena says hello.

speaker: Player
text: You sound like you're planning to kill him.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Oh, I'm through planning. I just left him a little mess that he has to take care of. If he's smart, he'll be just fine.

text: Anniversary gift? What are you talking about?

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Just a little something to remember me by. Something that symbolizes our years together. Something that will blow up in his face.

text: Of course, he'll never understand how appropriate it is. He can't talk his way out of this one. He's not smart enough.

text: What do you mean by "you old boys"?

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: You're just another of his buddies from that "hunting" club. I know your kind. You all cover for each other, I bet.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Oh, I'll be long gone soon enough. The next shuttle to... anywhere, really. I've had it with cleaning up his messes, repairing his droids.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: If he lives, he can try and get by on his own. I doubt he'll last long with no one to listen to his lies.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: When you see Tanis, and I know you old boys always stick together, tell him his wife hopes he enjoys the anniversary gift.

speaker: Marlena Venn
text: Having fun on the dunes, Tanis? I made sure you would. Here's the deal: Your precious droids have trapped you. They'll hold you until you die of thirst. Make a mistake while repairing them, they explode. Have a good death. My mother was right about you.

speaker: AdmrlSaulKar
text: Lord Malak, the preparations are nearly complete. Everyday the Star Forge adds more ships to our fleet, it is operating at nearly 300% of our projections. ## The fleet is assembling around the Star Forge, and awaits your instructions.

speaker: AdmrlSaulKar
text: The fleet is assembling around the Star Forge, and awaits your instructions. Malak: Patience, Commander.

speaker: DarthMalak
text: Patience, Commander. ## My new apprentice is nearly ready. ## Once Bastila joins her Battle Meditation to our enormous fleet, we shall be invincible.  Then we shall begin our final conquest of the Core Worlds, and the Republic will be crushed forever.

speaker: AdmrlSaulKar
text: As you wish, Lord Malak.

speaker: Sunry
text: Jolee! What... what are you doing here?
comment: jolee in party, first time conversation

speaker: Jolee
text: Elora sent me, Sunry. I'm here to get you out of this mess. The courts went and made us Arbiters for your case.

speaker: Sunry
text: Just like old times, eh Jolee? You come swooping in out of nowhere to save my tail from the fire.

speaker: Jolee
text: You saved my wrinkled butt more than a few times as well, friend, if I recall. But there'll be time for catching up later. Right now we need to focus on the case.

speaker: Sunry
text: The case is a complete frame-up. Anyone looking at the evidence could see that - or so I thought. But the Selkath seem to think, well that there's enough to go to trial.

speaker: Sunry
text: There aren't any witnesses. All that evidence against me is circumstantial... and completely flawed.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go over the evidence.

speaker: Sunry
text: Well... you know I was having an affair with Elassa... I went there to break it off that night.

speaker: Sunry
text: I can tell you it wasn't easy. She is... was... young and beautiful. But I love Elora, and I knew I had to do it. I broke it off as quickly as I could and then left.

speaker: Sunry
text: I found out later she'd been murdered when the Selkath authorities came knocking on my door...

speaker: Sunry
text: But let's look at the facts they've given:

speaker: Sunry
text: Elassa was brutally killed. Think about that - she was a Sith, trained in battle and I'm just a crippled old man!

speaker: Sunry
text: My war injuries make it difficult for me to walk even to hold things. See how my hands are shaking! How could I kill a Sith warrior at close quarters? I ask you!

speaker: Sunry
text: Further: They say they found my Hero's Cross at the crime scene. Would I leave my war medal behind if I killed someone? Even I'm not that stupid.

speaker: Sunry
text: Obviously the Sith planted the Cross. And what about the lack of forensic evidence? Skin and hair samples, clothing fibers - why isn't there anything like that at the crime scene? Sounds like an obvious frame-up to me.

speaker: Sunry
text: I hope you can see how the Sith are manipulating the Selkath, and probably even you, to set up this against me! We need to get this over with quickly and clear my name.

speaker: Sunry
text: Anything else I can help you with? I want my Arbiter to be well prepared before we go to trial.

speaker: Player
text: I need to investigate the case some more. Any ideas where I should look?

speaker: Sunry
text: I guess you could interview witnesses at the hotel where the murder happened. The Selkath already did that, but the fish folk don't have much rapport with off-worlders. Maybe one of them was holding something back.

speaker: Sunry
text: But I think you'd be better off investigating the Sith themselves. Maybe you could find some proof they planted evidence to frame me - though that might mean figuring out a way into the Sith Embassy.

speaker: Player
text: There's a few things we have to clear up.

speaker: Sunry
text: Go ahead, ask... ask what you need to. I've got nothing to hide.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Were you and Elassa having an affair?
comment: has data pad or heard of affair form Gonto Yas

speaker: Sunry
text: [Success] We... I... Oh, no... what must this look like... Yes. Yes we were having an affair.

speaker: Sunry
text: I know it was wrong, but I'm a weak man. Elassa was beautiful and young - how was I to resist her charms? But I didn't kill her! I loved her!

speaker: Sunry
text: Please, I know I made a terrible mistake getting involved with Elassa, but I was going there to break it off with her.

speaker: Sunry
text: I did it, but found out later that she was dead. I don't deserve to go to jail just for having an affair, do I? You have to help me prove that I wasn't the killer!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Sunry
text: Very well. I suppose there is still much you must do before the trial.

speaker: Sunry
text: Once you've gotten enough evidence to go to trial just tell the warden we're ready. The sooner I get out of this cell the better.

speaker: Sunry
text: [Failure] That's a Sith lie! They're trying to embarrass me and humiliate my wife! How dare you ask me that!

speaker: Player
text: Witnesses saw you at her hotel room, Sunry. You better tell me what's going on.

speaker: Sunry
text: The witnesses are lying! Maybe the Sith got to them - I don't know. But it's a lie I tell you! A hurtful, horrible lie!

speaker: Player
text: No offense, Sunry. I have to ask.

speaker: Sunry
text: Yes, I... I suppose you do. Please, forgive my outburst. This has been a terribly stressful time for me. I... I'm sure there is more you want to ask me.

speaker: Player
text: I know you're lying, Sunry. I found this datapad talking about you and Elassa.

speaker: Sunry
text: Then... then you know. Please, don't make a big deal about this. Elora already knew and I... I was going there to break if off with Elassa.

speaker: Player
text: There was a Rodian who planted evidence at the murder scene.

speaker: Sunry
text: A Rodian? I didn't know there were any Rodians on Manaan. Oh, except for Tyvark... and this one named Gluupor who was hanging around the hotel all the time.

speaker: Sunry
text: OK, so maybe there are a whole bunch of Rodians on Manaan, but what does that matter? If he planted evidence at the scene it's a clear sign of a frame-up. He probably took all the evidence of the real killer at the same time.

speaker: Sunry
text: The evidence of a Sith conspiracy keeps getting stronger, doesn't it? But I suspect there is still stuff you want to clear up.

speaker: Player
text: I know you're guilty, Sunry. I've got the Republic's data recording.

speaker: Sunry
text: So the truth is out. I never meant to kill her, you know. When I found out she was a Sith spy using me to gain information, something inside me just snapped.

speaker: Sunry
text: She didn't know I had found out, so I waited until she fell asleep and then I... I killed her. Simple, really. But once I realized what I'd done I... I panicked. I contacted those spies from the Republic to help me.

speaker: Sunry
text: They found the illegal monitoring device that the Sith had planted in the room, altered its recording to hide my part in it and cleared up the evidence. I figured that was the end of it.

speaker: Player
text: But the Sith found out the truth, didn't they?

speaker: Sunry
text: The Sith must have been spying on me and Elassa, trying to make sure she wasn't a double agent. They must have seen the Republic spies getting rid of all the evidence.

speaker: Sunry
text: And so they planted their own evidence. Elassa must have stolen that Hero's Cross from me long ago and given it to her Sith masters, like some kind of trophy.

speaker: Sunry
text: I just thought I'd misplaced it. But when the Cross turned up on her body, I knew the Sith had put it there. So now you know the whole story, what are you going to do?

speaker: Player
text: You're guilty, Sunry. Confess.

speaker: Sunry
text: You think I'm some kind of monster, don't you? All I did was kill a Sith! How many Sith have you killed? Dozens? Hundreds? Thousands?

speaker: Jolee
text: That's different, Sunry, and you know it. We don't kill them in cold blood while they sleep.

speaker: Sunry
text: I don't see how the two of us are any different. She was a spy! She was using me to get information so Malak's army could destroy the Republic! She deserved to die!

speaker: Player
text: Killing your lover while she sleeps is murder - even if she is a Sith!

speaker: Sunry
text: If I confess I'm looking at 20 years in prison! And the Ahto City officials might even place kolto sanctions on the Republic Embassy. Without kolto how can we treat the injuries to our soldiers on the front lines!

speaker: Player
text: I suppose you're right. I won't expose you.

speaker: Sunry
text: I'm glad you decided to see reason in this. If I'm convicted it could cause trouble for the Republic embassy here on Manaan. And none of us want that, now do we?

speaker: Player
text: These are just excuses, Sunry. We both know you have to own up to your crimes.

speaker: Sunry
text: No. I can't do that and put the Republic's supply of kolto in danger. No I won't! Now look, I may have done something stupid, and it may only be worse for my standing by it, but I will not confess.

speaker: Sunry
text: If you turn me in, the Republic will likely lose its kolto export privileges and then we'll lose the war for sure. Are you going to send all those thousands, millions - like on Taris - to their deaths, just for your sense of 'justice'?

speaker: Jolee
text: Sunry... this is wrong, and you know it. I am a Jedi... what is it that you expect me to do to defend your actions?

speaker: Sunry
text: You do whatever you have to, Jolee. I know what I did, but I also know what's at stake, here.

speaker: Sunry
text: No, I'll rot in here if I have to, but I won't betray the Republic. Do what you have to, but know what the consequences will be.

speaker: Carth
text: I hate to say it, but he has a point. The Republic needs that kolto.

speaker: Bastila
text: And you would propose what? Letting a murderer free on the chance it will help the Republic?

speaker: Carth
text: If need be. We are talking about a Sith, remember? I don't approve of what he did any more than you --

speaker: Bastila
text: But you're willing to overlook it. Are the principles that the Republic stands on so very weak, Carth?

speaker: Carth
text: The Republic's principles aren't worth a hill of beans if it falls, Bastila. I'll do whatever I can to save it.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You will confess your crimes. You WANT to confess your crimes.

speaker: Sunry
text: [Failure] Oh, That's low - using a Jedi mind trick to extort a confession from me. You might as well beat it out of me, you'd have better luck!

speaker: Player
text: If you confess the court might show mercy.

speaker: Carth
text: You're talking about acts of war. We're just defending ourselves! You murdered your girlfriend in her sleep.

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: The meatbag has a point, master. Killing is often justified, if illegal in the eyes of many.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know.

speaker: Player
text: I won't betray your secret. We'll go on with the trial.

speaker: Jolee
text: But Sunry is a murderer. I'm sorry, old friend, but you are. I... I can't approve of this. You go ahead, however, if that's what you think is best.

speaker: Player
text: You should have known the truth would come out eventually.

speaker: Player
text: You're nothing but a cold blooded killer!

speaker: Sunry
text: It's easy for you to judge me - but you weren't there! You don't know what it was like, realizing what I'd done. But it...but it doesn't matter anyway.

speaker: Player
text: The judges said that you left after the shot was fired.

speaker: Sunry
text: How would they know? They weren't there!

speaker: Sunry
text: I heard some of the witnesses said that too, but I swear she was alive when I left!

speaker: Sunry
text: I wonder if the Sith have been putting pressure on people to get them to convict me... It wouldn't surprise me at all. They've had it in for me since the war...

speaker: Sunry
text: You should ask everyone about that... they might admit to helping the Sith under pressure.

speaker: Player
text: On second thought, I will ask something else.

speaker: Sunry
text: Er... OK. What else do you want to know?

speaker: Sunry
text: Well I was at the hotel, I admit. And I did meet Elassa there that night. But it's not what you think!

speaker: Sunry
text: I... I was working with Republic Intelligence. We were pretending to feed information to the Sith while I turned Elassa into a double agent working for us.

speaker: Sunry
text: It was going well, too... Until she turned up dead...

speaker: Sunry
text: Hm... maybe the Sith had found out I was turning her and had her eliminated...

speaker: Sunry
text: Who are you? What are you doing here?
comment: jolee not in party, first time conversation

speaker: Player
text: Your wife asked me to come. I'm a friend of Jolee Bindo.

speaker: Sunry
text: Jolee? What's he doing here on Manaan? Never mind - I'm just glad he's here. So is this some kind of prison break? If it is we won't get very far before the Selkath cut us down I can tell ya.

speaker: Player
text: I've been appointed as your Arbiter.

speaker: Sunry
text: Well, I guess if you're going to be my Arbiter you'll need to hear what happened. I might as well start at the beginning.

speaker: Sunry
text: Ah, I see you're back. Not that I don't appreciate the visit, but I had hoped you were going to speak to the warden so we might begin the trial.
comment: jolee not in party, subsequent conversations

speaker: Sunry
text: I grow weary of staring at these four bare walls. But I suppose you know what you are doing. You know the role of Arbiter cannot be taken lightly.

speaker: Sunry
text: Jolee - coming to check in on an old man? I must confess, I... I would rather you were here to speak to the warden and begin my trial.

speaker: Jolee
text: Soon, old friend. But we don't want to go to trial until we've got the whole picture.

speaker: Jergan
text: Surely you understand what I'm talking about. I'd guess you've experienced many lonely evenings... something I'm hoping to avoid tonight.

speaker: Jergan
text: The exotic beauty returns. Hello again, my dear. Have you changed your mind? Do you want to take me up on my offer? Just twenty credits and I can arrange a meeting with the band.

speaker: Player
text: I want to meet the band. Here's twenty credits.

speaker: Jergan
text: Excellent. Wait here while I go set it up with my contact. I'll give him your credits, then I'll come back out and take you to meet the band.

speaker: Player
text: I can't afford that much.
comment: hard persuassion, small dark side hit

speaker: Jergan
text: Well, I would like to help you but I can't arrange the meeting for free. And I'm afraid your feminine charms would have little effect on the Rodian bodyguards backstage.

speaker: Jergan
text: If you manage to come up with the credits just come back and see me. I'll be more than happy to arrange for you to meet the band. Until then, please enjoy the music.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like you're running a scam to me.

speaker: Jergan
text: You sting me with your words! I merely thought I could offer you the rare opportunity to meet a celebrity before they were famous. But I see you're not interested.

speaker: Jergan
text: That's too bad. They really are charming fellows. Very well, then - I hope you enjoy the music. If you change your mind come speak with me again.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in meeting the band.

speaker: Jergan
text: Well, hello there! I see from your exotic appearance that you are not from Taris originally. Allow me to introduce myself - my name is Jergan.

speaker: Player
text: Pleased to meet you. My name's <FullName>.

speaker: Jergan
text: What do you think of our local music? The band is quite good, wouldn't you agree? They're on the verge of intergalactic stardom, you know.

speaker: Player
text: They're very good.

speaker: Jergan
text: Obviously you have an ear for music. Mark my words, they'll be famous soon enough. They were about to go on tour before this Sith quarantine stranded them here.

speaker: Jergan
text: Would you like to meet the band after the show? Maybe have a brief brush with fame before they become intergalactic superstars? I can arrange it, you know.

speaker: Player
text: How will you arrange that?

text: I have a standing arrangement with one of the Rodian bodyguards backstage. For the small sum of 20 credits he'll let me set up a meeting with you and the band.

speaker: Player
text: Sure, I'd like to meet them.

speaker: Player
text: I'll pass.

speaker: Jergan
text: Are you certain? This is a once in a lifetime opportunity - meet the legends before they were famous. All it will cost you is a small handful of credits.

speaker: Player
text: It's different, but I like it.

speaker: Player
text: I don't much care for the band.

speaker: Jergan
text: They are something of an acquired taste. But mark my words, they'll be famous soon enough. They were about to go on tour before this Sith quarantine stranded them here.

speaker: Player
text: These guys are the worst!

speaker: Player
text: What do you want, Jergan?

text: Tell him we have the moisture converters.

speaker: HK47

text: [Leave quietly]

text: [He looks past you, like you were never there.]

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: We will guard this landing place from now on. Yours is the only ship that will be allowed to dock here for a long time, outsider.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Thank you for your assistance, outsider. I doubt we will meet another of your kind like you.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Your presence is tolerated because of how you helped us, outsider.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: It will be a long time before we allow ourselves to be as weak as Chuundar made us.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: If another company comes to Kashyyyk, they will find it impossible to do what Czerka did.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: We will remember what happend here. Slavers will not take us again.

speaker: Sith Soldier

text: How are the Sand People doing so much damage? Blasters beat gaffi sticks, don't they?

speaker: Czerka Merchant Officer
text: Maybe the Sith will give us more support here on Tatooine. Couldn't get worse.

speaker: Czerka Merchant Officer
text: The sooner I get out of this dustbowl, the better.

text: Czerka Corporation should just close this whole place down. Heh. Who would miss it?

speaker: Freyyr
text: More of you Czerka core-rats? Is even the heart of Kashyyyk not free from your kind?

speaker: Jolee
text: He is almost feral after all this time. Calm yourself, Freyyr. We are friends. Don't you remember me?

speaker: Freyyr
text: After years in the Shadowlands, I remember only that outsiders are not to be trusted! I'll see you dead!

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, this may prove difficult.
comment: Freyyr attacks. Surrenders when reduced to low HPs. He should be tough. He's battle-hardened.

speaker: Freyyr
text: For years I have hid, hoping to someday free my world! I swear you will not take me! I swear!

speaker: Freyyr
text: I... I am beaten. Take my head, Czerka filth. You won't get another chance. So swears Freyyr of Kashyyyk.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not here to kill you. Just listen!

speaker: Freyyr
text: The words of outsiders are tainted with lies. You can't convince me otherwise.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know Zaalbar and Chuundar?

speaker: Freyyr
text: What? Those are the names of my sons! But they are lost to me now: one exiled, the other a traitor!

speaker: Mission
text: Hold on a second: Zaalbar and Chuundar are brothers? And you're their father? Wait a minute... does this mean Big Z is some kind of prince or something?

speaker: Freyyr
text: Why do you speak the names of my sons? How do you know of them? Tell me!

speaker: Player
text: My name is <FullName>. I came to Kashyyyk with Zaalbar.

speaker: Freyyr
text: To my shame, Zaalbar was exiled and enslaved. Do you dare claim to be my son's owner, outsider?

speaker: Player
text: No, he follows because of a life-debt.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Does he? Then he sees something of worth in you. I will listen... cautiously. Gullibility has harmed me in the past.

speaker: Freyyr
text: If I had seen the lies of Chuundar, he would have been exposed as a slaver. Zaalbar would not have been exiled...

speaker: Mission
text: Exiled? Big Z never told me that! Of course he never said he was royalty, either.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I did not believe Zaalbar's claims; I believed the elder boy, as tradition dictated. The shame of Zaalbar's attack blinded me.

speaker: Player
text: Go over exactly what happened with Zaalbar.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Zaalbar saw it first. He learned that Chuundar was dealing with the Czerka, leading them to our hunting parties.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Chuundar would blame disappearances on the dangers of the Shadowlands. Zaalbar was crazed when he found out.

speaker: Freyyr
text: He attacked Chuundar with his claws. I thought he had gone mad... shed his honor. I was bound by the old ways.

speaker: Player
text: So Zaalbar was exiled. When did you learn the truth?

speaker: Freyyr
text: A year later. By then, Chuundar had spread lies of my own madness. I had no allies when I confronted him.

speaker: Freyyr
text: He and his Czerka guards attacked me. I had to retreat to the deepest Shadowlands, but even there they followed.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's when I first saw him. I helped his pursuers lose him for a moment. Do you remember me now, Freyyr?

speaker: Freyyr
text: Yes, I think I do. I am sorry about attacking. It's been so long since I have offered my trust, or accepted that of someone else.

speaker: Player
text: Back to my other questions.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will answer, and then ask something of you.

speaker: Player
text: Why would Chuundar want you dead now?

speaker: Freyyr
text: Well, if Zaalbar is back, perhaps Chuundar is worried the people will realize things are not as they seem.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Chuundar has established himself as a leader that succeeded despite the "tragedies" that have plagued his family.

speaker: Freyyr
text: If it was shown that he conspired with the slavers, his honor would be gone. I wonder...

speaker: Player
text: Well, what happens now?

speaker: Freyyr
text: That would depend on you, <FullName>. You will either kill me or decide that I may yet benefit my people.

speaker: Freyyr
text: There is a way I might challenge Chuundar, but it would take a lot to convince people they have been lied to.

speaker: Player
text: How? Everyone is on his side.

speaker: Freyyr
text: He has a strong web of lies, but if I appeal to the traditions of my people, I might be able to gather support.

speaker: Freyyr
text: There is a legend of a great warrior from the old times. Bacca was his name, and he is greatly revered.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Bacca found a crashed starship, our first hint of life elsewhere. He was a cautious old wook, and feared the taint of invaders.

speaker: Freyyr
text: He constructed a vibroblade from the wreckage. It has long symbolized our independence. Only destined leaders have held it.

speaker: Player
text: Where might I find it?

speaker: Freyyr
text: That is the problem. It was the symbol of our great chieftains for centuries, but it was damaged a generation ago in ritual battle.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Here in the Shadowlands Rothrrrawr fought the Great Beast. He sought a challenge, but this arrogance got him more than he could handle.

speaker: Freyyr
text: He survived, but the blade of the sword stayed in the creature's hide. Our tales say it was taken because we had become undeserving.

speaker: Freyyr
text: The hilt is still in the court of our chieftain... with Chuundar. If the blade could be found, <FullName>, tradition could cast doubt on his rule.

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I've already found it. I wasn't sure what it was.
comment: Player DOES have the hilt of Bacca's sword

speaker: Freyyr
text: You have? Please let me see it. I must be sure!

speaker: Player
text: Here, take it. I'm sure it is the one.

speaker: Freyyr
text: It... it is! It may not look like much... but it is a very important relic of my people. Tradition dictates that it be respected.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I didn't think I was worthy to search for it, but I realize that was selfish despair. I should have challenged Chuundar long ago.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will make amends now. I have new hope. You have led me to this. Perhaps that is what the Great Beast wanted.

speaker: Player
text: We should proceed carefully.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will climb to the surface as quickly as possible and try to gather support. You will have to follow on the paths as soon as you can, <FullName>.

speaker: Freyyr
text: When you arrive, we will confront Chuundar in the throne room. My people will no longer be slaves.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, time to take the fight to Chuundar himself!

speaker: Player
text: Wait a minute. What's in it for me?

speaker: Freyyr
text: What? I... I have nothing. I've been here for years. When we have succeeded, I will see you are rewarded.

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I was mistaken.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Don't taunt me like that. False hope is a cruel thing.

speaker: Player
text: I have other questions.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will answer as best I can.

speaker: Player
text: Seen anyone hunting down here? Camouflaged attackers?

speaker: Freyyr
text: My invisible attackers are a menagerie of my own fears and regrets, so many more than actual beasts that walk.

speaker: Freyyr
text: No, I have not seen the creatures that you mention. I have been... preoccupied.

speaker: Player
text: I found a computer. Know anything about it?
comment: Player HAS spoken to the strange computer.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I tried to access it many times over the years. It would never acknowledge me. I'm no good with such things.

speaker: Player
text: It clamins to be ancient. It created the forests.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Well, now you are just having fun with me. It's probably just some malfunctioning Czerka cast-off.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Seriously though, if we are to challenge Chuundar based on tradition, I suggest you don't say these things to anyone.

speaker: Freyyr
text: You risk contradicting our most ancient tales. Perhaps this warrants investigating, but not now.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.
comment: Player has NOT spoken with the computer

speaker: Freyyr
text: I've never heard of such a thing... but there is something odd down here. A large computer installation.

speaker: Freyyr
text: It's probably just some Czerka cast-off, but you may find something useful. I can't figure it out, myself.

speaker: Freyyr
text: It is northwest of here. I gave up on it years ago.

speaker: Player
text: Back to my previous questions.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will try to answer as best I am able.

speaker: Player
text: I have found the blade of Bacca's sword.
comment: Player has the hilt of Bacca's sword

speaker: Player
text: I'll get back to you. Wait here.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I hope you can help. I must try to fix what has gone wrong here.

speaker: Player
text: I've decided to kill you for Chuundar!

speaker: Jolee
text: I don't support this action! Think on this, child!

speaker: Player
text: You are hardly a competent moral guide. Why question me?

speaker: Jolee
text: Look, I'm not your nanny-droid, but I just don't think following Chuundar is the best course.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, I'll talk to Freyyr and think about it.

speaker: Player
text: You mind your own business! I've made my decision.

speaker: Mission
text: Doesn't seem like much of a father anyway, kicking his son out like that.
comment: Kind of a brooding statement. She doesn't really hate Freyyr, but she sees a bit of her own family problems in the situation and it makes her resigned to killing him. She only knows this person was involved in hurting her only real friend, Zaalbar.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Then let my blood feed my beloved Kashyyyk!

speaker: Player
text: Describe the creature. Where can I find it?

speaker: Freyyr
text: Many have tried to hunt this beast, but only a few who have seen it have lived to tell the tale. And none have ever managed to kill the creature.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Many years ago, when I was far younger than I am now, a Jedi came to hunt the creature... a proud and boastful young man. Like many before him, he did not return.

speaker: Freyyr
text: The beast is cunning. It will not appear if there is an overwhelming number waiting to slay it. But if you gather in small numbers, we know how to lure it out.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Fresh blood will draw it out. Before Chuundar's rule put an end to the ritual, fresh kills were often left as offerings in the south of this area.

speaker: Player
text: I will try to find it. Can you give me any direction?

speaker: Freyyr
text: There is a place of ritual south of here. If the Great Beast is to be lured out of hiding, it must be done there, using the old ways.

speaker: Freyyr
text: You have already collected the body of a viper kinrath. Such bait would be tempting for the creature. Find a way to display it.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will stay here and try to think of what I will say to Zaalbar. I have wronged him. I hope he can forgive me.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will be here. Please, <FullName>, find the blade of Bacca's sword. I must make things right.

speaker: Freyyr
text: The flesh of a fresh kill would be tempting bait if displayed properly. Find an appropriate beast of sufficient mass to attract it.

speaker: Player
text: And you still think you are worthy of being chieftain?

speaker: Freyyr
text: No, I don't, but better me than Chuundar. He sells his own people for power. Please help, <FullName>. You've brought me hope...

speaker: Player
text: This bores me. I think I'll just kill you!

speaker: Jolee
text: I don't approve of this! Is Chuundar to be blindly obeyed?

speaker: Player
text: You're my moral guide now? That's not your style.

speaker: Jolee
text: Perhaps not. Do what you will. I'm just wondering if Chuundar is the wiser choice of ally.

speaker: Player
text: Ah, shut up. I'll ask him a few more questions.

speaker: Player
text: I've made my decision. The old fool dies!

speaker: Player
text: What, a scavenger hunt for some sword? You're kidding.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I'm afraid not. It was the symbol of our great chieftains for centuries, but it was damaged a generation ago in ritual battle.

speaker: Player
text: That's enough. Just die, you old hairbag!

speaker: Jolee
text: Is that it? You spared his life initially just to cut him off before he can fully explain himself?

speaker: Player
text: Oh, very well. Freyyr, do you know Zaalbar and Chuundar?

speaker: Freyyr
text: What? Those are my sons. Why do you speak their names? Tell me!

speaker: Player
text: My name is <FullName>. Chuundar sent me to kill you.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Did he? I'm surprised it took him this long. Very well, do your worst!

speaker: Player
text: Wait! I came here with Zaalbar.

speaker: Player
text: I intend to!

speaker: Mission
text: Doesn't seem like much of a father anyway. Hmph! Zaalbar was hurt bad by whatever happened here.

text: Fine, I'll tell him that I arrived here with Zaalbar.

speaker: Player
text: Then let him tell exactly what happened with Zaalbar.

speaker: Player
text: I'm leader here. I say he dies!

speaker: Freyyr
text: The old hermit saved me, I think. He clouded their minds for a moment. I have had a long time to hide... and regret.

speaker: Player
text: It doesn't matter. It proves I am no common Czerka slaver.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I suppose it does. I will listen... cautiously. Gullibility has harmed me in the past...

speaker: Player
text: Chuundar sends his regards. Now die!

speaker: Jolee
text: Did we come this far only to kill this old wook? I don't approve of this at all.

speaker: Player
text: What would you suggest? He attacked us first.

speaker: Jolee
text: I know he did, but not without reason. The only outsiders he's seen for years have been slavers.

speaker: Player
text: What can I say to prove we aren't enemies?

speaker: Player
text: This seems simple to me. Time to die, Freyyr!

speaker: Player
text: Back in line! I'm in charge here.

speaker: Jolee

speaker: Freyyr
text: Please, tell me you have made progress. Having the blade will gain me valuable support.
