speaker: Chuundar
text: You've made certain I cannot be challenged. With Freyyr gone, there is nobody to whine about the old traditions. Everyone believes in my way... even Zaalbar.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I will lead the Wookiee people to a great future... safely under my thumb. What should be the reward, brother? What will be your reward for joining me?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You've shown me how useless our traditions are, so what is there to want? I'll take Bacca's sword. At least it's still useful in combat.

speaker: Player
text: I think that would be fitting.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Hmm... I agree with the request. The sword has lost it's influence here, and removing it from Kashyyyk will kill the old ways completely. That would suit my plans well.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Here, let's get the blade off Father's corpse. I should be able to... yes... I think that does it.
comment: Freyyr was killed in the throne room (which means his corpse was there and as far as the player is concerned he had Bacca's sword hilt on him, )

speaker: Chuundar
text: Take it. It's harmless in the hands of an exile and an outsider. Freyyr was the true force behind it, and the new generation will forget him quickly. You've seen to that.

speaker: Mission
text: You're not fooling anyone, ya know.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Leave it alone, Mission. This is what I want now.

speaker: Mission
text: If you say so, Big Z.

speaker: Chuundar
text: That finishes our business. Take care, Zaalbar. We'll welcome you back someday. When I decide the people are ready. Not before.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Don't worry, brother. I know your way is the best. It's the only way our people will survive in a galaxy full of outsider lies.

speaker: Chuundar
text: And you, outsider, you'll understand why I don't invite you to stay. The uncontested ruler of Kashyyyk will not abide troublemakers...

speaker: Chuundar
text: No matter how helpful they may have been. Goodbye.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, yes. Far better to have both the blade and a possible rival as far from Kashyyyk as possible, hey? *sigh* I feel very tired of this place, now.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are free to leave with my brother, mad hermit. Nothing compels you to remain.

speaker: Jolee
text: Right you are. I think I'll do just that.

speaker: Chuundar
text: The only problem is that I only have the hilt of the thing. The blade was lost in the Shadowlands long ago.

speaker: Player
text: I have the blade.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are full of surprises. Let me see... this should be a simple matter. Yes, I think... there we go.

speaker: Player
text: I might be able to find the blade.
comment: Player does not have Bacca's sword hilt

speaker: Chuundar
text: Will you? Very well. Here, take the hilt. Find the blade and you should be able to assemble the sword.
comment: Give player Bacca blade. If the player has both the hilt and blade at once, the useable sword should appear in inventory.

speaker: Chuundar
text: And if you don't or can't, it'll still be gone from my sight. I think that takes care of everything.

speaker: Player
text: Well, that ends that. Perhaps something else?

speaker: Chuundar
text: I think I'll leave it for you to sort out. Take the hilt. Find the blade and you should be able to assemble the sword.
comment: Give player Bacca blade. If the player has both the hilt and blade at once, the useable sword should appear in inventory.

speaker: Player
text: Wait Zaalbar. I want credits out of this.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: RRAAAAAAGHGHGH!!! BACCA'S SWORD! NOTHING ELSE!
comment: huge roar. He's madder than he's ever been.

speaker: Mission
text: Whoa, Big Z! Settle down! I've never seen him this angry before!

speaker: Chuundar
text: Uh... it seems Zaalbar has made up his mind, and I agree. The sword has lost it's influence here. Removing it from Kashyyyk will kill the old ways completely.

speaker: Jolee
text: My, my. Best to give an angry Wookiee his due, I'd say.

speaker: Cand
text: Getting Wookiees angry is not a smart thing to do.

speaker: Juhani
text: Perhaps you should not be so self-serving.

speaker: Player
text: Shut up, Wookiee, I'm bargaining!

speaker: Player
text: I saw an ancient computer of some kind.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Did you? You were out of sight from my spies for a long time. Perhaps it was some crashed ship?

speaker: Player
text: It's been there since before the forest.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Now I think you are just making things up. Nothing is older than the forest, not even we Wookiees.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, you're wrong on that count, actually. Not that I would expect you to know that.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I might send someone to try and find this ancient computer, but I think you are mistaken. Crazy outsider.

speaker: Player
text: There were Czerka poachers down there.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Yes, and you made a mess of their operation. I am not pleased about that, but I can overlook it.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I will have to make amends to Czerka Corporation on the next slave shipment, but your service elsewhere was worth it.

speaker: Player
text: I met the hermit Jolee Bindo down there.

speaker: Chuundar
text: So, the insane outsider is real. Interesting. I trust you are removing him? I'd hate to see him come to harm.

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah! Save your threats, I'm sick of the forest. And I'm not too fond of what happened here. I'll take the ride.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Yes, better that he leave. It's hard to blame the Shadowlands for missing Wookiees when he lives down there.

speaker: Player
text: Will I be rewarded for my efforts?

speaker: Chuundar
text: I will see to it that you are given what you deserve. Finish with your questions and we will settle our accounts.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Oh, that's just great! Everyone is here now! It's a reunion!

speaker: Freyyr
text: Yes, son. By the blade of Bacca's sword, I've come to end your treachery! No more will you sell your own people!

speaker: Chuundar
text: You have Bacca's blade? So what! I have the hilt, held by each true Chieftain in recent memory! Even you claimed it was all-important!

speaker: Chuundar
text: We both have our ancient trinkets, so who will the people follow now? You? You are old and weak!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Shut up! Both of you! This ends today! I... I will not see Rwookrrorro suffer any more!

speaker: Player
text: You tell them, Zaalbar!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I... I don't know what to do, <FirstName>. Chuundar has been telling me things... he makes sense... I think. I don't know.

speaker: Player
text: Side with Chuundar. He has the power here!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Are you sure?

speaker: Player
text: Yes! Freyyr abandoned you! "Sorry" doesn't make it better!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Then... then we must go a new way. I'm sorry father. Your time has passed.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Damn right it has! Lay down and die, old man!

speaker: Mission
text: I... guess he *did* toss you out on your ear, Big Z. What kind of father is that?

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will fight to the last! For Kashyyyk! For... the lost honor of my sons!
comment: Freyyr hostile and killable. Expendable wookie guys fight on his side. Chuundar invulnerable, but stays out of the way. Expendable Czerka fight for him. Zaalbar fights against Freyyr. This may be a problem. He's not technically in the party right now. What if he dies?

speaker: Jolee
text: *That* is your advice? Side with the slaver? Fine, fine... it's your call.

speaker: Bastila
text: Are you sure this is wise? To support a slaver feels... wrong.

speaker: Carth
text: Are you going to second-guess everyone?

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course not. Only the idiots around me.

speaker: Player
text: I heard that.

speaker: Cand
text: Heh, now this is going to hurt some...

speaker: Player
text: No, it's better to side with your father!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Is it the best course?

speaker: Player
text: Without doubt! Chuundar is a slaver!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Then there is no other way. Chuundar! You have betrayed our people! You must pay!

speaker: Mission
text: Woo-hoo! Way to go, Big Z!

speaker: Freyyr
text: That's my boy!

speaker: Chuundar
text: You're too weak to fight, old wook, and I still have Czerka support! We'll see who dies today!
comment: Chuundar hostile and killable. Czerka guys fight on his side. Freyyr invulnerable, but stays out of the way. Expendable wookies fight for him. Zaalbar fights Against Chuundar. This may be a problem. He's not technically in the party right now. What if he dies?

speaker: Player
text: No, siding with your brother would be better.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have to fight? Talk it through!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Could we work together? It would be difficult...

speaker: Player
text: Convince them! Avoid this needless slaughter!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Then so be it! The fighting stops here! I will not have our world destroyed beneath you two!

speaker: Mission
text: Alright! Way to go, Big Z!

speaker: Freyyr
text: Perhaps there is hope. What say you, Chuundar?

speaker: Chuundar
text: What do I say? I still have Czerka support. I say you will die! Attack!
comment: Chuundar hostile and killable. Czerka guys fight on his side. Freyyr invulnerable, but stays out of the way. Expendable wookies fight for him. Zaalbar fights Against Chuundar. This may be a problem. He's not technically in the party right now. What if he dies?

speaker: Player
text: I don't care! Just get on with it!

speaker: Jolee
text: Wait... isn't that my line?

speaker: Player
text: Side with Freyyr. He is the honorable one!

speaker: Player
text: Quiet down. We'll use this to our advantage.

speaker: Player
text: Do none of you hairy heaps ever shut up?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: W-what?

speaker: Player
text: For not being able to speak Basic, you all sure yap a lot.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: This is important! If you have advice, say it now.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing. How do you want to proceed, Zaalbar?

speaker: Chuundar
text: Step forward and address mighty and wise Chuundar, outsider. I don't often allow visitors of your kind.
comment: Initial, plot not done. Player is led to this conversation and cannot go to the shadowlands until it is complete. Zaalbar MUST be present for this conversation. If he was not in the player's party, he must be brought from the player's ship. He is removed from the party and left in Chuundar's throne room for the duration. There will need to be some way to determine whether Zaalbar arrived with the player, or was brought from the ship. A few dialogue branches depend on this.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You are flanked by Czerka slavers! Are they not outsiders? Or have you sold all of Kashyyyk to them!
comment: Zaalbar was in the player party

speaker: Chuundar
text: Ah, brother Zaalbar. You've been exiled a long time. You shouldn't speak in that tone. Things are different now.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are a mad-claw without honor. You have no voice among your own people. I, on the other hand, am Chieftain.

speaker: Player
text: If you've made deals with slavers, the truth will get out eventually.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You may talk, but no one will believe you. I've had a long time to guide what my people think.

speaker: Chuundar
text: They trust me, the mighty Chuundar. Even with my brother insane and father enslaved, I rose to protect my people despite it all.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Father was enslaved? "Mighty Chuundar?" What are you talking about? You were the runt!

speaker: Chuundar
text: I am no runt! *ahem* Like I said, Zaalbar, a lot has changed in your years away. We will discuss this soon enough.

speaker: Player
text: What do you want? Why drag us here?

speaker: Chuundar
text: I haven't killed Zaalbar because he is my brother, and I hoped he and I could come to an agreement. You are irrelevant.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I may be able to put you to use on a menial task. Zaalbar will have to stay here, of course.

speaker: Player
text: What is this task?

speaker: Chuundar
text: A simple thing. Another Wookiee has suffered the same fate as Zaalbar, gone mad and been exiled. He now lurks the Shadowlands.

speaker: Chuundar
text: More importantly, he's pestering my Czerka allies during their Shadowland expeditions. It is not good for business.

speaker: Player
text: He's standing against you. The first of many, perhaps?

speaker: Chuundar
text: No one will follow a mad-claw. He is merely a nuisance. Besides, he cowers in the Shadowlands. My people know nothing of him.

speaker: Player
text: I won't do this. Do your own dirty work.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You don't have much choice. You can flee the planet if you want, but I am keeping Zaalbar here with me.

speaker: Chuundar
text: He'll stay until the mad-claw is dead. The Czerka would never let me hold you, but they don't care what I do with fellow Wookiees.

speaker: Mission
text: You can't do that! He can't do that, can he? He can't hold Zaalbar prisoner just because he's Chieftain, can he?

speaker: Player
text: Keeping Zaalbar makes this proposition even worse.

speaker: Chuundar
text: What made you think I wanted this to be easy for you? Besides, you won't need him. My people are trained to understand you.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I tell them it's to better understand the enemy. They think it will make the Czerka easier to fight. Actually it makes them easier to obey.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Remember, you can't beat me here. No one would dare oppose me to join with an outsider or an exile.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You are wrong, brother. Someone would.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you talking about, Zaalbar?

speaker: Chuundar
text: Do you speak of Freyyr, our father? Why? He was the one that ordered you exiled when you attacked me.

speaker: Chuundar
text: He went as mad as you when he finally discovered the slavers. He dared challenge them alone and has not been seen since.

speaker: Chuundar
text: That was years ago. Let him go, Zaalbar. I rule now. I'll take the Wookiees forward, but there are prices to pay.

speaker: Player
text: He makes sense, Zaalbar. Perhaps you should listen to him.

speaker: Chuundar
text: No more words, outsider. I've given my orders. I can't hold you here, but Zaalbar will stay until you kill the mad-claw in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Mission
text: Don't worry, buddy, we'll get you out of here. You can count on us!

speaker: Chuundar
text: The guards will let you pass now. Leave the village through the northwest and follow the platform to the south and then east.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You'll eventually see where Gorwooken waits for you. He'll lower you to the forest floor. Go.

speaker: Bastila
text: Then I suppose we have little choice. We should proceed with caution, however.

speaker: Carth
text: I don't like leaving someone behind, but I guess we don't have a choice.

speaker: Juhani
text: It is wrong to leave him imprisoned here. We should seek some way to free him when we have the chance.

speaker: HK47
text: Query: Shall I begin blasting, master? We could have your hirsute companion free in no time.

speaker: Player
text: Not yet, HK.

speaker: Cand
text: Let's go kill something and get the Wookiee out.

speaker: Player
text: Don't listen, Zaalbar. It's not worth it.

speaker: Player
text: Play along, Zaalbar. I will see what I can do.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah Zaalbar, you and me!

speaker: Chuundar
text: No outsider, Zaalbar is referring to Freyyr, our father. Why, Zaalbar? He ordered you exiled when you attacked me.

speaker: Player
text: You see, Chuundar, there *is* someone. Uh... make it good, Zaalbar.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are too quick to celebrate. Zaalbar talks of Freyyr, our father. Why, Zaalbar? He ordered you exiled when you attacked me.

speaker: Player
text: I need Zaalbar with me as a guide.

speaker: Chuundar
text: No, you won't need him to find your way. Over the years I have had my people trained to understand galactic Basic.

speaker: Player
text: I'll consider what you've said. I'll go now.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I'll allow you access to the Shadowlands. You will track and kill this insane Wookiee, and maybe then you will earn my favor.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Zaalbar stays here to ensure your loyalty. The Czerka would never let me hold you, but they don't care what I do with fellow Wookiees.

speaker: Player
text: You're a fool. You're making the job harder.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about the Shadowlands.

speaker: Chuundar
text: We only enter the Shadowlands for ritual hunting. I'd leave the troublemaker down there but he has proven too good at surviving.

speaker: Chuundar
text: He has managed to linger a number of years, cowering in his madness and shame. You are expendable. You will remove him.

speaker: Player
text: I'm only interested in what I'm looking for. A Star Map.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I don't know anything about something like that, and I don't care. Your concerns are nothing to me.

speaker: Player
text: What happened with you and Zaalbar? Give me your version.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Zaalbar didn't tell you? He took offense to my trading a few of our people for favors and weapons.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I didn't understand his objection. Imagine the destruction if Czerka Corporation had come in with blasters firing. I saved many lives.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Of course, I also gained weapons, and arranged for certain rivals to be taken. I protected my allies, and my power grew.

speaker: Player
text: Which explains why the Wookiees in this room haven't killed you.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Each has come to understand the benefit of working with the enemy. Unlike your exiled companion.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Young Zaalbar had no foresight. He couldn't control his outrage. He attacked me with his claws and damned himself doing it.

speaker: Chuundar
text: A few careful stories and everyone called him mad-claw. Even father Freyyr. I easily had him exiled.

speaker: Player
text: You've a complete lack of remorse for your actions. Like a big hairy Hutt.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I've heard of these Hutt creatures. They sound like smart traders. They would understand what your exiled companion could not.

speaker: Player
text: I would not abandon Zaalbar to you.

speaker: Chuundar
text: It isn't your choice, <FirstName>. I already have him. I have a personal matter to discuss with him. You have other duties.

speaker: Player
text: Is there a point to this? If this will only lead to a fight, I'd like to get to it.

speaker: Chuundar
text: There will be no fight. You wouldn't survive. The village believes in me. They would rise to kill you.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I also have the protection of Czerka Corporation guards as well. No, you have no chance while I am unopposed.

speaker: Player
text: A nice nest of lies you have constructed.

speaker: Player
text: Ignore him, Chuundar. You are dealing with me now.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are mistaken about your worth. You have no leverage here. I have made certain that my people only listen to me.

speaker: Player
text: And I am Darth Revan! You will listen to me, Chuundar.

speaker: Chuundar
text: You expect me to believe that, <FullName>? Even here on Kashyyyk we have heard the tale of how the Lord of the Sith was killed by the Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I wasn't killed, I was only captured. Now Revan has returned - and you don't want to get on my bad side!

speaker: Chuundar
text: [Success] There is something strange about you... a darkness I can smell in your scent. Maybe you are one of the Sith. Maybe you are even Darth Revan, as you claim.

speaker: Chuundar
text: But what do I care about Sith and Jedi? Czerka are the only outsiders here on Kashyyyk. And the mighty Chuundar does not bow down, even to them!

speaker: Chuundar
text: You are mistaken about your worth, Revan. You have no leverage here. I have all the power, and I have made certain that my people only listen to me.

speaker: Mission
text: Big Z! What are you doing here? What's going on?

speaker: Chuundar
text: As you can see, <FullName>, I have brought Zaalbar from your ship. Don't worry, Janos was very helpful. There was no damage done... yet.
comment: Zaalbar was NOT in the player party. Remove him from the player ship and place here.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about? How do you know me?

speaker: Chuundar
text: Did you think you could walk the upper boughs of Kashyyyk and not be observed? I've had climbers watching you, and your ship.

speaker: Player
text: Janos allowed it? You must work closely with him.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You work alongside the slavers. You are no better than they are!

speaker: Player
text: You had no right to enter my ship!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You have learned from the slavers. Learned to take what you want.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you think you had to do this behind my back?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: He has become like the slavers. He takes without care.

speaker: Player
text: I thought Zaalbar's presence might cause problems.

speaker: Chuundar
text: It has, but you couldn't hide him. Your ship carries his scent, his hair. My climbers found him quickly. Others have been watching you.

speaker: Player
text: I demand an explanation! You don't want me to get angry!

speaker: Chuundar
text: You need to realize your situation. I've had climbers watching you since you landed. Taking Zaalbar was easy.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Well, my mercenary returns. My climbers tell me you did well, <FullName>, although they couldn't follow you the whole time.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Chuundar told me who the mad-claw was. Have you done it then? Have you... killed my father?

speaker: Player
text: Freyyr was your father? I didn't know that.

speaker: Chuundar
text: I avoided his name when I sent you after him, but the pompous old wook must have said something!

speaker: Chuundar
text: You're an inattentive fool if you truly didn't know, but it doesn't matter. Zaalbar has begun to see my side of things.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I've been reminded of how Freyyr cast me out. I see how easily he has been disposed of, himself. We are stronger without him. Chuundar's way is better.

speaker: Chuundar
text: Of course it is. I will make our people strong with outsider weapons and influence. And for you, I shall see that your status is restored... in due time.

speaker: Player
text: Yes. It had to be done. Move forward.

speaker: Chuundar
text: So you did it for Zaalbar's well-being? It's possible, but it doesn't matter. Zaalbar has begun to see my side of things.

speaker: Player
text: I butchered him. Is there a problem?

speaker: Chuundar
text: Not with me, and I doubt Zaalbar will give you any trouble for it. He's coming around to my way of thinking.

speaker: Player
text: I wasn't offered much alternative.

speaker: Chuundar
text: That is true. I would have killed you. Besides, the old wook's time is done. Zaalbar has begun to see my side of things.

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: Those Vulkars are dumber than a Coruscant granite slug! They actually think being in that pathetic little gang of theirs makes them important.

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: Gadon keeps his hidden Beks in line, but Brejik's getting dreams of grandeur. If Davik's smart, he'll slap that young punk back down.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: I'm someone you don't want to get on the bad side of, and I'm not one for small talk.

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: Besides, you know the arrangement. You Sith don't interfere with Davik's business and you all get a nice cut of his action.

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: I don't have time to stick around here, anyway. Davik's got me working on a special assignment.

speaker: Player
text: I need to ask you some questions.

speaker: Canderous Ordo
text: Sorry, but I don't usually volunteer information to anyone who just asks.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Bastila isn't in the mood to talk right now - not with enemies so close by.]

speaker: Bastila
text: You will have to disable the energy shield around this temple before we can leave. There is a computer here on the Temple summit that has access to the power generators.

speaker: Bastila
text: You can also use it to disable the disruptor field that protects the Star Forge. Otherwise, the Ebon Hawk will not be able to leave the planet without crashing.

speaker: Bastila
text: With each passing moment your old apprentice becomes stronger, Master. We must act quickly to exact your vengeance. Malak will pay for stealing the mantle of Dark Lord from you!

speaker: Bastila
text: If you have questions, you should direct them towards the Jedi Council members.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Star Forge is under assault from the entire Republic fleet! If I don't use my Battle Meditation to turn the tide, Admiral Dodonna's capital ships will destroy the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: I have to stay here in the command center so that I can best use my Battle Meditation against our enemy. If I don't the Star Forge will be lost!

speaker: Bastila
text: You must go to face Malak without me. Find him, kill him and reclaim the title of Dark Lord of the Sith!

speaker: Bastila
text: I know we have not spoken often during our time together, despite my best efforts. And to this point I have respected your privacy. But there is something we must discuss.
comment: romance is dead at this point

speaker: Player
text: Fine. What is it?

speaker: Bastila
text: You must prepare yourself for when we face Malak. The confrontation will be difficult for you. I remember how hard it was when I first faced Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Is it true you killed Darth Revan?

speaker: Bastila
text: It's true that, due to my Battle Meditation, I was with the Jedi strike team that boarded Revan's ship. We did not kill Revan, however.

speaker: Player
text: That's not what I heard.

speaker: Bastila
text: Our mission was to capture Revan, if possible. It was Malak who turned on his own master, firing upon Revan's ship while we were still on board it.

speaker: Bastila
text: It was his desire to kill us and his master both. Thankfully we narrowly escaped the vessel as it exploded.

speaker: Player
text: So Malak did your job for you.

speaker: Bastila
text: As I said, we were there to capture Revan alive. The Jedi do not believe in killing their prisoners. No one deserves execution, no matter what their crimes.

speaker: Bastila
text: Remember that Revan and Malak were once great Jedi. Heroes in every sense of the word. They demonstrate the danger of the dark side to us all.

speaker: Bastila
text: I'm sorry. We really shouldn't speak of this anymore. The memory of my confrontation with Revan is... painful. Let's return to the mission, please.

speaker: Player
text: What else did you expect from the Sith?

speaker: Bastila
text: True, I suppose. And yet the outcome of that battle was... unexpected. To all of us. Revan's end was... unforeseen.

speaker: Player
text: But you would have killed Revan eventually, right?

speaker: Player
text: But killing Revan is what you're famous for.

speaker: Player
text: So who killed Revan, then?

speaker: Player
text: Oh, great. I never get tired of hearing how you killed Darth Revan.

text: And once you stop resisting, it is too late. It twists you up inside and... and turns you into a mockery of everything you once stood for.

speaker: Player
text: You seem to know that temptation very well.

speaker: Bastila
text: I am no less resistant to temptation than any other. I simply have the benefit of training that you do not. But even the training of the Jedi might not be enough to save us.

speaker: Bastila
text: We need only to look at the atrocities which have been committed by those under its sway to understand the terrible, corrupting evil of the dark side.

speaker: Bastila
text: Millions dead, and far more suffering. What sort of person would you have to become to perform such deeds gladly?

speaker: Player
text: I couldn't see myself ever doing such things.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps it's just the reasoning for those acts you don't accept.

speaker: Bastila
text: And how adept must one become at making excuses for one's actions, if suffering is the result? How long before you stop making excuses at all?

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying the light side is innocent of killing?

speaker: Bastila
text: One who serves the light side does not strike down an innocent. We take arms against the dark side and the injustice that follows it only.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know.

speaker: Bastila
text: Neither do I, and I hope I never do.

speaker: Player
text: How can you know it is so terrible?

speaker: Player
text: Stop with the dramatics, already, I get the picture.

speaker: Bastila
text: You say you understand, but I'm afraid you are taking this too lightly. The power of the dark side can be... alluring.

speaker: Player
text: We're not going to go over this again, are we?

speaker: Bastila
text: We must, for all our sakes. If you had the proper training under a true Master you would know all this. But because of our mission, I must be the one to try and help you understand.

speaker: Bastila
text: I've seen you give in to temptation and indulge your baser emotions on many occasions. I'm afraid you are on the path that leads to the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: I won't misuse my power, Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: My progress?

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: Why did the Council send me with you on this mission?

speaker: Bastila
text: Why? I could not accomplish this on my own, I need the aid of others - especially one who is strong in the Force. The bond between us made you a natural choice.

speaker: Bastila
text: Besides, the events on Taris proved that the Force wanted to bring us together for this mission, and there is little left to chance when the Force is involved. Is that not enough for you?

speaker: Player
text: If the Force wants us to be together, why do you keep resisting my undeniable charms?

speaker: Bastila
text: I said we were brought together for our mission: to stop Malak. I hardly think the Force would be pushing us towards a romantic involvement when the fate of the galaxy is at stake!

speaker: Bastila
text: Please try to stay focused. I doubt the Council would approve if they knew we were busy discussing our mutual attraction when we should be saving the galaxy from Malak.

speaker: Player
text: Mutual attraction? I knew you were interested in me!

speaker: Bastila
text: Mutual attraction? I never said... it's just an expression! Whatever our feelings... uh, I mean... whatever *your* feelings, you have to try to ignore them. Don't let this complicate things.

speaker: Bastila
text: Finding the missing pieces of the Star Maps is our only hope of locating the Star Forge and defeating Malak. The Council explained all this quite clearly.

speaker: Player
text: It just seems odd they would send me off without a Master to guide me.

speaker: Bastila
text: I admit, there were times that I wondered if this is more than just a mission to stop Malak. There were times when I wondered if this was also a way for the Council to test my own abilities.

speaker: Player
text: I get the feeling that there's more going on than I know.

speaker: Bastila
text: I wondered if the Council wanted to see how I would help and guide you on our quest. I wondered if they were testing me to see if I was ready to become a Jedi Master myself.

speaker: Bastila
text: And then I realized how foolish such thoughts were. As the Council explained, sending a Master in our group would only have drawn unwanted attention from the Sith.

speaker: Bastila
text: The fate of the galaxy is at stake, the Council would not risk it merely to test me. They calculated the risks and in the end chose the only option available.

speaker: Player
text: I guess that makes sense.

speaker: Bastila
text: You must learn to trust in the wisdom of the Council. Your destiny will come in its appointed time. You mustn't be so impatient.

speaker: Player
text: Me? You're the one who thought this was her big audition for 'Masterhood'!

speaker: Bastila
text: *Must* you be so frustrating? I admit, I had a moment of foolish pride. But I'm over it. Now I am focused on my true responsibilities.

speaker: Bastila
text: I am simply trying to help you and complete this mission, and yet you battle me at every turn!

speaker: Player
text: What can I say? It's fun.

speaker: Bastila
text: Fun?! Fun?! Driving me insane is your idea of a good time?

speaker: Player
text: Careful. Remember your self-control.

speaker: Bastila
text: You... you are a very odd man, do you know that? I simply don't know how to deal with you. All I want to do is help you, but you seem determined to drive me mad.

speaker: Player
text: Complain all you want, but I know you love it.

speaker: Bastila
text: I don't know if I should be outraged that you keep joking about serious matters, or if I should be grateful that you can always lighten the mood.

speaker: Bastila
text: Come on, come, let's move on... there's much to be done.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not so bad. You just have to learn to accept me for what I am.

speaker: Bastila
text: Unfortunately it isn't as easy as that. But your point is well taken.

speaker: Bastila
text: I must admit: I simply don't know how to deal with someone like you.

text: Hey, you started this.

speaker: Player
text: You're right. I suppose we should get back to the mission now.

speaker: Player
text: I'm still not convinced.

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila
text: I do. I have been trying to come up with the best way to say this for some time, but I suppose I should just come out and say it.

text: I know my manner can be a bit taciturn. I know you must be getting sick of my lectures about the dark side and... and everything else.

text: I spent all my years being hounded by my instructors. Being told so often how gifted and important I was until I was sick of it.

text: I remember when I was younger I used to swear that I would never become as self-absorbed and stodgy as the Jedi Masters. It's ironic, really.

speaker: Bastila
text: But enough soul searching for now. We should probably continue on with our mission.

speaker: Player
text: Great, you've had your say. Now leave me alone - for good!

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player
text: Then leave me alone. For good.

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: Just leave me alone... for good.

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: Thank you. I appreciate the gesture.

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: You're curious about something?

speaker: Bastila

text: I've always struggled for control over my passions. I've always been too quick to anger, too quick to get involved. My instructors constantly berated me for it.

text: I've often dreamed that I might be able to confront Darth Malak myself. I dream I can use all this power I have to kill him and stop all the death and destruction.

speaker: Player

text: I don't know. Would the power I used to kill Darth Malak be too tempting to keep using? Would I become the kind of evil I want to destroy?

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player
text: I think destroying that kind of evil would be worth it.

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player
text: You have to trust in the wisdom of the Jedi Code.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, of course. You're right. I... I have to remember my training. The Masters know well the corrupting influence of the dark side, although it is hard for me to imagine.

speaker: Player
text: It sounds like you have your own demons to face.

speaker: Bastila
text: I suppose I do. Part of me thinks that it would be worth anything to vanquish evil, even if it meant giving in to my base emotions.

speaker: Player
text: Life's too short to be afraid.

speaker: Bastila
text: Is it? The thought of what could happen to me if I lose control... somehow I think life could be very long, indeed.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe a little, sure.

speaker: Bastila
text: That... that's a relief to hear. That you would even be willing to risk so much is... is very brave. Braver than I could be.

speaker: Bastila
text: In our time together I've been watching you. You are a true servant of the light, you follow the tenets of the Jedi Order despite the lure of the dark side. And with so little training.

speaker: Bastila
text: For me it has always been a constant battle. Don't you find it difficult at all? You make it seem so easy. Or is that only an illusion?

speaker: Player
text: I just do what I think is right.

speaker: Bastila
text: And that's enough for you? If only it were as easy for me. If only the right path was always clear.

speaker: Player
text: It's a struggle for me, sometimes.

speaker: Bastila
text: That's a relief to hear. I have never found the Jedi path an easy one to walk, and it's good to know I'm not alone.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think about it much.

speaker: Bastila
text: You don't? Sometimes I find that it is nearly all I can think of. I have never found the Jedi training easy to master.

speaker: Player
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to talk about what you said before. About giving in to your emotions.

speaker: Bastila
text: Part of my purpose on this mission was to guide you in the way of the light; to help you avoid the temptations of the dark side. But I fear I've failed in that task.

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player
text: Why do you say that?

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Bastila
text: I simply hope that you are not the one who pays the price, ultimately, for the fact that I can't help you enough.

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player
text: We're made for each other, Bastila. You have to see that.

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I need time to think about all this. Things are... they are not going as I thought they would.

speaker: Bastila
text: We should... we should continue on with our mission, for now.

speaker: Player
text: How did you expect me to be?

speaker: Bastila
text: Well, just... different, I suppose. Things are not going as I thought they would. I... I need time to think about all this.

speaker: Bastila
text: Perhaps you can help me. And I will try to help you, if I can. Hopefully this will all work out, for the both of us. And for the sake of the mission.

speaker: Player
text: You're being too hard on yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I don't need your help, anyway. I can find my own way.

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Bastila
text: Fair enough. You will probably be better off on your own, in any case. I won't trouble you with this anymore.

speaker: Player
text: You're doing your best, I'm sure.

speaker: Bastila
text: That is kind of you to say, but I think the evidence speaks for itself. I think... I think I may have made a very big mistake.

text: Oh? You see that, too? I don't need you anymore.

speaker: Bastila
text: You have maintained the path of the light side. But it has been in spite of my influence, not because of it. It is increasingly obvious I am unable to guide you properly.

speaker: Player
text: No, I disagree!

speaker: Bastila
text: Perhaps you are not being truly objective, then. There is no need to spare my feelings on this point.

speaker: Player
text: Oh, get over yourself, already.

speaker: Bastila
text: Please don't make light of this. The very fact that I am plagued by this doubt is yet further evidence of my inadequacy.

speaker: Player
text: When we last talked you said you needed time to think. So?

text: Manaan is a water world inhabited by an aquatic race known as the Selkath. Their only surface city and spaceport is called Ahto.

speaker: Bastila
text: It is unique in that the Selkath are firm in their neutrality. They are neither part of the republic nor controlled by the Sith, and they wish to keep it that way.

speaker: Bastila
text: Tatooine is a dry planet that has not been inhabited long and has little law. This town of Anchorhead may be its only settlement.

speaker: Bastila
text: Kashyyyk is a planet where most of what you see is actually foliage that has grown to enormous heights. No one has ever been to the true surface of the planet below.

speaker: Bastila
text: Korriban is a sparsely populated planet controlled by the Sith. It feels... wrong. There is an old evil here that permeates the Force.

speaker: Bastila
text: We can't risk having any of the dark Jedi Masters recognize me. For the sake of the mission I must remain hidden in the Ebon Hawk while we are on this world.

speaker: Bastila
text: There's nothing I could say that would be helpful, I'm afraid.

speaker: Player
text: So do you feel better now?

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes. That brought me a lot of peace. More than I thought it would have.

speaker: Bastila
text: Thank you for urging me towards it. After all my training, I would have thought it would have been easier. Apparently I still have much to learn.

speaker: Player
text: So you kept the holocron.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, but I don't feel any better. After all my training, I would have thought myself above such anger.

speaker: Bastila
text: For it to come so easily disturbs me greatly. I don't need a holocron to remember my father, and I will never see Mother again.

speaker: Bastila
text: Have I learned nothing? It... no, I don't want to talk about this. Thank you, but I must think about what I have done.

speaker: Player
text: [Don't speak to her.]

speaker: Bastila
text: [You decide to ignore Bastila and continue on with your quest for now, though you might want to speak with her later.]

speaker: Bastila
text: I am confident that you can deal with that on your own.

speaker: Bastila
text: I wish I could help you with that.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* The Force should not be used for profit and personal gain. As Jedi we should be above such things.

speaker: Bastila
text: It troubles me to see you behaving this way. Such acts can lead to the dark side.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* The Force is not a thing to be trifled with. Continue to use it frivolously and you may find yourself straying down the dark path.

speaker: Bastila
text: We should guard and protect those weaker than ourselves... not bully and exploit them!

speaker: Bastila
text: That was beneath you. I hope in the future you will strive to be better than this.

speaker: Bastila
text: That was a truly noble act. The Jedi Council would be pleased.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: The second tomb on the left within the valley is the tomb of Naga Sadow. It is off-limits to all students, unless they are in the company of Master Uthar.
comment: if selected by the player, player is part of the Sith

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: Beware of the tuk'ata. They are a pack beast that have their nests in one of the tombs. We fight them off as best we can.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: There is an old Sith hermit that has been haunting this area, we understand. Watch out for him.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: A dangerous assassin droid has barricaded itself within the tomb of Marka Ragnos, the first one on the left. Be wary.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: Watch out for the tuk'ata. They will charge you on sight. Run back to the excavation area and we can protect you.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: Any artifacts found should be brought to the attention of Master Uthar immediately.

speaker: Sith Patrol
text: I am not here to get you out of trouble if you do something stupid, student. Enter the tombs at your own risk.

speaker: Phirk
text: You're pretty good, rookie. That was an impressive time you ran there.

speaker: Phirk
text: But Anglu's better than any of you Vulkar riders. That last time she posted is going to win this thing for the Beks!

speaker: Phirk
text: It might have stood up if it wasn't for Redros running the race of his life. Now we're all counting on you to get out there and beat his new time. You can't let the Vulkars win!

speaker: Phirk
text: Watch yourself out on the track, rookie. Every year we lose a couple of you first timers.

speaker: Phirk
text: It'd be a real shame if the Vulkars lost their newest rider because of one careless mistake. Yeah, that'd be a real shame.

speaker: Phirk
text: We Beks are losing enough members as it is without having them die on the track. Just be careful... and good luck.

speaker: Phirk
text: I saw you out on the track. You're going to have to do better than that if you want to collect the champion's prize.

speaker: Phirk
text: Anglu and Redros are the best riders out here, but with a little luck I think I can beat them this year.

speaker: Vorn Daasraad
text: What this? What going on here? What you doing with my assault droid?

speaker: Player
text: I've reprogrammed your droid, Vorn.

speaker: Vorn Daasraad
text: Turn my own droid against me - very clever. But it take more than rogue assault droid and you to take down Vorn Daasraad!

speaker: Player
text: If you surrender now I'll let you live.

speaker: Player
text: I'm going to enjoy killing you, Vorn!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You Republic people are so pathetic, sitting around grovelling at the tablescraps the galactic senators deign to give you. It makes me sick.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: The senators work for the good of the whole galaxy, not for individual gain!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Ha! Don't make me laugh, you gutless simp! It's the destiny of weak-minded fools like you to be ruled over by the strong, like we Sith!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: I'm warning you! Don't push me, or you'll get just what you're asking for!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Try it. Just try it. I'd love to see you throw the first punch. And with all the cameras around the Selkath would be all over you inside of 30 seconds.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You break their laws, you pay the price, Republic scum. But I can see that you're not man enough to back up your words anyway.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: If you ever feel like relieving yourself of your worthless existence, feel free to come by our enclave here. We have many, many ways to fulfill your wish.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: *grrr*

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You Republics make me sick. It's a good thing there are cameras all over the place on Manaan, or they'd have droids cleaning you up off the walls by now.

speaker: Bastila
text: Well, maybe those bloody Vulkars will think twice next time before trying to keep a Jedi prisoner! And as for you, if you think you can collect me as a prize...
comment: Bastila will init dialog with PC as soon as all Vulkars are dead Dialog has only one outcome - Bastila joins party and teleports with player to the base

speaker: Bastila
text: Wait... I don't believe this! You're... you're one of the soldiers with the Republic fleet, aren't you? Yes, I'm sure of it. How did you end up racing for these swoop gangs?

speaker: Player
text: My name's <FullName>. I'm here to save you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Save me? Is that what you were trying to accomplish by riding in that swoop race? Well, as far as rescues go this is a pretty poor example.

speaker: Bastila
text: In case you hadn't noticed, I managed to free myself from that neural restraint collar without your help. In fact, it's more accurate to say that I saved you!

speaker: Bastila
text: Brejik and his Vulkars would have left you for dead if I hadn't stepped into that fight. You're lucky I was here to get you out of this mess!

speaker: Player
text: I think you've got things confused. You were a helpless prisoner until I came along.

speaker: Bastila
text: I may have been a prisoner, but a Jedi is never helpless. Maybe you've heard of a little thing called 'the Force'?

speaker: Bastila
text: But I suppose I shouldn't be too hard on you. You did try to save me after all, even if it didn't go quite as planned. So let's get down to business - we're not out of danger yet.

speaker: Bastila
text: If I'm going to figure out a way for us to get off this planet I need to know what kind of resources we can draw on. First, are we the only two survivors left from the Endar Spire?

speaker: Player
text: Carth and I are already working on a plan to get off Taris.

speaker: Bastila
text: Carth Onasi is alive? Finally, some good news! Carth is one of the Republic's best soldiers. He's proved himself a hero a dozen times over! And he sent you here to save me?

speaker: Bastila
text: Maybe I misjudged you. Carth wouldn't have sent you if he wasn't confident in your... abilities. Forgive me - despite my Jedi training, I still tend to act a bit rashly sometimes.

speaker: Bastila
text: Please, take me to Carth right away. Between the three of us I'm sure we can figure out some way to get off this planet before the Sith realize we're here.

speaker: Player
text: We aren't the only survivors. Carth Onasi is alive as well.

speaker: Player
text: Hey, who said you were in charge here?

speaker: Bastila
text: The Republic, for one. I was fleet commander, remember? But I don't want you getting all worked up over nothing. So tell me - do you have a plan to get off this planet?

speaker: Player
text: No - but Carth and I will figure something out!

speaker: Player
text: I don't have a plan yet. Carth wanted to make sure you were safe first.

speaker: Player
text: I didn't need your help with those Vulkars. I can handle myself!

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, I suppose you can. Well, I appreciate your attempt to save me - even if it didn't really go as you planned. But let's get down to business - we're not out of danger yet.

speaker: Player
text: We don't have time for this. Carth is waiting for us.

speaker: Player
text: It's a long story.

speaker: Bastila
text: Well we don't have time for it now. We have to get out of here before the Sith show up to sort out this mess. Is there somewhere safe we can go?

speaker: Player
text: I've got somewhere safe to go. I was planning to take you there after I saved you from Brejik.

speaker: Player
text: Whoa - slow down. I'm in charge here. Remember, I saved you!

speaker: Player
text: Winning the swoop race was the only way I could save you.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind that. I won the swoop race, and you're my prize. I own you now!

speaker: Bastila
text: You must have banked a turn too sharply, because it sounds like all the blood has rushed from your brain!

speaker: Bastila
text: I'm Bastila Shan, a member of the Jedi Order and a fleet commander for the Republic. Nobody 'owns' me! Now we don't have time for joking around. What are you doing here?

speaker: tar03_bastguard
text: No one's allowed to talk to the prisoner. Brejik's orders. She wouldn't hear you anyway: she's got a neural disruptor collar on to keep her under control.

speaker: Rukil
text: False prophet! Deceiver! You have betrayed me! You have sold the hope of the entire village to the selfish and damnable Igear!

speaker: Rukil
text: All I have worked for is destroyed! All the hopes and dreams of my father and grandfather before him turned to dust! Begone, up-worlder - I have only curses to speak at you!

speaker: Rukil
text: You return, up-worlder. Are you ready to learn what you must learn? Are you ready to learn of the Promised Land?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Promised Land.

speaker: Rukil
text: Legends tell of a self-sufficient colony founded just before the famine and lost during the civil war; a paradise beneath the Undercity where droid servants tend to every need.

speaker: Rukil
text: For many years I searched for the Promised Land, just as my grandfather and father did before me. When I became old and gray my apprentice continued the search on my behalf.

speaker: Carth
text: Sounds like a myth to me. Something to give the people here some false hope to cling to so they don't go mad with despair.

speaker: Rukil
text: I have collected many clues hinting at its location; the journal of my apprentice provides yet more information. But still there are too many pieces missing from this puzzle.

speaker: Rukil
text: But I know my father and grandfather each had journals where they recorded their own discoveries. Perhaps with their journals I could at last uncover its hidden location.

speaker: Player
text: I have all three journals. Here - take them.

speaker: Rukil
text: Can it be true? Is it possible that at long last the dream of my father and grandfather before him will be fulfilled? I... I can hardly bear to look.

speaker: Rukil
text: Hmmm... yes. Yes! Of course! Now I understand - it all makes sense! Now I see why the Promised Land has been so hard to find! It is so obvious!

speaker: Rukil
text: You have done a great thing, up-worlder - a selfless act that will bring great joy to all the people of this village! I must take this to Gendar right away!

speaker: Gendar041
text: Rukil? What do you want now? Have you more fables of a hidden paradise just waiting for us to find it?

speaker: Rukil
text: You may not think these are fables after you see what I have brought you, Gendar! Look at these journals!

speaker: Gendar041
text: What... no. It can't be! Are these real, Rukil? Is this information accurate?

speaker: Rukil
text: I swear to you everything in these journals is true, Gendar. The Promised Land - I told you I would find it!

speaker: Gendar041
text: The entrance is far from here, Rukil. It will take us weeks to get there... perhaps even months. And we will have to cross many rakghoul infested areas.

speaker: Rukil
text: I do not deny the journey will be hard, Gendar. But surely it is better than the miserable life we have here!

speaker: Gendar041
text: Wise words, Rukil. Our supplies are high right now - we could leave by nightfall! I will tell the others to prepare for the journey.

speaker: Rukil
text: Thank you once again, up-worlder. I will say a final goodbye, for where we are going I fear you cannot come. The journey to the Promised Land is long and arduous.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye, Rukil - and good luck.

speaker: Rukil
text: We must part ways here, up-worlder. I sense your destiny is yet to be chosen, but the destiny of my people is at the end of the long journey ahead of us.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I should come with you. I could help you on the journey.

speaker: Rukil
text: No, up-worlder, I cannot ask that. The journey will take many, many weeks. And those who make the journey cannot return - that was the final secret of the Promised Land.

speaker: Rukil
text: When the colony was created it was designed so that people could enter willingly, but they could never leave again. This was to ensure secrecy on the project.

speaker: Player
text: I have one of the journals you're looking for.
comment: Player has 1 or 2 journals, but NOT all 3

speaker: Rukil
text: Yes, up-worlder... well done. However, I see that this journal alone does not have enough clues for me to solve this mystery. Too many pieces are still missing.

speaker: Rukil
text: I'm afraid that only with all three journals - my grandfather's, my father's and my apprentice's - will I be able to discover the location of the Promised Land.

speaker: Rukil
text: I will leave this journal with you for safe keeping for now. Perhaps it will aid you in your search for the others. I wish you luck, up-worlder - for the sake of the entire village.

speaker: Player
text: And you want me to find these missing journals?

speaker: Rukil
text: I have nothing to offer if you help me in this. I hope the knowledge that you are helping the entire village escape a life of darkness and suffering is reward enough.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry, Rukil. I'll find those journals.

speaker: Rukil
text: It is many decades since my father set out on his journey, but I remember he was eager to explore the sewers. You might want to begin your search there.

speaker: Rukil
text: I wish you luck in your quest, up-worlder. The future survival of this village - of my people - depends on you.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, I need an actual reward if you want my help.

speaker: Rukil
text: I see. Well, perhaps you are not the savior I seek after all. I can only pray that if you find the journals you will have a change of heart and bring them to me.

speaker: Player
text: What will I get if I find these missing journals for you?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not wasting my time looking for these journals!

speaker: Rukil
text: Please, up-worlder - I am too old to search for the missing journals myself, and the other villagers think the Promised Land is nothing but a myth.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in this.

speaker: Rukil
text: I offer you wisdom and you turn me away? Perhaps you are not ready to accept the role you must play in the destiny and salvaton of my people.

speaker: Rukil
text: Very well, up-worlder. Return to me when you are ready to learn what you must learn.

speaker: Rukil
text: You return, up-worlder. Are you ready now to learn what you must learn? Are you ready to hear the history of my people?

speaker: Player
text: Very well - tell me the history of your people.

speaker: Rukil
text: The great city of Taris covers the entire surface of this planet. There is no land to grow food. Kelp harvests and the creatures of the sea are our only food source.

speaker: Rukil
text: A century ago rising levels of toxic pollution poisoned the oceans and famine swept the planet. The rich hoarded food for their own use, and the poor were left to starve and die.

speaker: Carth
text: From what I've seen of Taris, it doesn't look like much has changed. Except for the Upper City, people here are just as bad off as the poor in your little history.

speaker: Rukil
text: But the poor rose up against this tyranny and civil war engulfed the planet. Millions died in the fighting and huge sections of Taris were destroyed or abandoned.

speaker: Rukil
text: The rebellion was crushed in the end, thousands were taken prisoner. The jails could not hold them all, and so the practice of banishing all prisoners to the Undercity was born.

speaker: Player
text: Is that how you came to be down here?

speaker: Rukil
text: Many brave men and women were banished here to the Undercity for their part in the rebellion. People like my father and grandfather were cast down, along with their families.

speaker: Mission
text: What did you expect? If they could get away with it the Tarisian nobles would stuff their own mothers down here to make more room in the Upper City.

speaker: Rukil
text: Now we live a dark existence beneath the streets of Taris, a life devoid of all hope but one: the Promised Land. And you will be the one to show us the way to get there.

speaker: Player
text: The Promised Land? What's that?

speaker: Player
text: How can I lead you to this Promised Land when I don't even know what it is?

speaker: Player
text: What does this have to do with me?

speaker: Player
text: Are you going to get to the point soon?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in the history of your people.

speaker: Rukil
text: Welcome back, up-worlder. How goes your quest? Have you found the journals of my father and grandfather?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have all the journals yet, but I will find them.

speaker: Player
text: I can't waste any more time with your quest.

speaker: Rukil
text: You - you come from the world above! Is this the time of destiny, then? Is this a portent of the salvation of my people? Or merely another false sign to mislead us from the path?

speaker: Rukil
text: Are you the herald of prophecy? The beacon to guide us through the darkness? Or are you merely another harbinger of shattered dreams and unfulfilled promises?

speaker: Mission
text: Watch yourself: this guy's star chart is missing a few galaxies, if you know what I mean.

speaker: Bastila
text: This old man's demeanor may seem crazed, but I sense there is a purpose behind it, a benevolent one. He is no danger to us.

speaker: Rukil
text: Speak to me, up-worlder! Tell me what fate you unleash upon us - salvation or damnation! Speak, up-worlder - I beg you!

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about, old man?

speaker: Rukil
text: A question. You are uncertain. Bewildered. Perplexed. Understandable, I suppose. Even after a hundred years of life I myself still become confused at times.

speaker: Rukil
text: Perhaps I can make things more clear. Some things, at least. My name is Rukil, the oldest Outcast here in the village. Rukil Wrinkle-Skin, the children call me sometimes.

speaker: Player
text: I'm <FullName>. What do you want from me, Rukil?

speaker: Rukil
text: Once I was honored for my wisdom, but over time the villagers fell away from the true path. Eventually there was only a single apprentice who followed me - and now she is gone, too.

speaker: Player
text: The true path? What does that mean?

speaker: Rukil
text: No, no, no. Not yet. I must be wary. Careful. You may be a false savior. Dare I share my secrets with you? No... not until you prove yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Prove myself? How can I do that?

speaker: Rukil
text: My apprentice is... lost. I sent her out into the Undercity to find... well, I cannot tell you. Not yet. Sadly, my apprentice has not returned.

speaker: Rukil
text: Please, up-worlder - will you help an old man? Will you seek out my apprentice in the Undercity? Her name is Malya. I must know of her fate, whatever it may be. I must know what she... found.

speaker: Player
text: Your apprentice is dead. I have her journal.

speaker: Rukil
text: It is as I feared, then. She joins the list of those who have given their lives in the service of our cause. But though I am saddened by this news, there is yet hope.

speaker: Rukil
text: By finding my apprentice you have proved yourself worthy, up-worlder. You are to be the beacon on our path to salvation. You will guide us to the Promised Land!

speaker: Player
text: Guide you? But I don't even know where the Promised Land is!

speaker: Rukil
text: You are marked, up-worlder - even my dim old eyes can see the mantle of destiny that cloaks you. Perhaps old Rukil knows you better than you know yourself.

speaker: Rukil
text: I am old - I have lived a hundred years in the Undercity, cast down into the darkness. I know the legends and history of our people - and now you must learn it, too.

speaker: Player
text: I think you have me confused with someone else.

speaker: Player
text: Hold on a second - I'm not guiding anybody anywhere!

speaker: Player
text: I will help you with this, Rukil.

speaker: Rukil
text: Finding her may be difficult; Malya could be anywhere in the Undercity... but if you find her I will know you to be our true savior! Only then can I reveal my secret knowledge to you.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back if I find anything out.

speaker: Rukil
text: I wish you luck, up-worlder. Come speak to me again once you have discovered the fate of my apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going to waste my time looking for your apprentice!

speaker: Rukil
text: Then... perhaps you are not the one I have been waiting for. Should you change your mind, up-worlder, speak with me again. Come to me if you learn the fate of my apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: What will you give me if I help you?

speaker: Player
text: Forget it, old man. I'm not interested.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this nonsense.

speaker: Rukil
text: Please, a moment up-worlder. I must know if you are the one I have been waiting for. Please, I beg for your help.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, enough of this. So long, you crazy freak.

speaker: Player
text: What happened to your apprentice?

speaker: Player
text: Get to the point, old man!

speaker: Player
text: Uh... okay, then. Could I ask you some questions?

speaker: Player
text: You're obviously an insane old kook.

speaker: Rukil
text: Old, yes. But not insane. Oh no, not insane at all! I am as rational as any man can be after a hundred years in the filth and darkness of the Undercity!

speaker: Carth
text: Be careful... this one might be crazy enough to be dangerous.

speaker: Rukil
text: Greetings once more, up-worlder. Do you bring news of my apprentice? Have you discovered her fate, and proved yourself to be a true savior of my people?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Rukil
text: You seek my wisdom, but I dare not share my knowledge with you. Not yet. Not until you prove yourself to be the one foretold, the one who will guide us to salvation.

speaker: Rukil
text: Find my apprentice. Discover what fate has befallen her and I will know you are worthy, and not another false prophet sent to mislead my people!

speaker: Player
text: I haven't found her yet, but I will.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You Republics sicken me! We'll do the galaxy a favor by wiping you out!

speaker: Pilot
text: Nice to see you again. Hold onto that Hawk... it'll do well by you.

speaker: Pilot
text: Greetings, friend. Fellow pilot, are you? Wouldn't mind taking a spin in the Ebon Hawk, myself. Sleek ship, that one.
comment: when first selected when talked to, the PC initiates a dialogue with the pilots 1 & 3. There is only one path out of the initial dialogue.

speaker: Player
text: Does everyone here know about the Ebon Hawk?

speaker: Pilot
text: In a small colony like this, everyone knows everyone's business.

speaker: Pilot
text: It's better than thinking too much about all the Sith lurking about, here.

speaker: Pilot
text: The Hawk's been in and out of here for ages. An out-of-the-way starport is a good place for, uh... privateers. Not saying you are one.

speaker: Player
text: And what if I am?

speaker: Pilot
text: Wouldn't make any difference to me. Just wish I had a ship like that, myself. Business is steady here with the Sith, but it's a boring haul.

speaker: Pilot
text: In case you're forgetting, partner, they don't exactly want us talking about their business.

speaker: Pilot
text: Ah, who cares about them? I've seen some of those things they're digging up in those ruins in the valley. Pretty creepy, if you ask me.

speaker: Player
text: What have they been digging up?

speaker: Pilot
text: Weird artifacts. Looks like alien stuff. Maybe aliens lived on Korriban a long time ago, who knows?

speaker: Pilot
text: Don't be stupid. I was talking to one of those Sith and he said there are tombs there dating back to when the Sith were here in ancient times.

speaker: Pilot
text: There were Sith here in ancient times? Sounds like he was feeding you a line. Korriban's only been settled for a short time.

speaker: Pilot
text: So says you. He said that the planet was settled by the Sith a long time ago, and then they all left or something. Those tombs are really important to them.

speaker: Pilot
text: Tombs, hey? That makes the stuff they send us even creepier. Wish I didn't have to haul it around.

speaker: Player
text: Where do you take these things?

speaker: Pilot
text: We used to haul everything to Taris, and the Sith would take it off our hands there. Not sure where we'll be bringing it now.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have any of these artifacts, now?

speaker: Pilot
text: No. We're not due for another shipment for at least another week.

speaker: Player
text: How would one get to these excavations, exactly?

speaker: Pilot
text: It's in a valley on the surface, beyond some mountains to the east. No land route... that's why they have us fly in.

speaker: Pilot
text: Shows what you know. The academy has a route through the mountain... that's how all their students get to the excavation site.

speaker: Pilot
text: Well, regardless, the Sith don't let anybody near that valley. Even when we land, they watch us like a Drayberian hawk and want us gone quickly.

speaker: Player
text: So no one could sneak into the valley by ship?

speaker: Pilot
text: Not a chance. You'd be better off sneaking through the academy, if you wanted to go to the valley.

speaker: Pilot
text: Hah! Now that'd be a sight to see.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Pilot
text: Sure thing. Good flying, friend.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not a smuggler, if that's what you mean.

speaker: Player
text: What kind of ship do you pilot?

speaker: Pilot
