text: Eh? Well, what do you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about this system.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well this gas giant here is Yavin, and it's got a whole bunch of moons around it. The only really interesting one is Yavin IV, though, and it's been pretty much picked clean.

speaker: Player
text: What was on Yavin IV?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: When Exar Kun started the Great Sith War 50 years ago, he used Yavin IV as a base, building a lot of his Sith temples there.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: When he lost, the Republic came and bombed the surface of the planet, destroying pretty much everything.

speaker: Player
text: 'Pretty much' everything?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well... you could still find a few things here and there on the surface. Some buried from the bombardment, some that look much, much older.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I've been there a bunch of times and found pretty much all there was to find. I took them back here and tinkered with them a bit, getting them up and working, or improving them.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I have a bunch you can look at if you're interested. Maybe... purchase?

speaker: Player
text: Sure, what do you have?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Yeah, I have a few things kicking around the place. Stuff the Trandoshans and smugglers have brought for me to look at, and a few things I've been making from parts.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They aren't cheap, though. They pay a lot for what I can make, and anything I sell to you I can't exactly sell to them, now can I?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But if you're willing to pay, I've got a few of my more advanced things you can look at. I'm always working on more, so you can check back some other time if I don't have what you want right now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Here, have a look.

speaker: Player
text: Not right now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Suit yourself. Anything else you want then?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about yourself.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Me? I'm nobody... doing nothing...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I've been in this system for over 50 years, before this station was even built.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I just sit around all day and tinker with this and that, trying out a few of my ideas.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you come here?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: This station is an old Republic supply depot from when they were fighting Exar Kun. Once they destroyed Yavin IV's surface, though, they didn't need it anymore.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Once they'd gone, I decided to move in and use the place myself. It's not very roomy, but I think it's turned out all right. And it's close to Yavin IV, where I got most of my parts.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Nobody comes here except the smugglers and Trandoshans anyway, so I get left alone the way I like it.

speaker: Player
text: Who are the Trandoshans?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: The Trandoshans? Mercenaries and bounty hunters... Scum, mostly. They look like big two-legged lizards.

speaker: Player
text: Oh. Sort of like Rodians.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: No! Nothing like Rodians! Trandoshans are ugly, disgusting creatures... but you'd never want to say that to their faces. Rip your head clean off, probably.

speaker: Player
text: Why are they here?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They found me here a couple years after the war ended. Usually they don't bargain with people they find alone in abandoned space stations, but we worked out a deal.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I'd give them a few of my more... applicable inventions at reasonable prices, and they'd keep me supplied with food and new materials.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: It's worked out well so far, for years really. With Davik gone, they've been getting ideas, though.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Anything else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: Do you have anything you'd be willing to sell me?

speaker: Player
text: Interested in a hand of Pazaak?
comment: if the player has already asked about pazaak

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Sure, if you want. You've already proven that I'm no match for you, but if you want a few free games just to play...
comment: if the player has won 10 games

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Sure, if you want. I don't play for small amounts, though, so if you want to play, it's for keeps.
comment: if the player hasnt won 10 games

speaker: Player
text: You don't happen to play Pazaak do you?
comment: if the player hasnt already asked about pazaak

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Pazaak? The card game? Actually I do.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: One of the aqualish smugglers who comes by here regularly likes to play a bunch, and I kind of picked up the habit from him.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I've actually gotten pretty good at it myself. I'll play you a couple rounds if you want. Be warned, though, I don't play for small amounts.

speaker: Player
text: Sure, let's play.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Right. This is going to be fun.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have a deck.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Hm... well I have a couple extras. I could sell you one for 100 credits. You want it?

speaker: Player
text: Here you go.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Thanks. Here's your deck. Now I'll show you how to play.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Give me the deck.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Success] Damn, I don't really need the money anyway. Here, take it.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now I'll show you how to play.

speaker: Player
text: Can I buy a Pazaak deck off you?
comment: if the player has asked, but still doesnt have a deck

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Sure, it'll be 100 credits.

speaker: Player
text: I think you have gizka loose...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Yeah I know... Some damn smugglers must have brought them and one escaped. Good luck trying to get them all, though. Those things breed like... like gizka!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: If you see any around, just squish the damn thing!

speaker: Player
text: What did those Trandoshans want?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They want me to give them more of my inventions... stuff that I haven't even finished working on yet!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Ever since Davik went down, the Exchange has been a non-factor in these parts. The Trandoshans are trying to muscle in on all the old Exchange businesses now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Maybe I can still work something out with them... Thank you for being here, though. It might have gone less... pleasantly if you hadn't shown up.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Is there something else you want?

speaker: Player
text: I'll be leaving now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Hm.. Well, suit yourself. I'll probably be here if you get back... Ha!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now it seems they might be trying for a power grab now that the Exchange is down... I don't know what's going to happen next, but it doesn't look good.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now all bets are off. I have a few supplies tucked away, but I can't stay here forever. I know they'll be back as well. But that's something to think about another time.

speaker: Player
text: What do they want with you?

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: Who are the smugglers?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Rodians, aqualish, Twi'leks, whatever... They all work an organization called the Exchange. You might have heard of them.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They run smuggling operations all over the galaxy. Weapons, slaves, whatever someone's willing to pay the price for.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They found my talents very useful.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Like the Trandoshans, they get me to patch up and upgrade what they bring, and pay me well for it. They also bring news and supplies.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have any gadgets you'd be willing to sell me?

speaker: Player
text: So you're from this system?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well... not exactly. See, I'm not as young as I look. Actually, I'm pretty old by most standards. I've been here since the war, really.

speaker: Player
text: Were you in the war?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: The Sith were building a whole lot of temples on Yavin IV by Exar Kun's order, and they needed people to build it for them... so they got slaves.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Most of the slaves were put to work on the buildings directly, but there are a lot of other things you need to make a planet a working base. Weapons, for instance.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: So they forced some Baragwin to work for them making weapons. You know Baragwin, right?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: And I was one of the ones working under the Baragwin. I guess you could say I had the talent for it. The Baragwin I worked for, he took me under his wing and made me his apprentice, even...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But almost all of them died when the Republic destroyed the place, so I guess it's useless to think about it.

speaker: Player
text: Who are the Baragwin?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: You don't know who the Baragwin are? They're the best damn weapons merchants in the galaxy, that's who they are!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They were in space selling arms to the highest bidder before my species even got off our homeworld.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Their weapons are the highest quality you can find, too. Better than either the Republic OR the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have any Baragwin equipment?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I might have a couple. You want to take a look?

speaker: Player
text: Sure.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to give me all your inventions.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Failure] I... What? No I don't! I don't know what you're trying to pull, but don't do it again!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now do you want to buy something or not?

speaker: Player
text: Let's see what you have.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in that right now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Suit yourself, suit yourself.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You can cut me a deal.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Success] Well, yeah, sure, I guess I can. You have a good face I think.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: A little odd, perhaps... but good.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not really interested in more questions right now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Sure, sure.

speaker: Player
text: You were a slave?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well, yeah, kind of. More like forced labor, really. We worked, or we died. Life gets really simple when someone puts it to you like that.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: We didn't have it near as bad as the ones who were actually building the temples themselves, though. I wouldn't be surprised if not a single one saw the temples completed.

speaker: Player
text: Did you get brought here?

speaker: Player
text: You're an inventor?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Maybe a little. I just tinker with stuff I've found lying around the ruins on Yavin IV, or that the Trandoshans and smugglers bring me. Of course, with them it's usually weapons and things...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But I just have so many ideas that people haven't seemed to come up with yet. It's really quite astonishing.

speaker: Player
text: There's stuff on Yavin IV?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Well, there's the old ruins from Exar Kun's war on that moon. But I've been here over 50 years and I can tell you it's been picked pretty clean by now. If I haven't found it, it's not there. All that's left is rubble.

speaker: Player
text: Have you found anything useful?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Some. Some things I'm still tinkering with, trying to get them working. Mostly I modify some of the things the Trandoshans and smugglers bring me and make them work better.

speaker: Player
text: What kinds of things do you work on?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Oh, all kinds. Weapons, armor, implants, computers. My interests are as varied as the fields they apply to... which is just about everything, heh.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I've scavenged what I could from the ruins on Yavin IV and I've been tinkering with it for a while.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about ancient Star Maps or the 'Star Forge'?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Never heard of them, or it. There were plenty of artifacts on Yavin IV, but no Forges or whatever.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: If that's all you're interested in, you'll probably want to try another system.

speaker: Player
text: How did you know Davik?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: He used to come here every once in a while to trade. He worked for the Exchange... big-time smugglers. The Trandoshans didn't really want to get on his bad side, so they let it go.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But now that he's gone, things are a bit more... uncertain.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Give them to me.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Failure] Sure, I can just... What? No, no, I can't do that. You trying to trick me or something?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Don't try stuff like that around here, kid. It won't work.

speaker: Player
text: So what's with you and Yavin IV?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Exar Kun.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Exar Kun was a Jedi... to start at least. He came here to Yavin and landed on the fourth moon... the one you can see through the window.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: There were some ancient Sith temples there, and in them Exar Kun gained terrible powers. He raised the Sith and waged a war against the Republic... much like what seems to be happening today.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But Exar Kun was far more powerful than any Sith Lord who has come since. The very ground trembled beneath his feet and when he looked at you, you just... just...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But that's all in the past now. I've got my life of staying here and tinkering with the stuff I've found in the ruins and the things the Trandoshans bring me.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Great Sith War.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Not much to tell. The Sith Lord Exar Kun tried to take on the galaxy. He lost, of course. They always seem to.

speaker: Player
text: What about this station?

speaker: Player
text: Why are you here?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Hm... you're good, I have to admit that.
comment: if the player just won a hand of pazaak

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I can't keep up with a player like you. You're just too good.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But I respect that. Tell you what, I'll give you a discount on anything in my store 'cause of that. Special deal just for you.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But I still think I can beat you a couple more times. You interested?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Hah! I still got it!
comment: if the player just lost a hand of pazaak

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But don't feel bad, kid, it happens all the time. Heh.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Interested in another game?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Eh?! Who is that? What do you want? I recognize your ship... Davik's, isn't it?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But who are you? You new or something?

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I'm new. Very new.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: You don't sound like a Trandoshan, and you're not one of Davik's... Who are you? What do you want?

speaker: Player
text: I'm a Republic soldier.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Republic, eh? The Republic hasn't been here in 50 years... don't see why they'd start now.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Still, I have nothing against the Republic, so as long as you don't get all worked up, I guess I can let you in.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: It would be nice to have someone to talk to for a change... Trandoshans and smugglers aren't exactly stunning conversationalists.

speaker: Player
text: Trandoshans and smugglers? What are you talking about?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They come by here every once in a while, it's how I keep in the loop, you know. But Trandoshan lizard-speak is kind of hard to follow and they have pretty limited imaginations...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Smugglers aren't much better either...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Look, this is getting kind of awkward through this door, if you'll just hold on a minute, I'll open this damn thing up and we can talk more face to face.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Just have to fiddle with this damn door lock... thing keeps jamming...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: There we go.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time to stick around in this airlock... Let me in!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Yeah, yeah, don't get antsy, I'll get there. Just have to fiddle with this damn door lock... thing keeps jamming...

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Open this door. I am your friend.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Success] Yes... I'll open the door for you, friend.

speaker: Player
text: I work for the Republic.

speaker: Player
text: I'm trying to save the galaxy from the Sith.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Sith? They haven't been here in 50 years... not since the last war. Don't see why they'd start making a habit of it now...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Still, all my business with the Sith is old news. Politics ain't my affair, so as long as you don't get all worked up, I guess I can let you in.

speaker: Player
text: I am the Dark Lord and I am very displeased with you.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: My first legitimate visitor in 20 years and he turns out to be a Sith-wannabe joker... just my luck.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well, I suppose even that's better than some more Trandoshans... They aren't exactly known for their stunning conversation.

speaker: Player
text: You have a problem with the Sith?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: All my business with the Sith is old news and I intend to leave it there. I don't need some young upstart bringing that stuff up again, so just drop it.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh, I can't leave leave you standing out there talking, though... you seem to do a lot of that. I guess you can come in if you'll be civil.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: My first legitimate visitor in 20 years and she turns out to be a Sith-wannabe joker... just my luck.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I do work for Davik.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Failure] Ha! Davik went down with Taris when the Sith destroyed it. That much I've learned from the local Exchange. So who are you?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I do work for Davik.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: [Failure] Yes, now I do recog... no... wait. What the... ?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I thought you might be, but no. Davik's gone now, destroyed on Taris. His people are all gone, too. So who are you?

speaker: Player
text: I don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Player
text: Open this door or I'll blow my way in!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Hm... you don't look like I thought you would. Too... human.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Don't see many of your kind out here at all anymore... not since the war at any rate. What brings you here?

speaker: Player
text: I'm on a quest for the Jedi Council.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: The Jedi Council? Don't tell me you're a Jedi... you sure don't look it!

speaker: Player
text: I AM a Jedi!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now, now, I never said I doubted you, it's just... well, there aren't exactly a lot of Jedi wandering around these parts, not after what happened last time.

speaker: Player
text: What happened before?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? What? Don't tell me you youngsters don't know anything about Exar Kun and that war...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But then again, there've been a lot of... mm... troubles recently I've heard.

speaker: Player
text: Enlighten me about Exar Kun.

speaker: Player
text: What have you heard about the current war?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Only what the smugglers and Trandoshans have told me. A new Sith Lord has risen up to replace the dead one, and he's beatng the Republic up pretty bad.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They didn't seem too displeased with that prospect.

speaker: Player
text: I am the true Dark Lord of the Sith!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Now far be it for me to say that you aren't, but I'm going to be a skeptic and say that the one with the armada and the troops is more likely to be the true Dark Lord.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Not that I doubt you, you understand, I'm just trying to keep an open mind.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: And whether you are or not, my past is behind me, so I've nothing against you either way.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: So if you don't mind saying, what exactly is the Council sending you out to do?

speaker: Player
text: I'm trying to defeat Darth Malak.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Darth Malak? Never heard of him... Or is he that new Sith Lord who's giving the Republic such a hard time now? I haven't been keeping up on recent news.

speaker: Player
text: He is the Dark Lord of the Sith.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: A new Dark Lord, is he? It always seems a new one pops up, no matter how many you kill...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Your business with him is none of my business, of course, and I don't want to pry, but why are you way out here? Running?

speaker: Player
text: I am NOT running!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? No, no, of course not. A big man like you? No, no. But why are you here in the middle of nowhere? The ruins?

speaker: Player
text: What ruins?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Yavin's fourth moon used to hold a great number of temples dedicated to the ancient Sith. When Exar Kun came here 50 years ago, he used the temples in his effort to crush the Republic.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: He failed, obviously, and the Republic bombarded the surface almost into oblivion during their counterattack. Now all that's left are a lot of craters and a little bit of jungle.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: You could find stuff there for years afterwards, but I've got pretty much everything there was to find there.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Mostly all I've been doing for the last couple years has been tinkering with what I've found there, getting some of it to work, and modifying the stuff the smugglers and Trandoshans bring me to look at.

speaker: Player
text: You spend all your time here in this station? Alone?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Yes, of course! You don't see anyone else around, do you?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well, not entirely alone at any rate... Trandoshans or smugglers come by every so often and drop things off and pick some of my inventions up.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you come here to the station?

speaker: Player
text: I seek the pieces of a map to a 'Star Forge'.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Mm... 'Star Forge'? Never heard of it. There's nothing in this system except ruins of Exar Kun's war...

speaker: Player
text: Exar Kun?

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here, then?

speaker: Player
text: None of your business, bug-eyes!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? No need to be rude. I was just trying to be friendly is all... You don't have to bite my head off.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: If you don't want to talk, then I don't really know what you're doing here. There's nothing really here in this end of space anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Anymore?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? No, no, of course not. A big woman like you? No, no. But why are you here in the middle of nowhere? The ruins?

speaker: Player
text: When I... acquired the Ebon Hawk, it had the coordinates for your station.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Acquired, eh? Well figures Davik would be lazy enough to leave it in the nav computer...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Didn't leave anything about this system, did he? Ancient ruins or anything?

speaker: Player
text: He is my former student.
comment: if the player knows hes revan

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Former... student? Ah-hah, yes, of course.

speaker: Player
text: He is beating the Republic pretty badly.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Eh? Oh that... That always seems to happen to the Republic. They always seem right on the verge of defeat and then manage to spring back. I shouldn't worry so much.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: And even if they do lose... so what? It's not like it's going to affect me way out here. The ruins on Yavin IV are gone and nothing's left of Exar Kun, so the Sith have nothing to bring them here.

speaker: Player
text: It matters to me!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Of course, of course, and I can see that you're starting to get all worked up about the whole thing, so I'll just leave it well enough alone.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: But why are you way out here? It's the middle of nowhere. Nothing to interest you here... unless you're looking for the ruins on Yavin IV.

speaker: Player
text: I'M the one who will defeat the Republic!
comment: if the player knows hes revan

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Ah... of course you are. Far be it for me to doubt you. But why here? It's the middle of nowhere... Unless you're here for the ruins on Yavin IV?

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you know these things?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Well, you see, I'm kind of out of touch with the rest of the galaxy. I haven't left this system in almost 50 years, and this station in the last five, so...

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Hey! It's not a bad way to live! I have all the gadgets I need to tinker with and the smugglers and Trandoshans bring me food and interesting pieces of equipment!

speaker: Player
text: They have sent me to stop Darth Malak.

speaker: Player
text: I am their only hope.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Only hope, eh? That's a lot of pressure to put on someone. I hope for their sake it's not misplaced.

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: I was wondering when you'd want to talk again. What brings you here this time?

speaker: Trandoshan
text: That's not good enough, Suvam. We know you have more... and we want it now!

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: What? You can't just rewrite our agreement whenever you feel like it! The Exchange won't stand for it!

speaker: Trandoshan
text: The Exchange is in no position to dictate orders anymore, Suvam...

speaker: Trandoshan
text: Who's that?

speaker: Trandoshan
text: A stranger... You haven't been telling us everything, now have you, Suvam?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: Tell you everything? What are you talking about? I don't have to clear everything through you!

speaker: Player
text: What's going on here, Suvam?

speaker: Suvam Tan
text: They're trying to extort me, that's what! They think that just cause the Exchange is gone, they can take whatever they want from me!

speaker: Trandoshan
text: We are... renegotiating our contract, Suvam.

speaker: Player
text: I think you guys better leave.

speaker: Trandoshan
text: Or what? You'll force us?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Leave. Now.
comment: if the player has force persuade

speaker: Trandoshan
text: [Success] We... leave... now.

text: I believe you, Revan. I sense there is something different about you. Something that has changed. You are not the same as you were before.

speaker: The One
text: Yet the power of magic - what you call the Force - is within you still. You can still destroy the Elders and fulfill your vow!

speaker: Player
text: The Elders are dead. I killed them myself.

speaker: The One
text: Dead? Is this why you returned, Revan? To tell us that you have fulfilled your oath? If this is true, then there is something I must ask you.

speaker: The One
text: There was one prisoner, an Elder who's mind broke beneath our tortures. He raved of ancient rituals, of lost power and forgotten secrets! Unfortunately, most of his dying screams made no sense.

speaker: The One
text: Yet in his last hours he spoke of a book; an ancient tome that recorded the most powerful knowledge of the Elders, and detailed the rituals that could unleash the secrets.

speaker: The One
text: I am certain this ancient tome will allow me to unleash what has, for so long, been hidden by the Elders. Bring me this book and I will use the knowledge within it to help you enter the Temple.

speaker: Player
text: Here is the ancient tome.

speaker: The One
text: Well done, Revan. But before I will consider your oath fulfilled, I must study this tome. I must see if it truly contains the ancient knowledge I seek.

speaker: The One
text: I will have the guards escort you back here once we have studied the contents of the manuscript you have brought us.

speaker: The One
text: I have studied this tome, Revan. Much of it is beyond me, it speaks often of 'technology' - a form of magic I do not comprehend. But one thing has become clear to me:

speaker: The One
text: This tome does not hold the great secrets I was hoping for. Although it contains many rituals, only one appears to be of any real consequence.

speaker: Player
text: That's not my problem! We had a deal!

speaker: The One
text: All is not lost, Revan. After studying this book I have come to understand that even the Elders themselves did not actually possess the ancient secrets. They were only the guardians.

speaker: The One
text: The knowledge of magic and power is locked away within the Temple itself. And this book is the key to the Temple, for only the rituals in this tome can lower the shields protecting it.

speaker: Player
text: So now you know how to get inside the Temple?

speaker: The One
text: I now have the rituals to lower the shields, but the Temple is guarded by yet another barrier. Only those with powerful magic - what you call the Force - can pass through the entrance.

speaker: The One
text: None among my tribe - or perhaps none among any of the Rakata - has this power. Only you can enter the Temple, Revan. But you cannot do it without our help.

speaker: The One
text: You can pass the barrier at the entrance, but you cannot get past the shield that surrounds the Temple. Only the ancient ritual, performed by those of pure Rakata blood, can lower the shield.

speaker: Player
text: Looks like we still need each other.

speaker: The One
text: Yes. You brought this tome to me as you promised. Now I must trust you again. We will help you enter the Temple, and in exchange you will bring forth the great secrets within.

speaker: The One
text: My priests can prepare and perform the ritual whenever you are ready, Revan. But in accordance with the traditions within the ritual tome, you must enter the Temple alone.

speaker: Player
text: Why do I have to go in alone?

speaker: The One
text: The Temple is a sacred place to the Rakata, its power is bound in ritual and tradition. I have studied the ritual closely.

speaker: The One
text: It is forbidden for more than one to enter the Temple at a time. This is one of the sacred traditions of our ancestors; I will not permit you to defile it.

speaker: Player
text: I will go into the Temple alone.

speaker: The One
text: If you are ready to enter the Temple, we can begin the ritual immediately.

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready to enter the Temple now.

speaker: The One
text: Remember: in accordance with ancient Rakata tradition you must enter the Temple alone. My priests will meet you at the shield's edge to perform the ritual.

speaker: Player
text: No, I'm not ready yet.

speaker: The One
text: As you wish. Come speak to me and when you are ready to enter the Temple and I will have my priests perform the ritual.

speaker: The One
text: But remember: when the time comes you must enter the Temple alone, in accordance with the traditions of the ancient Rakata.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! I'll find my own way into the Temple.

speaker: The One
text: You have the power to enter the Temple itself, but you cannot lower the energy shields the Elders built around it. Only a Rakata can invoke the ritual chant with the proper intonation.

speaker: Player
text: I see I have no choice. Okay, I'll go into the Temple alone.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going into the Temple without help!

speaker: Player
text: So you will help me enter the Temple?

speaker: Player
text: You better not be looking to double-cross me here!

speaker: The One
text: I will honor our agreement, Revan. There is little reason for me to betray you, in any case.

speaker: Player
text: That was the only tome I found in the Elder's compound.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back when I get that book.

speaker: The One
text: When you have it, bring it here to me. Until then, you may move freely about our village. I will be waiting for your return.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Don't worry. I will slay the Elders and honor our deal.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'll never help you against the Elders!

speaker: The One
text: You refuse to help us? Is that why you returned, Revan? To tell us you have broken your vow?

speaker: The One
text: No one defies the will of the One, Revan - not even you! My war beasts will destroy you, and the tribe will feast on your bones!

speaker: Player
text: You can't force me to kill your enemies!

speaker: The One
text: Force you? No, Revan - we were allies working to a common goal! It was you who suggested we forge our alliance.

speaker: The One
text: You vowed to kill the Elders and bring us the secret knowledge they protect. In exchange, we promised to use this lost knowledge to help you enter the Temple of the Ancients.

speaker: The One
text: When you vanished, we thought you had forgotten us - or been killed by the Elders. Now that you have returned our alliance still holds: destroy the Elders, and we will help you.

speaker: Player
text: Temple of the Ancients? I still don't remember anything.

speaker: The One
text: I suppose that if what you say is true - that you cannot remember when you were last here - then you must have many questions. Very well, Revan.

speaker: The One
text: I will help you to understand. And then you will destroy the Elders tribe and fulfill the oath you swore to us long ago.

speaker: Player
text: You should probably start with the last time I was here.

speaker: The One
text: You arrived with Malak - your servant - three of your galactic standard years ago. My scouts saw your sky ship plummet to the earth and they went to loot the crash site.

speaker: The One
text: They tried to take you prisoner, but you unleashed your magic - what you called the Force - upon them. Seeing your power they bowed before you and brought you here to me.

speaker: The One
text: You used your power to rip the Rakata language from my mind, even as you drove Basic into our skulls so we could help you in your quest to find something called the 'Star Forge'.

speaker: The One
text: But the answers you sought lay within the Temple of the Ancients, and we could not help you enter the Temple. The Elders alone hold its secrets, guarding them with their very lives.

speaker: Player
text: You say my ship crashed. Was it because of the disruptor field?

speaker: The One
text: I know nothing of this disruptor field, but throughout the history of our tribe ships have fallen from the sky. It has always been this way; though in recent generations it has become more frequent.

speaker: The One
text: We have little understanding of such magic to make metal fly, but my scouts rush to take whatever we can carry from the crash sites in the hopes we may one day unlock these secrets.

speaker: The One
text: This was how we acquired our rancor war beasts. Several very young specimens were recovered from a crashed vessel. We raised them to adulthood, training and breeding them to be loyal beasts of war.

speaker: Player
text: I need parts to repair my ship.

speaker: The One
text: That I cannot help you with. Although we have recovered many strange devices from the sky ships that crash to the earth, their use is a mystery to us.

speaker: The One
text: As a show of good faith, I will allow you to search the stores of our tribe, and take whatever you find. In exchange, I know you will destroy the Elders and bring the secrets they guard back to me.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Temple of the Ancients.

speaker: The One
text: There is little I can tell you about the Temple. I know the secrets of our ancestors are contained within, but the Temple itself is barred to us.

speaker: The One
text: When last you were here, you and Malak sought to enter the Temple. You sought ancient knowledge and a way to escape this world within its stone walls.

speaker: The One
text: But only the Elders know how to bypass the barrier that surrounds it. Destroy them and bring back their secrets to us, and we will help you enter the Temple. That was our agreement.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me more about the Elders.

speaker: The One
text: The Elders guard the ancient secrets. Within their compound is the knowledge of power and magic; including the knowledge of how to enter the Temple itself.

speaker: The One
text: I have lost many warriors storming the gates of their compound, but they use weapons of light and fire against us, and not even our war beasts are strong enough to breach their defenses.

speaker: The One
text: Sometimes we can capture an Elder when they venture forth from their compound, and we have learned something about them. That is how we know they guard the ancient secrets.

speaker: The One
text: But no matter what tortures we inflict upon them, they will not reveal their secrets to us. They fear the knowledge they themselves guard, and they will never willingly surrender it to us.

speaker: Player
text: I don't see any other choice, so I'll help you.

speaker: The One
text: The compound of the Elders is to the south, beyond the Temple of the Ancients. From torturing the few Elders we have captured, we know something of what lies beyond the gates.

speaker: The One
text: The Elders are few in number. If you can get past the exterior defenses, you could surely slaughter them all. Then you can bring us back the knowledge they guard.

speaker: Player
text: So where is this information? Is it in some kind of computer?

speaker: The One
text: Computer? That is a word our prisoners have used. When we forced them to explain it to us, they said this 'computer' was some type of thinking machine. More magic we cannot understand.

speaker: The One
text: Before they died, some prisoners did speak of such a machine inside their compound. But I do not believe it has anything to do with the secrets they are trying to protect.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you think that?

speaker: Player
text: If I kill the Elders, how can I bring you their secrets?

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back after I kill the Elders.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] I will kill the Elders and bring you their secrets!

speaker: The One
text: [Success] I see you that you have changed much since our last meeting. I am confident you will not betray us this time.

speaker: Player
text: I'm going to need some information if you want me to succeed.

speaker: The One
text: Yes, I suppose that is true. I will start at the beginning, with our first meeting.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] I'll help you, but you have to answer my questions first.

speaker: The One
text: [Success] I suppose that if what you say is true - that you cannot remember when you were last here - then you must have many questions. Very well, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: I will help you, but first you must answer my questions.

speaker: Player
text: What was this vow, exactly?

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, but I don't remember any of this.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore. That part of me is gone. I'm <FullName> now.

speaker: Player
text: Vow? I don't remember any vow.

speaker: The One
text: You have entered the Temple, Revan. You have seen the great secrets of the Ancients. Now you must fulfill your oath and share these secrets with me, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: You are a fool! I only used you to get into the Temple!

speaker: The One
text: And so you have betrayed us, Revan - just as you did the last time you were here.

speaker: The One
text: But this time you will not be allowed to escape with the knowledge that is rightfully mine, Revan! My war beasts will destroy you!

speaker: Player
text: The information you wanted was all on computers. You couldn't use it.

speaker: The One
text: Do you take me for a fool, Revan? You are hoarding the secrets for yourself! You will leave us and forget about us, just as you did the last time you were here.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I don't have the secrets on me, but I'll get them for you soon.

speaker: The One
text: You have returned. Do you wish to enter the temple now?

speaker: The One
text: My scouts have reported a great battle in the compound of the Elders. Tell me, Revan - in your slaughter did you find the book recording the great secrets of the past?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: The One
text: I am the One, warrior-chieftain of this tribe. Answering questions is the work of Gjarshi, our Loremaster. Seek him out if you wish to know of our tribe.

speaker: The One
text: But I will answer no more questions. The time for questions is done: now you must fulfill your promise. Slay the Elders and bring us their secrets. This is the will of the One.

speaker: The One
text: I have given you free reign within our camp, Revan. Take whatever supplies you may need from our caches, if you think it will help you destroy the Elders and recover the ancient tome.

speaker: Player
text: Enough talking. I think I'll just kill you now!

speaker: The One
text: Then we shall feast upon your flesh, Revan!

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Strange. You are of your kind, but are unlike them too. You helped where others did not. Iziz was right in this.
comment: Selected, player has rescued jawas in sand person enclave.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: But taking of more was there as well. You have made the unfair trade. We will remember, both good and not.
comment: player pressured Iziz for extra money.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: You have the thanks of the Jawa under Iziz. We will remember when you are the ones that have gone.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Why would you bother we of Jawa under Iziz? Yours do not care for ours. Do you miss we that are taken? No.
comment: Selected. player has not rescued Jawas in sand people enclave. This is a generic Jawa in the cantina.

speaker: Player
text: Please, could you try to speak more clearly?

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: Doubtful. The Jawa language is structured in an odd manner. You are lucky to understand what you do.

speaker: Bastila
text: It's not that hard to understand if you listen. It's just... odd.

speaker: Carth
text: Hence the 'unclear' part. Or did you miss that?

speaker: Bastila
text: Your sarcasm is not appreciated, Carth.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: The voices of Jawa under Iziz are not flawed. The ears of your kin are poor while we speak plain of our missing.

speaker: Player
text: "Of your missing?" Have some of your people gone missing?

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Is this interest? Not from your kind, though Iziz thinks otherwise. Speak to him if you are acting and pretending.

speaker: Carth
text: Hmm. These Jawas sure aren't the trusting type, are they?

speaker: Bastila
text: No doubt with good reason.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, for once, I'll agree with you.

speaker: Player
text: You two agreed? Somebody mark this day down.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Jawas are tired of giant-speak. Might as well slave to the gaffi. So you trade, but what is that if no help is given?

speaker: HK47
text: Query: Is the miniature organic implying falsehood? Shall I blast it, master?

speaker: Player
text: Iziz... is that your leader? Where is he?

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Iziz stands at the walls that hold out the sand. They listen poorly there too. Your kind hide behind bad ears.

speaker: Player
text: Jawa babble. I don't have time for this.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Your kind are like that, and Iziz is foolish to think that you are not. We know this. Leave us to the trouble.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: He sounds... not right. Unnatural.

speaker: Jolee
text: Seems fairly clear to me, though he doesn't seem used to people actually stopping to listen.

speaker: Player
text: "We that are taken?" Are some of your people missing?

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Back, but nothing changes, and ours are still lost. Iziz starts to know you will not help, and fades his hopes.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: Sorry... I'm rather busy with the excavation planning, right now.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: You aren't assigned to the excavation team, are you?

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: The tomb on the far left, there, is off-limits. Only Master Uthar can go inside.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: Where is that blasted transport crew? We're supposed to send off the next shipment of artifacts right away.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: Careful of the tuk'ata. It's all we can do to keep those beasts away while we work.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: We've had indications that there's a whole ancient Sith colony under this valley. Isn't that an incredible find?

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: The tombs are all full of traps and droids that still work, it looks like. Stay out of them, if you can.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: I was told that there's an escaped assassin droid in one of the tombs. Watch out for it.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: One has to wonder what made the Sith leave this planet originally. I bet the Jedi came and destroyed the colony.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: These tombs we've uncovered are only the tip of an entire ancient Sith fortress. I wonder what happened here?

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: Look, unless you're willing to lend a hand, leave us to our work.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: You're out here to look for artifacts, I suppose? Just be careful.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: There's supposed to be some crazy Sith hermit that keeps kidnapping students in these hills. Best be careful.

speaker: Sith Archaeologist
text: Sorry, I can't talk. We have to excavate this valley with hand instruments. There's all kinds of old traps left behind that still work.

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: I've heard the news - Gadon is dead. You have done well. Brejik himself would be here to congratulate you if he was not so busy preparing for the big swoop race.
comment: Will initiate in a cutscene if party enters the base and Gadon is dead. This leads to the swoop race cutscenes. (See next start condition for description of the first conversation)

speaker: Player
text: I've done my part, now you better live up to your end of the bargain!

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: Here are the 500 credits for eliminating Gadon and, as promised, we will let you ride for the Black Vulkars in the big swoop race.

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: We'll provide you with a swoop bike that has the prototype accelerator installed. Your modified bike will be fast enough to beat every other racer on the track.

speaker: Carth
text: And when we win the race, we get Bastila, right?

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: When you win Brejik will turn the girl over to you. You get Bastila, a Vulkar rider wins the race, and Brejik doesn't lose face for withdrawing his prize. Everybody wins.

speaker: Player
text: Why do I get the feeling you're not telling me something?

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: There is one small thing you should be aware of before you race tomorrow: the prototype accelerator isn't exactly stable yet - there's a chance it might explode during the race.

speaker: Carth
text: Explode? Are...are you crazy? Why would we risk riding that thing, then?

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: That's part of the reason Brejik installed it on your bike - none of our Vulkar riders are willing to risk their lives to win the prize. They're afraid of getting blown to bits.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you think I'm willing to risk my life?

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: You've already gone to a great deal of trouble to get your hands on this Bastila. You want this Republic soldier in your possession for some reason.

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: I don't know why - I really don't care. But I get the feeling you're willing to risk dying on the swoop bike if that's what it takes to get her.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not afraid to ride that bike!

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: I'm glad to see you're being reasonable. The race is tomorrow, so I'm afraid you won't have time to practice. But nobody will be able to keep up with your modified swoop.

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: All you have to do is hold on tight, try not to smash into anything, and hope the accelerator doesn't explode. Simple.

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: Get some rest and I'll come for you in the morning to take you to the swoop track. Good luck... you're going to need it.

speaker: Player
text: I guess I don't have any choice. I'll race for the Vulkars.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, let's do this.

speaker: Player
text: I've changed my mind - I'm not racing for you!

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: Who will sponsor you then, the Beks? I'm sure they'd love to back the assassin who killed their beloved leader. No, I think you'll race for us - you don't have any other options.

speaker: Player
text: Gadon died screaming like a skinned ronto. So will you if you don't hand over Bastila right now!

speaker: Kandon Ark
text: Don't do anything foolish. If you attack me then you'll lose any chance of ever getting your hands on that girl. Besides, we had a deal, remember?

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Looks like we have visitors - lackeys conned by Gadon Thek into trying to steal Brejik's swoop engine accelerator, I bet!
comment: Will initiate on sight with the party. Two possible outcomes: 1. Party refuses offer, they fight, Kandon dead. 2. Party accepts offer, Kandon gives them access codes to Bek elevators, party is moved outside Vulkar base into Lower City main entrance. If they come back, Kandon is not in the area.

speaker: Mission
text: Brejik stole that engine from Gadon! It was never yours to begin with!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Well I didn't go to all the trouble of acquiring this prototype just so you could steal it back for that old fool!

speaker: KandonArk102
text: Would you like me to dispose of these Bek spies, Kandon?

speaker: KandonArk101
text: No - hold on a second. I see you aren't wearing the Hidden Bek colors, so I'm guessing you aren't part of that feeble old man's gang. You must be a freelance mercenary.

speaker: Player
text: You're right, I'm not one of the Beks. My name's <FullName>.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Instead of stealing the prototype for the Beks, why don't you come work for us? The Black Vulkars could use someone like you.

speaker: Player
text: You've got my attention. What's your offer?

speaker: Mission
text: What? You can't betray Gadon! I won't let you!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Ah, Mission - the Hidden Bek's unofficial mascot! Your loyalty is admirable, but misplaced. Gadon only kept you around so they could laugh at you and your furry friend.

speaker: Mission
text: No, that's not true! You're lying!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Am I? How long have you known Gadon? How long have you worked for him? But they never offered to make you a Hidden Bek, did they?

speaker: Mission
text: They... they said I was too young!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: And you believed them? Come on, Mission. You're smarter than that. To Gadon and his crew you were nothing but a running joke. Weren't they always teasing you?

speaker: Mission
text: Well, yeah. Some of them were. But you Vulkars have tried to kill me more than once!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: That's only because you were with the Hidden Beks - and because we respected you. Brejik knows you're not a joke, Mission. He made sure the Vulkars took you very, very seriously.

speaker: Mission
text: But... but Gadon said Brejik...

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Gadon had to poison your mind against Brejik! It was the only way to keep you from seeing the truth. The Beks were mocking you, Mission. You don't need friends like that.

speaker: Mission
text: You're right! I don't need anyone but Zaalbar! If Gadon dies, he's only getting what's coming to him!

speaker: Player
text: You were about to tell me your offer, Kandon.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Brejik has grown tired of this petty war with Gadon and his pathetic followers. He needs someone to get rid of Gadon... permanently.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: If you do this task for him Brejik is willing to offer a very substantial reward. How does 500 credits sound? Oh, and we'll throw in that young Republic soldier we captured, too.

speaker: Player
text: I thought she was being offered up as the prize in the swoop race.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Well... we can't just give the girl to you. Not after Brejik's publicly offered her up as a prize in the big swoop race. But we can do the next best thing.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Whoever wins the swoop race gets the girl. Kill Gadon and we'll give you 500 credits, sponsor you as a Vulkar rider and equip your swoop with the accelerator. You can't lose!

speaker: Player
text: Okay, we have a deal. I'll kill Gadon for you.

speaker: Carth
text: Are you sure about this? I mean, I want to get Bastila back... but taking contracts to kill people is a bit much. Even if it is just more biker scum.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Excellent. Here - you might need these for this mission. They're access codes to Gadon's private chambers in the Bek base. Without them you won't be able to get at the old man.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: My guards will escort you to the main doors of our base. After you have killed Gadon return to the main doors and I will arrange for you to ride for the Vulkars in the swoop race.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: I'd suggest you don't come back until the job is done, or we might think you've decided to renegotiate on our offer. The Vulkars won't consider you a friend until Gadon is dead.

speaker: Player
text: Just give me the girl now or we have no deal.

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Brejik can't withdraw his prize without losing the respect of every gang in the Lower City. Besides, she isn't even here. Brejik's keeping her somewhere safe until after the race.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I want Bastila up front or no deal!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: *Sigh* I can see there's not much chance of convincing you to come work for us after all. Most unfortunate.

speaker: KandonArk102
text: Now can I kill them, Kandon?

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Yes, darling. Kill them. Kill them all.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it - I'm not going to betray Gadon!

speaker: Player
text: How about I just kill you instead?

speaker: Player
text: Brejik will let me have Bastila if I kill Gadon for him?

speaker: Player
text: Don't listen to him, Mission. He's twisting your mind!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! I know all about you Black Vulkars!

speaker: KandonArk101
text: Be smart; Gadon Thek is old news! He's a blind fool in more ways than one! Brejik is a visionary - soon he'll control the entire Lower City! Don't shackle yourself to a losing team.

speaker: Player
text: Enough yapping! Hand over that accelerator.

speaker: Carth
text: You're talking like Brejik didn't steal that engine, himself, to begin with!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The conquering hero returns! You did a great thing winning that swoop race for us!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Membership in the Beks is already starting to climb again. Won't be long now until we're back in control and Gadon can restore some order to the streets.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Used to be everyone wanted to join the Hidden Beks. But if the Vulkars win that swoop race I got a funny feeling a lot of our own people are going to join up with Brejik.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The Vulkars aren't the first group to try and take over from the Beks. Gadon knows how to deal with these upstarts. He may be blind, but he still can see the big picture.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The Vulkars are done for! Nobody will want to join them after seeing what Brejik did at the swoop race!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You heard what the Vulkars are putting up as a prize to the winner of the swoop race? A captured Republic soldier! Do you know how much she'd bring on the galactic slaver market?

speaker: Outcast Man
text: A few of the braver villagers dared to leave the safety of the fence. They... they never returned

speaker: Outcast Man
text: Thank you! My wife was one of those banished because she had the rakghoul disease. If you hadn't cured her, I would have never seen her again!

speaker: Outcast Man
text: The rakghouls took my wife! I can only pray she is dead... I cannot bear to even think of the alternative.

speaker: Outcast Man
text: They say anyone bitten by a rakghoul will become a rakghoul themselves. It can't be true, can it? It's too horrible!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Hey - I recognize you! You're the one who won the big swoop race!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: I can't believe what Brejik did after the race - talk about no class! But what else could you expect from a Vulkar?

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The Vulkars are gaining members every day from the smaller gangs. If they win the big swoop race there's no telling how many new recruits they'll get!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The Vulkars are out of control. Gang rivalry is one thing, but gunning people down in the streets is going too far! They don't even care if their victims are Beks or not!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The Vulkars won't last long against us now that Brejik's out of the way. Serves him right for trying to back out on his wager!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: I don't deal in slaves, but that Republic soldier Brejik's offering as a prize would be worth a lot of credits to the right buyer.

speaker: Jolee
text: [The old man knows better than to engage in chit-chat with enemies so close by.]

speaker: Jolee
text: [Even though he has joined your group, Jolee remains a somewhat mysterious character. Maybe you should speak to him about why he chose to come with you.]

speaker: Player
text: [Speak to Jolee.]

speaker: Jolee
text: Got something on your mind, do you?

speaker: Player
text: Why did you decide to come with me?

speaker: Jolee
text: You got yourself a fast little ship. Heh. I'd forgotten what engines sounded like. The closest thing to that on Kashyyyk is an uller in mating season. Ugh! Frightful.

speaker: Player
text: So you wanted a ride on my ship?

speaker: Jolee
text: Or it could be for the free food. What's the gunk that comes out of the synthesizer on this bucket, anyway? Do you never clean the darned thing?

speaker: Player
text: No, seriously, tell me.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm old, damn it! I'm allowed to be enigmatic when I want to be, and don't you go telling me otherwise.

speaker: Jolee
text: You know, you remind me of someone else I knew ages ago. Pleasant enough fellow, great destiny... all of that. Breath like a bantha.

speaker: Player
text: Did you annoy this person endlessly, too?

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh ho ho, very funny. Is it my fault that some people are so easily annoyed? They're like impatient little children. With blasters.

speaker: Jolee
text: Anyway, where was I? Oh, yes. Andor Vex, was his name. The Force swirled around him like a hurricane, that's how great his destiny was.

speaker: Player
text: I never heard of him.

speaker: Jolee
text: No, you wouldn't have. Sometimes swirling Force is just swirling Force. It gets us old Jedis excited at our age so we go "ooo, destiny!"

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, it turned out that poor Andor believed a wee bit too much in the infallibility of that destiny. That overconfidence turned out to be his downfall.

speaker: Player
text: Is there supposed to be some hidden meaning in this?

speaker: Jolee
text: I don't know. Are you overconfident? I hadn't noticed. Even if I had, I would never comment on it. We're talking about Andor, remember?

speaker: Jolee
text: Let's see... oh, yes. Andor's downfall. I was pretty young, myself, when it happened. At the time, I thought that Andor's destiny couldn't be more boring.

speaker: Player
text: How young are we talking?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, let's just say that I was a strapping young lad with a full head of hair and Coruscant was a small town with a well, heh heh.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was just about to abandon Andor to whatever the Force intended for him when his ship was overtaken by a Dimean warship.

speaker: Jolee
text: Now, you've probably never heard of the Dimeans, but at the time they were a nasty lot led by a nastier overlord named Kraat. Tall fellow. Big teeth.

speaker: Jolee
text: Kraat has us hauled onto the bridge of his ship for questioning, and that's when I knew that Andor's destiny was at hand.

speaker: Player
text: Andor killed Kraat, I take it?

speaker: Jolee
text: Of course he did! Haven't you been listening? It was not in the way you'd probably expect, though.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, Andor decides that his destiny makes him invulnerable and starts making all sorts of demands. Free me now, I'm not answering questions, blah blah blah. Don't you know who I am?

speaker: Jolee
text: Kraat decides he's had enough and begins crushing Andor's neck. I told the boy he should have kept his mouth shut. I think he agreed, too... or those could have just been gurgling noises. Well... well, anyway.

speaker: Jolee
text: Finally, Kraat has enough of Andor and tosses him aside into this giant energy intake shaft. Andor gets sucked in and starts bouncing around, heh, screaming... heh.

speaker: Jolee
text: Maybe Andor hit something sensitive on the way down or just didn't agree with the reactor core, next thing I know all the ship's alarms are ringing.

speaker: Player
text: You're kidding...

speaker: Jolee
text: Everyone panics and I run, barely making it to the ship in time before the explosion. Kraat dies horribly, and the Dimeans never quite recovered.

speaker: Jolee
text: Changed the political course of the entire sector for centuries to come. I'd call that quite a destiny, wouldn't you?

speaker: Player
text: I hate you, old man...

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, now, that's the ingratitude of youth for you. I relate an exciting tale and do I get thanked for it? No, no, it's all 'me me me!' Hmph.

speaker: Jolee
text: Anyway, go on. My throat is dry and you're making me cranky. Shoo!

speaker: Player
text: But how can you even be sure Andor was responsible?!

speaker: Jolee
text: What?! Are you kidding?! What are the odds of that happening, anyway? A billion to one?

speaker: Jolee
text: You should do so well as to be sucked into the engine of some evil Sith Lord, you know. Andor was a hero... sort of.

speaker: Player
text: And what does that have to do with you coming with me?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, hey, the chances may not be great, but when one has the opportunity to see something like that twice in a lifetime...

speaker: Player
text: How did you know?

speaker: Jolee
text: Swirling Force, remember? Jedi here? Granted, I was just interpreting the signs, but we get trained in that sort of thing. More or less.

speaker: Player
text: And? Go on.

speaker: Player
text: As boring as this story?

speaker: Jolee
text: You know, if you keep interrupting, it will take even longer. Have you no patience at all? How did you get as old as you are anyway?

speaker: Player
text: So why didn't you *leave*?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, he had a much better food dispenser than you do. That and the fact that even then I wasn't an altogether impatient *twit*.

speaker: Player
text: Does this story have a point, old man?

speaker: Jolee
text: Does it have to have a point? I thought we were just talking about Andor. Is something wrong with your attention span?

speaker: Player
text: You're making all of this up!

speaker: Jolee
text: I am not! I've no need to make things up, with my poor memory and all. You just sit still and let me finish, damn it.

speaker: Player
text: Is that what you see around me, too?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, it's not so much a hurricane as a slight breeze. But that doesn't mean anything: destiny is sometimes in the eye of the beholder.

speaker: Player
text: And you traveled with this man?

speaker: Jolee
text: I did. Just because someone has the Force swirling about them doesn't always mean they have a great destiny, but it doesn't hurt to check it out.

speaker: Player
text: Is this a comment on my breath?

speaker: Jolee
text: No, but it could be. An Anduvian salt tablet would clear that right up, you know.

speaker: Player
text: You're avoiding the question.

speaker: Jolee
text: So I am. Tell you what... when you get to be my age, you can go ahead and answer any question you like, too. You have my permission.

speaker: Player
text: If you don't want to answer the question, old man, just say so.

speaker: Jolee
text: How impatient can one person be? You must have driven your mother mad. All that gurgling and fussing... heh, babies are cute, but annoying.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, forget it.

speaker: Jolee
text: Wow, you're not much for interrogation, are you? Is this as hard as you try? Remind me to sign up for your next torture session.

speaker: Player
text: You never did actually say why you decided to come with me...

speaker: Jolee
text: No, I never did, did I?

speaker: Player
text: You know, I don't *have* to take you with me.

speaker: Jolee
text: Of course you do. I know things, remember? You think you could make it around this part of the galaxy without me? Don't answer that.

speaker: Jolee
text: At any rate, I already told you why I wanted to leave. I'd seen everything I wanted to on Kashyyyk. Time to go, time to move on.

speaker: Player
text: Move on to where?

speaker: Jolee
text: To bed. I'm old and tired, you know.

speaker: Player
text: No, really.

speaker: Jolee
text: How many kilometer-high trees can you find an interest in before you figure you've had enough? I'd bet you can't be bothered to stay in one room for more than fifteen minutes.

speaker: Jolee
text: And then there's all the critters in the Shadowlands... I'm just happy to be back in space, doing something new. Is that too much to ask?

speaker: Player
text: You could do that on your own.

speaker: Jolee
text: So I could. Not having a ship does tend to put a damper on that kind of idea, however.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'll admit... for all its flaws, Kashyyyk was home enough. But when you came along and I saw the destiny you had before you, I couldn't help but be intrigued.

speaker: Player
text: You know what my destiny is?

speaker: Jolee
text: Of course not. Weren't you listening last time? I can see that you have a destiny before you... but the details are far from clear.

speaker: Jolee
text: In fact, everything about you that I can see is odd. Slightly off, as if my eyes are trying to trick me. Something... something is very dark about you...

speaker: Jolee
text: ... but bah! I'm sure you don't need to hear my ruminations. You've probably got enough nosy Jedi offering you one opinion after another to make you sick.

speaker: Player
text: No, tell me more of what you see.

speaker: Jolee
text: Your future will come of its own accord, trust me. Sometimes navel-gazing at it doesn't get you anywhere.

speaker: Jolee
text: I wouldn't worry about it too much, if I were you. You remind me a bit of Nomi, heh heh, and that can't be all bad.

speaker: Player
text: Nomi? Who's Nomi?

speaker: Jolee
text: Nomi Sunrider. She came late to the Force, just as you have, and became one of the greatest Jedi ever. Oh, fine, fine lass.

speaker: Jolee
text: Whether you'll follow the same path remains to be seen. For one thing, we'll never get anywhere if you stand around chatting up old men all day...

speaker: Player
text: I don't bring you along for your amusement, you know.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, stop being such a baby. Are you always so quick to turn aside an ally? Got too many of them, do you?

speaker: Jolee
text: One thing I will say is that this little escapade does remind me a bit of my adventuring days before the war. Ahh, those were exciting times.

speaker: Jolee
text: Or at least it would remind me of those times if we didn't stand around. What's keeping you? You're too young to be so talkative. Shoo! Shoo!

speaker: Player
text: So... you're along as some kind of observer?

speaker: Jolee
text: Nonsense. Have I ever refused to help you when you asked? How confused can one person be, anyway?

speaker: Player
text: I don't need another mentor.

speaker: Jolee
text: Good, since I didn't offer to be one. You think anyone would want to mentor you with that kind of attitude? Not me, I'm past that.

speaker: Player
text: You got that right. I have enough Jedi watching me.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well I for one am quite content to let you make your own mistakes. Just because I want to see where this ends up doesn't mean I need to tell you how to get there.

speaker: Player
text: So you're coming along to *not* offer your opinions?

speaker: Jolee
text: I'll remind you that *you're* the one who started pumping me for information. Like an old man doesn't have anything better to do. Hmph.

speaker: Player
text: What interest do you have in my future?

speaker: Jolee
text: Interest? Well, I certainly don't have a vested interest... call it more idle curiosity. Your destiny is... rather unclear.

speaker: Player
text: Just keep your opinions on it to yourself.

speaker: Jolee
text: Have I offered a single opinion? No, I haven't, though you could do far worse than hear a couple of mine. Your destiny, after all, is rather unclear.

speaker: Player
text: Damn right it is.

speaker: Jolee
text: You got a smart mouth on you there, you know that? If ullers could talk, they'd sound like that.

speaker: Player
text: No, I guess not.

speaker: Jolee
text: There, now, was that so hard? An old man has to be allowed some petty eccenticities. Nice to see you agree, for once.

speaker: Player
text: I don't believe you.

speaker: Jolee
text: The hermit says he's tired of living alone in the giant forest and you find that hard to believe? How cynical are you?

speaker: Player
text: You looked plenty happy there, to me.

speaker: Jolee
text: You live in an overgrown stump with the tachs beating down your door and you tell me how happy you would be. I was pleased just to have visitors.

speaker: Player
text: Are you always going to be this elusive?

speaker: Jolee
text: Elusive? Me, elusive? Heh. Obviously you've never tried to grab a Twi'lek dancing girl after drinking too much Ondaran willek juice.

speaker: Player
text: Answer the question, old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: My, my, somebody woke up on the wrong side of the starship this morning, I see. Is that a chip on your shoulder or are you a bit surly today?

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned something about your 'adventuring days'?

speaker: Jolee
text: Did I say that? Strange the tricks memory plays on you when you get older.

speaker: Player
text: So you weren't an adventurer?

speaker: Jolee
text: Didn't I say that my past was my affair? You don't see me poking and prodding you with questions, do you?

speaker: Player
text: But you've already said so much... I'm curious.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm not here to satisfy your curiosity! No staring at the old man, that's what the sign says, dammit!

speaker: Jolee
text: And besides... you don't really want to hear about me. We're talking ancient history, probably before you were born. History bores kids. Proven fact.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah? Well old people love to talk about history. Proven fact.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh fine, fine, have it your way. Just don't cry about it later.

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes, yes, I was an adventurer. Happy now? I wasn't even done with my Jedi training back then. I had a full head of hair and an eagerness to see absolutely everything.

speaker: Jolee
text: Sound familiar? The Council was never very happy with willful, brash Jolee Bindo, you see. Even less so when I began my smuggling career.

speaker: Player
text: *You* were a smuggler?

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't look at me like that, dammit! I wasn't always the wrinkled coot I am now, you know. I can still fight, too, so wipe off that smirk I see there.

speaker: Jolee
text: At the time the Ukatis system was interdicted by its own King. He preferred to keep his people starving and poor, all the better to oppress them.

speaker: Jolee
text: The Senate was trying to negotiate a peace, but they were getting nowhere as usual. I decided I wasn't going to wait.

speaker: Jolee
text: I found myself a ship and a partner and we began smuggling food and supplies to the Ukatis citizenry through the blockade.

speaker: Player
text: Was it very dangerous?

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, it was. I was a half-decent pilot in those days... and with the Force guiding me, we made it through some tough spots nobody else would have.

speaker: Player
text: You were a pilot, too?

speaker: Jolee
text: Pilot, smuggler... several other things, too. Or did you suppose I was always a crotchety hermit?

speaker: Player
text: Where did you get the credits for all the supplies?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well... we didn't *buy* all the equipment, per se. Some were happy to donate goods. Some we just, ah, knew had more than they could use...

speaker: Player
text: So you stole it?

speaker: Jolee
text: 'Stole' is such a harsh word. They would have donated those goods readily enough if they were compassionate. I considered it a tax on the greedy.

speaker: Jolee
text: We only got caught once. A lone Ukatish frigate shot us down and forced a crash landing. I thought the Force had abandoned me, as I remember.

speaker: Player
text: What happened then?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, as it happens, getting shot down turned out to be very fortunate. That day was the day I...

speaker: Player
text: That was the day you what?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, that... that was the day I met my wife.

speaker: Player
text: Oh, I'm sorry...

speaker: Jolee
text: It's alright. When you're digging through the trash, you shouldn't be surprised when you encounter something unpleasant.

speaker: Jolee
text: I... If it's all the same to you, I'd prefer to stop talking now. My mouth is starting to draw flies.

speaker: Player
text: Your wife? You were married?

speaker: Jolee
text: You know another way to get a wife? But, yes... that's when I met her.

speaker: Player
text: Bad memory, I take it?

speaker: Jolee
text: No. No, that was a good memory. There are just... much worse ones that followed.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe it should have.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, so you're going to speak for the Force now, are you? I deserved to crash, is that it?

speaker: Player
text: Well that was pretty stupid of you.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. As I recall, I'm not the only person in this conversation who's been shot down out of the sky recently.

speaker: Player
text: I still can't believe you actually did that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Why not? There were millions of people crying out for aid. What else was I supposed to do?

speaker: Player
text: How about nothing?

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't be stupid. Are you doing nothing? If nothing's not good enough for you there's no reason it should have been good enough for me back then, either.

speaker: Player
text: A Jedi would never be a smuggler!

speaker: Jolee
text: You're very sure of that, are you? My, my, you must be very learned and experienced to know so many things. At any rate, I was still a Padawan at the time.

speaker: Player
text: How did that happen?

speaker: Player
text: You're right. I'd rather not be bored.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well that's a relief. Maybe an old man can finally get some peace around here. Now, run along and do whatever you were doing, already.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not a 'kid'.

speaker: Jolee
text: So you're not. Fine, have it your way. Just don't say I didn't warn you.

speaker: Player
text: You're just not used to company. Stop being an old coot.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. I might be. But a mouthy young thing like yourself shouldn't get to call me an old coot, dammit.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. I won't you questions ever again.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned something about your wife before?
comment: Jolee won't talk anymore past this

speaker: Jolee
text: I don't want to talk about that.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry. Maybe we can talk about it later.

speaker: Jolee
text: Maybe, but I doubt it. I'm made stubborn that way.

speaker: Player
text: Well, I do. Spit it out, already.

speaker: Jolee
text: Now that's a unique method of getting someone to talk. Thunder about like a bantha in a circuit shop. Does that work for you often?

speaker: Jolee
text: Let me tell you something. Once you've lived as many years as I have, you'll have yourself a long, long list of memories.

speaker: Jolee
text: If you're lucky, most of them will be good. If you're not, some will be bad. If you're really unlucky, some will be so bad you never want to be reminded of them again... ever.

speaker: Jolee
text: You'll go far away, to a place that doesn't hold any memories at all. And there you'll be happy just to forget and be forgotten.

speaker: Player
text: I would never do that.

speaker: Jolee
text: You say that now, but I'm talking to you from across the breadth of many years experience. That is a gap I simply can't cross for you.

speaker: Jolee
text: Let me ask you this: have you ever been in love? Truly in love, I mean, and not simple infatuation.

speaker: Player
text: Well...

speaker: Jolee
text: Exactly. You're still at the beginning of your life. There will be women in your life... perhaps many women... but if you're fortunate you'll find love once.

speaker: Jolee
text: The Jedi, with their damnable sense of over-caution, would tell you love is something to avoid. Thankfully, anyone who's even partially alive knows that's not true.

speaker: Player
text: Aren't you worried about the dark side at all?

speaker: Jolee
text: Love doesn't lead to the dark side. Passion can lead to rage and fear, and can be controlled... but passion is not the same thing as love.

speaker: Jolee
text: Controlling your passions while being in love... that's what they should teach you to beware. But love, itself, will save you... not condemn you.

speaker: Jolee
text: Ahhhh, but listen to me go on as if I had all the answers. What do I know of love anymore? I'm just a lonely old man who's not even a Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like love is something you should have avoided.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. Maybe. Do you want to avoid the greatest things in life simply because they come with some complications?

speaker: Jolee
text: Love causes pain, certainly. Inevitably love is going to lead to as much sorrow and regret as it does joy. I suppose there are perfect, eternal loves out there... but I haven't seen any.

speaker: Jolee
text: How you deal with the bad part of love is what determines your character, what determines the dark side's hold over you.

speaker: Player
text: You don't think love can work?

speaker: Jolee
text: I suppose it could. It would take a strong person to make that kind of commitment, I think. Someone with a great sense of self.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'll tell you one thing: sometimes, no matter how hard you try, you and the one you love simply aren't meant to be together.

speaker: Jolee
text: The trick is to know when that is, to know when it's time to fight and when it's time to part ways.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph... there I go waxing philosophical again. Somebody blast me already! Let's get going before I start talking in riddles, dammit!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe the Jedi just think you shouldn't take that risk.

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah. A life without risk is boring. Is that how you want to live? You want love, you've got to fight for it.

speaker: Player
text: So what happened between you and your wife, then?

speaker: Jolee
