text: I haven't changed my mind. I'm still not going to talk about it. You go and find your own love if you want to know so badly.

speaker: Player
text: You talk too much, old man. You don't know anything.

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't I? Hmph. Maybe you're right. It seems whatever I have to say is falling on deaf ears, anyhow.

speaker: Jolee
text: So go on, go on, run amok and kiss the bantha for all I care. I won't comment on it.

speaker: Player
text: No, I want to hear what you have to say.
comment: Jolee will not speak any more

speaker: Jolee
text: You do, do you? I wouldn't listen too closely... I'm no authority on anything. I just think that the greatest things in life shouldn't be avoided because they come with a few complications.

speaker: Player
text: Not even a Jedi? You mean not any more, right?

speaker: Jolee
text: Nope. Never was. Technically I never rose above the rank of Padawan, for various reasons. Does that surprise you?

speaker: Player
text: Not the way you describe your past, no.

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh. I suppose I'm not prone to live my life like most of the Jedi Masters do, that's true. My opinions on love are no different.

speaker: Player
text: You seem to have all the abilities of a Jedi...

speaker: Jolee
text: In my case, becoming a Jedi would have been a formality. I doubt the order and I would have gotten along well, considering my opinions on things such as love.

speaker: Player
text: Yes. You lied to me.

speaker: Jolee
text: No I didn't. I may never have become a Jedi technically, but I'm an old Padawan with a lifetime of experience. That applies both to the Force as well as topics like love.

speaker: Player
text: That's what I've always thought.

speaker: Player
text: What's this? Love advice from an old Jedi?

speaker: Jolee
text: And why not? All this nonsense about avoiding love is so much foo-foo. I shouldn't be the only one who realizes that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Exactly. You're still at the beginning of your life. There will be men in your life... perhaps many men... but if you're fortunate you'll find love once.

speaker: Player
text: Is that why you went to Kashyyyk?

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh. Partly, maybe. I doubt I could ever explain it to you fully, even if I wanted to.

speaker: Player
text: Run away? How pathetic and weak.

speaker: Jolee
text: There are worse things to call yourself, for better reasons. If you don't think it's even possible that you might be flinging those words at yourself one day, you're younger than I thought.

speaker: Player
text: I don't mean to pry, but...

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes you do. You may mean well enough, but my private affairs are just that: private.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you leave the Jedi?

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh heh. Who said I left the Jedi?

speaker: Player
text: You did. You said you weren't a Jedi any longer.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, technically, I was only a Padawan... not that that makes a difference to most. But as for the order, itself... no, I never left it. It left *me*.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean 'it left you'?

speaker: Jolee
text: You know what I hate? Well... you know, lots of things, really. But I'm old and easily annoyed. But that's beside the point. What I *really* hate are how most people view the Jedi.

speaker: Jolee
text: Everyone thinks that Jedi are perfect, that they can do no wrong. They think the Jedi Council is completely incapable of injustice.

speaker: Player
text: I certainly don't think that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. I guess you aren't as stupid as you sometimes act. No doubt you've been on the receiving end of Jedi justice at least once, eh?

speaker: Jolee
text: And I'm not even talking about how some of us fall to the dark side. No, that's plenty indication of our fallibility, but it's something else entirely.

speaker: Jolee
text: No, I'm talking about how, more often than not, your average robe-wearing Jedi can try to do the right thing and still be completely *wrong*.

speaker: Player
text: I don't get it. What do you mean?

speaker: Jolee
text: *sigh* I suppose I'm not being very clear, am I?

speaker: Jolee
text: Come to think of it, I don't have to be clear. Someone my age is entitled to ramble, dammit! But for your sake I'll try to explain.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'll tell you a little tale about a Jedi Master I once knew. Hortath, I think. Or was it Hartoth? I could never get it straight...

speaker: Player
text: Go on, I'll listen.

speaker: Jolee
text: Where was I, then? Oh. Oh, yes... Master Hortath. He was a kindly old Jedi who meant well, but the most near-sighted thing in the Core, I swear.

speaker: Jolee
text: He would walk into walls, knock over tables, mistake apprentices for rancor beasts... that sort of thing. And he was too proud to submit to proper treatment.

speaker: Jolee
text: Some used to counsel him and urged "Use the Force, Master Hortath. Allow the Force to see for you." But he refused to believe that his eyes were failing.

speaker: Jolee
text: He simply squinted more and more as the years went on, the other Jedi resignedly passing it off as the amusing quirk of a compassionate old man.

speaker: Player
text: And? I don't get it.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm not finished yet! Now shush.

speaker: Jolee
text: So one day a young Padawan meets Master Hortath in the courtyard and, not knowing of his blindness, asks him for directions to the Council.

speaker: Jolee
text: Quite sure of himself, Hortath gave the lad directions... which happened to lead back outside and away from the enclave.

speaker: Jolee
text: The Padawan is confused, naturally. He asks if Master Hortath is sure, and of course Master Hortath says that he is.

speaker: Jolee
text: The Padawan suggests that perhaps he should ask someone else... but the proud Hortath now feels insulted. He tells the Padawan to take the route he prescribed and no other.

speaker: Jolee
text: Rather dejectedly, the Padawan did as he was told... and so ended up leaving the Jedi Order forever.

speaker: Jolee
text: It was decided that the boy's fate was to leave the Order anyway... though whether that was out of respect for Hortath or because the boy went on to something else, well, we'll never know.

speaker: Player
text: So what does the Padawan leaving the Jedi have to do with the Jedi leaving you?

speaker: Jolee
text: Not much. I never knew the Padawan nor met Master Hortath, himself. He was before my time.

speaker: Player
text: I don't understand...

speaker: Jolee
text: The tale is about blindness and I thought the point was clear. At any rate, you think about it. You're the one who asked why the Jedi left me, remember?

speaker: Jolee
text: Now let's get going. My feet are itching for a good run.

speaker: Player
text: So... you knew this Master Hortath? Or the Padawan?

speaker: Jolee
text: No, no. Both of them were from before my time. Well before the Sith Wars, even.

speaker: Player
text: So what's the point?

speaker: Player
text: That's a stupid story.

speaker: Jolee
text: Considering that it's about blindness, I think that's an appropriate response. You're the one who asked why the Jedi left me, remember?

speaker: Player
text: Is this supposed to have a point?

speaker: Player
text: Go on.

speaker: Player
text: Is this going to have a point?

speaker: Jolee
text: *Sigh* You know the problem with the youth of today? They're young.

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't have time for any stupid stories.

speaker: Jolee
text: You're the one who was asking me about the Jedi, dammit! Now do you want the story or not?

speaker: Player
text: Fine, fine, but make it quick.

speaker: Player
text: Not. Can't be bothered.

speaker: Jolee
text: Boring you, am I? Well you just keep your questions to yourself next time. No need for old men to go and make nuisances of themselves.

speaker: Player
text: So the Jedi wronged you in some way, I take it?

speaker: Jolee
text: No, no. The Jedi always treated me well. It would be foolish and untrue to say otherwise. That's not what I meant, anyway.

speaker: Player
text: Nobody can be right about everything.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's true, but it's not what I meant. I guess I'm not being clear, am I?

speaker: Player
text: Let me guess: you disagree?

speaker: Jolee
text: Damn right I disagree. The Jedi are just as capable of injustice as anyone else. They may *try* harder, sure, but sometimes they get it wrong.

speaker: Player
text: You? Perfect? That's a laugh.

speaker: Jolee
text: Quiet, you. I'm not talking about me. Talking about the Jedi as a whole. They are just as capable of imperfection and injustice as anyone else, as you can obviously see.

speaker: Player
text: That's about the dumbest thing I ever heard.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, is it? Hmph. There are moments when I think you must be much older than you seem... but this isn't one of them.

speaker: Player
text: So are you a Jedi or not?

speaker: Jolee
text: Something wrong with your ears? I thought folks only went deaf when they got to my age. I follow the Jedi Way and use the Force, don't I? That makes me a Jedi last time I checked.

speaker: Jolee
text: But the order, itself, the Jedi Council and so forth... no, I'm not a part of that and haven't been for a long time. And good riddance, I say!

speaker: Player
text: But you said the Jedi left you?

speaker: Player
text: Why good riddance?

speaker: Player
text: So you're just some rogue Jedi. Big deal.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. A rogue, am I? You speak as if there must be something wrong with me, like not being part of the order makes me a criminal.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying you're still a Jedi?

speaker: Player
text: Don't play games with me, old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't get so uppity, dammit! The point I was trying to make, if you decide to actually listen, is that I never left the order. The order left *me*.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Sith?

speaker: Jolee
text: Bad, bad men. Women, too, to be fair.

speaker: Player
text: You must know more than that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, indeed. They make a fine sandwich, also. Heh heh heh. But don't tell the Jedi Council I said that.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything important about the Sith or not?

speaker: Jolee
text: *sigh* And just what gave you the impression that I know anything more about the Sith than you do?

speaker: Player
text: You did. You said you fought them.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh... that's right. Damn the ears of the young! I was expecting you to be your usual inattentive self when I mentioned that.

speaker: Jolee
text: So it's true, yes, I fought plenty of Sith. That was during the time of Exar Kun... oh, fourty years ago now? Has it been that long?

speaker: Player
text: Are these Sith the same as the ones who followed me?

speaker: Jolee
text: No, no, of course not. The Sith have come and gone for ages. They were not called Sith many thousands of years ago, perhaps, but the dark side was always present without a doubt.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, sure, occasionally the light side comes close to vanquishing the dark, but the dark always returns.

speaker: Jolee
text: The fact that Exar Kun was defeated didn't mean the Sith would never return, as they obviously have now. Everyone knows that.

speaker: Player
text: Who is this Exar Kun?

speaker: Jolee
text: Ah. Exar was a Jedi who was... corrupted... by ghosts of the old Sith. Or so they say. He attempted to conquer the Republic and create a new Golden Age of the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Sort of like Revan. I mean me. I assume he was killed?

speaker: Jolee
text: Better to say he was defeated... but essentially, yes. The victory did not come easily, however.

speaker: Player
text: Are these the same Sith that we're fighting now?

speaker: Player
text: So tell me what you know about the Sith.

speaker: Jolee
text: A Sith believes he commands the Force... but it is the dark side who commands him. You know this, there is little else I could truly add.

speaker: Player
text: What happened during the war with Exar Kun, then?

speaker: Jolee
text: That... is not a pleasant time to remember. After Exar Kun fell to the dark side, he attempted to recruit other Jedi to his cause.

speaker: Jolee
text: What surprised us... what took us completely unprepared... was how utterly successful he was. Many Jedi joined him and became Sith, themselves.

speaker: Jolee
text: Why they did I... I will never truly know. But they did. Battle broke out throughout the order... pupil against master, we fought ourselves...

speaker: Player
text: That must have been difficult.

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes. More than difficult... next to impossible. How do you fight against someone you love?

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah. I dislike such memories. It leaves a taste in the mouth that... it is a sadness I thought I had put aside long ago.

speaker: Jolee
text: Ask me again about the war some other time. Just... not now. I would prefer to be by myself for now.

speaker: Player
text: But you exterminated all the traitors, right?

speaker: Jolee
text: Easy now to call them traitors. Tell me... how do you fight against someone that you love?

speaker: Player
text: This isn't going to be more sad moaning, is it?

speaker: Jolee
text: I've often held the opinion that history has one basic flaw: it is seldom heeded.

speaker: Jolee
text: So go on and greet the world with your spite. Let's see where it takes you. You certainly don't need to hear any more from me.

speaker: Player
text: And he was killed?

speaker: Player
text: You're being elusive on purpose.

speaker: Player
text: Spit it out, old man, or things get rough.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not in the mood to play games.

speaker: Jolee
text: Who's playing games? Ask the next Sith you see if they're bad and they'll set you straight.

speaker: Player
text: Do you want to talk about the war now?

speaker: Jolee
text: Not particularly.

speaker: Player
text: I'll ask you some other time, then.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] No time like the present?

speaker: Jolee
text: [Success] I suppose you're going to nag me until I cough it up, aren't you? Nothing is private anymore, it looks like.

speaker: Jolee
text: *sigh* There's no escaping it, I guess. So be it.

speaker: Jolee
text: My wife's name was Nayama. She was the Ukatis enforcer who shot me out of the sky, if you remember.

speaker: Player
text: What does your wife have to do with the war?

speaker: Jolee
text: My wife had plenty to do with the war. Upon meeting her, I knew right away that she was strong in the Force. That's why she was able to shoot me down.

speaker: Jolee
text: Nayama was a marvel of a woman. Fiery, determined, smart... she dragged me to the capital and foiled three of my attempts to escape prison. Oh, and that body...

speaker: Player
text: The war...?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well... yes, that. Needless to say I eventually won her over. That was after I kidnapped her upon being broken out of the Ukatis prison, mind you. But uh, that's another story entirely.

speaker: Jolee
text: At any rate, I wanted to train her in the Jedi way. The Council refused my request, naturally. I was still a Padawan at the time.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was an experienced Padawan, surely... but not yet ready to be a full Jedi and certainly not ready to train another. Especially not one so old as my wife.

speaker: Player
text: So you disobeyed the Council. Like I did.

speaker: Jolee
text: I did. I wasn't the first and I won't be the last. The problem with self-righteous folk is they think they're more right than everyone else.

speaker: Jolee
text: I believed in her and trained her in secret. I ignored her willful nature... I loved her too much to see fault in her.

speaker: Jolee
text: And she loved me, too. I know she did. At the time, our love was a shared bliss... better than anything I had known before or since.

speaker: Player
text: So what happened?

speaker: Jolee
text: Exar Kun is what happened. Nayama was inspired by Exar's promises of a new Golden Age. She wanted to join him.

speaker: Jolee
text: She came to me, pleading with me to throw aside what she called the decrepit trappings of the Jedi... to join her in Exar's war.

speaker: Player
text: So she had fallen to the dark side?

speaker: Jolee
text: I... hadn't thought so. Not right then. I was too proud to believe that of her. I had trained her myself... I loved her.

speaker: Jolee
text: I pleaded with her to reconsider, to think about all that she was throwing away... to think about what she would become.

speaker: Jolee
text: She would have none of it. Finally, in frustration, she attacked me. She drew her lightsaber and attempted to strike me down.

speaker: Jolee
text: It was a scene being repeated everywhere throughout the galaxy. Pupil against master. In my case... it was a long and terrible battle, but I defeated her.

speaker: Player
text: You killed her?

speaker: Jolee
text: No... no. I had her at my mercy, disarmed and defenseless. She looked up at me and she knew... she knew I couldn't do it.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds familiar. Seems like the Jedi don't like killing their helpless enemies.

speaker: Jolee
text: But I should have. Sometimes I convince myself otherwise... but it's no use. She had fallen to the dark side when she raised her saber against me.

speaker: Jolee
text: And I let her go. To my shame, she went on to kill many Jedi during the war until she, herself, was slain in the final battle.

speaker: Jolee
text: I grieved for her death, inevitable as it was, even as the Jedi Council put me on trial for my actions once the war was over.

speaker: Player
text: They put you on trial?

speaker: Jolee
text: I had trained Nayama against their wishes. I had failed to kill her when I had the chance, and she went on to kill others.

speaker: Jolee
text: Not to mention that I had remained a Padawan throughout the war. A formality, perhaps, but with the trial it had to be decided if I was worthy to become a Jedi at all.

speaker: Jolee
text: It was a travesty, of course. I told you that even the Jedi were capable of great injustices, didn't I?

speaker: Player
text: The Jedi are always fair and merciful. They gave me a second chance.

speaker: Jolee
text: But I deserved to be tried. They found me innocent.

speaker: Jolee
text: Even though I... deserved every punishment and more... they let me go. Mitigating circumstances, they said. I deserved compassion, they said.

speaker: Jolee
text: They said I had learned wisdom the hard way. For all I had done during the war, they wished to raise me to full Jedi status at long last.

speaker: Jolee
text: That... that was when the Jedi left me. That was when they failed me.

speaker: Player
text: No, you're wrong! You did deserve compassion!

speaker: Jolee
text: For my pride? For my cowardice? Which do you think is the act more befitting a Jedi?

speaker: Jolee
text: They may have been able to forgive me. I... could never forgive myself.

speaker: Player
text: And you still believe love is worth the risk?

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes, I do, I suppose. Does that surprise you?

speaker: Jolee
text: Ahhh... it is all so long ago. Lost in the winds, I suppose. Nobody cares what an old man believes anymore, do they?

speaker: Jolee
text: Let's continue on with the task at hand. I would prefer to think of the present today.

speaker: Player
text: You should have been happy you got off.

speaker: Player
text: I agree with you. They destroyed my mind, after all.

speaker: Player
text: So that's the source of all this bitterness? They found you guilty?

speaker: Jolee
text: Not at all. They found me innocent.

speaker: Player
text: So you think you didn't deserve to be punished?

speaker: Jolee
text: Of course I deserved to be punished. They found me innocent.

speaker: Player
text: I can't believe they tried you for that!

speaker: Player
text: I don't think I could have, either.

speaker: Player
text: But... she was a Sith then, right?

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes. I think she truly fell the moment she raised up her saber against me. I have played that instant in my head... so many times.

speaker: Player
text: You were a fool.

speaker: Jolee
text: Was I? Sometimes I convince myself that I couldn't have done otherwise... that I couldn't have seen that she had truly fallen to the dark side. But, yes, I was a fool.

speaker: Player
text: So you killed her, of course.

speaker: Jolee
text: No of course I didn't kill her. How could I? I pleaded with her to reconsider, to think about what she was doing.

speaker: Player
text: What did you do?

speaker: Player
text: You disobeyed the Jedi Council?

speaker: Player
text: So you're saying you were an idiot.

speaker: Jolee
text: Easy to say so now. At the time I just thought I was right.

speaker: Player
text: And what did she think of all this?

speaker: Jolee
text: Nayama was intrigued by the idea of becoming a Jedi. She liked the idea of power too much, perhaps, but I certainly didn't see that at the time.

speaker: Player
text: Um... no, I don't remember.

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah. You got ears that work, don't you? I was a smuggler, way way back. I got shot down once over Ukatis. THAT story, yes.

speaker: Player
text: Are you going senile? I didn't ask about your wife, old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: No I'm not senile, dammit! Not yet, anyway. Hmmm... well at least I don't think so. At any rate, I'll tell the story the way I want to.

speaker: Jolee
text: [Failure] *Sigh* I'm not interested in your demands. I'll tell my story when I'm damn good and ready... which isn't now, so shoo!

speaker: Player
text: You said you'd tell me later... so spit it out already.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmm. Such a charming and persuasive manner you have there. Forget it!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Okay, here I am asking nicely.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. Have it your way.

speaker: Player
text: So when did you go to Kashyyyk?

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, that was not until many years later, to tell the truth. I spent quite some time wandering the galaxy.

speaker: Player
text: The Jedi just let you go?

speaker: Jolee
text: Why wouldn't they? I had refused my promotion to Jedi... I was a Padawan who had left the Order, nothing more.

speaker: Jolee
text: I traveled from one civilized system to the next, never staying long. I don't even think I knew what I was searching for.

speaker: Jolee
text: It wasn't as if my travels were pleasant, either. There were plenty of folks who distrusted the Jedi after the war... or worse.

speaker: Player
text: Worse? What could be worse?

speaker: Jolee
text: If people weren't treating me with suspicion, they were looking at me with greed. I don't know how many thought they could make use of me for their own ends.

speaker: Jolee
text: I got so sick of the treachery and deceit I left the civilized parts of the galaxy and headed instead for the uncivilized parts.

speaker: Player
text: So that's when you went to Kashyyyk?

speaker: Jolee
text: Actually I was on my way somewhere else when I crash-landed on Kashyyyk. The ship I was using was a rust-bucket.

speaker: Player
text: You survived a crash-landing on Kashyyyk?

speaker: Jolee
text: I'd taken some damage passing through an unexpected asteroid field, as I recall, but I wasn't completely without some systems. I could still guide her a bit when I crashed.

speaker: Jolee
text: It wasn't what a would call the smoothest landing, especially considering I ended up smack in the depths of the Shadowlands. But I lived.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't you just fix your ship and keep going?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. I'm no mechanic. And besides, after you plunge nose-first into the trunk of a five-kilometer high tree, chances are you don't have much ship left.

speaker: Player
text: So you crashed... and stayed?

speaker: Jolee
text: Sure, why not? It seemed like an interesting enough place to spend a couple of decades exploring.

speaker: Player
text: How did you survive in the Shadowlands?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmmm. That was a challenge at first. You've seen the kind of creatures that exist down there... and you missed the really big ones.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was still able to rely on the Force to keep me safe for the most part. The rest of the trick is keeping out of the way of most of the predators.

speaker: Player
text: It couldn't have been easy.

speaker: Jolee
text: No, that's true. Still... most of the creatures grew accustomed to me, and I to them. At least none of them ever heard of a Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: You're completely insane, you know that?

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah, what do you know? I'd done enough wandering by that point, thank you very much. I felt at peace in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Player
text: And the Wookiees didn't mind your presence?

speaker: Jolee
text: They did at first, oh yes. I can't say I was overly pleased to encounter a group of indigenous giant carpets either, I can assure you of that.

speaker: Player
text: Did you fight them?

speaker: Jolee
text: No, no. I was the intruder in their land, after all. They got to trust me well enough after a couple of decades of my aid.

speaker: Player
text: You helped them?

speaker: Jolee
text: When I could. I would assist the few young ones who would get lost in the Shadowlands or attacked unexpectedly by the wildlife.

speaker: Jolee
text: I must say... for a while there, the Wookiees actually thought I was some kind of benevolent forest god. Amusing, really. I set them straight eventually.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't you stop the slavery of the Wookiees, then?

speaker: Jolee
text: At first, when the slavers took to hunting down lone Wookiees in the fringes of the Shadowlands, I did my best to divert them.

speaker: Jolee
text: Later, when Chuundar made his deal I didn't see any point. I wasn't here to save them from their own sad follies, after all.

speaker: Player
text: It sounds like you enjoyed being a god.

speaker: Jolee
text: Nonsense. I had no idea that's what they were thinking for a long time. I just thought they were being friendly neighbours, leaving fruit and such for me.

speaker: Jolee
text: Later, when I started to understand some of their grunting, I realized they would say prayers to the 'hairless one' before descending into the forest.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. Hairless one. I used to have plenty of hair, I tell you. *Ahem* Well, at any rate, it took a few bruises, but I set the record straight.

speaker: Player
text: A few bruises?

speaker: Jolee
text: I traveled to Rrookworro and met with the chieftain in front of everyone. Freyyr swatted at me just to see if I was real or not.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was real, and while it was a light swat, Wookiees are terribly strong. I was knocked out cold for a day. The Wookiees all thought it was quite funny.

speaker: Player
text: Wasn't it all a bit primitive for you?

speaker: Jolee
text: Not really. Kashyyyk is a place you can feel very small in. It felt good to devote my time to helping people and living simply.

speaker: Player
text: And you didn't receive any news from the outside?

speaker: Jolee
text: What can I say? I did it all for the Wookiees.

speaker: Player
text: The Wookiees?

speaker: Jolee
text: The Wookiees. Well, okay, maybe I needed some time on a quiet and remote planet... but if you ever need a friend, an incredibly strong hairball isn't a bad call.

speaker: Player
text: You are a very strange old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: Why, thank you. You're not so bad, yourself, all things considered.

speaker: Jolee
text: At any rate, we should be moving along, don't you think? If you sat around this long in the Shadowlands, a tach would eat you.

speaker: Player
text: You sound quite fond of them.

speaker: Jolee
text: I suppose I am, in a way, despite the smell. For a race of gardeners, they've developed quite interestingly.

speaker: Player
text: Gardeners?

speaker: Jolee
text: You remember the alien computer, correct? Kashyyyk was meant to be an agricultural planet. The Wookiees were made for a reason.

speaker: Jolee
text: Or, at least, that's what I'm thinking. But I'm an old man who's had a long time to develop that opinion, so don't argue with me.

speaker: Player
text: I regret asking you about this, now.

speaker: Jolee
text: See? Now you know how I feel half the time.

speaker: Player
text: You spent two decades living like that?

speaker: Player
text: I still think you're insane.

speaker: Player
text: You seemed on fairly peaceful terms with them.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well that was after two decades of helping them. They certainly didn't trust me at first.

speaker: Player
text: You could have ruled them, you know.

speaker: Jolee
text: And why would I have been interested in that? You can't spend five minutes in a Wookiee village without coming out smelling like wet fur.

speaker: Jolee
text: No, no, let them rule themselves. They can screw up their history just like every other race before them. No, I helped them in other ways.

speaker: Player
text: With good reason, I imagine.

speaker: Jolee
text: I suppose so. Not everyone would understand why the Jedi would suddenly start killing themselves and tearing up half the galaxy, would they?

speaker: Player
text: I don't see why you were wandering in the first place.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was lost. I couldn't conceive of returning to the Jedi, so what would you propose I'd done?

speaker: Player
text: You were adventuring again, I take it?

speaker: Jolee
text: Nothing so extravagant. I merely traveled from place to place... I don't even think I knew what I was searching for.

speaker: Player
text: Let me guess. Traveling from planet to planet, doing good deeds...

speaker: Player
text: So if you liked Kashyyyk so much, why did you want to leave?

speaker: Jolee
text: Are we back to *that* again?

speaker: Player
text: I find it hard to believe you left the Wookiees just for some adventure.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmmm... what's the best way for me to approach this? Ah, perhaps it's time for a little story...

speaker: Player
text: Oh, no, not another story!

speaker: Jolee
text: You just keep quiet there, you! I've had to put up with all your busy-body questions, haven't I? Well, now you'll listen to a story, dammit!

speaker: Jolee
text: *ahem* Now where was I? Oh yes, the story... you almost made me forget about it. Nice try, but I'm not that old just yet. Heh heh.

speaker: Jolee
text: Now, then. A young man sees a terribly venemous snake in his small village. Nervous, he watches the snake carefully until it leaves.

speaker: Jolee
text: The young man follows the snake into the forest. He clears the branches out of its path and helps it over obstacles. He even works to keep it fed.

speaker: Player
text: This is a very long story.

speaker: Jolee
text: Shush! Many nights pass and still the young man continues to follow the snake. He even follows it into the sands of the great desert.

speaker: Jolee
text: In the desert, the snake eventually grows hungry. It turns and bites the young man, its poison quickly working its way into his system.

speaker: Jolee
text: Finally curious, the snake looks at the boy as he lays dying and asks, "Why were you foolish enough to follow me all the way out into the desert?"

speaker: Jolee
text: The boy looks back and replies, "Did I follow you? I thought I was leading you away from everyone else..." And then he died.

speaker: Player
text: Am I supposed to be the snake?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, now, that's what I wanted to see for myself.

speaker: Player
text: That's a long way to come just to risk dying.

speaker: Jolee
text: I've come a long way as it is, and I'm going to die anyway so that doesn't bother me in the least.

speaker: Jolee
text: I've told you before that you have a destiny before you. This does not mean, however, that your future is already written. They are not the same thing.

speaker: Jolee
text: You have the choice of which direction you take your destiny in. More than engine-sucking Andor, certainly... but even he had a choice.

speaker: Jolee
text: So far you've chosen to take a darker path. You know the consequences of that... we'll see if you decide to stay your course.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm not here to judge you or tell you which path to take. I'm here ready to offer you my help... should you ask for it.

speaker: Jolee
text: I do that because I think it's important. More important than remaining in my home and pretending the galaxy doesn't exist. That's why I'm here.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you, Jolee. I'm glad you came.

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh. I'm rather glad I came, too, really. You're a fine young lad. I hope... I hope things turn out well for you.

speaker: Jolee
text: Now, then... I've chatted enough for one lifetime. Let's get this show on the road, shall we?

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh. I'm rather glad I came, too, really. You're a fine young lass. I hope... I hope things turn out well for you.

speaker: Player
text: But I don't need you, really. You're wasting your time.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. So you say, but it's my time to waste. Perhaps I can influence your decision, perhaps not... only time will tell, won't it?

speaker: Player
text: I'd prefer you were safe... elsewhere.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's very kind of you, but while elsewhere may be safer, elsewhere isn't where I think I should be. Besides... what's an old man to fear from death, eh?

speaker: Jolee
text: So far you've chosen to take the lighter path. Can you stay that course, even through the challenges ahead? We'll have to wait and see.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not a snake, I can assure you of that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, then... let's hope you're not the young man, either.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying you're frightened of me?

speaker: Jolee
text: The real question is whether or not I'm as frightened as I should be, isn't it?

speaker: Player
text: And what's your judgment so far?

speaker: Player
text: Couldn't you just answer the question for once?

speaker: Player
text: Forget I asked anything. I refuse to listen!

speaker: Player
text: I want a reason why I shouldn't just drop you off somewhere.

speaker: Player
text: Am I really all that interesting to you?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Sunry. How do you know him?

speaker: Jolee
text: What? You think because I'm a hermit I've always been a hermit? Just because I haven't seen Sunry for twenty years doesn't mean he's not a friend.

speaker: Jolee
text: A man could have changed a lot in that span of time, though. But to become a murderer? Oh, mm mm mm. I can't see it. That's not the Sunry I knew.

speaker: Jolee
text: He was a good man. Put me up in his home for a year back after I left the order. War hero, too, or so I hear.

speaker: Jolee
text: I wouldn't mind helping the fellow, if we can. I owe it to him. Or you can be a young monkey-lizard and ignore me, I guess... well, I don't expect much these days.

speaker: Player
text: I have a tape that shows Sunry killing Elassa.

speaker: Jolee
text: So you do. I once had a holodisc that showed Mandalore doing the three-step jiggy with a rancor beast. Marvelous technology we have.

speaker: Player
text: Are you suggesting the tape was falsified?

speaker: Jolee
text: It may have been. I believe you should, at least, keep that possibility in mind.

speaker: Jolee
text: If somebody was going to go through all the trouble of making a false tape to indict Sunry you think it would have 'turned up' before now.

speaker: Jolee
text: Maybe it would be a good idea to show the tape to Sunry. Perhaps he has an explanation. Or perhaps he doesn't.

speaker: Jolee
text: It would be sad if this proved that Sunry did actually perform this crime, but... the truth is the truth. Whether I like it or not.

speaker: Player
text: So what do you think of Sunry's verdict?

speaker: Jolee
text: You did what was necessary. Sunry was guilty, as sad as that fact makes me, justice had to be done.

speaker: Jolee
text: Doesn't matter that his victim was a Sith or that he was once a hero. I only wish that my old friend hadn't done it.

speaker: Jolee
text: But that's the thing about wishes. They don't come true. And now Sunry's dead, which is a shame. He *was* a good man, you know... once.

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah. I don't want to talk about this anymore. My jaw aches.

speaker: Jolee
text: You defended him well enough. I wish we had had time to look into matters more fully, but wishing is only useful for the young and idealistic.

speaker: Jolee
text: What's done is done. The Republic will likely appeal the matter eventually and he'll be free. I just... I just would like to know if that's best.

speaker: Jolee
text: Sunry was a good man once. And a good friend. I'll miss him.

speaker: Jolee
text: Innocent, mm? I don't know what to make of it, to tell the truth. Do you think justice has been done?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, of course.

speaker: Jolee
text: I see. I am not so sure. If he did kill that woman, Sunry's going to have to live with that on his conscience.

speaker: Jolee
text: And if he's justified her death in his mind... well... Sunry was a good man, once. I only hope that is still the case. I enjoyed his company.

speaker: Player
text: No, not really.

speaker: Jolee
text: But that has little to do with the law, does it? A sad state of affairs, that. Too bad, really... Sunry was a good man, once.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about this place?

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, I know plenty about Kashyyyk. You think someone doesn't live here for twenty years and pick up a thing or two?

speaker: Jolee
text: Chances are that by the time I finished telling you about it all, you would have found out for yourself. So there's no reason for me to start blathering on.

speaker: Jolee
text: It should be enough for me to tell you that there's kilometer after kilometer of trees on this planet. The deeper you go, the more dangerous it gets.

speaker: Jolee
text: If you're smart, you stay on top with the Wookiees. Go deep, however, and you may find some things you weren't expecting.

speaker: Jolee
text: And that's about all I got to say about that. Now let's get going.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind.

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, I get it. Let's play with the old man's head, is it? He's half-senile, he'll forget I said anything! Wait uh, what was this about, anyway?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, unless you're one of the local species and end up being slaughtered or enslaved, Tatooine's a nice enough desert.

speaker: Jolee
text: Pfah. Korriban's a rock. Mind the Sith.

speaker: Jolee
text: Manaan's an unusual place. Not for its water, mind you... it's the kolto. Healing juice. Only place where it occurs in the galaxy.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. Hard to say what this planet is. Been lost for thousands of years, if not more. *Sniff* Smells like bad, bad karma so watch your step.

speaker: Jolee
text: It's a ship. To be more specific, it's *your* ship. You tell me.

speaker: Jolee
text: No more than you. Get going.

speaker: Player
text: Can you make a healing kit for me?

speaker: Jolee
text: How many could you possibly need? And besides, I don't have enough supplies on me to put some more together.
comment: if the PC has too many kits

speaker: Jolee
text: Ask me later when you're actually in need and I'm less tired. I'm not a kit factory, you know.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. I suppose I could whip up something, uh... you know... few herbs and such. You do know that the best alternative is not to get hurt, right?

speaker: Jolee
text: Not to say that you go leaping into the path of blaster fire or anything, but I know how you young people get. Here, take it.

speaker: Player
text: We have a stowaway on the ship. Do you have any advice for me?

speaker: Jolee
text: Stop bothering me with your questions! I can barely hear myself think.

speaker: Player
text: Have you seen all these gizka we have on board?

speaker: Jolee
text: *Sigh* I have no idea what you're talking about. Rabble rabble... what are you saying.

speaker: Player
text: [Don't speak to him.]

speaker: Jolee
text: [You decide to ignore Jolee and continue on with your quest for now, though it might be a good idea to speak with him later.]

speaker: Jolee
text: There'll be time for chatter after we find whatever has caused this disturbance in the Force. It's dangerous, so keep on your toes.

speaker: Jolee
text: *whisper* The Jedi Council wouldn't approve, but they always were a little stodgy about using the Force on people. Sometimes you gotta do what you gotta do.

speaker: Jolee
text: I know I'm just an old codger, but in my time I've learned what goes around comes around. These things have a way of coming back to you in the end.

speaker: Jolee
text: *whisper* Heh! Reminds me of my old smuggling days. Nothing better than the old Jedi mind trick for getting past an overly curious customs officer.

speaker: Jolee
text: You've got a real mean streak, kid. You might want to work on that; nasty people tend to come to nasty ends.

speaker: Jolee
text: Nice. Real nice. Maybe later we could find some insects to pull the legs off, huh?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hey, kid, that was a good thing you did there. Almost brought a tear to this old man's eye.

speaker: Outcast Woman
text: I had fine clothes, a beautiful bed - now I wear rags and I sleep on the ground like an animal! Were my crimes so horrible that I should now suffer like this?

speaker: Outcast Woman
text: We have no food, no weapons - nothing! How can we live like this? We are doomed.

speaker: Tach
text: [This tach may be Rulan Prolik in disguise, but you can't tell for sure. Maybe if you kill it, it will revert to its true form... assuming it's Rulan.]

speaker: Player
text: [Attack the tach.]

speaker: Player
text: [Leave the tach alone.]

text: The droid is busy carrying out the instructions you programmed into it earlier. It can't be reprogrammed right now.

speaker: Pool Droid
text: The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

speaker: Pool Droid

text: Program droid to crawl into pool and self destruct. (<CUSTOM44> repair part(s))

speaker: Player
text: Leave it alone.

text: You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid. (1 repair part)

speaker: Pool Droid
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: So you're the one Roland has got to help us interrogate this prisoner. I hope your Jedi powers will come in useful, this one has been most resistant.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: He's a Sith spy we picked up a little while ago snooping around outside trying to get in. We thought he was suspicious and brought him inside when the Selkath weren't looking.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: But it seems the Sith have done a pretty good job of conditioning this guy, and we haven't been able to break him yet.

speaker: Player
text: What did they do to him?

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: The Sith protect their really important spies with some sort of mental Force feedback system. They can turn their minds in on themselves so Force compulsions won't affect them.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Combine this with conventional training to resist interrogation and it sometimes takes months to get them to tell what they know.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Do you want to interrogate him now?

speaker: Player
text: Yes.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: While the training the Sith gave him will protect him from most normal interrogation techniques, and also from Force persuasion, we have found a few hooks you might find useful.
comment: if the player has not interrogated him before

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: He was with another man when he was first spotted. We think it was another spy, but we didn't manage to catch him.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: We also seized some personal documents he had on him when he was captured. It would seem that he's married to a woman named Tela.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: We checked this in our computers and it seems to hold up. We've sent a couple agents to investigate, but it may be a while.

speaker: Player
text: What do I have to work with?

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: What we have here is your standard issue truth serum. It should make him spill his guts in no time. BUT, there is a catch...

speaker: Player
text: A catch?

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Because of his conditioning, he's able to resist it at small doses. But if you give him too much, his body realizes what you're trying to do and shuts his mind down completely.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: If you do that, you'll have to inject him with an antidote that neutralizes the truth serum. Unfortunately, that, too, has a drawback.

speaker: Player
text: I detect a pattern here...

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: It causes short term memory loss. This may work to your advantage, because you can try the same tactic over and over again. But if you use it too much, he may forget everything we want to know.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Shall we get started then?

speaker: Player
text: Not right now.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: No problem. He's not going anywhere for a LONG time.

speaker: Player
text: Let's get started.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Ok, but you should know what we have to work with here first.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Let's get it started then.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [The prisoner looks dazed.  He has been injected with a dose of truth serum by the Republic officer. It's up to you to try to persuade him to talk with you now.]

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: Uhhh.... *groan*

speaker: Player
text: Inject him with truth serum.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: He's already too full of this stuff as it is. You should question him now, because he's as pliable as he's going to get!

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: You should be careful not to give him too high a dose. He should be more pliable now.

speaker: Player
text: Interrogate him.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: Wh... What do you want?

speaker: Player
text: Relax. I'm not here to threaten you.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: You're not? You... Lies! You work for the Republic!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] We're the only ones who will take you in now.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: The Sith will never trust you again, spy! We're the only place you have left! Tell us what we want to know!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Urgg... No! Never!...

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Damn, he blanked out!

speaker: Player
text: Inject him with the neutralizing agent and start over with a new dose of truth serum.

speaker: Player
text: Stop talking to him.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Giving up so soon? I think he could last a bit longer. Come back if you want to try to break him again. He's not going anywhere for a LONG time.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] But they... they wouldn't.... would they?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] If you talk, we can make it worth your while.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] Ha! Worth my while... The Sith don't pay very well, but they'd kill me...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I don't want to hurt you unless you make me.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] Please... Please don't hurt me...

speaker: Player
text: Let's try something else.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Faiure] There's nothing you can do to me, Jedi, that the Sith wouldn't do worse! I'm not afraid of you!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] You think me weak enough to give in to false promises of wealth and riches? The Sith are stronger than that! We will have it all eventually anyway!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Never! I am Sith, I will never betray them! Your Republic is weak and will soon fall at any rate!

speaker: Player
text: We know about your companion.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: What... what companion?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] We don't really need you. Your companion will tell us what we need to know anyway.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: The gutless Sith worm is already starting to crack. We'll have what we need within hours.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] He wouldn't talk... or has he already? No...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] If you don't tell us, he will suffer.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] But he... I... Please don't hurt us.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Perhaps we would give you back to the Sith, but keep him.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Of course they would never believe we let you go so easily. But they would all too happily believe you betrayed them.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] Alright! Alright! I'll tell you what you want to know.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: What's the passcode to the Sith base?

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: It... It's... zeta 245698 alpha... just... no more.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Good. With this pass, you should be able to get into the Sith base without trouble.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Just don't delay too long, or they might learn that he's been captured.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] You can't do this to me! They would kill me in ways too horrible for you to imagine!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] The Sith are not that easy to fool! We would see through your petty deceptions and destroy you for the way you try to humiliate us!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Nothing you could do to us would make us talk! We Sith are stronger than you give us credit for!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Ha! The Sith are stronger than you; each one of us! You'll never break us!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe we should do something about Tela.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: T... Tela? How did you find out about her?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] We could make life easy for both of you here in the Republic.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] Yes...it could be... so much easier...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Talk or something may happen to her.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Success] No! Please don't hurt her! Please...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] We have her already. She may be spared if you talk.

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Ha! You couldn't have her! You're bluffing, Jedi scum!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] Do whatever you want! I know you will fail! My fellow Sith are probably even now trying to free me!

speaker: Sith Prisoner
text: [Failure] You think bribes will work? You must be dumber than I thought to think that a Sith would join the losing side just for credits!

speaker: Player
text: What was he doing out there?

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: We're not sure exactly... If you can convince him to talk, we should be able to find that all out.

speaker: Player
text: I will interrogate him now.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this now.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Well if it's so important, just go then. Not like losing that droid would do anything harmful... like getting us banned from Manaan!

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Good job in getting the pass code out of him. I was sure he couldn't be broken.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: You're back. Do you want to interrogate the prisoner?

speaker: Player
text: I have a passcard to the Sith base.

speaker: Intelligence Officer
text: Oh, OK. If you need to find out anything else from this prisoner, though, he'll be here for quite a while, I'm thinking.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: Why do you bother me, human? I do not wish to speak to you.

speaker: Player
text: I just wanted to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: I am not here to give you knowledge. Do business with me or leave.

speaker: Player
text: Business?

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: I trade and sell Pazaak Cards for those that have interest. If you have interest, then we can do business. Otherwise leave.

speaker: Player
text: Let's see what you've got.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: Very well.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, I'll leave.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: Good.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you just standing here in a corner?

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: I am here for my own reasons. Those who know of me and wish to do business, know I can be found here.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: You will either do business with me or leave.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind.

speaker: Shady Rodian
text: Leave, human.

speaker: Jedi
text: Good day to you. I am afraid I cannot speak to you at the moment. I apologize.

text: The kath hounds seem to have calmed down. The settlers must be relieved.

text: Please, don't disturb me; I have pressing matters at hand.

text: I hear that the Sith have defeated another Republic battlefleet. I do not know how much longer the Republic can last.

speaker: Jedi
text: I fear it is only a matter of time before the Sith find us here, too...

text: Dantooine has a splendid environment. I would hate to see it damaged by too many settlers.

speaker: Jedi
text: If you are seeking information, perhaps the Jedi Council will help. I am afraid I cannot.

speaker: Jedi
text: It is relaxing to come outside and enjoy the fresh air once in a while. It relieves stress.

text: Freyyr is returned to us! The madness of Chuundar will be undone. It is a great day, and I'm told it is becasue of you, <FullName>.

text: And you, Zaalbar, you fought for us even when shunned. All of Rwookrrorro is grateful, and also shamed for the way you were treated.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am proud of today. Yesterday is forgotten.

speaker: Player
text: I need to ask you some questions.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I will answer if I can.

text: Are there local concerns besides the slavers?

text: Rorworr was missing, but you know that. You caught his killer and made sure he was executed.

text: I am grateful you have kept order, but the whole matter makes me sad.

text: I'm looking for a Star Map.

text: I don't know about that. You outsiders from away are always looking for strange things. It makes you crazy.

text: Maybe you should search for that fool living in the Shadowlands. Our hunters say they see him from time to time and sometimes he helps them.

text: Madam, I am not a fool. I survive because I am careful.

speaker: Wookiee
text: See, you are all crazy. You can't be him. The hunters say he is a great warrior and fearsome.

speaker: Player
text: Farewell.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Goodbye then. Thank you.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I don't know how he stays alive. Maybe animals won't eat crazy-meat. I don't know.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Rorworr was missing, but you know that. You caught his killer and showed that justice can be merciful.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Rorworr is missing. He's one of our most promising warriors. I still hope he will be found alive, but no one knows where he is.

speaker: Player
text: Who could I talk to about that?

speaker: Wookiee
text: Woorwill and Jaarak are his friends. You could speak with them. They are in Jaarak's home on the central village tree platform.

speaker: Player
text: Who do I talk to if I know about this?

speaker: Wookiee
text: His friends Woorwill and Jaarak would like to hear any news. They are in Jaarak's home on the central village tree platfom.

speaker: Wookiee
text: If there was a crime, tell Worrroznor, Holder of the Laws. His home is east of the central village tree.

speaker: Player
text: It was like managing foolish children.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You taint yourself with your words. You are a friend to us. Don't ruin it with your crazy outsider ways.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad I could help.

speaker: Wookiee
text: And we are glad you did. Thank you. We will be strong again.

speaker: Wookiee
text: What can I do for you?

text: Leave me, human outsider. I do not wish to speak with you.

text: I want to ask you some questions.

text: Because I demand it! Do not anger me!

text: Surely that is no way to gain co-operation from the Wookiees. Some subtlety is not out of the question, is it?

speaker: Wookiee
text: We are threatened everyday. You are just another body in the army we face from all sides, at all times.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You see the dignity of my people? We will overcome.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Don't speak for me, mad-claw. You left in shame. Time has not changed that.

speaker: Player
text: Why do your leaders allow slavers to take your people?

speaker: Wookiee
text: What right do you have to question Chuundar? What could you possibly know about us?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me so I might understand.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Your interest is surprising. I had not thought an outsider would care. Still, I shouldn't talk of our troubles.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Chuundar is our leader, and deserving of respect. Even with our doubts.

speaker: Player
text: Who would you rather have as leader?

speaker: Wookiee
text: There is no one. Chuundar is unquestioned. You have seen to that, have you not? Speak no more of it.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to tell me your doubts about Chuundar.

speaker: Wookiee
text: [Success] I should tell someone... we whisper it anyway. Everyone wonders about it.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Chuundar has done much. He keeps the slavers from the village, and rules fairly. He keeps order, and keeps us strong.

speaker: Wookiee
text: But... his father was better. Freyyr the Chieftain would not have allowed the slaver docking platforms to be built. That's why he was killed.

speaker: Player
text: When did Freyyr die?

speaker: Wookiee
text: I don't want to think about this. You test my patience, outsider.

speaker: Player
text: What if I told you Chuundar is in league with the slavers?

speaker: Wookiee
text: I would not believe you. You are an outsider. You lie. You cheat. You enslave us. There is nothing you could say to make me believe.

speaker: Player
text: I want to go back to my previous questions.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Be brief. I tire of this.

speaker: Player
text: Any recent trouble other than the slavers?

speaker: Wookiee
text: The body of Rorworr was found. He was a promising warrior. We will mourn him fiercely.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You know this. You made certain his killer was executed. Was it for justice, or just the payment you recieved?
comment: Player had Jaarak killed after dead local hero plot.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Go on, mercenary, leave me alone. I haven't the money to pay for your loyalty.

speaker: Player
text: I seek something called a Star Map.
comment: player has not found star map

speaker: Wookiee
text: I don't know about anything like that, but I don't understand you body-bald fools. You are all slavers or crazy.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you say we're crazy?

speaker: Wookiee
text: Our hunters say one of you has been living in the Shadowlands, and that is crazy! I don't know how he survives.

speaker: Wookiee
text: It's probably just hunter-tales, though. No one could live in the Shadowlands for the years he has. No one.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, a gifted few, perhaps.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Maybe insanity makes you taste bad. I don't know. You tell me.

speaker: Player
text: If the Shadowlands are so dangerous, why go?

speaker: Wookiee
text: We go for ritual, to prove ourselves. Some exiles are forced to live there. What other choice do they have? Slavery?

speaker: Player
text: What exiles live there now?

speaker: Wookiee
text: I know of none. I do not enter the Shadowlands. I only hear stories. Nobody really believes them.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Please, do not bother me again.

speaker: Player
text: Chuundar wants me to find an insane Wookiee in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I am ashamed that he would ask outsiders to track such a creature. Why couldn't our own hunters remove his dishonor?

speaker: Wookiee
text: If you must be the one, then so be it. Be merciful and quick. A Wookiee without the honor of self-control is a mere animal.

speaker: Wookiee
text: And when you are through, do the same to your slave Zaalbar. His taint is a curse upon us too. Bah, I will speak no more of him.

speaker: Wookiee
text: This is no secret to you. For whatever reason, you made certain justice was merciful in this matter.
comment: player pleaded for Jaakar's life in dead local hero plot.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I still do not trust you, but you have a small measure of thanks for this.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Another of our people is missing. If the slavers were responsible, more would have disappeared. This was just one Wookiee.

speaker: Wookiee
text: It may be that he died in the Shadowlands. If he did, there is honor in that, and he will be mourned.

speaker: Player
text: Who would know more?

speaker: Wookiee
text: What makes it your business? Bah, I have nothing to say. Speak with his friends, if you must.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Woorwill and Jaarak maintain a vigil in Woorwil's home on the central platform on the village.

speaker: Player
text: Who should I talk to if I have information about his disappearance?

speaker: Wookiee
text: His friends Woorwill and Jaarak will want to know. If it was not natural, Worrroznor must be told. He is the Holder of the Laws.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Woorwill's home is on the central tree of the village. Worrroznor maintains court on the platform just to the east of there.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Soon after the mad son Zaalbar was sent away. Freyyr seemed to succumb to the same kind of insanity.

speaker: Wookiee
text: It is thought that he died fighting slavers. I like to think so. Chuundar has bravely risen to lead us, despite his troubles.

speaker: Wookiee
text: [Failure] No, no I don't. You see, your kind are all mad. You don't understand a thing said to you.

speaker: Wookiee
text: There is no one left that is willing to stand up to the slavers. We wait for the coming of Bacca's heir.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by that? Explain.

speaker: Wookiee
text: The ancient Bacca was our greatest leader. At his death, he swore that his spirit would live in our true chieftains.

speaker: Wookiee
text: His sword would be the sign, and legends say we have always prospered under those that held it. No longer.

speaker: Wookiee
text: No one has seen the blade for years. It is a foolish hope. We now follow Chuundar. He is sane and honorable.

speaker: Player
text: I don't give you much thought. You are primitives.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Primitive? Our traditions are ancient! There is great order and honor in how we live! Even with our... troubles.

speaker: Player
text: Then I will ask about other things.

speaker: Wookiee
text: No, I will not fear you. Ask what you will, but save your threats. I am numb to them.

speaker: Juhani
text: Threatening her may not get you the results you want.

speaker: Player
text: I am not your enemy. I serve the greater good.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I shall believe that when I see it. I will speak with you, but do not mistake that for trust.

speaker: Player
text: I travel with a Wookiee. I am a friend.

speaker: Wookiee
text: You have a Wookiee marked by exile as a slave. If he is your property, he is no Wookiee. Not until he kills you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am not a slave. I have made a life debt.

speaker: Wookiee
text: To an outsider? You truly are a mad-claw. Don't taint my ears with your ravings. I'll speak to your owner, not you.

speaker: Wookiee
text: I will speak with you a moment, but do not pretend to be a friend. I trust only the word of Chuundar.

speaker: Player
text: I go where I wish. Will you stop me?

speaker: Player
text: I will leave you. Goodbye.

speaker: Wookiee
text: Why do you bother me, human? I don't wish to speak with you.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: What?

speaker: Beast
text: RRRRAAAAAAARRRRRGGGG!!!!

speaker: Beast
text: Run, run!

speaker: Iziz
text: You come back, but you are the one we remember that threatened. Why rescue the tribe of Iziz only to threaten?

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a Star Map. Know anything about it?
comment: player does not already have star map. Remove Komad from the hunter's lodge. he doesn't return until after the completion of the dragon plot

speaker: Iziz
text: If that is what you seek, take this map to the Eastern Dune Sea. It will let you take the long journey.
comment: player does not have a map

speaker: Iziz
text: Go, and find the lair that we once dug. A dragon lives there, inside with your Star Map. You do what you must.

speaker: Iziz
text: Whatever happens, just leave we of Jawa alone. We will have no more of you. We remember all that comes before.

speaker: Iziz
text: You have a map to the Eastern Dune Sea. You have been handed the directions. If you fail now, blame yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I don't need anything else from you.

speaker: Iziz
text: Go. We remember the threats. Jawas will always remember.

speaker: Iziz
text: You of your kind, Iziz of Jawa would thank you for what was done. Mine have returned because of you.
comment: selected Player has rescued the Jawas

speaker: Iziz
text: We hope we traded fair with you. Was there something else that you might want?

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map. Can you help?
comment: player does not already have star map. Remove Komad from the hunter's lodge. he doesn't return until after the completion of the dragon plot

speaker: Iziz
text: You have saved the tribe of Iziz, and we of Jawa are willing to trade. I know of this, but it is far away.

speaker: Iziz
text: In the sands of the east, the Eastern Dune Sea, we dig for the People of Sand and find this strange thing of the people before.

speaker: Iziz
text: We did not take it because of dragons in the lair. That is where you have to go. Take this map to the eastern dunes.
comment: Player does not have map Give player map.

speaker: Player
text: A dragon? What kind of creature is that?

speaker: Iziz
text: The greatest of the desert. There is no larger. Bigger than the big machines. Jawas don't know how to fight something so big.

speaker: Iziz
text: There is a hunter, a Twi'lek. He has seen many things. Look in the Eastern Dune Sea when you go and he may help.

speaker: Player
text: I dealt with the dragon. I saw no map.

speaker: Iziz
text: I do not know what your eyes did not see. It is there, in the darkest of the lair. Look, and you will see.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you. Goodbye.

speaker: Iziz
text: You are a good friend of the Jawas. We will remember when your kind are gone. Ask if you need any more of anything.

speaker: Player
text: That will be fine. Good luck.

speaker: Player
text: I think I should ask for more.

speaker: Iziz
text: Iziz and the tribe are all of the same possessions. We have given what was agreed by all. There is little more.

speaker: Player
text: All right. Just get out of here, then.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] You know the rescue was worth more.

speaker: Iziz
text: [Success] Proper trade gives value where deserved. You are right to call the deal an error.

speaker: Iziz
text: More for you, but that is all. Thanks are yours, but now we must go. We remember, and thank.

speaker: Iziz
text: [Failure] The deal was fair traded. Your service was given what value it was deserved, plus thanks.

speaker: Player
text: Then I'll have to take it out of your hide!

speaker: Cand
text: That's the way - squeeze that little guy for every credit he's got!

speaker: HK47
text: Request: Let me deal with him, master. It would be so much fun!

speaker: Jolee
text: Oh, I get it. He's small and helpless so we can just do whatever we want, right? Sometimes I just don't know about you, kid.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, why are you being so mean to this little guy? What did he ever do to you?

speaker: Carth
text: I know Jawas don't have the best reputation, but that doesn't mean we can just treat them like this!

speaker: Juhani
text: I do not approve of this. This is not how a Jedi should behave.

speaker: Bastila
text: This nothing but wanton greed and cruelty! Beware, lest these things lead you to the dark side.

speaker: Iziz
text: Threats upon me! Take what you want from we of the tribe, but we remember! We remember when you are gone!

speaker: Iziz
text: Leave us to be. This is not right. Why save only to threaten?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You will pay me more and like it.

speaker: Iziz
text: [Success] Eeee... trade needs to change... you should take more. Iziz says it is so.

speaker: Player
text: You'll give me more or you will regret it.

speaker: Iziz
text: Already do you have a map for the eastern dunes. Follow it and you will find what you need in the lair of the dragon.

speaker: Iziz
text: It is as was agreed, as Iziz hoped it was. I have things to give you... take and be welcome.
comment: Player previously talked to Iziz and recieved the quest Give player some item. An older sounding weapon or something that the Jawas might have scavenged.

speaker: Iziz
text: You are not known, so why you did this, I don't know, but thanks are given just the same.
comment: Player had not previously talked to Iziz to get the quest.

speaker: Iziz
text: You will have some things for yourself, as thanks for what was done. Take and be welcome.
comment: Player previously talked to Iziz and recieved the quest Give player some item. An older sounding weapon or something that the Jawas might have scavenged. Same item that is given above on "It is as was agreed, as Iziz hoped it was. I have things to give you... take and be welcome." line.

speaker: Iziz
text: You there, of your kind, can you help Iziz of Jawa? There are troubles from the ghosts among the sands.
comment: Initial Jawa initiates on proximity Iziz speaks in a odd manner. The description for Jawas mentioned that their language is hard to understand, and when quoted, they are usually speaking in a cryptic manner. I've set them up as creatures that have a sense of history and the age of the planet, but no real recorded history that could provide details.

speaker: Player
text: Could you be clearer? I'm having trouble understanding you.

speaker: HK47
text: Statement: It is doubtful he can be clearer. Their language is difficult even for droids. He is using a trade language to try and help.

speaker: Iziz
text: The trouble is yours, not of Jawa. We must use a language of trade because you listen complicated to what we say simply.

speaker: Player
text: Why wouldn't I understand your true language?

speaker: Iziz
text: That is not a problem for Jawa to have for you. You have the ears that do not listen.

speaker: Player
text: What is it that you want, Jawa?

speaker: Iziz
text: Iziz, I am. Leader of the tribe that is mine. You are the same in kind, a leader that stands before your tribe?

speaker: Carth
text: Leader of our tribe? Heh. That's a new one.

speaker: Iziz
text: There are troubles that we have. The giants made of sand, they are horned ghosts that take us away.

speaker: Player
text: HK-47, can you help me out here?

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: 98% probability that members of the miniature organic's tribe are being held by Sand People, master. Doubtless he wishes assistance.

speaker: Player
text: What about the other 2%.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: 2% probability that the miniature organic is simply looking for trouble and needs to be blasted. That may be wishful thinking on my part, master.

speaker: Player
text: So, Iziz, what do you want me to do?

speaker: Iziz
text: There has been no help given by asking the great group that digs with machines. Now Iziz asks you.

speaker: Iziz
text: You have stopped their attacks, so you have been where we are trapped. We will offer a trade for this help.

speaker: Iziz
text: Long have we scavenged, among you and those that came before. We have things you will like for this service.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about where your people are. Maybe I'll help.

speaker: Iziz
text: You know! You must know! You have stopped the attacks! Far to the south, where they hold everything stolen.

speaker: Player
text: A few more questions, all right?

speaker: Iziz
text: Iziz answers hoping you will free the tribe that he holds.

speaker: Player
text: Why have they taken your people?

speaker: Iziz
text: We find things, and they use them. Jawas slave, serving. They lead with the whip and gaffi.

speaker: Bastila
text: So these Jawas are scavengers who are enslaved by the Sand People? I think I am beginning to understand his plight.

speaker: Iziz
text: With the group that digs, we trade and are free. With People of the Sand, we serve and die. We prefer you.

speaker: Player
text: I'll expect payment if I do this, Jawa.

speaker: Iziz
text: A trade can be made of this for that. Iziz will see it done. We thank.

speaker: Player
text: I'll check it out when I leave the city. Goodbye.

speaker: Iziz
text: Iziz hopes you have the luck you need.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested.

speaker: Iziz
text: Iziz will reward you if you find them anyway. Just please also look.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about "those that came before."

speaker: Iziz
text: You stand on Anchorhead, a place named and named again. You come to dig, but it was already dug.

speaker: Iziz
text: Settled over and over. Also long ago, ships fell after battles above. Now we scavenge and find the pieces.

speaker: Carth
text: Hmm. I wonder just how long ago the little fella is talking, here?

speaker: Bastila
text: It could be that this Jawa knows things about this planet's history that the Republic has no inkling of.

speaker: Iziz
text: You dig the ore and dirt. In time from now, we will dig you, just like digging those that came before.

speaker: Iziz
text: People of the Sand in the sand. There is a place in the far south where they live.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm thinking they're with the Sand People, who live in the south. Either that or I need my ears cleaned.

speaker: Iziz
text: The approach holds great fighting. Bring the tribe from in to out and there will be payment in trade and thanks.

speaker: Iziz
text: I ask that you find us, and then bring away from the People of Sand. Then we will offer a trade with you.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested, Iziz. I'm looking for more important things.

speaker: Iziz
text: Here is where we could be friends, for the Jawa find important things all the time. Things from before.

speaker: Player
text: Go away. I don't have time for you.

speaker: Iziz
text: Like all of you, of your kind. Never listening, never wanting. Jawa are more than scavenger traders.

speaker: Iziz
text: A little help would be returned. We know of things... things you don't. Leave then, and never know.

speaker: Player
text: Giants made of sand... Sand People?

speaker: Iziz
text: That is they! You know them well, because you have already stopped their killing. I would ask just a small sum more.

speaker: Iziz
text: That is how you know them. Giants are different for us, we being smaller. People of Sand are who I mean.

speaker: Player
text: Stupid creature, can't you make more sense?

speaker: Iziz
text: You speak to me for another time. What are you wanting? I have asked the task and wait for your action.

speaker: Iziz
text: Those of Jawa remain with the People of the Sand. Slaves under whip and gaffi. Will you help to find?

speaker: Doba
text: I've got to to give you credit... you put in a solid run, rookie. There's no way I could match your times.

speaker: Doba
text: But Anglu's knocked you off the leaderboard. The Beks are going to win this thing unless you get out there and beat her time with that souped up swoop of yours.

speaker: Doba
text: But you can't compete with Redros. He's the best rider we've got. He's a lock to win the champion's prize with the race he just ran!

speaker: Doba
text: Hey, look at this: fresh meat on the track. Well don't get your hopes up, rookie... no first year rider has ever won the swoop racing season opener.

speaker: Doba
text: Your might have an edge because of that prototype accelerator Kandon gave you, but it won't help if it blows up while you're out on the track.

speaker: Doba
text: Gadon must be getting desperate if he's grabbing first timers off the street. When we Vulkars win this year, it'll be over for you Hidden Beks!

speaker: Doba
text: Well, you didn't get yourself killed out there rookie, but your time isn't going to get you into the winner's circle.

speaker: Doba
text: Don't bother me... I've got to stay focused if I want to compete with the likes of Anglu and Redros.

speaker: Settler
text: I heard the rogue Jedi girl was killed. Good riddance! We don't need any Dark Jedi here on Dantooine!

speaker: Settler
text: One of the Jedi managed to turn that Dark Jedi girl back to the light side. That's a relief!

speaker: Settler
text: Did you hear about the young Jedi girl from a couple days ago? I heard she hurt her master pretty bad...

speaker: Settler
text: I heard another Republic fleet was wiped out in this sector! I hope they don't find the Jedi here!

speaker: Settler
text: Master Quatra was hurt very badly. She might die. I heard it was her own apprentice that did it.

speaker: Settler
text: Did you hear? The Sandrals and Matales massacred each other! It's horrible!

speaker: Settler
text: Ahlan Matale locked himself up in his estate with his son. I wonder what the boy did.

speaker: Settler
text: The children of Nurik Sandral and Ahlan Matale apparently fled here to the Enclave. Their families are both very mad.

speaker: Settler
text: Did you hear? Shen Matale and Rahasia Sandral are getting married! I would never have thought their fathers would allow it!

speaker: Settler
text: Ahlan Matale likes to lord his wealth over the rest of us. What I wouldn't give for him to eat his own words... His son seems like a nice boy though.

speaker: Settler
text: I heard there was fighting coreward towards Coruscant. I wonder if the Republic will survive...

speaker: Settler
text: Rahasia Sandral is a nice young woman. But her father has been keeping her at their estate since her brother went missing...

speaker: Settler
text: You know those stones to the east of here? I heard they did some digging and found they aren't natural.

speaker: Settler
text: The Council's been telling us not to go near the stones to the east. Just as well, the kath hounds near there seem a lot more vicious...

speaker: Settler
text: I heard the Jedi finally got off their behinds and did something about the Mandalorians! Took them long enough!

speaker: Settler
text: Those damn Mandalorians have been raiding farms all over this continent. The Jedi won't do anything, so where does that leave us?

speaker: Settler
text: I hear the Sith have been beating the Republic pretty bad. They must've spent the whole time building ships since we beat them last time.

speaker: Settler
text: I don't understand why the Jedi Council are hiding here. Shouldn't they be helping the Republic?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Unghhh! Stop! I... I yield!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are... too strong for me. I was a fool to think otherwise. I am... at your mercy.

speaker: Player
text: Mercy? You won't find any here!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Then it ends here.

speaker: Player
text: I... have no other choice. I'm sorry.
