speaker: Player
text: You ask for mercy? You, a Sith?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... suppose I am. Something tells me that you are... not like the other students. I don't know why that is.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... was right the first time, back at the cantina, wasn't I? There is something different about you... more so than I even suspected.

speaker: Player
text: I can't talk about that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: No, I don't suppose you can.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: So what happens now? Will you show me mercy? Will you... just let me leave?

speaker: Player
text: I can't do that. I'm sorry, but I have to kill you.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... understand. May the Force serve you well.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me why you tried to kill me, first.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I had no choice. You... reminded me too much of a time before I became a Sith. I... didn't want to think about that.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Maybe you *should* think about it.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Success] I... suppose you could be right.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: All the things I wanted to do, all the wrongs I wanted to right... I haven't done any of it. They just get farther and farther from my mind.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: All I've cared about is power and... and myself. This isn't the person I was.

speaker: Player
text: There's still time to change that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You're right. Maybe... maybe what I needed most was peace, after all. The Jedi tried to show me that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I don't know if I can ever go back to them... but my place isn't here. Thank you... thank you for showing me that.

speaker: Juhani
text: Remember this in the future. Mercy, compassion: these are the things that give the light side the power to stand against the dark.

speaker: Jolee
text: Take an old man's advice, Yuthura. I know the Jedi aren't as perfect as they think they are, but they're way is a lot better than the way of the Sith.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You have a destiny, my friend, and I wish you well on your way to it. May the Force... be with you.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, but I have to kill you now.

speaker: Player
text: Go... before I change my mind.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Very well. I... won't stop you, or mention what you've done here.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You have a destiny to fulfill, and that does not involve you joining the Sith... at least not yet. I won't keep you from it. May the Force serve you well.

speaker: Player
text: You could come with me.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: That's... tempting, but I don't think I could. Your path... it goes somewhere I can't follow.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Maybe you need to think about your own path.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are too powerful. You would never be my second for long... if the academy even truly interested you.

speaker: Player
text: No, it never interested me. You were a fool... now you must die.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... I see. Then let us end this here.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not here to become a Sith. I got what I came for.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I didn't think you were here to train. Not really. I should have realized that sooner.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not all that different. I just don't want to kill you.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: That alone makes you different. Most of the Sith here... would not think twice about it.

speaker: Player
text: Indeed. I am Darth Revan.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I see. I should have known... right from the beginning. But you are no longer the Dark Lord you once were, are you?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are Revan... but yet you are not. What I sense of your destiny is... is still unclear.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are... too strong for me. Gather your hatred and strike me down... if that is your will.

speaker: Player
text: I have no problem with that. Die!!

speaker: Player
text: Go on. Get out of here.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As I thought. You are no Sith. A real Sith would have no hesitation in striking me down.

speaker: Player
text: Good point. Time to die!!

speaker: Rakatan Guide
text: The ancient traditions state that you must enter the Temple alone. I will not perform the ritual if there are others with you.

speaker: Jolee

speaker: Rakatan Guide
text: No other can go with you into the Temple. You must enter alone. That is the way of the ancient ritual.

speaker: Rakatan Guide

speaker: Player

speaker: Rakatan Guide

speaker: Player

speaker: Jolee
text: I had a... a premonition. A vision through the Force. There's great danger inside that Temple. I can't let you face it alone.

speaker: Captive

speaker: Selkath
text: I have no wish to talk with your kind, off-worlder! I have heard the rumors. We Selkath know your kind are to blame for the poor kolto harvest.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to ask you some questions.

speaker: Selkath
text: Consult your own diplomat if you have questions, off-worlder. If you do not know of him, go to the Republic enclave and find him.

speaker: Selkath
text: He is paid to be of service to your kind - I am not. I believe this concludes our conversation.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry. I'll be going now.

speaker: Selkath
text: First you interrupt my thoughts, then you scuttle off. You off-worlders are a curious bunch. It is no wonder I find so few of you worth talking to.

speaker: Player
text: You need an attitude adjustment!

speaker: Selkath
text: If you are fool enough to draw your weapon, you will find yourself locked up for a long, long time.

speaker: Selkath
text: I have nothing further to say to a thug such as you.

speaker: Player
text: You Selkath blame without any proof!

speaker: Selkath
text: We have a saying here on Manaan - you can know the what is beneath the water by the ripples on the surface. Do you understand, off-worlder?

speaker: Player
text: I think so.

speaker: Selkath
text: The Manaan authorities may not have the proof to proceed with official diplomatic sanctions against the Republic, but we Selkath know who is to blame.

speaker: Selkath
text: I see no further point in continuing this conversation.

speaker: Player
text: Not really.

speaker: Selkath
text: We know that you have some connection with the souring of relations between our government and the Republic. Whatever your Republic may be up to, we Selkath shall find out!

speaker: Selkath
text: Your kind has done nothing but disrupt our lives since you came here! We want nothing to do with any of you!

speaker: Selkath
text: Why do you disturb me, off-worlder? Are you trying to recruit me to your cause? You should save your lung gas - this Selkath's neutrality is not for sale.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Selkath
text: It is well known that off-worlders have been recruiting the Selkath to join their organizations in an effort to undermine Manann's neutrality.

speaker: Selkath
text: Just recently the Sith were given harsh diplomatic penalties for these actions. Now you are trying to recruit me.

speaker: Player
text: I'm the one who exposed the Sith!

speaker: Selkath
text: So you say, off-worlder... but I have my doubts. I believe this conversation is completed.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not trying to recruit you.

speaker: Player
text: I think you're paranoid.

speaker: Selkath
text: Why are you disturbing me, off-worlder? I did not indicate I wished to converse with you.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Greetings. I don't think I've seen you at the academy before. Here to investigate the ruins?
comment: if selected and the player is a student at the academy (kor_yuthura1 equals 2). Other Sith at the site will be gathered in clumps or working on the dig (if this is possible, animation-wise). NOTE: Need to add an immediate interjection by Juhani, if she is in the party

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: My name's Dak Vesser. I'm assigned to the valley ruins, as you can see. We've been painstakingly uncovering these tombs for many months, now.

speaker: Juhani
text: Dak? That is you, isn't it? I... hardly recognized you.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: It's been a long time, Juhani.

speaker: Juhani
text: What are you doing here? Did... did you fall to the dark side?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: I didn't 'fall', Juhani... I had my eyes opened. And don't look at me like that. Last I recall, you were having your own doubts.

speaker: Juhani
text: I was. I'm not anymore. Dak... you could...

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Save it. The Jedi aren't for me... not anymore. Look... I'm not going to ask why a couple of Jedi are in the Valley of the Dark Lords.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: I don't want to know. It's better that I don't. In fact, I'll just get out of here and leave you to whatever it is you're planning to do. Fair enough?

speaker: Juhani
text: Running away? Again?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Why not? It's what I do best.

speaker: Player
text: I take it you two know each other?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Yes. Isn't it obvious? I don't want to talk about it here, however.

speaker: Juhani
text: I don't think there's much to talk about.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Have it your way, Juhani. You always do.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Look... I don't want to be here after you leave. There'll be too many questions. So ask what you have to ask and I'll be on my way.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about these ruins?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Well... it seems that the Sith once inhabited Korriban a long time ago. There was a fortress here that was destroyed at some point before the Sith abandoned the planet completely.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Why they left, we don't know. Perhaps the Jedi drove them off. The tombs in this valley are the only parts of the fortress we've found mostly intact.

speaker: Player
text: Made any unusual findings?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Some. Most of the interesting stuff is still in the tombs, but Master Uthar prefers to leave them to be explored by the students, as a challenge.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: In time, they will probably become safe enough for us to enter. Until that time, however, we're stuck to digging up the valley piece by piece.

speaker: Player
text: The tombs are dangerous?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Definitely dangerous. Most of the students that go inside them don't come back out. Master Uthar prefers it that way.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about these tombs?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: There's four tombs here. On the right are the tombs of Ajunta Pall and Tulak Hord. On the left are the tombs of Marka Ragnos and Naga Sadow. All four were ancient Sith Lords.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the tomb of Ajunta Pall.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: That's the first tomb on the right. There's a rumor that there's a powerful artifact still in there, but nobody's retrieved it, yet.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: That tomb supposedly has ancient battle droids and traps that are still functioning. It's amazing that their power sources have lasted so long, really.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the tomb of Tulak Hord.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: That's the farthest tomb on the right. We don't know much about Tulak Hord, unfortunately... the tuk'ata have a nest in that tomb, I think.

speaker: Player
text: The tuk'ata?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: A local pack animal that's very dangerous. Occasionally the guards track down a queen and kill it... that usually pacifies them for a bit.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the tomb of Marka Ragnos.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: That's the first tomb on the left. Someone mentioned that a crazy droid has holed itself up in there, but I don't know much about that.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the tomb of Naga Sadow.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: It's the second tomb on the left when you enter the valley. Naga Sadow was the leader of the old Sith Masters here, we think.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Darth Malak found something in there a while back, however, and ever since then only Master Uthar can enter it.

speaker: Player
text: What did he find? Do you know?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: No. A lot of the discoveries are kept secret, even from the students. I only heard that Darth Malak found something there by rumor, to be honest.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: So do I.

speaker: Juhani
text: Goodbye, Dak... and... thank you.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Goodbye, Juhani.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Alright. Just be careful if you head into any of those tombs.

speaker: Player
text: Anything else I should know?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Nothing that I can think of. There's supposedly some old Sith hermit that haunts these hills and kidnaps students. Might want to watch out for him.

speaker: Player
text: Have you heard about a Star Map being found here?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: A Star Map? No, I haven't heard anything about that. Something like that could be in Naga Sadow's tomb, I suppose... that tomb's off limits to the students.

speaker: Player
text: Naga Sadow's tomb?

speaker: Player
text: How can I trust you not to say anything?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Does it matter? I'm going. Isn't that enough for you?

speaker: Juhani
text: Let him go. He... won't say anything.

speaker: Player
text: So you're leaving? Just like that?

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Master Uthar won't allow us to dig with lasers or sonics... we have to use hand tools only so we don't accidentally destroy anything we run across. That makes progress very slow, however.

speaker: Dak Vesser
text: Back again? Something... oh. Juhani... is... that you?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Welcome to Anchorhead, potential customer. Czerka Corporation stands ready to serve, after some formalities, of course.
comment: Initates with the player when they first exit the ebon hawk This is the customs official in the landing area just outside the ebon hawk. Like on Kashyyyk, he will not let the player disembark without paying the landing fee. Player can persuade his way out of it, though. Moves a short ways back after initiating dialogue, but always stays in the bay.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: First, your ship is not on our list of planned arrivals for today. There is a docking fee of 100 credits because of this.

speaker: Player
text: What do I get for my 100 credits?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: The immediate benefit is access to these very docking facilites. This is the only port in Anchorhead.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Once you've paid we will offer trade services as well. We're not unreasonable, we just want to cover expenses.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I don't need to pay the fee.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Success] You know... I don't think you need to pay the fee. We'll let it go, this time.

speaker: Jolee
text: *whisper* Heh! Reminds me of my old smuggling days. Nothing better than the old Jedi mind trick for getting past an overly curious customs officer.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: This will cover any future landings as well. It's like a registration, so we can serve you better when you return.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Now, as a customs officer, I can provide information on services. Is this visit business or pleasure?

speaker: Player
text: Give me some background on Tatooine.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: There isn't much to tell. It's a very old planet, well past its prime. Czerka Corporation is the only company with any interest in it.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: It's not a very pretty world, but there is opportunity here if you know where to look.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Czerka Corporation's operations here.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I can't really get into that. It hasn't been a very smooth operation. I shouldn't get into it.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Come now friend, let me in on the details.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Success] Ah, it's common knowledge, so there's no harm in telling you. It's a tale of bad business.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: You see, Czerka Corporation staked their claim to this planet based on some very promising geological surveys.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Unfortunately, that information was incorrect, and possibly even an attempt at sabotage by a rival company.

speaker: Player
text: So Czerka Corporation set up shop on a barren planet.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Not totally barren. There were a few years of good mining, and limited operations are still in place.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: But the ore is flawed. It has peculiar properties. They've had to look at other forms of business.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean when you say the ore is "peculiar"?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Czerka Corporation has really tried to hide this, but it just seems that Tatooine metal is unfit for effective manufacturing.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I would imagine that this outpost will eventually be abandoned. Nobody is making any money here.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Of course, this rock may have been settled a few times, so look for some other company to get stuck with it.

speaker: Player
text: What other forms of business are being looked at here?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Pursuits that appeal to the casual traveler. There are some fearsome native species that provide exciting hunting.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: There are also lengthy barren wastes that serve as fine swoop tracks. Attracting business has been slow, however.

speaker: Player
text: What is known about the history of the planet?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Very little. There are hints that it might once have been a lush world, but I can't picture it as anything but a desert.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Native sentient species have no records going back that far. That was hundreds of years ago. Maybe thousands.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Of course, the native species are not very willing to tell anyone anything. They're barely more than animals.

speaker: Player
text: What species do you mean?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: The Sand People. They're vicious, and attack outsiders on sight. More animal than anything, really.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Maybe they know the history of Tatooine, maybe they don't. Impossible to tell. They won't cooperate.

speaker: Player
text: Have you had trouble with the Sand People?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Not personally, but they've given Czerka Corporation a rough time. It's hard enough mining this rock without suffering random attacks.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: But it is getting better. I think someone went out on the dunes and laid down the law. Heh. I'm sure Czerka Corporation paid them well.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get information about jobs like that?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: It depends on what level of risk you want to take. You could ask at the Czerka office if any bounties need collecting. That's in central Anchorhead.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: While you're at the office, ask for a hunting license so you can sell trophies to Fazza in his lodge just north of them.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I suppose you could also take up swoop racing. Talk to the Hutt at the registration office by the track. That's in west Anchorhead.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I can't say I know which of these jobs is the most dangerous. I stay away from all of them.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for very specific things. Who should I ask?
comment: Player does not already have the star map

speaker: Customs Officer
text: That's not much information. Could you tell me more?

speaker: Player
text: No, I'm sorry.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Then you're on your own. Ask around Anchorhead. Someone may be able to help you.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for older things. Antiques. Artifacts.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: You a digger? I've heard of ruins being found now and then, but they've always been stripped by Sand People soon after.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: You're not going to get anywhere with them. I guess you could ask around, but I doubt you'll learn anything different.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: You could always ask a Jawa. It's hard to tell what they know.

speaker: Player
text: I'll need good paying work. What is there to do?

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I really need to get going.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: As you wish. If you need anything else, I'll be here.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a Star Map. Very old. Very complex.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: A Star Map? That's old holo-tech, isn't it? Not much reason to outfit this dry rock with tech like that.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: You could ask around, but for something like that you'll probably have to go digging. I wouldn't know where to begin.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my other questions.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I will answer as best I can. What will you need while on Tatooine?

speaker: Player
text: I'm done with you. Stay out of my business, or else!

speaker: Customs Officer
text: There is no need for that. I'm just doing my job. You are free to move as you wish.

speaker: Player
text: Any other sentient races?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: The Jawas are scavengers and a bit primitive. Hard to understand. They have an affinity for Droids.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Some of our scientists believe that they may not be native to the planet, but how they got here they may not even know. As I said, they're hard to understand.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: They usually end up slaves to the Sand People. They aren't fighters. Good traders, though.

speaker: Player
text: Where should a person look for opportunity?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I think the company has even put a bounty on them, but I'm sure not going to try for it.

speaker: Player
text: What about the city of Anchorhead? How old is it?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: The site is quite old. From the look of it, it's been settled before. Czerka Corporation claimed it only a few decades ago.

speaker: Player
text: What was here before?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Some other corporation that went under, probably. Not a lot of records are kept about backwater places like this.

speaker: Player
text: What species was giving you trouble?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Failure] I'm sorry. It's not really a big secret, but my superiors don't like people talking about it.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to tell me more about it.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Success] I... I can tell you more, I guess. It's not a big secret or anything. Just not good business.

speaker: Mission
text: *whisper* Well, that was easy. I sure wish I had special mind-affecting Force powers.

speaker: Cand
text: *whisper* I'm amazed at how many people that works on. The entire galaxy must be filled with weak-minded fools.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Failure] No, no, no. I'm sorry but we have to charge something. Maintenance is expensive out here.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, fine, I'll pay.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I thought you would. Without these fees, Czerka Corporation would have closed this port years ago.

speaker: Player
text: Is there any way you could reconsider the fee?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I assure you that the fee is non-negotiable. We have a very thin margin of profit on this world.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] The money I save I'll spend in your stores.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [Success] That does make sense. I suppose I could let it go this time. We need the business.

speaker: Player
text: I can't pay the fee right now.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Then I'm afraid you won't be visiting Anchorhead. Czerka Corporation hopes you will be a customer in the future.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Guards! This ship is refused access. See that they don't disembark.
comment: Player is forced back aboard the ebon hawk

speaker: Customs Officer
text: [You have no choice but to return to your ship.]

speaker: Player
text: I just want information about the planet.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: I'm sorry. While Czerka Corporation would like to encourage interest in Tatooine, we must first deal with the docking fees.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Our operations here are very expensive. We must recoup basic costs somehow.

speaker: Player
text: What if I don't have the money?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: That would be unfortunate. Czerka Corporation can't afford to extend credit. Everyone pays. That's the rule.

speaker: Player
text: What if I say no?

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Czerka Corporation maintains this docking station at great expense. It is within our rights to refuse landing permission.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: And I warn you, we've had troublemakers before. The bay is lined with autoguns. Violence is not a survivable option.

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Welcome back. Is there something I can do for you?
comment: Selected by the player AFTER player has paid the fee

speaker: Customs Officer
text: Hello again. Czerka Corporation remains willing to serve, but there is still the matter of the 100 credit docking fee...
comment: Initiates with the player the second time they exit the ebon hawk, if the player has not yet paid the fee.

speaker: Rodian035
text: You seem to be taking great interest in our progress. Do you need something, little man?

speaker: Rodian036
text: Quiet, Luugro! That's Calo Nord, the infamous bounty hunter!

speaker: Calo032
text: There's a bounty on your little green heads. I'm here to collect.

speaker: Rodian035
text: The only way you'll collect that bounty is over our cold, dead bodies!

speaker: Calo032
text: That's the plan.

speaker: Rodian
text: [Since there is no bounty on your head that he can collect, Calo Nord has no interest in you.]

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Is there anything more boring than being out on patrol? Ah, I guess I shouldn't complain.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Some of the troops got stuck patrolling the Undercity sewers. That's one assignment I wouldn't want!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Out of our way, citizen - we're on official Sith business! Just stand aside if you know what's good for you!

speaker: Utility Droid
text: [The droid ignores you, being programmed only for simple cleaning and maintenance procedures.]

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Back off, Republic scum! A man like you couldn't hope to satisfy a Sith woman!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Back off, Republic dog! You couldn't hope to compare to a real woman!

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: Thank you - I owe you my life! Those bounty hunters were going to take me away and kill me! My wife warned me not to take a loan from Davik.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: I guess you Sith aren't all bad... uh, I mean... look, I don't want any trouble. I'll just be going now.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: Now I can't pay him back. It's not good to owe a crime lord money. He'll just keep sending more bounty hunters after me until I'm dead!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I can help you.
comment: Party has 50 credits. Party loses 50 credits, small light side hit

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: You already helped me by saving me from those bounty hunters. So unless you have a spare 100 credits to give me so I can pay off Davik, there's nothing else you can do.

speaker: Player
text: Here's 100 credits. Take them.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: You're giving me 100 credits? Just like that? I... I don't know what to say! Thank you! Thank you!

speaker: Carth
text: You're giving him a hundred credits? Generous.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: Now I can pay off Davik. You've saved my life! Thank you! I better take these credits to him right away!

speaker: Player
text: I'm just glad I could help.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: I'm getting out of here before any more of Davik's goons show up. You should do the same.

speaker: Player
text: Hand over all your credits if you want to live!

speaker: Carth
text: Are you joking? We don't need this guy's credits. Just go on, we were happy to help.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: What? You're robbing me? You're no better than those bounty hunters! Here - take my credits! Now I'm getting out of here!
comment: Merchant escapes area, party gains 50 credits, small dark side hit.

speaker: Bullied Merchant
text: Look out! Those bounty hunters will kill you!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Did you hear about the big fight at the swoop races? I wasn't there, but someone told me Brejik flipped out on the podium and wouldn't pay up!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Ah. There's too many people in this cantina since they added the music room at the back! I come here to relax, not to fight with crowds.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: People are saying someone broke into the military base. Could mean trouble for us all if the Sith decide a Tarisian citizen was involved.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: I'm surprised the Sith haven't done anything to try and bring in Davik. After all, everyone knows he's the crime lord who runs this planet.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: The Sith are hunting for any Republic soldiers who escaped the battle overhead. They even sent a patrol into the Undercity to look for survivors!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: You... you're the one who killed Bendak Starkiller, aren't you? What a match - best duel I ever saw! You know, you might want to lay low for a while.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Bendak Starkiller is coming out of retirement! Everyone's talking about it! Some spacer agreed to fight him in an illegal death match! I wonder how I can get a ticket?

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Look at Niklos sitting over there with his Pazaak deck. I used to play, you know. But I wasn't very good. I finally sold my deck and gave it up.

speaker: Jedi Droid
text: The Council has decreed you may come and go as you please.
comment: SCRIPTED  the first time the player tries to leave since becoming an apprentice

speaker: Jedi Droid
text: The Council has decreed you must not leave the enclave. Please return to your room.
comment: SCRIPTED  when the player approaches the exit and has not been accepted for training Dialog Mission Statement   These lines are for the droid blocking the exit from the Jedi Enclave.   When the player talks to the droid, it will tell him whether or not he is allowed to exit. Only apprentices or higher are allowed to exit. Exit points in conversation: Exit stream 1: The line is said and the conversation ends. Exit stream 2: The line is said and the conversation ends.

speaker: Carth
text: This is Carth Onasi on your personal communicator. I'm tracking your position through the Endar Spire's life support systems.

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila's escape pod is away - you're the last surviving crew member of the Endar Spire! I can't wait for you much longer; you have to get to the escape pods!

speaker: Carth
text: But be careful. There's a Sith patrol just down the corridor. Use your STEALTH skill to sneak past him.

speaker: Player
text: Okay.

speaker: Player
text: How do I use my STEALTH skill?

speaker: Carth
text: First, make sure you have a stealth field generator equipped on your belt. You can't use your stealth skill without one.

speaker: Carth
text: Use the mouse and click on the Stealth button to activate it.

speaker: Carth
text: The generator will wrap you in a cloaking effect so you can sneak past the Sith. Just be careful you don't get too close or he might notice someone's there.

speaker: Player
text: Can you repeat that?

speaker: Carth
text: Be careful! There's a whole squad of Sith Troopers on the other side of that door! You need to find some way to thin their numbers.

speaker: Carth
text: You could reprogram the damaged assault droid to help you, if you have enough repair parts.

speaker: Carth
text: Or you could use computer spikes to slice into the terminal and use the Endar Spire's security systems against the Sith.

speaker: Carth
text: You made it just in time! There's only one active escape pod left. Come on, we can hide out on the planet below!

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Carth
text: I'm a soldier with the Republic, like you. We're the last two crew members left on the Endar Spire.

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila's escape pod's already gone, so there's no reason for us to stick around here and get shot by the Sith. Now come on - there'll be time for questions later!

speaker: Player
text: How do I know I can trust you?

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Very resourceful. I assume you had some part in this; you learned your lessons well from me.
comment: Init when party enters the bridge

speaker: Carth
text: The only thing you taught me was betrayal and death, Saul.

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Don't be a fool. I am giving you and your companions a chance to surrender. A chance to live. Darth Malak himself is on his way, he will be arriving any moment.

speaker: Bastila
text: He speaks the truth, Carth. I can feel the Dark Lord's presence approaching.

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Malak will destroy you, but if you throw down your weapons now I will ask my Master to be merciful.

speaker: Carth
text: I've seen enough of Sith mercy!

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: You always did like to do things the hard way. Lord Malak would have preferred live prisoners, but corpses will have to do.

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Carth... Carth....
comment: init when everyone else is dead

speaker: Bastila
text: The Admiral, he's still alive!

speaker: Carth
text: It's time to finish this.

speaker: Player
text: No, Carth, don't give in to your hatred!

speaker: Carth
text: Don't you understand what this man has done to my life? Do you know the pain he's brought me?

speaker: Bastila
text: Killing him won't ease the pain, Carth. Do not become what you despise.

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Carth... *cough*... must tell you... *cough* must tell you something... *cough, cough*... come closer....

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: [Unintelligible Whisper] You didn't know, did you? *cough* Ha-ha-ha.

speaker: SaulKarath402
text: Remember my dying words. *cough* Remember them whenever *cough*... whenever you look at those you thought were your friends!

speaker: Carth
text: He's gone. He said... it can't be true, can it? No. No... no - it can't! Damn you, Saul! Damn you!

speaker: Player
text: What did he say, Carth?

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila - it is true, isn't it? And... and you knew! You and the whole damn Jedi Council. You knew the whole time!

speaker: Bastila
text: Carth, it's not what you think. We had no other choice! Please, you don't understand...

speaker: Carth
text: So make me understand!

speaker: Player
text: What are you two talking about? What's going on?

speaker: Bastila
text: Not here, Carth. Please... there's no time. Malak is coming. This isn't the place.

speaker: Bastila
text: Please, Carth, I'm asking you to trust me. For just a little while longer.

speaker: Player
text: She's right, Carth. This isn't the time. We can get into this after we escape.

speaker: Carth
text: I'll trust you, Bastila but as soon as we're off this ship I expect some answers!
comment: end cut scen and Carth rejoins party

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course, Carth. As soon as we get to the Ebon Hawk I'll explain everything. To both of you. I promise.

speaker: Player
text: Whatever this is about, Carth deserves an answer. So start talking, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it, Carth. Whatever he said he was only trying to hurt you.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, he's dead, your family's avenged. Can we get out of here now?

speaker: Player
text: Forget him, Carth, we have to get out of here before Malak arrives!

speaker: Player
text: Take your time, Carth. Make him suffer for what he's done to you!

speaker: Bastila
text: No, Carth, not like this! Do not give in to the hate.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Can I help you? These are the offices of Czerka Corporation. I trust you have business with the company?
comment: Initial selected This is an officer of Czerka corp Track: Player has bounty pass: yes/no Player has gaffi sticks: yes/no

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: If this is about employment, I'm afraid all regular mining positions are full. And before you ask, we are also no longer selling hunting licenses.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a miner named Griff.
comment: Only if Mission plot has reached the proper stage.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Griff? Uh... there's no Griff here. Never heard of him. No, I... I don't remember a single Griff on the Czerka Corporation payroll.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe 20 credits will refresh your memory?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: That... may help in this instance. Let me think... perhaps I remember this Griff character.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We hired that Twi'lek some time ago. Not a good worker according to his crew chief: always complaining and faking injuries to get out of work.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: He entered false time sheets and slept through his shifts. We even suspected him of stealing Czerka Corporation supplies, although we could never prove it.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, that sounds like him.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We would've fired him but we needed workers. It would have been better for him if he had been fired. Then the Sand People wouldn't have gotten him.

speaker: Player
text: The Sand People?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: He was lost in a Sand People raid we suffered not too long ago. There were prisoners taken, but our rescue parties never found anyone alive.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: In the end it just wasn't cost effective to keep searching. All miners sign a waiver absolving Czerka Corporation of liability in these circumstances.

speaker: Player
text: So your workers are all expendable?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Czerka Corporation cares deeply for all of its employees. That's why we've started a bounty program to thin the Sand People numbers.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We didn't find his body so we have to assume he was taken prisoner. Whether he's still alive, I couldn't say.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: That's all I can tell you. I shouldn't even have said this much; this is all privileged corporate information. I could lose my job!

speaker: Player
text: Is there some type of reward for saving him?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: As I said, all employees have signed waivers absolving Czerka Corporation of any financial liability if this occurs. It is the industry standard.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I suppose you could apply for special dispensation from the Czerka Corporation Representative Kiosk on Coruscant. Business hours only, please.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. I want to ask you about something else.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Very well, though I do have work to get back to.

speaker: Player
text: I have gaffi sticks to redeem for bounties.
comment: Player has hunting liscense. AND (Player has gaffi sticks OR player has Chieftan's Gaffi)

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Of course. You have done a good job for us and I'm happy to pay you.
comment: player has already turned in the Chieftans Gaffi Remove gaffi sticks. Pay 100 percent of their value for each

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about hunting licenses.
comment: player has not been given a license

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: As I said, we are no longer selling them. There are too many people cavorting about outside the walls as it is.
comment: Player has not already acquired a pass

speaker: Player
text: Why would I need a license anyway?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We use them to insure that only people judged fit by Czerka Corporation are allowed outside the city.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We don't allow casual exploration because of legal concerns. Czerka Corporation takes no responsibility for loss of life on the dunes.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: It's just so we can keep track of people. No one leaves the city without a Czerka hunting license.

speaker: Player
text: There is no way to get a license?
comment: player has not been told about Sand People bounty

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Well, normally we charge 200 credits, but I could make an exception if you agreed to perform a task for us. It's similar to hunting.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: The Sand People are becoming a problem. They destroy our sandcrawlers and kill our miners. One particular tribe is the worst.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: It's as if their chieftain has decided to wage a war against us. I would like their attacks... terminated. Bring me their gaffi sticks as proof.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: If you agree to do this, I'll give you a hunting license now and pay a bounty for each stick later. I'll give a bonus for the chieftain's.

speaker: Player
text: Why pay for the gaffi sticks? Why not their heads?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Which would you rather have dumped on your office floor? Besides, they are ceremonial weapons unique to each warrior. It's just as good.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to do this.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Then you are free to not leave the city, just like everyone else. Czerka Corporation will welcome your eventual change of mind.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Please, feel free to enjoy the door behind you.

speaker: Player
text: I will agree to do this for you.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Excellent. Now, just so we understand each other, this is an enforceable contract. Czerka Corporation takes this very seriously.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Here is your license, and a few directions. We believe one of their enclaves is in the far south of the Dune Sea.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: You might try following one of our sandcawlers. They are regularly attacked. I wouldn't mind you escorting them.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my first questions.

speaker: Player
text: I'll go get to it then.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Very good. Czerka Corporation looks forward to your future business.

speaker: Player
text: What was it you wanted me to do for a license?

speaker: Player
text: Have there been a lot of people leaving the city?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: With the downturn in mining, people want any chance at credits they can get. Most wouldn't survive a day, let alone qualify as hunters.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: The last license issued before the ban was given to a woman named Marlena Venn. She'll do fine; she had a mean streak a parsec wide.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: She also paid double. Exceptions like this are rare, unless it suits the company to offer them.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about our agreement.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: You have fulfilled your end of the bargain and Czerka Corporation is grateful. The Sand People will be less of a threat without their chieftain.
comment: player has turned in chieftan's gaffi

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I will of course continue to give you bounties on regular gaffi sticks. Every one helps.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go. Goodbye.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Farewell. Czerka Corporation welcomes your future inquiries.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Yes, we are still waiting for you to return with the Sand People Chieftain's gaffi stick. I will reward you well when you do.
comment: player has not yet turned in chieftan's gaffi

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We don't have any new information on the subject. It is still possible that they have an enclave in the far south of the Dune Sea.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: And I would remind you that you did agree to do this task for Czerka Corporation. We expect completion in a timely manner.

speaker: Player
text: There may be a nonviolent solution to this.
comment: player has been sent to purchase moisture vaporators. Sand People not hostile

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I should remind you that you were not retained as a diplomatic representative. You are a hunter, and should go after your prey as we agreed.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: You are not authorized to do anything other than deliver what was promised. Do so, and don't talk of this foolishness again.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about Czerka Corporation.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Of course. Czerka Corporation records are available at our Representative Kiosk on Coruscant. Business hours please.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: For your needs here, we maintain a fully stocked storehouse. Speak with Greeta Holda about any purchases.

speaker: Player
text: I wanted to ask about your activities on Kashyyyk.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I'm sorry, but day-to-day operations of Czerka Corporation outposts are fully regionalized. I have no information on Kashyyyk.

speaker: Player
text: Which is very convenient if one branch is charged with misconduct.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I'm sorry, I'll have to direct you to our Representative Kiosk on Coruscant. Business hours only, please.

speaker: Player
text: May I ask how your operations here on Tatooine are doing?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Certainly. Please pose your questions to the Representative Kiosk on Coruscant. Business hours please.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Why the secrets? The company stuck you here. Tell me.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] I suppose you're right. It's not like you can't tell the state of things just by looking around.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Mining operations here have not been a success. The ore is substandard, and there's less of it than surveys indicated.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: With the Sand People raids on top of it all, it's no wonder this planet has been abandoned before.

speaker: Player
text: What makes the ore substandard?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: No one knows. There are odd energy fluctuations on this planet, but they defy analysis or explanation.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: But the effect is obvious. Ore taken from Tatooine is useless for construction. It degrades incredibly fast.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Word is getting out about it too. We're running out of buyers. Czerka Corporation is not doing well here.

speaker: Player
text: Does this mean you have plans to pull out?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: The company would have to be foolish to stay. It will be costly, but in the end, leaving will be cheaper than staying.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I imagine all the heavy equipment will be abandoned. It's not worth shipping out things like sandcrawlers.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Maybe the Jawas will find a use for them when we're gone. Ha! That's a laugh!

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean the planet was abandoned before?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: We can't ignore evidence that Anchorhead was settled more than once before, and abandoned each time.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: There's probably about a century between each attempt. Just long enough for records about why it failed to disappear.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: The Jawas scavenge ancient tech all the time. It's a remote world. Who knows what's here?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Failure] I'm sorry, but I can't help you. I'll have to refer you to the Representative Kiosk.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] It would be better if you told me now.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] Of course, I could just tell you now. No sense in being so secretive. It's all fairly obvious.

speaker: Player
text: Anything out of the ordinary happening?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I assume that by "out of the ordinary" you are referring to the destruction of Taris? That is all anyone is talking about.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I'm afraid Czerka Corporation is not offering any comment on those events. We wouldn't wish to anger the participants.

speaker: Player
text: Know about anything more local?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: If you are looking for local events, I suggest you go to the swoop track. One of the few leisure industries on Tatooine.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Hmm... there was also a Jawa here earlier, saying something about needing help. I think he's out by the city gates.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I can't be more specific about what he wanted. Our droid translators had difficulty with the message.

speaker: Player
text: No desire to mistakenly associate with the losing side, hmm?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Czerka Corporation policy is not subject to your approval. It is a sound business model. Save us your commentary.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I see that, but do you have the all important Chieftain's Gaffi? That was what you agreed to get for us.
comment: Player has not yet turned inthe Chieftans gaffi

speaker: Player
text: Just the regular ones for now.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Then I'll take those off your hands, but the real prize is still out there.
comment: Player has normal gaffi Remove gaffi sticks. Pay 100 percent of their value for each

speaker: Player
text: Yes, here it is.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Well, that is a very big headache that you have removed. I'm sure there are still Sand People out there, but they will be quieter now.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I think I'll give you a bonus for this. You've more than lived up to your side of the bargain. Czerka Corporation thanks you.
comment: take chieftans gaffi, give player reward.

speaker: Player
text: That amount will suffice.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: I'm sure. Czerka Corporation thanks you again.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] For a bit more I could maintain my vigilence in the future.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] It would be valuable to have someone on call if the Sand People made another incursion. I think you're right.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Yes, here is an additional reward. Once again, Czerka Corporation thanks you.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Failure] I think you'll find that the reward I have given is more than adequate for the task. No more is deserved.

speaker: Player
text: Hand over more or I bury you the same as the Sand People.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: *ahem* While I respect your... forcefulness, I must remind you that ours are the finest, and only, guards in Anchorhead.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: It would simply be inadvisable to attempt such an action in here. There would be no place for you to run. I don't fear you here.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to give me an additional reward.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] And I wouldn't want you to leave without this additional reward. Yes, of course I wouldn't.

speaker: Jolee
text: *whisper* Nicely done, kid. Those extra credits could come in handy on our little search. Besides, it's not like Czerka Corp. can't afford it.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* Czerka may be a corrupt organization, but that doesn't justify us using the Force for personal gain.

speaker: Carth
text: *whisper* I don't know much about the Jedi code, but I know I'd rather see those credits in our hands than in the hands of Czerka Corp or the Sith.

speaker: Juhani
text: *whisper* A Jedi shoud not use the Force to acquire credits - even if we are taking them from a corrupt corporation like Czerka.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Once again, Czerka Corporation thanks you.

speaker: Player
text: I was mistaken. I'll be back later.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Very well, but we need this matter taken care of.

speaker: Player
text: Did the Sand People kill Griff or not!

speaker: Player
text: You mean he's dead?

speaker: Player
text: So you fired him?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Are you certain of that? I would leave sooner if I knew.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] Oh, you mean that Twi'lek! Must have slipped my mind for a second. Yes, of course I remember Griff.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Failure] I'm sorry, but Czerka Corporation officials do not accept bribes. Now, unless you're interested in our bounties or some other business I'm going to have to ask you to leave!

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuasion] You want to tell me about Griff.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: [Success] Can you spare me a few moments? I have something I want to get off my chest. I want to tell you about one of our workers. His name was Griff.

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Hello again. I hear you've made an impression down at the swoop track. Czerka Corporation wholly supports local events.
comment: Secondary, player has signed up for swoop racing

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Er... not financially, you understand. Now, was this about bounties or something else?

speaker: Protocol Officer
text: Greetings again from the offices of Czerka Corporation. Is this about bounties or something else?

speaker: Hulas
text: I am not surprised to see you here, <FullName>. I am surprised you came alone, however. I thought you would know by now how dangerous we Genoharadan are.

speaker: Player
text: I knew you were too much of a coward to come alone!

speaker: Hulas
text: Really? If you knew this, you should have been smart enough to bring your friends with you. You helped me betray the other Overseers: you should know I don't play fair.

speaker: Player
text: I honored our agreement. This is between you and me alone.

speaker: Hulas
text: You have seen me betray the other Overseers, yet you still believe a Genoharadan cares anything about honor? That is a foolish mistake, <FullName>. One you won't live to regret.

speaker: Hulas
text: You have great potential, <FullName>. Even the Genoharadan's best agents would not likely have been able to eliminate the other three Overseers.

speaker: Hulas
text: You even have the potential to become an Overseer yourself, one day. That's why I have to kill you here: eliminating the competition is the key to maintaining my power.

speaker: Player
text: I killed the other Overseers. I can kill you too, Hulas.

speaker: Hulas
text: The other Overseers were alone and unprepared. I am ready for you - and I have friends. Goodbye, <FullName>. Our time together was... interesting.

speaker: Hulas
text: Brothers of the Genoharadan: attack!

speaker: Player
text: Let's get this over with.

speaker: Hulas
text: My thoughts exactly.

speaker: Hulas
text: You are here, <FullName>. But I see you did not come alone.

speaker: Player
text: I see you've brought some friends as well, Hulas.

speaker: Hulas
text: You shouldn't be surprised. You saw how I manipulated and betrayed my fellow Overseers. You should know the Genoharadan seek every advantage we can get.

speaker: Hulas
text: I had hoped you would be gullible enough to show up alone, but obviously I underestimated you... although I see from their expressions that your friends have no clue what is going on here.

speaker: Hulas
text: Not that it matters. If I win here, what you know of the Genoharadan will die here with you. If you win, the guild will vanish until they select new Overseers... if they even survive.

speaker: Player
text: Three Genoharadan Overseers out of four are dead, Hulas. Time to finish the job!

speaker: Player
text: I knew you were too much of a coward to come alone.

speaker: Rakatan Warrior
text: You have my thanks. I shall try to return to the One and tell him what has happened.

speaker: Rakatan Warrior
text: Get us out of here and you shall have the gratitude of the Rakata!

speaker: Rakatan Warrior
text: The One will not let the Elders live!

speaker: Matrik
text: What... what are you doing here? I don't want any trouble with the Sith. Please, just go before... please, just go.

speaker: Matrik
text: Hey - you can't come in here! This is a private apartment!

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to collect the bounty on your head, Matrik!

speaker: Matrik
text: I knew one of Davik's scum would find me eventually. But if I die at least I'll have a clear conscience! I wonder, can you say the same?

speaker: Player
text: Clear conscience? What are you talking about?

speaker: Matrik
text: My testimony helped put some of the biggest criminals on Taris away for life. But Davik didn't like seeing his friends go down, so now he's got a bounty on my head.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe there's some way I could help you out of this mess.

speaker: Matrik
text: I don't think there's much anyone could do. And I'm getting sick of running. I've decided to make my stand right here.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you could turn the tables. You know, have Davik eliminated.

speaker: Matrik
text: Getting inside Davik's base is nearly impossible. Even if I got rid of him, the Exchange would just appoint someone to his place and I'd still have a price on my head.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you could fake your own death?

speaker: Matrik
text: I've already thought of that. I even came up with a plan of how to do it. But I can't pull it off while I'm holed up in here.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me your plan and I might help you out.

speaker: Matrik
text: The trick is getting Davik to buy it when there's no body found at the scene. If it looks like I died in a massive explosion, he won't be suspicious when my corpse never turns up.

speaker: Matrik
text: If I had an accomplice go back and tell Davik that they were the one who set off the explosion to eliminate me, I think I'd be home free.

speaker: Matrik
text: I have some demolitions experience from my own days in the Exchange so I could set it all up. But I'd need to get my hands on a permacrete detonator.

speaker: Player
text: I could get you a permacrete detonator.

speaker: Matrik
text: They don't usually sell them in stores here in the Lower City, but the Upper City might carry them. You might want to look there first.

speaker: Player
text: I have a permacrete detonator right here. Go on... take it.

speaker: Matrik
text: Let me see... yes, this should do the trick. There won't be anything left of this apartment but some scorching on the walls after I set this bad boy off!

speaker: Matrik
text: Okay, the timer's set! Now let's get out of here before it blows!

speaker: Matrik
text: That was quite the blast! Don't go back in there... the whole roof might cave in on your head.
comment: Matrik inits with the player as soon as they exit the room and the explosion effect has fired. At the end of this dialog have him escape area and destroy himself. If players try to open door after this it won't open and they get the message of "The stench of smoke assails your nostrils as you approach. The door, however, is blocked by rubble on the other side and will not open."

speaker: Matrik
text: Look, I'm not a man for long goodbyes but I want to say 'thanks'. If it wasn't for you I'd be a dead man. But now I won't have to worry about anymore bounty hunters coming after me.

speaker: Matrik
text: So good luck, and goodbye. Now that I'm 'dead' I can't be seen wandering the streets.

speaker: Player
text: I've got a permacrete detonator on me... but it'll cost you.

speaker: Matrik
text: I don't have any credits - all I've got is the clothes on my back. But if you help me with this, you can go to Zax in the bounty office and claim the price on my head.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll just kill you and collect the bounty instead.

speaker: Matrik
text: Well, you're going to have to earn it!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'll just take my detonator and go.

speaker: Matrik
text: You think I'm going to just let you walk out of here with the detonator that could be my ticket to salvation? You better think again, friend!

speaker: Player
text: I think it's time for me to collect your bounty, Matrik!

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to get involved in this.

speaker: Matrik
text: Can't say I blame you. If I had it all to do again I might think twice before going up against the Exchange. I understand if you just want to leave.

speaker: Matrik
text: Just be careful that nobody sees you as you leave. I don't want anyone to find out I'm hiding here.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you could pay Davik off?

speaker: Matrik
text: It wouldn't work. This goes beyond money. The Exchange wants to make an example of me. Davik won't stop until I'm dead.

speaker: Player
text: I have no conscience. Time to die.

speaker: Bastila
text: No, wait! I want to hear what this man means by 'clear conscience'.

speaker: Carth
text: Hold on a second. I want to hear what he means by 'clear conscience'.

speaker: Matrik
text: I don't think you know who you're dealing with! I don't let criminals and thugs walk all over me!

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing in here? This place looks abandoned!

speaker: Matrik
text: None of your business. Just turn around and go back the way you came, if you know what's good for you.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Are you in some sort of trouble? Do you want to talk about it?

speaker: Matrik
text: [Success] I... I guess I could tell you. You'll probably find out on your own eventually, anyway. Zax is giving his bounties away like candy, or so I hear.

speaker: Matrik
text: My name's Matrik - I used to work for the Exchange, but all the violence and killing started to get to me. I knew what I was doing was wrong, so I turned state's evidence.

speaker: Matrik
text: [Failure] It's not something you want to get mixed up in. Look, do yourself a favor and just leave me alone.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to rob this place. Sit down and shut up and you won't get hurt.

speaker: Player
text: I don't like your attitude!

speaker: Matrik
text: That's it - you've pushed me too far! You shouldn't push a man on the edge!

speaker: Player
text: Don't get upset. I'll go now.

speaker: Matrik
text: Good... get out of here. Stay out of my apartment and my business!

speaker: Matrik
text: I was afraid you wouldn't come back. Did you manage to find a permacrete detonator?

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't have a permacrete detonator yet.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Matrik
text: Back again? You know I'm a man on the lam. I don't really want visitors coming and going from my hiding place.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me again why you're hiding here.

speaker: Matrik
text: You again? Look, there's nothing in here for you so you might as well leave.

speaker: Malare
text: [This woman appears to be looking for someone... maybe even one of your companions back on the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Malare
text: Excuse me... I know it's been a very long time, dear, but aren't you Bastila, Helena's little girl? Yes - it is you! I can see it in the eyes. My how you've grown!

speaker: Bastila
text: I am Bastila, yes. I take it that you know my mother?

speaker: Malare
text: Oh, yes. I worked for your father on an expedition years ago. Your mother showed me holos of you before you... well, before you left. Such a pretty little girl you were.

speaker: Bastila
text: Is there something I can do for you, miss? As you can see, we are in quite a hurry.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be rude, Bastila.

speaker: Malare
text: Oh, I didn't mean to take up your time. I just wanted to ask you if your mother's condition has improved any since I saw her.

speaker: Bastila
text: My mother's condition?

speaker: Malare
text: Oh, you... you don't know? Oh, dear. I just thought... I assumed that she had found you. When I talked to her last, she was desperate to find you...

speaker: Bastila
text: I have not seen my mother since I joined the order. Do you know what has happened? Did she... say anything about my father?

speaker: Malare
text: I'm sorry, dear, but your mother is very ill. So she told me. She didn't say anything about your father, however. I didn't see him.

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. Where did you meet her, do you remember?

speaker: Malare
text: She's here on Tatooine, dear. In the cantina. You really should go see her, considering her condition.

speaker: Player
text: I guess we should go see your mother, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: Part of me would rather not see her at all. But if she is really sick... well, we shall see.

speaker: Player
text: We're too busy for this nonsense, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: I agree. Should we get the chance, however, I would speak to her. Perhaps it has something to do with my father.

speaker: Malare
text: I saw her on Tatooine, dear. She said she'd been there for awhile. Maybe she's still there?

speaker: Bastila
text: Thank you for informing me. I really must be going, now.

speaker: Player
text: What's this all about?

speaker: Bastila
text: It seems my mother has been looking for me. Strange. Should we get the opportunity, could we look for her on Tatooine?

speaker: Player
text: I thought you and your mother didn't get along?

speaker: Bastila
text: We never did. I am interested in hearing about my father, however.

speaker: Player
text: Certainly, if you think it's important.

speaker: Bastila
text: It is important enough that my mother was attempting to seek me out. Perhaps it has something to do with my father.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. We've got better things to do.

speaker: Player
text: We're on an important mission here, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, of course. I would never jeopardize our mission. However, if we get the opportunity I would like to visit Tatooine.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila's right. We don't have time for this.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: If it wasn't for those damn Selkath neutrality laws, I'd teach that Sith a thing or two!

speaker: Player
text: You have to learn to control your anger. Anger leads to the dark side.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: I... I suppose you're right. You probably know best - you are a Jedi, after all. I guess getting mad doesn't help any.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: As long as the Sith stay out of my way, I'll stay out of theirs.

speaker: Player
text: The Republic must respect the law.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be such a coward - teach those Sith a lesson!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: I can't do anything that would get me in trouble, or the Selkath might slap export penalties on the Republic.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: We need the Selkath's kolto for the war effort against Malak.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: You are so lucky. You got accepted into the academy, didn't you? I'm beginning to think I never will. *sigh*

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Hey! You've got one of the medallions! You've been accepted! How did you ever manage that?!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: If you're looking to get into the academy, you're going to have a tough time. There's lots of us here trying to get accepted.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: When one of the Sith thinks you're ready for the academy, he gives you a medallion. I wish I had one of those...

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Can you imagine if I actually became a Sith? The power I'd have! I could do anything!!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Do you know where I can find Yuthura Ban? I understand she's the one who determines if you are accepted into the academy or not.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: You'd better be careful around some of those Sith. They'll eliminate any prospects just to remove a potential future threat!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: I've had two friends killed by the Sith already. It must be some kind of test... I'll survive and make it into the academy, I know it!

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Wow. This is going to look really bad on my record.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: The patrol Captain will speak for us. He's the ranking officer in this unit.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: You know, we're gonna get stuck with the bill for this.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: I thought he said shoot. I swear he said shoot.
comment: Random over head, but not when player speaking to Captain.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Well, this means extra duty for sure.
comment: Random over head, but not when player speaking to Captain.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Why do they always have to be so difficult?
comment: Random over head, but not when player speaking to Captain.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: They won't miss one, will they?
comment: Random over head, but not when player speaking to Captain.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: We should just say it bolted, or something.
comment: Random over head, but not when player speaking to Captain.

speaker: Dorak
text: These ruins have long been known to us, but we believed them to be merely burial mounds. Perhaps they are more than we first suspected, if Revan and Malak found something there.

speaker: Player
text: Yes... they seemed to be searching for something

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila has described this shared dream to the Council in great detail. We feel it is more than a dream. It is a vision. The Force is acting through you as it acts through Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I am having visions now?

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: You and Bastila share a powerful connection to the Force... and each other. This is not unheard of. Connections often form between Master and student, but rarely does a bond develop so quickly.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Whatever dangers may lie ahead, we cannot ignore the destiny that has brought you and Bastila here to us. Together.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying I'm... joined with her?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You and she are linked, as is your fate to hers. Together, you two may be able to stop Darth Malak and the Sith.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: But do not let your head be filled with visions of glory and power! Such thoughts are the path to the dark side.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The way of the light is long and difficult, as you must learn. Are you ready for such hardship?

speaker: Player
text: Yes. I'm ready for whatever awaits me.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Understand that there is little choice in this matter, for you or us. Across the galaxy the numbers of our Order dwindle. We have sent many Jedi in quest of a way to thwart Malak's advance... many have not returned.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Sith hunt the Jedi down like animals, ambushing and assassinating our brothers wherever they are found. We fear it is only a matter of time until they discover even this hidden refuge.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Other Jedi have fallen from the light and embraced the dark side, giving their allegiance to the Sith and Malak, their dark lord.

speaker: Player
text: Jedi are turning to the dark side?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The lure of the dark side is not easy to resist. Malak's power grows as more and more planets fall to his conquering armies.

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: If Malak is not stopped the Republic will fall, and the Jedi will be hunted to extinction. The galaxy will enter a time of darkness and tyranny not seen for a thousand generations.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Council has decreed that you and Bastila must investigate the ancient ruins you dreamed of... once the Council deems you ready.

speaker: Dorak
text: Perhaps there you will find some clue, some explanation, of how Revan and Malak were corrupted. And perhaps there you shall find a way to stop them.

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready now. I accept this mission.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The Force flows through you like no student we have ever seen. But you are willful and headstrong... a dangerous combination.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Before we send you to investigate the ruins, you must be trained in the ways of the Jedi so that you can resist the darkness within yourself... within all of us. Otherwise you are doomed to fail.

speaker: Player
text: We don't have time for this!

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You must learn patience and discipline. The ruins are a place of corruption. The dark side is strong there. We cannot risk sending you there unprepared.

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: We must begin your training at once. You have a destiny upon you that you must be prepared to face. The entire fate of the galaxy is upon you.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I can only hope you will prove up to the task.

speaker: Player
text: As you wish, Master Vandar.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I surrender myself to the will of the Council.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: [Success] We must begin your training at once. You have a destiny upon you that you must be prepared to face. The entire fate of the galaxy is upon you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know if I want to do this... it sounds dangerous.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You have a strong affinity with the Force. With such power comes great responsibility... and danger. You may wish to deny what you are, but the Council cannot turn a blind eye.

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: Neither will Darth Malak. Your strength is a threat to him. In time he will learn of you and the Sith will hunt you down. It is inevitable. Defeating the Sith is the only way to save yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Very well, I will help you.

speaker: Player
text: It seems I have no choice...

speaker: Player
text: I will learn your Jedi powers and defeat Malak!

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Of course, Masters. Anything to further the light.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: [Success] Hm, yes. Your devotion is most commendable.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Do not fear Masters, I will not fall.

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: [Success] If Malak is not stopped the Republic will fall, and the Jedi will be hunted to extinction. The galaxy will enter a time of darkness and tyranny not seen for a thousand generations.

speaker: Player
text: How can he be stopped?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Perhaps our hope lies in the dream you and Bastila shared. The Council has come to the conclusion that you and Bastila must investigate the ancient ruins you dreamed of.

speaker: Player
text: I will try my best.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Of course, Masters. I seek to follow the light.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Good. It is well that you see how important this is and have the devotion to follow it.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Player
text: I trust in your greater wisdom.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to talk about it.

speaker: Player
text: What?? How would Bastila know if we shared a dream?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: She says that she felt your presence within the dream, the presence she has felt within you ever since...

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Master Vandar!

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: ... ever since Taris. It is not unknown for this to happen between two people strong in the Force.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I don't know what Bastila is talking about.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: [Failure] See? Dishonesty! We are taking an incalculable risk in even considering training this one!

speaker: Zhar Lestin
text: You cannot deny what you are. These dreams are part of you. The Force is part of you, though a part you cannot yet control. But through training and discipline we can teach you to live as one with the Force.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: It is good to see Juhani has returned to the way of the light. You are to be commended for your role in this. Your actions give us great hope for the future.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Your training is now complete, young Padawan. And perhaps now it is time we dealt with the matter of the dream you and Bastila shared.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: When we heard of the ruins in your dreams, Master Dorak recognized it as one of a series of ancient structures here on Dantooine. This one in particular lies to the east of this Enclave.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We sent a Jedi to investigate... but he has not returned. Perhaps sending him in the first place was a mistake.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Force is guiding you through your visions; it may be that exploring the ruins is a task tied to your destiny. That is why the Council has now decided you should be the one to investigate this.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The secrets to stopping Malak may be hidden within those ruins. You must investigate them and find what Revan and Malak were looking for.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to ask you some questions.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: A Jedi must ever be seeking knowledge. What is it you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Bastila?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila will be a great Jedi someday. Even among the Masters and the Council it is rare to find one so skilled in the art of Battle Meditation.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila was there when Revan was slain. Did you know that?

speaker: Player
text: I had no idea.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila herself does not like to talk about it. She was accompanying the strike team that confronted Revan when the Dark Lord was destroyed. Her role in the death of such a promising young Jedi as Revan upset her greatly.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: But Bastila knew she had to set her personal feelings aside for the sake of the galaxy and the Republic. The Force is strong with her now, and without her skill in Battle Meditation we would have lost this war long ago.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The way ahead will be difficult for young Bastila... and for you. But you must draw strength from each other. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: Carth mentioned something about it.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything you can tell me about Revan and Malak?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: I knew Revan as a promising young pupil. Revan was strong in the Force, but also headstrong and proud. Such traits are not unusual in a Padawan. Perhaps that was why I did not see the true extent of the danger.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Many of the young Jedi admired Revan, including Malak. When Revan set off to challenge the Mandalorians, Malak was the first to join the cause.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: And when Revan fell to the dark side it was inevitable Malak would fall as well.

speaker: Player
text: So Revan was stronger than Malak?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Revan was always the more powerful of the pair. When Revan fell we had hoped the Sith threat was ended. But Malak quickly assumed Revan's role and embraced the dark side as fully as his Master ever had.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You should speak to Master Dorak after this council. As Chronicler of this Academy, he can give you more details of these events. But we must concern ourselves with the present.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Now Malak leads the Sith armada against the Republic, hate and vengeance drawing him ever further down the dark path, fueling his powers until they have surpassed those of his old Master.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Only you and Bastila together can stop Malak now.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying Revan was responsible for Malak's fall?

speaker: Player
text: Why doesn't Master Vrook like me?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Master Vrook may seem harsh and critical, but he understands the dangers that lie in your path. He wants you and Bastila to be fully prepared when you finally face Lord Malak.

speaker: Player
text: What should be done about the Sandral and Matale families?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: If Shen Matale is not returned to his father it may ignite a savage and bloody feud between the Matale and Sandral estates. We must not allow that to happen.
