speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You should ask Master Vrook about that, Padawan. He is in charge of our relations with the settlers.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The way ahead will be difficult for young Bastila... and for you. You must draw strength from each other. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: What happened to Belaya?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We do not know. She was training here until your unfortunate incident with Juhani, then she simply disappeared...

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We would like any word of her you may bring. I do not believe she has died, or fallen prey to beasts, but I worry that she may have done something rash.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: She had always been close to Juhani, and her death may have hit Belaya... hard.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Is there anything else you wish to ask?

speaker: Player
text: I will investigate the ruins right away.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Be sure to bring Bastila with you. There is a powerful link between you, and you will need to draw strength from each other during the trials ahead.

speaker: Player
text: What happened to the Jedi who went to investigate?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We do not know. That is one of the things you must investigate. We... fear the worst.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Is there anything else you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: I have found and slain Belaya. She had turned to the dark side.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: That is most... unfortunate. She was always a model student and most eager to learn. I grieve that she had fallen to her passions.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Remember her example as well as that of Juhani: the dark side is not an enemy to be taken lightly.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Go to Master Zhar and inform him that Juhani has returned to us. I think you may be nearing the end of your apprenticeship.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: It is most regrettable that Juhani could not be saved. We in the Council had high hopes for her in the future.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: In every heart there is some means of redemption. Could you find none in Juhani?

speaker: Player
text: I couldn't see a way to save her.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Perhaps that was the case. It is most regrettable, indeed.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Heed her example: all are susceptable to the lure of the dark side. We must always remain vigilant against it.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Go to Master Zhar and inform him that the grove has been cleansed. I think you may be nearing the end of your apprenticeship.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] She attacked without speaking.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: [Success] Perhaps that was the case. It is most regrettable, indeed.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] She was too evil to ever come back.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila has told us of your discovery in the ancient ruins. The Council has decided it would be best if you complete your apprenticeship before you embark on any further investigations in this matter.
comment: DIALOGUE  talking to the council, having explored the ruins, but before becoming a padawan

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: As grave as the Sith threat may be, we cannot allow you to leave here until your apprenticeship is over. The danger of the dark side is too great to send you out unprepared.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Master Zhar feels you are ready to begin the final tests of your apprenticeship. Return to us when you have completed your training.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Good evening, apprentice. I trust your training goes well?
comment: DIALOGUE  after being accepted for jedi training but before becoming a padawan

speaker: Player
text: My training is progressing quite well.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: I have faith that you will achieve the rank of Padawan soon. Master Zhar is most impressed with your progress. May the Force be with you, apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: I seek knowledge of the Jedi Code.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: All Jedi must know the code, its tenets are the fundamental teachings of our Order. Think and meditate on these truths, apprentice:

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: There is no emotion; there is peace. There is no ignorance; there is knowledge. There is no passion; there is serenity. There is no chaos; there is harmony. There is no death; there is the Force.

speaker: Player
text: I must be going now.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Very well. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Ah, you have returned, young Padawan. Have you discovered what it was that Revan and Malak sought in those ruins?

speaker: Player
text: We found an incomplete Star Map and mention of something called a Star Forge.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: This news of a Star Forge is disturbing. Action is required, but we must not do so in haste. We must discuss recent events in light of this new information.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: We should consult the Jedi archives to see if there is any mention of this 'Star Forge' and what it might do. We must learn why Revan and Malak sought it out.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Return to your ship with Bastila and we will summon you when we are done.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Padawan, you have done well in discovering the Star Map hidden within the ancient ruins. But there is more you must do in the battle against Malak and the Sith.
comment: SCRIPTED  talking to the jedi council after discovering the star map

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We Jedi know victory over the Sith will not come through martial might. The Council has a mission for you, Padawan.

speaker: Dorak
text: I have consulted our vast archives in an effort to discover the nature of this 'Star Forge', but all my efforts have been in vain.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Still, the Council are in agreement: the Star Forge must be found! Revan and Malak sought it out when they began their tragic fall; the Star Forge is surely a powerful tool of the dark side.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Star Map in the ruins showed you four planets, but it was incomplete. It did not show the location of the Star Forge itself. We believe there may be similar Star Maps on other planets.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Each Star Map is likely a small piece of a larger puzzle. Find the Star Maps on Kashyyyk, Tatooine, Manaan and Korriban and we believe they will lead you to the Star Forge.

speaker: Player
text: I am ready to do the Council's will.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Jedi numbers have been ravaged by this war, by defections to Malak's cause and by Sith assassins. But we realize the importance of this mission.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Yet if we sent a company of Jedi Knights with you we would surely draw the full attention of Malak and the Sith, dooming your efforts to failure.

speaker: Player
text: Am I to undertake this task alone?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Secrecy is our best defense against the Sith, but it would be foolish to send you on this quest without someone to aid you, young Padawan.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Bastila will accompany you, for there is a powerful connection between you two... a connection that might be the key to unraveling the mysteries uncovered by Revan.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: And Juhani has also asked to accompany you. After long deliberation we have granted her request.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Juhani nearly fell to the dark side. Perhaps her presence will serve as a reminder to you of the dangers of that path.

speaker: Player
text: There are others I want to join me.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Of course those who aided you on Taris will also come; they possess skills you may find useful in your quest. Remember that secrecy and discretion are paramount to your success.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You will not be able to hide the fact that you are Jedi, nor should you. But the true nature of your mission must not reach Malak's ears.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You may return here at any time. Dantooine will be a sanctuary for you, a safe haven. Here you can find supplies and whatever advice or other aid we may give you.

speaker: Player
text: You can count on me. I will not fail.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: You can leave whenever you wish; the sooner the better. The longer you wait the stronger Malak becomes. But first a warning, young Padawan:

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The lure of the dark side is difficult to resist. I fear this quest to find the Star Forge could lead you down an all too familiar path.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The fate of the galaxy is in your hands, young Padawan. We pray you are up to the challenge.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: When do I leave?

speaker: Player
text: Why should I risk my life to stop Malak?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: This was already explained to you. Your command of the Force makes you a threat to Malak. Eventually he will destroy you, and all the Jedi, unless you stop him first.

speaker: Player
text: Great... Bastila and the cat woman. Anyone else you want to stick me with?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Keep the example of Juhani fresh in your mind. You may need a reminder of the dangers of the path that leads to the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Great... Bastila again. Anyone else you want to stick me with?

speaker: Player
text: Good. Others will only slow me down.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like a suicide mission to me.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Ever brash, ever disrespectful! This is what we have pinned our hopes on?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Peace, Vrook. We have discussed this; there is no other choice.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] No, I could not find anything.

speaker: Bastila
text: What are you talking about? The Council must be told of what we found there!

speaker: Bastila
text: We found an incomplete Star Map, Master Vandar. And an ancient droid that mentioned something about a Star Forge.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Lies! Bastila has already told us about this 'Star Forge' and the map you found!

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Peace, Master Vrook. I'm certain the Padawan only meant they had not found anything beyond what Bastila would surely have told us.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: There has been a report of a terrible battle near the Sandral estate to the south of the Enclave. Apparently a large force of droids attacked the estate.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The defending droids returned in kind. The attacking family was apparently the Matale family launching an attack on the Sandral estate.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Both entire families were slain, including the boy Shen who had been reported missing.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: There was a mention that someone noticed one or more other persons leaving the battle area after the conflict had finished. You were in that area, were you not? Did you see something?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] No, I was somewhere else.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: [Success] Is that so... I cannot find fault with your statement, but something in your manner is odd. But no matter, more pressing things are at hand.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You must always remember the destruction and chaos that the dark side can reap, and avoid it at all costs.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* It is obvious Master Vandar senses something is not right with your story. Yet he chooses to believe you, and I will not question the wisdom of a Jedi Master.

speaker: Juhani
text: *whisper* It is obvious Master Vandar senses something is amiss in your tale. Yet he chooses to believe you, and I will not question the wisdom of a Jedi Master.

speaker: Carth
text: *whisper* It's obvious he doesn't believe you. He must have some reason for letting you get away with this lie. I swear, I'll never understand these Jedi.

speaker: Mission
text: *whisper* Anyone can see that he doesn't believe you. He must have some reason for letting this slide. Probably trying to teach you some Jedi lesson or something.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] That's horrible! I didn't know!

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Perhaps it was Mandalorian raiders.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: We have heard that there was a close confrontation between the Sandral and Matale families by one of the southern estates earlier. We also heard that it was by your actions that direct conflict was avoided.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: It is good to hear that you have learned the lessons of the Jedi Order well enough to avoid conflict when necessary.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Rahasia Sandral and Shen Matale have come here seeking shelter against their families. The Council has decided to give it to them.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Their love for each other was being denied by overly possessive parents and we learned that it was only by your intervention that they managed to escape here.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: While it is regrettable that the fences between the families were not repaired, it is good that these two young lovers can live their lives free of oppression.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: I have heard that the Sandrals and Matales have agreed to cooperation in the construction of a new estate to house their children. Apparently a son of one family and the daughter of the other are getting married.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: I also I hear that we have you to thank for this happy occurrence. I am glad that you are using the authority our Order wields to achieve some measure of good.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You must not fail in your mission. Find the Star Maps that lead to the Star Forge. This is the only way to stop Malak and his Sith followers. You and Bastila are the galaxy's last, desperate hope.
comment: DIALOGUE  after having been given the main quest

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: But beware the dark side. Bastila will guide you, but she herself is young and new to the ways of the Jedi. You must help her as much as she helps you.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You must not fail in your mission, young Padawan. Find the Star Maps that lead to the Star Forge. This is the only way to stop Malak and his Sith followers.
comment: DIALOGUE  after being given the main quest

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: You and Bastila are the galaxy's last, desperate hope. May the Force be with you in this quest.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: You are here from the Council, are you not? Looking for Shen Matale?
comment: SCRIPTED  the first time the player talks to rahasia Dialog Mission Statement   These dialogs are the conversations the player canhave with Rahasia inside the Sandral estate.   The first dialog is when the player first meets Rahasia, either after having talked to Nurik, or having gone in the back door and found her in her room.   The second dialog is if the player has offended Rahasia in a previous conversation.   The third dialog is if the player has talked to Shen and been told he won't leave without her.   The fourth dialog is for conversations after Rahasia has asked the player to free Shen, but before learning that he won't leave without her. Exit points inconversation: Exit stream 1: When this conversation start DAN_MEET_DONE is set to TRUE to show that the player has met Rahasia. The player can either be nice, or be mean. If nice, DAN_ROMANCE_PLOT is set to 2 to show that Rahasia has asked the player to help. There is a possibility of a minor dark side hit if the player is rude, and it exits to stream 4.   If the player is mean, DAN_HATE_DONE is set to TRUE to show that Rahasia hates the player. There are possibilities for a minor or a medium dark side hit in this path for being uncaring. Party members interject comments and the stream ends. Exit stream 2: The player can either apologize (and get a minor light side bonus) and have DAN_HATE_DONE set to FALSE, or be insensitive and take another minor dark side hit. NOTE: there is the possibility of infinite dark side hits if the player keeps going on like this. If the player apologizes, this stream exits to stream 1, otherwise the conversation ends. Exit stream 3: DAN_LEAVE_DONE is set to TRUE to show that Rahasia has agreed to leave with Shen and the conversation ends. Exit stream 4: The lines are said and the conversation ends. If the character has not previously been given the key to the door (or found it), Rahasia gives the player the key.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: My name is Rahasia - Nurik is my father. He has not been himself since Casus disappeared. He is mad with grief, and he is convinced the Matales are responsible. He is not thinking rationally.

speaker: Player
text: Does this have anything to do with what happened to Shen?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: My father is a good man. When my mother died, he raised me and my brother by himself. He loves his children, and we love him. I just don't want you to judge him too harshly.

speaker: Player
text: I only want to find Shen Matale.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: You must understand that Father has been under a terrible strain. I have no wish to disobey him, but there are matters where even my father's authority is not absolute.

speaker: Player
text: Please, tell me what has happened.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: My father has kidnapped Shen Matale. He is holding him prisoner here in the compound. He feels this is a way to get back at the Matales, a way to get even for the disappearance of my brother Casus.

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. Well there is the answer we seek. The Jedi Council should be informed of this at once.

speaker: Carth
text: You don't think that perhaps there's more to look at here, do you? That maybe everything isn't what it appears?

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course not. It seems very simple to me. The Council must be allowed to decide the next step.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: No! Since Casus went missing my father has become unstable, he might hurt him if you do that! He no longer even cares if the Matales are responsible for what happened to Casus.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: I am afraid my father will simply kill Shen out of a mad, misguided lust for vengeance!

speaker: Player
text: I must tell the Jedi Council at once!

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: The Jedi Council does not have the authority to search our estate, and if Father finds out his secret has been revealed he might kill Shen right away.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: Please, find Shen and rescue him before my father does something he will regret forever. I would take you to the prison, but I cannot let my father see me with you.

text: What is the problem between your families?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: Please find Shen and free him! You are my only hope!

speaker: Player
text: Why do you care about Shen?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: Shen and I... we... Well, we have been taught by our families to hate each other, just for being related to our fathers.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: But I met Shen alone one day in the city, away from his father, and...

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: ... and Shen was so charming, so sweet. He didn't care at all that I was a Sandral, he just accepted me for who I was, with no reservations.

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: We talked and met again over months and fell in love. My brother Casus met him too and they were beginning to become friends, but then this whole mess had to happen...

speaker: Player
text: I will go now.

speaker: Player
text: This isn't my problem.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you telling me all this?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral
text: Shen is an innocent victim in all this. My father is not a bad man, but his grief has driven him to madness. He must be stopped.

speaker: Player
text: What happened to Casus?

speaker: Rahasia Sandral

text: Don't worry, honey - alien girls aren't really my thing. I'm much more interested in an attractive female of my own species.

speaker: Player
text: You're the guy who put the bounty on Dia's head, right?

speaker: Holdan
text: You're here about that? I guess Zax must have mentioned me to you at the bounty office. Fair enough - I don't care who takes her out, just so long as the job gets done.

speaker: Holdan
text: I can't let her get away with what she did - that wench tried to cut me with her vibroblade!

speaker: Player
text: Dia's dead. I killed her myself.

speaker: Holdan
text: Really? Huh... I guess that's it then. A real shame it had to come to this. She was a good looking gal despite her temper. Ah, well. Plenty more ladies out there for me.

speaker: Player
text: Where's my payment?

speaker: Holdan
text: If you want to collect the bounty, go talk to Zax. I gave him the credits for safe keeping. As far as I'm concerned my part in this is over.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Holdan
text: I don't want to waste my time answering a bunch of questions... I'm here to have a few drinks, watch the dancing girls and enjoy myself.

speaker: Holdan
text: I've got to be mentally ready. Davik's got an assignment for me off planet as soon as the quarantine ends.

speaker: Player
text: You work for Davik?

speaker: Holdan
text: I'm one of his top couriers. Davik's always sending me off planet to deliver and bring back packages. He knows he can trust me to follow my orders to the letter.

speaker: Holdan
text: Plus, I used to be an intergalactic customs agent so I know all the tricks they use to catch smugglers. That gives me the edge I need on my courier runs.

speaker: Player
text: You're pretty open about what you do.

speaker: Holdan
text: It's not like it's some big secret. It's kind of hard for Davik to keep a low profile when he belongs to a big intergalactic crime syndicate like the Exchange.

speaker: Player
text: Do you think Davik could get me off Taris?

speaker: Holdan
text: Davik's ship is the fastet one in the entire quadrant, but even the Ebon Hawk can't get off Taris until the quarantine is lifted. The Sith fleet has the planet surrounded.

speaker: Holdan
text: Any ship leaving orbit without the proper access codes will be disintegrated by the Sith auto-targeting laser cannons - and those codes are locked safely away in the military base.

speaker: Holdan
text: Davik's pretty upset about it. His smuggling operation isn't making any money, but even with his underworld connections he can't get his hands on those codes.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Holdan
text: Hate to see a pretty lady leaving, but you ain't the only girl in this place. I guess I'll go back to enjoying the dancers.

speaker: Holdan
text: Fine by me. That means I get to go back to enjoying the dancing girls.

speaker: Player
text: So what happens now?

speaker: Player
text: Why would she do that?

speaker: Holdan
text: Because she's crazy! She started screaming that I was making advances, and the next thing I know she's coming at me with a knife.

speaker: Bastila
text: It sounds to me like the woman was defending herself.

speaker: Holdan
text: I admit I was drunk. Maybe I got a little fresh. But it was no big deal. She didn't have to cut me!

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like maybe you got what you deserved.

speaker: Holdan
text: Hey - you weren't there. She totally over-reacted!

speaker: Player
text: I want the bounty on Dia's head removed.

speaker: Holdan
text: Hey, it's like I told you before - you come up with 200 credits and I'll remove the bounty. Otherwise she's got to pay the price.

speaker: Player
text: Here's 200 credits. Now get that bounty removed.

speaker: Holdan
text: Don't worry - I'll stick to my end of the bargain. I'll go tell Zax right now that the bounty is off the table.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] If you hire someone to kill Dia it will look like you weren't man enough to do it yourself.

speaker: Holdan
text: [Success] Well... I guess you might be right. Besides, I've noticed some of the girls around here are giving me the cold shoulder since all this started. Okay, you win; Dia can live.

speaker: Holdan
text: [Failure] If I let her get away with it I'll look even worse! She's got to pay - either with her life, or 200 credits to buy my forgiveness.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Force Persuade] I think it is time you forgave her. You are partly to blame for her behavior.

speaker: Holdan
text: [Success] Well... maybe it's time I forgave her. I am partly to blame for what she did, I suppose. Okay, you win; Dia can live.

speaker: Player
text: Take that bounty off Dia's head or you're a dead man!

speaker: Holdan
text: You're threatening me? I work for Davik Kang! If you kill me you'll be signing your own death warrant. Do us both a favor and don't waste my time with stupid threats!

speaker: Player
text: I'll go talk to Dia and see if she can come up with the credits.

speaker: Holdan
text: You can do that if you want, but I doubt she's got 200 credits. That's a lot, and she's just a working girl. But that's the breaks, right?

speaker: Holdan
text: What? I can't do that! Think how it would look. I work for Davik, I've got a certain reputation to uphold. I can't let her get away with this. There has to be payback!

speaker: Holdan
text: Although I do feel a little guilty about all this. Dia's a good looking gal - it'd be a shame to kill her. Tell you what - I'll take 200 credits in exchange for lifting the bounty.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. This isn't worth my trouble.

speaker: Player
text: So how do I collect this bounty?

speaker: Holdan
text: Just kill Dia and then go talk to Zax. I gave him the credits for safekeeping. He'll pay you off when the deed is done.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what happened with Dia.

speaker: Holdan
text: What do you mean what happened? She took her vibroblade and came after me like she was harvesting a bantha pelt!

speaker: Mission
text: Yeah, sure. You were as innocent as a Jawa in a droid chop shop!

speaker: Carth
text: Yeah, right. Sounds to me like she was defending herself.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Holdan
text: My name's Holdan, baby. Maybe you've heard of me... I work for Davik Kang, you know.

speaker: Player
text: Keep your hormones in check - I just want to ask some questions.

speaker: Holdan
text: I don't like the tone of your voice. I work for Davik Kang - I'm used to people treating me with respect!

speaker: Player
text: I don't care who you work for - you seem like a slimeball!

speaker: Holdan
text: I don't have to take this abuse from you! I came here to relax. Shove off and find someone else to bother - I want to watch the dancing girls.

speaker: Holdan
text: I don't normally go for these alien girls, but I've had some bad experiences with my own species lately. Maybe it's time for a change, you know what I mean?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not really interested in your love life.

speaker: Holdan
text: What do you want now? This whole thing with Dia is over, so we don't have anything to discuss.

speaker: Holdan
text: This better be important - I'm trying to watch the dancing girls. You got some news about Dia or something?

speaker: Holdan
text: Hey, baby - back again, I see. I guess the old Holdan charm is still working: the ladies just can't leave me alone!

speaker: Holdan
text: You again? This must be the official let's all bother Holdan day. Can't you see I'm trying to watch the dancing girls?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Greetings again, hunter. Your time out on the dunes has brought wear to your face. It is a trait that you and I share.
comment: After player has encountered the Komad out on the dunes hunting

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It is the weight of decisions made for the good of all. I don't think the others would understand. All they know is that a dragon is dead. I am content to leave it at that.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about you and hunting.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You are in dire need of better entertainment, human. My life has not changed since we last spoke.
comment: Player has already been told his name.

speaker: Player
text: Where is the best hunting?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The best hunting is wherever the best hunter is. It's a trite answer, human, but the only one I can give.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Our hunt proved it. We found a dragon where other hunters should have noticed. It will be the last one seen for a long time.

speaker: Player
text: Why are such large beasts so hard to find?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: They are elusive. Perhaps they sensibly avoid the places where their kind have died. I don't know.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I'm just glad we found him him using the old ways. That was a victory.

speaker: Player
text: Your traditional methods aren't popular?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Some try to lessen the risk by mass-hunting with battle droids. I would rather hunt solo, taking the risk as my own.

speaker: Player
text: Who uses battle droids?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Tanis did, but he appears to be no longer with us. Perhaps you already knew this, human? I can't say.
comment: Tanis is dead, killed out in the desert when the player found him.

speaker: Player
text: How long have you been at this?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: A decade? Two? I don't enslave myself to time, human. There is day and there is night.

speaker: Player
text: You really don't know anymore?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Tatooine will not change in my lifetime. Why bother trying to keep up with the rolling of the years?

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the other hunters?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Probably not as much as you would learn speaking to them yourself, even if they tell you nothing.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You have already shown an understanding of the needed skills when dealing with predators.
comment: Player has resolved the gammorean ambush by killing them or intimidation.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Having dealt with the Gamorreans, I think there is little else that will phase you.

speaker: Player
text: What about the hunters besides the Gamorreans?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Ah... put simply, Dorak Quinn is honorable. Tanis Venn is not so much, but I've no real quarrel with him.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my first questions.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I will answer. The day drags on, however.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? What do you do?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I am Komad Fortuna, a hunter and member of this lodge. It is not the life for everyone, but I am content.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something. Who knows this planet best?
comment: Player does not already have the star map

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No one that will return your questions. To truly know the dunes you have to live there, as the Sand People do.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Only they truly explore the land, but they attack without debate, if you see them at all.

speaker: Player
text: Have you ever seen the Sand People with anything odd?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The Sand People carry nothing but weapons and bloodlust. To them, outsiders are invaders to be repelled.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Once or twice, however, I have seen them emerge from older ruins with sacks and other containers.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I've always been driven off, and if I examine the site later, there is nothing left.

speaker: Player
text: What kinds of ruins were these? Where were they?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: They were old storehouses of some kind, but you couldn't find them now, human. The sand covers all.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The only ones who would know what was there are the Sand People, and you would have to take it by force.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Finding their encampment is easy enough. Walk south until you are attacked.

speaker: Player
text: What about the Jawas?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The Jawas may know the land as well, but are more interested in trading than talking. They scavenge to escape jobs akin to slavery.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Their language is difficult. If you can get anything more than the price of a droid out of them, I'll be impressed.

speaker: Player
text: I have to leave. Goodbye.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Good hunting.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, what will you pay for me not to kill you?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You talk far too big, human. This isn't the place for such things. Guards are a short yell away.
comment: Set a global that marks Komad as pissed off. It will be checked int he desert version of him.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Get out of my sight.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: [Success] [Komad squints, sensing your influence but not being able to fight it. He seems saddened by your action, as though he expected better.]
comment: This line is not VO. DO NOT RECORD.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Goodbye, human. Perhaps we will meet again, but I sincerely hope not.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] They wouldn't get here in time. Pay me.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: [Success] Of course the guards would take their time getting here... I don't wish trouble.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It is unfortunate that you would choose this course, human. You never know when you will need an ally.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: [Failure] Perhaps you are unfamiliar with how things work around here. The guards are always quick to act.

speaker: Player
text: Pay me or end up dead. It's that simple.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No, things are never quite so black and white. I am protected here, as are you. Nothing will come of this.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps you are right. You are safe... for now.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: There seems to be no reason for your anger, human. You would be wise to control it, lest it bury you.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: But, perhaps you are safer speaking with me. You've shown a weakness in the face of... two-legged predators.
comment: Player resolved gammorean ambush by bribing the gammoreans.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Perhaps you should reassert yourself? I don't know. I didn't think the Gamorreans so threatening.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The most obvious are the Gamorreans, however. Gurke and his crew are not the best company.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: They hunt, but often come back with salvage instead of hides or pearls. I think their prey walks upright.
comment: Set a local that will filter the dialogue on the gammoreans. "trustgammoreans"

speaker: Player
text: Wouldn't the guards have something to say about that?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The dunes are far from the reach of their blasters. Besides, Gurke spends his money in company stores.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Tanis did, but he no longer hunts, thanks to you. I'm glad a peaceful resolution was found.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I will not speak of it while they live. It is their shame to admit or hide. They know the effect it has.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Perhaps they will kill so many wraid that they also kill the hunt. After that, perhaps the solo hunter will still prosper.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It depends on what you seek. Wraid are plentiful and are the spoils of the sport hunter. Dragons appear only to the true hunter.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Patience is key. Krayt dragons hunt alone, and their prey is whatever can catch their attention.

speaker: Player
text: So dragons are rare? Are they dangerous?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: They are both rare and dangerous, and an honor to hunt. If you survive, you are blessed and favored. Respect them.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Probably from worry at getting your hands dirty. I really don't have much to talk to you about. You are not my kin.
comment: Player did not help with the hunt

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You have no place here with me, human. Leave me to my thoughts.
comment: Player pissed him off out on the dunes.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Yes, is there something you wish, human?

speaker: Player
text: Information, if I could trouble such a worthy hunter for a moment.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Save your words, swoop rider. They do not suit you.
comment: Player has signed on with the swoop bike races

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Spare me the flattery, human. Such talk is rarely sincere.
comment: player has not signed on with the bike races

speaker: Player
text: Just a few questions, if that's all right?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I will answer, though it is rare for one of you swoop riders to show much interest in anything besides racing.
comment: Player has signed on with the swoop bike races

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I see no harm in it. There are hours yet before I set back out on the dunes.
comment: player has not signed on with the bike races

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Why are you here, swoop jock? Hunting doesn't give your kind the instant thrills you need, does it?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Hmm? You know, I don't have that much to tell you. You really have to learn the dunes for yourself.

speaker: Mission031
text: I told you to leave me alone - so give me some space, Bug-eye! Your breath smells like bantha poodoo!

speaker: Rodian033
text: Little girl should not be in bar. This no place for little girl. If little girl smart, she run away home now.

speaker: Mission031
text: Who you calling a little girl, Chuba-face?

speaker: Rodian033
text: Little girl needs lesson in manners!

speaker: Mission031
text: Just a sec, boys. Zaalbar... a little help here? I need you to rip the legs off some insects.

speaker: Zaalbar031
text: Mission - I'm busy. They just brought my food!

speaker: Mission031
text: Quit complaining... you can finish eating later. Besides, you need the exercise so get over here.

speaker: Rodian033
text: We no want trouble with Wookiee. Our problem with you, little girl!

speaker: Mission031
text: You got a problem with me, then you got a problem with Big Z. So unless you want to take on my furry friend, I suggest you greenies hop on out of here.

speaker: Rodian034
text: Little girl lucky she has big friend.

speaker: Mission
text: Say, I don't recognize you and I know pretty much everyone in the Lower City. You must be new down here. I guess that makes me and Big Z your official welcoming committee!

speaker: Player
text: Hey - we speak the same language!

speaker: Mission
text: It's not that strange. Most aliens can speak Basic, they just prefer to use their own language. But I grew up here on Taris so I just sort of got used to speaking the native tongue.

speaker: Carth
text: You showed a lot of guts dealing with those Vulkars, kid. You got a name?

speaker: Mission
text: My name's Mission Vao and this big Wookiee is my best friend, Zaalbar. I'd offer to give you a tour, but the streets down here aren't safe. But if there's anything else you need...

speaker: Player
text: I'm trying to find a way into the Black Vulkar base.

speaker: Mission
text: The Black Vulkar base? You'll never get in there - they attack on sight. But if you got a problem with the Vulkars, you should go speak to the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Mission
text: Their base is open to anyone - I hang out there all the time. Gadon, the leader of the Hidden Beks, is a pretty good guy. He'll probably be able to help you out.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Mission
text: Well, you came to the right person! If you want info on Lower Taris I'm the one to talk to! Davik, the Lower City gangs... I've even got the scoop on that bounty hunter Calo Nord!

speaker: Player
text: How do a Wookiee and a Twi'lek street urchin end up as best friends?

speaker: Mission
text: We just kind of fell in together. It ain't easy on your own here in the Lower City - everyone's always looking to push you around.

speaker: Carth
text: So we noticed. Still, you seem like an odd pair.

speaker: Mission
text: When I met up with Zaalbar it seemed like a good match. I knew we could look out for each other. With my street smarts and his muscle, we make a great team.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Mission
text: You're going? Yeah, this dive is pretty boring. No action around here. Come on, Big Z, let's go.

speaker: Zaalbar031
text: But I haven't finished eating!

speaker: Mission
text: Can't you think about something besides your stomach for five minutes? Come on - we'll go see if there's anything good to eat at the Bek base.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Davik.

speaker: Mission
text: Davik's part of the intergalactic crime syndicate, but I guess everyone knows that. But I hear he's got a new ship for his smuggling operations - the Ebon Hawk.

speaker: Mission
text: I don't know much about space travel, but I hear that ship's fast enough to break the Sith blockade. Of course, this is all just second hand rumor.

speaker: Carth
text: Where would he keep it? Do you know?

speaker: Mission
text: If Davik does have a ship, he's got it locked up in his estate. Nobody gets in there, except the people working for Davik and the Exchange.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Lower City gangs.

speaker: Mission
text: There's only two gangs worth worrying about here in the Lower City: the Black Vulkars and the Hidden Beks. Sometimes Zaalbar and I hang out at the Bek base.

speaker: Mission
text: The Beks are led by Gadon Thek - he's a good guy. Lost his sight in a swoop bike accident a few years ago, but even blind he's a great leader.

speaker: Mission
text: Not like that traitor Brejik! Before he took over the Vulkars he was a Hidden Bek. Gadon considered that ungrateful space slug his adopted son.

speaker: Player
text: Why did Brejik leave the Hidden Beks?

speaker: Mission
text: When Gadon went blind everyone figured he'd step down and appoint Brejik in his place. But Gadon figured Brejik wasn't ready yet. He wanted him to wait a few years.

speaker: Mission
text: But Brejik was too impatient. He left to join the Vulkars, and ever since he's been waging a war to wipe Gadon and his Beks from the face of Taris!

speaker: Mission
text: This gang war in the Lower City is totally the Vulkar's fault. They're the ones killing everything that moves out on the street. It's like they've gone insane.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Calo Nord.

speaker: Mission
text: Calo Nord's one of the most famous bounty hunters in the galaxy. He's killed more people than the Iridian Plague! I've seen him kill people just for trying to talk to him!

speaker: Mission
text: He hangs around Zax's bounty office, but I don't think he's looking for work there. All the postings there are small time - way beneath a bounty hunter of his caliber.

speaker: Mission
text: I figure Calo's been hired by Davik to do a special job for the Exchange. I'd wager a thousand credits that as soon as the quarantine ends, he'll be getting off this rock.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks - I'll go see Gadon now.

speaker: Mission
text: Yeah, we should be going now, too. Come on, Zaalber. This dive is boring. Maybe we can find some action in the Undercity.

speaker: Player
text: That's weird: a Twi'lek who speaks galactic Basic!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: GRRROWLLL, stop where you are, outsider. You enter the domain of Chuundar, Chieftain and leader!
comment: This guard is outside of the village. Once the player is in range, he initiates. The player has no escape, they have to go and talk to Chuundar. Player is teleported directly to Chuundar throneroom. This guard shoudl remain where he is after the player speaks to Chuundar.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Stand aside! This human is with me and I want access to the home of my people!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: You have no rights here, mad-claw! This human should not have brought this taint upon our land! You must answer to Chuundar!

speaker: Player
text: What does he mean, Zaalbar? What taint?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: He means me. I am the taint that you have brought back.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Shut up! GROWWLL! You are nameless with dishonor, mad-claw! Yours is a foulness that disgusts me!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: RRaaaghh! Enough talk! You and the outcast mad-claw will be taken to Chuundar now!
comment: Zaalbar is with the player Player and zaalbar appear in throne room.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: RRaaaghh! Enough! The mad-claw from your ship is already before Chuundar. Come!
comment: Zaalbar is not with the player Player and zaalbar appear in throne room.

speaker: Player
text: Take me to Chuundar. I would speak with him.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: The choice is made for you already! You make a demand for something you can't alter, can't help!

speaker: Player
text: You will not take me anywhere, mongrel!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Look about you, fool. You face a legion of Wookiees in their home terrain! It is a losing fight for you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: He is right. There are too many. Please, let us go to Chuundar. He has much to explain.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: You will be taken before Chuundar and he will judge your worth, and punishment for the taint you have returned to us.

speaker: Player
text: And if I refuse to go see Chuundar?

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: There is no refusing. If you will not walk, we will bind you. Shall you be carried through the trees like a child?

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: He will decide if you are fit to walk the village of Rwookrrorro. You've already soiled our world with what you brought on your ship.

speaker: Player
text: My ship? What do you mean by that?

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Chuundar sent us to search it. We found the exile. The nameless mad-claw, once called Zaalbar.

speaker: Player
text: Who gave you access? You had no right!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Freyyr has returned to us because of you, outsider. You are one of the few outsiders we will allow to remain among us in the village.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Chuundar has said that you can remain here, but watch where you step while in our village, outsider.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Do you... do you have the cure, up-worlder? Have you come to save us from the horrible fate of the others?

text: I have brought you a serum to cure the rakghoul disease.

text: Here, take this rakghoul serum. I have enough for both of you.

text: I feel the disease burning away! It... it is like a miracle! I am cured!

text: Thank you, up-worlder. You have saved us from a fate worse than death. I only wish I had some reward to give you. Maybe you can find something worthwhile in the wreckage of that Republic escape pod.

text: Republic escape pod? What are you talking about?

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Not long ago an escape pod crashed in the Undercity, far to the northeast of the village. We were going to try and salvage equipment from it when we were attacked by the rakghouls and infected.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: I'd tell you more if I could, but our salvage team never reached the pod. It's probably still there, unless some of the other up-worlders already found it and picked it clean.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We should go now, up-worlder. We're anxious to return to the village and see our families again. Thank you once again for everything you have done.

speaker: Player
text: I was just happy to help.

speaker: Player
text: What will you give me in exchange for this cure?

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We... we have nothing, up-worlder. We are Outcasts. All we have are the clothes on our backs.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please, up-worlder. Show us mercy. Give us the cure out of the goodness of your heart!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'm not wasting the cure on an Outcast!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Go then, up-worlder. Leave us here to die, abandoned by everyone!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry - I'm here to help you.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: You... you will help us? Bless you, up-worlder! But... you must hurry!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We have the rakghoul disease. It is only a matter of time until we are transformed into terrible creatures like those who attacked you when you first came into the pen.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: It is too late for them. Soon it will be too late for us and we will transform into those horrible rakghouls ourselves!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry... I'll be back when I find a cure for you!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please hurry, up-worlder. We don't have much time until the transformation.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Don't forget about us, up-worlder. If you find anyway to cure us of this disease, please come back and help us.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll kill you so you don't infect anyone else!

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Why have you come back, up-worlder? Do you come to mock us in our suffering as this disease destroys us?

speaker: Player
text: Get away from me you diseased mongrels!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: When the rakghouls infected me I never thought I'd see my family again. Thank you for all your help, up-worlder.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please... you have to help us. We beg you. We don't want to end up like the others. Please help us. We can't end up like them.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? Why are you locked away from the rest of the village?

speaker: Outcast Man
text: I once lived above, with the rich and privileged. But I was cast down here - a punishment far worse than my crimes deserved!

speaker: Outcast Man
text: The rakghoul disease can infect you. It can transform you into one of those monsters! I've seen it happen!

speaker: Outcast Man
text: You are the one who brought us the rakghoul cure! The entrie village thanks you. I just regret we have nothing to give you as a reward.

speaker: Outcast Man
text: A lifetime lived in this dark place can drive you mad! Just look at poor old Rukil if you don't believe me - he's lost his mind!

speaker: Rakatan
text: You must speak with our Guide if you wish to perform the ritual now.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Isn't it strange? Nobody seems to know what happened to Master Uthar or Yuthura. They're both just... gone.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Have you heard? Yuthura Ban is dead. I hear Master Uthar is looking for a new apprentice. How awful...

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Have you heard? Master Uthar is dead and Yuthura Ban has taken over the academy. How brutal...

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Oh, ah... hello. I don't remember seeing you here before. My name is Kel... Kel Algwinn.

speaker: Player
text: Is something wrong?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: This one isn't raving like the others. A doubter.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... oh, uh, nothing.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Y-yes. My master always says I am too trusting, too willing to show weakness. You're a Sith, so I really shouldn't... you know...

speaker: Player
text: But I'm not a Sith, yet.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Oh, I know that. I mean... you aren't yet, but you intend to be. I mean you're just like everyone else here.

speaker: Player
text: And you're not?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Well I... I... I didn't mean it like that.

speaker: Player
text: Well, how did you mean it, then?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... I shouldn't trust you. I can't trust you, can I?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Sure you can.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: [Success] I just... don't feel I belong here. I thought maybe I did at first, but now... I don't know. I just have so many doubts.
comment: persuade successful set global that Kel told the player

speaker: Player
text: Master Uthar probably wouldn't like to hear that.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Yes, I'm... I'm sorry. P-please don't, don't tell anyone... I'll get over it, I guess.

speaker: Player
text: You're no Sith. I've never seen anyone so pathetic!

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... I am too a Sith! I'm more a Sith than you are! I'll show you!!

speaker: Player
text: Alright. Suit yourself.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Err... well, good luck with your training.

speaker: Player
text: If it doesn't feel right, then perhaps you don't belong here.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: But where would I go, then? What would I do?

speaker: Player
text: Have you thought about the Jedi?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... don't know. I never really thought about it. Maybe I should seek it out, give it a try. Thank you... thank you so much!
comment: Kel leaves permanently give player a small Light Side bonus

speaker: Player
text: It doesn't matter. Have you considered that the dark side just isn't your way?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Uh, eh, maybe you're right. *sigh* I'll go and... tell Master Uthar that I'm not ready for this. Maybe it won't be so bad. Th-thank you.

speaker: Player
text: Leave, obviously. You're not ready to be a Sith. You'll wind up dead.

speaker: Player
text: Everyone has doubts. Keep it up... you'll come around.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I guess you're right. The dark side is... where I belong. No going back now. Th-thank you.
comment: set global that Kel has been turned back to the Dark Side small Dark Side bonus for the player

speaker: Player
text: Is that it? Don't bother me with your petty weaknesses.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: [Failure] No... no, I shouldn't bother you with it. Forget I said anything.

speaker: Player
text: Out with it. This is getting tiresome.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... forget I said anything. Just... go back to your training, please. I have work to do.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to trust me.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: [Success] I just... don't feel I belong here. I thought maybe I did at first, but now I... I don't know. I have so many doubts.

speaker: Player
text: No, of course not. What kind of Sith are you?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I, uh, I suppose you're right. Never mind. Forget I said anything.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the Code of the Sith?
comment: player has received first test, not completed it

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Yes, of course. I must admit I've never really understood it very well. Enough to please Master Uthar, I guess... but I still have trouble with it.

speaker: Player
text: What's the problem?

speaker: Player
text: All things take time. Not to worry.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Yeah. Yes, I suppose so. Thanks.

speaker: Player
text: And you're a full Sith? How pathetic.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Don't say that! Leave me alone, or you'll be sorry!

speaker: Player
text: I doubt that.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I am a Sith, better trained than you! I'll show you!!

speaker: Player
text: Fine, fine. Have it your way.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Just leave!

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the excavations in the valley?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Of course. It's full of ancient Sith ruins, from a time before the Sith left this region of space. Rather exciting, really. I've, uh, never studied it myself... I couldn't help you much.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: If you're really interested, there's a fellow by the name of Dak who's out in the valley now. He knows plenty about it.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Player
text: I can't persuade you to tell me?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Uh, n-no, I really can't. A Sith... like you... would use any means to succeed.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying you're not a Sith?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Please don't tell anyone what I told you. They would tell me to leave... or worse.
comment: selected Kel told his secret, plot not resolved

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Oh, hello again. You're, uh... doing well in your training?
comment: selected again Kel has not told his secret

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: I'll stick with the bounties Davik puts out... they're usually less dangerous than the government funded contracts.

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: I saw Calo Nord in the tap room. He's a legend in this business! I wonder if he'd give me an autograph?

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: These are good times for bounty hunters! I've made a small fortune on the bounties Zax has been paying out.

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: Did you hear? Somebody killed Gadon Thek! I bet it won't be long until the Beks put out a bounty on Brejik's head in retaliation!

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: Word is somebody stole the Vulkar's prototype swoop engine! I wonder if there's a reward to bring it back?

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: I saw you kill Bendak Starkiller! I was just about to bring him in, too!

speaker: Bounty Hunter
text: See the price on Bendak Starkiller's head? Too bad no one will collect. Bendak never leaves the safety of that Upper City Cantina.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Leave me be. If I don't get these converters working, I lose my job.
comment: This is a generic mechanic dialogue that can be placed in the spaceport landing area in multiple locations. One-liners randomly displayed.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Why are you bothering me? You've got a ship. You can leave this rock.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Some ships I fix, some I scrap. Depends if the owner disappears in the dunes.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Business is up a little, so leave me to my work.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: You a swoop racer? Crazy fool.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: You here to hunt wraid? I work a wrench. Boring, but I know it won't kill me.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Czerka Corporation keeps me working. Don't care what else they do.

speaker: Docking Bay Mechanic
text: Tatooine's a dustbowl, and that's all it'll ever be.

speaker: Lur Arka Sulas
text: Though you have aged, young sentient, I do believe you are indeed the one I seek. I am here to return you to your father.
comment: ** Lur Arka will be situated in the Dantooine starport, and can be talked to at any time. If the player has learned Sasha's language and talked to her, this will initiate a cut-scene where both Lur Arka and the player are moved to the starship entrance and Sasha appears at the bottom of the ramp. Lur Arka will then init dialogue (this is the top node where EBO_LURARKA = 4). END DIALOGUE #1 - Lur Arka and Sasha leave the area permanently, XP is rewarded END DIALOGUE #5, #6 - The player is rewarded with some XP, start the cut-scene as described above other endings are not important

speaker: Sasha
text: Yooba na abds?

speaker: Lur Arka Sulas
text: I see that <FirstName> was correct about your linguistic difficulties. I am positive that your parents can assist you with that.

speaker: Sasha
text: Me abd liaz! Me na awnts palkie!

speaker: Lur Arka Sulas
text: Calm yourself, child. I will take you home.

speaker: Sasha
text: Sasha na esowon in bristag. Bristag me laesfa.

speaker: Player
text: Lur Arka na bads. Nuh-gisen laesfa, Sasha.

speaker: Sasha
text: Laesfa? Me palkie laesfa?

speaker: Sasha
text: Yb, bristag. Yb-abu, <FirstName>!

speaker: Lur Arka Sulas
text: Thank you for your assistance, sentient. I am sure the girl's parents will be most appreciative of your efforts.

speaker: Player
text: Just go. I've had enough of this.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I suppose I must spend some time talking to you since you are here in an official capacity. What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of Sunry?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Sunry was a Republic soldier, a hero even. Do you think his Republic masters would let someone so valuable go so easily?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I think not. I think Sunry maintains his contacts with the Republic and seeks to escalate the situation here.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Is there something else you require?

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything suspicious about this case?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I find this case to be fairly straight forward. Sunry is from the Republic, Elassa from the Sith. The great empires battling now live out their conflict through their minions too.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Is that all?

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Republic and the Sith Empire?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I do not buy into the Republic line that this is some epic battle of the 'good' Republic against the 'evil' Sith Empire.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: The Sith empire is merely an expansionistic power, much like the Republic was early in its history.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: It is simply the turning of history, where the old is swept away by the better new.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Is there anything intelligent you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: I have no more questions for now.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Then go and do not disturb me unless you have trial business to discuss.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Do not disturb me, off-worlder, I am busy.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: At last, my search is over! I was beginning to fear someone else had killed you and deprived me of the pleasure.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: You may have defeated the pathetic bounty hunter my Master sent after you, but you are no match for me! I have studied at the foot of the Dark Lord himself!

speaker: Player
text: How did you get down here?

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: Do you think those Republic subs are the only way to reach the ocean floor? Malak and Revan found a way down here long before the Hrakert station was built.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: I acquired a ship and followed the same route Revan and my Master used on their own journey. Then it was simply a matter of waiting for you to return for the Star Map.

speaker: Player
text: You're Malak's apprentice? Can't say I'm impressed.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: Your words mean nothing to me... unless you wish to beg for your life. No? Then I shall try to make this both quick and painful!

speaker: Player
text: When will Malak learn? I'll kill you just like I killed Calo Nord!

speaker: Player
text: You're a fool if you think you can defeat me.

speaker: Player
text: You were on the Endar Spire! You killed Trask. You'll pay for that!

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Don't you believe a word of what Czerka Corporation said in there, there is always a peaceful solution to conflict. They are just lazy.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean? What are you talking about?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Czerka miners have been attacked by Sand People, so the company Czerka Corporation wants them killed. They didn't ask you to do it?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: The Sand People aren't animals. I've watched them, and they are intelligent. There must be a way to peacefully stop the attacks... I know it.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: But no one will try, of course. You can't even leave the city without Czerka approval and they want the Sand People dead.

speaker: Player
text: The Czerka said that the Sand People attacked first.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Well, yes they did. They attacked the Czerka, who deployed numerous giant sandcrawlers and started tearing up the desert with ion shovels and whatever else.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: What would you have done? To the Sand People, it must have seemed like an invasion. There were no negotiations for territory or resources.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: I don't think the killing has been justified, but as a conservationist I'm hoping someone at least tries to talk this out.

speaker: Player
text: What would you suggest, then?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Communication. If we could just speak to them... but they don't talk. At least, not in any language an average translator can understand.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: There was even a Jedi here a few years ago that couldn't seem to get through to them. I... think that ended in blood too.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: I'm not saying it would be easy, but someone has to try. Maybe with a real translation droid, not these old protocol scrap heaps walking around.

speaker: Player
text: Who would have a capable droid?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Well, *you* do, don't you? You bought that strange old droid off of Yuka Laka, didn't you? He said it was quite sophisticated.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: I'm sure I heard Yuka Laka say that it could speak a Sand People dialect. Although he'd say rust is gold to make a sale...

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: With that droid, maybe you could talk to them. I wouldn't survive... maybe with desert robes as a disguise someone could get into their enclave.

speaker: Player
text: Where would that enclave you mentioned be?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: What? It's no secret where they are. The attacks get worse the further southwest in the Dune Sea you go. Then people die on both sides.

speaker: Player
text: Where would you get robes to match theirs?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: I suppose you could take them off of the warrior raiders in the Dune Sea, but there's no way I'd survive anything like that.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Plus you would have to explain why you killed their warriors if you are trying to make peace... but I suppose there is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I'll look into it.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Sure, that's what Czerka Corporation keeps saying, and then they just start shooting again. The fighting won't stop until they are all dead.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Or until the Czerka leave. The one is as likely as the other with the way things are going. Bah, what do I know.

speaker: Player
text: I will deal with the matter as I see fit.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: That's what the infuriating Czerka Protocol officer said, but I'm not foolish enough to believe it. Everyone just wants to wipe the Sand People out.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Go on then, but you're just like the Czerka. Shortsighted fool. If you could just talk to them... maybe get a true translation droid...

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Ah, I'm wasting my time. Go on, get out of here.

speaker: Player
text: I don't care. Get out of my way.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: They are pretty rare, even on well-stocked worlds, but I'm sure I heard something about an unusual droid in the shop here on Tatooine.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't *you* do something? Why should I?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Someone else has to! I've got no influence with Czerka Corporation, I can't afford what Yuka Laka charges for his droids, and I wouldn't survive...

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Well, what I mean is, whoever tries to deal with the Sand People would first have to survive their initial attacks. I wouldn't.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Someone could maybe get into their enclave if they could disguise themselves, but you'd have to get real desert robes and that would be dangerous too.

speaker: Player
text: Why hasn't anyone tried talking to them?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Well, there is the small matter that they don't seem to speak a language that your average translator can understand. Is that their fault?

speaker: Player
text: Intelligent or not, the Sand People have killed people.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Yes they have, but Czerka Corporation deployed numerous giant sandcrawlers to tear up the desert with ion shovels and whatever else.

speaker: Player
text: Why would you know any better?

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: Perhaps I'm no expert on diplomatic situations, but I know when there is a lack of due care for the evironment and the residents of it.

speaker: Player
text: Is this about Czerka wanting the Sand People chieftain killed?
comment: player has been told about sand people by Czerka

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: So, you are the killer that they hired. Just going to walk out there and wipe them out? I'd expect no less from fools.

speaker: Player
text: Move aside, I have things to do.

speaker: Dayso Cooh
text: I'm sure you do. Czerka probably hired you to kill the Sand People in retaliation for a few attacks. Just another bloodthirsty fool.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Just move along. There's nothing to see here.

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: Where did you hide those Sith uniforms? Did you sell them to the Tarisian underground? Start talking - I want answers!

speaker: tar02_alienprisoner
text: Please - I'm only a visitor to Taris, trapped here by your quarantine. I know nothing about the Tarisian underground or your missing Sith uniforms!

speaker: Player
text: What's going on in there?

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: A few of the Sith trooper uniforms have gone missing. We've got evidence that this alien knows something about them, so the commander's interrogating him.

speaker: Carth
text: *whisper* I know all about Sith interrogations. This isn't going to end well.

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: I'm getting sick of your lies, you alien scum! We got your ugly mug on a security tape from the base! Start talking before I splatter your slimy brains all over this room!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Uh-oh. I think the commander's losing his temper. I'm glad I'm out here - it took me an hour to clean the blood stains from my uniform after the last interrogation.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe the alien really doesn't know anything.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Then I guess we don't lose anything when the commander blows his head off, do we? Anyway - what do you care?

speaker: Player
text: Stop the interrogation right now!

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: Who said that? What's going on out there?

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Just stay out of this, if you know what's good for you!

speaker: Player
text: I won't let you kill a defenseless prisoner!

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: What was that? Did I hear you right? 'Let' us kill him? How can you stop us?

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: Time to teach this soldier how we deal with insubordination!

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: Time to teach this civilian the penalty for defying the Sith!

speaker: Player
text: You're right. Do whatever you want.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Smart move.

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: This is your last chance: where did you hide those uniforms you stole?

speaker: tar02_alienprisoner
text: I swear, I don't know what you mean. I'm just... NOOOO!

speaker: tar02_sithcommander
text: Get in here, search the room. I know those uniforms are in here somewhere.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to get involved in this.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: You're a little too curious for your own good, civilian! This doesn't concern you!

speaker: Player
text: Uniforms? What are they talking about?

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Hey, we don't need any reinforcements. All we're doing is searching for some missing Sith uniforms.

speaker: Player
text: I know... I'm the one who stole them!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: What??? Traitors! Spies! Attack!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Good - get back to patrolling the streets. We can handle this in here.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: What do you want, civilian? Do you have any information about the missing Sith uniforms? Make it quick!

speaker: Player
text: Uniforms? What are you talking about?

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: You're awfully curious about this... maybe a little too curious! I think you know more about those missing uniforms than you're saying!

speaker: Player
text: If I wanted uniforms I'd just kill you and take yours!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: A threat?! I knew you were a spy!

speaker: Player
text: I don't know what you're talking about!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Right... like I'm going to believe that! A crate of Sith uniforms goes missing and you just happen to wander into the apartment of our prime suspect? That's pretty convenient!

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: You're part of some Tarisian underground resistance, aren't you? Time for you to learn how the Sith deal with spies!

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry... I'll be going now.

speaker: Sith Trooper
text: Not so fast, civilian... why are you here? Are you a spy? You came to buy Sith uniforms from this alien, didn't you? Didn't you?!

speaker: Saul Karath
text: Carth, it has been far too long since we last spoke. I see the recent months have not been kind in your case. I barely recognized you.
comment: Dialog mission statement: Player is taunted and tortured by Saul Interrogation will see Carth or Bastila suffer (depending if player is female or male) If PC refuses to answer, Carth or Bastila will pass out If PC answers then "Lev_TortureBetray" global is set No matter what happens conversation ends when Saul has PC tortured, PC passes out, wakes up with Carth and Bastila both outside torture cages and cell empty, Carth or Bastila will speak to them (depending on male/female player)

speaker: Carth
text: But I recognized you, Saul. I see your face every night even as I promise myself I will kill you for what you did to my home world.

speaker: Saul Karath
text: Did you learn nothing in your time under me? As a soldier you should understand that casualties were unavoidable. This was an act of war.

speaker: Carth
text: It was a cowardly act of betrayal! Your fleet bombed a civilian target into oblivion without warning or provocation. And the blood of those innocent people is on your hands!

speaker: Saul Karath
text: In war even the innocent must die. The Sith would not accept me until I proved I had truly turned my back on the Republic by bombing the planet.

speaker: Carth
text: My wife died in that attack, Saul. And for that, I swear I'll kill you.

speaker: Saul Karath
text: You used to be a man of action, not of empty words. Cling to your lust for revenge if you must, but spare me your tired threats. I've heard them all before.

speaker: Saul Karath
text: You are an insignificant part of these events, anyway. Lord Malak is far more interested in your Jedi companions. He has great plans for them.

speaker: Bastila
text: We will never serve Malak or the dark side! The Sith will be destroyed, Admiral Karath... as will you if you don't turn away from this path.

speaker: Saul Karath
text: Your words are brave, Bastila, but the lure of the dark side is hard to resist - or so I've been told. I wonder if your companion is as devoted to the light as you are?

speaker: Player
text: You're wasting your time, Saul. I'll never betray the Jedi!

text: We saw what you did out there on the cameras...

text: Destroying the machinery was the right thing to do, for everyone.

speaker: Sami
text: That creature... the giant firaxan shark, the guardian of the kolto or whatever it was, seems to have calmed down a lot. It may even be safe to go outside now.

speaker: Sami
text: But we'll still stay here and wait for the Republic rescue crews. Thank you for not making a huge mistake.

text: Why did you have to poison the water?? We don't know what effect it could have on the environment around here... or on the kolto.

speaker: Sami
text: Whatever it is that's coming out of the vent now doesn't look the same at all... I only hope you didn't pollute whatever was making it... We never were able to synthesize it.

speaker: Sami
text: I think we're just going to sit here. We have a lot of food and water, so we should be alright for a while.

speaker: Sami
text: If you can make it out to the kolto harvesting machines, try to reprogram them to self destruct. Maybe that will cause the creature to stop its psychic screams.

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me how to disable the harvesting machine again?

text: You can reprogram the harvesting machines to overpressure their self-oxidizing fuel, so that the fuel tank cannisters will rupture and the entire machine will destroy itself.

speaker: Sami
text: The Hydrolium gas we use is a gas at 1 to 3 million sangen, a liquid at about 4 million sangen, and a solid above that. When it's a liquid it's VERY explosive.

speaker: Sami
text: If you inject enough of the Hydrolium gas into the tank, the pressure will be so great that it will turn to liquid form and start a chain reaction inside the machine.

speaker: Sami
text: Once you do that, you can open the doors to the submersible bay and go back to the surface. Make sure you tell the Republic there are still some survivors down here.

speaker: Sami

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Luo

speaker: Player
text: It is like being able to shoot lightning from your fingertips.

speaker: Player
text: Fire that only genetically gifted people can use.

speaker: Luo
text: But maybe you mean something greater, something in all peoples that can harness its power.

speaker: Player
text: The true nature of the Force is being able to project your will upon reality.

speaker: Luo
text: Project your will? To force things to be the way you want?

speaker: Player
text: The only true Force is to be able to change destiny.

speaker: Luo

speaker: Player
text: The strong of will can have whatever they desire.

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: Luo

speaker: Luo

speaker: Luo

speaker: Player

speaker: Luo
text: I hope that someday, you will find me worthy to teach, Master.
