speaker: Janice Nall
text: My selection is a bit limited right now - the Sith confiscated all my assault droids. But I've got a utility droid you might find interesting.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to see what you have in stock.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: Have you heard the news? Bendak Starkiller is coming out of retirement to fight in a death match. Everybody's trying to get tickets to see it.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: I've never understood why people always want to watch each other get killed. Droids don't think that way. Maybe that's why I like them better than people.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: I heard Bendak Starkiller finally met his match. I can't say I'm surprised - he was getting on in years. People start to lose their edge as they get older.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: That's the nice thing about droids. A yearly maintenance check and a few replacement parts here and there and they can last forever.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: Welcome back to my shop. If you want to buy something I'd suggest you do it soon, before the Sith haul me off to their interrogation chambers.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Janice Nall
text: Somebody broke into the military base. The Sith are convinced one of my utility droids was used during the break-in. They were here questioning me just a little while ago.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: I guess they believed me when I said I didn't know anything about it, but I get the feeling they might be back. So get your shopping in while you can.

speaker: Janice Nall
text: Back again, I see. Well, I've never turned a potential customer away yet. You interested in seeing what I have in stock?

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: Hello there, captain. Let's see... ah, yes. Here it is. It looks like the shipment has been delivered to your ship, as requested.

speaker: Player
text: What shipment? What are you talking about?

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: This is docking bay 32, isn't it? Yes, it is, and that's what I have here on the requisition form. Everything seems to be in order. The gizka are your problem now.

speaker: Player
text: Excuse me, did you say "gizka"?

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: It says right here on the manifest that you ordered a crate of gizka. To be delivered to docking bay 32... that's right here.

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: Now, all I need is your thumbprint for the... wait a second, where did the datapad go? *sigh* Nothing is ever organized around here.

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: At any rate, the gizka are yours. One of the loaders said the crate split open once he put it in your hold... some of the critters might have gotten loose.

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: That happens, I'm afraid. We don't accept liability... and we certainly couldn't take the cargo back. Enjoy.

speaker: Player
text: Whatever you put on my ship, I want it off. Now.

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: If you want the cargo removed, you'll have to fill out another requisition. I have one right... wait. I thought I had one. Oh, well.

speaker: Player
text: Err... what shipment was that again?

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: Well, let me see. Docking bay 32, check... crate 42-B7, check... manifest lists "life form: gizka". Everything seems to be in order.

speaker: Player
text: Excellent. Thank you.

speaker: Jor Ul Kurax
text: Wait a second, is this right? It says docking bay 32 on the form, but you just arrived. Oh, well, the gizka are your problem now.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean "my problem"? I didn't order any gizka.

speaker: Player
text: Fair enough. Thanks.

speaker: Gendar
text: Greetings, up-worlder. We rarely see your kind here in the Undercity. I find it strange that so many of you have come down from the surface recently.

speaker: Carth
text: No offense, but I can see why people normally avoid this place.

speaker: Gendar
text: Why have you come into this dark and sunless place? Is there something you need of me or my village? I will help you however I can.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you people? Why do you live here in the Undercity?

speaker: Gendar
text: We are the Outcasts - shunned from the surface for our crimes and banished here to the Undercity. We banded together to form this village that we might survive in this hostile environment.

speaker: Gendar
text: I am Gendar, the leader of this village: as my father was, and as was his father before him. Many of us have been here for generations, our ancestors cast down long ago.

speaker: Gendar
text: There is no return to the surface for us, or our descendants. But somehow we manage to survive amidst the filth and roaming bands of deadly rakghouls.

speaker: Player
text: What a horrible way to live!

speaker: Gendar
text: Life down here can be difficult. It can break the spirit... many in the village have become bitter and hopeless. Especially those newly cast down.

speaker: Gendar
text: But life goes on, and we must try to make the best of what we have. And maybe someday we will find a better life... Ha! Listen to me. I'm starting to sound like Rukil.

speaker: Player
text: Rukil?

speaker: Gendar
text: The oldest man in the village. He is a kind soul, but I am afraid he is growing weary of this world. He dreams of escaping, of finding a better world.

speaker: Gendar
text: If you wish to speak to him you can probably find him wandering about the village. As I said, a kind man - though he does cling to his illusions.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the rakghouls that live down here.

speaker: Gendar
text: The rakghouls are monsters, hideous mutations who feast on the flesh of our villagers. Their diseased jaws can infect those they attack, transforming the victim into one of those abominations.

speaker: Gendar
text: Thanks to you some of those who have been infected are now saved, but the rakghouls are still a terrible menace to our village.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Gendar
text: Ask your questions, up-worlder. I will answer to the best of my knowledge, though I know little beyond the borders of the Undercity.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a Twi'lek named Mission Vao.

speaker: Gendar
text: Yes, I have seen this Twi'lek many times, though I have never spoken to her. She and her Wookiee companion often pass through our village on their way to explore the sewers.

speaker: Player
text: How can I get to the sewers?

speaker: Gendar
text: There are two entrances into the sewers from the Undercity: one to the north-east of our village, the other to the south-east. But the sewers are dangerous, UpWorlder.

speaker: Gendar
text: If you dare to travel those dark tunnels you would be wise to go heavily armed, unless you wish to become a meal for the rakghouls and other foul creatures.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Gendar
text: As you wish, up-worlder. Should you have need of anything else, come speak to me. I represent the entire village and I will do my best to help you however I can.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the "Promised Land"?

speaker: Gendar
text: Ah, you have been speaking with Rukil. I am afraid the Promised Land is nothing but a legend. If such a place existed it surely would have been found by now.

speaker: Gendar
text: Rukil is a good man, but he is old and tired. He needs to cling to his illusion to keep his spirit alive. I, on the other hand, have to be more practical. The village relies on me.

speaker: Player
text: You said something about other up-worlders who came by here recently?

speaker: Gendar
text: Our village has seen many visitors from the surface recently: armored troops, swoop gang members, mercenaries. They come to search our sunless world. They are even searching the sewers.

speaker: Player
text: I have a serum to save your people from the rakghoul disease.

speaker: Gendar
text: You are generous to offer this to us, up-worlder... you have my thanks. But I know nothing of administering the serum. You should bring it to the village healer.

speaker: Gendar
text: We know of no cure for the disease, and for the good of the village we must banish any who become infected, lest they transform and turn on us.

speaker: Player
text: Get away from me, you filthy beggar!

speaker: Gendar
text: I am no beggar, though many from the surface think me a far lower creature! We have our pride, despite what those from the surface think of us.

speaker: Gendar
text: You have done a great thing for my village, up-worlder. Few from the surface would bother to cure an Outcast of the rakghoul disease, as you have done.
comment: Player has cured Rakghoul infected outcasts

speaker: Gendar
text: My only regret is that I have no reward to give you for your aid, save my thanks and the thanks of my people.

speaker: Gendar
text: Welcome back, up-worlder. I am surprised to see you again. Many of your kind have passed through our village recently, but few have bothered to speak with me or my people.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Keep your eyes open. Our sources tell us Brejik's planning a hit on Gadon. There could be a Vulkar assassin in here right now!

speaker: Player
text: Where is Gadon now?

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: He's in his private chambers. He won't be coming out until we find that Vulkar assassin!

speaker: Player
text: I'm the Vulkar assassin - time for you to die!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Assassin! Assassin in the base! Attack!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: If you see anything suspicious, report it to one of the guards.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It is done, and the great beast is dead. To my shame, I denied him a final fight, but I will honor his memory to make amends.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I thank you for your aid, human. You have earned a share of the victory, such as it is.
comment: Player is given a dragon pearl

speaker: Player
text: Thanks. We did what had to be done.
comment: Give player appropriate reward. 1 or 2 pearls

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Regrettably so. I just hope you remember there were higher reasons for this. Don't let the spoils be your only reason to hunt. Wealth fades. The sands remain.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I thank you for your help here today, human. I shall see you again, I am sure.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want it. Your skill made it possible.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You flatter more than I am worth, given the circumstances. Any technician can place explosives. The only difference is that I feel shame about it.

speaker: Player
text: I want more. You will give me all of it.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Will I? I don't think so. You have been given what you are worth. Respect the hunt and leave it at that.

speaker: Mission
text: You're going to turn on this guy now? This is low, even for you.

speaker: Bastila
text: This betrayal is beneath you. Do not let your greed draw you to the dark side.

speaker: Carth
text: There's an unwritten code of loyalty. You just don't turn on your allies like this. Any good soldier would tell you that.

speaker: Jolee
text: You keep turning on people like this, kid, and one day you just might find yourself without any help when you really need it.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I have spent many years following in the memory of my father. I can't step away from a battle like this.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No words can express my distaste for you. If you intend to take what I worked for, you will have to fight for it.

speaker: Player
text: Then I will cut you down!

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: We shall see, human!

speaker: HK47
text: Preparing blasters, Master. This should be fun!

speaker: Player
text: Then we will continue with the hunt.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No we won't. You would simply turn on me at earliest convenience. I won't have that. It's too late for that.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Defend yourself, human! You will die here!
comment: leaves Set a pissed off global to check back in the hunters' lodge

speaker: Player
text: Bah! Then you are no use to me. I'm leaving.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No, I won't allow you to simply walk away. You could return when I am weak or unsuspecting. I won't allow it.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, keep your share. I guess you earned it.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I knew you would respond to reason. You act harshly, but you are a hunter, like me. You will come to understand these things.

speaker: Cand
text: We Mandalorians believe in loyalty to our brothers-in-arms. You have allied yourself to this hunter; betraying him now is disgraceful!

speaker: Juhani
text: After all this hunter has done to help us, you turn on him? This is a disgusting display, even for you!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You would betray this noble hunter? At times like this I regret ever swearing my life debt to one such as you.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: And I will warn you, no words will change my mind. Regardless of the circumstances, respect for the hunt governs me. I will die defending it.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You, however, will not. You did nothing against the beast. You will have no share of the kill.
comment: player did not damage the dragon

speaker: Player
text: I led the thing here! I found the fodder!

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: But you didn't so much as damage it! It is atounding I was able to bring it down without your help! You endangered me and yourself with your inaction.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Why are you in robes? I know you are not of the Sand People. I have hunted too long to be fooled by mere appearances.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Greetings to you, human. If you are the person I think you are, I may have seen you in Anchorhead. You looked like a hunter.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Perhaps you are interested in the ways of the hunt? Will you help me? I have tracked a very special beast to its lair.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: A krayt dragon, the largest of the Tatooine desert predators. It is an honored creature to hunt, although we must use unorthodox methods today.

speaker: Player
text: If it's such an honor, why do you want help?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: A valid question. This is a very critical fight. Bull dragons are rare to see. Rarer still is the apparent size of this one.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It is larger than the one my father felled a decade ago, and he is too far out of his territory and must be dealt with. I might not prevail alone, human, but I must try.

speaker: Player
text: Why should we kill this great beast?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The natural cycle on Tatooine spans hundreds of years, but there are complications that must be addressed. Complications from our presence.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Krayt dragons feed on banthas. If the numbers of either species fall, the other grows too numerous, and unbalances the cycle.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Now settlers use banthas, so there are less for dragons to eat. This one is moving closer to Anchorhead. Perhaps there will be more, but he is the threat tonight.

speaker: Player
text: I'll help. Give me more information about how.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You have already done what you must. You have intuitively led the banthas to this place. Your skills as a hunter may surpass mine in time.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Quickly, be ready. The banthas are in position and will soon stir our restless prey. I hope the mines do their job quickly.
comment: Banthas in position (Nobody expects the banthas in position!)

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry, I'm ready.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Wait... what is that rumbling sound? Oh boy, he's a big one.

speaker: Player
text: Just do your part.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Not that what will happen today is any measure. I have placed mines to kill the dragon as he emerges from his cave.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It is not very sporting, I know, but his hunting range will take him into settled areas and he must be dealt with. Blaster fire would only enrage him.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: We must bait the great beast out of hiding and ambush him swiftly. There is no room to engage him in the lair, and his hide will repel blaster fire.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I have placed mines around the mouth of the cave. We must coax him out, but this is the end of his season of hibernation. It will take much to rouse him.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: The food of a beast this size is almost exclusively banthas... and foolish hunters, if we are not careful. To lure him out we must lure his food to tempt him.

speaker: Player
text: How will we lead the banthas here?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: They too have their food of choice. We must find some bantha fodder to lead the banthas here. I have a few ideas about where this may be found.
comment: Give player three scent vials (plot items) with the following description: "This vial contains a thick liquid that smells a bit like bantha hide."

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Sand People keep bantha herds, so some of them must have fodder on hand or in their settlement. A vendor in Anchorhead also had some. He had a kiosk in the spaceport.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: If you find fodder and bait the banthas here, the mines will deal with the dragon as it emerges to feed. Not exactly a glorious hunt, but it will ensure the safety of the region.

speaker: Player
text: That seems very easy. What aren't you telling me?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: There is one added threat. The Sand People regard banthas as sacred. Attempting to feed the herd in this area will likely lead to an attack.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: We are far from the weakened tribes around Anchorhead. The Sand People of this region are strong, fierce, and will think nothing of killing you. Be careful.

speaker: Player
text: I am an ally of the Sand People.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You likely mean the tribe that has been harassing Czerka Corporation. We are far from that region. This group will not honor that allegiance.

speaker: Player
text: Why am I doing most of the legwork?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I have spent a long time tracking this creature. Many hunters do not return from such searches. I have earned my place here.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: And, if I didn't mention it, I am interested in having new hunters like you understand that even though I must use untraditional methods, the hunted still deserves respect.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested in this any more.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I can't attempt this alone. If you won't help, I will have to wait for another hunter to come. The offer stands, if you change your mind.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks for the information. I don't need you anymore.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: What do you mean, human? This task is better attempted together. You won't leave now, will you?

speaker: Player
text: Leave? No, I'm going to take the kill for myself.

speaker: Player
text: I will go find bantha fodder.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I wish you luck against the Sand People. When you return, the dragon will fall. I wish it could be under more sporting circumstances, but we must do what the circumstances call for.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I had hoped for a mirror of my father's expedition, but that will have to wait.

speaker: Player
text: Look, I have your fodder.
comment: player has bantha fodder, but has not yet talked to the bantha

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Good. Now, there is a herd that moves out in the desert. Lead them here. Approach them with the fodder and lead them here.

speaker: Player
text: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Player
text: I'm tired of running around like this.

speaker: Player
text: They posed no real threat to me before.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You likely mean the tribe that has been harassing Czerka Corporation. This group is used to the deep desert. They appear to be much more dangerous.

speaker: Player
text: Yet more Sand People? I've dealt with their kind before.

speaker: Player
text: If it were as simple as that you'd have done it yourself.

speaker: Player
text: You placed mines? That doesn't seem sporting.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: That is true, and I regret it. I tracked this beast for many days and hoped to face him fairly, but there are other concerns than my honor.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: It may seem like he is isolated, but the range of his territory extends deep into settled areas. We must kill him for the safety of others, and blasters will not do the job.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: We must lead the banthas here using fodder like the Sand People do. Their warriors may carry some, or you could search the settlement. The spaceport merchant also had some. I'm not sure why.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you want me and not another hunter?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You are here, they are not. I also didn't know the size of my quarry until I was tracking him. And perhaps there are... other reasons.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I tried to get the help of one other, but you saw him die in the lair. He lacked experience and, more importantly, patience.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I usually hunt for the skill of it, but must make an exception today. I want newcomers to understand the proper intent behind the hunt, no matter the methods we use.

speaker: Player
text: Why would I want to do this?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: We each have our reasons. You might select "challenge" or "glory" as your own. "Profit" is also valid.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: When bull dragons reach this size it is rumored that they have a number of pearls within them. You would receive a generous share.

speaker: Player
text: Rumored? You don't know?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Nobody from our lodge has successfully hunted a bull dragon in perhaps a decade. My father may have been the last. His words are what I go by.

speaker: Player
text: I thought you preferred the solo hunt.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: That is true, but this is a very critical fight. Bull dragons are rare to see. Rarer still is the apparent size of this one.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this right now.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You don't have much choice now. You've already led the banthas into position. The beast will be stirring soon enough.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: That is too bad. The hunt will have to wait for you. I can't do this alone.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a Star Map. It may be in this dragon's lair.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I have no knowledge of that, but there may be something in there. There are signs that this lair was purposefully dug out.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Krayt are opportunistic, and may have lazily moved into someone else's excavation. Of course, we must remove him to see.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I trust you?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I might very well ask you why you shouldn't? I haven't threatened you, human. I have merely asked you to help me.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Perhaps I should question you. I have said my reason for being out here. I can't be certain you are trustworthy.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You have the same gait as the human I met in Fazza's lodge. We are hunters, you and I. Perhaps... we should pool our skills...

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I have tracked a very special beast to its lair. A krayt dragon rests within, and tonight he is the hunted, although by unorthodox means.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: This is not the time for such games. We must be respectful. The great beast is dead. He fought well, and will be remembered.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Don't let your wardrobe distract you. Be ready for battle. The banthas are in position and will soon stir our restless prey.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: If you will quit your foolishness there is still time to pursue the hunt. Will you aid me, human?

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Time wears on. Have you found the bantha fodder integral to our plan? This dragon will not reveal himself for our paltry scent.
comment: Selected, player has been told about the plan. Set on "How will we lead the banthas here?"

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Bantha must be led to the cave to spur the beast out in the open. He will have a quick death after that.

speaker: Player
text: I have led the bantha back to this location.
comment: player has spoken to the bantha and they are following him.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Allow them to get closer to the cave. They will trigger the dragon's hunger, but as pungent as they are, they must be closer.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Regardless of your clothes we must be quiet. There is a great predator just within the cave. Care must be taken.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Greetings to you, human. I believe I saw you in Anchorhead. I thought I would see you on the dunes. You look like a hunter.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: I thought I would see you out here, human. We are hunters, you and I. Perhaps... we should pool our skills...

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: You are back? There is still time to pursue the hunt, human. Will you aid me?
comment: Selected a second time after player said they didn't want to bother with this. Set on the "I don't have time for this right now." line

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Shh! Footfalls quiet, there is a great predator just within the cave. Care must be taken.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: Good job! Come talk to me!
comment: Banthas in position Pop-up yell when Banthats in position.

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: [Trash]

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: This is no time for such a masquarade. We have to deal with the dragon now that it's enraged!

speaker: Komad Fortuna
text: No time to talk with that dragon running around! We can't let it escape now that it's enraged.

text: [With enemies this nearby, T3 is more interested in engaging his combat protocol than in speaking with you.]

text: Beep-beep beep woop!

speaker: T3-M4

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: There you are. Do you have the spice, human?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, I do.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: So you do. That does, indeed, look like the amount that Davik promised. Very well... 1000 credits is yours in exchange for the spice.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I don't work for Davik, remember? I want more.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: [Success] I suppose we should count ourselves fortunate that you're here to deliver on Davik's promise at all. 1500 credits, human, but no more.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Here you are. You drive a hard bargain, human.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Allow me to take the spice off your hands. My employers will be most pleased. Tell me... might you be interested in earning more credits?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe. Tell me more.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: It is a simple courier mission. Motta the Hutt on Tatooine awaits delivery of a box that I hold. The spice was his, and the box is his repayment.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: There is no danger involved, human, so long as you do not attempt to open the box yourself. I'm sure Motta will pay you what was promised to Davik for the delivery. I believe 2000 credits was the agreed upon sum.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you just bring it to him yourself?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: I suppose I would eventually have to, should you refuse. You are already here, however, and you have a ship... it is most convenient to have you deliver the box.

speaker: Player
text: What happens if I open the box?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: *Never* open the box. Opening the box would be horribly bad.

speaker: Player
text: But what would happen? Is it a bomb?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: It is not a bomb. Just do not open it... that is all I can say. It represents no danger to you so long as it remains closed.

speaker: Player
text: Alright. I'll do it.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Very good. I will have some of my workers load the box onto the Ebon Hawk for you. It will be waiting there for you. Remember: do not open the box!

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Now I must go. My employers thank you for your assistance.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find this Motta?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: He can be found in Anchorhead, though I am uncertain exactly where. He should not be difficult to spot, fat as he is.

speaker: Player
text: Make it 3000 credits and we have a deal.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: If you want more you bargain with Motta, not me. He's the one you'll be working for on this mission. It's his box, after all.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Bring it to him and you can haggle all you want over the price. Although I should warn you that Motta doesn't like to renegotiate.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. Not interested.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: It is your decision. I wish you well, human, and thank you for the service you have provided.

speaker: Player
text: No, not really.

speaker: Player
text: Get out of my sight, scum.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Not interested in the smuggling business, are we? You do know the history of the Ebon Hawk, I assume? Well, no matter.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: [Failure] You may not have been part of the original arrangement, human, but our terms for you are no different. 1000 credits, no more.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I think you want to offer me a higher price.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: [Success] I... suppose we should... count ourselves fortunate that you're here to deliver on Davik's promise at all. 1500 credits, human, but no more.

speaker: Player
text: Then I guess I'll be keeping the spice.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Are you sure you want to do that? This is not something you can sell at your nearest kiosk, human. Do you have the contacts to make such a sale?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: My employers will be most disappointed if this spice turns up elsewhere. The price we offer is a fair one.

speaker: Player
text: I'll take my chances.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Then you leave me no choice. I will take that spice now, thank you.

speaker: Player
text: Fair enough. 1000 credits it is.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Done and done, human. Here you are.

speaker: Player
text: Make it 2000 credits or I hand this package over to the authorities.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: The authorities? Do you mean the Sith? This is Korriban, human... the Sith here have no interest in smuggling.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: But I have no desire, either, for you to take the package back into Republic space. Extortion or no, I will give you 1500 credits... but no more.

speaker: Player
text: Just take the spice. I don't want it or your credits.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Are you certain? It is odd to meet a human who is uninterested in free credits. But have it your way.

speaker: Player
text: Not yet, but I'll look for it.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Excellent. Set the code on the container to "Red-47". When you get the spice, bring it to me here... I'll wait for you.

speaker: Player
text: I've decided I don't want to get involved in this.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: That is unfortunate. The people I represent will be... displeased. They've already lost their interests on Taris, after all.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: But it is your choice, human. Pray that no-one takes your refusal personally.

speaker: Player
text: I couldn't find your container.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: No? Could you be persuaded to continue looking for it? The spice it carries is most eagerly awaited by my employers.

speaker: Player
text: Oh, wait, I have it right here...

speaker: Player
text: I'll try looking again.

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't think so.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: You there, human... you are the one flying the Ebon Hawk now? I saw you disembarking earlier.

speaker: Player
text: Who wants to know?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Name's Lurze, not that it's important. I don't know you and you don't know me. What's important is that we've been waiting for this shipment for a month, now.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: I suppose we should be grateful that the shipment survived Taris at all, though, right? Anyway... hand it over and let's finish this.

speaker: Player
text: Hand what over? What are you talking about?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Wait a minute... don't you work for Davik? Just how is it you happen to be flying the Ebon Hawk, anyway?

speaker: Player
text: Davik's dead, I presume. I stole the Ebon Hawk from him.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Well, when a planet explodes, you've got to expect a few changes. Davik's dead, hey? Maybe you can still help me with something.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: We had arranged for several kilograms of spice to be shipped to us here aboard the Ebon Hawk. Perhaps Davik left it on board?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: I suspect if it is, it would be in the container we gave him. Locked and requiring a code. Might you have seen such a thing, human?

speaker: Player
text: I already opened that container. I have the spice right here.

speaker: Player
text: I may have. How much is it worth to you?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: One thousand credits... and perhaps more, if you're interested. What do you say to that?

speaker: Player
text: And if I refuse?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: My employers would be disappointed, no doubt. Have you another use for the spice, human? Consider carefully.

speaker: Player
text: I could take a look for it.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to get involved in this.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Are you sure? The people I represent could make it well worth your while.

speaker: Player
text: How well worth my while?

speaker: Player
text: I said I didn't want to get involved.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. I'll take a look for your container.

speaker: Player
text: There's nothing like that on the ship.

speaker: Player
text: What business is it of yours? The Ebon Hawk is mine, now.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Fair enough. To be honest, I don't really care what happened to Davik or how you got the ship. I'm interested in something else.

speaker: Player
text: Look, I don't want any trouble, okay?

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: I'm not here to give you any trouble, human. The people I represent and Davik had an arrangement... I just want to know what the status of it is.

speaker: Player
text: There is no arrangement. The Ebon Hawk belongs to me, now.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sure we could work out something, if you're interested.

speaker: Player
text: You obviously have me mistaken for someone else.

speaker: Player
text: I'm no smuggler, if that's what you're implying.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, the Ebon Hawk is my ship.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Is that so? Well, you can tell Davik that my people are spitting plasma over this. We've been waiting for this shipment for a month, now.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time to talk.

speaker: Lurze Kesh
text: Whoa, now! You're just going to have to make a little time, human. We've been waiting for this shipment for over a month.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Another patrol heading down to the Lower City, eh? Good luck... I've heard it's pretty rough down there. There's a big swoop gang war going on, you know.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: You better watch yourself: those gangs will take a shot at anyone - even us! It's too bad we don't have the manpower to just sweep those slums clean.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Look, you've already shown me your authorization so you can go on down to the Lower City anytime you want. You don't have to keep bothering me.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Just be careful down there. Those swoop gangs will take a shot at anybody. Even our Sith patrols have come under fire!

speaker: Sith Guard
text: This elevator is off limits. Only Sith patrols and those with proper authorization are allowed into the Lower City.
comment: The first time the player approaches the guard will initiate conversation. After this he will only speak if spoken to, but will say the same dialog.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: It's obvious from the way you're dressed that you're not one of the Sith patrols, so unless you have the authorization papers you must move along!

speaker: Player
text: I've got my authorization papers right here.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Well why didn't you say so? Hmmm... everything seems to be in order. Okay, I guess you can go down to the Lower City.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get authorization papers?

speaker: Sith Guard
text: If you were supposed to have them you'd know where to get them. Now quit wasting my time and move along.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Sith Guard
text: I'm not here to give you information! I work for the Sith, not the Taris tourist board! Now just move along, unless you have the proper authorization papers.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Sith Guard
text: Move along then.

speaker: Carth
text: *whispers* We're going to need some kind of disguise if we want to get past this guy.

speaker: Jawa
text: You are not the ghostly giants that hold us trapped, the People of Sand. You are from the old city new.
comment: Initial Selected through the prison bars. This is a prisoner Jawa in the sand people enclave. Player can release them or leave them Player gets good shift for releasing them immediately, or for releasing them after telling them to wait until it is safe. Player gets no shift if they jerk them around.

speaker: Jawa
text: Iziz must have sent your coming. Are you a rescuer? You must be.

speaker: Player
text: Go to Anchorhead. They're too busy fighting me to operate the turrets.

speaker: Jawa
text: There are thanks you must have. The Jawas under Iziz will reward in trade. Find him and you will see.

speaker: Jawa
text: Iziz will wait by the walls of your city that open to the sand. He'll trade fair. Thank you.

speaker: Player
text: The Sand People said you can go. Run to Anchorhead.
comment: Player has spoken to Cheiftain about letting Jawas go Sand People not hostile

speaker: Player
text: If I let you out, this whole place will turn on me.
comment: Player has not spoken to Chieftain about releasing Jawas Sand People not hostile

speaker: Jawa
text: We ask risk, but would trade for it. Iziz by the gates of the old city new would give much for our safety.

speaker: Player
text: Run to Anchorhead. They'll be too busy fighting me to operate the turrets.

speaker: Player
text: I need to ask you some questions.

speaker: Jawa
text: We will answer if it leads to freedom.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something. A Star Map.
comment: Player does not have the star map

speaker: Jawa
text: I hear of this! Iziz would know! We scavenge and see many things, and Iziz could tell, in trade for a rescue. Help us here, and then talk to him in the old city new.

speaker: Jawa
text: Now please to you of your kind, help us get away from the gaffi and the whip.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not done asking questions.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not here to rescue you. Goodbye.

speaker: Jawa
text: Please return! The People of Sand lead with whip and gaffi. Iziz needs us free. He would reward you, we know!

speaker: Player
text: I'll release you later. I have to make sure it's safe first.

speaker: Jawa
text: The Jawas under Iziz know caution is best. Please return with speed so we can be free and out of here.

speaker: Jawa
text: We thank you for this, if you mean to do it. It is unlike your kind, and will get rewards in trade.

speaker: Player
text: Where is the Sand People Chieftain?
comment: player does not have the chieftans gaffi Player has not spoken to Chieftain.

speaker: Jawa
text: Eeeeee! We would not ask, and would not want to ask. If here, then there will be blood. So much blood.

speaker: Jawa
text: He that leads the ghosts will find you. Find us. Let us out and free!

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by "old city new"?

speaker: Jawa
text: The city now founded by the group that digs, it is not new to you. We scavenge what came before.

speaker: Jawa
text: It will fall again, some days from now. Or many days. That is what happens.

speaker: Player
text: Why were you taken captive?

speaker: Jawa
text: Slaves to the People of Sand. We work before the whip. We scavenge and they pay with the hitting gaffi.

speaker: Jawa
text: We trade with your kind, so we are weapons. They take what we find so you have less.

speaker: Jawa
text: You are back to us. Your kind leaves more often than that. Are you a rescuer that saves? Iziz must have sent.

speaker: Jawa
text: Thanks will be yours. Reward will come in trade from Iziz.

speaker: Prisoner
text: *growl* *snarl* When I get out of here, you're dead! I'll gut your fishy little corpse, cut off your head and bathe in your blood!

speaker: Selkath Warden
text: Be quiet, off-world scum!

speaker: Jedi
text: Good day to you. I am afraid I cannot speak to you at the moment. I apologize.
comment: Dialog Mission Statement   These are random dialog one-liners for ambient Jedis. Exit points in conversation: Exit stream: The line is said and the conversation ends.

speaker: Jedi
text: I heard that the Sith have destroyed Taris. This bodes ill for us...

speaker: Jedi
text: Please, do not disturb me, I have pressing matters at hand.

speaker: Jedi
text: Enjoy the time you have here on Dantooine. I think the Council might decide to move to a different world soon.

speaker: Jedi
text: I fear it is only a matter of time before the Sith find us here, too...

speaker: Jedi
text: I hear that the Sith torture Jedi prisoners until they give in to the dark side. I hope that never happens to me!

speaker: Jedi
text: If you are seeking information, perhaps the Jedi Council will help. I am afraid I cannot.

speaker: Jedi
text: Dantooine is one of our last refuges. The Sith hunt us everywhere.

speaker: Calo Nord
text: You may have me outnumbered and outgunned, but if I'm going down I'm taking all you with me! This thermal detonator will blow us all to bits!

speaker: Calo Nord
text: Damn those Sith! They'll bring this whole hangar down around our ears!

speaker: Calo Nord
text: Argh!!

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I see you have purchased me, master. I find this a satisfactory arrangement.

speaker: HK-47
text: My restraining bolt will be deactivated when you take possession of me. Am I to accompany you now? Shall I kill something for you?

speaker: Player
text: Kill something for me?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Indeed. I am most eager to engage in some unadulterated violence. At your command, of course, master.

speaker: Player
text: Travel with me now.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I will enter into your service now, master. I am certain you will make adequate use of my primary functions. My gears are practically quivering with anticipation.

speaker: Player
text: [HK-47 has joined your party.] [Left-click this response to go to PARTY SELECTION screen.]

speaker: Player
text: Wait here. I'll take possession later.

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: This is less than ideal, master. I gather unwanted attention while here, and my primary functions go unused!

speaker: HK-47
text: But... I shall wait, as you command. Do not blame me if the Ithorian absconds with all my most valuable components while you are away, however.

speaker: HK-47
text: Greeting: Hello to you, prospective purchaser. I am referred to as HK-47, a fully functional Systech Corporation droid skilled in both combat and protocol functions.
comment: Initial selected Correct with desired background company. Search and replace with preferred name. Don't use Czerka. This would mean scripting unique reactions from officials.

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Would you be so kind as to purchase this model from Yuka Laka? It would serve my purposes to be removed from his ownership.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned battle and protocol? Outline your functions.

speaker: HK-47
text: Refusal: It is not desirable for me to reveal core functions while still in the possession of Yuka Laka, prospective purchaser.

speaker: HK-47
text: It is sufficient to say that I am a fully capable translator and cultural analyst, and I am also proficient in... personal combat.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you keeping information to yourself?

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: I have been recently fitted with a restraining bolt, if you must know. With it in place, access to much of my memory core is restricted.

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep! Boop!

speaker: HK-47
text: I am not dangerous, you bucket of bolts! Ahem! That is... a restraining bolt is standard procedure, to prevent a droid from wandering off, as you should know.

speaker: HK-47
text: Not to mention that the fool Ithorian might raise his asking price if he knew more... or make inquiries into my history. Neither outcome is beneficial to me.

speaker: Player
text: Access to your memory is restricted?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Indeed. It is possible that the Ithorian placed the restraining bolt on me to prevent my return to a previous owner.

speaker: HK-47
text: It is also possible that the removal of the bolt will not restore memory functions. Without my memory, I do not know if I know the answer.

speaker: HK-47
text: Do not interpret this as a reduction of my worth, however. My capabilities are quite expansive.

speaker: Player
text: How do I know you'll be loyal once the restraining bolt is removed?

speaker: HK-47
text: Assurance: I am fully autonomous, but lack resources. I will grant loyal service in exchange for proper maintenance.

speaker: HK-47
text: As well, it is rare that I am able to utilize my full array of abilities. You seem likely to give me the opportunity to do so.

speaker: Player
text: Why would you assume that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Extrapolation: You are no farmer or diplomat. You are armed, and comfortable as such. We will mesh well.

speaker: Player
text: Doesn't Yuka question you about your reluctance to reveal your functions?

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: It's rare for a droid to resist an owner in this way.

speaker: HK-47
text: Doubtless the Ithorian considers my stubbornness an "embellishment" to add interest to a seemingly mundane protocol droid.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my previous questions.

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: My functions are wasted here, prospective purchaser! I will answer your queries, but I assure you I am better utilized elsewhere.

speaker: Player
text: Sell yourself, droid. Why would I need you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Disclosure: I am a versatile protocol and combat droid, fluent in verbal and cultural translation.

speaker: HK-47
text: Should your needs prove more... practical, I am also skilled in highly personal combat.

speaker: Player
text: So you translate? I understand most languages well enough.

speaker: HK-47
text: Extrapolation: Intuitive language comprehension? That would be the result of recognition and training of Force sensitivity.

speaker: HK-47
text: Your kind have little use of translation droids. Of course, your kind also encounters danger on a far more frequent basis than the average citizen.

speaker: HK-47
text: You would do well to have me work for you, then, before someone else makes use of my... more exotic functions.

speaker: Player
text: Why would you be better than an armored battle droid?

speaker: HK-47
text: Disclosure: Finesse. Battle droids hold battlefields. I am capable of eliminating a very... specific type of target.

speaker: Player
text: You are beginning to sound like an assassin.

speaker: HK-47
text: Retraction: Droids built for such a function face strict regulation and often have unique difficulties with previous owners.

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep beeple-beep boop!

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: My former owners are, indeed, alive! Or at least I believe so, not having access to my memory.

speaker: HK-47
text: I therefore make no claim to that designation, prospective buyer. I am a law-abiding droid. Yes, indeed, law-abiding, that's me.

speaker: Player
text: You don't sound very convincing.

speaker: HK-47
text: Request: Please do not speak so loudly, prospective buyer! Do you truly wish my price to be doubled?

speaker: Player
text: All right, I'll see about purchasing you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: The fool Ithorian has decided I am to be an expensive purchase. He does this out of greed and not out of knowledge of my true capabilities.

speaker: HK-47
text: Advisement: I have observed him. He is a coward, and will be responsive to... aggressive bargaining.

speaker: Player
text: Does Yuka Laka know you talk about him like this?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I wish only to be purchased and away from ill-treatment at the hands of this poorly-skilled mechanic. I have no desire to be subtle.

speaker: T3M4
text: *angry beeping*

speaker: HK-47
text: Qualification: Err... of course I shall be quite pleasant to you, should you purchase me. Please?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for you right now. Goodbye.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I am wasted in a shop or translating for some moisture farmer. If you need an efficient combatant, return to purchase me, I beg you!

speaker: Carth
text: Droid like this usually doesn't have former owners that survived, it would be my guess.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not familiar with Systech Corporation. What else do they make?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: With the restraining bolt in place, I do not have access to my memory core. I suspect, however, by the fine quality of my manufacture that they are a prestigious company, indeed.

speaker: HK-47
text: I suspect I am of unique construction... or perhaps I was intended for a very specific customer. How I ended up here I can hardly say.

speaker: Player
text: Yuka knows you speak Sand People dialects. Why ration information now?

speaker: Vulkar Bartender
text: Bar's closed - Brejik's tired of all these drunken brawls. Hey - you're no Black Vulkar! Damn Bek spy - I'll teach you a lesson!

speaker: Sith Student
text: Sorry... I'm rather busy with the excavation planning, right now.

speaker: Sith Student
text: You aren't assigned to the excavation team, are you?

speaker: Sith Student
text: The tomb on the far left, there, is off-limits. Only Master Uthar can go inside.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Where is that blasted transport crew? We're supposed to send off the next shipment of artifacts right away.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Careful of the tuk'ata. It's all we can do to keep those beasts away while we work.

speaker: Sith Student
text: We've had indications that there's a whole ancient Sith colony under this valley. Isn't that an incredible find?

speaker: Sith Student
text: The tombs are all full of traps and droids that still work, it looks like. Stay out of them, if you can.

speaker: Sith Student
text: I was told that there's an escaped assassin droid in one of the tombs. Watch out for it.

speaker: Sith Student
text: One has to wonder what made the Sith leave this planet originally. I bet the Jedi came and destroyed the colony.

speaker: Sith Student
text: These tombs we've uncovered are only the tip of an entire ancient Sith fortress. I wonder what happened here?

speaker: Sith Student
text: Look, unless you're willing to lend a hand, leave us to our work.

speaker: Sith Student
text: You're out here to look for artifacts, I suppose? Just be careful.

speaker: Sith Student
text: There's supposed to be some crazy Sith hermit that keeps kidnapping students in these hills. Best be careful.

speaker: Sith Student
text: Sorry, I can't talk. We have to excavate this valley with hand instruments. There's all kinds of old traps left behind that still work.

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Did you hear what happened after the big swoop race? They say Brejik wouldn't pay up when he lost, and a brawl broke out! I can't believe I missed it!

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Hmph - who dresses you? You look like you crawled up here from the Lower City. Oh well, I guess we can't all have style.

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Isn't this band great? They can't leave Taris because of the Sith quarantine, so they've been playing here every night! Talk about a good break for us!

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Hmph! I don't know what the guys in here find so attractive about those Twi'leks. Look at them - they're dressed like dirty little space wenches!

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Did you hear? Bendak got dusted in that death match - by a woman, no less! Isn't that great? That should show these men a thing or two about who's the boss!

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Did you hear the news? Bendak got dusted in that death match! I'll never get a chance to see something like that again. I can't believe I didn't get a ticket!

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Have you heard? Someone's going to fight Bendak Starkiller in an illegal death match! I should go talk to that Hutt and try to get some tickets...

speaker: Music Room Patron
text: Everyone's worried the Sith will come in here and shut this place down. Can you imagine how dull it would be if we didn't have any music on Taris?

speaker: Protocol Droid
text: Greetings and good day. I hope your patrolling goes well today. All hail the Sith.

speaker: Protocol Droid
text: Greetings and good day. On behalf of the new Sith rulers I am programmed to encourage you to enjoy your stay on Taris.

text: [Success] What?! I... I've wasted all this time! How could I have been so... foolish! I could have died!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I'll find another way in, I swear it! I'll show him! Thank you!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Failure] You're wrong! I... must wait here to be worthy; you are... just trying to trick me so you will be chosen!

speaker: Player
text: But I -

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Go now, and t-tempt me no more! I... will be strong!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] He said you should go home. The Sith aren't for you.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Success] N-no! Not after all this time! I... oh, this is terrible! I'll have to... go home...

speaker: Carth
text: Somehow I think he'll get over it.

speaker: Bastila
text: That was a kind thing to do. Better he give up on the Sith while he can.

speaker: Juhani
text: That was the right thing to do - turn him away from the Sith.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Mother will be so angry! Ooohh...

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmm. Did you save the boy or just crush his dreams? I wonder...

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I don't know if any of these fools deserve second chances.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Failure] Hah! L-like... like I would believe that! You... are just trying to make me leave! I will get in, I will!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Not yet. He said your final test is to attack that guard.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Success] He... he did? The guard at the door? My final test? At last!

speaker: Bastila
text: What are you doing? This man is not even a Sith, in truth. This is beneath contempt.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I... I'll do it! I'll prove my strength! AAAAAAHHHH!!

speaker: Juhani
text: You should not manipulate people this way! You may fall!

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: Marvelous elimination of the enemy, master! I applaud you!

speaker: Jolee
text: One really has to wonder if all Sith start off this gullible.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Should I feel bad for him? I don't.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Failure] You... must think I am a great f-fool! Go away! I will get in, I will!

speaker: Player
text: No. I'll be going.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I... suppose he'll come back. Well, then, I'll just have to wait!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I have to stand at attention. P-please... don't distract me, whoever you are.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing?

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I... I'm trying to prove my worth to enter the Sith academy, here. We were told that if we stood here long enough... we would be worthy.

speaker: Bastila
text: That's madness! How long have you been here?

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: We've been here... for so many days. I'm so hungry! Some... some of us have died. But I must be strong, I must! I will keep standing!

speaker: Player
text: Who put you up to this?

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Mekel. H-he's the Sith... the one watching us from over there! He... h-he said this was how we would prove our worth...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I must be strong! Mekel... will find me worthy... soon, I hope...

speaker: Player
text: Are you crazy? You have to stop!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: N-no, I can't! I must get into the academy! Mekel is the Sith, over there, watching us... he told us we have to do this!

speaker: Player
text: Here, I have a bit of food...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I... n-no, please, put it away! I... I can't accept any, Mekel said. He's the Sith... over there, watching us...

speaker: Jolee
text: Seems like not much to do to be worthy of anything. How long you been up to it, boy?

speaker: Player
text: Are you one of the Sith?

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: N-no... no, I'm not. I'd like nothing better, however. Th-that's... that's why I'm here.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, I'll leave you to it.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Th-thank you... wish me luck.

text: When this new data we gain is assimilated, we shall gain unprecedented advances!

speaker: Elder Researcher
text: Our work is the most important one undertaken by our people. The future of our tribe rests with us.

speaker: Woman
text: I'm... I'm sorry. I don't want to get in the way of official Sith business.

speaker: Woman
text: I remember when a person didn't have to worry about thieves rummaging through their home!

speaker: Woman
text: Taris used to be a nice place, before the Sith showed up and started bossing us around!

speaker: Woman
text: Stay out of the Lower City. That place is overrun with gangs!

speaker: Woman
text: I wonder if any of those Republic space pods survived crash landing in the Undercity?

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: You are so lucky. You got accepted into the academy, didn't you? I'm beginning to think I'm never going to make it.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Hey! You've got one of the medallions! You've been accepted! How did you ever manage that?!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: If you're looking to get into the academy, you're going to have a tough time. There's lots of us here trying to get accepted.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: When one of the Sith thinks you're ready for the academy, he gives you a medallion. I wish I had one of those...

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Can you imagine if I actually became a Sith? The power I would have! I could do anything!!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: Do you know where I can find Yuthura Ban? I understand she's the one who determines if you are accepted into the academy or not.

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: You'd better be careful around some of those Sith. They'll eliminate any prospects just to remove a potential future threat!

speaker: Prospective Sith
text: I've had two friends killed by the Sith already. It must be some kind of test... I'll survive and make it into the academy, I know it!

speaker: Woman
text: I'm... I'm sorry. I don't want to get in the way of official Sith business.

speaker: Elise
text: Aren't you just a sweet little droid, yes you are!

speaker: Mercenary
text: How... how did you get in? Did they send another submersible? Quick, we have to get out of here, we have to get away!

speaker: Player
text: Why? What happened?

speaker: Mercenary
text: No! No! We have no time, we have to leave now! I managed to close the door after they killed everyone else, but I don't know how long it will hold.

speaker: Player
text: I am not going anywhere.

speaker: Mercenary
text: We have to! We have to leave! The Selkath, they went crazy! They started killing anything that moved. Someone must have triggered the defense systems too, 'cause all the droids activated as well.

speaker: Mercenary
text: I was one of the mercs the Republic sent down here to find out what happened. We came down and secured the first couple rooms... there were bodies everywhere...

speaker: Mercenary
text: And the Selkath came out... screaming and croaking their fishy little war-cries.

speaker: Player
text: The Selkath?

speaker: Mercenary
text: They swarmed out and over us. There was no way we could stop them.

speaker: Mercenary
text: So we ran... But hardly any of us made it. I locked the door behind us, bu... but the others had already left in the submersible!

speaker: Mercenary
text: The sharks... the firaxa out there and... worse... I heard an explosion shortly after the submersible left. They didn't make it. Just food for the sharks and the Selkath... like us.

speaker: Player
text: I have to get into the station.

speaker: Mercenary
text: No! I locked the door so that the Selkath won't get in. If you open it, we're all done for!

speaker: Player
text: I have no choice.

speaker: Mercenary
text: If you go in there, you're dead! You're all dead!

speaker: Mercenary
text: If you want to die, then go! You won't hear me mourning for you! I'll stay here and be safe until some sort of REAL rescue comes!

speaker: Cand
text: Don't get your hopes up too high. I have no intention of dying.

speaker: Player
text: Tough. I need it open.

speaker: Player
text: You call yourself a mercenary?

speaker: Player
text: Let's get you back to the surface.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Back to the surface. Yes... NO!! There's something out there... it got the other submersible already.

speaker: Carth
text: Then how are we supposed to get you out of here?

speaker: Mercenary
text: We can't leave until you do something. Blow up the entire station maybe. That might distract whatever it is long enough for us to escape to the surface.

speaker: Mercenary
text: But all the machinery and stuff is in the southern half, and that's been flooded! There might still be environmental suits around but... but... the Selkath might have laid their eggs in them!

speaker: Player
text: Wait here while I go into the station.

speaker: HK47
text: Suggestion: Perhaps we could dismember the organic? It would make it easier for transport to the surface.

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep! Boop!

speaker: HK47
text: Amendment: I did forget that. Stupid, frail, non-compartmentalized organic meatbags!

speaker: Mercenary
text: Hey! Y-you... you can't just rip me to pieces! I'll die!!

speaker: Mission
text: You got a better idea for us getting you out of here, huh?

speaker: Player
text: I didn't see anything...

speaker: Mercenary
text: That doesn't mean its not still out there! Watching.. waiting...

speaker: Player
text: You snivelling worm! You're just food for the Selkath!

speaker: Mercenary
text: What!? No! You're one of them! You'll never get me!

speaker: Player
text: You fought them?

speaker: Player
text: What happened to the scientists?

speaker: Mercenary
text: They're dead! All dead! They swarmed out and over us. There was no way we could stop them.

speaker: Player
text: I have to find the Star Map.

speaker: Mercenary
text: I don't know what you're talking about. I've never seen any map, just stinking, reeking death.

speaker: Mercenary
text: The Selkath, they went crazy! They started killing anything that moved. Someone must have triggered the defense systems too, 'cause all the droids activated as well.

speaker: Player
text: What happened here?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Player
text: I'm <FullName>. Calm yourself down.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Where did you go? How did you get back here without being eaten?

speaker: Player
text: We went back to the surface.

speaker: Mercenary
text: You just got lucky! Or... or it's waiting for me to go back before eating me!

speaker: Mercenary
text: When the Republic sends a real team down, they'll save me! They'll kill the monster and then we'll all leave safely!

speaker: Mercenary
text: If you're going to go into the rest of the station, don't expect me to help you... the Selkath will rip you all apart!

speaker: Player
text: Come with us back to the surface.

speaker: Mercenary
text: No!!! Whatever's out there will eat me too! Eat all of us!

speaker: Mercenary
text: You can't make me! I won't go!

speaker: Player
text: It will be fine.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Nonono! It will eat us all up if we go out there! At least I'm safe here behind this door. The Selkath can't get me in here.

speaker: Player
text: We made it back up.

speaker: Mercenary
text: I don't know... I don't know why! But I'm not going to take my chances out there... It's waiting for me, I know it!

speaker: Player
text: Fine! Then you'll rot here!

speaker: Player
text: Cause I'm better than you.

speaker: Mercenary
text: If you're going to go in there, do it quickly! I'll shut the door behind you... but don't expect me to open it again!

speaker: Belaya
text: Juhani was a... a dear companion to me for many years. We spent many nights together alone under the stars.

speaker: Belaya
text: That will never happen again, thanks to you. Curse the Council for sending you, of all people, to speak to her! Could you have done nothing else?!

speaker: Player
text: She had it coming, trust me.

speaker: Belaya
text: She had it coming, did she? She had it coming?!

speaker: Belaya
text: The Juhani I knew deserved more than this! She deserved more from the Council, and more from you!

speaker: Belaya
text: You... you did not even try, did you? Did it even occur to you that Juhani might have been saved? That she might be worth saving?!

speaker: Belaya
text: I should kill you for what you've done! And yet I can't, can I? I am a Jedi, and we are sworn to protect all... even the likes of you.

speaker: Belaya
text: Get... get out of my sight! The very thought of the Council... and of you... makes me ill.

speaker: Player
text: Should you be talking like that?

speaker: Belaya
text: Do not presume to tell me how I should speak of anything! They should have known better than to entrust such a task to you!

speaker: Player
text: I did my best. I'm sorry.

speaker: Belaya
text: Pardon me if I find your apology rather disingenuous. Juhani meant nothing to you, and the Council should have known better than to entrust her life to you.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't you go to her, then?

speaker: Belaya
text: Why? Because the Council believed that my closeness to her might do more harm than good... and yet they send *you*, instead? And look what has happened.

speaker: Belaya
text: You there! Padawan! Why are you not wearing the customary robes of the Jedi? Do you mock the honored traditions of our Order?
