speaker: Player
text: Are you a Jedi?

speaker: Belaya
text: My name is Belaya. I have come here to further my learning in the ways of the Force. Many Jedi come here to train under Master Zhar.

speaker: Belaya
text: Any who belong to the Order should surely know this. You must be neglecting your studies, Padawan.

speaker: Player
text: I believe you are mistaken. I am not a Padawan. I am <FullName>. I came here with Bastila.

speaker: Belaya
text: Bastila? I have heard of her. They say she has already mastered the art of Battle Meditation, remarkable in one so young. Though I have heard she has a foolish pride in her own talents.

speaker: Belaya
text: But as for you... you claim you are not a Padawan? I find this hard to believe. The Force is strong within you. I can feel its presence.

speaker: Belaya
text: If this is some type of jest, it is in very poor taste. The Jedi Order is not a subject for jokes.

speaker: Player
text: I am telling you the truth.

speaker: Belaya
text: Please forgive the abruptness with which I first greeted you. It was harsh, and perhaps unfair. My Master often warns me I must learn to control my emotions. I see I have much left to learn.

speaker: Belaya
text: I wish you a pleasant stay here on Dantooine. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: I didn't come here to be scolded by you!

speaker: Belaya
text: No, I suppose you did not. I apologize.

speaker: Player
text: Back off! I'm no Padawan! I'm <FullName>. I just came here with Bastila.

speaker: Belaya
text: You have done a great thing. One of our own had strayed, but you have returned Juhani to the Order. For this you deserve the highest praise.
comment: DIALOGUE  the first time after saving juhani

speaker: Belaya
text: Greetings, apprentice... though I understand you shall not have that lowly title much longer. Master Zhar tells me your progress has been remarkable.
comment: DIALOGUE  after the character has become an apprentice but before becoming a jedi

speaker: Belaya
text: Soon, he feels, you will attain the rank of Padawan. Then you will truly be a full-fledged Jedi. How are you enjoying your training?

speaker: Player
text: It's difficult, but worthwhile.

speaker: Belaya
text: With power comes responsibility, and only by learning discipline and sacrifice can we truly learn to master our potential.

speaker: Belaya
text: I wish you luck in your training, apprentice. There is much you must yet learn. May the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: I want to learn to use the Force, not listen to your philosophical babbling!

speaker: Belaya
text: You speak as if this were some foolish game! Have you no idea what is at stake?

speaker: Player
text: I am still learning the Jedi Code.

speaker: Belaya
text: All Jedi must know the code. Its tenets are the fundamental teachings of our Order.

speaker: Belaya
text: There is no emotion; there is peace. There is no ignorance; there is knowledge. There is no passion; there is serenity. There is no chaos; there is harmony. There is no death; there is the Force.

speaker: Belaya
text: Think and meditate on these truths, apprentice, if you ever wish to become a Padawan.

speaker: Player
text: I am looking to alter my lightsaber, and I heard about some caves.

speaker: Belaya
text: There are caves on Dantooine that hold those rare crystals. But be warned, apprentice: They are dangerous. You should not meddle in things beyond you.

speaker: Belaya
text: A battle took place earlier to the south of the Enclave. A lot of people died and many droids were destroyed.

speaker: Belaya
text: I wonder what dark force could have caused this to happen...

speaker: Belaya
text: Shen and Rahasia have been welcomed here in the compound for as long as they wish to stay. I am glad that your help enabled them to remain together.

speaker: Belaya
text: Master Zhar tells me you have successfully completed the tests, and I even see you have constructed your own lightsaber.
comment: DIALOGUE  the first time after the jedi becomes a padawan

speaker: Belaya
text: You should be proud of your accomplishment... but never forget that you still have much to learn.

speaker: Belaya
text: As your power grows you will constantly face temptations to slip to the dark side. This is the eternal struggle of the Jedi.

speaker: Belaya
text: Greetings, young Padawan. I trust your training goes well.
comment: DIALOGUE  after the player becomes a padawan

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Greetings to you. Err... while I am pleased to welcome you to planet G5-623, I do not see your ship on my docking schedule.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: The Czerka Corporation will see to your needs, of course, but there will be a 100 credit docking fee. In advance, I fear.

speaker: Player
text: Docking fee? Why do I need to pay that?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: This outpost is remote and expensive to maintain. The 100 credits given will ensure that it remains here... for your use, of course.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Upon collection of the correct fees, I will extend what resources the Czerka Corporation can offer. I'm sure you understand.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I don't think I need to pay the docking fee.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Success] Perhaps you don't need to pay the docking fee. Any services you need will more than make up for it.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* The Force should not be used for profit and personal gain. As Jedi we should be above such things.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I see you have a Wookiee with you. Can I assume you understand their language? For a fee, Czerka Corporation can provide a translator for you during your visit.

speaker: Player
text: I'm trained in the Force. I'll have no trouble.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I don't have any experience with that. I just know that only the most adaptive people can understand the Wookiee language.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Now then, please follow me to our information center. I will answer any further questions there.
comment: Walks to his office. Has "Don't bother me yet" line for while he's walking. Has conditions for once he is safe in his office.

speaker: Player
text: That will not be necessary.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Very well, though only the most adaptive people seem to comprehend the Wookiee language, such as it is.

speaker: Player
text: I understand more than you can know.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Er... very well. It is no concern of mine. I will simply assume you are one of the rare sort that take to languages easily.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: We will also arrange for translation services, for a nominal fee, of course. You'll be encountering a number of Wookiees while here.

speaker: Cand
text: *whisper* I'm amazed at how many people that works on. The entire galaxy must be filled with weak-minded fools.

speaker: Juhani
text: *whisper* You should treat your power with respect, not use the Force on a whim like it is some toy!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Failure] No... no I'm... quite certain that you need to pay the fee. It is a mere 100 credits, after all.

speaker: Player
text: Very well, I will pay the 100 credit fee.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: You are welcome on Edean, trade designation G5-623. Czerka Corporation welcomes your business. We should discuss your interests in my office.

speaker: Player
text: I can't pay you the 100 credits.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: That is unfortunate. This outpost will have to remain closed to you until you can secure the credits. I am sorry. Good day.
comment: Player sent back to his ship.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [You have no choice but to return to the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Player
text: I refuse to pay. What will you do about it?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka Corporation protects its interests. If you won't pay, you won't be granted access to the planet and are free to leave.
comment: Player sent back to his ship.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I will await you here if you change your mind.

speaker: Player
text: Don't make demands. I'm <FullName>, and I'll land where I wish.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I respect your... obvious determination, but I can't allow you to remain unless you pay the proper fees.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: The Czerka Corporation appreciates your cooperation, and hopes this will not devolve into a... violent matter.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I don't need to pay the docking fee. Stand aside!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Failure] I fail to see the basis for your arguement. Please, there is no need to be hostile.

speaker: Player
text: It's easily settled. I'll pay with your blood!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: W-we are not unarmed here! We have many guards and security droids. If we can control Wookiees, we can control you.
comment: Everyone on landing level hostile. Wookies below don't care, however.

speaker: Player
text: Is the price negotiable?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Very simply put, no. Operation of these remote outposts is an expensive endeavor.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] I represent wealthy clients. You should let me pass.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Success] *sigh* Normally I wouldn't do this, but I don't feel like arguing. I'll consider a promise of future business payment enough.

speaker: Player
text: Could I get some information about the planet? I thought this was Kashyyyk.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: That is what the dominant indigenous species calls this world, but maintaining this outpost grants Czerka Corporation naming rights in the trade guides.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: But, I'm sorry, I really must insist that docking fees be paid before I impart any further services. I must follow proper procedure.

speaker: Player
text: What services does 100 credits get me?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Well, we are limited in many ways, but I doubt you will find even basic facilities anywhere else in this remote sector.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I greet you again. Will you accept the terms of landing at this outpost? We are quite far from any similar services.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Please, follow me to my office in our information center. We will discuss your needs and how Czerka Corporation can serve you.
comment: P.W. - This used to have the generic walk ways script on it. But I removed it so that it uses the end of dialogue instead.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Greetings again. How can Czerka Corporation serve you during your visit to Edean?

speaker: Player
text: I need supplies. What is available here?
comment: Set a local on this node so this only appears once. This then modifies the "asking about weapons only" line

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: For material goods, I would suggest you speak with the general vendor near the docking area. He keeps his store well-stocked.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: They charge fair value for mundane goods and armor. If it is weapons you want, you will need to deal with the Czerka representative. That would be me.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: If you're here to purchase local species, however, you must wait for a licensed Czerka Corporation trader to return from deliveries outside the system.

speaker: Player
text: Purchase local species? What do you mean?
comment: Only shows up if the player has not asked a SLAVE question already. Set local on area to filter this and other slave questions.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: He means that they are slavers. They take my people from their homes and sell them to the highest bidder.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Your current Wookiee seems displeased with the situation, but I fail to see a concern. You seem to be a satisfied customer.

speaker: Player
text: Zaalbar is no slave. He has pledged a life-debt to me.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Ah, a very difficult thing to stage. I commend you for it. So much easier than relying on restraining collars.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Do not demean the life-debt! Do not!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I must warn you that you will be blamed for the actions of your Wookiee. Please... call him off.

speaker: Player
text: Why? I should let him kill the lot of you!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I am merely a servant of the corporation! The Wookiee leadership is in agreement! Harvesting is made as delicate as possible!

speaker: Jolee
text: [Force Persuade] Hmph. 'Harvesting'. Tell us about this agreement with the Wookiee leadership.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Success] I can tell you about the agreement. We supply arms in exchange for a supply of healthy Wookiees.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: We are kept profitable and an agreeable leader is kept in power. It keeps the process from becoming a constant firefight.

speaker: Player
text: What is this leader's name?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I believe his name is Chuundar. I don't deal directly with them, thank goodness. Far too brutish.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Grrrr.... that was not a name I wanted to hear.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: It sounds as though your thrall has an opinion about our arrangement with this leader, but it doesn't matter. Chuundar is unquestioned.

speaker: Player
text: What about it, Zaalbar? What's the matter?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: This is not something I will talk about. Not yet.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Please, is there anything else? I have work to do.

speaker: Player
text: I've other questions to ask.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I will answer if I can.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the planet. You called it G5-623 before.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: G5-623 is the numerical designation. The galactic Basic name is "Edean," chosen by corporate ballot among stockholders.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: It would seem you are already acquainted with this world, given your choice of traveling companion.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have been away for a very long time.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: You let the beast speak for you? You allow it more liberties than most of our customers.

speaker: Player
text: Allow it more liberties? What do you mean?
comment: Only shows up if the player has not asked a SLAVE question already. Set local on area to filter this and other slave questions.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Aren't you here to take delivery of a Wookiee thrall? There are few other reasons to visit this barbaric world.

speaker: Player
text: Why do the Wookiees tolerate you doing this?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: It is not me, personally. I merely represent Czerka Corporation at this outpost. There are other directors at other stations, of course.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Arrangements have been made with the Wookiee leadership. Harvesting is handled as delicately as possible, relatively speaking.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Tell me about it. I might be more understanding if I know.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Success] If it will ease your temper, I will give specifics. We supply arms in exchange for a supply of healthy Wookiees.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: [Failure] It's not good policy to talk about our corporate strategy. I'm sorry, but I can't say any more.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what you mean or I'll bloody your floor!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: RrrrraaAAAARRRR!!!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Now, there's no c-call for that. It is a simple matter, really. We supply arms in exchange for a supply of healthy Wookiees.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to tell me about these agreements.

speaker: Player
text: Disgusting slaver! Why shouldn't I kill you!

speaker: Player
text: I'd think you would need more firepower to keep order.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: We do things as humanely as possible. There are other outposts, but the operation is very lean overall.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to talk about the slaving operations here on Edean.
comment: Only shows up if the player HAS asked a SLAVE question already. Read local on area set by other slave questions

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I've a very limited number of things I can say. What do you wish to discuss?

speaker: Player
text: I can't allow this to continue.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: It's not up to you. This planet is not a member of the Republic, and its backward citizens hold no rights.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I'm sorry you are offended, but this operation is very humane. Even the Wookiee leadership knows it is more beneficial to work with us.

speaker: Juhani
text: Slavery under any guise should not be tolerated!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Besides, even if you did do something drastic here, the Czerka Corporation has other outposts on Edean. It would change nothing.

speaker: Player
text: What's to stop me turning my Wookiee loose on you?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Oh, just say the word!

speaker: Player
text: I'm through speaking with you for now.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Very good, feel free to inspect our operation here, but I would advise against going too far from the main landing area.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: The planet is still very much untamed, and we do not send out patrols for lost tourists.

speaker: Carth
text: Humane, you call it? Beneficial? Sounds like a bunch of excuses, if you ask me.

speaker: Bastila
text: It's not our place to judge, Carth. As he said, it would change nothing anyway.

speaker: Carth
text: Are you saying you approve of this?!

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course not. I would gladly end it, had I the power. However, we are here for other reasons, if you will recall.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to ask about the Czerka Corporation.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka Corporation has branches in many systems, mostly concerned with weapon production for personal and ship-mounted use.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Of course, the many outposts on this world are only concerned with bio-aquisitions.

speaker: Player
text: Bio-acquisitions? What do you mean?

speaker: Player
text: What weapons do you have available?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka maintains a well-stocked armory that is open to all our valued customers. You may browse it at your leisure.
comment: Attach the store file here for weapon store

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I'm sorry, but I have no information on that. Are you sure you meant to come here? This world is very primitive.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Much of it is still unexplored, even by the locals. The forest gets ever more dangerous the further you descend. The lowest levels, the Shadowlands, are largely unknown.

speaker: Player
text: Farewell for now.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: At any rate, "Edean" is more pleasing than "Kashyyyk." The language of the dominant indigenous species is quite crude.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: In fact, a translation droid must usually be placed with them, but their physical strength makes up for the inconvenience to the owner.

speaker: Player
text: To the owner? What do you mean?
comment: Only shows up if the player has not asked a SLAVE question already. Set local on area to filter this and other slave questions.

speaker: Player
text: What else is on this planet?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: An endless array of dangerous creatures, it seems. The great trees harbor any number of dangers below.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: We've detected odd energy signatures on occasion, but exploration is costly amongst creatures even more difficult than Wookiees.

speaker: Carth
text: Odd energy signatures? Have you ever checked those out?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: We send expeditions, of course, but they come back with little, if they come back at all.

speaker: Player
text: What did you mean when you referred to a Wookiee's "owner?"
comment: Only shows up if the player has not asked a SLAVE question already. Set local on area to filter this and other slave questions.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I don't know why you asked me these questions, but it doesn't matter. Chuundar is unquestioned as leader. Our operation is quite secure.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Force Persuade] You wish to tell us more about this agreement with the Wookiee leadership.

speaker: Juhani
text: [Force Persuade] You wish to tell us more about this agreement with the Wookiee leadership.

speaker: Cand
text: Maybe you should start talking, or I might decide to get a little... restless.

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: The meatbag speaks without clarity. Detail this agreement or the master will splatter your organs all over the floor!

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Please! It is not my decision! It is... an acceptable practice, I assure you!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Hey - I recognize you! You're the one who won the big swoop race!

speaker: HiddenBek113
text: Best swoop race I've seen in years! I couldn't believe it was your first race! You've got real talent, rookie!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: I can't believe that traitor Brejik used to be one of us. Gadon may be old and blind, but I'd rather follow him than a turncoat like Brejik!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: We should have wiped the Vulkars out long ago, but Gadon Thek thought he could reason with Brejik and prevent a war. Guess we know better now.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: If the Vulkar's hadn't stolen our swoop engine prototype we'd be a lock to win the big race this year!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: With Brejik dead it won't be long until those Vulkars of his collapse. I bet within a week Gadon will have the Lower City back to normal.

speaker: Hijata
text: It's really strange. Nobody seems to know where Master Uthar or Yuthura Ban have disappeared to. Some of the sensitives are claiming they're dead.

speaker: Hijata
text: Rumor has it that something has happened to Master Uthar and Yuthura Ban. Do you know anything?

speaker: Hijata
text: I heard that Yuthura Ban was dead. I suppose that means Master Uthar will be taking a new apprentice, soon.

speaker: Hijata
text: Did you hear? Yuthura is dead. Master Uthar said so. I bet she got too impatient and failed to assassinate him. Idiot.

speaker: Hijata
text: Master Yuthura has taken over the academy. Everyone's talking about it! I guess she finally got rid of Uthar, somehow.

speaker: Hijata
text: Have you heard? Yuthura... I mean Master Yuthura has taken over the academy! Well done, I say!

speaker: Hijata
text: You aren't even a full Sith. Don't bother me.

speaker: Hijata
text: Get out of my way. I don't have time to deal with hopefuls.

speaker: Hijata
text: Come back when you've taken your final test. If you survive it.

speaker: Hijata
text: If Master Uthar gives you an order, you'd better follow it. There were some students who disobeyed him and now they're hiding out on the surface somewhere.

speaker: Hijata
text: There are some students in hiding that refused to follow an order. Master Uthar wants them found and dead... and is offering a reward for it, too!

speaker: Hijata
text: Just be careful if you go into the valley. I hear there's a hermit living in the hills that kidnaps students.

speaker: Hijata
text: The former master of the academy, Jorak Uln, is supposedly hiding out in the hills on the surface as some kind of mad hermit.

speaker: Hijata
text: Word is that one of our experimental droids went mad and escaped and is hiding in the ruins. I wonder why we don't just gather up and destroy it?

speaker: Hijata
text: One of my friends went to find that crazy droid that's hiding in the ruins in the valley. He hasn't come back, yet.

speaker: Hijata
text: Ha! It's great to be on the winning side, isn't it? We've been crushing the Republic at every battle so far!

speaker: Hijata
text: The latest reports say the Republic is on the run. Before long the Sith will be ruling the entire galaxy.

speaker: Hijata
text: Darth Malak is one of the greatest Sith leaders ever. I hope he comes back to the academy before I leave.

speaker: Hijata
text: It is my most fervent hope to serve under Darth Malak once my training is complete. Don't you feel the same?

speaker: Hijata
text: Rumor around the academy is that you had something to do with those rebel students being caught, finally. They got what they deserved, I say.

speaker: Hijata
text: I was told that you actually met the old master of the academy, Jorak. Is the hermit as mad as they say?

speaker: Hijata
text: The buzz is that you took care of that crazy droid out in the ruins. That's pretty impressive.

speaker: Hijata
text: Hmm. So you got enough prestige to win out, I hear. We'll just see if you make it through your final test.

speaker: Hijata
text: Sorry, I don't have time to speak. My training awaits.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: My protocol droids are not programmed to interact with customers, so should you desire assistance I can aid you.

speaker: Player
text: Let me see what you have in stock.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: Explore my inventory at your convenience. Settler families have purchased all my droids, but I have many upgrades and other wares for purchase.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know of the Mandalorian raiders?

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: Only that they have been a nuisance to the farmers and settlers in the region.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: They do not have the resources to penetrate this base, so I do not know of them first-hand.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: Is there something else I can do for you?

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: Please return again soon to Aratech Droids, Inc. for all your droid needs.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: I greet you, human. How may this outpost of Aratech Droids serve your needs?
comment: DIALOGUE  subsequent times before being accepted

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: I hear that there is much strife amongst the Sith as of late. It bodes well for the cause of the Jedi. How may I serve your needs today?

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: The Czerka Corp., the perennial rivals of my company, have suffered some major setbacks on the world of Kashyyyk, I hear.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: Aratech will benefit greatly from this, I believe, and our benefit extends to our customers as well. Hopefully prices will fall in the near future. How may I be of assistance today?

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: I hear you have earned a name for yourself in racing speeders. I am sure that one such as you has many needs that I can hope to fulfill.

speaker: Karal Kaar
text: I greet you, Padawan. Members of the Jedi Order are always welcome in all the outposts of Aratech Droids. How may I serve you today?

speaker: T'sllth
text: Very good, though I should expect no less from the Sector Champion. Would you like to race again? It would require another 20 credit positioning fee.

text: I'll pay for a practice run.

text: Certainly. Your swoop will be towed into position immediately. It shouldn't take long to begin the run.

speaker: Player
text: Why is there a fee?

speaker: T'sllth
text: We find that racers are more careful when they are funding the course with each race. Besides, we must defray maintenance costs somehow.

speaker: T'sllth
text: And please, no haggling. I am not authorized to give a discount even if I wished to.

speaker: Player
text: I want an officially timed race.

speaker: T'sllth
text: Please speak to the Course Regulator for information on challenging the current leaders in each race category.

speaker: Player
text: No thanks. Goodbye.

text: Very well. Goodbye.

text: That was a good run. You would do well in a tournament. Would you like another unofficial run? It would require another 20 credit positioning fee.

text: Welcome, Sector Champion. Would you like to book the swoop course for a practice run? For a small fee of 20 credits you can keep your skills in top shape.

speaker: T'sllth
text: Hello there. Are you looking to book the swoop course for a practice run? There will be a small positioning fee of 20 credits to have your swoop bike readied.

text: Rahasia and I cannot thank you enough for what you have done for us. Now we finally have a place to share our love, without fear of reprisals from our families.

text: So... any kids on the way yet?

text: Go away.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: You there - human. You are the rider who won the Great Swoop Race in the Lower City, yes?

speaker: Player
text: That's right.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: I have a message from Canderous Ordo. He says to meet him in the cantina.

speaker: Player
text: Canderous? Isn't he that Mandalorian that works for Davik?

speaker: Twi'lek
text: Yes, that's the one. Given his connections, you can see why it would be wise to attend this meeting.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: Canderous didn't say why he wanted to meet you. He only said he had an offer you couldn't refuse. Given his connections, you can see why it would be foolish to ignore his request.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks for the message. I'll go meet him in the cantina.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: A wise choice, human. I would advise you not to wait too long. Mandalorians are known for many things, but patience is not one of them.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, I got the message. You can go now.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: I would advise you not to put this meeting off for too long, human. Mandalorians are known for many things, but patience is not one of them.

speaker: Player
text: I'll think about it.

speaker: Player
text: Why does he want to meet me?

speaker: Player
text: You must have me confused with someone else.

speaker: Twi'lek
text: No, human. I don't think so. I saw the swoop race: you were there. You posted the best time. You are the one I was sent to find.

speaker: Player
text: What do you want?

speaker: Twi'lek
text: Me? I want nothing. I am only a runner. I work for the man who hired me.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Your actions beneath the surface have shown that you are no friend to my people. I wish nothing to do with you.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I am sorry, human. You have made your relationship with the Sith quite clear. I have no further business with you.
comment: if player declared allegiance to sith

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I was only kidding!

speaker: Shaelas
text: [Success] I do not find that form of humor amusing, human!

speaker: Shaelas
text: Your words are strange, human. You claim one thing, then the exact opposite. Perhaps this is what your species calls humor. If so, its appeal eludes me.

speaker: Shaelas
text: However, I believe you now speak the truth about your dislike of the Sith.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Though I suspect we have little in common, human, I share your dislike of the Sith. They have brought grief to my family.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I am not a fool, I know the Sith do not respect our laws as the Republic does. Were it up to me, I would do everything in my power to aid the Republic in the war against Malak.

speaker: Shaelas
text: But intergalactic politics stay my hand. Still, I know the Sith are evil - and I fear what they will do to my people. And what they may be doing now.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Shaelas
text: Many of the Selkath have vanished, human. Most who have gone missing are on the cusp of adulthood, the youth who will someday lead this planet. My own daughter, Shasa, is among those who have disappeared.

speaker: Shaelas
text: These disappearances coincide with the arrival of the Sith, and I cannot dismiss the connection. The Sith are up to something, human. Something sinister - I can feel it!

speaker: Player
text: You want me to investigate these disappearances?

speaker: Shaelas
text: I will give you 500 credits if you can uncover the fate of my daughter and the other missing Selkath youth. Not much, but all I can afford. I have no official authority in this matter, and my personal wealth is not vast.

speaker: Shaelas
text: There is no one else I can turn to, human. The Republic agents are too closely watched by the Sith, and the Ahto City authorities cannot act without proof of Sith involvement.

speaker: Player
text: I shall look into these disappearances for you, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I cannot imagine where to begin the investigation, though I suspect the Sith did not act alone. Perhaps the off-worlders in the mercenary enclave know something.

speaker: Shaelas
text: If you learn anything, human, report back to me at once. If you uncover the fate of my daughter and the other missing Selkath youth, I will reward you as promised.

speaker: Player
text: I've got better things to do than look for missing tadpoles.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I see, human. Despite your rebuff, my offer still stands - I have nowhere else to turn. Return to me if you obtain information on my daughter and the other missing Selkath youth, and I will reward you as promised.

speaker: Player
text: What's in this for me?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, I'm not interested.

speaker: Player
text: Just get to the point, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: [Failure] I do not believe you! Go. We have nothing more to speak of.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] It was a joke.

speaker: Shaelas
text: [Success] Yes... A joke. I was mistaken.

speaker: Player
text: Whatever...

speaker: Shaelas
text: Human, you return. Have you information for me? Have you discovered the fate of the missing Selkath youth? Have you news of my daughter, Shasa?

speaker: Player
text: Not yet. I shall investigate further.

speaker: Player
text: I have information for you, Shaelas.
comment: discovered the Iridorian or discovered the Selkath youth in training, or discovered the Sith datapad.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Excellent. You have done well. What have you learned?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith hired an Iridorian mercenary to lure the Selkath youth to the Sith base.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I see. This information is useful, for a start. But it does little to explain the truth of this matter. We must know what purpose the Sith have for these youth.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Are they prisoners of the Sith? Are they even still alive? I must know more, human. I must know what has happened to my daughter!

speaker: Player
text: I will look into this further.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I cannot officially ask you to enter the Sith base, human. That would be a violation of Ahto City's strict neutrality laws. However, I fear such a brazen act may be the only way to learn the truth.

speaker: Shaelas
text: But entering the base will not be easy. And should you be captured or killed, I will have to disavow any knowledge of your actions.

speaker: Player
text: I'll infiltrate the Sith base, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I wish I could be of more help, human. I will wait here. Return to me when you have something more to report.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it - I'm not about to break into the Sith base looking for your web fingered offspring!

speaker: Shaelas
text: You shall have no reward from me until I learn the fate of my daughter, human! If you change your mind and discover her fate, you can report to me here to collect your reward.

speaker: Player
text: What do you suggest I do?

speaker: Player
text: Does this mean I don't get paid?

speaker: Shaelas
text: This information is mere bait - the catch yet awaits, human. Once you discover the ultimate fate of my daughter, I will gladly give you the 500 credits I promised.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are training the Selkath youth in the ways of the Dark Jedi.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Yes... this makes sense. It is a wonder I did not see this before. Manaan's greatest strength is our neutrality.

speaker: Shaelas
text: If Malak brainwashes our youth and indoctrinates them in the ways of the Sith he will have a strong following among the Selkath people - strong enough to seize control of Manaan and our kolto!

speaker: Shaelas
text: My daughter, Shasa - she too has been indoctrined into the Sith camp?

speaker: Player
text: Your daughter is dead, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: No! Say it is not so, human! No - not Shasa! The Sith will pay for this! If it is the last thing I do they will pay!

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps this datapad will help.

speaker: Shaelas
text: A datapad? Let me see. Of course - this details the entire Sith plot! With this evidence I can go to the Ahto City authorities!

speaker: Shaelas
text: The Sith will face severe fines and export restrictions for their actions - a poor substitute for my daughter's life, but with any luck the kolto embargo will weaken the Sith war effort.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I... I thank you for what you have done here, human - though I wish my daughter's fate had been otherwise. Here are the credits I promised you.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry it had to be this way, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Please, excuse me now, human. I desire no company but my own.

speaker: Player
text: Keep your credits, Shaelas. I wouldn't feel right about taking them now.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I... I thank you once more, human. I wish all your species were as kind and noble as you.

speaker: Player
text: I hope so.

speaker: Player
text: I killed your daughter, Shaelas. Just as I'll kill you if you tell anyone about this. Now give me those credits!

speaker: Shaelas
text: You... you are a monster! I came to you for aid, and you betray me and slaughter my innocent Shasa! You are no better than the Sith!

speaker: Player
text: Blah, blah, blah - give me the credits if you want to live.

speaker: Jolee
text: Nice. Real nice. Maybe later we could find some insects to pull the legs off, huh?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Your actions disturb me. Among my kind, those who take pleasure in the suffering of others are considered dangerously unstable.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Take your blood money, human! May it bring you as much grief and misfortune as you have brought me!

speaker: Juhani
text: You are a representative of the Jedi Order. When you behave this way you disgrace us all!

speaker: Carth
text: This isn't right! We should be helping people, not making their lives miserable.

speaker: Bastila
text: We should guard and protect those weaker than ourselves... not bully and exploit them!

speaker: Mission
text: I know you're supposed to save the galaxy and all, but could you try being less of a scummy core slime while you're doing it?

speaker: Player
text: I've convinced your daughter to turn her back on the Sith ways.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Human, if you speak the truth I am forever in your debt! And yet, my joy is tempered by the knowledge that the Sith still walk freely about Manaan.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Hopefully the testimony of my daughter will be enough proof of their actions, to make the Ahto City authorites take action.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe this datapad will help.
comment: XP bonus, player has data pad

speaker: Shaelas
text: A datapad? Yes, I see! This datapad has all the details of the entire Sith plot! With this the Manaan authorities will be forced to take action!

speaker: Shaelas
text: I doubt the Sith will be banned from Manaan, but at the very least they will face harsh restrictions on their kolto exports!

speaker: Shaelas
text: You have done much for me, human. Here are the credits I promised you - I only wish I had more to give.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you, Shaelas.

speaker: Mission
text: Wow, sometimes helping people feels pretty good, you know?

speaker: Juhani
text: This is how we Jedi should always act: with honor.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Please excuse me now, human. I must go speak to the Manaan authorities about this Sith plot and what they have done to my beloved daughter.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm glad to see we're still the good guys here. Sometimes I think we forget that.

speaker: Player
text: Keep your credits, Shaelas. A Jedi has no need of such rewards.

speaker: Shaelas
text: You refuse my reward? Truly you humans are a noble breed! Perhaps my species has underestimated your kind.

speaker: HK47
text: Statement: Oh, master. I'm so very disappointed in you.

speaker: Cand
text: Mighty generous of you. A little too generous, if you ask me.

speaker: Bastila
text: That was a truly noble act. The Jedi Council would be pleased.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hey, kid, that was a good thing you did there. Almost brought a tear to this old man's eye.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am proud to call you my friend, <FullName>. You have a noble and generous spirit.

speaker: Player
text: Give me my money and get out of here.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I would not have expected such rudeness from a Jedi... but you have rendered a valuable service. Here is your money.

speaker: Player
text: Your daughter is still with the Sith, Shaelas.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Shasa, my daughter, what have those Sith monsters done to your mind? I will report this to the authorities, though I fear without proof there is little they can do to get my daughter back.

speaker: Player
text: Your daughter has joined the Sith.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Shasa... No! This is most terrible! Most terrible indeed!

speaker: Shaelas
text: I must go now, human, to inform the Selkath authorities of what is transpiring. Here is the money I have promised you.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe a few credits could refresh my memory.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I am confused, human. How will credits facilitate your cognitive functions? Oh... I believe I understand.

speaker: Shaelas
text: This is what you off-worlders call a shakedown, is it not? I am not wealthy, human. I have offered 500 credits for information on my daughter and the other missing Selkath. Is this not enough?

speaker: Player
text: Very well. I'll tell you what I know.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I am pleased you have not chosen to exploit my loss for your personal greed, human. What have you discovered?

speaker: Player
text: If you want news on your daughter, find a way to get those extra credits.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Very well, human. You prey upon my grief and concern over my missing daughter, but I am desperate. Here is another 100 credits - that is all I have.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I have already given you an additional 100 credits! I have nothing more to give, human! Have you no heart, no compassion?

speaker: Player
text: Fine. I'll tell you what I know.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I suppose I should thank you, human - though you have already exploited my grief well enough for your own gain. What information do you have for me now?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry - no credits, no info.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I... I have nothing more to give, human. The 500 credits I promised you for the fate of my daughter are all I have left.

speaker: Shaelas
text: I suppose I can do nothing more but wait here, in case you change your mind. I can only hope you find find it in your heart to take pity on a grieving parent.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, nothing yet.

speaker: Player
text: I've decided I've got better things to do than be your errand slave.

speaker: Shaelas
text: Greetings, human. My name is Shaelas. I have heard that you may have had some part in the incident at the Sith Embassy recently. Is this true?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are a blight upon the galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: My allegiances are my own business.

speaker: Shaelas
text: You are wise to be so guarded, human. But my sources are rarely wrong, and they have informed me that you are no friend of Malak's people.

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I kind of like the Sith. They've got style.

speaker: Shaelas
text: You like the Sith? You are obviously not the person I am looking for to complete this task.

speaker: Player
text: I'm just kidding.

speaker: Player
text: What task?

speaker: Shaelas
text: Greetings, human. My name is Shaelas. I have heard it said that you are no friend of the Sith. Is this true?

speaker: Shaelas
text: Human, I wish to speak with you.
comment: when player approaches before first conversation

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Deserter! Traitor! I'll make an example of you!

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Well that's just great! I don't have the men to keep this location safe!

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'll be back, though! There's money here!

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Who are you, another civil merchant like that coro-slime up on the docking ring? This is my territory.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I don't make deals and I don't persuade easily, so go back topside. Mess with my profits and I'll see you dead.

speaker: Player
text: Are you the poachers Jolee told me about?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: That crazy old fool is still alive? I suppose he's still upset that we don't all live in little homemade shacks like he chooses.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I've got a job to do here, and there's nothing you or that old coot can do about it.

speaker: Player
text: I might be interested in some work.
comment: Not "on the job" There is a local that will be set on the node where the player accepts the job. It will prevent this node from appearing again.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I could use an extra hand. A couple men have gone missing. If I lose many more I'll have to close up shop.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: We are hunting the little simians, the tach. They have a gland that acts as a stimulant when powdered.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I figure I've got two or three wealthy years to butcher the lot of them. You want in before I make them extinct?

speaker: Player
text: What does the job pay?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I really can't quote a price. Depends on the market. I give fair value for each one, rest assured. That promise will have to do.

speaker: Player
text: I want the job. How do I hunt these tach?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: All right then, I'll set you up. First you need to be able to draw them out. It's easy.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'll spray you with this scent... it drives them crazy. They can't help but attack you, even if it's a hopeless fight.
comment: Set global to show that player now activates angry tach triggers. When animation list is updated, place some sort of effect on the player to signify that they have been sprayed with scent.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Then you just carve them up. There's a big fleshy bulb in their brains that you want to scoop out. You can't miss it.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'd feel guilty if the money weren't so good. Come back here when you've got the glands and I'll pay you.

speaker: Player
text: Back to my general questions, all right?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Hurry up. You're eating into my profits.

speaker: Player
text: I've got a tach gland to sell you.
comment: Player "on the job" and has some tach glands

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'll take whatever you have. Keep it up and we'll both be rich. At least until we bleed this planet dry, hahaha!
comment: Give player 10 credits for each tach gland they have. Take glands

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: If you made it this far you know a fair bit already. What would I be able to tell you?

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'm no nav officer. I work on the ground, and I haven't seen anything like that around here.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Of course, we haven't been much deeper than this. The eastern forest gets even more dangerous.
comment: update with direction to the forcefield barrier

speaker: Player
text: You aren't safe with blasters?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: It's not worth it. You're fighting the plants as well as the animals. Kshyy vines are tough as metal, and grow back fast.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Instead, head office installed repulsor fields to keep the big predators out. Permanent placements too. We'll be fine for years.

speaker: Player
text: I have other questions about the Shadowlands.

speaker: Player
text: I'm leaving.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Good. I'm not down here to direct traffic.

speaker: Player
text: Are you part of the slaving operation?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: What? No, I don't do much of that. It's too much of a headache. I'm in the business of harvesting animals.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Some of the more exotic species have organs that can be removed and put to some surprising applications.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I've already told you about that. You agreed to help bring them in.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Talk to me about work and maybe I'll tell you more.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything odd down here?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Besides you? Besides any number of predators that can kill in seconds? I suppose there's old Bindo.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: He's got a camp here somewhere. I'd leave him alone, though. Anyone who'd live down here is just plain crazy.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: There's not much else. We've got a repulsor field to the east so not much passes through here now.

speaker: Player
text: If the Shadowlands are so dangerous, how do you survive?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: It ain't easy. We've set up a perimeter of sonic emitters to keep the bigger preds away. It's worked so far.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: As long as the emitters are operational, we're pretty much safe. It makes harvesting a lot easier.

speaker: Player
text: What if I want you to leave the Shadowlands?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Is that old hermit Jolee trying to talk you into doing his dirty work? We've spent too much on setting up just to walk away.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: As long the sonic emitters keep the preds away and I've got bodies to guard the perimeter, we're staying right here.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I mean, if I can put up with my own worthless guards complaining about this place, Jolee whining through you is nothing.

speaker: Player
text: I've got some tach glands to sell you.

speaker: Player
text: You're just a Czerka slaver. Nothing special.
comment: The player will be allowed to threaten this guard twice. The first time will get a warning. The second time will result in an attack. The condition should be set on the second branch following this node.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: All right, I'm done talking with you. You've got under my skin one too many times! I'll bury you down here!
comment: Goes hostile along with all his men.

speaker: Cand
text: Just you try it.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I don't need this kind of garbage from you. Watch your mouth. I'm the only law there is down here.
comment: Set the "threaten" condition on this node, so that the next time the player threatens the guard, the above node is the path followed.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: If you've got something to say, get on with it. Otherwise, leave me alone. I've credits to earn.

speaker: Player
text: I should just kill you. No one will ever know.

speaker: Player
text: I have more questions about the job.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Hurry up, I'm wasting too much time on you as it is.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you care that you could wipe out the whole species?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Uh, no. I'll be rich by then, and won't need to do it anymore. I don't have to worry about it.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Besides, if there's no more tach, the predators that eat them will die off and we'll have an easier time milking this planet.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe you should just pay me so I don't shut you down.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'm warning you, I didn't get this job because of my sense of humor. You smart mouth me again and we'll have a problem.
comment: Set the "threaten" condition on this node, so that the next time the player threatens the guard, the above node is the path followed.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Hell, I have guards everywhere and a perimeter of sonic emitters. I don't fear anything in the Shadowlands, including you.

speaker: Player
text: This wholesale slaughter can't be allowed!

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I'm hard-pressed to come up with a way for you to stop me. I'll defend this operation if I have to.
comment: Set the "threaten" condition on this node, so that the next time the player threatens the guard, the above node is the path followed.

speaker: Player
text: I paid the docking fee. Who cares where I go?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: So you're playing tourist? That isn't smart. The Shadowlands are all business. Mess around and you'll end up dead.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: That said, if you want to make some credits while you're looking to die, I might have a job for you.

speaker: Player
text: Chuundar has given me permission to be here.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: He's got no authority with me. I'm with Czerka Corporation. He's just some pet we keep so the locals stay in line.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: As long as you don't get in my way, you can wander where you want. I've got a job to do.

speaker: Player
text: Are you going to stop me? I go where I want.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Look, I don't care if you want to play tourist down here, but you behave yourself or we'll have a problem.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: I've got a job to do, and I won't be gentle if you get in my way, understand?

speaker: Commander Dern
text: Back again, hmm? Unless you've business with me I suggest you turn around and walk away.

speaker: Commander Dern
text: That's it! You are dead!

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: [This droid is speaking a language you do not recognize.]
comment: some kind of hissy reptilish language

speaker: Player
text: What language is that? What are you trying to say?

speaker: Player
text: I don't understand you.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: You are neither Builder nor slave. If you seek the secrets of the Star Forge you must first prove yourself worthy. Only then will the sealed door behind be opened.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: I am here to aid those who seek the knowledge of the Builders. What do you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you again?

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: I am the Overseer. The Builders programmed me to enforce discipline among the slaves while this monument to the power of the Star Forge was constructed.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: At project completion all slaves were executed. I was reprogrammed to serve should a Builder return in search of knowledge of the Star Forge.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Builders?

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: The Builders are the great masters of the galaxy, the conquerors of all worlds, the rulers of the infinite empire and the creators of the Star Forge.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: More than this, I am not programmed to say.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Star Forge.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: The Star Forge is the glory of the Builders, the apex of their infinite empire. It is a machine of invincible might, a tool of unstoppable conquest.

speaker: Player
text: How do I prove myself worthy and unseal the doors?

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: The chambers on either side contain the proving grounds. Within them, those who understand the will of the Builders can unlock their secrets and open the doors.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: But those who fail will be destroyed by the security systems of the temple itself. More than this, I am not programmed to say.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: I shall remain here as programmed by the Builders.

speaker: Ancient Droid
text: You have proven yourself worthy, the sealed door is open. If you wish to learn the secrets of the Star Forge you must pass through the door to the room beyond.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Well, it seems you are more than I thought. Freyyr has come back, and told me of what you did for him.
comment: This is the second version of Chorrawl, placed halfway between the village and basket AFTER player has HELPED Freyyr. He replaces the previous version of him. He takes the player directly to the throne room so that they player can't explore the village while all the crap is going down.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: My fellow hunters split on what should be done. Some were loyal to Chuundar alone... we had to fight.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Freyyr went to the throne room to challenge Chuundar. I will take you to him now.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I follow you?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: I can guide you off the path. We will approach from behind, avoiding Czerka and those loyal to Chuundar.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: It is the only way. I'm sorry, but I won't allow you to proceed any other way. This is too important.
comment: Palyer taken to Chuundar throne room.

speaker: Player
text: You fought each other? Why?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: We follow the Chieftain, whoever that is. If the position is in doubt, we each fight for the side we believe in.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: This must be decided quickly or there will be much more bloodshed. Come, it is this way.

speaker: Player
text: Lead on. We should hurry.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Yes, much is about to be decided. Only one can lead us. *Must* lead us. Come.
comment: Palyer taken to Chuundar throne room.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: By order of Chieftain Freyyr, you are allowed full access to the Shadowlands and our village. You have our thanks, outsider.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Chuundar has said you may pass into the Shadowlands. Gorwooken will lower you down in the elevator basket.
comment: Selected after player has been sent to the Shadowlands by Chuundar.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Gorwooken climbed to the basket from the upper branches, but you will have to walk, outsider.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: The path is seldom used. There may be vermin nesting along it. Be ready to fight.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Grrrowwlll!! You are not permitted to pass into the Shadowlands. Only Chuundar may allow you entry.
comment: This wookie guards the road to the Shadowlands. Initial selected before the player has spoken to Chuundar This guard is removed if the player helps Freyyr.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: I have already told you to take your filthy madclaw and leave. Speak with Chuundar in the village and don't bother me further.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Especially when you bring filth such as this with you. This madclaw has no place here.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Who are you to question my place? You follow Chuundar into the arms of outsiders.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: And yet you travel with outsiders yourself! Speak no more! Chuundar will decide if you are permitted to enter the Shadowlands.

speaker: Player
text: Where is this Wookiee I need to see?

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Speak with Chuundar in the village of Rwookrrorro. He will decide if you are worthy.

speaker: Player
text: What was that about, Zaalbar?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: We should proceed to the village. I'm sure we will both get answers there.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: Can't you see I'm auditioning? This is my shot at the big time; I can't risk screwing it up by talking to you.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: Ah, what's the use? There's no way Bib's going to hire me unless he gets a chance to see me dancing with a partner. Maybe I should just give up.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you have a partner?

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: My last partner left me. She was always trying to upstage me, even though it was obvious I had ten times her talent. When I finally told her that, she stormed off. I guess the truth hurts.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: My partner before that was even worse. If I wasn't tripping over his staggering feet I was ducking under his flailing arms. I ditched him after less than a week.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I could be your partner.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: I admit I'm getting desperate: I'd hate to blow this audition. But I don't know if I'm ready to just pair up with a random passer-by. How do I know you're any good?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] How hard can it be?

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: [Failure] You think this is easy? I've trained for years to develop my talents. Dancing isn't just wiggling your butt in the air, you know! Well, except for the Corellian Cheek-Step.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: If you think you can just step up and start dancing at a professional level, you better think again.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm good enough to get you through your audition.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: [Success] Well, you do have that certain look about you: a confidence of movement. *sigh* I guess you'll have to do. But I'm warning you - don't screw this up!

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: Mr. Surool, I've got a partner now. I'd really like to audition for you again.

speaker: BibSurool
text: Okay, Lyn, you've got one more chance. I'll give you a minute to get your partner set up, then let's see what you've got.

speaker: BibSurool
text: Okay, I've got time to watch you for three more dances. Make them count.
comment: Fade to black, set everyone out in cutscene mode.

speaker: LynSekla
text: Okay, just follow my lead. Remember, the more complicated our steps and the closer we dance the more it will impress Bib.

speaker: LynSekla
text: But don't get in too close if you can't handle it. I don't need some clumsy oaf tripping me up. Try not to screw this up for me, okay?

speaker: Player
text: [Join Lyn by dancing beside her.]

speaker: BibSurool
text: Hmmm. Simple, but nice. Just remember: the Starlight Entertainers don't want simple. We're only looking for the top performers in the galaxy.

speaker: LynSekla
text: Look, I know you're trying to be careful about screwing up, but you've got to give me a little more than that. Bib's seen thousands of dancers: we need to do something that will impress him.

speaker: LynSekla
text: The next dance is a little different, so watch me for the steps then jump in.

speaker: Player
text: [Join Lyn by dancing close beside her.]

speaker: BibSurool
text: Good, good. One, two, three, one, two, three... nice tempo. Looking good, Lyn. Okay, one more dance to go.

speaker: LynSekla
text: Okay, one dance to go. Bib looks happy. As long as we don't screw up I think we've got it! Follow me and please, just keep it simple.

speaker: Player
text: [Join Lyn by dancing very close and face to face.]

speaker: BibSurool
text: Looking good. Looking very good. Feel the music. Let it flow through you.

speaker: LynSekla

speaker: LynSekla
text: Thank you. I couldn't have made it without you. I'd give you a big hug, but... well, frankly you're a little beneath me now. Like Bib said, I'm going to be a star!

speaker: LynSekla

speaker: LynSekla

speaker: Player
text: Face it: you just aren't good enough to make the cut.

speaker: LynSekla

speaker: LynSekla

text: [Ruin Lyn's audition by taking a dive.]

speaker: LynSekla

speaker: Lyn Sekla

text: I'll partner up with you, for a price.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: Is that a joke? I'm a professional entertainer, I don't pay people to dance with me! Besides, who says I'm looking for a partner anyway?

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: That Twi'lek over there is Bib Surool, the manager and talent scout for the Starlight Entertainers. They're one of the biggest performing troupes in this quadrant.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: When I heard he was stuck on Taris, I figured it was my lucky break. If I can impress him he might hire me on as a dancer and I can finally get off this slime-pit of a world.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: But I don't have a partner, and the Starlight Entertainers never perform solo. If he can't judge how I dance with someone else, I'm sunk.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: Back again? Dancing isn't easy, you know. It requires focus and concentration. You can't keep bothering me like this.

speaker: Lyn Sekla
text: It's hard enough for me to impress Bib without showing him how I dance with a partner. I don't need any distractions to make it worse.

speaker: Maana Demknot

speaker: Player
text: Step back, fool! I don't like your tone!

speaker: Maana Demknot
text: See, that same attitude! That "don't even talk to me" look she had! I swear, "Helena" must be your word for pit rancor.

speaker: Bastila
text: Have you seen a woman that may resemble me somewhat? She is my mother.

speaker: Bastila
text: Ask whether they have seen my mother.

speaker: Bastila

speaker: Jedi Knight
text: The Sith will want to cut off our escape. We'll stay here and protect the ships so we can get out of here once Malak's dead!

speaker: Janitor
text: D...don't hurt me... I'm just the janitor here. I don't know nothing that would be useful to you Sith!

speaker: Janitor
text: Hey, there - watch where you're walking! I just cleaned these floors.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry I was rude to you earlier.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you again?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Janitor
text: Don't know how much I can tell you, but seeing as how you're new here I guess I can try and help you out.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Taris.

speaker: Janitor
text: Decent enough place to live, I guess. Except for the lower levels. That's where the swoop gangs hang out. Just stay in the Upper City and you'll be fine.

speaker: Janitor
text: You also might want to check out the cantina. I used to go there when I was younger. Good place to get a drink and find out what's going on in the Upper City.

speaker: Player
text: Where is the cantina?

speaker: Janitor
text: Just keep following the apartment complex ring until you come to the elevator. It'll take you out to the Upper City streets. From there just head south a ways. You can't miss it.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Janitor
text: I should get back to work anyway. I'll probably see you around - I'm here most of the time. This building doesn't clean itself, you know.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get some equipment?

speaker: Janitor
text: Well, the best place to go is probably Kebla Yurt's store. She's right across from the cantina, so you can stop in for a drink if you get thirsty while you're shopping.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Sith and this quarantine?

speaker: Janitor

text: I prefer to keep to myself, mostly. But there's plenty of people at the cantina who'll be more than happy to tell you what they think about the Sith and their quarantine.

speaker: Janitor

speaker: Player

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I have heard what you have done, and how Juhani has been slain. I had hoped that this would not have to come to pass.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Could you find nothing in Juhani that could be redeemed?

speaker: Player
text: I could not see a way to save her.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I am skeptical of your methods and your intentions. But if nothing could be done, then that is the way of things.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Keep in mind the danger of the dark side, lest you fall into its grasp.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] She didn't give me a chance.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: [Success] I am skeptical of your methods and your intentions. But if nothing could be done, then that is the way of things.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] She was too far gone to the dark side.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I see you insist on wandering the halls of our Enclave when you should be busy studying your lessons.

speaker: Player
text: My training is going well.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: It appears that soon you will achieve the rank of Padawan. Master Zhar is most impressed with your progress. But I cannot help but wonder if you move forward too quickly.

speaker: Player
text: I seek knowledge of the Jedi Code.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: You do not know the Jedi Code? Without knowledge of those doctrines all your training will be for naught! All Jedi must know the code, its tenets are the fundamental teachings of our Order!

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: There is no emotion; there is peace. There is no ignorance; there is knowledge. There is no passion; there is serenity. There is no chaos; there is harmony. There is no death; there is the Force.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Learn these truths, apprentice... or we shall all regret the decision to accept you into the Order.

speaker: Player
text: I would like to ask some questions.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I suppose such desires are inevitable, though I fear you may seek knowledge for which you are not prepared. Yet I will do my best to guide your quest.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Bastila?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Bastila? The young Jedi holds great promise... and great danger. She can do much for both the Republic and the Council. Without her skill in Battle Meditation the Sith armada would have conquered the galaxy long ago.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: But despite her command of the Force Bastila is still young. She is a Jedi, but she has not attained the rank of Master. The Council would do well to remember this before we lay the fate of the galaxy on her slender shoulders.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: You would do well to focus more closely on your lessons. The Force is strong with you, but you need training and guidance in the ways of the Jedi, lest you suffer a fate similar to that of Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything you can tell me about Revan and Malak?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Revan was once a promosing Padawan. But ever eager to learn more about the Force, Revan sought knowledge of ancient Sith magics, foolishly ignoring the dangerous lure of the dark side.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: When the Mandalorian invasion came, Revan seized the opportunity it presented. Many Jedi flocked to the Outer Rim to follow the charismatic young Knight... and many fell under the sway of the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: What happened on the Outer Rim to corrupt Revan?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I do not believe Revan and Malak were corrupted on the Outer Rim. They had begun their journey down the dark path long before the Mandalorian threat appeared.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Here on Dantooine they discovered a sinister cave, a place where the strength of the dark side overwhelms the light.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Perhaps this discovery was what first corrupted them... or perhaps they sought the cave out because they were already corrupted.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Whatever the explanation, the Order was unable to turn them back to the light. Had the Council taken more decisive action in this matter, perhaps Revan and Malak could have been stopped. But in this we failed.

speaker: Player
text: I should be going now.

speaker: Player
text: You often seem angry with me, Master Vrook. Have I displeased you?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: If you find me overly critical, perhaps it is because you do not fully understand what is at stake. For fifteen thousand years the Republic has brought peace and stability to the galaxy.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Now the Republic may be destroyed because we, the Jedi, have failed them. Revan and Malak were paragons of the ideals the Order seeks to uphold, yet they succumbed to the temptations of the dark side.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: When Revan fell, Malak took up the mantle of Dark Lord of the Sith. Should Malak be stopped, what is to stop another Jedi from taking his place? This is the burden we Masters must carry.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Only through strict training and relentless lessons can we prevent the Dark Master from being reborn.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: That is why the Order can brook no failure in our apprentices and pupils. That is why I can accept nothing but perfection from you.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you always criticizing me?

speaker: Player
text: Why does the Council not stop the Mandalorian raiders?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: So you heard about them, did you?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: They have been harmless up until now. It is tragic that someone had to die before we took action.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: You have our leave to deal with the murdering Mandalorian raiders should you encounter them.

speaker: Player
text: I must be going now.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Hmph! Well, get along then! Maybe you'll find the time to do something useful.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: There was a battle near one of the southern estate recently. Many people were killed. Do you know anything about it?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] No, I was somewhere else.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: [Success] Hmph. Indeed. I cannot prove anything, but I have my suspicions. I will keep my eye on you, Padawan.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] That's horrible! I didn't know!

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Perhaps it was Mandalorian raiders.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Shen and Rahasia have been granted asylum here at the Enclave until they can find a way to deal with their families. I hear you had something to do with that.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: It is the way of the Jedi to provide help to those in need, and you seem to have lived up to this duty. I congratulate you, Padawan.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: It is well that you are still alive, Padawan, in that you have not yet managed to fail us completely. Why is it that you are now bothering me instead of seeking out the Star Map?

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Sandral and Matale feud?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The Sandrals and Matales have been at odds ever since they came to this planet. And have been making my life difficult the entire time, as well.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Now Ahlan Matale accuses Nurik Sandral of stealing his son, Shen. Nurik Sandral's own son Casus has been missing for a while now. We do not know what has happened.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Ahlan is rash enough, and stupid enough, to start a war over any imagined slight. We would resolve this, but we have too few Jedi to spare. It must be resolved peacefully!

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Their estates are both located to the south of the Enclave - the Sandral fairly far. It would normally be your duty to assist in such matters, but your primary task takes precedence.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: If you are stuck on the planet for a while you may investigate. I would recommend starting at the estate of Ahlan Matale.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: You have a mission to attend to, Padawan. And as much as I may wish it otherwise, you are our only hope.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The Council has placed the fate of the galaxy within your hands. I pray both you and Bastila are able to emerge from this ordeal as servants of the light. May the Force be with you, young Padawan.

speaker: Player
text: I have found the body of the Jedi Nemo. He was slain by kath hounds.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Ah, Nemo. He was a brave and honorable man. He had great strength with the Force.

speaker: Player
text: His strength was not enough...

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: But remember your task, Padawan!

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I would not have thought that kath hounds alone would be able to overcome him. Perhaps there was more...

speaker: Player
text: It is a most grievous loss...

speaker: Player
text: What happened to Belaya?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: The Jedi Belaya would seem to have disappeared. She had a lesson scheduled with Master Zhar but did not show up.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I have heard someone say that she had been seen leaving the Enclave, but I do not know where she would have gone.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: If you meet her, you may want to ask her why she left. We do not force anyone to stay here, so do not think to take that route.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Is there anything else, then?

speaker: Player
text: I have slain Belaya on Korriban. She was a Dark Jedi.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: I find that... disturbing. It is our failings as teachers that enabled this to happen.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: Do not give in to the same dark urges as she did or you may suffer a similar fate.

speaker: Player
text: I am sorry, Master Vrook. I will go.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: As you strive to defeat our enemy, you must always guard against the enemy within yourself.

speaker: Player

speaker: Selkath Port Official
text: The other rule is also very simple - keep the peace. Here on Manaan we maintain a careful neutrality, and we react very harshly to people who jeopardize our neutral status.

speaker: Selkath Port Official
text: Any confrontations between the Sith and Republic are dealt with swiftly and decisively. Is this understood?

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

text: Don't be foolish, human! Of course we have laws against murder, theft and other crimes. But these laws are hardly different than those of any other planet.

speaker: Selkath Port Official
text: Manaan's neutrality is closely linked to our kolto production - that is why I made special mention of the laws regarding smuggling and keeping the peace.

text: How can you be neutral when the Sith are trying to conquer everything?

speaker: Selkath Port Official

speaker: Selkath Port Official
text: Should Manaan ever come under attack, we would destroy the supply of kolto and vanish beneath the oceans of our world. Even the Sith are not willing to risk the loss of a commodity as valuable as kolto.

speaker: Player
text: You seem to have it all worked out.

speaker: Player
text: That seems awfully short sighted...

speaker: Selkath Port Official
text: Your opinion is biased by your own alliances, human. Only we Selkath can best protect the interests of Manaan and Ahto city.

speaker: Player
text: Pathetic laws of pathetic fish don't concern me.

speaker: Selkath Port Official
