speaker: Zax
text: I've not seen you here before, human. You are new to the bounty office, yes? My name is Zax - I'm the one in charge here.

speaker: Zax
text: Are you looking for work? There are many bounties available here; legal and otherwise. But they all pay quite well.

speaker: Zax
text: Or are you here for information? Everyone knows I'm one of Davik's best agents... I'm the Hutt with all the answers.

speaker: Player
text: Gurney said I should speak to you about the rakghoul serum.

speaker: Zax
text: You have the rakghoul serum? It's worth 1000 credits to Davik.

speaker: Player
text: Why does Davik want the serum so badly?

speaker: Zax
text: Medicine is big business. If people are sick with the rakghoul disease they need the cure. Davik can charge anything he wants and people will still pay.

speaker: Player
text: Davik plans to prey on the sick? That's monstrous!

speaker: Zax
text: What do you care? You're not sick. You give me the serum, I'll give you 1000 credits. You won't get a better deal anywhere else.

speaker: Player
text: Here's the serum. Give me the 1000 credits.

speaker: Zax
text: Here's the credits. Davik will be very pleased when he see this. Very pleased, indeed. Now, what else do you need?

speaker: Player
text: I need some information.

speaker: Zax
text: I have information, but it's not free. For a fee I'll tell you everything you want about the street gangs, Davik - other stuff, too. But first you have to come up with 100 credits.

speaker: Player
text: Here's 100 credits.

speaker: Zax
text: Good. Now that you've paid the fee you can come back and ask questions anytime. You won't have to pay again; nobody ever said I wasn't a fair Hutt.

speaker: Zax
text: What do you want information on now? Gangs? Davik? Other stuff?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about those escape pods that crashed into the Undercity.

speaker: Zax
text: Escape pods? You shouldn't bother with them. When they crashed the Black Vulkar gang got there first and cleaned them out.

speaker: Zax
text: If there was anything valuable inside those crash pods it's inside the Vulkar base now.

speaker: Player
text: I need to get inside the Black Vulkar base.

speaker: Zax
text: Why? You need to get shot full of blaster holes? Only the Vulkars get into the Vulkar base... unless... maybe the Hidden Beks could help you out.

speaker: Zax
text: You got a problem with the Vulkars, you go see Gadon Thek. He's the leader of the Hidden Beks, a rival gang. He's a smart man - maybe he can help you.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Lower City gangs.

speaker: Zax
text: There are two main gangs - the Black Vulkars and the Hidden Beks. Used to be the Beks ran things, but now the Vulkars have a new leader. Brejik wants to take over for himself.

speaker: Zax
text: But the Vulkars are out of control now. They've sealed their base and they're shooting people in the streets. Sometimes they don't even pay Davik the money they owe him.

speaker: Zax
text: Things were much better with Gadon and the Beks in charge. Gadon's a smart man - he knows how to keep peace. Maybe if the Beks win this gang war things will go back to normal.

speaker: Player
text: I want information on something else.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Zax
text: Goodbye, human. You come back if you want to earn credits. Bounties pay good money. And remember to come see me if you want information.

speaker: Player
text: Is there some way I can get off this planet?

speaker: Zax
text: The Sith quarantine has grounded all the vehicles. Everyone wants to leave, but it's just not possible. Davik has the fastest ship in the sector, but even he can't get off the planet.

speaker: Zax
text: The Sith fleet is orbiting Taris, and they use auto-targeting cannons. If a ship takes off those cannons will disintegrate it instantly, unless it had broadcast the launch codes.

speaker: Player
text: Codes? What codes?

speaker: Zax
text: The Sith use launch codes when they leave the planet. If you transmit them from your ship, the auto-targeting cannons won't fire at you. Only people with the codes can leave Taris.

speaker: Zax
text: The codes were locked up in the military base, but somebody broke in recently. Maybe to steal the codes. But even if someone had the codes, how would they get a ship?

speaker: Zax
text: No, there's no way to get off Taris. You'd need a ship, the launch codes - and even then the Sith fighters would chase you down. We're all stuck here - even Davik.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Davik.

speaker: Zax
text: Davik's a busy man - he runs lower Taris. Before the Sith came he almost run Upper Taris, too. Extortion, slavery, smuggling; Davik controls it all.

speaker: Zax
text: He's part of the Exchange - a big intergalactic crime syndicate. You'd be smart to stay on his good side. Even the Sith know better than to pick a fight with Davik on Taris.

speaker: Player
text: I want to meet Davik.

speaker: Zax
text: Ha-ha-ha! You can't meet Davik. Nobody meets Davik unless Davik wants to meet them. Even I only meet Davik once, long ago.

speaker: Zax
text: He's the king of the Lower City - he doesn't just walk around here like you or me. Davik stays in his estate and works through agents, like that big Mandalorian Canderous Ordo.

speaker: Zax
text: But the Sith keep the codes locked up safe in the military base. Nobody gets in there - too dangerous. And even if someone did get the codes, where are they going to get a ship?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about something else.

speaker: Zax
text: Okay, human. What do you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the bounties.

speaker: Bastila

text: Well, it's my experience that the targets of these bounties are usually criminals, themselves. So don't get all in a twist over it.

text: I'll "get in a twist" if I think it is called for, Carth. I simply suggest we should use caution if we intend to participate in this... business.

speaker: Zax
text: There's two government contracts. One's an assassin named Selven, the other is Bendak Starkiller. He's a famous death-match duelist. Between them they've killed hundreds of people.

speaker: Carth
text: I can't see anything wrong with getting rid of people like that - as long as we don't end up on the list of their victims.

speaker: Zax
text: But not all the bounties are dangerous. Davik got some special contracts. One's for a girl named Dia - she attacked Holdan, one of Davik's men. Another's for a man named Largo who owes Davik money.

speaker: Carth
text: Okay, I don't know about Davik's special contracts. Justice is one thing, but doing a crime lord's dirty work is something else.

speaker: Zax
text: And then there's Matrik. He used to work for Davik, then he betrayed the Exchange and now Davik wants him dead. I'll put all this information in your datapad.

speaker: Player
text: I want more details on the bounties you're offering.

speaker: Zax
text: All the information is in your data-pad already, but if you don't want to look there then I guess I can fill you in. Who do you want to know more about?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the assassin Selven.

text: Is this a joke, human? We've already dealt with that bounty! Why are you asking about it now? It's over. Don't waste my time with old bounties!

speaker: Player
text: I have more questions about the bounties.

speaker: Zax
text: Okay, this is the bounty office, so it's the right place to ask about bounties. What's your question?

speaker: Player
text: Davik's bounties sound more like contract killings.

text: Davik works for the Exchange. They don't play games. If you don't pay your debts or you betray them or you attack them they get even. People bring Davik's bounty on themselves.

speaker: Zax
text: Anyway, if you don't like them you don't have to take them. Collect the other bounties - government contracts. Those people are ruthless killers. They need to be stopped.

speaker: Player
text: How do I collect the credits for these contracts?

text: It's simple - you find people, you kill them, you tell me, I pay you. I know everything that's going on in Taris. So if you kill one of them I'll know.

speaker: Player
text: I've got a bounty I want to collect on.

speaker: Zax
text: A bounty? Well, human, that is what I'm here for. Which bounty are you here to collect on?

speaker: Player
text: [Tell him about Matrik.]

speaker: Zax
text: The traitor Matrik is now a dead traitor. This is a lesson for anyone thinking about turning against the Exchange.

speaker: Zax
text: Here - 300 credits. That's the price for all bounties.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks. Pleasure doing business with you.

text: You do good work, human. There's lots of bounty hunters on Taris, but most are lazy. Maybe if you keep cashing in bounties they'll work harder.

text: [Persuade] I want 400 credits for this job.

text: Maybe I just won't pay you anything for this bounty? That would teach you some respect, wouldn't it? You want to reconsider and take the 300, human?

text: You can't talk to me like this!

text: Yes, I can, and there's nothing you can do about it. There's a security system in this building - you attack me and you'll be vaporised. Go away, human. Next time you'll know better.

text: [Lie: Tell him Matrik is dead.]

text: It's good Matrik's dead but maybe you went overboard, human. Next time use a blaster, not a bomb! Bombs are messy. But at least the job is done.

speaker: Player
text: [Tell him about Bendak.]

text: So, you killed Bendak in death-match duel. Ironic, isn't it? Bendak has a bounty on him for killing people in duel, and you collect it by killing him in a death-match.

speaker: Player
text: [Tell him about Selven.]

text: So Selven's dead. All the other bounty hunters who went after her ended up dead themselves, you know. You did well, human.

speaker: Player
text: [Tell him about Dia.]

text: Too bad. Dia was a nice girl. But she attacked Holdan, and Holdan works for Davik. That was just stupid.

speaker: Player
text: [Tell him about Largo.]

text: Largo should have known better than to run. Maybe now people will learn the lesson: you owe Davik money, you pay!

speaker: Zax
text: Selven's a government bounty; she's a very dangerous woman. When she started she was just another killer working for Davik. Then she began freelancing to the highest bidder.

text: One day she killed six citizens in the street... and their bodyguards, too. They were all Ulgos, a powerful merchant family with many enemies. Selven was hired to kill off the whole family.

speaker: Zax
text: She was very good at her job. Each day, more Ulgos died. Poisoned at home, shot down in the street; guards and droids couldn't protect them. After a month there were no Ulgos left on Taris. Not one.

text: Did they ever find out who hired Selven to kill them all?

text: It was never proven. But after the Ulgos were all dead, the Organa family demanded the government put out a contract on Selven. They said nobody was safe as long as Selven was still free.

speaker: Zax
text: But the Organa family were powerful rivals of the Ulgos. Some think they were the ones who hired Selven, then they tried to have bounty hunters kill her to keep the secret from coming out.

speaker: Zax
text: But Taris politics aren't your concern. You're just a bounty hunter. You kill Selven, you get the credits. That's the only important thing, right?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you about one of the other bounties.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Zax
text: Okay, but this is the bounty office. This is a place of business, so what kind of business have you got?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Bendak Starkiller.

speaker: Zax
text: Bendak's a government contract, but he's a legend on Taris. He started out as duelist in the Upper Cantina. He never lost, but he only fought death matches. He killed hundreds in his day.

speaker: Zax
text: Then death matches got banned. Duel rings switched to non-lethal combat. But Bendak wasn't ready to retire. He keep dueling on the illegal, underground circuit. He kept killing people.

speaker: Zax
text: Finally the government had no choice but to put a bounty out on him. But Bendak's a big folk hero, so not too many try to collect. Those who do all wind up dead, anyway.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about this girl Dia.

speaker: Zax
text: Wait - I almost forgot. That bounty's been pulled, human. Holdan told me he doesn't want her dead anymore. Sorry, no credits for Dia.

speaker: Zax
text: Dia's one of Davik's private bounties. She used be a waitress in the cantina here until she had a fight with Holdan. She cut him with her vibroblade, almost killed him. That was a mistake.

speaker: Zax
text: Holdan works for Davik, he's not one to let her get away with that. When he was recovering in the medical bay, he put out a bounty on Dia. She's been hiding ever since.

speaker: Player
text: I get the feeling there's more to this story.

speaker: Zax
text: Maybe. Doesn't really matter to me. I get the bounty from Davik's men, I don't ask questions. You can talk to Holdan if you want to know more - he's inside the cantina.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about this merchant Largo.

speaker: Zax
text: Actually, now that I think of it that bounty's no longer on the table. Davik told me Largo's bounty is off the table. I guess the merchant came up with the credits. Don't bother with that one anymore, human.

speaker: Zax
text: He's nothing special, just another of Davik's private bounties. He borrowed money from Davik for his business. But things went bad and he wasn't able to pay Davik back. So he ran.

speaker: Zax
text: Davik doesn't like it when people who owe him money run. He put out a contract on Largo to send a message to the other merchants who owe him money.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Matrik.

speaker: Zax
text: Davik is very interested in this bounty. Matrik used to work for Davik. He wasn't important, but he was there a long time. He saw lots of things that it was wise to keep quiet about.

speaker: Zax
text: Then one day he betrayed Davik. He went to the Taris authorities and testified at trials against the Exchange. Lots of people were arrested and Davik's operations shut down for a while.

speaker: Zax
text: It cost Davik thousands and thousands of credits to get business back on track, and he lost lots of good people. Of course he's not about to let Matrik get away with that.

speaker: Player
text: But didn't the government protect Matrik after the trials?

speaker: Zax
text: They hid Matrik for a while, but when the Sith took over they shut the witness protection program down. It's expensive, and the Sith didn't care if Matrik died.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] That seems a little high just for information. I'll give you 50 credits.

speaker: Zax
text: [Success] This Sith quarantine makes it hard to earn credits. And Davik gets mad when his agents don't bring in enough.

speaker: Zax
text: Okay, give me 50 credits. But don't tell anyone I gave you a deal or everyone will want a bargain and I'll go out of business.

speaker: Zax
text: [Failure] Sorry, human.  If you get a break on the price then I have to give everyone a deal. I won't let you whittle my prices down! If you can't pay, then I won't talk.

speaker: Zax
text: Maybe you could take some bounties and earn some money? Then you could afford to pay for my information. You're happy, I'm happy, Davik gets his cut... it works out for everyone.

speaker: Player
text: You work for Davik?

speaker: Zax
text: Not officially, no. I work for the bounty office. But Davik pays me to keep my eyes open and report to him... and for me to post his bounties.

speaker: Player
text: Davik posts bounties in a government office? Is that even legal?

speaker: Zax
text: I used to have to keep our relationship secret, but since the Sith arrived nobody cares what happens in the Lower City. Davik can do whatever he wants.

speaker: Zax
text: But enough talk - back to business. This is the bounty office, so we should talk bounties. Or are you looking for information?

speaker: Player
text: You don't try to hide the fact that Davik has you on his payroll?

speaker: Player
text: I can't afford that much.

speaker: Zax
text: Then we don't do business. Davik pays me to earn credits, not to answer questions. If you don't pay, then I don't talk.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going to pay just to ask you some questions.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I've got the serum, but I want 1500 credits for it!

speaker: Zax
text: [Success] You're brave, human, to bargain with a Hutt. But I like you. Okay, 1500 it is.

speaker: Zax
text: [Failure] You don't get to bargain with me! I make you an offer, and you take it or you don't. But you don't get to negotiate a new price!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'll just give the serum to Zelka.

speaker: Zax
text: Ha-ha-ha! Zelka can't pay you for the serum - he's broke! You go see Zelka. I'll be here when you come to senses and see that 1000 credits is better than no credits.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have the serum.

speaker: Zax
text: You find the serum, you come see me. Davik wants the serum, and I'll pay good money to get it for him. The same price as for the bounties.

speaker: Zax
text: Back again, human? I hope you didn't come just to chat. Davik hired me to do business and make credits, not to make small talk.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: The spies of Chuundar have followed you as closely as possible, <FullName>. They tell me you have killed the mad-claw.

speaker: Player
text: Take me up so I can speak with Chuundar.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: I will take you directly to him. He is waiting in the throne room.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not ready to go up. I'll be back later.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Very well. I will wait here for you to return.

speaker: Player
text: That mad-claw was Freyyr, Chuundar's father.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: That is not my concern, outsider. I serve Chuundar and no other.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: You! <FullName>! Our spies say that the mad-claw you were sent to kill is on his way to Rwookrrorro right now!

speaker: Gorwooken
text: You should have followed the will of Chuundar! Now you will face his wrath!
comment: Gorwooken and a group of wookie guards fight the player.

speaker: Cand
text: Now this is what I live for!

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Hello again, <FullName>. I've heard nothing of your progress, so I will assume there hasn't been any.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: I'll take you back to the surface, but you must do Chuundar's task. Don't keep him waiting.

speaker: Player
text: Just take me up for now.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: Very well. Just one moment.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to ask you some questions.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: I'll operate the basket, as Chuundar has commanded, but I won't answer your questions while I stand in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: This place is sacred ground. Many of my kind have proven themsleves here, and many have died as well.

speaker: Gorwooken
text: You aren't worthy of this place. I won't speak to you while we're here.

speaker: Christya
text: Wow, are you really a noble? You must be pretty rich, right? Is your family important?
comment: Christya has moved to Tap Room, player approaches.  She is talking to a man sitting at the bar.

speaker: Noble021
text: I can trace my lineage back five generations to one of the founding houses of Taris. In fact... uh, we seem to have some unexpected company, my darling.

speaker: Christya
text: Oh, don't pay any attention to him. He's just some Pazaak player I met. He's not an actual noble, like you! C'mon, sweetie... let's go back to your mansion.

speaker: Christya
text: I saw your match against Niklos. He doesn't lose very often. I bet you could make a lot of credits as a professional Pazaak player!

speaker: Christya
text: You know, you're my kind of guy; rich and handsome - just the way I like them. Why don't we slip away to the tap room together?

speaker: Christya
text: The bartender can mix us up something special for only twenty credits. If you play your cards right Pazaak might not be the only game you get lucky at tonight.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds good to me! Here's 20 credits.

speaker: Christya
text: I love a man who's not afraid to spend his credits! I'll meet you in the tap room. Don't be too long - I'm not a patient girl.
comment: Player loses 20 credits, Christya goes to Taproom.

speaker: Player
text: 20 credits? That seems expensive for a couple of drinks.

speaker: Christya
text: Well, I'm used to the finer things in life. I'm not about to lower my standards for any man. So how about it - you want me to get those drinks for us?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have that much on me.

speaker: Christya
text: Really? You must not be as good at Pazaak as I thought. Well, I'm not going to waste my time with some penniless gambler!

speaker: Christya
text: Suddenly I find you very boring. Maybe I can find someone more interesting in the tap room.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, not interested.

speaker: Christya
text: What's the matter, you shy? Suit yourself. I'll be here if you change your mind, just waiting for a nice, rich Pazaak player to come along...

speaker: Christya
text: I saw your match against Niklos - if you could even call it that. You aren't much of a Pazaak player, are you?

speaker: Christya
text: Don't you love watching the Pazaak players? All that strategy. All those credits... It's enough to make a girl get all flushed!
comment: Player has not played Pazzak, or player is female.

speaker: Elder Droid
text: Beep beep beep-oop!

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: This isn't good. I can't afford this.
comment: Initial selected or triggered by proximity This is the Captain of a group of three Czerka guards, all standing around a dead wookie. This character has a unique plot item on him. It is a Czerka Corp. Resource ID. It interacts with the Droid (Kas22_droid1_01) further up the path. It has the following description: Czerka Corp. Resource ID This is an electronic identification card for use in a Czerka Corp. Resource Droid. Such low maintenance droids are usually deployed in dangerous areas so that patrol groups can have access to emergency supplies. They are designed to shut down if tampered with, minimizing potential theft by unrecognized personnel.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: You think I can? Do you know what they get for a healthy one of these things?

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: We'll work it out later. We've got company.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: What do you want, spacer? I'm Patrol Captain Dehno and you're interrupting Czerka Corporation business.

speaker: Player
text: My name is <FullName>. What happened here?
comment: This question can only be asked once. Set a local so tit does not appear again. This local will also be used to filter another line further down. The "Do your superiors approve of you killing wookiees?" line.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: This Wookiee slave got a little... rebellious. We had to put it down.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You "put *it* down"? We're not animals!

speaker: Player
text: Zaalbar, let me handle this.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: But their disregard for the life of this Wookiee is too much!

speaker: Player
text: I have asked you to let me handle this. Honor my request.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will do so. For your sake, not theirs.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Careful now... that growl sounded pretty threatening. Keep your slave on its leash or we'll have another accident.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Just shut up, you trigger-happy idiot.

speaker: Player
text: Do your superiors approve of you killing Wookiees?
comment: This line needs to have a condition on it so that is only appears after the "What happened here?" line is asked by the player. This is because it is a mirrored link in the "second time talked to" starting condition.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: No, of course they don't. Why would you ask me that? Are you doing some sort of snap inspection?

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: You're trying to get me to admit to incompetence, aren't you? Not going to happen. I stand by my patrol.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: This Wookiee got out of hand and *had* to be put down. We'll find another easy enough.

speaker: Player
text: This may cost you more than you know, fool.
comment: This line only appears if the player HAS NOT been paid all ready. Set on "Now, if you don't mind, we have a patrol to get back to." line

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: It... is a bit costly. Look, why are you asking this?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] You know why. Hand over compensation or this gets reported.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: [Success] What... you're a Czerka inspector, aren't you! Slimy little... I've heard about these shake-downs.

speaker: Bastila
text: *whisper* I do not approve of this game you are playing! This Wookiee's death is a tragedy, not a chance for your profit.

speaker: Juhani
text: *whisper* The Jedi should be protectors of the weak! You shame us all by your actions here.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Give it up, men. If we don't pay this leech we'll get a black mark on our records a sunspot couldn't burn off.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: But I, I... if you say so, sir. I don't think we have enough... here.

speaker: Player
text: That will be fine. Thank you.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Yes, I'm sure it will be. If I see anything on our records I'll have you fed to a katarn. In bite-sized chunks.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You lied to gain profit from the death of this Wookiee? You may as well have killed him yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I can't change what they did. Why not profit?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You can't justify this. Don't try.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Uh, if we're done here, we have a patrol to get back to.

speaker: Player
text: Shut up. I do as I wish.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: So I see.

speaker: Cand
text: I like the way you handled that. Are you sure you don't have some Mandalorian blood in you?

speaker: Mission
text: I'm glad Big Z isn't here to see this. I don't know if he could handle it.

speaker: Carth
text: It's a good thing Zaalbar isn't here to see this. I doubt he'd approve of what you're doing. Actually, I don't know if I approve, either.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Now, if you don't mind, we have a patrol to get back to.
comment: Set local so special starting condition is used if player speaks to them again. Also stops the payment path from appearing again in secondary dialogue.

speaker: Player
text: I demand more!

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: You are making this difficult. You know, maybe it's too much trouble to pay you. Maybe there's a better way.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: I think this troublemaker needs an accident. In fact, I think this Wookiee attacked this fool and we arrived just a little too late to help.

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: I think this meatbag has hostile intentions, Master! This is going to be fun!

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Uh, Captain, we have blasters. Don't Wookiees use those bowcaster things?

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Would you just shut up and shoot?

speaker: Player
text: I'll just take it from your corpse then!

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: What the...? Blasters ready, men! This fool wants to die!

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: [Failure] What are you trying to get away with here? You can't just walk up and start demanding things.

speaker: Cand
text: And who are you to stop us, little man?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to pay me so this stays off your record.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: [Success] I... I think I should probably pay you so this stays off my record. Yes, that's best.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Uh, Captain.... what's going on? Is this one of those inspector shake-downs?

speaker: Player
text: I won't allow you to enslave or kill another Wookiee.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Is that a joke? Who do you think you are?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] This posting is trouble, friend. Get out while you can.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: [Success] You make some sense. I wonder, what do you know about what might happen here?

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Men, I think we should petition for a transfer. The corporation will survive a fight here, but us frontline guards won't.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: If... you say so, Captain.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Yes, I say so. Move out. This place just isn't worth the trouble.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Request a transfer. Move your patrol off-world.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: [Success] I... I think I should pull in some favors and... get us moved off-world, men.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Uh, are you all right, Captain?

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Are you questioning my orders? You don't want to do that.

speaker: Player
text: It doesn't matter. You won't enslave another wookiee!

speaker: Player
text: It doesn't matter. I'll end your miserable life where you stand!

speaker: Player
text: I don't actually care, one way or another.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Well... all right then. Carry on. We've work to do here.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Thanks for taking care of that, Captain.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: You shut up. I'm not done with you two.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Czerka Corp.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: The company has branches on many planets. I'm just a Patrol Captain. It's not my job to monitor it all.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: If you want quotes on policy, get someone else. I just escort the slaves and guard this area.

speaker: Player
text: I have questions about Kashyyyk.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: You mean Edean? Backwater world.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: There are a few patrols in the lower areas, but I haven't heard what they are after.

speaker: Player
text: I'm leaving. Never mind.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: Good. Watch yourself. These old paths are dangerous.

speaker: Player
text: Mind your place, Zaalbar! Remember your debt!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will honor my debt, but I can barely stomach this.

speaker: Player
text: Does this make you mad, Zaalbar? I bet it does.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: What are you getting at? Do you want these men dead? I would not need much encouraging!

speaker: Player
text: Control yourself. Let me take care of this.

speaker: Player
text: Do it. Kill them. We'll make them pay.

speaker: Juhani
text: You murdered him!

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: That's right! We had to do it and it shouldn't come out of our pay.

speaker: Bastila
text: Put it down? You... you murdered him?

speaker: Carth
text: Put it down? You killed him, you mean.

speaker: Player
text: Just hurry up and tell me what happened.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: What is it now? If you don't mind, I have important matters to discuss with my patrol.
comment: Secondary selected, player not paid, no resolution to plot yet.

speaker: Patrol Captain Dehno
text: What are you doing back here? Look, you got what you wanted, so just let us get back to corralling these animals.
comment: If player was paid for his silence

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: I'm sorry, I'm on duty, citizen. Please refer any questions to our diplomatic corp. Thank you.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Hey, there. Say - I don't recognize you... you must be one of those new lab techs, right? What are you doing over here on the mechanics' side of the building? You lost, rookie?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Can't say I blame you. They don't tell you new hires much, do they? Heh. Just throw you in the deep end and expect you to swim. Terrible way to run things, if you ask me.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: If you've got a question, just ask. I'll be happy to help. Don't be shy - the only stupid question is the one you don't ask. At least, that's what they say.

speaker: Player
text: Where are they keeping that prototype swoop engine accelerator?

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: The accelerator? It's down in the garage, of course. The service elevator is the only way in. But you lab techs aren't allowed down there.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: That's a restricted area. Only people with authorization cards, like us mechanics, can get past the laser cannons guarding the service elevator.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get a mechanic's authorization card?

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: All mechanics have to store their authorization cards in the locker room when we're off duty. That's the rule. My own card is locked up right now - I put it away as soon as my shift was over.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: And I'm not about to lend my card out to anyone. You know how much trouble we can get into if Brejik finds out we aren't keeping our authorization cards properly secured?

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Of course, not all the mechanics here follow the rules as closely as they should. I've even heard of a few guys trading their cards for a spice fix! Heh. Stupid addicts.

speaker: Player
text: You better go get me that card if you want to live!

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: You think just 'cause I'm a nice old man I can't defend myself? You got another thing coming, punk!

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Sure, I'll help you however I can. I remember what it was like my first day here.

speaker: Player
text: How can I get past the security system protecting the garage service elevator on the first floor?

speaker: Player
text: What's wrong with the heat in this place?

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: There's nothing wrong with the heating system. Brejik just yanked the magnetic power cell out. All you have to do is pop that cell back in and the system is up and running again.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: But until we figure out a way to make the heat work without disabling the thermal security system on the garage elevator, that cell's going to stay locked away in the Control Room.

speaker: Player
text: Time for you to die, old man!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Okay, then. If you need anything else, just come see me. I remember what it was like my first day.

speaker: Player
text: Could I borrow your authorization card?

speaker: Player
text: Give me your authorization card or I'll kill you!

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Hey, now - that kind of talk won't win you many friends with the other lab techs! Of course, the Vulkar gang members might take a shine to you.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: In any case, threatening me won't help you - I don't even have my card on me.

speaker: Player
text: Where is your card?

speaker: Player
text: I need information, so start talking or I'll put a blaster hole in your chest!

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Hey, now... no need to be that way! Leave the violence to the Vulkar gang members, okay? We mechanics and lab techs are more civilized than that, right?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry... wrong room. I'll be going now.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: No problem. I was always getting lost my first day too, rookie. I look forward to working with you.

speaker: VulkarMech01
text: Back again, rookie? How things going? Everyone treating you okay? Is there something you need?

speaker: Niklos
text: I do not lose at Pazaak very often, but you have made a habit of beating me. I think it is obvious what that means - you cheat!

speaker: Player
text: You can't make an accusation like that without proof!

speaker: Niklos
text: I haven't been able to figure out how, but I know you're cheating. I'm simply too good to lose this often. And I refuse to play Pazaak with a cheater.

speaker: Mission
text: Geez, what sore loser! I haven't seen this much whining since I gave Zaalbar that bath!

speaker: Niklos
text: You can leave now, cheater. I won't be wasting anymore time with you.

speaker: Player
text: It's not my fault you're bad at Pazaak.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be a sore loser. I just want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Niklos
text: You cheat me out of my hard earned credits, and you expect me to answer your questions?

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Niklos
text: Goodbye, cheater.

speaker: Niklos
text: If you ever wish to test yourself against the best Pazaak player on Taris, heh, you know where to find me.

speaker: Niklos
text: You were lucky to win the last match. But luck is no substitute for skill in Pazaak. If you are foolish enough to play me again I won't repeat the mistake of underestimating you.

speaker: Player
text: You think it was luck? Let's do it again!

speaker: Niklos
text: I'm going to enjoy relieving you of your credits almost as much as I'm going to enjoy humiliating you. Ha ha ha.

speaker: Player
text: Let's play.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Niklos
text: Questions? Heh. I don't come here to answer questions. If you want to play Pazaak, let's play. If not, then quit crowding my gaming table.

speaker: Player
text: I want to play Pazaak, but I don't have a deck.

speaker: Niklos
text: You don't even have your own deck? Then why are you bothering me? You can't play Pazaak without your own deck!

speaker: Niklos
text: If you're serious about Pazaak, go speak to old Garouk on the other side of the tavern. His gambling days are over, and he's looking to sell his deck.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Niklos
text: My name is Niklos. I'm the unofficial champion of the Pazaak circuit here on Taris. If you don't mind losing your wager we could play a few hands.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, not interested right now.

speaker: Niklos
text: Pazaak is not for everyone - it requires both nerve and skill. Perhaps you should practice before risking your credits against such a skilled player as myself. Heh heh heh. Unless you like losing?

speaker: Player
text: Deal the cards - I'm going to wipe that smirk off your face!

speaker: Niklos
text: Confidence is inspiring in one who has such a propensity for failure. Foolish, heh, but inspiring.

speaker: Niklos
text: What do you want? Have you come here just to bother me, or do you wish to test yourself against the best Pazaak player on Taris? Heh heh heh.

speaker: Niklos
text: I saw you getting a Pazaak lesson from that old fossil Garouk. Learning the rules of Pazaak is easy, but actually playing the game is a much greater challenge.

speaker: Niklos
text: Normally I wouldn't bother with a novice like you, but since Gelrood was banned for hustling cards I haven't been able to find a good game around here. Do you wish to play a hand?

speaker: Niklos
text: Back again? Well... do you have a deck yet? Would you like to play some Pazaak?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you again?

speaker: Player
text: I don't have a deck yet.

speaker: Niklos
text: You still don't have a deck? Then why are you bothering me? Until you get a deck from Garouk we have nothing to discuss.

speaker: Assault Droid
text: [The droid does not respond to you.]

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: We are watching you off-worlder... We know that you have had some influence in recent events...

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Obey our laws here on Manaan, off-worlder. A law-abiding visitor is a visitor that does not go to prison.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Move along, off-worlder. I've had enough of you.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: What do we have here? A lost off-worlder, perhaps? You're probably here for the swoop races. Track is through the west corridor. Get moving.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Wait, I recognize you. I watched you take top prize at the swoop tournament. Nice work, Sector Champion, but you haven't won me over.

speaker: Player
text: Could I ask you a few questions?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I'm no guide. The Sith don't suffer questions for long.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the swoop races?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Are you hoping that I will look more favorably on you because you have taken the Sector Champion title? You are mistaken.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I am fond of the sport, true, but it's more about hating racers I don't think should win than actually paying tribute to those I favor.

speaker: Player
text: Who do you like?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hukta Jax shows the proper spirit of competition, and it has brought him to the top before.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: The Gamorrean? You're joking.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Brute force to the finish, he's very efficient.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my first questions.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hurry it up. This is a poor use of my time. You should know not to annoy one of my kind.

speaker: Player
text: I wanted to ask questions about Manaan.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Then seek out a helpful fish for answers. I have no interest in the affairs of the Selkath and you have no reason to inquire about mine.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think I asked your opinion, Sith.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: What did you say? You don't want trouble from me, friend. You might as well take a blaster to your own head.

speaker: Player
text: You don't look so tough to me.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: So, you have some courage. Dumb as a B'omarr castoff, but you've got courage. What do you hope to accomplish with this threat?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Even if you expected to live through my attack, the Selkath would lock you up for fighting in their streets.

speaker: Player
text: I made no threat. I merely voiced an opinion.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Ah, so you wish to goad *me* into action so the Selkath turn their unyielding laws my way? Amusing. Perhaps you aren't so foolish.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You've made your jest on the one world where you would not be immediately struck down. I suggest you walk away while your assumption holds true.

speaker: Player
text: Then I will beg your pardon and leave.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I thought you might. Walk away. Now.

speaker: Player
text: I meant no harm. I apologize.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I'm sure you didn't. Walk away. Now.

speaker: Player
text: I have to leave. Goodbye.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Of course you do. Good riddance.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: What do I think? I think it's a shame when an unworthy newcomer unseats his betters. I am not easily won as a supporter.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I believe Queedle Molta has taken top spot. I prefer the professional racers. His win was just a fluke. An aberration.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I hate the rabble the races attract. They're always trouble.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: What do you want now? You press your luck, pestering a Sith soldier. It doesn't seem wise on your part.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Don't count on the small measure of celebrity you have attained at the swoop races. All are equally inferior before the Sith.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: As I have said in the past, the swoop races attract the lowest of rabble. As you are one of them, I suggest you leave me alone.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Did you hear what happened after the big swoop race? They say Brejik wouldn't pay up when he lost, and a brawl broke out! I can't believe I missed it!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Hmph - who dresses you? You look like you crawled up here from the Lower City. Oh well, I guess we can't all have style.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Isn't this band great? They can't leave Taris because of the Sith quarantine, so they've been playing here every night! Talk about a good break for us!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Hmph! I don't know what the guys in here find so attractive about those Twi'leks. Look at them - they're dressed like dirty little space wenches!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Did you hear? Bendak got dusted in that death match - by a woman, no less! Isn't that great? That should show these men a thing or two about who's the boss!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Did you hear the news? Bendak got dusted in that death match! I'll never get a chance to see something like that again. I can't believe I didn't get a ticket!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Have you heard? Someone's going to fight Bendak Starkiller in an illegal death match! I should go talk to that Hutt and try to get some tickets...

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Everyone's worried the Sith will come in here and shut this place down. Can you imagine how dull it would be if we didn't have any music on Taris?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Greetings once again, Revan. I am glad that you have returned. I couldn't believe that you had betrayed us, despite what the Council said.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: My name is Orsaa. I am the Keeper of History for the Elders. The last time you were here you had many questions for me.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The Council told us all of the destruction of your memories, but still I had hoped you might recall something of our past discussion.

speaker: Player
text: I wish I could remember, but I don't. Sorry.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: There is no need to apologize. It just pains me to know that all you had learned from me has been forgotten. Still, I would be happy to instruct you again.

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I do have a few questions for you.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Yes, of course. Although you must forgive me if some of this starts to seem familiar. After all, we did go into the history of the Rakata at some length the last time you were here.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: I will do my best to enlighten you with the knowledge I hold. What subject do you wish to learn about?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the beginnings of the Rakata Empire.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Long ago, we Rakata were a great space-faring people. Our ships combined techonolgy and the power of the Force, and we were able to pilot them to the farthest reaches of the galaxy.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Everywhere we went, we found civilizations less advanced and weaker then our own. But instead of helping them advance, we conquered and enslaved them.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Back then, we could still command the Force. That, combined with our advanced technolgy made our march of conquest irresistable. Soon the Infinite Empire stretched across the entire galaxy.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Over time, we lost our ability to use the Force. Some believe we had used the Force for so long that we evolved biologically, and became immune to its effects.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: In any case, once we lost our sensitivity to the Force our Empire began to fracture. We had to revert to more conventional space travel using inferior technology. Our ultimate collapse was inevitable.

speaker: Player
text: How did the Rakata Empire collapse?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Long ago the Rakata ruled all the known galaxy; all the species bowed down to us. But we were a corrupt people, and in our fall from glory there are terrible lessons that must be learned.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The Infinite Empire was built on slaughter; it was inevitable it should collapse upon itself. War, plague and slave rebellion forced us to retreat back here to our hidden home world.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Here, conflict among power-hungry warlords escalated into full civil war. Terrible weapons of mass destruction were unleashed, driving most of the Rakata far beneath the earth for shelter.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The devastation ravaged the world. Our people were scattered, our cities levelled, our very existence all but erased. The glory of the Infinite Empire is now nothing but dust and bones.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: In the past few thousand years small bands of Rakata have begun to return to the surface, but they are primitive and superstitious creatures. Only we Elders remember anything of the true past.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you about something else.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know how to disable the disruptor field that caused my ship to crash?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The disruptor field is one of the ancient defenses of the Star Forge; a great generator within the Temple of the Ancients fuels it. You will have to enter the Temple to disable it.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know where I can find parts to repair my ship?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We do not have what you need, but the tribe of the One often take pieces from the ships that crash onto the planet, though they do not understand the technology they are hoarding.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: You might find the parts you need in their camp, back towards the beach where your ship first crashed. Or you could try to salvage the parts you need from the wrecks scattered about the island.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks for the information. I guess I can kill you now!

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Guards! Guards! We are under attack!

speaker: Player
text: I have to go now.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Yes, of course. You have much to do, and little enough time to do it. But if you ever have any questions for me, I will be happy to try and answer them.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the tribe of Elders.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We Elders are descendants of the holy priest caste of the Infinite Empire, survivors of the terrible weapons unleashed by the warlords during the final collapse of our Empire.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Inside the Temple of the Ancients, our ancestors were safe from the devastation that forced the other Rakata to flee undergound. We emerged from the Temple to find an empty and ruined land.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: At last we understood the terrible power of our own technology. To ensure it could never be unleashed upon us again, we sealed the ancient knowledge within the Temple.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the other Rakata tribes here?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Many centuries ago, the other Rakata began to emerge from the underground warrens where they had sought shelter from the devastation of the warlords.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: But these Rakata were as violent as the warlords they had fled many millennia ago. After centuries of battle and bloodshed, the tribe of the One has emerged as the strongest of them all.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Now the One, lured by half-remembered legends of his people, lusts to possess the terrible power locked inside the Temple. We can never allow that to happen.

speaker: Player
text: Have you tried reasoning with the One?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: When the One first arrived on this island, we sent emissaries under a flag of truce to try and negotiate with his tribe. But all our envoys were brutally slaughtered.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We do have the technology to destroy the One and his followers. But if we kill them all, then we will only prove that we have learned nothing over the past 20,000 years.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The One is mad with power. We choose not to fight him, so our only course of action is to stay here in isolation where we are safe; just as we have done for the past 20,000 years.

speaker: Player
text: Can't you just use your technology to destroy the One?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We have the technology to destroy the One and his followers. But if we kill them all, then we will only prove that we have learned nothing over the past 20,000 years.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We tried to negotiate with them. We went emissaries under a flag or truce when the One first arrived on this island. But all our envoys were brutally slaughtered.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Temple of the Ancients?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The Temple is a sacred place of terrible secrets. All the dark mysteries of the Rakata are housed within its stone walls, which pulse with the living power of the Ancients.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Only those who can command this power - what you call the Force - can enter the Temple. Many centuries ago there were still a few among us who could pass within its walls.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: But living in the shadow of the Temple we became desensitized to this power. As you yourself said the last time you were here, we Elders are no longer 'Force sensitive'.

speaker: Player
text: Can any of the Rakata enter the Temple?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: None of the Rakata can control the Force now, but long ago there were those who could pass through the barrier.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Our ancestors created the energy shield around the building as a second line of defense. But the energy shield was created using technology within the Temple itself.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Once we helped you and Malak to get past the barrier, you discovered a way to lower the shields at will from within the Temple itself. After this you had no further need of us.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: The once hallowed ground of the Temple is now overrun with the followers of Malak who can command the Force: those you call the Dark Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: So why is there an energy field outside the Temple then?

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me about the Star Forge?

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Much of our knowledge of the Star Forge is lost. It was built during the height of the Infinite Empire, long ago. All we know now is that it casts a terrible shadow across our world.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: We Elders have longed to destroy the Star Forge for many generations, to cleanse ourselves of its evil presence. But we have neither the knowledge, nor the capability.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: When you and Malak last came here, we saw you as saviors. We let you into the Temple so you could destroy the Star Forge, but instead you harnessed its dark power for yourselves.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: You awakened a dormant evil, your fleet helped spread the corruption of the Star Forge throughout the galaxy. And now you return as our last hope to stop what you once started.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe later.

speaker: Player
text: Look on the bright side: we can have all those discussions again.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Yes, I suppose that is true. As you can imagine, I have few opportunities to share my knowledge with those outside our enclave.

speaker: Player
text: You're a historian? Maybe I could ask you some questions.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, I don't remember you.

speaker: Keeper Orsaa
text: Yes, Revan. What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to kill you all!

speaker: Chorrawl
text: I am done with you, outsider. Go away. I won't be your entertainment.
comment: Pissed off at player, set on "Go away, rabid fool. I won't listen to you anymore." line and "You disgust me. Your scent poiso..." line.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: What do you want, outsider? I won't let you follow us on our hunt. Chorrawl is not here for your amusement.
comment: Initial selected or proximity initiated This wookie is one of five that are hunting katarn in the area between the village and the basket to the shadowlands. They are standing amidst some dead Katarn This character has a second version that replaces this one after the player has helped Freyyr. See kas22_wooka1_02

speaker: Player
text: Don't test me, Wookiee. I go where I wish.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: You can't push me into battle, outsider. I know what happens to Wookiees that are said to be "difficult."

speaker: Chorrawl
text: I won't be your trophy, dead or as a slave. Leave me. You have no place here.

speaker: Player
text: I am <FullName>, and I act for Chuundar.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Chuundar! Bah! Why should I care if you act for him when he does not act for us?

speaker: Player
text: Explain what you meant by that.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: No, not to you. You are an outsider and only care about our weaknesses. I won't say anything to you.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Just a few questions. I'm a friend.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: [Success] Hmm... only a moment, outsider. I won't be this patient for long.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know of a crazed Wookiee in the Shadowlands?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: The only crazed creature I know of is one of your kind, outsider, not mine. We see him from time to time.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: We leave him alone. He has our respect because he has braved the lands alone. Sometimes he helps lone travelers. He is crazy, though.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph! I merely have an appreciation for solitude.
comment: indignant. Doesn't like being this fabled hermit they keep speaking about.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Ha! You claim to be a legend, but I'd know the mad hermit if I saw him. 3-meters tall, with eyes of madness.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of Chuundar?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: He is our Chieftain and will be obeyed. That is our way. Whether I trust what he says or not doesn't matter.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: In time, someone will replace him. For better or worse, I don't know. That will be for Bacca to decide.

speaker: Player
text: How will Bacca decide? What does that mean?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Bacca was our greatest warrior. His ancient sword is the tool of ascension, the mark of a chieftain.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Chuundar no longer displays it, not since he took the role of chieftain years ago. If someone else could produce it...

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Bah! I talk like a mere child! This is foolishness.

speaker: Player
text: Could a blood relative of Chuundar challenge him?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: It truly would take Bacca's Blade for that to happen. Chuundar is the last member of his family.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: There were others, but they were marked with madness. We don't speak their names. They are without honor.

speaker: Player
text: How has Kashyyyk fared under the Czerka Corporation?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: You taunt me with a foolish question like that. How do you think? My people go missing or die.

speaker: Carth
text: Why not do something about it, then?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: We can't fight back. Chuundar has bartered to reduce the slaves taken, but if any Czerka die, it increases again.

speaker: Mission
text: Big Z once told me he had seen paradise destroyed by the greed of outsiders. I never understood what he meant until now.

speaker: Player
text: I seek an ancient Star Map. Have you seen it?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: I don't concern myself with outsider toys. Search where you will, I'm not wasting my time.

speaker: Player
text: I will leave you now.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Yes, go, and don't expect a friendly welcome if you return. This world is my home, not yours.
comment: Set local that says he is pissed.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: How has my world fared? It is slowly dying.

speaker: Juhani
text: Why do you not do something about this tyranny, then?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Our finest warriors hunt the Shadowlands in groups, yet he lives there alone. Avoid him. Madness is to be feared.

speaker: Player
text: How long has he been down there?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Many years. It is impossible to know how many. A decade? Two? Perhaps he can answer your questions. Or kill you.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: [Failure] You Czerka slavers, caring about nothing except what you want... what you can take!

speaker: Chorrawl
text: You disgust me. Your scent poisons the air. Your feet foul the ground. Go away, outsider. Go away.
comment: Set local that says he is pissed.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I want you to answer my questions.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: [Success] I... I should answer your questions... yes, perhaps one or two.

speaker: Player
text: Show me proper respect or you'll regret it!

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Your kind threaten my very planet. I live with it daily. Why should your words now goad me into battle?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: No, I won't fight you. At best, my warrior comrades would slaughter you, only for ships to burn our homes later.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Go away, rabid fool. I won't listen to you anymore.
comment: Set local that says he is pissed.

speaker: Player
text: I will leave you then.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: You do that. Walk quickly, outsider. Kashyyyk fights back, even if we can't.

speaker: Player
text: Could I ask some questions?

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Why would you listen to me? Your kind have only been interested in caging or killing us.

speaker: Player
text: I don't mean you any harm.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Feh! I'll believe that when our planet is free of you. Your kind are here only to take or destroy.

speaker: Chorrawl
text: Why do you bother us again, outsider? We have nothing to say to you.

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: Davik says you missed your last payment.

speaker: Bountyhunt023
text: Davik doesn't like you missing payments!

speaker: Bulliedmer021
text: Here - I've got fifty credits! A down payment. That should buy me some time, right?

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: Sorry, you're out of time. Now it's all or nothing. Davik can't have people not paying his debts!

speaker: Bulliedmer021
text: But I don't have that much! How can I give you credits I don't have?

speaker: Bountyhunt023
text: That's too bad. Davik's going to want to make an example of you! You're coming with us.

speaker: Bulliedmer021
text: No - help! Somebody help! They're going to kill me!

speaker: Carth
text: *whisper* I know we have to be careful about drawing attention to ourselves, but are we just going to let them drag this guy off?

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: Hold on a second. Looks like we got ourselves a witness here!

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: What's the matter, you forget the arrangement? You Sith don't bother us on Davik's business and we don't bother you!

speaker: Player
text: I'm ordering you to leave this man alone.

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: We take our orders from Davik, not you!

speaker: Player
text: It's time for a new arrangement!

speaker: Bountyhunt023
text: Guess we have to teach you to mind your own business!

speaker: Player
text: Sorry. I'll be going now.

speaker: Bountyhunt023
text: Smart move to mind your own business.

speaker: BountyHunt022
text: Come on. We don't want to keep Davik waiting - that's only going to make things worse.

speaker: Bountyhunt023
text: Davik doesn't like witnesses.

speaker: Player
text: Leave this man alone or you'll have to deal with me!

speaker: Player
text: I don't like your attitude. I better teach you a lesson.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: No... that is not the one. My ancient sword is black as the night sky... I remember now.
comment: the only thing that needs changing here is the script k_pkor_shadegood... that needs to have a visual effect added over the coffin (the shade lord is 'redeemed') and XP added to the player.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... I am sorry...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Yes... that is the one. That is the blade that destroyed me.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Take it... take it and the other blades, even... take them and go. My darkness awaits me...

speaker: Player
text: There's no need to remain here, is there?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: No... need? What choice have I?

speaker: Player
text: You can return to the light side and end your torment.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Return? But... I betrayed my old masters. They would never let me return to the light side. It is too late... too late...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I don't believe the light side would turn you away. You have suffered long enough.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: [Success] If... if I could return. Oh, my Master... it has been... so long... and I regret so much...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: [Failure] No... I... do not think so. I have the eternity... I deserved. I made my choice long ago.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Be at peace...

speaker: Player
text: And suppose you are right. What then?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Then I have... the eternity I deserved. It has taken me... so long to realize that. I made my choice long ago.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps you are right. I'll go.

speaker: Player
text: You can leave this place.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: No, I cannot. Here... here is where I rest. Here is where my eternity awaits.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know. I'll go.

speaker: Player
text: I want to know more about the Star Map.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Our... oldest secret is buried, but not here. I... remember nothing else. I cannot help you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't believe that. Tell me what you know!

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I shall not tell you... our oldest secret! I shall not! Begone!

speaker: Player
text: I command you to tell me!

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Never! I shall... destroy you first! Die here... remain forever with me!

speaker: Player
text: What a disappointment. The 'great Ajunta Pall'.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Then feel my power! You shall... die here, with me!!

speaker: Player
text: Fine, I'll go.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Take the blades and leave me to my darkness...

speaker: Player
text: You're a pathetic excuse for a Sith Lord if I ever saw one.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Do not... do not say such things! I... still have power! Go! Go from my... ancient tomb!

speaker: Player
text: I might think more of you if you told me about the Star Map.

speaker: Player
text: I'll go, then.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Do not let the dark flame guide you, young one...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Too long... too long in the cold and the dark. I am disturbed again? A human...
comment: when the gong is rung, the Sith Lord Shade should spawn in and initiate dialogue with the PC. There is only one starting condition. There are only two valid endings near the bottom of his dialogue... one is where he goes hostile and fights the party (the piece of the Old Key should spawn into the sarcophagus when he is dead) and one where he returns to the Light Side, disappears and the key is spawned into the sarcophagus as above.

speaker: Bastila
text: What is this? A... spirit, full of the Force. Be careful. I sense an extremely old and confused mind behind this presence...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Do... I know you? It... seems as if we have met before...

speaker: Player
text: Er... no, I don't think we have ever met...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Are you certain? You... the Force is with you. So strong, so bright. You remind me of... someone I once knew, so long ago...

speaker: Player
text: Who... or what... are you?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... had a name, once. Ajunta Pall. Yes, that was my name. I was one of many. We were servants of the dark side... Sith Lords, we called ourselves. So proud.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: In the end we were not so proud. We hid... hid from those we had betrayed. We fell... and I knew it would be so...

speaker: Player
text: You were a Sith Lord? From the ancient times?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Ancient? Has it been so long that you use the word 'ancient'? I have... been here so long, so lost, I cannot... cannot remember...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: We were the first. The first to rebel, to betray... to surrender ourselves to the dark side. So strong, we thought... so wrong...

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by 'those we had betrayed'?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Our Jedi Masters. Those who had taught us to use the Force... who warned us against the dark side. Yet we embraced it in secret, reveled in its power.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: We were... discovered? Or did we act? I can no longer remember. But here is where we came... to hide, to grow. And here we fell.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about this place?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Our temple... our tomb. Built far from our enemies. We revered power and threw off the teachings of our old masters.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: It... we were not the first to fall to the dark side. But we... had more power than those before us. It... came from elsewhere...

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean? Came from where?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Our oldest secret. Only... only we would know, we lords. Only we would know where our power came from...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Tell me the secret.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: [Failure] I cannot, human. It is a secret of so long ago... I no longer remember. You who bristle with the Force... you must find this place...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Or... have you? Or did you? Or... will you? Oh, so... many images...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... see your dark heart, human. Dark as mine was, proud as mine was. You... you will find the old place... and you will regret it.

speaker: Player
text: I shall regret nothing.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: So much power... it is blinding. I...I remember so little...

speaker: Player
text: How did you fall? What happened?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: We... hid from the Jedi, but it was not they who destroyed us. Is it not... obvious what we did?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: We destroyed each other. We desired the secrets of each other, to increase our power... we battled until finally our fortress rained down on top of us.

speaker: Bastila
text: The ancient Sith... destroyed each other. The fundamental flaw in their philosophy, one would think.

speaker: Carth
text: I suppose that's the nature of the dark side. Power, but no longevity. Eventually it just consumes itself.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: And so here our old secret is buried and none of us hold it any more... is that not right? Our power fled. Oh, what became of us? Do... do the Sith still thrive? Did they ever return?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith fled, yes. And they returned.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: So much... so much time has passed. And yet we have learned nothing... nothing...

speaker: Player
text: Why do you remain here?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Remain? Do I... remain? I... have regretted for so long... all that I have done.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: My sword... I filled it with my pride. And it is... buried with me, now. A corpse as I am a corpse.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I am dead, as my faith... is dead. And I shall remain here... surrounded by blackness in death as in life...

speaker: Player
text: I feel sorry for you.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Most of my brethren would desire... only to take what power I have left. Even if it would destroy them.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I wish my sword to be... taken away from here. I do not wish it to rot away as I have. I command this of you.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. I'll gladly take it out of here.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: There are... three blades within my sarcophagus. Only one is truly my sword, but it has been so long... I do not remember which.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Find the sword that is mine and... place it on the statue. If it is truly mine, then it is yours.

speaker: Player
text: And if the sword isn't yours?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Then you must... die. This is how it... must be.

speaker: Player
text: How will I know which sword it is?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I do remember one thing of my sword... listen to me carefully...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: "I am that which grips the heart in fright, hearkens night and silences the light." It was... written of my sword long... long ago.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Go, then... find my sword and place it on the statue...

speaker: Player
text: What do you want me to do with it?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: If... if you are wise, you will not keep it. In the end, it is what destroyed me...

speaker: Player
text: Sorry... nobody commands me to do anything.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Then you shall not leave this place. I... have power, still. I can... still command!

speaker: Player
text: I need this sword you speak of.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: Of course you do. You... seek my power. Will it destroy you... as it did me?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I should just be on my way, then...

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... cannot allow you to leave. Not until you have... done what I will ask of you.

speaker: Player
text: What about your sword? Do you still have it?

speaker: Player
text: This secret... is it the Star Map?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... I do not remember. A map? Perhaps it is a map. But it has not been buried with me. All I have now is my sword.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith have thrived and are more powerful than ever.

speaker: Player
text: The dark side will always thrive. You should know that.

speaker: Player
text: They returned, and endanger us all... and the light side must battle them.

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. The Sith consumed themselves, did they? Hm. I suppose that eventually that'd be all they'd have left to fight.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: I... see your heart, human Jedi. I see your power, your pride. You... you will find the old place, the dark place... and you will regret it.

speaker: Player
text: Why? What is at this place?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Tell me the secret.

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: [Failure] The Force no longer touches my mind, human. And... even if it did I, I no longer remember our secret. The Force bristles in you... you must find this place with it...

speaker: Player
text: Are you... Ajunta Pall?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Yes, of course. Don't you remember me?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: [Success] I do... and yet I do not. The Force is so strong with you, human... yet the face, the soul... it has been so very long...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I was here once before, I think. Do you remember me?

speaker: Spirit of Ajunta Pall
text: A... Jedi? Here? Why have you come to this dark place, Jedi? Why... disturb my sleepless rest?

speaker: Player
text: I am not a Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: Disturb your rest? Are you some kind of... ghost?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Jolee
text: Now this you don't see every day. This... this is an old spirit full of the Force. I sense great sadness and regret. Walk carefully...

speaker: Juhani
text: Beware this... this spirit. It may not be what it appears. Great emotion lies within...

speaker: HK47
text: Analysis: This emanation barely registers on my sensors, master. Blaster fire may be ineffective... but I am prepared to test that at your word.

speaker: Larrim
text: Good day, officer. Don't mind me, I'm just standing here minding my own business. I'm not looking for any trouble with the Sith.

speaker: Larrim
text: Well, I don't see too many of your kind around here. Most of the residents in this run down old apartment are illegal aliens. My name is Larrim, by the way.

speaker: Player
text: Pleased to meet you, Larrim. My name is <FullName>.

speaker: Larrim
text: I know it's really none of my business, but you look like someone who might need to purchase one of those new energy shields. They're the latest thing, you know. Very high tech.

speaker: Player
text: What's so great about these energy shields?

speaker: Larrim
text: When you use one it surrounds you with a radiant aura-particle mesh that absorbs blaster bolts. Pretty handy in a fight. The shield even protects against lightsabers, or so I hear.

speaker: Larrim
text: The shields aren't perfect, of course. They can only absorb so much energy damage before they burn out, and ion blasters will take your basic dueling shield down pretty quick.

speaker: Carth
text: And I can tell you from experience that they aren't any good at all against a simple vibroblade. That's why the Republic has been training soldiers in hand-to-hand and melee combat.

speaker: Player
text: Where did this technology come from?

speaker: Larrim
text: I've heard rumors of the Echani using shields like this, but I never saw anything like them around here. Not until the Sith came. Where they discovered the technology is anybody's guess.

speaker: Larrim
text: The shields are too rare and too expensive to hand out to an entire army, but a shielded strike team can take out a whole battalion of soliders armed with conventional blasters.

speaker: Larrim
text: It gave the Sith a huge edge in the early battles, but it wasn't long before the Republic was able to copy the technology and come up with energy shields of their own.

speaker: Larrim
text: Now both sides are scrambling to come up with new weapons to slice right through the shields, but until they do you're going to see melee combat coming back to the forefront in this war.

speaker: Player
text: Anything else?

speaker: Larrim
text: Not much more to say, really. Except that I've managed to get my hands on one of those shields. It isn't cheap, but it could mean the difference between life and death.

speaker: Larrim
text: You want to see what I have in stock? I know my kiosk isn't much to look at, but my prices are reasonable and the merchandise is sound.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you have a kiosk set up here?

speaker: Larrim
text: I run a little shop here in this old building, selling basic equipment to the illegal aliens renting out these apartments.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned something about illegal aliens living here.

speaker: Larrim
text: By law, most aliens aren't allowed to have a residence in the Upper City of Taris. They allow a few of us Twi'leks up here, but for the most part it's humans only.

speaker: Larrim
text: But no self-respecting Upper City human would want to live in the apartments in this dump. So the landlord has been renting out the apartments illegally to aliens.

speaker: Larrim
text: Better than letting them sit empty, I guess. Otherwise you get squatters and people hiding out from the authorities living in the abandoned apartments, and they don't pay rent.

speaker: Player
text: Aren't you worried about getting caught?

speaker: Larrim
text: The Taris authorities pretty much turned a blind eye to this place. A few illegal aliens just weren't worth the bother. And once the Sith took over, they felt the same way.

speaker: Larrim
text: Besides, I don't live here myself. I just run a small business providing supplies to the residents. You want to see what I have in stock?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Larrim
text: Questions? I'd rather not. It might be bad for business if people saw me answering a bunch of questions for a human.

speaker: Larrim
text: Most of the residents here are illegal aliens, questions are frowned on. I don't want to lose the trust of my customers. If you really need information, go talk to Kadir the janitor.

speaker: Larrim
text: He's bordering on senile so all the residents figure he's harmless. They won't mind you talking to him, and he might be able to help you out with your questions.

speaker: Player
text: Let me see what you've got for sale.

speaker: Larrim
text: No problem. Just step on up and have a peek.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Larrim
