text: See you around. Come on back if you need any equipment. I've got some merchandise you might be interested in.

speaker: Player
text: I've heard enough about these shields.

speaker: Larrim
text: Oh, okay. Well then, you might be interested in knowing I have one for sale. It isn't cheap, but it could be the difference between life and death.

speaker: Larrim
text: And they aren't any good at all against a simple vibroblade. That's why the Sith and the Republic are training their troops in hand-to-hand and melee combat.

speaker: Player
text: I know all about energy shields.

speaker: Player
text: I don't care what your name is... and I'm not telling you mine!

speaker: Carth
text: Look, I know we're trying to keep a low profile but this kind of attitude will draw attention we don't need.

speaker: Larrim
text: Hey, I wasn't trying to pry or anything. I know people here like their privacy. It's just that I might be able to help you out.

speaker: Larrim
text: Back again? So, what can I do for you? You want to see what I have in stock?

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: The village of Rwookrrorro is now under the joint protection of chieftain Chuundar and Czerka Corporation. All further interaction by outsiders is forbidden.

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: I think you will agree that now that we have achieved such an optimal business arangement, we don't wish to risk further instability.

speaker: Player
text: What if Zaalbar has something to say about this?

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: I would assume that he has very little to say, or he would have said it before.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have made my peace with Chuundar. I see that his way is best. You showed me that. There is nothing here for me anymore.

speaker: Player
text: What are your plans now?

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: I am merely a guard. You will have to address any further concerns with Janos back at the outpost docking port.

speaker: Player
text: What if I don't approve of this?

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: Then you shouldn't have helped to make it happen. It is far too late for such a confrontational tone. Please, address further concerns with Janos.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: Czerka Corporation welcomes your future inquiries... through the proper channels.

speaker: Rwookrrorro Guard
text: Take your concerns to Janos at the docking port. Rwookrrorro is under the joint protection of Chuundar and Czerka Corporation.

speaker: Redros
text: You had an impressive run there, rookie. But it wasn't good enough, was it?

speaker: Redros
text: Anglu's already got you beat. It takes more than a souped up swoop bike to make a champion, so I guess I'm going to have to win this thing for Vulkars!

speaker: Redros
text: I'm twice the rider you'll ever be, rookie! You can go out there for another run if you want, but why bother? You'll never match the time I posted!

speaker: Redros
text: Another rookie on the track, eh? Give you punks a helmet and a swoop bike and suddenly you all figure you're racers.

speaker: Redros
text: But the only reason you're here is because I passed on that prototype accelerator. It's too unstable, and you can't collect the champion's prize if you're dead!

speaker: Redros
text: But judging by the look of you I'd say I don't have much to worry about. The Beks are really scraping the bottom of the barrel now.

speaker: Redros
text: I figured you weren't nothing special, rookie. And after watching your last run I see I was right.

speaker: Redros
text: You again? Look, I plan on winning this thing so I can't be wasting my time talking to some rookie!

speaker: Lorgal
text: Yes, human? Have you come to sneer and jeer like the others? Come to see Lorgal the Great Liberator caged like an animal?

speaker: Player
text: Liberator? You're nothing but a murderer!

speaker: Lorgal
text: Kill a million people with a mighty star cruiser and you are a war hero. Kill a hundred with a thermal detonator and you are a terrorist.

speaker: Player
text: It's not the same! You kill civilians and children!

speaker: Lorgal
text: You are obviously blind to the Republic chains shackled around your neck. You cannot see me for the hero I am; you think I am nothing but a criminal who deserves death.

speaker: Lorgal
text: There are many who want me dead, including the guards in this room. But the Republic doesn't kill prisoners without a trial. That is why I am protected.

speaker: Lorgal
text: This energy cage keeps me safe from blaster and blade. The Republic will keep me alive for transfer to Coruscant, and then all the galaxy will witness my trial!

speaker: Lorgal
text: You cannot touch me in here, human. No conventional weapon can penetrate this cage. Nothing can stop me from spreading my manifesto during my trial!

speaker: Player
text: [Use Force Choke to kill Lorgal.]

speaker: Player
text: [Use Force Kill to kill Lorgal.]

speaker: Player
text: I've got better things to do than argue with prisoners.

speaker: Lorgal
text: Yes, leave me. You are a tool of the Republic, a slave who cannot even see your own chains. But do not fear: someday I - or someone like me - will destroy the Republic and free you all.

speaker: Player
text: You deserve to die for your crimes, Lorgal.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to kill you, Lorgal. And I think I'll enjoy it.

speaker: Carth
text: It's done. Bastila is dead.

speaker: Carth
text: Soon the Republic fleet will break through and the capital ships will be able to bombard the Star Forge. Then it will finally be over.

speaker: Player
text: You could still save yourself, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: There's no point. There's no other place I'd rather be than here.

speaker: Carth
text: You're very brave to make the decision you did. I... I love you. You know that, right?

speaker: Player
text: I love you too.

speaker: Carth
text: There isn't much time. It should be over soon.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you, Carth. For everything.

speaker: Player
text: I just wish we had more time.

speaker: Carth
text: This is all the time we have. It should all be over soon.

speaker: Player
text: We could still leave, Carth, go somewhere...

speaker: Carth
text: You know that can't happen. There's no turning back for you... there's just an ending.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure this is the best way?

speaker: Carth
text: It's the only way. The only alternative is a path I know you don't want to take.

speaker: Carth
text: We have to kill her! Her Battle Meditation is the only thing stopping the fleet from getting through!

speaker: Carth
text: There you are! What happened?

speaker: Player
text: Darth Malak is dead. It's over, finally.

speaker: Bastila
text: That's wonderful news!

speaker: Bastila
text: There's no time to celebrate just yet. I was able to use my Battle Meditation to allow the Republic to break through the Sith fleet. The capital ships are in bombardment range!

speaker: Carth
text: And that means we have to get out of here right now, before this entire complex comes down around our ears! Everyone else is already on the ship! Let's move!!

speaker: Carth
text: No time to celebrate just yet. With Bastila dead, the Republic has broken through the Sith fleet! The capital ships are in bombardment range!

speaker: Carth
text: That's great news! I knew you could do it!

speaker: Player
text: There was no way to turn him to the light side. I had to kill him.

speaker: Bastila
text: I don't think anyone actually expected that he could be redeemed. I'm surprised you would even think of trying.

speaker: Carth
text: I don't think anyone actually expected that he could be redeemed. I'm surprised you would even think of trying.

speaker: Player
text: I killed him... and a lot of help you were, by the way.

speaker: Carth
text: Hey! I was doing what I could, thank you very much!

speaker: Carth
text: So you killed Darth Malak. Somehow I... I always knew you would.

speaker: Player
text: Carth?! How did you get here?!

speaker: Carth
text: The Republic fleet picked me up from the planet. I told them of your betrayal... but I also told them I couldn't abandon you.

speaker: Carth
text: I had to come. I said I'd find a way to save you from yourself, and I will.

speaker: Player
text: It's good you came. I'll enjoy killing you.

speaker: Carth
text: I don't believe that. I don't think you do, either.

speaker: Bastila
text: Carth. I knew I sensed your presence. I should have known you would find a way to meddle in this one last time!

speaker: Carth
text: Don't interfere, Bastila. This is between me and Revan.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are a fool. Revan has already made her choice, and there is no turning back!

speaker: Bastila
text: Don't listen to him, master! Let me strike him down! Seize your victory!!

speaker: Player
text: No, let him speak. I want to hear what he has to say.

speaker: Carth
text: I love you. Even now. Even after... after...after all you have done. I love you like I haven't loved anyone or anything since my wife died. And I didn't even think that was possible.

speaker: Carth
text: You may not love me. You may not love anything anymore now that you've gone over to the dark side... but I believe that there's still some part of you I can reach.

speaker: Carth
text: There's a part of you that believes in hope... and mercy... and love. And that part knows that it will soon be gone forever.

speaker: Bastila
text: Your words are meaningless. You have no idea of the power we now wield! Revan will rule the galaxy!!

speaker: Player
text: It's not too late for you to join me, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: No, it's too late for that. And it's too late for you to turn back... but you can end this here. There's still time for one final act of redemption.

speaker: Carth
text: Kill Bastila. Without her Battle Meditation the Republic fleet can destroy the Star Forge and rid the galaxy of this evil.

speaker: Player
text: And what happens to me?

speaker: Carth
text: Stay here on the Star Forge. With me. We won't have time to get off before the Star Forge is destroyed, not if you stop Bastila. But our sacrifice can save the Republic.

speaker: Carth
text: If you don't, all you'll have is...is emptiness and darkness. You don't want that. Please don't want that. Stay... let's end this now. Together.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be stupid. I could never agree to that.

speaker: Carth
text: I wish... I wish there could have been another way.

speaker: Bastila
text: Kill him, Master!!

speaker: Bastila
text: The fool is dead. Now there is nothing in the way of your victory!

speaker: Player
text: I think it's time to end this, all right... with your death.

speaker: Player
text: I... alright. I'll do it. For you.

speaker: Bastila
text: No! I won't let you do this! Don't be a fool, Revan!!

speaker: Player
text: I... am *not* Revan!!

speaker: Bastila
text: No! No-ooo!! You can't do this! Not when we're so close!!

speaker: Player
text: You could join us, Bastila. Turn away from the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Time for this to end, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: You're mad!

speaker: Player
text: That will never happen. Bastila... kill him now.

speaker: Player
text: It's too late to turn back, Carth. Even if I wanted to.

speaker: Carth
text: I know. It's too late to turn back... but you can end this here. There's still time for one final act of redemption.

speaker: Player
text: Kill him, Bastila. He means nothing to me.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, kill him. Nothing he could say will matter.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth. It's too late. We both know that.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad I get to kill you personally, Carth. For old times' sake.

speaker: Player
text: I don't need you, Carth, and I won't change my mind.

speaker: Player
text: You should have stayed wherever you ran to.

speaker: Carth
text: And abandon you? No, I couldn't have done that.

speaker: Player
text: And how, exactly, do you propose to do that?

speaker: Carth
text: All you have to do is listen to me. That's all I ask.

speaker: Player
text: Somehow I'm not surprised you found a way here.

speaker: Player
text: Carth. You should still be on the planet, shouldn't you?

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: You are a student at the academy. You may enter by the door.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: You again? I told you to locate Yuthura Ban in the cantina. She is the only one who can bring new students into the academy.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: Greetings, student. I see you have the medallion that marks you as one of the chosen.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: I do not recognize you, however. Have you been accepted into the academy very recently?

speaker: Player
text: Yes. Today, in fact.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: I see. And who might your friends be?

speaker: Player
text: They are my slaves.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: Ah. I trust you will be responsible for ensuring your slaves are not disruptive, then?

speaker: Carth
text: No more disruptive than our 'master' will be.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: What was that?

speaker: Bastila
text: Ahh... ignore him, sir. He is mentally deficient. And he drools.

speaker: Carth
text: Hey!

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: You will want to bring your medallion to Yuthura Ban. She is the one who brings all selected students into the academy for their training.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: I believe she can be located within the cantina here in the colony. I suggest you go to her while she is still there, student.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh, nothing.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Grrr... I will not play the part of slave for long. Not even to pass this fool.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: If your animal acts up he will be destroyed. This would reflect badly on you, understand?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hmph. Suddenly I'm a convincing slave, am I? Maybe you should have left me on the ship.

speaker: Cand
text: I always think we should leave you on the ship, old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't get smart-mouthed with me, young man. You're not too old to put over my knee.

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: Disruptive? What does he mean by that? I have never been disruptive, master.

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep! Boooop!

speaker: HK47
text: Well, besides *that*.

speaker: Player
text: They are none of your business.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: So long as the Sith do not object to them, neither will I. They will be your responsibility, of course.

speaker: Jolee
text: Aren't we always?

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: And if the Sith do object to us, master, I shall fill them full of new holes!

speaker: Player
text: That's none of your business, soldier.

speaker: Player
text: No. I have been away for a while.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: You are neither a Sith nor do you bear the medallion of a student of this facility. Please leave at once.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm Darth Revan. I was Lord of the Sith. Let me in.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: [Failure] I see. And who might your friends be?

speaker: Player
text: It's obvious you don't believe me. But I really am Darth Revan!

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: On your way, citizen.

speaker: Player
text: How do I become a Sith, then?

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: You must be admitted to the academy. That decision must be made by a Sith who has already been accepted, here.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: The final decision, however, remains with Master Yuthura. I believe she is currently at the cantina if you wish to seek her out. Now go.

speaker: Player
text: What's this medallion you mention?

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: It is the device given to one who has been accepted into the academy, but has not yet proved their worth as a student.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: If one of the Sith decides you are worthy, you will be given one... which you must then take to Yuthura Ban, who I believe is in the cantina. It is she who decides which hopefuls enter the academy.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I need to get inside. I have been sent to speak with the Master of the Academy!

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: [Failure] No-one gets inside, citizen. Messages and deliveries must be relayed through official Sith channels only.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You will let me inside.

speaker: Sith Academy Guard
text: [Failure] I have been conditioned to resist mental persuasion, citizen. Please do not attempt that again.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Sith Droid
text: This entrance to the Sith Embassy has been closed temporarily due to a maintenance failure. The main entrance to the Embassy will reopen when the problem has been fixed.

speaker: Player
text: I heard the Embassy was attacked.

speaker: Sith Droid
text: What?! How did you... Um... This unit has no knowledge of what you're talking about.

speaker: Sith Droid
text: Those with legitimate business with the Sith should return when the repairs have been completed.

speaker: Player
text: How can I get inside now?

speaker: Sith Droid
text: The secondary external entrance is reserved for Sith personnel only and is not to be used by visitors.

speaker: Player
text: I will be going.

speaker: Man
text: Please, don't take me in for questioning... I don't know anything! I swear!

speaker: Man
text: I've got a ton of things to do today. I can't talk to you.

speaker: Man
text: I heard the gangs have overrun the Lower City. Why don't the Sith go down there and restore order?

speaker: Man
text: I heard the Sith are sending salvage teams down into the Undercity to recover those Republic escape pods.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: I... I must g-get into... the academy... must...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: You... you have a medallion! How... how did you... unghhhh...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Leave... leave me be! I won't listen to your... manipulations. I... I *will* make it into the academy!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: Just... just a few hours longer... just a few hours, surely...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: You'll get your... turn soon enough, fool. And when you do, *Cough* I will be there, laughing as you collapse from... heat exhaustion and Mekel's beatings!

speaker: Nubassa
text: Greetings! Forgive me if this seems an odd question, off-worlder, but might you have any exotic species for sale? Nothing dangerous, mind you.

speaker: Player
text: Exotic species? What sorts of exotic species?

speaker: Nubassa
text: Anything non-sentient and non-carnivorous will do, though creatures that are easy to manage are preferred. Is that understandable?

speaker: Player
text: Why would you want to buy animals?

speaker: Nubassa
text: Ah, good question. The Selkath have little exposure to life from other planets, you see, but our government hopes to change that.

speaker: Nubassa
text: We are setting up a zoological compound for visitation by the public, and are hoping to stock it with non-offensive foreign creatures of all types.

speaker: Nubassa
text: The only problem right now is actually procuring the exotic species we need. Selkath import restrictions are quite prohibitive, to say the least.

speaker: Player
text: So you want to smuggle them in?

speaker: Nubassa
text: I would not use such a harsh word, off-worlder. Let us say that I am interested in engaging in private trade. That is allowed, according to our laws.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Finding off-worlders that deal in such trade is most difficult, however. I have become quite desperate. Might you have what I seek?

speaker: Player
text: I have some gizka, if you're interested.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Gizka? You speak of the small, bipedal amphibians with the overly high reproductive rate, correct? Oh, no, I am afraid I cannot take those.

speaker: Nubassa
text: A compatriot of mine made the mistake of purchasing a pair of such creatures several months ago. Within weeks our storage facilities were nearly overrun.

speaker: Nubassa
text: If you are in possession of such creatures, I hope you keep them separated. If not, then you have my condolences.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Is there no way I can convince you to take them off my hands?

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] I... suppose having a few of the creatures would not be of harm. We do have experience handling them now, I suppose.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Since they are so difficult to maintain, however, I would ask that you provide 100 credits. Then I will take them off your hands.

speaker: Player
text: Deal. I want those things off my ship as soon as possible.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Very well. It is a pleasure doing business with you... I will have my people show up to remove your gizka as soon as possible.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Thank you very much. For an off-worlder, interacting with you has been most pleasant.

speaker: Player
text: But... I actually don't have 100 credits.

speaker: Nubassa
text: You do not even have 100 credits? Then you are in dire straits, indeed. You certainly do not need these pests on your vessel.

speaker: Nubassa
text: In the interest of maintaining peace, I shall remove them and use what I can. Thank you for your assistance, off-worlder... I hope your situation improves soon.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You don't need any credits to take them.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] What am I thinking? It is impertinent of me to ask you for credits when you are attempting to make a sale. My apologies.

speaker: Nubassa
text: I shall send some of my people by to remove the gizka on your vessel. Thank you for your co-operation.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] I... I do not... no, I am afraid that you are mistaken. I do require coin to compensate for my aid. These gizka are not easy to manage.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. 100 credits it is.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I was hoping to sell them. How about we just call it even?

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] *sigh* I suppose it is better than nothing. We must have some creatures in our exhibit, after all.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] The cost of maintaining such creatures is very high. I would be removing pests for you at my own expense?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] You want me to *pay* you? How about you give me 100 credits?

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] I... suppose it is natural for off-worlders to desire commerce, even when it is unfair. Very well, I shall do as you ask, in the interest of peace.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Here are your credits. I shall send someone by to remove the gizka from your vessel. Good day, off-worlder.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] That is unfair of you to ask, off-worlder. You are attempting to sell me something I have already stated I do not need.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] I do not think so, no. They have proven to be far too much trouble in the past.

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I would *really* like to get rid of these creatures.

speaker: Nubassa
text: I am sure you would. They are practically a nuisance. I have no need of them, however, as I stated.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] How about if I paid you 100 credits as well? Would that help?

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] *sigh* I suppose it would. I am not looking forward to the trouble this will cause, but if it will help you out... I will do what I can.

speaker: Nubassa
text: I shall send some people by your vessel shortly to remove the gizka. Good day to you, off-worlder.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] But these are special gizka. They don't reproduce like the others do.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] They do not? Well, that is marvelous news! We would have the benefit of obtaining the gizka without the inconvenience of their numbers!

speaker: Nubassa
text: If you wish, I will send some others over to your vessels right away to remove the gizka.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] The gizka are for *sale*... they aren't free.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] Ah. I hope 100 credits will be sufficient, then? I realize that such a rare strain of gizka might be worth more, but it is all I can afford.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Thank you for your assistance, off-worlder. Dealing with you has proven far more pleasureable than I anticipated.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] I am willing to take these gizka off your hands because of their unusual nature... I certainly will not purchase them!

speaker: Player
text: Fine, take them, then.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. No deal.

speaker: Nubassa
text: As you wish. Our negotiation is hereby suspended.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds good to me.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Failure] I have never heard of such a creature. I suspect you are merely desperate to offload your difficult circumstance onto another. Shame on you, off-worlder!

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] But you want to take these gizka off my hands.

speaker: Nubassa
text: [Success] Hmm. But maybe we could use these gizka, after all. It is better then having nothing at all to show, I suppose.

speaker: Player
text: Thanks anyway, then.

speaker: Nubassa
text: My pleasure. Should you encounter some other exotic species, do please let me know.

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't have anything for you.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Well, if you do come across something potentially interesting, please remember me. My name is Nubassa. I hope to see you again!

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for questions.

speaker: Nubassa
text: Greetings again, off-worlder. Have you happened upon any exotic species since we last spoke?

speaker: Player
text: How has the hunt been?

speaker: Nubassa
text: Poor, to tell the truth. I am beginning to think we shall have no species at all in our zoological exhibit. *sigh*

speaker: Ugzak
text: Gurke is through with you, and so is me.

text: What you looking at, hah? *snort*

text: Maybe we hunt everything tomorrow. Nobody else gets anything!

text: Too many new humees in town.

text: Bah! Tube-heads can't hunt. Why they allowed here?

speaker: Elder Guide
text: The ancient traditions state that you must enter the Temple alone. I will not perform the ritual if there are others with you.

speaker: Elder Guide
text: I will begin the ritual. It will take many hours, but when it is complete you must be ready... the shields will not stay down for long. Prepare yourself.

speaker: Elder Guide
text: *Chanting*

speaker: Elder Guide
text: Wait... someone is coming!

speaker: Security Droid
text: Obey the laws here on Manaan, human.

speaker: Carth
text: [A veteran warrior, Carth knows better than to speak with you when enemies are so near.]

speaker: Carth
text: They're waiting for you inside.

speaker: Carth
text: [Something seems to be bothering Carth. Maybe you should speak to him and see if you can get him to open up about it.]

speaker: Player
text: [Speak to Carth.]

speaker: Carth
text: Yes? What's on your mind?

speaker: Player
text: Do you think you'll see Dustil again?
comment: Dustil and Carth reunited Carth has not been talked to about it

speaker: Carth
text: I think so. If he's anything like he used to be, Dustil hates to be tricked. There's no way he'll let the Sith trick him again.

speaker: Carth
text: As for whether or not he'll be my son again... I don't know. He's so full of anger and hate... I wasn't expecting him to be like this.

speaker: Carth
text: Maybe we can work it out. I hope so. I guess I'll have to wait and see. Thanks, by the way... for all your help.

speaker: Player
text: Do you want to talk about it?
comment: Dustil is dead Carth has not been talked to about it

speaker: Carth
text: There's nothing to talk about. I failed my son... just as I failed my wife. I thought that if I ever found him...

speaker: Carth
text: I just can't believe he's dead. I... you should have stopped him! You should have done something to prevent this!

speaker: Player
text: Me? Why am I suddenly at fault?

speaker: Carth
text: Oh, don't give me that innocent look! You can talk a Hutt out of his credits, you could have found a way... you could have saved him!

speaker: Player
text: That seems a lot to expect from me.

speaker: Carth
text: Is it? You seem just fine at pulling off the near-impossible... when you want to.

speaker: Carth
text: I can't help but wonder if part of you didn't enjoy this. I thought we might be friends, but with you... heh, who can tell?

speaker: Player
text: You think I enjoyed it? That's pretty low.

speaker: Carth
text: Is it? I find it hard to tell which side you're on, sometimes. Still... not all the blame is yours. Most of it is mine.

speaker: Carth
text: I... I wish we hadn't come. I wish I'd never found him.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry for your loss, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm sorry, too. And I'm sorry I ever met you.

speaker: Carth
text: I... no, I didn't mean that. Please... maybe it would be better if we continued with the mission. I want to... take my mind off this.

speaker: Carth
text: Saving the galaxy is what's important now. My son... I can mourn my son later. When we're done. So... let's just go.

speaker: Player
text: You didn't fail him, Carth. You did your best.

speaker: Carth
text: No, I did fail him. And so did you. I wish I'd never met you.

speaker: Player
text: Wishing won't help matters, will it?

speaker: Carth
text: No. If it did, I would never have met you.

speaker: Player
text: Stop trying to put all the blame on me.

speaker: Carth
text: All the blame? No. Part of the blame, though... part of the blame is yours. The rest is mine.

speaker: Player
text: We're not friends, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: No, I see that. I don't know what I was expecting, telling you all I did. The blame is mostly mine for this, anyway.

speaker: Carth
text: Why didn't you want to? You knew how important finding Dustil was to me! You... you've helped others, why not him? Why not me?

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth. I wish I could have stopped this.

speaker: Carth
text: You could have. But... you're only partly to blame. I'm to blame for all the rest.

speaker: Player
text: He was a Sith, Carth, remember?

speaker: Carth
text: He was my son!!

speaker: Player
text: You're right. I should have tried.

speaker: Player
text: Don't try blaming me for your problems, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to know some more about you, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: Me? Well, I've been a star-pilot for the Republic for years. I've seen more than my share of wars... I fought in the Mandalorian Wars before all this started.

speaker: Carth
text: But with all that, I've never experienced anything like the slaughter these Sith animals can unleash. Not even the Mandalorians were that senseless.

speaker: Carth
text: My home world was one of the first planets to fall to Malak's fleet. The Sith bombed it into submission, and there wasn't a damn thing our Republic forces could do to stop them!

speaker: Player
text: You're talking like it's your fault. Like you failed somehow.

speaker: Carth
text: It shouldn't be my fault. I did everything I could... I followed my orders and did my duty. That shouldn't mean I failed them! I didn't!

speaker: Player
text: Them? Do you mean the people of your home world?

speaker: Carth
text: Yes. No... no, that's not what I mean. I mean... I'm sorry. I'm not making much sense, am I?

speaker: Carth
text: You probably mean well with your questions. I'm just not accustomed to talking about my past very much. At all, actually.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm more used to taking action... keeping my mind focused on the business at hand. So let's just do that. If you have more questions, ask them later.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth. I didn't mean to upset you.

speaker: Carth
text: I know. Don't worry about it. I just... must not be making much sense.

speaker: Player
text: Hey, why are you getting so mad at me? It's not like this was my fault!

speaker: Carth
text: I know that. I'm not angry at you... don't think that. I must not be making much sense.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth. This must be very painful for you.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm just a soldier; I go where the fleet Admirals tell me to. I follow my orders and I do my duty. It just... *sigh* doesn't seem right that doing that means I failed them! I didn't!

speaker: Player
text: Calm down. I was just asking.

speaker: Carth
text: You're the one who wanted to know more about me. Well this is it, this is what I am.

speaker: Player
text: Is this a good time to ask you some more questions?

speaker: Carth
text: I'm all ears, beautiful.

speaker: Player
text: 'Beautiful'? Isn't that a little inappropriate?

speaker: Carth
text: Is there something else you'd prefer I called you?

speaker: Player
text: How about my name?

speaker: Carth
text: Don't get yourself in a twist over it, gorgeous. I didn't mean anything by it.

speaker: Player
text: There you go again!

speaker: Carth
text: Oh, for crying out -- fine. If it'll make you feel better, you call me something. Go ahead, come on, I can take it.

speaker: Player
text: What? Don't be ridiculous.

speaker: Carth
text: What? Are you afraid you'll hurt my feelings? Come on, spit it out. You can do it.

speaker: Player
text: How about "sexist worm"?

speaker: Carth
text: Is that it? You can do better than that!

speaker: Player
text: Lobotomized Gamorrean!

speaker: Carth
text: Ouch. Heh heh heh. That *is* better. Well, I bet "beautiful" doesn't sound so bad in comparison now, does it?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe not, but I still don't want you calling me that.

speaker: Carth
text: Stubborn as ever. Okay, you got me. I bet you have your heart set on those questions. Are they really necessary?

speaker: Player
text: Not if you have a problem with it.

speaker: Carth
text: No. No, I don't have a problem with it, really. Go ahead and interrogate me.

speaker: Player
text: This isn't an interrogation. I never said that.

speaker: Carth
text: No, I was just joking, though you do seem to be full of questions. It's rather refreshing, to be honest.

speaker: Carth
text: Let me ask you something first, though. I've been going through the battle aboard the Endar Spire over and over in my head since we crashed.

speaker: Carth
text: Some things just don't add up for me. Maybe you could tell me what happened... from your perspective.

speaker: Player
text: Like you said when we first met: Bastila didn't have time to use her powers.

speaker: Carth
text: True. Bastila is as powerful as they say... she's the one who defeated Darth Revan, after all.

speaker: Carth
text: Hmm. I guess that no Jedi ability, no matter how powerful, makes up for being completely surprised and outmatched.

speaker: Carth
text: We didn't choose that battle, anyway. It got forced on us. Hell, I'm just surprised that any of us are alive to talk about it.

speaker: Carth
text: Come to think of it, it's more than a little surprising that you happen to be here, isn't it? Just what is your position with the Republic fleet, anyway?

speaker: Player
text: Why? Are you accusing me of something?

speaker: Carth
text: Not at all. I just think it's a bit odd that someone who got added to the crew roster at the last minute just happens to be one of the survivors.

speaker: Player
text: You'd rather I wasn't?

speaker: Carth
text: Don't be ridiculous. You've more than proved yourself since the crash... we wouldn't have made it this far without you. But still...

speaker: Player
text: Are you implying *I* had something to do with the crash?

speaker: Carth
text: No. Well... maybe. Don't get me wrong, it just seems odd that someone Bastila's party specifically requested to transfer aboard happened to survive.

speaker: Player
text: I have no idea what you're talking about!

speaker: Carth
text: The Jedi requested numerous things when they came on board... hell, they practically took over the ship, as far as I could tell.

speaker: Carth
text: Considering your connection to Bastila and the Jedi... whether you know it or not... your presence here seems a little convenient.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm probably wrong and this is probably nothing, I know. I learned a long time ago not to take things at face value, however. And I *hate* surprises.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by surprises?

speaker: Carth
text: I mean I have to expect the unexpected. Just to be safe.

speaker: Player
text: Are you always this suspicious?

speaker: Carth
text: Look... it has nothing to do with you, personally. I don't trust anyone, and I have my reasons.

speaker: Carth
text: And, no, I'm not going to discuss them. So can we just keep our mind on more important things?

speaker: Player
text: I consider this important.

speaker: Carth
text: Alright, alright. You must be the most damned persistent woman I've ever met.

speaker: Carth
text: We'll talk about it... but later. Right now I just want to get going.

speaker: Carth
text: Alright, Alright. You're pretty damned tenacious, you know that?

speaker: Player
text: You haven't heard the last from me on this.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, let's do that.

speaker: Carth
text: Good. Like I said before, I prefer action to talk, anyway.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. Let's just get back to something important, then.

speaker: Player
text: You do know we're on the same side, right?

speaker: Player
text: Try something and it'll be the last mistake you make.

speaker: Player
text: I'm telling you, Carth, I had nothing to do with the crash.

speaker: Carth
text: I expect you're right. I've got no real reason to suspect you of anything. Still... it's better to be safe than sorry, right?

speaker: Player
text: Shouldn't we be trying to work together?

speaker: Carth
text: I am working with you. I'd be a fool not to. I'd also be a fool not to expect the unexpected.

speaker: Player
text: Why would Bastila request my transfer?

speaker: Player
text: It doesn't make any difference. Go ahead and be paranoid.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm not trying to be paranoid. It's just that I learned a long time ago that something which looks like a coincidence probably isn't. Especially when the Jedi are involved.

speaker: Player
text: What's so odd about me being added to the crew at the last minute?

speaker: Carth
text: You were the only one. Not to mention that Bastila's party was the one who requested your transfer.

speaker: Player
text: I used to be a smuggler, if you must know. I was recruited into the fleet for my knowledge.

speaker: Carth
text: A smuggler? I should have guessed. Isn't it odd, however, that a smuggler who was added to the crew at the last minute just happens to be alive?

speaker: Player
text: I'm a scout. I was recruited into the fleet for my skills, if you must know.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, that makes sense. Still... it seems a bit strange that someone who was a last-minute addition to the crew roster is one of the survivors.

speaker: Player
text: I'm just a soldier. I'm sure there isn't anything unusual about that, is there?

speaker: Carth
text: Hell no... unless you consider that you were a last-minute addition to the crew roster and you just happen to be one of the survivors.

speaker: Player
text: Why ask me? I don't see the point.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm just trying to figure it out. I saw enough men lose their lives needlessly during the Mandalorian Wars. It's... difficult to see that happening all over again.

speaker: Carth
text: We lost the ship and a lot of good people... and for what? On the hope that Jedi powers would save us, somehow. Not that Bastila had much of an opportunity to act.

speaker: Player
text: I wasn't in a position to know what was going on, really.

speaker: Carth
text: Neither was I, to tell the truth. I was onboard as an advisor for the most part. The battle began so fast, it's anyone's guess as to what actually happened.

speaker: Player
text: Are you getting testy again?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't get testy. I get angry. And if I was angry, you wouldn't have to ask me if I was, let me assure you.

speaker: Player
text: Excellent. Soon all your secrets will be mine!

speaker: Carth
text: All my secrets are purely of the mundane variety, unfortunately. Nothing worth extracting, though you're welcome to try.

speaker: Player
text: I just would like to know you better.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh. Well, if it's an interrogation you wanted, why didn't you say so?

speaker: Player
text: Don't be such a child. It's just a few questions.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh no, how can I resist a challenge to my manly pride, huh? Ha ha! Fine, you've made your point. Interrogate at will.

speaker: Player
text: Are you getting angry again?

speaker: Carth
text: If I was, you wouldn't have to ask. So don't worry about it.

speaker: Player
text: Ha ha! You are such a pain, you know that?

speaker: Carth
text: Guilty as charged. I'll bet you still have those questions in mind, though. Are they really necessary?

speaker: Player
text: Brainless, lice-ridden bantha!

speaker: Player
text: Sexless marsh-toad!

speaker: Player
text: How about "pushy thug"?

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. Let's get back to my questions.

speaker: Carth
text: All business today, eh? Are these questions really necessary?

speaker: Player
text: That's no good, either.

speaker: Player
text: Now that one I like. Call me that from now on.

speaker: Carth
text: I might consider it. What are you going to call me, in exchange?

speaker: Player
text: How about "handsome thug"?

speaker: Carth
text: I like the first part of that. I'm a bit more partial to "the most handsome pilot in the galaxy". What do you think?

speaker: Player
text: Don't hold your breath.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then, I guess "gorgeous" will have to do until then, won't it?

speaker: Carth
text: Kidding aside, I bet you're not about to give up on those questions of yours. Are they really necessary?

speaker: Player
text: I think I'm going to be ill.

speaker: Player
text: I'll think about it.

speaker: Player
text: I'd prefer you didn't call me anything. It's demeaning.

speaker: Player
text: How about 'gorgeous'? I like that better.

speaker: Player
text: Keep addressing me like that and you might lose an ear or two.

speaker: Carth
text: Heh heh. A little bit touchy, are we? Is there something else you'd prefer I called you?

speaker: Player
text: I like the sound of that.

speaker: Carth
text: Which? The fact that I'm all ears or the beautiful part?

speaker: Player
text: Carth, are you flirting with me?

speaker: Carth
text: Not really. Just a habit. You have something you'd rather I call you by?

speaker: Player
text: The beautiful part. Keep calling me that.

speaker: Player
text: Why do I get the impression that you're not serious?

speaker: Carth
text: Maybe I'm just avoiding your questions. Is this really necessary?

speaker: Carth
text: I guess I did say you could ask me questions later, didn't I? Is this really necessary?

speaker: Player
text: Answer the damn questions, already.

speaker: Carth
text: Pretty snappy with the orders, are we? Okay, you got it... sir.

speaker: Player
text: I want to discuss something with you.

speaker: Carth
text: You do? Fair enough. What do you want to discuss?

speaker: Player
text: I want to talk about these issues you seem to have with me.

speaker: Carth
text: *Sigh* I knew you wouldn't understand where I was coming from. Let me try to explain.

speaker: Carth
text: You're probably one of the most skilled women I've ever met. You've saved my butt more than once and I'm lucky you're here to help me, no question.

speaker: Carth
text: But that doesn't mean I'm going to stop watching you or being wary. I'm just not built that way. Period.

speaker: Player
text: Not built that way? That sounds like an excuse.

speaker: Carth
text: Maybe so. But I've been betrayed before by people I... well, it won't happen again, that's all.

speaker: Player
text: So you want some guarantee that I won't betray you?!

speaker: Carth
text: I don't know that you'll betray me. But there are no guarantees... not for you, not for me. You don't have to take it personally.

speaker: Player
text: Don't tell me not to take it personally, you hairless Wookiee!

speaker: Carth
text: Hairless Wookiee? Alright, sister, just... just... just calm down before your head explodes.

speaker: Player
text: We'll just see whose head explodes, you ungrateful monkey-lizard!

speaker: Carth
text: Is that your idea of an insult? Come on, sister, take your best shot.

speaker: Player
text: Gamorrean pig-man!

speaker: Carth
text: Oh, ouch. I think you hurt my man-feelings with that one.

speaker: Player
text: Well, you had it coming.

speaker: Carth
text: I guess I did. Feel better now?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe a little.

speaker: Carth
text: Good. Then maybe we can talk reasonably about this.

speaker: Carth
text: All I've been trying to say is that this isn't personal. If you were smart, you wouldn't trust anyone, either... not me, not Bastila and especially not yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Ahhh... so you don't trust yourself, is that it?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't need to be analyzed, thanks. Can we just get back to business?

speaker: Player
text: I don't need someone around who doesn't trust me.

speaker: Carth
text: And I don't need all these questions. What I do need is to try and save the galaxy, if that's even possible.

speaker: Carth
text: Why is whether or not I trust you or anyone so damned important to you? Why... why do you even care?

speaker: Carth
text: We don't have time for this, so can we please just... drop it. For now? Can we pick it up later if you really must, I... want to get underway.

speaker: Player
text: So leave. Be on your own, it's obviously what you want.

speaker: Carth
text: It's not what I want. I have a duty and I intend to see it through. The galaxy's in danger and I want to save it... that's what I want!

speaker: Player
text: You sure you don't want to talk about it?

speaker: Carth
text: No, I don't want to talk about it. What I want is to save the galaxy... if that's even possible.

speaker: Player
text: That settles that, I guess.

speaker: Player
text: Pretty pithy advice, I see.

speaker: Player
text: I wouldn't want to live like that.

speaker: Carth
text: Not all of us have the luxury of a choice. I'm conditioned this way, sorry.

speaker: Player
text: Not really. This is still serious.

speaker: Carth
text: *Sigh* Look... all I mean is that if you're smart, you won't trust anyone... not me, not Bastila and especially not yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Don't patronize me.

speaker: Carth
text: Wouldn't think of it. Feel better now?

speaker: Player
text: Drooling Bomarr cast-off!

speaker: Player
text: Don't tell me to calm down, you ignorant bantha!

speaker: Player
text: I'm beginning to wonder if you're even capable of trusting anyone.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, you can stop wondering. I'm not.

speaker: Player
text: Right. And how am I supposed to know that *you* won't betray us?

speaker: Carth
text: Me?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, you! Why should I trust you, after all?

speaker: Carth
text: You shouldn't. If you're smart, you won't trust anyone... not me, not Bastila, and especially not yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Why not you? Accusing other people is a good cover for a traitor.

speaker: Carth
text: I don't remember ever saying anything about "traitor". All I mean is that if you're smart, you won't trust anyone... not me, not Bastila and especially not yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I didn't ask for your advice, nor do I need it.

speaker: Player
text: No, I do take it personally!

speaker: Carth
text: Well, that's too bad, then, because it's not going to change.

speaker: Player
text: I'm starting to get pretty tired of this attitude of yours.

speaker: Carth
text: Yeah, well, you wouldn't be the first. Look... I don't expect you to be my friend. This is just the way I am, no need to take it personally.

speaker: Player
text: Of course it won't happen again if you never trust anyone!

speaker: Carth
text: Look... I'm not trying to insult you. This is just the way I am, no need to take it personally.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you so hostile? What did I do to deserve this?

speaker: Carth
text: You, uh... haven't done anything *yet*. But there's no guarantee that you won't do anything in the future. I've been betrayed before by people and I... well, it won't happen again.

speaker: Player
text: And what, exactly, are you watching me for?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't know that, yet. Like I said before, it's probably nothing. But I've been betrayed before by people and I... well, it won't happen again, that's all.

speaker: Carth
text: You've got the skills of an elite commando, and you've saved my butt more than once. Between that and your facility with languages, I'm lucky you're here.

speaker: Player
text: We didn't finish our conversation last time.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to know now if we have a problem.

speaker: Player
text: I just want to talk with you.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh? You want to argue some more, is that it?

speaker: Player
text: I'm always up for a good fight.

speaker: Carth
text: Ha! Can't say I've met a woman quite like you before. You're really something.

speaker: Carth
text: I just don't trust easily, and for good reasons... which are my own.

speaker: Player
text: But we have to work together, Carth, so it has plenty to do with me.

speaker: Carth
text: Ahhh, damn it. I suppose I won't get any rest until I talk, will I? You want to know why I don't trust anyone? Fine, here goes.

speaker: Carth
text: Five years ago the Jedi had just finished the war with the Mandalorians. Revan and Malak were heroes. I was damn proud to have served in their fleet.

speaker: Carth
text: It was completely unexpected when they turned on us, invading the Republic while we were still weak. Nobody knew what to think, least of all me.

speaker: Carth
text: Our heroes had become brutal, conquering Sith... and we were all but helpless before them. Think about it... if you can't even trust the best of the Jedi, who can you trust?

speaker: Player
text: What do I have to do with Malak and Revan?

speaker: Carth
text: It... it's not that. It's... That's not what I mean. There were... there were others. Good, solid, trusted men who joined them.

speaker: Carth
text: Malak and Revan and the Sith deserve to die for what they've done... but the ones who fled the Republic and joined them are even worse.

speaker: Carth
text: The dark side has nothing to do with why they joined with the Sith. They deserve no mercy!

speaker: Player
text: You say that with such... hatred.

speaker: Carth
text: I know. I... should apologize to you. I've become so accustomed to expecting the worst in others, and you've done nothing to deserve that.

speaker: Carth
text: It's just... never mind. Let's just continue with what we were doing. I'd rather not talk about it.

speaker: Player
text: I haven't joined the Sith, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: They turned to the dark side, obviously. Why is it so personal?

speaker: Carth
text: I... of course the Jedi turned to the dark side. There were others, however, who weren't Jedi. Good men... trusted men who joined them.

speaker: Player
text: I suppose you can't. That must have been hard to take.

speaker: Carth
text: I... it wasn't even that. There were others: good, solid men. Trusted men who turned on us, as well, and joined their cause.

speaker: Player
text: What reasons? I want to know.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. You can stuff your reasons, then.

speaker: Player
text: I can make you talk, Carth. Trust me.

speaker: Carth
text: Heh heh. Well I might be willing to take you up on that challenge. But uh, you're just not going to let up, are you? Fine... you want to know why I don't trust anyone? Here goes.

speaker: Carth
text: So I've seen. If I were Malak I'd be a bit nervous to have you on my tail.

speaker: Player
text: I just want to know why you distrust me so much.

speaker: Carth
text: What does it matter that much? Why can't you just leave it be?

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't want to argue with you.

speaker: Carth
text: And I don't really want to argue with you, either. You seem... sincere enough, I guess.

speaker: Player
text: I want to continue our discussion from before.

speaker: Carth
text: I thought I said I didn't want to talk about it anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you think you'd feel better if you discussed it?

speaker: Carth
text: Listen, sister... just because we're working together does not mean you get to badger me with constant questions!

speaker: Player
text: Do we have another problem, now?

speaker: Carth
text: Blast it if you aren't the most frustrating woman to talk to! Isn't there someone else you can harass for a little while?

speaker: Player
text: *I'm* frustrating? Look who's talking!

speaker: Carth
text: What? Me? What did I do?

speaker: Player
text: Oh, that's rich. Where have you been?

speaker: Carth
text: I... *sigh* Okay, I give up. You win.

speaker: Carth
text: Look, I suppose I... could use someone to talk to. I'm just not used to it. And I don't know why you're so interested. But here goes.

speaker: Carth
text: When I think of all the men who have betrayed us, the one that stands out above them all is the one I respected the most. Saul.

speaker: Player
text: You say that name like I should know it.

speaker: Carth
text: You don't? I thought everyone did. Admiral Saul Karath is the commander of the entire Sith fleet. He's half the reason Malak has done so well in the war.

speaker: Carth
text: Saul was my commanding officer back when the Mandalorian Wars first began. He taught me everything about being a soldier... and I looked up to him.

speaker: Carth
text: Saul approached me before he left. He talked to me about how the Republic was on the losing side... and about how I should start thinking of my survival.

speaker: Carth
text: I know now that he was trying to recruit me into the Sith, but I couldn't have conceived of it back then. I argued with him and he got angry and he left. I never saw him again.

speaker: Player
text: You didn't think he would betray the Republic?

speaker: Carth
text: Saul was my mentor... he led us to so many victories against the Mandalorians, even when things looked to be at their worst.

speaker: Carth
text: I just... I couldn't conceive of it. He... he couldn't be serious. I was wrong, of course... he not only left us for the Sith, he... he gave them the codes to bypass our scanners.

speaker: Carth
text: I remember waking up as the first of the Sith bombers snuck past our defenses and began destroying half of our docked ships. I knew right away what had happened.

speaker: Carth
text: I... could have stopped him. I could have stopped it all.

speaker: Player
text: So you blame yourself for trusting your friend?

speaker: Carth
text: I blame Saul, not myself. I was... I was stupid and I ignored the danger. He nearly destroyed us all.

speaker: Carth
text: I've fought Saul for years, now, and if I ever catch up to him... he will regret what he's done. He will regret it.

speaker: Player
text: So that's all of it, then?

speaker: Carth
text: No. No, it's not.

speaker: Carth
text: But I don't want to talk about it right now. Let's go.

speaker: Player
text: That's terrible. I feel awful for you.

speaker: Carth
text: Well... there's more to the story, I guess.

speaker: Player
text: I'd do the same thing in your shoes.

speaker: Player
text: Do you really believe that?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't know. Maybe. He might have killed me if I'd tried, or I might have killed him. I was stupid, however, and I let him go.

speaker: Player
text: And that's why you feel so sorry for yourself?

speaker: Carth
text: Don't even start with that! I don't feel sorry for myself. I feel angry... at Saul and all those others. It's all I can think about sometimes!

speaker: Player
text: How could you have not seen through that?

speaker: Carth
text: I didn't want to, maybe. Are you so sure you would have?

speaker: Player
text: That name sounds familiar.

speaker: Carth
text: With good reason. Admiral Saul Karath is the commander of the entire Sith fleet. He's half the reason Malak has done so well in the war.

speaker: Player
text: You don't know? Typical male.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. I'll leave you alone, since I'm so frustrating.

speaker: Carth
text: Wait... *sigh* I didn't mean it that way. Don't go, damn it.

speaker: Player
text: What exactly is it about me that frustrates you?

speaker: Carth
text: Oh no, I'm not falling for that one. I wasn't born yesterday, you know.

speaker: Player
text: Really? It's hard to tell.

speaker: Player
text: And you say I'm frustrating to deal with.

speaker: Player
text: Alright, then, I'll leave you alone if that's what you want.

speaker: Player
text: Well, I wouldn't want you to feel harassed. Have it your way.

speaker: Player
text: You're damn right it does.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going to repeat myself, Carth, You owe me.

speaker: Carth
text: I... suppose you're right. Fine, then. But I don't know why you're so interested, but here it goes.

speaker: Carth
text: Not particularly. I... guess it wouldn't hurt, exactly, either, though I don't know why you're so interested.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, but I'm bored, so spit it out.

speaker: Carth
text: Cute. Nice to know that you're so full of concern. *Sigh* Well, I guess it wouldn't hurt, though I don't know why you're so interested.

speaker: Player
text: I think you owe me an explanation, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: You've been very quiet, lately, you know that?
comment: available after the first starmap uncovered K_SWG_CARTH = 4

speaker: Carth
text: Have I been quiet? I suppose I have. I guess I just don't like being left out of the loop.

speaker: Player
text: You were born out of the loop.

speaker: Carth
text: Very cute. If you got any cuter, you'd pass for a Gamorrean's sister.

speaker: Player
text: The things you say!

speaker: Carth
text: Look, I'm serious. No one seems to want to tell me anything, and it's starting to irritate me.

speaker: Carth
text: For one thing, I want to know what the Jedi Council said to you. They pulled you in there and refused to tell me a thing about it.

speaker: Bastila
text: *That* is none of your concern, Carth, and you would do well to leave the matter be.

speaker: Carth
text: I respect you, Bastila, but you've been as close-mouthed as the rest of the Council. If you won't talk to me, then maybe somebody else will.

speaker: Player
text: Why should anything the Jedi do seem strange to you?

speaker: Carth
text: I may not know much about the Jedi, but I do know they aren't famous for taking on old Padawans and sending them on dangerous assignments.

speaker: Player
text: They said there's a bond between Bastila and myself.

speaker: Carth
text: A bond? What kind of bond? You mean to say that they told you you were "tied" to Bastila in some way? Heh. I have trouble believing that.

speaker: Carth
text: I've been watching you... you can be cruel and impulsive. A Jedi without self-control or training, and yet the Council sends you on your way? Why?

speaker: Carth
text: I'm not trying to provoke you or imply that you're somehow responsible for the Jedi Council... but give me a hand, here! There has to be a reason!

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying I'm not needed?

speaker: Carth
text: No, I don't... I didn't mean that you weren't wanted, or that I want to go! It's just... damn it!

speaker: Carth
text: I'll tell you this much... I am *not* going to wait around until I'm betrayed again!

speaker: Player
text: I am *not* going to betray you! I am *not* Saul!

speaker: Carth
text: Well, we'll just see about that, won't we?

speaker: Carth
text: Look, I didn't mean it that way. I want to get to Saul, not... no... no, forget it. It seems all I can do is insult you, isn't it?

speaker: Carth
text: Just forget I said anything. Let's... let's... just get on with what we were doing.

speaker: Player
text: And just what are you going to do about it?

speaker: Carth
text: Nothing. Not yet. You just better hope I don't get a reason to.

speaker: Player
text: I am *sick* of listening to this. Just shut up or leave!

speaker: Carth
text: Fine. You got it. Conversation over.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here and that's not going to change. Get over it.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sick of listening to you rant! Why don't *you* leave?!

speaker: Player
text: Bastila and I have a bond. We have to do this together. That's all I'm going to say.

speaker: Carth
text: And what does that mean? Is this more of that destiny garbage that the Jedi keep talking about? Well, that can't be it!

speaker: Carth
text: You're a neophyte Padawan who's been saddled with the responsibility of tracking down these Star Maps. Why? That's not normal!

speaker: Player
text: I've done pretty well so far.

speaker: Carth
text: That's completely beside the point. The Jedi encouraged you to stay with us, and I don't believe the reasons they gave.

speaker: Player
text: They thought it was more important that I help find the Star Maps than stay.

speaker: Carth
text: And why is that? You were a great help on Taris, but why would they keep you with us? Don't they... don't they have to train you?

speaker: Player
text: It's none of your business, frankly.

speaker: Carth
text: None of my business? Uh, I'm sorry... aren't I a part of this mission? The Jedi may be in charge, but I'm risking all the same things you are!

speaker: Player
text: Isn't that the point? Aren't we all in this together?

speaker: Carth
text: Are we? Why, then, does it seem like the Jedi know everything and leave the rest of us out in the cold?

speaker: Player
text: Get ahold of yourself. I'm sick of your paranoia.

speaker: Carth
text: You can be sick of whatever you like. What I'm sick of is being kept in the dark!

speaker: Carth
text: I'm rather curious to know what went on... and why they didn't keep you on Dantooine for training. Isn't that strange?

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you ask Bastila?

speaker: Carth
text: I would be more than happy to, but she's as close-mouthed as the rest of the Council. I'm hoping you'll be the one to enlighten me.

speaker: Player
text: Better than a Gamorrean's mother.

speaker: Player
text: Left out of the loop? I don't understand.

speaker: Carth
text: Left out of the loop. You know. Not being told anything... strung along. It's really starting to irritate me.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not the one leaving you out of the loop, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: No? Well, you certainly aren't helping matters any, either, and it's really starting to irritate me.

speaker: Player
text: Oh, poor baby. You need filling in on some detail?

speaker: Carth
text: Listen, sister, I don't remember reading anywhere that it's a requirement that you remain with us after we left Taris, yet here you are.

speaker: Player
text: Same could be said for you.

speaker: Carth
text: Well... yeah, true enough, I guess. But, damn it, I'm tired of nobody telling me anything!

speaker: Player
text: I have more of a purpose here than you do, flyboy.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, damn it, I want to know why that is! I want some questions answered!

speaker: Player
text: Yes, here I am. And I'm not going anywhere.

speaker: Carth
text: You want to be smart, do you? Fine. So long as I get some questions answered.

speaker: Player
text: We didn't end our last discussion very well...
comment: available after the first starmap uncovered K_SWG_CARTH = 5

speaker: Carth
text: I, ahhh... I'm not very good at this. I... I know I owe you an apology. Uh, more than one, probably.

speaker: Carth
text: I was just so desperate to finally face Saul directly in the battle over Taris, and now the Jedi have us looking for these... these Star Maps.

speaker: Carth
text: I know this mission is important, it's just... I feel a bit useless. I can fight, sure, but I'm no Jedi... all this feels completely out of my league.

speaker: Player
text: And how does that excuse your actions?

speaker: Carth
text: It doesn't, I know. It's... been a while since I even had to think about that sort of thing.

speaker: Carth
text: I just hate not knowing what's going on and feeling this... helpless. But I shouldn't have taken that out on you. I've been a royal pain in the backside, haven't I?

speaker: Player
text: Not really. I couldn't care less what you think.

speaker: Carth
text: I guess there's no harm done then. Still I, uh... I should know better by now.

speaker: Carth
text: So... I'm sorry. Will you accept my apology?

speaker: Player
text: I don't know. Maybe you should work for it, a bit.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh? I don't know if I like the sound of that...

speaker: Player
text: Don't you want me to accept your apology?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't know. What am I going to have to do for it?

speaker: Player
text: Blow away the bad guy. Save the damsel in distress. The usual.

speaker: Carth
text: Oh, the usual. Well that's not so hard. Let's get to it, then, shall we?

speaker: Player
text: Just make sure you don't need to make any more apologies. Deal?

speaker: Carth
text: Done! Let's get underway, then, shall we... partner?

speaker: Player
text: Just a little kiss. How about it?

speaker: Carth
text: I...heh, I really think that we should, ah... get going.

speaker: Player
text: No kiss, then?

speaker: Carth
text: I'm sorry. I'm glad things are better between us, now. We should... we should go.

speaker: Player
text: I was only joking, Carth, relax.

speaker: Player
text: No need to start sweating, Carth. I was only teasing.

speaker: Carth
text: So... you do accept my apology. Huh. Good. Good. I'm glad.

speaker: Carth
text: You know you, uh... you aren't so bad to have around, you know that?

speaker: Player
text: I know. I'm very charming, I'm told.

speaker: Carth
text: More than that. But... anyway... we should be off...

speaker: Player
text: I knew there was a reason we kept you.

speaker: Carth
text: Right. Off we go.

speaker: Player
text: I have my uses. Let's go.

speaker: Player
text: Only if you agree to work with me, for once.

speaker: Player
text: No, I won't. Just keep quiet and do what you're told from now on.

speaker: Carth
text: Don't drown me in sentiment, already. *Sigh* Fair enough, let's move on.

speaker: Player
text: You sure have.

speaker: Carth
text: Ha! Well... I guess I should be at least a little pleased that I haven't lost my touch.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry about it, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: No, I do worry about it. I've traveled the lanes more than once, I should know better than this.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you return to the front lines, then?

speaker: Carth
text: Because this is more important. This may really, finally, make a difference... I suppose even if I can't figure out everything that's going on, I still want to help if I can.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe if you pull yourself together you won't be so useless.

text: I don't understand.

text: No, Carth. There's no room in my destiny for you.

speaker: Carth
text: Despite whatever part of Revan is inside you, the... the darkness that must surely be there, it isn't who you are.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad to hear that.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I care if you hate me?

speaker: Carth
text: Maybe you shouldn't. I would hope that my standing by you would mean something to you, but maybe it doesn't. Maybe it just can't.

speaker: Player
text: We need to talk. About me being Darth Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have any advice on our little stowaway?

speaker: Carth
text: Sorry. I can't be of much help with that.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know if anything can be done about all these gizka?

speaker: Carth
text: I'm not really sure. You can figure it out on your own, can't you?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about this place?

speaker: Carth
text: Taris? The planet's all one big city... but it's golden years are long past, and things have gotten worse since the Sith occupied it.

speaker: Carth
text: From what I hear, the wealthy live on the tops of all the tall towers. And if you're poor, you live down in the shadows... and it gets worse the lower you go.

speaker: Carth
text: That's all I can think of, at any rate.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind.

speaker: Carth
text: You got it.

speaker: Carth
text: Dantooine's a boring place. It's all plains and herders and small settlements. Perfect for the Jedi to lose themselves in, I guess.

speaker: Carth
text: Manaan's a neutral world. They're the only source of kolto... the healing fluid... and they use that to remain free from both the Republic and the Sith.

speaker: Carth
text: Tatooine's just a desert planet. I hear the mining isn't going so well... I'd bet the colony gets abandoned before long.

speaker: Carth
text: Kashyyyk is covered by a giant forest, I hear. Trees kilometers high. The Wookiees live on the higher branches, I think.

speaker: Carth
text: Korriban's a desolate world, and a Sith planet. There's only one small colony here, I'm pretty sure.

speaker: Carth
text: I don't really know much about this place, sorry.

speaker: Player
text: [Don't speak to him.]

speaker: Carth
text: [You decide to ignore Carth and continue on with your quest for now, though it might be a good idea to speak with him later.]

speaker: Carth
text: What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: Do you want to talk?

speaker: Carth
text: Not right now. I think this datapad we found is the evidence we need. We have to bring it to Dustil right away.

speaker: Carth
text: No. What I want is to find something... anything... that will convince Dustil that we're telling the truth.

speaker: Carth
text: There must be *something* here in the academy we can bring to him, something that would show him what the Sith really are!

speaker: Carth
text: We're hit! Damage is critical! The Hawk won't hold!

speaker: Carth
text: I'm no Jedi, but are you really supposed to be using the Force for things like this?

speaker: Carth
text: Why did you do that? Sometimes... sometimes I just can't understand how you can be so cruel.

speaker: Carth
text: This isn't right! We should be helping people, not making their lives miserable.

speaker: Carth
text: That was totally uncalled for.

speaker: Carth
text: With all the violence and bloodshed we've seen, it's kind of nice to help someone for a change.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm glad to see we're still the good guys here. Sometimes I think we forget that.

speaker: kor38b_gastrig
text: [Noxious fumes surround you.]

speaker: kor38b_gastrig
text: [Your party chokes and falls over.]

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ha ha ha! Another idiotic student has stumbled into my little web, eh?
