speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Well... the contact nerve toxin in the air should knock you out quickly enough. Ha ha! Welcome!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Awake already, are you? Good! This is the tomb of Sith Lord Tulak Hord, if you don't know. I've taken up residence here, for now... it's dusty and full of critters, but it's home.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ah, yes! Introductions of course! I suppose it is time, isn't it?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: This other student here that I captured earlier you should know well enough. His name is Mekel. Say hello, Mekel.

speaker: Mekel
text: Uhhh... gurgh...

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Poor lad. He's had a hard day. My name is Jorak Uln. I was once the head of the academy, so I'm sure you've heard of me.

speaker: Player
text: No, never heard of you.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Liar. I know the spark of recognition when I see it. Nice try.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Anyhow, I'd like to propose that we move onto the main event. You see, I'd like to discover if you've got the pluck of an old-fashioned Sith.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Most of the drek Uthar has been passing through these days is so pathetic. Take young Mekel here... I already tested him. Didn't I, Mekel?

speaker: Mekel
text: Uhhhr... I... ohhh...

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Yes, yes, you're welcome. You see, Mekel here has the cruel disposition of a Sith... but not the *gumption* that I'm looking for.

speaker: Player
text: What if I told you I was Darth Revan?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ha ha! Then I'd say you have quite an imagination. Not a bad thing, but not *quite* what I'm looking for in a proper Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Look... I'm sure we can talk about this...

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I'm sure we could. We could chat all day about it, but where would that get us? I'm quite determined, and you are quite helpless.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Perhaps you have some questions? I'm not above delaying the test a bit. The results are always the same.

speaker: Player
text: And if I pass your test?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Why, then you go free! Tell you what... I'll even pass onto you my own personal thesis on ancient Sith philosophies.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: They're based on all I've learned studying Tulak's tomb. It'll make you a better Sith, I'm sure. The chances of you passing, however, are sadly remote.

speaker: Player
text: What if I refuse to take your test?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Well, forgive me for resorting to the cliche, but you would die, of course.

speaker: Player
text: You're a madman!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ahhh, what's a little mental instability between tutor and pupil? What's important is that I'm here to better the Sith as a whole. It's a big job.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! I refuse to play along!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I don't remember offering you a choice. You can refuse to answer my questions, of course, but then I'm afraid I will just have to assume the worst.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: So, then! This is how it goes: I'm going to pose a moral question to you. Get it right, and I torture Mekel. Get it wrong, and I torture you.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Mekel, here, is a bit weak... he probably won't be able to take much more punishment. Mind you... get too many wrong and you'll die, yourself.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I don't know what you think of Mekel. Maybe you don't like him. Maybe you think he deserves to be murdered? Well, here's your chance. Fair enough?

speaker: Player
text: What if Mekel dies?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Then you win. If you die, then he wins. I thought this was self-evident. Did you not grasp the concept earlier?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Well, then. Any last comments before we begin, Mekel?

speaker: Mekel
text: Uhhhnn... we can... both survive... attack him together!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Now, now, dear lad. Do you really think your friend here will answer questions wrong just to spare little you, risking their own life?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: And how many correctly-answered questions before you die, hmmm? No, don't be silly... you had your chance, remember?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: On that note, let's begin!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Now, then. Your immediate superior amongst the Sith is an effective commander and a fine leader. He trusts you and you like him. You see an opportunity to kill him. What do you do?

speaker: Player
text: I kill him in secret and put the blame on someone else.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Incorrect! Do that and no-one is in command. You derived no benefit from the kill, and neither did the Sith. We are not savages, you know.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ah, well. It is time for your punishment.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: And so we come to round two. You come across a group of humans who are threatened by dangerous animals. They plead for help, offering you a reward. What do you do?

speaker: Player
text: I accept the reward and assist them.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: So you've made a profit and now have some sniveling, useless fools trailing after you. No, no, no. Bad idea. Bad idea.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: At any rate... here is your punishment.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Let's see... ah, yes. You discover an aspect of the Force that gives you great power. Do you share it and strengthen the Sith as a whole or keep it to yourself?

speaker: Player
text: I keep it to myself.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Correct! Let them rip the secret from your cold, dead hands... if they are strong enough. Oh, certainly, you might share it with a few... selected... minions, but that of course is a completely different story. Ha ha!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Well, it's sad to say, but it's that time again, Mekel.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Will you look at that? Poor Mekel has gone and died on us. Tsk tsk. And here I thought he was good for at least one more.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Well, then... with young Mekel dead, I suppose you've gone and passed my little test, haven't you? That indeed would be a first.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I think you must have cheated a little, but there's nothing wrong with a Sith cheating a little. I'll keep my word.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I'll just give you my tablet. Perhaps we'll meet again... Sith. That would be fun, no?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Still going? Alright, then. One of your underlings has made a major mistake which makes you look bad. He is normally very competent and skilled. Do you kill him or give him another chance?

speaker: Player
text: Kill him.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Correct! Publicly, if you can. There is no room for that level of failure. Not killing him would be seen as a sign of weakness... and then where would you be?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ahhh, Mekel. The time has come once again, hasn't it?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Last question! You're about to die. Do you pass on your knowledge to your apprentice to make him stronger... or do you use your last breath to strike at your enemies?

speaker: Player
text: Neither. A true Sith never dies.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: What?! How did you know that? That was my trick question! Bah! Telepathy. No, wait! Someone told you didn't they!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Hmph. Regardless, I suppose rules are rules. Time for your medicine, Mekel, my boy.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Now... this is odd. The test is over and you're both still alive. Well that's never happened before. Hmmmn. What to do, what to do...

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I suppose this means you can go, Mekel. I'll have to just figure out what to do with our friend, here. Run along, now.

speaker: Mekel
text: Or... or I could use the Force to free them! And we could kill you!! Seems you didn't think of that, old man!!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: What?! Mutiny! Behave, students! I'll... that's it! Detention for all of you! Permanent detention!!

speaker: Player
text: I pass on my knowledge.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Fool! It is a trick question! A true Sith *never* dies!! Ha ha ha ha ha!!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I'll enjoy this one. Time for your medicine!

speaker: Player
text: I strike at my enemies.

speaker: Player
text: I won't give you the satisfaction of an answer.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Hmph. Such insolent students I get, these days. You deserve this, and then some!

speaker: Player
text: Give him another chance.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Another chance to make you look poor to your superiors? To make it look like you are weak and deserving of attack? No, no, no. Think again.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Hmmm. Not that good help is easy to find. Oh, well, here's your reward.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'm not playing along.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: You're not trying to make me angry, are you? That would be pointless posturing on your part. Is this so hard?

speaker: Player
text: I share it.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: You gained an advantage and you share it freely? Let them rip the secret from my dead hands, I say! I mean... 'share it'?! Are you mad?!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: *sigh* Well, you did ask for this. It's for your own good.

speaker: Player
text: I refuse to answer this.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: And here I thought this question was an easy one. Ah, well, suit yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I take the reward and leave the weak fools to their fate.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Correct! The humans would no doubt just be preyed upon by something else, later. Stand up for yourself, I say! We're not Jedi shepherds, after all.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Sadly, Mekel, the ingenuity of your fellow student is your loss. This is going to hurt.

speaker: Player
text: I ignore them completely.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: And pass up the opportunity to gain? What kind of Sith are you going to be if you don't grab fate by the nose hairs? No, no, no. That is bad form.

speaker: Player
text: I do nothing. He's a fine leader, you said. He's good for the Sith.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Incorrect! What sort of thinking is that? If all the Sith thought as you did, we would all be soft like the Jedi. Tsk.

speaker: Player
text: I use the opportunity to kill him and take his position.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Correct! He was a fool to let down his guard. You will not make the same mistake, and the Sith as a whole benefit.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: You see, Mekel? It is not so difficult. Time for your punishment.

speaker: Player
text: This is completely unfair!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Oh? Just how long have you been a Sith, anyhow? A bit dainty around the edges, aren't we?

speaker: Player
text: Mekel is a monster. He deserves to die.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: No hesitation before the kill. Now that's what I like to hear.

speaker: Player
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Player
text: Go ahead. Do your worst.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Now, now, is that any kind of attitude to take with higher education? I'm doing you a favor, really.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: I'm sure we could. You could even try using your feminine wiles on me. But, quite frankly, I'm quite determined and not above killing a woman. Even a pretty one.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: No? Blast it! What have they been teaching you children in that academy these days!

speaker: Player
text: Yes, I've been told about you.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: That's good. It's nice to still be the topic of discussion ocassionally. Maybe there's a class on me? Mmm... hmm... maybe not.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Liar. You think I can't tell? Obviously the academy is lax in its training, as usual. Stupid Uthar.

speaker: Player
text: The old hermit in hiding?

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: What?! Old hermit?! Can't that blasted Uthar teach a single thing right these days?! Slander! That's what it is!

speaker: Player
text: I don't care who you are! You're dead!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Oh, my, my, my. Such glorious vim! If I could bottle it and drink it, I would. Hmmm... there's a thought.

speaker: Player
text: I demand to be released at once!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Ha ha ha! I maaay do that. In time, in time. But for now, I've decided to keep you in restraints. No point in you getting strange ideas in your head and ruining my fun.

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: No, no. Let's keep things on a more civilized note, shall we? Now then... introductions are always the place to start, if I remember correctly.

speaker: Player
text: I'll kill you for this, old man!

speaker: Jorak Uln
text: Oh-ho! Spiteful little thing, aren't you? Let's not forget, however, who has whom at the disadvantage, shall we?

speaker: Waitress
text: Please don't hurt me - I just serve the food here, that's all! I'm not like these others - I'm not even a Black Vulkar. Please don't kill me!

speaker: Player
text: How did you end up here in the Vulkar base?

speaker: Waitress
text: My name is Ada. My father owed Davik some money, but he couldn't pay. Davik killed my father and sold me into slavery here at the Vulkar compound to pay off the debt.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry, I just want to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Waitress
text: But I don't know anything! I'm just a prisoner here - a slave! The Vulkars don't tell me anything, they treat me like dirt, they beat me if I screw up their orders.

speaker: Carth
text: You may know more than you think, miss. Help us and we'll help you, okay?

speaker: Waitress
text: Well... alright. I still don't know how much help I can be. But I sure hope you get rid of all the Vulkars. I hate them!

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find the prototype swoop engine accelerator?

speaker: Waitress
text: What? I... I've never heard of such a thing. I guess it might be in the garage on the lower level - that's where all the Vulkars go to work on their swoop bikes.

speaker: Waitress
text: But I've never been down there. The elevator is protected by a security system - only the Vulkars are allowed to go down there.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for a prisoner. A woman named Bastila.

speaker: Waitress
text: Is she that Republic soldier? I heard one of those Vulkar mention her, but she's not here. He said Brejik didn't trust his men around her.

speaker: Waitress
text: I guess she's too important to be a slave here in the kitchens, getting pawed and groped and kicked and spit on like me. Brejik must have taken her somewhere safe.

speaker: Player
text: If I let you go can you find your way out of here?

speaker: Waitress
text: Now that you've killed the guards who were supposed to watch me I think I could find my way out of here.

speaker: Player
text: Hurry, then - get out of here.

speaker: Waitress
text: I... I'm free to go? You're not going to kill me? I... I don't know how I can ever repay you. Thank you! Thank you! I... I have to get out of here before any of the Vulkars see me.

speaker: Player
text: Answer my questions and I'll let you go.

speaker: Player
text: Leaving you alive is too risky. Sorry, sister... looks like your order is up!

speaker: Carth
text: No, no wait. This girl is no threat to us. Just run along, miss, and get out of here. And do it quickly before the Vulkars come back.

speaker: Waitress
text: No - I won't go out like this! Not after all I've been through! I won't just let you kill me without a fight!

speaker: Player
text: You better give me some information if you want to live.

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: Lord Malak was most displeased when he learned you had escaped Taris alive! He has promised a great reward to whoever destroys you.

speaker: Uriah
text: Hi there... not too many people come in here to speak to me anymore. Most prefer the fancy surroundings of the Upper City Cantina.

speaker: Uriah
text: But nobody up there carries the kinds of Pazaak cards I sell. Are you interested in purchasing some individual cards to bolster your Pazaak deck?

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Uriah
text: I'm talking about Pazaak. You know - high stakes gambling. Each player brings their own deck to a Pazaak match, and the better your cards are the better your chances of winning.

speaker: Uriah
text: My name is Uriah. Everybody knows I'm the man to see if you want to add some cards to your Pazaak deck. My prices are quite reasonable.

speaker: Uriah
text: So, what do you say? Are you interested in buying some of my Pazaak cards to augment your own deck?

speaker: Player
text: Show me what you have for sale.

speaker: Uriah
text: I haven't been able to restock my inventory since the Sith quarantine started. But I've still got a pretty good selection.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have my own deck.

speaker: Uriah
text: You don't? Well, not much point in you looking at my inventory then. My individual cards aren't much good without the basic deck.

speaker: Uriah
text: If you're interested in Pazaak you should go speak to Garouk in the Upper City cantina. He's looking to retire and sell his deck. Might even give you a lesson, too.

speaker: Uriah
text: Anything else you need?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Uriah
text: If you want information you should speak to Zax in the bounty office. He's Davik's unofficial earpiece. But I'll try and answer your questions as best I can.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Davik.

speaker: Uriah
text: I'm not stupid enough to start bad mouthing Davik Kang in this place. Not with Zax so nearby. Go to the bounty office and talk to him if you want the scoop on Davik.

speaker: Player
text: I want some general information on the Lower City.

speaker: Uriah
text: Don't know what I can really tell you. There's a gang war between the Hidden Beks and the Black Vulkars, but everybody knows about that.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Uriah
text: The Beks are run by a man named Gadon Thek. They used to run things here in the Lower City and life wasn't too bad. But now the Vulkars are trying to move in.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Black Vulkars.

speaker: Uriah
text: The Vulkars are led by Brejik. He's tough and ruthless and maybe even a little insane. He's also determined to take control of the entire Lower City away from the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Uriah
text: When the Hidden Beks ran things, people could walk the Lower City streets in safety. But now the Black Vulkars attack people on sight. Watch out for them.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about those Republic escape pods that crashed down in the Undercity?

speaker: Uriah
text: The Undercity? You don't want to be going down there - the place is crawling with rakghouls! Do yourself a favor and forget about those escape pods.

speaker: Uriah
text: Besides, there's probably nothing left of those pods anyway. The Hidden Beks and the Black Vulkars would have stripped anything valuable from them within hours of the crash.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Uriah
text: Suit yourself. If you ever need to purchase some Pazaak cards to strengthen your deck just come speak to me again.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Uriah
text: My name is Uriah. I'm the man to see if you want to get an edge over your competitors in the grand old game. You follow me?

speaker: Uriah
text: Ah, the hero of the swoop race makes an appearance to brighten our day in this dingy cantina. People all over the Lower City are talking about your glorious victory.

speaker: Uriah
text: I've never cared much for the swoop race myself. I guess that's why I sell Pazaak cards. You need some cards to augment your deck?

speaker: Uriah
text: Back again? Is there something else I can do for you? Are you looking for some cards to augment your own Pazaak deck?

speaker: Garouk
text: Good luck: I hope the game's as good to you as it was to me. Now, is there anything else I can do for you?

speaker: Player
text: I'd like a Pazaak lesson.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Garouk
text: Of course, of course. My mind isn't as sharp as it used to be - that's why I'm giving up the gambler's life. But I think I can still manage to answer some simple questions.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Garouk
text: My name's Garouk. I used to be a card shark - one of the best Pazaak players on the Outer Rim. But that was before I retired from the gambling life.

speaker: Player
text: You're giving up gambling? Why?

speaker: Garouk
text: Don't get me wrong, the game's been good to me over the years. I've traveled the span of the galaxy, from the Core Worlds to the farthest reaches of the Outer Rim.

speaker: Garouk
text: I've won countless fortunes... and lost countless more. But that was long ago, and things have changed. Gambling is a young man's game.

speaker: Garouk
text: That's why I'm looking to get out. My offer still stands - fifty credits gets you my old Pazaak deck and a free lesson. A great offer if you can afford it.

speaker: Player
text: I can't afford that.

speaker: Garouk
text: I'm sorry to hear that, but fifty credits is my best offer. I'm practically giving the deck away at that price. If you want it, it's yours. If not, no hard feelings.

speaker: Player
text: Sure, I'll buy your deck.
comment: Player loses fifty credits, Pazzak deck added to inventory,

speaker: Garouk
text: Glad to see you're interested in the grand old game. The rules are pretty simple. Here: I'll load them up into your datapad so you can check them out anytime you want.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Garouk
text: Of course, of course. No sense in a youngster like you wasting your days away with an old man in a dingy bar. But if you ever want to chat, you know where to find me.

speaker: Garouk
text: That's why I sold my old deck to you. I don't have what it takes anymore, and I hate to let my cards go to waste.

speaker: Player
text: I want some general information on Taris.

speaker: Garouk
text: Mmm. Don't know what I can tell you that would be any use. The Upper City is nice enough, though it was better before the Sith showed up. But they don't bother an old guy like me much.

speaker: Garouk
text: Don't know much about the Lower City. It's rough down beneath. I just stay up here where it's safe and mind my own business.

speaker: Garouk
text: I don't see much point in worrying about that kind of stuff now that I've given up the gambler's life. Is there anything else I can do for you?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about those Republic escape pods that crashed down in the Undercity?

speaker: Garouk
text: I spend my days here in the cantina, sipping ale and chatting with the folks who wander by. I don't have much use or care what goes on outside these walls.

speaker: Garouk
text: Pretty soon all of Taris will be talking about how you beat Bendak in that fight, Stranger. You're famous now - but that's not necessarily a good thing.
comment: Dialog mission statement: Player can talk to Garouk and learn about playing Pazzak. Exit points: 1. Runs Pazzak tutorial, gives player basic Pazzak deck if he doesn't alreay have one. 2. Nothing happens

speaker: Garouk
text: The more well known you are the more chance the Sith will take an interest in you. And nobody wants that kind of attention.

speaker: Garouk
text: Is it true what everyone's saying? That you're going to fight Bendak Starkiller in a death match? You know, I'd love to see someone take that arrogant fool down!

speaker: Garouk
text: Back again? Is there something old Garouk can do for you, or did you just come to chat with a lonely old man?

speaker: Garouk
text: Hello there, youngster. You interested in buying the Pazaak deck of an old man looking to get out of the gambling game?

speaker: Garouk
text: Just fifty credits and I'll sell you all my cards. I'll even throw in a free lesson to boot. It's a great deal, if you can afford it.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: [This man appears to be looking for someone... maybe even one of your companions back on the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: Excuse me, have you seen a mechanic about? Short fellow, bald. I've been looking --

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, I'll be a Wookiee's uncle. Davin! Davin Kotras!

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: Ha! Jolee? Jolee Bindo? Why, you old freak! Last time I saw you, you were still wandering the galaxy in that old tug. I thought you were dead, old man.

speaker: Jolee
text: I crashed somewhere and decided to stay. Heh heh.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: Yeah, yeah, I'll just bet. Damn, old man, you look exactly the same as the last time I saw you! You pickle well.

speaker: Jolee
text: You're too kind. Not the young lad anymore yourself, I see.

speaker: Player
text: Jolee, we should be going...

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes, yes, right you are. Sorry, Davin, but duty calls. Maybe I'll run into you again soon.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: Of course, old man. Oh, wait... if you've been traveling in this sector, I suppose you heard about Sunry?

speaker: Jolee
text: No. Why? What's there to hear?

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: He's been picked up by the Selkath authorities here on Manaan. For murder.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's preposterous.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: I know. Elora is beside herself, as you can imagine. Maybe you could help them? I'm sure Sunry would appreciate a Jedi's assistance right about now.

speaker: Jolee
text: Perhaps I will at that. It's up to my old friend, here, actually. I'm just tagging along.

speaker: Player
text: We're on Manaan already. We could certainly check it out.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'd appreciate that. Sunry's an old friend... I'd hate to see him hurt.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: Same here. Well, heh, it was good to see you again. Give my regards to Elora, if you see her.

speaker: Jolee
text: I will. Be safe, old friend.

speaker: Player
text: We have more important things to do.

speaker: Jolee
text: I was expecting that. Still... if we get the chance, I'd be grateful. Sunry's an old friend... I'd hate to see him hurt.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not making any promises.

speaker: Jolee
text: Perhaps I will at that. It's up to my friend, here, actually. I'm just tagging along.

speaker: Player
text: We could check into it when we're on Manaan next.

speaker: Davin Kotras
text: He's been picked up by the Selkath authorities on Manaan. For murder.

speaker: Player
text: We don't have time for reunions.

speaker: Player
text: Care to introduce your friend, Jolee?

speaker: Jolee
text: What, are you deaf? His name's Davin. Old friend from my wanderer days. By the by, Davin, I really should be running off...

speaker: Gurney
text: Don't worry, if I hear anything you Sith will be the first to know... for a price of course.

speaker: Gurney021
text: You blew it! If you had brought that rakghoul serum to Zax he would have made it worth your while. But no - you had to go and do the honorable thing!

speaker: Gurney021
text: Now Zelka's mass-producing the serum and it's all but worthless. You cost me one hell of a finder's fee! You're as bad as Zelka - helping people when there's no profit in it!

speaker: Gurney021
text: I'm glad you took that serum down to Zax - I got a nice little finder's fee for helping Davik get his hands on the rakghoul cure. He gave me more than Zelka pays in a month!

speaker: Gurney021
text: Maybe if Zelka charged a little more for his services he could pay me what I'm worth - and maybe this place wouldn't be struggling so hard to stay in business.

speaker: Gurney021
text: Remember - if you get your hands on that rakghoul serum take it to Zax in the Lower City bounty office. He works for Davik, and he'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Gurney021
text: Psst. You there! Wait a minute. I need to talk to you about the rakghoul serum. I've got an offer for you you might want to hear.

speaker: Player
text: An offer? What are you talking about?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Zelka isn't the only one who wants to get his hands on the rakghoul serum. Davik Kang will pay you ten times what Zelka can if you can get the cure.

speaker: Player
text: Davik Kang? Who's that?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Oh, come on - everybody knows who Davik Kang is! He's the big boss around here. Gambling, smuggling, extortion - he's got a piece of all the action on Taris.

speaker: Player
text: You mean Davik's a crime lord?

speaker: Gurney021
text: I prefer to think of him as a role model. He started with nothing, and now he's got it all: credits, power, women. It's the Tarisian dream, right?

speaker: Player
text: Why does Davik want the cure so badly?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Davik's interested in anything that can turn a profit. He could make a fortune selling the serum to anyone infected with the disease - not like Zelka, who'll practically give it away.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I find Davik if I want to give him the cure?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Davik isn't the kind of guy you can just walk up to, you know? He likes to keep his business at arm's length.

speaker: Gurney021
text: The best thing to do is take the rakghoul serum to Zax. He runs the Lower City bounty office, but everyone knows he also works for Davik. He'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you care who gets the cure?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Look, Zelka can't afford to pay me much. If you sell the serum to Davik, I can probably get a nice finder's fee for directing you to him.

speaker: Player
text: What if I tell Zelka you're helping Davik get the cure?

speaker: Gurney021
text: Hmph. I'll just deny it. Who's Zelka going to believe - me, or some off-world stranger? Now, be smart about this. You'll get a better deal selling to Davik.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'd rather give the serum to Zelka. He'll use it to help people.

speaker: Gurney021
text: Helping people is all well and good, but you have to help yourself first, right? I'm telling you Davik will pay big credits for the cure. More than Zelka could ever afford.

speaker: Bastila
text: And then only the wealthiest patrons could acquire the cure. That is hardly fair.

speaker: Carth
text: If you haven't noticed, not much about this place is fair.

speaker: Bastila
text: That doesn't mean we have to actively work to make it worse, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: We're not in a position to be much more than just realists, are we?

speaker: Bastila
text: I am a Jedi. I will always try to help, if I can.

speaker: Gurney021
text: If you find the rakghoul serum, just take it to Zax in the Lower City bounty office. He works for Davik. He'll pay you what that cure is really worth!

speaker: Gurney
text: Hey, heh, who said anything about fair?

speaker: Carth
text: And then only the rich could afford the cure. Just let the poor suffer, right?

speaker: Player
text: I'll keep your offer in mind.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not interested.

speaker: Gurney021
text: Oh, don't be an idiot. Just listen to me for one minute and you won't be sorry. Davik Kang wants the cure, and you'd be smart to give it to him.

speaker: Gurney021
text: Can't you see I'm busy with my duties? Go talk to Zelka if you need something.

speaker: Daviktroop041
text: Don't... don't move! I'm... I'm not afraid to use this blaster if I have to!
comment: Dialog Mission Statement: Canderous encounters player wandering the undercity. Trooper initiates dialog. Players can speak to Canderous and then Rakghouls attack. After the attack Canderous and his men leave. Exit point 1: Rakghouls attack. Canderous and Trooper 41 are invulnerable. Everyone else can be killed. Exit point 2: Canderous and his men march off.

speaker: Canderous
text: Settle down, kid. We've already lost enough men to those damn rakghouls! The last thing we need now is more casualties from a needless firefight.

speaker: Canderous
text: Hm... by looks of you I'd say you're down here for the same reason we are: to salvage something from those downed Republic space pods.

speaker: Canderous
text: Let me give you some advice: forget about it. Do yourself a favor and just head back the way you came.

speaker: Player
text: Are you threatening me?

speaker: Canderous
text: Mandalorians don't make threats, we make promises. But I'm just trying to give you a friendly warning.

speaker: Canderous
text: This isn't a good place to stand around chatting. The Undercity is crawling with rakghouls. I've already lost half a dozen men to those monsters.

speaker: Daviktroop041
text: Canderous, I heard something! Over there, in the shadows! Sounded like a rakghoul!

speaker: Canderous
text: Looks like we've got company! Get those blasters ready, boys!

speaker: Player
text: Why - is there some danger down here?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Daviktroop041
text: That's Canderous Ordo! He's the most famous Mandalorian mercenary in this sector of the galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: I go where I want, when I want.

speaker: Canderous
text: Trying to pick a fight with a Mandalorian - I can see you're not too bright. But I'm on a mission for Davik, so I don't have time for fun and games.

speaker: Canderous
text: Damn! I told Davik this salvage mission was a bad idea! His men aren't trained for this kind of thing, and I can't babysit them all!

speaker: Canderous
text: Okay, boys... we're getting out of here before I lose anyone else. I can't carry all this salvage back by myself!

speaker: Canderous
text: You'd be smart to get out of here as well. Even if you can handle the rakghouls I doubt there's anything worth finding anymore.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by that?

speaker: Canderous
text: Davik sent me down here with this motley crew to scavenge whatever we could from the Republic escape pods that crashed during the recent battle overhead.

speaker: Canderous
text: But the Lower City gangs got here first. Anything worthwhile in those Republic pods is probably in their hands now. Davik won't like that.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Davik?

speaker: Canderous
text: What are you, an off-worlder? Everybody knows Davik. He's a member of the Exchange. You know - the interstellar crime syndicate.

speaker: Canderous
text: Smuggling, gambling, extortion - Davik controls it all here on Taris. That's why I'm working for him. But lately the Lower City gangs have been giving my boss some trouble.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Lower City gangs?

speaker: Canderous
text: This isn't really the place to have these kind of conversations. But I guess I could spare a couple seconds for you - after all, you did help us out with those rakghouls.

speaker: Canderous
text: The Lower City is overrun with gangs, but the two most important ones are the Hidden Beks and the Black Vulkars. Used to be the Beks were the big dog and kept the others in line.

speaker: Canderous
text: But lately the Black Vulkars are moving in on Bek turf and challenging them for control. The Vulkars are even starting to defy Davik!

speaker: Canderous
text: Take these escape pods, for example. Everyone knew Davik would want first crack at them, but I know for a fact those damn Vulkars have already sent their own salvage party down here.

speaker: Player
text: I better get going now.

speaker: Canderous
text: Come on boys... let's move out!

speaker: Player
text: So you're just going to run back to the surface like some coward?

speaker: Canderous
text: Normally I'd make you regret those words, but I'm not wasting another minute down here. I'm responsible for this whole company, and they won't survive down here much longer.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: You Sith should shut this guy up. I think he's violently dangerous. Just listen to him!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: This crazy street preacher keeps on about war and days of reckoning and the Sith just might lock him away.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: This guy's just stirring up trouble! Sure, there's a lot of aliens on Taris, but most of them stick to the Lower City.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: I'm no alien-lover, but I don't want to see them all killed! This kook's way out of line.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It is done. Freyyr... is dead. Speak with Chuundar, he will decide what happens now.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Chuundar is dead... and good riddance. Speak with my father. He will decide what is to happen now.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: You wear the uniforms of the Sith, but your actions prove you are not one of them. I... I do not know who you are, but I owe you my life.

speaker: Player
text: Why were those Sith interrogating you?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: I... I don't know. They thought... they thought I was part of some underground resistance. I don't know why they would suspect me... I'm completely innocent.

speaker: Player
text: Is there any kind of reward for saving you?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: I'm sorry, but I have nothing. As I tried to tell my captors during the interrogation, I am a poor traveler trapped here by the Sith quarantine - nothing more.

speaker: Player
text: Now I get the pleasure of killing you myself!

speaker: Carth
text: What are you doing? There's no need to go around drawing attention to ourselves. You there... just get out of here.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: Yes... I have no desire to be here when another patrol comes to investigate these deaths. Goodbye, and thank you once again.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: But... but... no! I won't die like this!

speaker: Player
text: Go on, get out of here.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: Thank you, human. The Sith would have killed me... of that I am certain. I don't know who you are, but it is clear you are no friend of the Sith.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: Among my people there is a saying: the enemy of my enemy is my friend. Like you I hate the Sith. That is why I stole those Sith uniforms for the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: In the Lower City there are some who do not bow to the conquerors. Swoop gangs like the Hidden Beks are gathering resources to one day strike against the Sith oppressors.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: If you wish to strike another blow against the Sith you would be wise to journey to the Lower City and speak with Gadon Thek, the leader of the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Player
text: What are the Hidden Beks planning?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: You would have to ask Gadon Thek to know the answer to that question. They approached me, and my only role was to obtain the Sith uniforms for them.

speaker: Player
text: Can you take me to Gadon?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: Access to the Lower City is restricted, I have never actually met Gadon. My only dealings were with members of his Hidden Bek gang.

speaker: Player
text: Can I get one of those uniforms from you?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: I am sorry, but all the uniforms I had were given to the Hidden Beks. I suppose you could take the uniforms from the bodies of the Sith soldiers in this room if you wanted.

speaker: Player
text: How about a reward for saving you?

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: I'm sorry, human, but I have nothing of value. The credits the Hidden Beks gave me for helping them against the Sith are long since spent.

speaker: Player
text: I should be going now.

speaker: Alien Prisoner
text: As should I. The Sith know my face now, I must find somewhere to hide on this world. Thank you once again, human.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith were right! You are a spy!

speaker: Player
text: The Hidden Beks? Who are they?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Yes! I heard that! Excellent job!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Thank you for locating the cache. Naturally I would see you rewarded, but I would prefer that everyone believe that I extracted the information.

speaker: Player
text: What?! Are you joking?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Of course not. Information extraction is my specialty... I'm not about to let it be known that some whelp did my job better.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: You had some fun, didn't you? Now run along and let's not turn this into anything unpleasant.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going to let you get away with this!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Oh? I suppose one would need to be alive to go running to Master Uthar to report the location of the cache, wouldn't they?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Does that mean that you are ready to battle a true Sith, then? Shall we make an issue of it?

speaker: Player
text: That's right! Let's go!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Ha! Gather your anger, then... and let us see who is superior!

speaker: Player
text: No, forget it.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Good. That's the way I prefer it. Now... to get rid of the prisoner and get to that cache...

speaker: Player
text: Fine, I don't care.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: What?! What have you done?!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: I told you not to put the prisoner into shock, didn't I?! Now how are we supposed to find out where the weapon cache is?! Uthar will be furious!!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Bah! Now I may as well take this fool and dump him somewhere. He's useless to us! I cannot believe you are so incompetent!

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Ahhh, maybe you can do better than I. This Mandalorian is proving more resistant than I expected.

speaker: Player
text: What are you trying to do?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: I'm trying to get him to tell us where his weapon cache is hidden. So far all the serum combinations I'm using are proving ineffective.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: If I bring his drug threshold too high, he'll go into shock and be useless. Too low and he just refuses to talk. It's been maddening.

speaker: Player
text: How do you drug him?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Just activate the console... it gives you a variety of options for serum dosage. The right amount applied at the right rate should do it.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: The real trick is that the only way to gauge your progress is to watch the prisoner closely for his reaction. Our scanners can't pick up his vitals.

speaker: Player
text: You want me to try it?

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Certainly. Just don't kill him or send him into shock. He's supposed to be questioned, not executed.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: If you manage to get the location of his cache out of him, it'll save me a lot of trouble. Up to you.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: If you manage to get the location of his cache out of him, I'll be sure to pass on the good word to Master Uthar.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Fine, go on then. I *must* know where his weapon cache is! Damn him!

speaker: Player
text: Err... no thanks.

speaker: Sith Interrogator
text: Don't bother me. I'm trying to think how I'm going to question this prisoner. I need to know where that cache is!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Talk to Ajuur, he's in charge here.

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Bendak is down! It's over! It's over! The fight is over! Bendak Starkiller is down! Bendak Starkiller is dead!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: All hail the Mysterious Stranger, the greatest duelist to ever grace the rings of Taris!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: The Stranger is down! The Mysterious Stranger is down!
comment: Player loses duel, announcer runs in and begins speaking

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: This is unbelievable, folks! Deadeye Duncan has won a fight! Is it possible we have a new contender for the title of worst duelist ever? Only time - and a possible rematch - will tell!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Gerlon Two-Fingers gets the win! And, for a change, it wasn't against Duncan. This has got to be a tough loss for the Mysterious Stranger. Imagine: losing to a crippled opponent!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Ice wins! Once again the Queen of Mean has dispatched her opponent in the ring. Hard luck, Stranger, but Ice is tough. She never goes down easy.

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Marl has done it again! Twenty years and still going strong for the veteran. And a hard lesson for the up and coming rookie. Better luck next time, Stranger.

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Twitch has done it! Once again the wild-eyed champion has defended his title! But don't give up, Stranger - we all want to see you go after the champ again!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: It's over! The fight is over! The Mysterious Stranger has won!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: But really, are any of us surprised? Deadeye losing isn't news. You have to do better than that to impress us, Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Gerlon losing to a rookie: is this a sign that his injuries have finally caught up with him? Or is the Mysterious Stranger for real? Only time will tell!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Ice is knocked out cold! Looks like we have a rising star in the Mysterious Stranger, folks: but how high can this star soar? You'll just have to watch and see!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Marl is down, and questions abound! Is this the end for the long time vet? Is it time for Marl to hang up his spurs? And what of the Mysterious Stranger?

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Twitch is waiting in the wings... do you dare take a shot at the champion himself? Will the wild-eyed wonder finally be unseated?

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Twitch's reign of terror is over! Ladies and gentlemen, we have a new champion - the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Ladies and gentlemen, come with me now on a journey to the savage days of years gone by... to a time when two combatants entered the arena, and only one came out alive.
comment: cut scene  spot lights and effects in the ring to get the crowd fired up

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: They're illegal, they're banned, they've been outlawed for nearly ten years - but we've got one for you tonight! A good, old fashioned death match!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: In this corner, a living legend. A man who's very name would make his opponents shake in their boots... if any of them were still alive. Ha ha ha! Out of retirement for one last battle: Bendak Starkiller!
comment: wild cheering after Bendak's name announced, Bendak walks into ring

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: And who would be crazy enough to step into the ring with such a lethal legend? Who would be mad enough to face almost certain death merely for your enjoyment?

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Ladies and gentlemen, feast your wondering eyes on... the Mysterious Stranger!
comment: more cheering, player walks into ring

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: And now, the moment we've all been waiting for... LET THE DEATH MATCH BEGIN!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Ladies and gentlemen, draw your eyes to the center ring! We have a very special presentation in store for you:

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Hold on to your seats and stay back from the edges of the ring! He's wild, he's unpredictable, he's borderline psychotic... and he's the best damn duelist in the game today. Give it up for Twitch!
comment: Wild cheering, chants of "Twitch, Twitch, Twitch!" in the background.

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: But Twitch's opponent plans to take the champion down! Night after night, battle after battle we've watched this young phenom rise through the ranks...

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: In this corner, the challenger for the title of Taris Dueling Champion - the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: He's a legend in the sport, a twenty year veteran who still knows how to show the young kids a trick or two. Let's have a big hand for... Marl!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: But there's always some young gun coming up to knock the veterans off... and we've got one of the best right here! I give you, the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: Over in this corner, a woman with steel on her bones and ice water in her veins. She's cold and quick as death itself. You know her, you love her... Ice!
comment: Loud applause, hoots and hollers, some wolf whistles

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: And in the other corner, a rising star taking that first step into the big leagues... I give you the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: In this corner, one of the greats; a man so tough even a disfiguring injury couldn't end his career. I give you Gerlon Two-Fingers!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: And in the other corner, a relative newcomer to the Taris dueling scene. Emerging from the shadows with no history, no past and no name... the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Duel Announcer
text: You've seen him lose night after night after night. But this time, he's after fresh meat. In this corner I give you Deadeye Duncan!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: What... what do you want? I'm not doing anything wrong. I'm just standing here... please, don't take me in for questioning!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Hey - didn't you just win the big swoop bike race in the Lower City? Yeah, it was you, I'm sure! That race was amazing!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Too bad Brejik wouldn't pay up on his wager! Oh well - he got what was coming to him.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: I hear there's a gang war between the Hidden Beks and the Black Vulkars raging in the lower city.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: I hear the crime lord Davik has a ship that can break through the Sith blockade.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Have you got your tickets for Bendak Starkiller's return to the duel ring? I hear it's going to be an illegal death match!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: Check this out... we got a real live celebrity here. The Mysterious Stranger mixing with the common folk!

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: I lost a bundle betting against you, Stranger. Next time I'll know better.

speaker: Taris Citizen
text: That new mercenary working for Davik - I heard he's a Mandalorian! I wonder if he fought in the Mandalore Wars?

speaker: Selkath Apprentice
text: The Master has promised to teach me great things. I am most eager to learn.

speaker: Selkath Apprentice
text: We shall give you a chance to prove your claims against the Sith, human.
comment: Declare on sight, go hostile and attack

speaker: Eli Gand
text: So, new spacers have come to wild Kashyyyk? Please, look well upon the wares of Eli Gand. I live to serve your needs.
comment: A vendor that is stationed on the landing ramp on Kashyyyk. Dark-haired human Eli Gand (ee-lie gand) A stranded fair-haired human spacer is next to him. Matton Dasol

speaker: Matton Dasol
text: Just be sure to pay cash. The interest on his loans will drain you like a Deluvian fatworm on a Hutt's backside.

speaker: Eli Gand

speaker: Rodian Prisoner

speaker: Rodian Prisoner

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Though I think your time would be better spent interrogating the Sandrals as to the whereabouts of my son Shen!

speaker: Player
text: Why are you so certain the Sandrals are to blame?

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Many years ago I brought my family here to Dantooine to escape the crush of humanity on the Core Worlds.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Soon after we settled here, the Sandrals arrived. And they have been a plague upon my house ever since!

speaker: Carth
text: Somehow I imagine the story from the Sandrals would sound just about the same, don't you?

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: The injustices the Sandrals have committed against the Matales are far too numerous to name, but the Council is well aware of our many disputes.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Recently, I discovered several Sandral droids trespassing on my land.

speaker: Player
text: What were they doing here?

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: I have no idea what nefarious purpose lay behind their arrival - my own assassination, perhaps. Destruction of my property. Maybe a simple spy mission. I wasn't about to find out.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: My own security droids destroyed the invaders - not a single one survived.

text: At least you're efficient.

speaker: T3M4
text: [Alarmed] Beep beep!

text: Err... no, I don't think the droids were very frightened, Teethree.

text: It was shortly after this incident that Shen, my only son and heir to the Matale estate, vanished.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Obviously Nurik, the unscrupulous head of the Sandral clan, has abducted my son in retaliation for the destruction of his droids!

speaker: Player
text: I shall go and speak to Nurik Sandral.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: The only resolution possible is the immediate return of my son!

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Why does the Council insist on stalling? The life of my son is at stake! Is it possible... yes, of course. Now I understand.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: I am a man of the world, Jedi. I know how things are done. I will make a... contribution... of 1,000 credits to the Council in exchange for rescuing Shen from the Sandrals.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: I will present the credits directly to you, of course. Whether the Council ever learns of this "donation" is completely up to you.

speaker: Player

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Eventually I will take whatever action is necessary to rescue my son... including razing the entire Sandral estate!

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: It is the Sandrals who have started this. Not I.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: I don't need to stand here and listen to such impertinence!
