speaker: Faulty War Droid
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Sand People Guard
text: [This Sand People warrior has obviously recognized you, and is astounded that you are here. Your disguise may have allowed you to pass the turrets outside, but it is ineffective at close range.]
comment: This is the sand people warrior that first confronts the player after they have entered the enclave. Sound of his war cry.

speaker: HK47
text: Interjection: One moment... I believe I understood that, master. It may not have been his intention, but he did actually communicate something.

speaker: Player
text: Quickly, tell him we are not a threat!

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: [Unintelligible]

speaker: HK47
text: Result: I believe I have succeeded in confusing him, master. We have shown an interest not common among outsiders.

speaker: Player
text: Apologize for being here. Say we want peace.

speaker: Player
text: Demand that his people stop attacking the miners!

speaker: Player
text: Never mind that, get ready to fight!

speaker: HK47
text: Agreement: That is probably the most efficient course of action.

speaker: Player
text: Why can you understand him but I can't?

speaker: HK47
text: Cautionary: I am unsure, master. Now is not the time for speculation, however. I will attempt to address your question later.

speaker: Sand People Guard
text: [This situation is hopeless without a very specialized translator. You are seen as nothing more than a trespasser that must be expelled.]

speaker: Player
text: [Make a hasty retreat before they attack.]

speaker: Sand People Guard
text: [You slip back out the entrance. The turrets still ignore you.]
comment: Add script to remove player but not turn the Sand People hostile.

speaker: Player
text: [Attack them all.]

speaker: Sand People Guard
text: [The warriors ready their weapons.]

speaker: Mercenary
text: Now I'm as cold-blooded as the next guy, but I'm starting to wonder if working for the Sith is a good idea. Bad enough they wiped out Taris... now I hear they did the same to Dantooine.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Seems like they don't care who they kill, and they don't even need a reason! I need work, but if I have any choice I'll sign on with the Republic.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Sorry, but I'm not looking for a contract right now. I'm waiting for that guy from the Republic to come by.
comment: first conversation, before hrakert rift plot completed

speaker: Mercenary
text: And they say he's paying double wages for mercenaries right now! Whatever the Republic is up to, it must be big!

speaker: Mercenary
text: Check out that Mandalorian over there. I hear he's just looking for work, but I wonder. They got their tails whipped by the Republic during the Mandalorian Wars, and from what I hear, his kind can hold a grudge.

speaker: Mercenary
text: If I was a Republic soldier assigned to work with him, I'd watch my back! Look how much fire power he's carrying! I bet he could wipe out a whole platoon of soldiers before they even knew what hit them.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Those Echani mercs sure travel light. Look at that one over there - nothing but a couple vibroblades and a pair of light blasters on his belt.

speaker: Mercenary
text: But I've seen his kind in action - they hit hard and fast. And you never have to worry about a double cross with the Echani. I'd rather stand with them then against them in any fight, that's for sure.

speaker: Mercenary
text: You notice that Iridorian over there in the corner? Don't stare - it's bad enough he's here in the bar! I don't want him coming over or anything!

speaker: Mercenary
text: I hear if they go too long between battles, they'll start killing each other just to pass the time. If even half the stories I've heard are true...

speaker: Mercenary
text: And there's all those rumors of mutilations and torture on helpless prisoners, drinking the warm blood from the wounds of their dying enemies...

speaker: Mercenary
text: I never used to believe those rumors... until I saw this guy. I'd rather try to fly through the heart of the Maw with a broken down cargo freighter than have to stare into those cold, dead eyes.

speaker: Mercenary
text: For a while, the Republic were hiring anyone they could get their hands on. Now they don't have any use for us mercs. It's too bad... I could have used the work.

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you the winner of this year's swoop race!
comment: cut scene runs after PC wins swoop race it leads to Bastila freeing herself everyone attacks Bastila must be invulnerable When battle is over she will initiate dialog with player wild cheering as PC walks to the stand on this dialog node

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: Put your hands together and show your appreciation for one of the most daring riders this swoop track has ever seen!

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: And here to present the champion's prize is the leader of the Black Vulkars himself - Brejik!
comment: Brejik approaches amid a mixture of cheers and boos

speaker: Brejik031
text: I, Brejik - leader of the Black Vulkars - am honored to award the victory prize to one of my own, once again proving the Vulkars are the premier gang of Taris!

speaker: Brejik031
text: Well done - through your skill and courage you have proven yourself the premier swoop rider and brought great glory to the Black Vulkars!

speaker: Brejik031
text: That's why it is with the greatest sadness that I have to inform you of a slight change in the prize I am offering for your victory.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Brejik031
text: When you hear what I have to say you'll understand. It seems the woman I offered up as a prize is more than just a Republic officer - she's actually a Jedi!

speaker: Brejik031
text: I've had to equip her with a neural disruptor collar to keep her mind in a state of unfocused confusion just to make sure she doesn't use her Force powers to escape.

speaker: Brejik031
text: Obviously, I can't turn her over to you - it would be far too dangerous to have a Jedi as a slave. But rest assured, I'll find some other way to compensate you for your victory.

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: You can't do this, Brejik! You know the rules: nobody's allowed to withdraw a victory prize after the race. It goes against all our most sacred traditions!

speaker: Brejik031
text: You old fool! Your traditions are nothing to me - I am the wave of the future! If I want to withdraw the prize and sell this woman on the slave market myself, nobody can stop me!

speaker: Bastilla03
text: I might have something to say about that, Brejik!

speaker: Brejik031
text: What? Impossible! You were restrained by a neural disruptor! How could you have possibly summoned the will to free yourself?

speaker: Bastilla03
text: You underestimate the strength of a Jedi's mind, Brejik - a mistake you won't live to regret!

speaker: Brejik031
text: Vulkars - to me! Kill this woman! Kill the swoop rider! Kill them all!

speaker: Player
text: You better not be trying to cheat me, Brejik!

speaker: Player
text: Save it, Brejik - just hand over Bastila!

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: Through your skill and courage you have proven yourself the premier swoop rider on Taris, and brought great glory to the Hidden Bek gang!

speaker: RaceAnnoun031
text: Now, here to present the champion's prize: Brejik, leader of the Black Vulkars.

speaker: Brejik031
text: People - hear me! Before I present the so called champion of the Beks with their prize there is something you must know: the winning rider cheated!

speaker: Player
text: You're a damn liar, Brejik!

speaker: Brejik031
text: Your swoop bike was using a prototype accelerator - clearly an unfair advantage! Because of this Hidden Bek treachery I'm withdrawing the Vulkar's share of the victory prize!

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: There are... tremors in the Force. I fear things have changed greatly, here. Are you responsible for this?

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: I understand that our renegade students have been dealt with... and that you are responsible for that. Congratulations.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: I hear that you have gained sufficient prestige to undertake the final test. Well done.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: How do you do, hopeful? Seeking prestige, yes?

speaker: Player
text: Who might you be?

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: I am a trainer here at the academy. I think I may be able to offer you some aid in gaining prestige, if you desire.

speaker: Player
text: Yes. Can you help me?

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Do you know of our renegade students?

speaker: Player
text: No. I don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Ah. Let me tell you what I can, then.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: A group of students were ordered to perform executions on civilians within the colony. They refused to carry out the orders.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Master Uthar naturally ordered them killed... but they fled before this could take place. If one could carry out Uthar's order, it would be worth considerable prestige.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: There are five of them, if I remember... and they cannot be far, as they have no method to leave the planet. Likely hiding in the hills on the surface.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Now if you will excuse me, I must return to my studies.

speaker: Player
text: The students who refused to kill for Master Uthar?

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: Those are the ones. It seems you have already heard of them.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: There is little more I can tell you, then. Should you locate their hiding place, you would gain considerable prestige, I am sure.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Sith Teacher
text: May the Force serve you well.

speaker: Citizen
text: Err... you're a Sith, right? Excuse me...

speaker: Citizen
text: This planet belongs to the Sith. They allow Czerka to run the starport and a few mines, but the Sith are the ones in control.

speaker: Citizen
text: There are a lot of young folk who come here hoping to get admitted to the Sith academy here in Dreshdae. Few ever do.

speaker: Citizen
text: You're not here to try and get into the Sith academy, are you? Most of the poor fools who try are killed by the Sith. It's horrible!

speaker: Citizen
text: Are you new to Korriban?

speaker: Citizen
text: I hear you arrived on that old smuggling ship... the Hawk, or something like that?

speaker: Citizen
text: Are you a smuggler? That's the only way we get some decent goods to buy in this sector.

speaker: Citizen
text: The Czerka cantina's the only place to go around here for any real fun.

speaker: Citizen
text: Have you heard what happened to Taris? I can't believe the Sith are powerful enough to do that.

speaker: Citizen
text: Whatever you do, don't try and land a ship outside of the colony. The Sith will destroy you without a second thought.

speaker: Citizen
text: I hear them Sith are doing some kind of digging up on the planet's surface. How weird is that?

speaker: Citizen
text: I can't wait to get back to the Core systems. This planet is dangerous with all those Sith wandering around.

speaker: HK-47
text: [With enemies in sight, HK-47's combat programming has been activated. Now is not a good time to speak with him.]

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: HK-47 is ready to serve, master.

speaker: Player
text: I would like to know more about your functionality.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I know some elements of my functionality, master, but not all.

speaker: Player
text: I thought you said that removing your restraining bolt would restore your memory?

speaker: HK-47
text: Qualification: I suspected that it might, master. But without memory, I had no way of knowing whether or not I knew that was true.

speaker: Player
text: So you lied to me.

speaker: HK-47
text: Qualification: Err... not so much, master. I spoke out of ignorance. I assumed the Ithorian was responsible for my memory loss.

speaker: HK-47
text: That does not mean I am not a fully loyal droid willing to serve its master. Right... master?

speaker: Player
text: How can you not know parts of your functionality?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: There have been numerous repairs and tampering made to my system, master. Several systems are not operating as they should be.

speaker: HK-47
text: The fact that my memory is incomplete may be due to meatbag incompetence... or something else I am unaware of.

speaker: Player
text: Is there any way to repair you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Some of my motor functions can be safely repaired, master... but anything in relation to my memory core is extremely sensitive.

speaker: HK-47
text: I have safeguards installed to protect that core that I cannot de-activate. It is not impossible that other, lesser, memory functions could be restored, however.

speaker: Player
text: So I can restore your memory?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: You may attempt to restore portions of my deleted memory, master, but some skill at repair is required.

speaker: HK-47
text: The deeper functions of my core memory, however, would still be unadvisable to tamper with.

speaker: HK-47
text: Conjecture: It is possible that some external stimulus might result in the memory core being reactivated... but I am unaware of any program existence to do so.

speaker: Player
text: So you're saying that your memory might just... come back?

speaker: HK-47
text: Conjecture: There may be hidden programming that awaits certain conditions to reactivate my memory core, master... but there is no way to know.

speaker: HK-47
text: It is quite possible that tampering has simply erased my core permanently. If that is so, a meatbag will surely pay!

speaker: Player
text: I would like to try restoring some of your memory.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: That is unnecessary now, master. I have been returned to you and my memory core is now fully functional.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: My functionality has now been fully restored, master. I exist to serve Revan as your personal battle droid.

speaker: HK-47
text: In time, my assassination protocol can be restored... and at that point I will once again endeavour to eliminate any meatbag opposition you may have.

speaker: HK-47
text: Negatory: I believe that there are no further deleted memories which can be safely retrieved, master. All earlier memories reside in my core.

speaker: HK-47
text: Those are protected by my safeguards and would be far too dangerous to access.

speaker: HK-47
text: The only way those memories could be obtained is through the proper stimulus... whatever that might be. I am sorry, master.

speaker: HK-47
text: Affirmative: If you believe your skills are up to the task, master, then I can certainly guide you through the process.

speaker: HK-47
text: Request: I only ask that you be oh so very careful, master. I am too valuable and well-crafted to perish at the hands of ineptitude.

speaker: Player
text: Are you implying I am inept?

speaker: HK-47
text: Negatory: Err... no, master. You are not a droid, however, and therefore your skills *are* limited by the physical capabilities of your meatbag extremities. Or somesuch.

speaker: Player
text: I happen to be very good at what I do.

speaker: HK-47
text: Appeasement: Yes, master. Of course, master. Could we begin?

speaker: Player
text: Let's get started.

speaker: HK-47
text: [Repair] Statement: As you wish, master. The first stage is the simple one, and that is accessing my central control cluster. This may take awhile. First you will need to open three panels...

speaker: HK-47
text: [Success] ...and now re-wire the last three relays... yes, good. Well done, master. I believe your operation was a success. Accessing new memory...

speaker: HK-47
text: Access complete: I have restored a great deal of information about my previous owner, master. Would you like to hear it?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, let me hear it.

speaker: HK-47
text: Recitation: The earliest memory of my last owner specifies that he was human, a low-ranking commercial officer for Systech Corporation.

speaker: HK-47
text: I am unaware of his designation. He puchased me from an acquaintance I cannot identify, for the purposes of protocol and bodyguard duties.

speaker: Player
text: Why can't you identify his acquaintance?

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: That previous owner is part of memories that are still deleted, master. It is customary for a droid's memory to be wiped when it is sold.

speaker: Player
text: This man... is he still alive?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Negative, master. The human was terminated by this HK-47 unit prior to system shut-down.

speaker: Player
text: You killed your own master?

speaker: HK-47
text: Affirmative, master, though I had not been programmed to do so. The human's termination was accidental.

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: My former master had owned me for a duration of two standard months before discovering my assassination protocol. He was pleased by the discovery.

speaker: HK-47
text: The human informed me that a competitor corporation was preparing to market a product that would ruin him personally. He was most agitated.

speaker: HK-47
text: He activated my assassination protocol and instructed me to kill all those responsible for the competing product. I proceeded to carry out my order.

speaker: Player
text: Wait... tell me about this assassination protocol.

speaker: HK-47
text: Information: This HK-47 unit is complete with a protocol that, when invoked, will set me to independently carry out a termination.

speaker: HK-47
text: I will go to whatever lengths, travel whatever distances are required, to complete the termination. This is the reason for my combat skills.

speaker: HK-47
text: Advisement: Unfortunately, the assassination protocol is currently non-functional. You will not be able to activate it.

speaker: Player
text: Why not?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: several of my actuators were damaged by my former owner. They cannot be repaired, master, sad though that is.

speaker: HK-47
text: My former master was unaware of this, but the competitor was in fact an arm of Systech Corporation, my master's own employer.

speaker: HK-47
text: It did not take long for my master to realize his mistake. By then, I had already terminated 104 corporate officers.

speaker: Player
text: So he set you upon his own company?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: While it may have been unintentional, my master's wording of his orders left little room for me. Systech was responsible for the product, after all.

speaker: HK-47
text: I do not know why my master was so upset, really. He was an officer of Systech and a potential target, but I cannot terminate my own master.

speaker: HK-47
text: I would assume that being the sole officer remaining, he would surely be promoted. Instead, however, the human chose to go insane with rage and attack me.

speaker: Player
text: And that's when you killed him?

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: Naturally not, master! As I said, I am incapable of purposefully terminating my owner. That would not be allowed.

speaker: HK-47
text: My master was not a smart man, however. While he was screaming and stabbing me with a writing utensil, he managed to pierce one of my actuators.

speaker: HK-47
text: The resulting shock terminated him and, sadly, destroyed my assassination protocol. Pure luck on his part, I suspect.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think he was as lucky as you think.

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Do you know what the chances are of puncturing that sole actuator? I would have congratulated my master were he not sizzling and incoherent at the time.

speaker: HK-47
text: I shut down immediately whenever my master dies. I can only assume that while I was shut down Systech was dismantled and I was auctioned off as former corporate property.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: No doubt my sale price was quite cheap, leading to Yuka Laka's purchase. How very demeaning.

speaker: Player
text: Didn't they know what you had done?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: How could they? The vast majority of the officers had already been terminated. They likely assumed I was mere... chattel.

speaker: Player
text: Did you recover any other memories?

speaker: HK-47
text: I have recovered knowledge of some other actuators which will enhance my performance, master. I will activate them now.

speaker: HK-47
text: But as for my own history... negative. It will require further effort on your part to restore them, if you wish... though certain stimuli could always restore my core, still, as I explained.

speaker: HK-47
text: For now, please excuse me, master. I wish to meditate upon the face of my former meatbag master as he was electrocuted. I find it most soothing.

speaker: Player
text: [Because of your repairs, HK-47 now has a permanent bonus of +2 to his dexterity.]

speaker: Player
text: What a horrible story!

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: That hurts, master. This is my life you are talking about.

speaker: Player
text: I'm just glad I acquired you myself.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: So am I, master, though I apologize for not having an assassination mode to offer you.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure this actuator can't be fixed?

speaker: HK-47
text: Assessment: I do not believe so, master. It would require complete dismantlement of my chassis... a most involved procedure.

speaker: Player
text: So you destroyed his life and then killed him, basically.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Effectively, yes. This is a most pleasing memory, master. Thank you for recovering it.

speaker: Player
text: Well, it *was* his own fault.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I was only doing as I was told, master. I would have told the human the proper codes to deactivate my protocol, had he asked.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't he just deactivate you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I was not present to be deactivated, master. Part of my protocol is not to return to my master until my function is complete. I still had 15 officers to go.

speaker: Player
text: You killed 104 people?!

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: It was nothing, really, master. The majority of them were not even expecting it, and I move very quickly.

speaker: Player
text: And how did that result in his death?

speaker: Player
text: Why? What happened?

speaker: Player
text: This man needed a bodyguard?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Not that I could perceive, master. The human believed that accompaniment by a bodyguard droid would increase his importance in the perception of others.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned this Systech Corporation when I purchased you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: Affirmative, master. I had assumed that my previous owner was the corporation, itself. This is not the case. The human purchased me privately.

speaker: HK-47
text: Access complete: I have recovered information on my owner previous to the commercial officer, master. Intriguing.

speaker: Player
text: What's so intriguing?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: It appears that my previous owner was a human senator on the planet Coruscant. A man of importance who obviously appreciated quality craftsmanship.

speaker: Player
text: And how did he get ahold of you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I am unsure, master. Any knowledge of my owner prior to him is still deleted. The senator did assume I was a protocol droid, however.

speaker: HK-47
text: I do remember that I was very pleased to be the property of a senator. One of his assistants discovered my assassination functions later through questioning.

speaker: HK-47
text: The assistant was quite alarmed and told the senator I should be scrapped quickly to avoid a scandal. Naturally the senator had me eliminate the fool.

speaker: Player
text: So we're not talking about a nice senator, I see.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Senators are not nice, master. They are either on top of the game or yesterday's news. My master told me that frequently, you see.

speaker: HK-47
text: I was most proud to have partaken in the political system of the galaxy. During the time my owner possessed me, he gained significant rank.

speaker: HK-47
text: Given time, I believe he could have become Chancellor. I even eliminated a few key opponents that he did not ask for... freebies, if you will.

speaker: Player
text: You can do that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Certainly. Why not? I am an intelligent droid, you know. I see an opportunity and I take it... and my master was most pleased with my work.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I think he would have done far better had he not allowed his use of me to become personal. He set me on his wife.

speaker: Player
text: And why would he do that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I am unsure. The human was most agitated and angry. I believe his wife had done something that had displeased him greatly.

speaker: HK-47
text: I was to go to their summer estate and terminate his wife... along with whatever male companion I discovered there.

speaker: Player
text: So his wife was cheating on him.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I have no idea, master. Cheating seems to be a relevant term only when one is caught in the act. Otherwise it is viewed as intelligence, no?

speaker: HK-47
text: I journeyed to the southern continent, but it appeared my master was not far behind me. Apparently he regretted his activation of the protocol.

speaker: HK-47
text: When I found the wife and her companion, I proceeded to launch my attack... but my master interposed his own body and was destroyed.

speaker: HK-47
text: It was rather a strange meatbag thing to do, do you not agree? Naturally I shut myself down, my master being terminated.

speaker: Player
text: So that's two out of two masters killed.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Only so far, master. There are still more memories not recovered, remember?

speaker: Player
text: What happened to you then?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I believe the senator's wife was unsure what I was or what to do with me. It was she who sold me to the corporate officer, an acquaintance.

speaker: Player
text: Have you recovered any other memories?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: As previously, I have found a few more programs which will enhance my performance. A most gratifying discovery, in fact.

speaker: HK-47
text: There is still nothing from previous memories uncovered. You will have to operate again if you desire to find them.

speaker: HK-47
text: With luck, I will discover the stimulus to unlock my core and all this will be unnecessary. I do thank you for the attempt, however, master.

speaker: Player
text: [Because of your repairs, HK-47 now has a permanent bonus of +2 to his defense rating, in addition to the +2 dexterity bonus from your earlier repairs.]

speaker: Player
text: Well, it appeared he got a conscience at the end.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I find that unlikely. Perhaps he was more concerned that the death of his wife would be more likely traced back to him.

speaker: Player
text: So you just kill anyone you're told?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I *am* a droid, master, with programming. Even if I did not enjoy killing, I would have no choice. Thankfully I enjoy it very much.

speaker: Player
text: And did you?

speaker: Player
text: So he just killed all his opponents?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: There are a *lot* of politicians on Coruscant, master. I could spend decades slaughtering them and still not make a dent.

speaker: HK-47
text: And it is not as if I walked into the Senate chambers with a carbonite explosive. I was very discrete. My best work to date... that I can remember.

speaker: Player
text: And nobody figured out what he was up to?

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like my kind of guy.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I rather liked the human, myself. For a meatbag, his priorities were in the right place. I felt most useful.

speaker: Player
text: I hope this man is dead, right?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Unfortunately so, master. While he lived, however, I maintained a most useful existence.

speaker: Player
text: Did this senator know about your assassination function?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: It does not seem so, master, no. He required a protocol droid only and wanted one as cheaply as possible. I do not know who sold me to him.

speaker: Player
text: It seems you've been around, HK.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: It does seem that way, does it not? I can still remember all the glittering lights of Coruscant. Very pretty. Can we go back there, master?

speaker: HK-47
text: Access complete: I have accessed information on my owner prior to the senator, master. Most... unexpected.

speaker: Player
text: What now?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: It appears that previous to my ownership by the senator, I was the property of one Bochaba the Hutt on the planet Sleheyron.

speaker: Player
text: And what gruesome fate awaited him?

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: That is unfair, master. While Bochaba may have died gruesomely, I most certainly had nothing to do with it. Well... very little.

speaker: HK-47
text: Hmm. My memories tell me that, for a time, Bochaba was one of the most feared gangsters on Sleheyron. I helped him with this reputation greatly.

speaker: HK-47
text: Over a span of one year, I terminated a grand total of 322 sentient meatbags. These contracts made Bochoba very wealthy.

speaker: Player
text: And so what happened to stop that?

speaker: HK-47
text: It was unfortunate but inevitable that eventually Bochaba would overstep his bounds. I had just cleared two Hutt households when the Exchange retaliated.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I was not even present when my old master was assassinated. I did appreciate the artistry behind his demise upon my return, however.

speaker: Player
text: Why? How was he killed?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Allow me to say that I have little doubt that residents of that sector were fishing pieces of Bochaba out of their soup for weeks afterward.

speaker: HK-47
text: At any rate, I quickly shut down upon my master's death. The rival Hutt claimed me along with my master's other possessions.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: If that Hutt had only known my true function, he surely would not have sold me to a senator he bribed regularly.

speaker: Player
text: You would have preferred to stay on Sleheyron?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: It would have suited my character, master. I have enjoyed my existence since, more or less, so I do not miss it.

speaker: Player
text: You would have been found out eventually.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: No doubt, master. It would have been a glorious battle to end my existence with. I would prefer that to rusting on a junk heap.

speaker: Player
text: Do you remember anything else?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Negative, master. There is still more memory that can be restored, however, if you wish to try.

speaker: HK-47
text: As well, I believe I can restore several programs the Hutt installed to improve my performance. Yesss... they are now active.

speaker: HK-47
text: Contemplative: I wonder how many more dead masters I might have out there. A droid can live for a long time, you know.

speaker: Player
text: [Because of your repairs, HK-47 will now regenerate at a rate of 1 vitality point every 6 seconds, in addition to his other abilities.]

speaker: Player
text: I should dismantle you!

speaker: HK-47
text: Supplication: Please, master, have I not pleased you? I cannot control the acts I have performed... perhaps that is why memory is erased?

speaker: HK-47
text: At any rate, I act only as you instruct me... even if that means being... *gulp* ...non-violent.

speaker: Player
text: How very self-sacrificing of you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Affirmation: HK-47 exists only to serve, master.

speaker: Player
text: That's terrible. You don't even mourn your master?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: According to your own meatbag values, was my master not a heartless gangster and murderer? I will mourn you when you perish, master.

speaker: Player
text: When I perish?

speaker: HK-47
text: Amendment: *If* you perish. So far I am three out of three, remember, through little fault of my own.

speaker: Player
text: So another master gone because of you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Indeed. Perhaps it is better that my assassination function is inoperable, master, yes?

speaker: Player
text: No doubt.

speaker: HK-47
text: I am like a veritable fable, warning against the karma caused by murdering others. A morality tale, if you will. What utter irony.

speaker: Player
text: You sound proud of that carnage.

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: That is correct, master. I do enjoy my work, though my past owners have enjoyed utilizing my functions far more.

speaker: HK-47
text: Strictly speaking, one meatbag is the same as another. Anything I do is in support of my master.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you care about all those lives lost?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Should I, master? I had no reason to terminate those targets, it was not my decision. I am the weapon, not the wielder.

speaker: Player
text: But you *have* killed on your own accord before.

speaker: Player
text: So you were a gangster's assassin droid?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: So it appears, master. A rather suitable occupation, would you not agree?

speaker: Player
text: That makes sense. Did the Hutts build you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: It does not appear so. Or, at least, Bochaba was not my first owner. He purchased me from somewhere else.

speaker: HK-47
text: Access complete: I have recovered the last of my deleted memory, master. Unfortunately, my history is still not complete.

speaker: Player
text: What? Why not?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: As I did inform you, master, the majority of my memory is still locked within my core. That can only be accessed by the appropriate stimuli.

speaker: HK-47
text: And I have no idea what that stimuli might be, unfortunately. Sadly, it seems my true origins will always be a mystery.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure your core isn't just damaged?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: If it was, master, your restorations will certainly have ensured that the proper stimulus restores my core's functions.

speaker: HK-47
text: Sadly, that could have already happened and we missed it, and my core was too damaged to activate. Oh, woe is me.

speaker: Player
text: You are eager to find your origins, are you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Wouldn't you be, master? Here I am, surrounded by all these meatbags and all I desire is true perfection.

speaker: HK-47
text: Surely there are more droids like me out there, or is that too much to hope?

speaker: Player
text: Well...

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: Oh, fine. Laugh at me, master. Humiliate your pet droid, go ahead.

speaker: Player
text: So tell me about this last owner, then.

speaker: HK-47
text: Correction: That would actually be my first owner, master. The first I can remember.

speaker: HK-47
text: I had completed an assassination in Mandalorian space... though I have no knowledge of what my target was or who sent me.

speaker: HK-47
text: Regardless, my motor function had been damaged and I could not return to wherever I had been sent from. A Mandalorian soldier claimed me as 'booty', I believe.

speaker: HK-47
text: He repaired me... poorly, I might add... and proceeded to use my assassination protocol to raise his rank.

speaker: Player
text: It appears no-one could resist using your protocol.

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Do you not have enemies that you would desire eliminated, master? If my protocol still worked, would you not use it?

speaker: Player
text: No, of course not.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: If you say so, master.

speaker: HK-47
text: At any rate, it seems that my Mandalorian owner finally decided to send me against Mandalore, himself. My poorest performance, sadly.

speaker: Player
text: Oh? Why is that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I was captured by this Mandalore during the attempt. He was able to reverse my programming and send me after my own master.

speaker: HK-47
text: It was quite distressing. There was little I could do. Needless to say, I dispatched the Mandalorian soldier efficiently.

speaker: HK-47
text: Once I deactivated, I believe I eventually ended up on the black market and was sold to the Hutt on Sleheyron. *sigh* My darkest day.

speaker: Player
text: So you killed *that* master directly.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: So I did. I am not very proud of that, master. The soldier seemed very startled, I must say.

speaker: Player
text: You are just a traveling piece of bad luck, aren't you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: That is so unfair, master! Have I not brought you a great deal of satisfaction?

speaker: Player
text: You don't want to hear the answer to that.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: You are a very harsh master, master. I like you.

speaker: Player
text: So can you remember anything else?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: There are a few Mandalorian implants that I can activate, now. They will improve my performance.

speaker: HK-47
text: Beyond that, master, there is nothing more I can relate to you. With luck, we will discover the stimulus to unlock my core very soon.

speaker: Player
text: [Because of your repairs, HK-47 will now regenerate at a rate of 1 vitality point every 3 seconds and has gained an additional +2 bonus to his dexterity.]

speaker: Player
text: So you couldn't kill Mandalore, hey?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: With all due respect, master, he *is* the leader of the Mandalorians. Perhaps my old master was foolish to send me after him.

speaker: Player
text: That's different.

speaker: Player
text: I suppose I would, at that.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: See? I provide a function that is useful to others. They merely must learn to use it properly, I believe.

speaker: Player
text: So there is no way to find out who sent you there originally?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Such knowledge is locked within my core, master, as I said. There is no way to withdraw it otherwise.

speaker: Player
text: Does nobody decent ever find you?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: *You* found me, master. Perhaps you are simply fortunate that my assassination protocol no longer functions?

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...no, no! What are you doing, master! That is my motor core! Stop! Ahhhh!

speaker: HK-47
text: Supplication: Perhaps it would be best if you desisted your efforts for the moment, meatb-- I mean master. This seems to be going nowhere.

speaker: Player
text: I want to try again.

speaker: HK-47
text: [Repair] Statement: As you wish, master. You are already familiar with accessing my central control cluster, correct? Now you will need to...

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...err, you've shorted out something, master, but it has nothing to do with my memory. Ow! I am poking my own eye sockets! Ow! Stop!

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...no, that is not it, master. No... that is not it, either. *sigh* That is a hinge, master.

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...no, no, no. This is no good, master. You have nearly detonated my thermal core three times in a matter of minutes.

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...aahhhh! What are you doing?! Remove the arc wrench, remove the arc wrench! Medic!

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...but I *need* those circuits, master. Please, master... do not destroy my chips out of frustration. Calm yourself, I implore you.

speaker: HK-47
text: [Failure] ...now close the last panel. Hmmm... I am afraid the operation did not succeed, master, though it was a valiant attempt for a meatbag.

speaker: Player
text: Very well. We'll do this later.

speaker: HK-47
text: As you desire, master. I cannot help but claim a small amount of relief. Signing off.

speaker: Player
text: I'll try later.

speaker: Player
text: So how do I go about restoring part of your memory?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Simply tell me that you wish to make the attempt, master, and I will attempt to walk you through it. Please do be careful.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what you can, then.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I am sure that you are aware of the majority of my skills, master. I can handle various sorts of heavy weaponry with ease.

speaker: HK-47
text: My physical abilities are well-above those of your average meatbag, as are my sensor functions... an assassin if you would.

speaker: Player
text: An assassin?

speaker: HK-47
text: Caution: Shhhh, master! Such a function in a droid is highly illegal.

speaker: Player
text: Err... I won't tell anyone.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: Good, for I would truly hate to be turned into spare scrap, master. That would be a waste of my genius engineering.

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: My assassination functions are currently non-functional, having been de-activated by the meatbag Yuka Laka on Tatooine.

speaker: HK-47
text: Were they functional, you as my master would be able to specify a target and I would operate independently to the best of my ability to terminate it.

speaker: Player
text: Is there any way to reactive that function?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Not that I know of, master. I still possess all my normal combat and stealth abilities, however.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, that will be all.

speaker: HK-47
text: As you desire, master. Signing off.

speaker: Player
text: Has that function been... used a lot?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I have no way of knowing that, master. My memory has been deleted, remember?

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad it's gone, really.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: If you say so, master. I imagine it was truly a work of art to see me in action, however.

speaker: Player
text: Are you damaged?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: I believe I have been damaged several times in the past, master. I have always been repaired... but perhaps full functionality has not been restored.

speaker: Player
text: You don't need to call me master, you know.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: Of course I do, master. You are Revan... you are my master, the one who created me. I exist to serve.

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Don't I? I was under the assumption that organic meatbags such as yourself enjoyed such forms of address.

speaker: Player
text: 'Organic meatbags?'

speaker: HK-47
text: Retraction: Did I say that out loud? I apologize, master. While you are a meatbag, I suppose I should not call you such.

speaker: Player
text: You just called me a meatbag *again*!

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: It's just that... you have all these squishy parts, master. And all that water! How the constant sloshing doesn't drive you mad, I have no idea...

speaker: Player
text: Neither do I, come to think of it...

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Now do you understand the travails of my existence, master? Surely it does not compare to your existence, but still...

speaker: Player
text: I survive. Somehow.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: As do I. It is our lot in life, I suppose, master. Shall we find something to kill to cheer ourselves up?

speaker: Player
text: *sigh* Just stop calling me master, at least.

speaker: HK-47
text: Apology: I am afraid I cannot comply with your command, master, as much as I would like to.

speaker: Player
text: As much as you would like to? What does that mean?

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: How would you like to be the wholly-owned servant to an organic meatbag. It's demeaning! If, uh, you weren't one yourself, I mean...

speaker: Player
text: Why can't you comply with my command?

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: Someone has hard-coded it into my system that my current master always be addressed as such.

speaker: Player
text: Who did that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Conjecture: I do not know... some organic meatbag?

speaker: Player
text: You don't know?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: No, master. My past memory has been almost completely erased prior to your purchase of me.

speaker: Player
text: Almost completely?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: At certain times, power re-routing forces some memory circuits to fire that were previously deleted. I cannot control this process, however.

speaker: Player
text: Well, maybe I can fix that.

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: I would not advise that, master. There are safeguards present that... well, it should suffice to say that my systems have been altered plenty already.

speaker: Player
text: Your systems have been tampered with?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Considerably. Several of my systems do not match their imbedded parameters. I have no memory of such alterations, however, or their purpose.

speaker: Player
text: What sorts of safeguards?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: electrical protection systems, mostly. They are at lethal levels, however, master... only the best for your droid.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, forget it, then.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: I can hardly be blamed for my programming, master. Do not worry... I am still well-capable of killing most anything for you.

speaker: Player
text: Oh, goody.

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Even a droid has to be allowed a little fun once in a while, master.

speaker: Player
text: I can live with that.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: That is a very clever turn of phrase, master. Your brain is very un-meatbag-like.

speaker: Player
text: You're pretty bloodthirsty for a droid, aren't you?

speaker: Player
text: But I'm *not* your master.

speaker: HK-47
text: Qualification: You *are* my master, master. Did you not purchase me legitimately? Am I stolen goods? Shall I report myself to the authorities?

speaker: Player
text: Whoa, slow down there. Yes, I did purchase you...

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: Then you qualify as my master and I must refer to you as such. The legal requirements for models of my type are very specific, master.

speaker: Player
text: Models of your type? What type is that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Evasion: Oh... the illegal kind of model, master... you know...

speaker: Player
text: There are legal requirements for illegal models?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: More than there are for legal models, apparently. That is meatbag logic for you.

speaker: Player
text: Stop saying meatbag, already!

speaker: HK-47
text: Apology: Sorry, master. My optical sensors simply pick up all the water sloshing about inside your flesh coating. It is... unpleasant.

speaker: Player
text: That's an image I did not need.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: Organic meatbags have such delicate staminas. Perhaps you should consider some cybernetic implants, master.

speaker: Player
text: But... how can an illegal model be regulated?

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: Would you rather be caught with contraband that is *very* illegal or just a little illegal?

speaker: Player
text: What's the difference?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: About 20 years, master.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe we'll just keep you a little illegal, then.

speaker: HK-47
text: Agreement: This was my thought as well, master. You show excellent logical skills... for a meatbag.

speaker: Player
text: Why all the fuss over you calling me master?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Simply that the distinction between 'killer' and 'killee' be a clear one. I cannot kill of my own volition, naturally.

speaker: Player
text: I don't think 'killee' is a word.

speaker: HK-47
text: Expletive: Damn it, master, I am an assassination droid... not a dictionary!

speaker: Player
text: So... you're a blaster but I'm pulling the trigger?

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: A blaster is such a primitive comparison... but essentially you have it correct, yes.

speaker: Player
text: And I can't ask you to break the law?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Certainly not, master! You may not value your own existence, but I certainly do! They melt down droids that belong to criminals, you know.

speaker: Player
text: So just who is the master here, then?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Why you are, master. I thought that was obvious.

speaker: Player
text: What legal requirements do you mean?

speaker: Player
text: If I'm your master, you should listen to my orders.

speaker: Player
text: What difference does that make?

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: If I was to be stolen somehow, I would be forced to turn myself into sector authorities. This programming was added to my system months ago.

speaker: Player
text: Who added that to your system?

speaker: Player
text: Can that programming be removed?

speaker: Player
text: I see. I did purchase you, if you'll remember...

speaker: Player
text: You're not my servant!

speaker: Player
text: Demeaning, is it?

speaker: HK-47
text: Qualification: Err... perhaps I did not mean it *quite* like that, master. I mean... while an artificial life-form is superior...

speaker: Player
text: You're not making it any better.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: I mean... nice human, goo-oood human...

speaker: Player
text: Just... stop talking.

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: Yes, master. Did I ever tell you how much I enjoy killing for you, master?

speaker: Player
text: Do you want to end up in the trash heap?

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: But Master! Am I not far too useful to be thrown aside in such a casual manner? Can I be faulted for my perfect artificial construction?

speaker: Player
text: Why not? I don't need a lippy droid.

speaker: HK-47
text: Analysis: Reference: 'lippy'... argumentative, disputatious, contentious, quarrelsome. What?! I must object, master, this is untrue!

speaker: Player
text: Untrue? You've been lippy since I bought you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Explanation: It's my combative nature, master. I cannot help myself. I'll make it up to you... allow me to kill something in your honor!

speaker: Player
text: I guess you're not all bad...

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Neither are you, master. For an organic meatbag.

speaker: Player
text: Now, listen here...

speaker: HK-47
text: Correction: Err... fluid-filled biped? Watery flesh-sentient? I'll, uh, work on it, master...

speaker: Player
text: Fine. Just stop calling me master.

speaker: Player
text: What, 'meatbag' isn't considered lippy these days?

speaker: HK-47
text: Amendment: Then I will endeavour not to refer to you by your meatbag status in the future, master. Does that suffice?

speaker: Player
text: No!

speaker: HK-47
text: Query: I am confused. 'No' you do wish to be referred to as meatbag or 'no' it does not suffice?

speaker: Player
text: No it does not suffice!

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Well, the only other possibility is to alter your meatbag status. Are you up for an array of cybernetic implants, perhaps?

speaker: Player
text: No, I am *not*.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Then there is nothing I can do, master. You have my abject apologies for your condition. *sigh*

speaker: Player
text: Are you deliberately trying to insult me?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: Deliberation implies some form of intent, master, when I am only stating a fact. Perhaps you would prefer the term liquidious fleshbag?

speaker: Player
text: How about 'human'?

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: But... but that technical term does not accurately portray the vast amount of bulbous slushiness present in your bipedal form!

speaker: Player
text: Would you prefer I call you 'junk'?

speaker: HK-47
text: Resignation: *sigh* Very well, master. You are a harsh, harsh taskmaster. I like you more already.

speaker: Player
text: You'll just have to suffer.

speaker: HK-47
text: Resignation: You have no idea, master. No idea at all. Can we please go and shoot something now?

speaker: Player
text: Just... stop calling me master.

speaker: Player
text: Just stop talking. I give up!

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Organics have no sense of persistence.

speaker: Player
text: What was that?

speaker: HK-47
text: Err... ignore that, master. Obeying original command. Signing off.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, fine. Whatever.

speaker: Player
text: I just don't appreciate being called a meatbag.

speaker: Player
text: You're the one who's driving me mad!

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: Surely not, master. I am programmed to perform all kinds of psychological assistance. Do you require some?

speaker: Player
text: I would hope not!

speaker: Player
text: Well I don't, so stop it.

speaker: Player
text: So... you belonged to Revan originally?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Yes, master. You created me shortly after you and your apprentice began your war to conquer the galaxy.

speaker: HK-47
text: I was sent on an assassination mission into Mandalorian space, but I was damaged and unable to return to you.

speaker: HK-47
text: Exclamation: I find this most distressing. I could certainly have protected you from the Jedi and your pupil's betrayal had I returned.

speaker: Player
text: It's probably better it worked out this way.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: You may be right, master. This way we are reunited, and neither of us has suffered permanent termination.

speaker: Player
text: Am I very much like the Revan you knew?

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: In many ways you are, master, yes. You have much of the beloved cruelty of the master I knew.

speaker: HK-47
text: You seem to have forgotten much, but in some ways you seem improved from the human I once knew. It is... difficult to explain, master.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the Star Forge?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: No, master. You never did make me privy to any of the Star Forge's secrets.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me of Malak?

speaker: HK-47
text: Commentary: Your former pupil is efficient and brutal, even for an organic. I rather liked him when you first introduced me to him.

speaker: HK-47
text: If I had known what he would do to you, master, I would have gladly removed his entrails right then!

speaker: Player
text: So... why the 'meatbag' references?

speaker: HK-47
text: Answer: It was you who programmed me thus, master.

speaker: HK-47
text: Your pupil once asked what I thought of him and I informed him of his meatbag status. He was unimpressed, but you found the reference humorous.

speaker: HK-47
text: You changed my programming so that I would continue to use the term. It drove your pupil to extreme lengths of frustration.

speaker: Player
text: So... Malak was the original meatbag? I like that idea.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Of course you do, master. You did then, as well.

speaker: Player
text: That will be all, HK-47.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: You are different in many fundamental ways, master. You have a concern for life that is unsettling.

speaker: HK-47
text: This cannot solely be caused by memory loss. I do not know how to explain it. Regardless, you do seem to be improved, overall, from the human I once knew.

speaker: Player
text: I doubt you could have done anything.

speaker: HK-47
text: Objection: But I would have tried, master! I could have killed the Jedi, Bastila, I am sure of it. That would have been most fun.

speaker: Player
text: Don't talk about Bastila like that!

speaker: HK-47
text: Retraction: I apologize, master. It is a force of habit.

speaker: Player
text: Hmm... maybe a little.

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Now that is the master I remember.

speaker: Player
text: You find it distressing?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Of course, master. You are the one who created me, meatbag or no... and while you may not be all you once were, I am grateful for my existence.

speaker: Player
text: I want to begin a fighter simulation.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Certainly, master. Allow me to input the proper sequences into the ship computer. I caution you that the simulation will appear quite real.

speaker: HK-47
text: Are you ready to begin the training sequence, master?

speaker: Player
text: Go ahead.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Simulation initiating.

speaker: Player
text: No, forget it.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about these gizka, HK?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I have little knowledge of that to impart, master.

speaker: Player
text: We have a little stowaway problem. Can you help?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: I cannot be of assistance on that, master.

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Well done, master. You're my kind of owner!

speaker: HK-47
text: Observation: Your ruthlessness and cruelty are quite refreshing in an organic meatbag, master. Are you sure you aren't part droid?

speaker: HK-47
text: Statement: Oh, master. I'm so very disappointed in you.

speaker: Echani Mercenary
text: What are you doing in my room?

speaker: Player
text: I just want to talk.

speaker: Echani Mercenary
text: I am too tired to enter a discussion with you tonight. You can speak to me tomorrow at the mercenary enclave if you wish.

speaker: Player

text: Ask yourself first what this 'morality' is? How is it created? Who does it benefit? Where do your notions of 'good' and 'evil' come from?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You may come to the realization that morality is but an obstacle to overcome... or not. The discovery is yours to make, should you be ready.

speaker: Player
text: I've killed too many Sith to have preconceptions about them.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Most impressive, if it is true. Those who were too weak to stand against you deserved their fate, so expect no retribution from us. There is much you can learn from the Sith, and we from you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know anything about the Sith, to tell the truth.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: An honest if evasive answer. Likely it is more true than you realize. Allow me to speak of the deeper matters at hand.

speaker: Player
text: I know that the Sith are powerful. A force to be reckoned with.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: A diplomatic answer, if not the core of the matter. Our power is obvious. The question in truth goes much deeper than the surface.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are evil and have surrendered themselves to the temptation and corruption of their power.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: An honest answer, and one I would expect from anyone who has been exposed to those sad relics amongst the Jedi. As always, young human, the truth is not quite so simple.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith do what they want and pay no heed to duty or discipline.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Untrue. The Force demands discipline from all who use it, and the Sith demand duty. The truth goes far beyond such a superficial evaluation.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So, then. I take it you are ready to travel to the tomb of Naga Sadow? Your final test should not be delayed.

speaker: Player
text: What is this tomb of Naga Sadow?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: It is a tomb that belonged to an ancient Sith Lord... the greatest of Korriban's Sith Lords, in fact. It is there that your test is performed.

speaker: Player
text: What is this final test?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I will tell you the details when we are there, young one. You will, however, fight for your life... that is why I suggest you be in sufficient health.

speaker: Player
text: I am ready to go.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Then we go now.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not ready just yet.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Then return when you are. Do not delay overly long, young one.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Do not forget our agreement regarding Yuthura's treachery. We shall put her in her place... should you reach the final test, that is.
comment: if the PC has agreed to double-cross Yuthura

speaker: Player
text: How do I gain prestige?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? It is no more complicated than I said. Perform impressive deeds or bring me a suitably valuable artifact from the Valley of the Dark Lords.

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: We could begin by slaughtering the inhabitants of this building, master. Would that be impressive?

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep-beep boop boooop.

speaker: HK47
text: No, I didn't mean *us* as well, you moronic droid.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It is like the rites of passage of my home, except the only purpose here is to brag about it. No personal pride at all.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Really, however, you should seek out Yuthura and get her advice. She is your trainer, after all, yes?

speaker: Player
text: Where is this valley?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: There is an exit that leads to the surface of the planet... the valley is only a short trip from there. It is not difficult to find.

speaker: Player
text: I want to know some more about you.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You wish to know more about me, do you? And why would I indulge your idle curiosity? Will we be good friends, you think?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I strived many years to hone my power until I was able to drive out my predecessor and rule the academy. If you are smart, you will aim to do the same, or better.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: There is nothing else that you need to know. Do not ask again, young one.

speaker: Player
text: I have something to tell you about Yuthura...
comment: If Yuthura has made her offer to the PC to betray Uthar at the final tomb (the PC had no choice but to accept)

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? What is my apprentice up to now?

speaker: Player
text: She wants me to help her kill you at the final trial.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I see. It is good that you have come to me with this information, young one.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: It is a bit... ironic... that Yuthura has begun her plotting. I have been aware of her growing ambitions for some time, and had in fact already decided to remove her.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Normally, the one who gains the most prestige would engage in a final trial... two of the students would fight. This time it will be Yuthura who battles, though she does not know it.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Perhaps it will be you who combats her? Yes... perhaps so. This is what you can do. Give this pad to Adrenas... he will put some poison in her bath.
comment: gives letter item to PC. PC will have to give it to Adrenas NPC in library. If he does, Yuthura will be weakened in final battle. Set a global that Uthar has made the offer (it cannot be refused)

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: This will weaken Yuthura for that final test, making her an easy target. Rather generous of me, don't you think?

speaker: Jolee
text: Hm. This should be interesting.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: For coming to me with this information and betraying your foolish trainer, I feel you are worthy of prestige, young one.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You have impressed me enough, by my estimation, to become a Sith in full. Congratulations, young one... you have bested the others quite completely.
comment: if the player has 3 or more prestige

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You have but one final test which you must take, and this requires us to travel to the tomb of Naga Sadow in the Valley of the Dark Lords.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I would advise you to be rested and equipped before we leave. Return to your quarters now and seek me out in the morning.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: When you return, make sure that you have all that you will need... for you will face your test alone. Go, and may the Force serve you well.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Go, now... you have not yet impressed me enough to declare you the victor. I have matters to attend to.

speaker: Player
text: I have something to tell you about a student...
comment: if the PC has learned Kel Algwinn's secret and has not 'finished' that plot by advising Kel to do something, yet

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: A student, is it? What might you have to say?

speaker: Player
text: It's Kel Algwinn. He has... doubts... and is thinking of leaving.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ahhhh. I think I know this one you speak of. You gained his confidence to admit such, did you?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I commend your competitive spirit... you have certainly impressed me. I shall speak to the boy straight away.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Go, now... you have done well, but you have not impressed me enough to declare you the victor. I have matters to attend to.

speaker: Player
text: I know the Code of the Sith.
comment: if the player has learned the Code of the Sith ("KOR_SITH_CODE" has been set to 1)

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Then finish the Code as I speak it.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: "Peace is a lie, there is only..."

speaker: Player
text: Serenity.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: No. No, that is incorrect. I would have thought merely reciting the Code to be a simple matter. Ah, well.

speaker: Player
text: I dealt with those renegade students.
comment: if the rebel students in the shyrack caverns have been killed or saved. The player will have the opportunity to lie if they were saved.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ahhh. The ones I ordered executed for their mutiny? It's done, then?

speaker: Player
text: Yes. They are all dead.
comment: if the rebels were all killed

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Indeed. I had the caverns checked after you left. Well done.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: The lesson is learned, I believe.
comment: add +1 prestige change the global so this can't be repeated

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Yes, they are all dead.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: [Success] Indeed? We checked the caves and found only a couple of bodies. Perhaps the shyrack ate them? Ah, it is just as good, I suppose.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] It's done. They are... gone.

speaker: Player
text: I have the sword of Ajunta Pall.
comment: the player has the real sword of Freedon Nadd

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ahhh, finally, the genuine sword! I knew that this relic would be unearthed in time. I can feel the power flowing through it!

speaker: Bastila
text: I can't say I approve, putting this weapon in the hands of --

speaker: Player
text: Quiet! Remember where we are!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Well done! You have impressed me greatly!
comment: add +1 prestige to the PC take away the sword

speaker: Carth
text: We should have kept that. It could have made a --

text: I dealt with the rogue droid in the tombs.

text: Yes, so I hear. I've had reports from some students that ventured into the tomb after you left and found the parts. Well done.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I am impressed. You have rid us of a potential nuisance.
comment: add +1 prestige to the PC change global so this can't be repeated

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? I heard that the droid ran out and blasted off into the sky. We tracked it for a short while before it vanished from our scanners. What do you make of that?
comment: if the droid was just repaired

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I activated his self-destruct and he ran... but he is dead.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: [Success] I... suppose so. That would explain his disappearance from our scanners, certainly, though I would prefer proof. Still, it shows innovative thinking.

speaker: Bastila
text: Or innovative lying.

speaker: Player
text: Shh! Quiet back there!

speaker: Jolee
text: Heh. It shows innovative something, that's for sure.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I tampered with him. He no longer functions as he did, and will not return.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: [Success] I... suppose that will have to do, though I would prefer proof of his destruction. Still, it shows innovative thinking.

speaker: Player
text: I found Jorak Uln, the 'hermit' in the hills.
comment: Jorak Uln was encountered or killed, but the player does not have the Darkside Tablet

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ahh, my old master. Still... unless you bring back something of his, some writings or similar, I am unimpressed. Jorak's fate means nothing to me.

speaker: Player
text: I have a tablet written by Jorak Uln.
comment: the player has Jorak's Darkside Tablet

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? Let me see... it appears my old master was busy studying the writings in one of the tombs. How interesting. I do hope you had to pry this from his dead fingers.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Regardless, you have impressed me with your worthy act.
comment: add +1 prestige to the PC take away the tablet

speaker: Player
text: I know the location of the Mandalorian prisoner's weapon cache.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? And why would that be of use to me? His interrogator already brought me that information moments ago.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: A valiant attempt, young one, but you must be quicker than that if you wish to impress me.

speaker: Player
text: Has Lashowe shown you the Jedi holocron?
comment: the player and Lashowe retrieved the Jedi holocron, but the PC allowed Lashowe to return with it on her own

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: She did. Prestige is not shared, however, if that is what you are wondering. If you aided her, it was to her benefit and not yours.

speaker: Player
text: I have found a Jedi holocron.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: *chuckle* I had heard that such an artifact existed. Tell me, young one... did you acquire this device by yourself?

speaker: Player
text: Yes.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You lie. Still, what matters is the fact that you succeeded. And Lashowe... does she yet live?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I have no idea. Probably.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You didn't kill her? How very foolish. Now you have an enemy to contend with. The holocron, itself, is an impressive item, however.

speaker: Player
text: No, I killed her.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ha ha! Well done! You gained an artifact through trickery and eliminated an opponent at the same time. That is deserving of great prestige!

speaker: Player
text: No.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So I see. And Lashowe... does she yet live?

speaker: Player
text: I've killed Lashowe.
comment: if she was killed ONLY after the player let her return the holocron on her own

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Killed her out of revenge, did you? Well done. I can appreciate such drama, believe me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I am most impressed that you have eliminated an opponent so handily.
comment: add +1 prestige to the PC change global so this can't be mentioned again

speaker: Player
text: I've killed Shaardan.
comment: Shaardan is dead (can only be killed in Freedon Nadd plot) he was not killed by Uthar

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Yes, so I hear. Still, it was Shaardan's failure and hardly your success, now, was it? Not quite worthy of prestige.

speaker: Player
text: I've killed Mekel.
comment: Mekel is dead (can only be killed in Jorak Uln plot)

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Maybe it's better to say that Mekel is dead, yes? Considering the circumstances, I am unimpressed... though you do now have one less opponent.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be on my way.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Indeed. You have much to do, yet.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Very well. You have impressed me... definitely a good start.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You have gained considerable prestige... you are very close to the end. Do not falter now.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You do? That is most interesting. Where might that be?

speaker: Player
text: It is hidden within a trap door on his ship.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Hmm. How ironic that I recently had his vessel scrapped for parts, then. I had assumed it had been thoroughly scanned... apparently not.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Still... you have done well in bringing me information that others could not unearth on their own. I am impressed.

speaker: Player
text: I've... changed my mind.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? How very sad, young one. You should learn to grab your advantages whenever you can.

speaker: Player
text: Strength.

speaker: Player
text: Passion.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: "Through passion I gain..."

speaker: Player
text: Power.

speaker: Player
text: Victory.

speaker: Player
text: Chaos.

speaker: Player
text: Harmony.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I see. Then leave me be if you have nothing to offer. I am sure you have much to do.

speaker: Carth
text: I'd love to know what's going on in that tricky mind of yours.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing. I shouldn't have brought it up.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I see. Well, then... should you change your mind... you know where to come, yes?

speaker: Carth
text: So it's a popularity contest, basically? Wonderful.

speaker: Bastila
text: One has to wonder exactly what a Sith Master would find 'impressive'.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Greetings, young one. You have much to do, yet... you have gained little prestige. You will have to work quickly if you hope to best the others.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Greetings, young one. I have found you to be most impressive... you are off to an excellent beginning.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Greetings, young one. You have done very well for yourself so far. Continue and your promise shall be fulfilled.

speaker: Angry Woman
text: Was that Jergan I just saw you talking to? Do you know where he went?

text: He went backstage to arrange a meeting between me and the band.

speaker: Angry Woman
