speaker: Angry Woman
text: When I tried to get backstage to look for him, nobody even knew who he was! He can't set up a meeting with the band - he's just some sleazy con artist spinning lies!

speaker: Angry Woman
text: I doubt he'd be dumb enough to show up here again; he knows I'm looking for him! And if I ever find him he's going to pay for ripping me off - with interest!

speaker: Player
text: No. I have no idea where he went.

speaker: Angry Woman
text: Well if you see that slime ball tell him Lana is looking for him! I gave him 20 credits and he promised to get me backstage to meet the band. Then, he disappeared!

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Greetings. If you haven't heard, there's some trouble over at the academy. A power struggle, most likely, but news is sketchy. So... anything Czerka can do for you?

speaker: Player
text: What does Czerka do here on Korriban?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: We do some mining here and are responsible for local shipping and support of the Sith on Korriban.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Our starport is mostly just freighters and such, but we do get many travelers that come here to learn from the Sith.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I must say... Czerka is in need of droids right now. That's a mighty fine-looking one you have there...

speaker: HK47
text: Objection: This unit is not for sale, meatbag.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Errr... yes, of course, no offense meant. Heh. Touchy, isn't it?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: This office is actually our administrative headquarters for this region. Rather inauspicious, isn't it? We offer good prices here to those traders that keep the colony supplied.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: If you're in need of anything, this is the place to come.

speaker: Player
text: Can I see what you have to offer?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: You certainly can. Allow me to punch up our stock.

speaker: Player
text: Czerka works with the Sith?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Well why not? This is Sith space now, and the company has to survive regardless of who is in charge. The Republic, the Sith, eh... the economy has to keep going.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Profit at any cost... just like on my world.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I'm not sure what your pet is muttering, but keep a restraining collar on it. It won't last long if it gets loose. Now, was there something else?

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions about the colony?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Certainly.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the colony?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: There truly isn't much to tell, citizen. Dreshdae was established by the Sith, and we arrived to take advantage of some of the planet's mineral wealth.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: The only thing that's really unusual about Dreshdae, I suppose, is that the Sith built their academy on the east side of the colony. You don't find those just anywhere.

speaker: Player
text: Have you ever heard of a Star Map?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: A Star Map? We sell navigational components, if that's what you mean.

speaker: Player
text: No, I mean as in old ruins.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Well... the Sith have some old ruins that interest them up on the surface of the planet. If this map of yours is there, however, they've said nothing about it.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Sith academy?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Not much. The Sith are a rather secretive lot, and they don't allow many into the academy. I hear they claim that Korriban was inhabited long ago by other Sith.

speaker: Mission
text: That would explain why this place is so creepy. This whole planet makes my head-tails twitch!

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: But no one truly knows if that's true. The planet is certainly uninhabited outside of Dreshdae and always has been.

speaker: Player
text: Who is allowed in the academy?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Only prospective students. We get many who come here each year, hoping to get picked. Many are simply considered too weak, I'm afraid.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I understand there is one main person amongst the Sith who decides which students are worthy... Yuthura Ban, I believe her name is.

speaker: Player
text: Where do I find this Yuthura?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Other than in the academy itself, I'm sorry, I don't know.

speaker: Player
text: How can one reach the ruins on the surface?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Czerka sends freighters to the surface every now and again to ferry artifacts to the Core.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: The men are not allowed out of their ships, however, as only Sith are allowed on the surface. Beyond that I really can't say.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Can't say or don't know?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: [Success] Well... all I know is that they call the site the Valley of the Dark Lords. Apparently, there are Sith Lords of old buried in tombs there.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I don't know anything else. Neither will you, I'm sure... only the Sith students are allowed access to the site.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Do come again.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: [Failure] Does it matter? I don't intend to speak of it, regardless.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] It is very important that you tell me what you know.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: [Success] They... they call the site the Valley of the Dark Lords. Ancient Sith are buried in tombs there, along with many artifacts of old... some of great power, apparently.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Now, was there anything else?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Greetings. You've heard of that awful business on Edean, yes? Our corporate outpost there has been destroyed by the Wookiee savages.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: This could put back the use of Wookiee labor considerably. We may even have to abandon the planet completely.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You make our freedom sound like a tragedy.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I see you got one of your own early. May as well, while you can. Now then... was there something I could do for you?

speaker: Mission
text: Yeah, I sure bet the Wookiees would hate to see ya go.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Well, certainly. Now they are doomed to remain savages forever... or possibly become extinct. Very sad. Now then... was there something you needed?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Ah, well. What can you do? Sorry... was there something you needed?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: If you've come for any medical supplies, I have to warn you that the kolto source on Manaan has been poisoned.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: It's a tragedy, considering the war and all... casualties are going to go through the roof. Czerka is pulling all its kolto out of storage as we speak.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Hmm. Aren't you the human who won the swoop race on Manaan? Congradulations and well done! It was most exciting to watch!

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: It is an honor to have you in our offices. How may Czerka serve you?

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Tsk. I suppose you've heard about the destruction of Taris, yes? Awful business, that. Czerka lost a fortune there, not that the Sith care.

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: I understand you're receiving training at the monastery, citizen. Congratulations!
comment: when selected afterwards player being trained at the academy

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Greetings again, citizen. Something you need?
comment: when selected afterwards player not being trained at the academy Sandpeople have not taken over Anchorhead

speaker: Czerka Representative
text: Greetings and welcome to Czerka Corporation.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: N-now hold on, we don't want any trouble... please?

speaker: Player
text: I'm no threat. I'm just wearing their robes.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Scared the living Force right out of me with that trick. You do that way too well. I thought our number was up for sure.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: I doubt we could hold out on our own against another wave of them.

speaker: Player
text: I would assume this was done by the Sand People?

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: You would be right. Came out of nowhere. Wait... Damn it! Here they come again! How do they do that!

speaker: Player
text: You miners are cowards. A single attack wiped you out?

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Nothing in the job description covers this. Wait... well I guess we'll see how you fare. Here they come again!

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Did the company send you? It's about time they drove these animals out!

speaker: Player
text: I've agreed to try and stop the Sand People attacks.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Well you've got a lot of work ahead of you. Do you know about their enclave in the south? Don't even try to go near it.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: They've taken all the Czerka weapons that were supposed to protect our sandcrawlers. That place is a fortress. A death trap.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: You'll have to find some way to sneak into the place. Glad it's not my job.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the Sand People?

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Just that they attack everything on sight. Well, I suppose they don't attack each other, but any outsider is as good as dead.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: The company tried to arm us, and even set up remote self-powered turrets on the mining route, but...but that just made things worse.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: We're not soldiers. They still kill us, and then take our weapons off our corpses. They even had the Jawas disable the turrets and set them around their enclave.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: It's like a fortress now. I don't know how you're going to break through all of that. Me, I'd sneak in. Well, actually, I would just get back to Anchorhead.

speaker: Player
text: The Sand People are using turrets?

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: They use whatever they scavenge. They seem to hate our technology, but they love to turn it against us. That goes for blasters and turrets too, I guess.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: It's not like you need to be a genius to operate them. They probably don't even bother with special settings. They just watch for people approaching and switch them on.

speaker: Player
text: I have other questions about the desert.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: I don't have time for this sort of thing. I'm through with the desert. You can take your Sand People, krayt dragons, and crazy hunters.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Yeah, so do we. There's no way we're repairing this thing while getting attacked over and over. The desert can have it.

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: Ah, the Jawas will salvage it eventually anyway. Then we can buy it back and start over. Heh. Makes sense to me.

speaker: Player
text: [Leave]

speaker: Mining Team Captain
text: They... left? Well if that don't beat all.

speaker: Race Announcer

speaker: Race Announcer

speaker: Race Announcer

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: Hey - didn't you just win the big swoop bike race in? Yeah, it was you, I'm sure! Best race I ever saw!

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: I can't believe Brejik tried to back out of his wager! He deserved what happened to him!

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: I can't wait for the big swoop race! I hear the Vulkars have a new engine that's going to break all the records!

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: This gang war is getting out of hand! The Vulkars aren't just attacking the Hidden Beks anymore - they go after everyone!

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: I saw Davik's new starship at the spaceport before the quarantine. They say it's the fastest ship on Taris! He calls it the Ebon Hawk.

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: Have you got your tickets for Bendak Starkiller's return to the duel ring? I hear it's going to be an illegal death match!

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: Did you hear the news? Gadon Thek is dead! I wonder what's going to happen to the Hidden Beks now?

speaker: Lower Taris Citizen
text: I heard Davik's hired a Mandalorian mercenary to work for him. I didn't know there were any of them left after the Mandalore wars.

speaker: Ithorian Patron

text: Scurry away. I had family on Taris and I'm not in a mood to talk.

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Trapped out here... can't do anything. I wonder which planet is next?

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Jawas... can't stand them. They never bathe, you know.

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Good thing there's nothing on Tatooine to get the attention of the Sith. Right?

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Sith... Jedi... do either of them really care when normal people get caught in their fighting?

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Don't care if we've got Sith rule or Republic rule. Either way I work the mines.

speaker: Ithorian Patron
text: Leave me, human. If you're here to stir things up, I want no part of it.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: You've the look of a seasoned Pazaak player about you. I dabble in it from time to time myself. Care for a game?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Sol'aa
text: I am Sol'aa and, to be perfectly blunt, my business is my own. I do offer you, though, the company of my time for a game or two of Pazaak.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: Do you care for a hand?

speaker: Player
text: Sure, I'll play.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: Let's get started then.

speaker: Player
text: Not right now.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: Ah, well. Come back if you ever feel up to a game.

speaker: Player
text: Do you have any cards to sell?

speaker: Sol'aa
text: As a matter of fact, I do. If you see any you like, I am willing to part with them for a small sum.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: I haven't seen you around here before... I'm a traveller in search of a little entertainment.

speaker: Sol'aa
text: Care to have a hand of Pazaak with me?

speaker: Player
text: What's Pazaak?

speaker: Sol'aa

speaker: Sol'aa

speaker: Trask
text: We've been ambushed by a Sith battle fleet! The Endar Spire is under attack! Hurry up - we don't have much time!

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? [Left-click this answer to select highlighted response.]

speaker: Trask
text: I'm Trask Ulgo, ensign with the Republic Fleet. I'm your bunk mate here on the Endar Spire. We work opposite shifts; I guess that's why you haven't seen me before.

speaker: Trask
text: Now hurry up, we have to find Bastila! We have to make sure she makes it off the ship alive!

speaker: Player
text: Who's Bastila? [Left-click this answer to select highlighted response.]

speaker: Trask
text: Bastila's the commanding officer on the Endar Spire. Well, not an officer, really. But she's the one in charge of this mission.

speaker: Trask
text: One of our primary duties is to guarantee her survival in the event of enemy attack! You swore an oath just like everyone else on this mission. Now it's time to make good on that oath!

speaker: Trask
text: I've heard all about your reputation: elite combat training, tops in your class. It's no wonder you were hand picked for this mission.

speaker: Trask
text: Word is the officers haven't seen a recruit with your kind of potential in twenty years. But all that potential doesn't mean a thing if you can't deliver when it counts!

speaker: Trask
text: We're soldiers, we're trained for combat. Bastila's going to need men and women like us at her side during this attack!

speaker: Player
text: Okay, let's go help Bastila!

speaker: Trask
text: So hurry up and grab your gear. You need to suit up so we can get out of here.

speaker: Player
text: Okay.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I get my equipment?

speaker: Trask
text: You can move the mouse to the edges of the screen to rotate the camera. Alternately, moving the mouse while holding down the right mouse button will rotate the camera as well.

speaker: Trask
text: To move towards the footlocker, hold down the right mouse button and face the camera towards it, then hold down the left mouse button as well to cause the character to run forward.

speaker: Trask
text: You can left-click on an object to select it. Once the footlocker is selected, left-click on it again to perform the default action and open it.

speaker: Player
text: Can you repeat that?

speaker: Player
text: Oath or no oath - I'm heading to the escape pods!

speaker: Trask
text: Don't be stupid! You won't stand a chance against the Sith by yourself. We've got to stick together if we want to make it out of this alive.

speaker: Trask
text: I heard what everyone's saying about you: you've explored the farthest reaches of the galaxy, you've visited planets I've never even heard of.

speaker: Trask
text: People with your skills and abilities are hard to find; it's no wonder the Republic recruited you for this mission. But now's the time to prove yourself!

speaker: Trask
text: I know you're a scout and not a soldier, but Bastila needs all troops at her side during this attack!

speaker: Trask
text: I know all about your reputation, how you used to smuggle spice and blasters along the Corellian Run. I guess the Republic figured since they couldn't catch you, they might as well hire you.

speaker: Trask
text: And I'll admit, the Republic is in desperate need of someone with your kind of skills. Desperate enough to overlook your shady past.

speaker: Trask
text: But now that you've signed on for this mission you're part of the Republic fleet. And Bastila needs all troops at her side during this attack!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it - I'm looking after my own skin! [Left-click this answer to select highlighted response.]

speaker: Trask
text: You swore an oath to protect Bastila when you signed up with this mission, just like everyone else in the crew! Now it's time to make good on that oath.

speaker: Trask
text: I know she may not have an official rank in the fleet, but she's the one in charge of this mission and it's our duty to protect her!

speaker: Player
text: The Endar Spire? [Left-click this answer to select highlighted response.]

speaker: Trask
text: Did you fall out of your bunk and hit your head? The Endar Spire is the ship we're stationed on - this ship! You probably don't even know who I am, do you?

speaker: Trask
text: Come on, we have to hurry! The Sith might already be boarding the ship to try and capture Bastila.

speaker: Trask
text: Put your equipment on so we can get out of here.

speaker: Player
text: How do I equip my items?

speaker: Trask
text: Use the EQUIP screen to equip the armor and weapons from your inventory. You can access this screen by selecting the EQUIP menu icon in the upper right corner of the screen.

speaker: Trask
text: Use the mouse to look through your inventory slots. The menu on the right displays items you can equip in each slot.

speaker: Trask
text: Left-click the mouse to select an inventory slot, then scroll through the available items on the right and left-click to equip one.

speaker: Trask
text: Okay, let's move out.

speaker: Trask
text: We should stick together; you'll have more success with a party than on your own.

speaker: Player
text: [TRASK has joined your party.] [Left-click this response to go to PARTY SELECTION screen.]

speaker: Trask
text: Because of the attack this room is in lockdown, but don't worry - I've got the override codes. You'll have to use me to unlock the door.

speaker: Player
text: How do I use you to unlock the door?

speaker: Trask
text: You always control the leader of the party. You can switch who is the party leader by left-clicking on their portait in the lower left corner of the screen.

speaker: Trask
text: Left-click my portrait now to switch me to the party leader, then use me to open the door.

speaker: Trask
text: Left-click to target the door, then left-click it again with the mouse to open it.

speaker: Trask
text: Now that the door's open you better take the lead again.

speaker: Player
text: [SWITCHING <FullName> BACK TO PARTY LEADER] [Left-click this response to continue.]

speaker: Carth
text: This is Carth Onasi - the Sith are threatening to overrun our position! We can't hold out long against their firepower! All hands to the bridge!

speaker: Trask
text: That was Carth contacting us on our portable communicators. He's one of the Republic's best pilots! He's seen more combat than the rest of the Endar Spire's crew put together.

speaker: Trask
text: If he says things are bad, you better believe it. We have to get to the bridge to help defend Bastila!

speaker: Trask
text: There's a map of the Endar Spire and a copy of Carth's message in your electronic journal, just in case we get separated.

speaker: Player
text: Let's move out.

speaker: Player
text: How do I use my journal?

speaker: Trask
text: You can access your journal, map and other important menus by clicking on the menu icons in the upper right corner of the screen.

speaker: Trask
text: You can use the mouse to switch between the menus listed on the tabs at the top of the screen.

speaker: Trask
text: That door's locked, and I don't have the codes to open it. You'll have to use your SECURITY skill on it if we want to get past.

speaker: Player
text: How do you use security on a door?

speaker: Trask
text: Target the door using the mouse. When you have selected the door, the TARGET MENU will appear. The icons on the TARGET MENU are the additional options you can use on the door.

speaker: Trask
text: Look at the TARGET MENU and find the SECURITY icon. Remember, the SECURITY icon only appears if you're controlling a character with the SECURITY skill.

speaker: Trask
text: Once you see it, left-click it with the mouse to use your SECURITY skill on the door.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me more about the TARGET and ACTION MENUs.

speaker: Trask
text: In the lower right of the screen you'll see a list of icons. This is your ACTION MENU. You can select items from this menu by using the mouse.

speaker: Trask
text: Left-click the icon you want to use to activate that power or item. Clicking on the arrows above and below the icon will cycle to other powers or items in that list.

speaker: Trask
text: The first icon of the ACTION MENU is for Friendly Force Powers. The second is for Medical Items such as Medpacs and Antidote Kits.

speaker: Trask
text: The third icon is for Miscellaneous Items such as Stimulants and Energy Shields. The fourth icon is for Mines, and only appears if you have a mine in your inventory and have the DEMOLITIONS skill.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the TARGET MENU.

speaker: Trask
text: The icons in your TARGET MENU will change depending on whether your targeting circle is on a door, a container, a friendly creature or an enemy. Left-click the mouse to select a target and bring up the TARGET MENU. Left-clicking on the target again will perform the Default Action on it.

speaker: Trask
text: The first icon is for combat FEATS. The second icon is for Hostile Force Powers such as Choke and Kill. The third icon is for Grenades.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, let's move on.

speaker: Player
text: How do I select icons again?

speaker: Trask
text: Use the mouse to select the FEAT, power or item you want to use, then left-click to select it.

speaker: Trask
text: That door's locked. I don't have the codes to open it, but switch me to the party leader so you can use my security skills to slice into the access panel and open the door.

speaker: Player
text: How do I switch you to the party leader again?

speaker: Trask
text: I've got a feeling that won't be our last battle with the Sith. Good thing we have medpacs to heal our wounds. It might be a good idea to use one now before our next battle.

speaker: Player
text: How do I use a medpac?

speaker: Trask
text: To use an item like a medpac - or another self-targetting item or power - you'll need to know how to use your ACTION MENU.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the ACTION MENU.

speaker: Player
text: I know about the ACTION MENU. How do I use a medpac?

speaker: Trask
text: First, left-click on their portrait to take control of the injured character. Use the mouse to look through the Medical Items in the ACTION MENU until you see "Medpac" in the information box.

speaker: Trask
text: Notice the up and down arrows on this icon. This means you have more than one available option for this icon. You must choose between a medpac and an advanced medpac.

speaker: Trask
text: Use the mouse wheel to scroll up or down to switch between your medpac and your advanced medpac. Left-click the mouse to use the selected item on the character you currently control.

speaker: Trask
text: Just remember that you have to actually be hurt for a medpac to work. You can't use it when you're uninjured.

speaker: Trask
text: The bridge is just beyond that door. You better equip your melee weapon. There isn't much room on the bridge, and it's suicide to use a blaster in close quarters.

speaker: Trask
text: I should equip a melee weapon, too. Either that, or I'll have to stay back and use my blaster.

speaker: Player
text: What if they have lightsabers?

speaker: Trask
text: Your melee weapon is made using a cortosis weave. It's strong enough to stand up against anything, even a lightsaber.

speaker: Trask

text: Hello there. I haven't seen you in my shop before... allow me to introduce myself. My name is Kebla Yurt. Welcome to the Equipment Emporium.

speaker: Kebla021
text: You looking to buy some supplies? My shop's the largest one in all of Upper Taris. Best selection on the planet. Whatever you need, I've got. Well, mostly.

text: Gluupor think... Gluupor think he can't talk more right now. Gluupor feels the need to lie down... maybe just stay here...

speaker: Gluupor
text: [Failure] No one pay Gluupor to do anything... that why Gluupor so poor...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] How about if I give you 100 credits to tell me?

speaker: Gluupor
text: [Failure] Gluupor not saying anything... Gluupor have nothing to say.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to tell me who paid you and for what.

speaker: Gluupor
text: [Success] Gluupor want to tell you. Gluupor want to tell you Sith paid him money to plant medal on body.

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor want to tell you this because you are Gluupor's friend. Good friend... maybe give Gluupor money? Maybe not...

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about a Star Map?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor not know what you talking about. But then again, Gluupor not very bright.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about the Selkath youths who have gone missing?

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor heard of it, yes. But Gluupor been locked in this room for days. Gluupor think it rather poor insight to think he knows something.

speaker: Player
text: I'll ask more questions later.

speaker: Gluupor
text: Gluupor answer later too, then. Selkath not let Gluupor leave while trial still on...

speaker: Gluupor
text: Why you back, human? Gluupor already tell you everything. Why you not leave Gluupor alone?
comment: if gluupor has told the player, but the player has not yet arranged to see the man who hired him

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Have you heard the news? They say the Sith slaughtered a secret Jedi oupost on Dantooine in a vile and cowardly sneak attack.
comment: dantooine has been destroyed, first time conversation

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Yet despite this monstrous act, the Selkath authorities insist on maintaining their neutrality - and the Sith walk amongst us like vermin in the streets of Ahto City!

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: But my feelings about the Sith are well known around Ahto City. I shall spare you further outbursts. What may I do for you?

speaker: Player
text: Let me see what you have in stock.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: As you wish, human. My inventory contains the finest Aratech equipment you can find on Manaan - all of it far superior to the Czerka Corp swill the Sith are so fond of.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: As you wish, human. Please return when you have need of anything from my vast inventory.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Come in, come in! You honor my humble store with your presence. All of Manaan has heard tell of your glorious swoop riding exploits.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: I carry many other choice items of the highest quality. Items a celebrity of your stature might be interested in.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about the Sunry case?

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Unfortunately, I cannot offer any great insight into this matter. I suggest you investigate the murder scene, or perhaps talk to the other residents of the hotel where the crime occured.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Welcome, welcome. This is a great time to be alive, as the Czerka Corp. has been driven from one of its outposts.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: They lost their "trading" outpost on Kashyyyk - merely a slaver's den I've been told. News of this sort is welcome indeed to me. What can I do for you today?

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: I have heard from several customers that you are now the Arbiter during the murder trial of Sunry, the Republic war hero.
comment: First time talked to while player is Arbiter in Sunry plot.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: I admire you for accepting this position. I have no doubt Sunry has been framed by the Sith. If there is anything I can do to aid your investigation, I will be happy to help.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Greetings, human. I welcome you to my store. But if you have come seeking med kits, I must apologize for the price in advance.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: The Selkath say the kolto harvest is the lowest it has ever been, and healing salves have become extremely expensive.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you dislike the Sith so much?

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: How can you ask such a question? They are cruel and ruthless, and care nothing for the welfare of others. And the Sith regard my species with particular disdain.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: The Selkath now seem more distant than before... They treat members of the Republic at arms length only... I hope this does not negatively impact our trade.

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: If they give too much deference to the Sith, then the monsters will simply come in and take over!

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: It is a most terrible day when such violence happens in a peaceful city such as this. The Sith Embassy... attacked... Terrible!

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: I only hope that this is not the worst to befall them...

speaker: Tyvark Luowan
text: Greetings, friend. I bid you a warm welcome to Tyvark's shop. My store is here to serve everyone - except the Sith who walk the city like roaches!

speaker: Sith Victim
text: [The Mandalorian is imprisoned and cannot respond.]

speaker: Senni Vek
text: Forgive me for the intrusion, human. My name is Senni Vek. I believe you dropped this datapad and I wish to return it to you.

speaker: Player
text: I didn't drop anything.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: I'm certain you did, human. Please, take the datapad. It's yours, I'm sure.

speaker: Player
text: Uh... thanks.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: My pleasure, human. You should examine it to make sure it is not broken.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: Goodbye, human.

speaker: Player
text: What is this, some kind of con game?

speaker: Senni Vek
text: No, this is no game. I simply saw you drop this datapad and I wish to give it back to you.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, there must be some mistake.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: There is no mistake, human. This datapad is yours and yours alone. Please, take it.

speaker: Player
text: I don't want it.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: Are you certain, human? Please, take the datapad.

speaker: Player
text: Fine. Give me the stupid datapad!

speaker: Player
text: No. It's not mine. I won't take it.

speaker: Senni Vek
text: Very well, human. I will keep the datapad and I will leave. Goodbye, human.

speaker: Player
text: I'll beat you to death with that datapad if you don't go away right now!

speaker: Igear
text: I saw you talking with Rukil. He told you his legends about the Promised Land, didn't he? He told you all about his missing apprentice and the other lost explorers, right?

speaker: Igear
text: You know, most people don't believe his stories - they figure he's nothing but an old kook. But I think there might be some truth in what he's saying. That's why I want to stop him!

speaker: Player
text: Stop him? What are you talking about?

speaker: Igear
text: For an Outcast, I've got things pretty good. The village relies on me to bring in food and supplies - I'm an important man. If it wasn't for Gendar I'd be running this place.

speaker: Carth
text: I get the feeling if it wasn't for Gendar, this place would be a lot worse off than it is.

speaker: Igear
text: But if Rukil ever finds his Promised Land, I'm sunk. People won't need to rely on me anymore. I'll just be another nobody like all the rest of the villagers. I won't let that happen!

speaker: Player
text: That's horrible! How can you be so self-centered?

speaker: Igear
text: Don't judge me! I learned a long time ago that if I want to survive down here I've got to look out for number one.

speaker: Igear
text: The two explorers who went searching for the Promised Land might have found something. They might have found clues or evidence - just like Rukil's apprentice!

speaker: Igear
text: They would have recorded that information in their journals. I'll pay you if you bring all three journals to me - the two from the explorers and the one from Rukil's apprentice.

speaker: Igear
text: Then I can destroy the evidence and make sure nobody ever finds the Promised Land! I've saved up enough credits from my business here to make it worth your while if you help me.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! I won't betray Rukil and the village for you.

speaker: Igear
text: Don't be a fool. I'm the only one here who can pay you for those journals. Rukil has nothing - he won't be able to come up with any kind of reward.

speaker: Igear
text: Once you have all three journals just bring them to me and I'll give you a decent reward. Now, was there something else you needed?

speaker: Player
text: I have those journals you wanted.
comment: Player has all of Rukil's journals

speaker: Igear
text: I knew Rukil's legends about the Promised Land were true! Quick - give me those journals so I can destroy them!

speaker: Player
text: First hand over those credits you promised.

speaker: Igear
text: Right - your reward. Here's 100 credits; that's a pretty hefty payment for some old notes and maps, eh?

speaker: Player
text: 100 credits sounds fair. Here's the journals.

speaker: Igear
text: Excellent - now Rukil will never lead these people to the Promised Land! Now, is there something else you need? You want to look at my inventory?

speaker: Rukil04
text: False prophet! Deceiver! You have betrayed me! You have sold the hope of the entire village to the selfish and damnable Igear!

speaker: Rukil04
text: All I have worked for is destroyed! All the hopes and dreams of my father and grandfather before him turned to dust! Begone, up-worlder - I have only curses to speak at you!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] 100 credits? After all I went through? I want double that!

speaker: Igear
text: [Success] Well, I don't want Rukil to get his hands on them journals. I'll give you 200 credits - that's all I have.

speaker: Player
text: 200 credits? It's a deal!

speaker: Player
text: I've changed my mind. I'm going to give them to Rukil.

speaker: Igear
text: Fine - go to Rukil! But he won't be able to pay you anything for those journals. Come back and see me when you're ready to stop acting crazy and you want to cut a deal.

speaker: Igear
text: [Failure] I don't think you understand how much 100 credits is worth down here in the Undercity. This is a small fortune!

speaker: Igear
text: I want those journals, but I'm not rich like you up-worlders. 100 credits is all I can afford.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Igear
text: Oh, you better ask Gendar - he's the spokesman for the village. I just run the store. I don't want to make him mad by answering any questions. Gendar already doesn't like me.

speaker: Player
text: Why doesn't Gendar like you?

speaker: Igear
text: Gendar seems to think I should share the profits of my store with the whole village. He figures we're all in this together so it should be share and share alike.

speaker: Igear
text: But I'm the one who runs the store! I'm the one who makes the deals! The others just bring me salvage to trade with the up-worlders - why should they get anything?

speaker: Player
text: That's a pretty selfish attitude.

speaker: Igear
text: Hey, you don't know what it's like down here! I have to claw and scrape to survive - nobody else will look out for me. But Gendar doesn't agree with my philosophy.

speaker: Igear
text: He caught me hoarding supplies a while back. I figured I'd wait until food was scarce and then I could offer it to people who'd follow me instead of Gendar. Then I'd be the leader!

speaker: Igear
text: But Gendar made me share my hoard. Ever since then he hasn't trusted me. He keeps me around because of my store, though. Without it this village wouldn't stand a chance.

speaker: Player
text: How do you manage to run a store here in the Undercity?

speaker: Igear
text: If a villager comes across any useful salvage in the Undercity they bring it to me. Every so often members from the Lower City gangs come down to trade for the salvage.

speaker: Igear
text: They'll exchange food and medicine for engine parts, old blasters and the like. Sometimes they even give me credits if I have some really good stuff.

speaker: Player
text: Let me see your inventory.

speaker: Igear
text: It ain't the best stuff - mostly salvage and such. But the prices are right.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Igear
text: Yeah, okay. You come back and see me if you want to deal.

speaker: Player
text: I agree with you - your store, your profits.

speaker: Igear
text: Exactly my point. But Gendar doesn't see it that way.

speaker: Player
text: That's why Gendar's mad at you? There has to be more to it than that!

speaker: Player
text: I'll think about it.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like a good deal to me.

speaker: Player
text: So what do you want me to do?

speaker: Player
text: You want me to kill Rukil to shut him up?

speaker: Igear
text: I don't want you to kill Rukil - he's not the problem. It's those damn explorers that went before him. What if they actually found something?

speaker: Player
text: Why are you telling me this?

speaker: Igear
text: Oh, don't worry, I'll make this quick. I've got an offer that might be worth your while.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this.

speaker: Igear
text: Hey, you ain't from the village! You're from the up-world, ain't you? Yes, you've got credits I bet.

speaker: Carth
text: Watch yourself. There's something slimy about this guy. I wouldn't trust him as far as I could throw him.

speaker: Igear
text: My name's Igear. I run a little salvage shop here. You want to buy something from my store? I got some good deals.

speaker: Igear
text: Hey there, up-worlder. You want to see what I got for sale in my inventory? Or do you need something else?

speaker: Belaya
text: You! I remember you!

speaker: Belaya
text: What are you doing here?! Did the Jedi Council send you? I swear I will expose you if they have!

speaker: Player
text: Err... do I know you?

speaker: Belaya
text: So you do not even have the decency to remember me? I have cursed your name every moment since we last met on Dantooine.

speaker: Belaya
text: I am Belaya, once of the Jedi but now of the Sith... it was your murder of Juhani that placed this bitter blackness in my heart!

speaker: Belaya
text: I couldn't touch you on Dantooine, but I can, here! The Sith have taught me the power of freedom... and revenge! FOR JUHANI!!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] No, the Jedi certainly didn't send me here.

speaker: Belaya
text: [Success] I see. So you have come to join the Sith as I have? I should have known that would happen, as should the Council.

speaker: Belaya
text: The Council is nothing but a slow and doddering farce, placing all their trust in you... and you failed them, just as you failed Juhani.

speaker: Belaya
text: Do you even remember me? I am Belaya, and it is your murder of Juhani that brought me here. Fortunately, I have learned the power of revenge!

speaker: Belaya
text: [Failure] You do not fool me for a second! The Council fawns over you and places all their hope in you to save them... you wouldn't turn on them!

speaker: Belaya
text: You are a spy... and a murderer. It was you who killed Juhani and placed this bitter blackness in my heart that I cannot get rid of!

speaker: Player
text: I'll not suffer your insults!

speaker: Belaya
text: But you will! You pretend to be a Sith, but I know who you are! I have cursed your name every moment since we last met on Dantooine!

speaker: Waiter
text: I'm sorry. I'm too busy to talk. I have to get these drink orders to the customers!

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Huh? Who are you? The spice labs are off limits! You better tell me what you're doing here or I'll call the guards!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Sorry. I'm new here. I must have gotten lost.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: [Success] Another new mechanic? Brejik's gone crazy - he's hiring anyone who ever picked up a blast torch!

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Well, you can't just go wandering around the spice labs! All you mechanics have to stay on the north side of the floor- you should know that!

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: No way! We lab techs aren't allowed to talk to you mechanics; too many of you are spice addicts looking to score. Brejik doesn't trust you guys.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Look, you should just go. This is my private room - there's nothing for you here. All the spice stays in the lab next door. Now get out of here or I'll have to call the guards.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, I'm going. Don't get upset.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Glad to see you're being reasonable.

speaker: Player
text: How are you going to report me with a blaster hole in your chest?

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Brejik warned me I might have to protect myself from spice addicts looking to score - looks like he was right!

speaker: Player
text: I'm just looking around.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: Looking for some spice, I'll bet! They warned me that a lot of you mechanics were addicts who would come snooping around looking for a fix.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to kill you.

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: [Failure] Lost, huh? Right. I bet you're here to steal some spice! You mechanics are all the same!

speaker: Vulkar Lab Tech
text: You again? If anyone catches you here they'll shoot first and ask questions later. Why aren't back on the north side where you mechanics belong?

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Only the Arbiters are permitted into the prison cells, human.
comment: first time conversation or not an arbiter

speaker: Player
text: I am sorry. I will be going now.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Sunry's trial is over, human. You are no longer an Arbiter of the Selkath courts. I cannot allow you into the cells.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: You may come and go as you please, Arbiter - you will find the door unlocked.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: If you wish to begin your trial, you must make the request with the warden. It shall then be passed on to the judges.

speaker: Rakata
text: The One is the greatest warrior in the long history of our tribe. He will lead us to victory over all our enemies!

speaker: Rakata
text: We are the greatest of the Black Rakata. No leader is stronger than the One, and no other tribe commands the war beasts as we do.

speaker: Rakata
text: The One is studying the secrets of the Red Rakata. In time he will use them to unlock the knowledge trapped within the Temple of the Ancients!

speaker: Rakata
text: Once the Red Rakata are destroyed there will be none who dare to stand against our tribe!

speaker: Sith Patron
text: This Tarisian ale is fantastic! We should have conquered this planet ages ago!

speaker: Sith Patron
text: This cantina isn't the fanciest joint I've ever been in, but it's a good place to unwind after a hard shift at the military base.

speaker: Sith Patron
text: Taris isn't such a bad place. I've been stationed in worse places than this during my commission.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: Damn those Sith - they're bombing the whole planet! I knew they'd turn on us sooner or... well, look what we got here! Thieves in the hangar.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: So, you figured you'd just steal my ship for your get-away and leave me high and dry while the Sith turn the planet into dust? Sorry, but that ain't going to happen!

speaker: Calo082
text: I'll take care of them, Davik. I've been looking forward to this for a long time!

speaker: Davik Kang
text: Make it quick, Calo. The Sith mean business. If we don't get to our ships and find somewhere safe, the bombs they're dropping will kill us all.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Sorry, but you're too late to recruit me. I've just hired on with the Sith. Of course, if the Republic has a better offer...

speaker: Player
text: I'm not a recruiter.

speaker: Mercenary
text: Then why are you bothering me? I'm here on Manaan to find work as a mercenary. I'm not here to chat with tourists.

speaker: Player
text: You'd work for the Sith? They're evil!

speaker: Mercenary
text: Hey, keep your lectures. The Sith pay well, and they pay up front. That's all I care about.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you a few questions.

speaker: Mercenary
text: I don't have time to sit here and answer your questions. I have to get ready - the Sith want me to report to their Embassy first thing tomorrow.

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: Bastila! You were a fool to betray the Master... and an even bigger fool to return to the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: The only fools are those who still follow Malak. Open your eyes and see the true Lord of the Sith: Revan has returned!

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: Revan is nothing! Malak earned the title of Dark Lord by defeating his old Master - and now I will become Malak's new apprentice by doing the same!

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: You... talked to Mekel? Have I proved my worth? Did he say anything...?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Mekel is tricking you. He'll never let you into the academy.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Success] Oh... oh. All this... for nothing...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Failure] N-no! That can't be... you're wrong! I... can't have wasted my life...

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] He said you should go home. The Sith aren't for you.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Success] Go... home...? I...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: [Failure] I... don't believe you! You just want to... be chosen! But... it will be me! It will be... me...

speaker: Player
text: No. I'll be going.

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: No, p-please... I... I cannot...

speaker: Prospective Sith Student
text: P-please... don't hurt me... I am too weak with hunger...

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Hardly any shifts available this week. I should give up digging.
comment: This is a generic dialogue for the rodians that do a circuit on the streets of Anchorhead 17.12a

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Never thought I'd see moisture farming as a better living than mining.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Leave me alone. I'm leaving this rock, I swear.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Anchorhead... sure different than they said when I was recruited. Can't make a life here.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: I bet they shut this place down... I would.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Another company loses everything on Tatooine. Sand People must love this.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: The raids on the crawlers hardly make a dent... the mines are failing anyway.

speaker: Duros Miner
text: Go on, leave me alone.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: The droid is now active. It will attack any enemies that come in range.

speaker: Player
text: Activate droid's shields. (<CUSTOM42> repair part(s))

speaker: Combat Droid
text: [Success] The droid's shields are now active.

speaker: Player
text: Engage droid in patrol mode. (<CUSTOM42> repair part(s))

speaker: Combat Droid
text: [Success] Patrol mode engaged. Once you end this session the droid will begin patrol and destroy any enemies it encounters.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: WARNING: Once you end this session the droid's program will be locked in. You will not be able to modifiy the droid anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Leave it alone.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: The droid engages its patrol mode and moves off to carry out your programmed instructions.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: [Failure] You do not have enough repair parts.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: This droid is damaged and inactive.

speaker: Player
text: DROID REPAIR TUTORIAL

speaker: Combat Droid
text: Some droids in the game are disabled or damaged and can be repaired by the player. Fixing a droid in this manner requires repair parts.

speaker: Combat Droid
text: More complicated repairs require more repair parts. The number of repair parts required varies depending on the REPAIR skill of the character working on the droid.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, welcome to my home, such as it is. Pull up a stump and be comfortable. We should discuss a few things.

speaker: Player
text: Like who you are, for example?

speaker: Jolee
text: Ah, what is there to tell? Jolee Bindo is the crazy old man in the dangerous woods. I'm content with the impression I give.
comment: Initial, Having never asked this question before.

speaker: Player
text: But you use a lightsaber in battle. You are a Jedi.

speaker: Jolee
text: I follow the Jedi Way and I command the Force, yes, and I suppose that makes me as much a Jedi as anyone... but what of it?

speaker: Player
text: There's something you should know about me. I used to be... I used to be Darth Revan.

speaker: Jolee
text: *Sigh* I have no idea what you're talking about. Rabble rabble... what are you saying.

speaker: Player
text: Didn't you hear me? I used to be Revan, until the Jedi wiped away my identity!

speaker: Jolee
text: Does it change anything? I'm not here to judge you. You'll do what you have to, and I'll help if I can.

speaker: Jolee
text: I've seen my share of the dark and the light. And frankly, both extremes annoy me. Of course... I have felt the rumblings of change...

speaker: Mission
text: It's kind of nice to meet a Jedi who isn't all hung up on this light side, dark side stuff. It gets pretty tiring, you know?

speaker: Jolee
text: Perhaps you will be of some assistance to me after all. Let us discuss what you came here for.

speaker: Player
text: You are difficult to deal with. It worries me.

speaker: Jolee
text: Ah, and it makes you think I may have the taint of the dark side in me, doesn't it? Ooh. Is that what you are wondering, huh? Ooh.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, I assure you, I see more grey than dark or light. I'm just a stubborn old man, tired of the foolishness of others.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Jolee
text: *Sigh* Fine, fine, just be brief.
comment: player has not gotten rid of the poachers MUST ONLY APPEAR IF TALKTIMES IS SECONDARY

speaker: Player
text: I have made certain the poachers are gone.
comment: player has gotten rid of the poachers MUST ONLY APPEAR IF TALKTIMES IS SECONDARY

speaker: Jolee
text: Yes, I heard the fuss of it. I told you I wanted a non-violent solution, and I had my reasons for it. You should have thought about that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Czerka Corporation will find the bodies and blame the Wookiees. This may cause more troops to be deployed. That means more disruption.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm not pleased, but what's done is done and I'm not here to judge you. Hopefully you'll take care of that yourself.

speaker: Player
text: I couldn't find a peaceful solution. I regret that.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, perhaps I have a duty to point out what you should have learned from this. Or perhaps... no.

speaker: Jolee
text: Was that convincing? It's been a while since I've been in the company of someone that needed that kind of babysitting.

text: Good to finally meet you, Davik. My name's <FullName>.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: You know, Canderous was right. The Exchange is always looking for new talent. You could have a bright future with our organization.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: With a recommendation from Canderous - and a thorough background check - you could become part of the Exchange. Many would kill to prove themselves worthy of this honor.

speaker: Player
text: Your offer intrigues me, Davik.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: Come with me - I will give you a tour of my operations. I'm certain you'll be most impressed.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: Ah, there she is - the Ebon Hawk. My pride and joy; the fastest ship in the Outer Rim! Note the state of the art security system I've had installed to protect her.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: The shields are completely impregnable. Nobody can get past them without the codes to try and steal my baby. Unfortunately, the Sith military blockade has grounded my vessel.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: The Ebon Hawk can outrun any vessel in the galaxy, but even she isn't fast enough to avoid the auto-targeting laser cannons of the orbiting Sith fleet.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: I am, of course, working on acquiring the Sith departure codes so that I may come and go as I please. However, progress has been slow... but we should continue our tour.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: These will be your accommodations. The slave quarters are just down the hall. If you need anything during your stay - food, a massage - feel free to call upon their services.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: If all goes well with your background check you will be invited to join the Exchange. I'd advise you to accept the offer when it comes - or suffer the dire consequences of refusal.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking forward to working with you, Davik.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: You will stay in these rooms as my guest for the next few days; I will not accept no for an answer. Feel free to visit the slave quarters at any time during your stay.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: I must warn you that if you are found anywhere outside the guest wing during your stay - or if you bother my other guests - my security forces will deal with you most harshly.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: I will return after the investigation into your background is complete. Until then, make yourself comfortable. Come, Calo, let us leave our guests in peace.

speaker: Cand
text: Okay, we're inside. Now all we have to do is figure out a way to get past the Ebon Hawk's security system and we can get the rest of your group and get off this planet!

speaker: Cand
text: No sense waiting around here, though. The sooner we get off Taris the better.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, but I can't stay.

speaker: Player
text: Am I a prisoner here?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, I'm not interested.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: Don't be so hasty. Our allies end up much better off than our enemies - as both Canderous and Calo Nord could surely tell you. The Exchange has much to offer.

speaker: Player
text: It was nothing I couldn't handle.

speaker: Player
text: Brejik had to learn that double-crossers tend to end up dead!

speaker: Davik Kang
text: An important lesson to learn, no doubt. In my line of business I've seen far too many people suffer for not understanding it.

speaker: Player
text: I didn't know you were a swoop fan.

speaker: Davik Kang
text: A casual fan at best, but everyone on Taris follows the big season opener. But we have more important issues to discuss now.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Ah, the Arbiter. Since you have been permitted to defend Sunry against these accusations I shall assist how I can.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of Sunry?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Sunry was a great warrior in his time. He fought for the Republic against the Sith aggression and proved valorous.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I have great respect for his accomplishments and find it tragic that he finds himself in his current condition.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: If the Republic had more individuals like him right now, I do not believe the Sith would be so great a problem for your people.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Is there any other way I can assist you?

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything suspicious about this case?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I find it questionable that a man with such a reputable past as Sunry would murder a Sith woman. Especially not from behind.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But knowing the Sith, there was probably some deception involved. They seek to do the same thing to us here.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: There has been much pressure by the Sith on our government - and even on the judges themselves - to deliver a guilty verdict in this case.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But the letter of the law is absolute, and we will not be compromised for Sith power-games.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Is there anything else you need?

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Republic and the Sith Empire?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I find this great battle being waged across the galaxy both disturbing and, ultimately, tragic.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: For all its faults, your tottering Republic has benefitted the vast majority of the galaxy for many millenia. To see it fall into ruin in such a short time...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I do not like the Sith, that I make no effort to hide. I will even admit that if given the option, I would rule that we should join the Republic.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But I must remain impartial and rule on this case as the law requires.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Do you have any additional questions?

speaker: Player
text: I have no more questions for now.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: If there is anything else you require, feel free to inquire with me.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Republic citizens are welcome on Manaan, but official inquiries should go through the proper channels.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Your function with the courts is complete. You should not interrupt our proceddings in this manner.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Judge Shelkar can answer questions of off-world visitors during normal hours.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Allow me to introduce myself. I am Crattis Yurkal, proprietor of the general store here on Dantooine. Not much to look at now, I'll admit, but I'm in on the ground floor!

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: I mean, look at this planet - majestic fields, rolling plains, wide open terra firma. Elbow room - that's what people want.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Once word gets out, we'll have settlers and tourists from the galactic core just dying to come here.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: And guess who'll be waiting for them? Not that blasted Czerka Corp., that's for sure! Not this time, no sir! This time it'll be Crattis Yurkal who makes the big bucks! But listen to me...

speaker: Crattis Yurkal

speaker: Player

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: But I'm sure you'll find all my inventory is of the highest quality... and I've got a few special items you won't find anywhere else!

speaker: Player
text: What do you have against the Czerka Corporation?

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Don't get me started on Czerka Corp.!

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: They've got a monopoly on half the galaxy already, and they do everything they can to keep anyone else from getting a foothold in their territory: extortion, bribing officials and government diplomats.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Not to mention driving up prices on essentials like food and water on distant colonies. I've heard stories of them letting people starve to death because they couldn't afford their jacked-up prices!

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: And since they've thrown themselves in with the Sith, things have only gotten worse.

speaker: Player
text: Worse? How has it gotten worse?

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: The Sith are tangled up in an expensive war with the Republic. They need supplies, equipment, resources.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: There's lots of opportunities for a company with no morals, like Czerka Corp., to make some major profits. Malak has given them exclusive trading rights wherever the Sith have control.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: It's bad enough they're helping to finance the Sith war effort, but I've heard rumors of even worse stuff.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Slaving, pillaging planets of their resources, genocide of indigenous species. The Sith and Czerka Corp. seem like a perfect match to me. Ah, listen to me going on...

speaker: Player
text: Do you mean Czerka Corp. are allied with the Sith?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe we could discuss this some other time.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Be sure to come back every now and again. I'm always getting more inventory in. You never know what I might have in stock, and my prices are always better than those crooks at Czerka Corp.!

speaker: Player
text: What have you heard about the Mandalorian raiders?

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: They're vermin, mostly. Leftovers from the Mandalorian Wars. They lost their armies and worlds and now wander the galaxy raiding weak farms and outposts.

speaker: Cand

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: Any reasonably well-defended base could withstand them. This Enclave, for instance, would never fall to them.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: They do make trouble for the farmers though... They're almost as much of a burden on ordinary people as that damn Czerka Corporation! But I digress...

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
text: You must be the one I've been hearing about... the new recruit, as it were. <FullName>, I think they said.

speaker: Crattis Yurkal

speaker: Crattis Yurkal
