text: I wish I had some type of reward to give you, but we Outcasts have nothing. All I can offer is the gratitude of the entire village.

speaker: Outcast Healer
text: Back again. Is there something else you need?

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: How dare you invade my chambers! How rude! I am a personal guest of Davik himself! I left specific instructions that you guards were not to disturb me until morning!

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: How can Davik expect me to invest in his ventures with this kind of incompetence on display? I should summon the other guards and report you to your commanding officer!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Uh... Davik just wanted me to make sure you didn't need anything.

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: [Success] Well, I suppose I can forgive the intrusion in this case. Tell Davik I admire a host who has his underlings check up on the well-being and comfort of his guests.

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: I don't require anything right now - you can tell Davik everything about my stay has been most pleasing so far. Here's a five credit chip for your trouble, sirrah.

speaker: Player
text: I don't work for Davik, you over-inflated windbag!

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: Don't work for Davik? Then what are you... oh blast! Assassins! Guards, save me!

speaker: Player
text: Thank you, sir.

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: Now scurry on back to Davik. If I find I have need of anything I'll buzz for you. Until then I expect you to respect my privacy.

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: [Failure] That is no excuse for incompetence! I gave very specific orders that were not followed. I'm going to summon the guards and report you to your superiors!

speaker: Player
text: You touch that alarm and you're a dead man!

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: What? How dare you speak to me like that! I could ask Davik to have you flayed alive for such insolence!

speaker: Player
text: That's it - time for you to die!

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: What? But... help! Assassins! Guards - help!

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: You again? My instructions were not complicated. Give me one good reason why I shouldn't call the other guards and have your incompetence reported to the commanding officer!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] I'm just checking up on you again.

speaker: Tarisian Noble
text: [Success] Well, if you think I'm going to tip you again you're sadly mistaken. Now leave me be.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Great Chuundar has finished with you, <FullName>. You may walk the sacred boughs of our village, but expect no further audience.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Go, and expect no more to be said!

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: You have been given a task, outsider. Be thankful for your time on our world and do as you have been bid.

speaker: Player
text: I want to speak with Chuundar again.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: You be allowed audience when you return after completing his task. Only then will you have reason.

speaker: Player
text: I will need directions.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: The village exit is northwest of here. Once outside, follow the platform to the east until you get to where Gorwooken is waiting.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: He will lower you to the Shadowlands, though I would prefer that you were simply dropped. You'll die down there anyway.

speaker: Player
text: What can I expect to find in the Shadowlands?

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: If the forest holds any justice you will die down there, as would all outsiders.

speaker: Player
text: I want directions for what's in the village.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Others may speak to you, <FullName>, but I won't. I don't want you here. The sooner you are gone, the better.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going then.

speaker: Wookiee Guard
text: Return when Chuundar's task is complete. That is what the Chieftain wants.

speaker: Jordo
text: [This man appears to be looking for someone... maybe even one of your companions back on the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Jordo
text: Carth! Carth Onasi, is that you?

speaker: Carth
text: Jordo?

speaker: Jordo
text: It *is* you, isn't it? I knew it when I laid eyes on you! You old spacedog, how have you been? I thought for sure you'd be fighting on some ship out there.

speaker: Carth
text: I was. I crashed.

speaker: Jordo
text: Ha ha ha! That's pretty rich. I can't imagine what it would take to keep you on the ground.

speaker: Jordo
text: Must have something to do with your friend, here, hey? How's it going?

speaker: Player
text: Can we hurry this up...?

speaker: Jordo
text: Oh, I apologize. You folks are probably busy, aren't you? I just wanted to catch up with Carth, that's all.

speaker: Carth
text: So, what are you doing here, Jordo? The last time I saw you was on, um... well, Telos, actually.

speaker: Jordo
text: Yeah... it's a shame about home. Telos still hasn't recovered. The family and I moved on, and I'm working for Czerka now.

speaker: Jordo
text: I didn't see you after... er, what I mean is, my condolences on your wife. I heard what happened. At least your boy made it through alright.

speaker: Carth
text: My... boy? You mean... Dustil?

speaker: Jordo
text: Yes, of course. I saw him not long ago here on Korriban, though he didn't recognize me. You... didn't know he was here?

speaker: Carth
text: No! Jordo, Dustil has been missing since the attack on Telos! Are you... are you absolutely certain it was him?!

speaker: Jordo
text: Yeah. I'd recognize Dustil anywhere. Positive. He's, uh... he's joined the Sith, Carth...

speaker: Carth
text: What do you mean he's joined the Sith?

speaker: Jordo
text: There's an academy for the Sith on Korriban. He's a student there. I saw him suited up in their outfit and everything. Sorry... I thought you knew.

speaker: Carth
text: No... no, I... I didn't. Well, thanks for telling me, Jordo.

speaker: Jordo
text: Sure, no problem. Good to see you again, Carth. Hope everything works out with Dustil.

speaker: Carth
text: Dustil... Dustil is alive! We have to go to the Korriban academy and find him!

speaker: Player
text: We have other priorities, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: You think I don't know that? I just... if there's a chance we can try to find him... I don't want to wait to track him down, if possible.

speaker: Carth
text: All this time I've thought he was... he must be a man by now...

speaker: Player
text: I understand. We'll go as soon as possible.

speaker: Carth
text: Thank you. I... I just have to see him. I have to know what happened to him.

speaker: Player
text: Are you sure that's wise?

speaker: Carth
text: I don't know. I don't know why Dustil would be with the Sith... but I... I have to find out. There's simply no choice.

speaker: Jordo
text: Yes, of course. I saw him at my last stop, on Korriban, though he didn't recognize me. You... didn't know he was there?

speaker: Player
text: You're a friend of Carth's, I take it?

speaker: Jordo
text: Sure am. We joined the militia together back on Telos. That was a lot of years ago, of course.

speaker: Player
text: Nice to meet you, Jordo.

speaker: Jordo
text: Must have something to do with your pretty friend, here, hey? How do you do, miss?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Excellent work, my young Sith. Your enemy lies dead at your feet and you are victorious... the final test is complete.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I must say that... unnhh! What... what is happening?! My strength is... fading! What have you done?!

speaker: Player
text: Oh. That must be the poison kicking in, finally.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You... you fool! You will never... never be a Sith, now!!

speaker: Player
text: I got what I came here for. The Star Map.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You... I will destroy you, mongrel! I will rip the flesh from your bones!!

speaker: Player
text: Never? I'm hurt by that. Really, I am.

speaker: Player
text: That's the idea! Time to die, scum!

speaker: Player
text: My mission is to recover the Star Map, not become a Sith.

speaker: Player
text: You are as evil and twisted as Malak. You Sith deserve to die!

speaker: Player
text: I did what I had to to wipe your kind of evil from the galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: You didn't think I actually wanted to be a Sith, did you?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: What?! But, but... why did... you come?! Why... are you here, if not to become Sith?!

speaker: Player
text: You two were pathetically easy to turn on each other.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I must say that it is quite disappointing that you must die now, as well, seeing as you didn't inform me earlier of Yuthura's plans.

speaker: Player
text: What? But I passed your test!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So you did. And now I shall destroy you as I would any other Sith who betrayed me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So let's get this over with, shall we? I have a new batch of candidates arriving tomorrow.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be a fool, Sith. I'll destroy you.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Destroy me? I am not Yuthura, young one. I am a Sith Master... and I tire of foolish upstarts.

speaker: Player
text: It's okay. I'm not here to join the Sith anyway.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Is that so? So you were a spy all along? How interesting.

speaker: Player
text: It figures. You are as evil and twisted as Malak.

speaker: Player
text: I am not here to join the Sith, anyway. My mission is done.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I must say that it is quite disappointing that you must die now, as well, since there's no telling how far your scheming with Yuthura went.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You are truly a Sith in spirit, and one gifted with great power. Of this I no longer have any doubt. There is much more for you to learn, perhaps... but not here.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: There is... something very strange about you, young one. Something I cannot place. You are like no other student I have ever met.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Why that is, I cannot say. Your path takes you elsewhere, however, and soon.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Go on to your destiny, then, and return here afterwards... if that is what you still desire.

speaker: Player
text: So am I a Sith now or not?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You have passed the final test, but I see it is not yet your destiny to join the order. Perhaps that will come in time, young one.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: There is much you must accomplish, first. The dark side has plans for you. As I said... return once that is done, if you desire.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps we shall meet again.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: May the Force serve you well, young one.

speaker: Player
text: Alright, I'll go.

speaker: Player
text: My desire is to see you dead, actually.

speaker: Player
text: My desire is to see all evil such as yourself defeated.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Is it... is it possible that you are not what you seem to be? Tell me, young one... tell me what you really are.

speaker: Player
text: I am Darth Revan. Bow before me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Ah, I see. So it is... Darth Revan, not dead as we were led to believe.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: And yet... and yet you are *not* Revan, are you? What has occurred between the time of your reported death and now I can only guess at, but you have changed much.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Regardless, your destiny does take you away from here... to confront your old pupil, without a doubt. Yes... that is what lies before you.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Go to your destiny, then, my Dark Lord. I shall say nothing of what you have done here. Should you prove victorious and wish to return, then I and all Sith shall be your servants.

speaker: Player
text: I was once Darth Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Who or what I am is not important.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I see. No matter what you might be, then, I am certain that your path takes you elsewhere... and soon.

speaker: Player
text: If you were not blind, you would already know.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Do not let your attention waver! Strike her down!!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So you return to us with the lightsaber in hand, as I knew you would.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The Force has served you well.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You took a great risk in acquiring the artifact. You used your mind and your power... no peaceful meditation, no pacifism.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Sometimes you must fight in order to achieve. This gives you your passion, this makes you stronger. This is what makes you superior.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: That is the lesson we teach with that part of the final test. Do you understand?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are not the only ones who fight and take risks.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: True, but most would say they fight only when they must... or not at all. We are the ones who know that struggle is what makes us superior.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying a Jedi couldn't have gotten the lightsaber?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: When a Jedi acts, it is with skill, true. But the Jedi teach you that your passions are counter-productive. That strength is only found in peace.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Did you not feel a moment of excitement in the tomb? Did your passions not flow and make you feel stronger and more alive?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: What purpose would be served by restricting yourself from such? I would say only the purpose of the Jedi. Through this they would control you and restrict your potential.

speaker: Player
text: I wouldn't say I exerted myself getting this.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Perhaps not, to someone of your natural strength. The point is in the recognition of the nature of the act rather than its sheer difficulty.

speaker: Player
text: I don't believe you. I don't feel superior to anyone.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: If you came to the academy, you must have felt the stirrings within you that cry out for the freedom of the dark side, that cry out for release.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I can only show you the path that will lead to power and superiority. You have followed it this far... you must decide if you are capable of continuing.

speaker: Player
text: And if I'm not?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: This is where your path ends, young one. There is no turning back once you have embarked on it.

speaker: Player
text: I think I understand.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Good. The last part of your test will now commence. Here you will learn the lesson of competition.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: All life must compete in order to flourish. Such is the natural way of the universe. To stand still is to know death... one must always be moving forward.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So is it the same amongst the Sith. Compete or die. Mercy is irrelevant.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So it behooves you in this final test to strike down one you are familiar with, for no other reason than to prove you are superior and without mercy.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Normally this would be against another student. You, however, get a special treat. You will fight Yuthura, here... my own apprentice.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You talk too much, old fool.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So... you know, do you? Well, it makes no difference. You have become too ambitious, Yuthura... it is time for you to die.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: No, it is time for *you* to die, master. My pupil stands with me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Oh? Is this true, young one? You wish to join Yuthura in her foolish scheme?

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, Uthar... I'm with Yuthura on this one.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Do you hear that, my master? That is the sound of a new leader rising to replace you.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So the time has come, has it? I... I will... ugh... no! My... strength leaves me!!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are weak, Uthar, and the Force has abandoned you. We have made sure of it!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: So the time has come, has it? You both wish to stand against a Sith Master and perish, do you? THEN SO BE IT!!

speaker: Player
text: I'm with you, Master Uthar.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You fool! You have no idea what you've done!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: The final test continues as it should. Proceed and be rewarded, young one.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The only 'reward'... you... no! My strength... is leaving me!!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: It appears, my dear, that some tests are fairer than others. I wish you luck.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You... betrayed me?! I thought... we were friends! Damn you!!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The only 'reward' you will get is death!!

speaker: Player
text: You're both mistaken. I choose me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You are indeed a fool if you think to oppose us both, young one.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: To think I actually believed for a moment that you and I were friends. So be it.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Do not fret, my dear. All will be... ugh... no! My strength... leaves me!!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The poison! You will pay for this, you... you... damn you! My blood burns!!

speaker: Player
text: What can I say? I'm no fool.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You will never leave here!!

speaker: Player
text: You were too easy to turn on each other.

speaker: Player
text: Your evil was all too eager to turn on each other, remember?

speaker: Player
text: I did what I had to. Time to die, Sith.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The poison! You will pay for this! We will destroy you!!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Do not fret, my dear. All will be as it was quickly enough.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You will pay for this, you... you... Damn you! My strength... it's... poisoned!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You will pay for this, fool! We will destroy you!!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Hmph. To think that I actually hoped you could be of use to me.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: This makes no sense. You will never become a Sith if you turn on us both! What could you hope to accomplish?

speaker: Player
text: I have the power to kill you both; I am the true Sith here!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Betrayed! He *is* a spy!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Betrayed! She *is* a spy!

speaker: Player
text: You think I wish to be a Sith? I am a spy for the Jedi, fools!

speaker: Player
text: I used you both to complete my mission.

speaker: Player
text: I would never become an evil Sith. I came for the Star Map.

speaker: Player
text: My mission is to defeat Malak, as well as all you Sith.

speaker: Player
text: I did what I had to, to wipe your kind of evil from the galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: I'm tired of playing along with you Sith scum! You both die!!

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Sadly, Yuthura, it is you who are mistaken. Your pupil is more ambitious than you realize... isn't that so, young one?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What?! So this is what you had planned all along. You wish me killed.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Indeed. You have become too ambitious, Yuthura. It is time for you to die and someone more... talented... to take your place.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You must locate the ceremonial lightsaber and return here to us. Yuthura and I cannot help you in this, young one.
comment: final test has begun ceremonial saber not possessed

speaker: kor39_finaltomb
text: [A day passes in preparation. Uthar then takes you and Yuthura to the Sith tomb. Your companions are not permitted to join you.]

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Very well. We are now ready for your final test, young Sith. You have earned the right to see if you shall become one of us.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Indeed you have.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: I dislike your tone, Yuthura. What are you up to, now?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Nothing of course, my master. I was merely agreeing with you. Should we not get on with the test?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Yes. Yes, of course. We are in the sacred tomb of Naga Sadow, young one, the one discovered by Darth Malak and Darth Revan years ago.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You are to follow in their footsteps and reach the ancient Star Map that lies deep within. There you will find a lightsaber, amongst other things.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: The lightsaber is for you: your initiation present. Return to us once you have it, for you the test does not end there.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Be very cautious, here. This tomb is like the others in this valley, and many of its old defenses remain active.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Do you understand what I have told you? Are you ready to begin?

speaker: Player
text: I don't understand... why not just give me the saber?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: If you do not strive to achieve something, then it will be meaningless to you, wouldn't you say?

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me anything about what I will face?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: No. That is part of the test. Overcome the obstacles that lie ahead on your own.

speaker: Player
text: Can I leave the tomb?

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: You cannot. No one enters and no one leaves until your test is complete.

speaker: Player
text: Find the Star Map. Return with the lightsaber. I understand.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Good. Yuthura and I will await your return.

speaker: Uthar Wynn
text: Is that a tone of mischief in your voice, dear Yuthura? You should know by now that no scheme is certain.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As should you, my master. But I was only agreeing with you. Should we not get on with the test?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... I don't know what you're talking about, master. I am not... scheming. Should we not get on with the test?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: [This man fearfully avoids your eyes. He couldn't say anything to you even if he wanted.]
comment: This line is NOT VO. DO NOT RECORD.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: You again? Oh no, you can just keep walking. I'm not dealing with you again.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Something you want? I don't have a lot of time for talk, so please make it quick.
comment: Initial selected This is the mechaninc outside the sand crawler garage

speaker: Player
text: I just want to ask some questions.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Of course, I always have time for a pretty face... any face, really. What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: Describe your job and who you work for.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I repair the sandcrawlers when they return from the mines. They get pretty banged up, even without the attacks.

speaker: Player
text: What attacks do you mean?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: The Sand People attack them pretty regularly. Czerka Corporation is getting pretty sick of it, I hear.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: They have offered bounties on Sand People for a while now, but few hunters take them up on it. Too dangerous.

speaker: Player
text: Where can I learn about these bounties?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Try at the Czerka offices right here. They'd know.

speaker: Player
text: When do the sandcrawlers head out?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Oh, the big crawlers head out at dawn. That's so they avoid the bigger predators. The wraid, I mean.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Doesn't help avoid the Sand People though. They attack pretty regular, no matter what Czerka Corporation tries.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know where the attacks come from?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I have no idea. I don't go out on the desert if I can help it. I'm sure the Sand People will find you if you walk far enough.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Tatooine and Anchorhead?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Well, it's a hole in the galaxy, as far as I'm concerned. I doubt this outpost will last much longer.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: But, that's happened before and will happen again. Anchorhead has been resettled a few times now.

speaker: Player
text: Why have previous settlements failed?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Well, Tatooine fools people. It looks like it might have a good supply of resources, but it doesn't.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Before a company learns this, they've already set up communities to support operations they now can't afford.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Company pulls out, cities dry up, and after a few years, someone that doesn't know why it failed tries again.

speaker: Player
text: Czerka Corporation isn't doing well here?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: No one is. I guess it looked like a promising mining planet, but the metal... I tell you, it just isn't right.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I've been a mechanic my whole life, and I've never seen anything corrode as fast as Tatooine metal.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: It's why whoever was here before left, and why Czerka will leave, and why whoever comes next will leave.

speaker: Player
text: That's all I need. Goodbye.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: All right then. Back to work, I guess.

speaker: Player
text: I've signed on to try and stop the Sand People attacks.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Have you? Not many hunters have tried in the past. Good luck to you, is all I can say. The Sand People are vicious.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I see the damage on the crawlers when they come back... if they come back.

speaker: Player
text: The attacks will stop. I've dealt with the Sand People.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I guess they have been happening a lot less frequently lately. If you did have anything to do with that, thanks.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I hope Czerka paid you well for it. Whatever it was, it wouldn't have been enough for me.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing. Goodbye.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Hey... aren't you a swoop-jock? I can't help with bike problems. I work with the heavy stuff.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Hmm? All right, but I'm not sure what I could say to interest you. I just work on the crawlers.

speaker: Player
text: I'll take however long I want. Understand?

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Uh, is there some kind of a problem? I'm just doing my job, I don't want any trouble from you.

speaker: Player
text: I think you're my problem. Maybe I should do something about it.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: Hey... why are you threatening me? I just repair the crawlers. It's not like I'm packing away the credits.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Is there a point to this? This man is no danger to us.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: I don't need this. What are you trying to prove?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Never speak to me again, worm. Never.

speaker: Sandcrawler Mechanic
text: [Success] [His face turns an ashen white. He is suddenly very, very afraid of you, and could not speak even if he wanted to.]

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Sorry, but your kind aren't welcome in here. The Hidden Beks don't care much for you Sith.

speaker: Player
text: You better change your tone if you know what's good for you!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: The swoop gangs rule down here, not you! You may have conquered Upper Taris, but you don't have enough troops to sweep the whole Lower City.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: You come down here in force and we'll pick you off in hit and run battles, then vanish like smoke into the back alleys and hidden tunnels where you'll never find us!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Stick to the Upper City where people are actually scared of you; your threats don't count for much down here.

speaker: Player
text: Let me in or I come back with a hundred Sith troopers!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Yeah, you do that. Go back to the Upper City where your shiny uniforms will make the citizens quake in their boots.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Hey, you can't just walk in here! This is the Hidden Bek base. How do I know you're not a Vulkar spy sent to kill Gadon Thek?

speaker: Player
text: I'm no spy!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Maybe so, but this door is locked and it's going to stay that way until I'm satisfied you're no threat to Gadon or the Hidden Beks.

speaker: Player
text: I have to speak to Gadon. It's important.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: A lot of people want to go inside and speak to Gadon. He's a hero of the common folk. But the days of the Hidden Bek's open door policy are gone.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Between the Sith conquest and the Vulkar gang war Gadon has more enemies than he used to. We're being careful about who we let in now.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Maybe a bribe could get me in?

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: [Failure] My loyalty's not for sale! I've been with the Hidden Beks for years, and I'm not going to desert Gadon now just because everyone is turning against him!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I could be an ally against all those enemies.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Well, we do need all the help we can get. And you don't look like you're with the Vulkars or the Sith.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Besides, it's not like you can do anything to harm Gadon in the heart of his own base. Not with Zaerdra watching his back.

speaker: Player
text: So you're going to let me in?

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Go in and speak to Gadon if you want. Just remember to be on your best behavior... the Hidden Beks are watching you.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry. I'll be going now.

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Fair enough. But here's some free advice: get off the streets. The Black Vulkars are taking shots at anyone wandering the streets of the Lower City.

speaker: Player
text: I need Gadon's help. I was told to speak to him.

speaker: Player
text: I go wherever I want!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: Hey - I recognize you! You're the one who won the swoop race!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: You were racing for those damn Vulkars! You'll pay for that!

speaker: Hidden Bek Lookout
text: You better be careful out here. Those damn Vulkars will be looking to get even with you for winning that race and killing Brejik.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Canderous! I haven't seen you since the Republic broke our ranks at the battle of Malachor!
comment: first time conversation if canderous is in the party

speaker: Cand
text: Ergeron, I see you've got some new guns to add to your collection. Times must have been profitable for you since the war.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Very profitable. When the Republic defeated our fleets, I learned a valuable lesson: it's far better to be a freelance mercenary in a war than to be a soldier for the losing side.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: If you're here to offer me a job, I'm not interested right now. I've got so many offers I can't keep up as it is.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Maybe that Iridorian skullslacker at the bar, or the Echani nerfherder cowering in the corner is available.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Normally I'd charge you for information, but times are good right now and I'm feeling generous. So ask your questions, free of charge.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about the murder of Elassa?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Not really. They say some Republic war hero killed her. Maybe you should check out the Republic Embassy.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about ancient ruins or a Star Map?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: If there ever were any ruins on this world, they've long since disappeared beneath the oceans.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you hate the Republic for defeating your people?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: I'm a realist. It was war, after all. And even though the Republic destroyed my people, the leaders of the armada were Revan and Malak, so I hate the Sith just as much.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: And with this war, there's plenty of opportunity to take bloody vengeance against both sides and make a nice profit along the way. We Mandalorians are always practical. Not like those blood-thirsty Iridorians, or those honor-bound Echani.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Is there anything else you want?

speaker: Player
text: What do you have against the Echani and the Iridorians?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Nothing, except the Echani are a bunch of fey dancers, prancing into battle with tiny weapons not fit for Mandalorian children. They hardly wear any armor because it slows them down when they run away.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: But the Echani are better than the Iridorians. Those savages keep hacking at fallen foe even after death, mutilating the corpse out of pure blood lust.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: I even heard they'll turn on each other when the battle fever hits. Who wants to work with someone like that? I can pretty much name my price right now, especially since the Republic is so desperate for mercs all of a sudden.

speaker: Player
text: Why is the Republic hiring so many mercenaries?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: They ain't saying, but the price sure is right. Of course, I haven't heard of anyone coming back, so I'm guessing the job ain't easy.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: So why are you telling me? If you're going, go. I don't need a status report.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the young Selkath who have gone missing?

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: Not really. I have no interest in the Selkath other than the fact that they are charging me an exorbitant amount to stay on this world.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: The Iridorian over there, however... He, I believe, may know more. He has been seen with several of them before.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: So the Sith smoked a Jedi outpost on Dantooine. No survivors, or so they say. First Taris, now Dantooine. Wouldn't surprise me if the Republic starts hiring mercs to make a counter attack.
comment: first time after dantooine has been destroyed

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: They might even hire some Echani or Iridorian mercenaries, if they're desperate. I bet a Mandalorian could make some good money working for the Republic right now.

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: All of a sudden the Republic isn't hiring mercenaries anymore.
comment: first time after hrakert rift plot

speaker: Mandalorian Mercenary
text: And now the kolto harvest is at an all time low. More than just coincidence, if you ask me.

speaker: Firith Me
text: You with the Selkath? You here to see me about the murder too?

speaker: Firith Me
text: I told the damn fish everything I knew, what more do you all want from me?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about Sunry and Elassa?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Sunry I only heard of once or twice in passing. Some sort of old-time war hero against the Sith. Seen him around in the hotel too. Going to Elassa's room always of course.

speaker: Firith Me
text: Kept the rest of the building up half the night with their damn antics usually!

speaker: Player
text: You mean Sunry was having a relationship with Elassa?

speaker: Firith Me
text: I'm not saying anything like that. What they did in that room, in private, is their business.

speaker: Firith Me
text: And there isn't any rule against Sith and Republics seeing each other for personal reasons. Although if you think her Sith Master didn't know, heh, you must be fooling yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Sith Master?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Uh... well Elassa was a Sith... so of course she'd have to have someone above her... yeah. I didn't see anything!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] What did you see?

speaker: Firith Me
text: [Success] Well... one time... I saw Elassa coming in wearing this big cloak. I was on my way to my room, and she normally wears stuff like that so I didn't pay her too much attention.

speaker: Firith Me
text: But this time I accidentally brushed up against her - accidentally of course! - and her cloak fell open...

speaker: Firith Me
text: Now I don't have no qualms about the Sith! I leave them alone and they leave me alone. And seeing as how Elassa had a Sith lightsaber under her cloak, I'm not going to poke that hornet's nest.

speaker: Player
text: She was a Dark Jedi?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Seems so... But I'm not getting myself in any further with the Sith. I know how ruthless they are.

speaker: Firith Me
text: Now that's all I'm going to tell you. I'll testify it to the court, but you aren't going to get anything else out of me.

speaker: Player
text: A lightsaber does not mean anything.

speaker: Firith Me
text: I don't know what it means to you, but to me it kind of screams 'Dark Jedi'. And I'm not getting myself in any further with the Sith. I know how ruthless they are.

speaker: Player
text: I have a lightsaber too, you know.

speaker: Firith Me
text: I know, I know, but you're a Jedi. Elassa never claimed to be.

speaker: Firith Me
text: [Failure] I didn't see anything and there's no way you can make me say otherwise! Now quit asking!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Maybe if I tossed in 100 credits?

speaker: Firith Me
text: [Success] Since you put it that way...

speaker: Firith Me
text: [Failure] 100 credits isn't enough for the kind of trouble I'd be having if I told you. Sorry, you're gonna have to look somewhere else.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You know you want to tell me.

speaker: Firith Me
text: [Success] You know, I think I could trust you. Heck, I don't know why I shouldn't tell you.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, okay, I'll ask something else.

speaker: Firith Me
text: Thanks...

speaker: Player
text: What did you see the night of the murder?

speaker: Firith Me
text: I was in my room, minding my own business with the lastest copy of Pazaak Weekly - checking out the listings for the big tournament that's gonna be held here soon - when I heard a blaster shot.

speaker: Firith Me
text: Being still alive - and therefore smart enough not to stick my head out immediately - I didn't go out right away. I looked out after a minute and saw Gluupor in the hall by Elassa's room, and Sunry running like the wind.

speaker: Firith Me
text: You can't tell me that someone who was running like that - and he was pretty fast for a cripple! - isn't guilty.

speaker: Player
text: I have nothing more to ask for now.

speaker: Firith Me
text: Yes, well I'll be right here... Not like they're letting me go anywhere else...

speaker: Player
text: Elassa roomed here often?

speaker: Firith Me
text: Yes. She rented a room every week or so. Coincidentally it was right about the same time that Sunry would show up. They didn't seem all that discreet either.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing for now.

speaker: Firith Me
text: You again... didn't I tell you people everything I knew? So why do you keep coming back to me?

speaker: Player
text: Nothing more for now.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You Sith don't scare me. Down here the swoop gang's are in charge and you don't have enough troops on Taris to do anything about it!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Hey - I recognize you! You're the one who won the swoop race!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You were racing for those damn Vulkars! You'll pay for that!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You better be careful out here. Those damn Vulkars will be looking to get even with you for winning that race and killing Brejik.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: Brejik is nothing but a punk! I don't know why those Vulkars follow him - Gadon's ten times the man he is!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: The swoop race coming up will show those Vulkars who's in charge here! When we win half the people following Brejik will desert him!

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You need to get inside - the Black Vulkars are gunning down everyone they find on the streets! You should go to Javyar's cantina, you'll be safe there.

speaker: Hidden Bek
text: You should get off the streets - those Black Vulkars will take a shot at anybody!

speaker: Tariga
text: Greetings, fellow student. Have you heard the news? Master Uthar reports that his apprentice, Yuthara, is dead. How unsettling.

speaker: Tariga
text: You return to the academy in an odd time. Master Yuthara has just taken over leadership. No doubt there will be many other changes to come.

speaker: Tariga
text: Have you seen Master Uthar and Yuthara? There are many in the academy who seem to be searching for them.

speaker: Tariga
text: Greetings, fellow student. Are you planning on going to the Valley of the Dark Lords? I am headed there soon, myself.
comment: Tariga should only appear at the exit to the valley when the player has been given the second challenge when selected

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Tariga
text: I am known as Tariga, a student here at the academy. It is my pleasure to be assigned to the Sith ruins, to study their past and unearth new relics.

speaker: Player
text: You're human, but you speak like a Twi'lek...

speaker: Tariga
text: I was raised on a planet in the Outer Rim. We were not part of the Republic, so we never adopted their language. I can understand Basic, but I am not fluent in speaking it yet.

speaker: Tariga
text: I am, however, quite fluent in the Twi'lek tongue, so I prefer to use it when dealing with others. It is nearly as well known as Basic, and no one will make fun of my accent.

speaker: Tariga
text: I think I made the right choice. I doubt I would have been assigned to the Sith ruins in the Valley of the Dark Lords if I was stuttering and stumbling over an unfamiliar language.

speaker: Player
text: How do I get to this valley?

speaker: Tariga
text: The exit at the end of this hall will bring you to the surface. There you merely follow a natural path through the rock and you will come to the valley, itself.

speaker: Tariga
text: You will find many Sith working on the dig at the southern end of the valley. If you head into the northern end where the strange pillars are, do beware of the tuk'ata beasts.

speaker: Player
text: What are these tuk'ata?

speaker: Tariga
text: Local beasts that hunt in packs and are not at all afraid of attacking students... or even armed patrols. They have proven to be a hindrance to our progress.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Arrogant hunters always assume the animal knows how important they are.

speaker: Tariga
text: Several attempts have been made to destroy their nests in the tombs, but their numbers have proven to be too great.
comment: Gives the PC some tuk'ata bait

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the valley?

speaker: Tariga
text: There are four tombs that have been uncovered so far, each holding the remains of a Sith Lord from a time long ago when the Sith were first on Korriban.

speaker: Tariga
text: We have found evidence that there were larger structures underground, a veritable ancient fortress... but it appears to have been destroyed. The tombs are all that remain intanct.

speaker: Tariga
text: Currently we are allowed access only to three tombs... the one furthest to the left may only be entered by Master Uthar and those he brings with him.

speaker: Tariga
text: Fortunately there is still much else for us to find. I am pleased that you have joined us.

speaker: Player
text: Anything I should be watchful for?

speaker: Tariga
text: Yes, indeed. Shortly before entering the valley, you will pass by a cave entrance. Do not enter it... it is full of dangerous creatures we call shyrack.

speaker: Tariga
text: The only other danger to speak of is the tuk'ata. There are guards that will protect you if you remain in the south part of the valley, however.

speaker: Player
text: What are these shyrack?

speaker: Tariga
text: Flying creatures that lay webs in their tunnels. The webs can only be burned or moved by explosives I believe. Best to avoid them entirely.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Tariga
text: I wish you well, fellow student.
comment: once the player has passed the second test, she will leave permanently

speaker: Tariga
text: I wish you well in your explorations.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Greetings, Padawan. You must be the one Master Bolook has enlisted to help him with this problem.

speaker: Information Droid
text: I am an information retrieval droid. I can assist you by accessing the records of both the Jedi Enclave and the central government facilities here on Dantooine.

speaker: Information Droid
text: If you have any need of my services, please do not hesitate to talk to me.

speaker: Information Droid
text: I have already retrieved some information from the archives on Calder Nettic, Rickard Lusoff and Handon Guld. I have also had time to examine the body of Mr. Nettic.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Is there any information you require?

speaker: Player
text: What did you find out about the body?

speaker: Information Droid
text: My preliminary analysis of the body indicates that he was killed approximately 3 hours ago by a single energy blast to the torso.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Is there any other information you need?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the blood sample.

speaker: Information Droid
text: I have just received back an analysis of a sample of the blood found on the weapon. It had been sent back to the Enclave just before you arrived.

speaker: Information Droid
text: The blood on the weapon is definitely not Calder's. Unfortunately there was a bacterial contaminant in the sample that had been taken back to the laboratory, and it had become degraded.

speaker: Information Droid
text: We cannot get any more specific analysis from that sample other than the fact it did not belong to Calder.

speaker: Player
text: Is there a report of Handon's blaster being stolen?

speaker: Information Droid
text: I am sorry, but I seem to be failing you. I have searched and searched, but I cannot seem to come up with anything at all.

speaker: Information Droid
text: I thought to find the record of the missing weapon report Mr. Guld filed with the authorities, but there does not seem to be one.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the weapon found at the scene.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Calder and Handon?

speaker: Information Droid
text: The Southwood speeder rental business has records that, over the past several weeks, a speeder had been rented by Mr. Nettic and Mr. Guld.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Calder and Rickard?

speaker: Information Droid
text: According to the municipal authorities near the Garang spaceport, there had been news of violent drunken activity in a cantina attached to the port.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Apparently a Mr. R. Lusoff was making accusations at a Mr. C. Nettic about cheating him in a business deal. Jedi Tooka was dispatched to the scene and restored order.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about these plains.

speaker: Information Droid
text: These plains are rife with wild animals, not all of them benign. The iriaz are mostly docile, but can easily be provoked to violence. Kath hounds, on the other hand, are much more deadly...

speaker: Information Droid
text: There have been over 35 catalogued attacks on settlers by kath hounds in the last 2 weeks. A general advisory was given out three days ago to carry a weapon at all times when on the plains.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Small farms and holdings dot the plains, and can provide safe refuge for those in need.

speaker: Player
text: I will have more questions later.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Very well. I will be here to assist you.

speaker: Information Droid
text: Greetings, apprentice. You must be the one Master Bolook has enlisted to help him with this problem.

speaker: Ice
text: Congratulations, Stranger. I never thought anyone would beat Starkiller. Did you know it was because of him that I became a duelist in the first place?

speaker: Ice
text: As a little girl I used to dream of meeting him one day. When I finally did, the guy was a complete slime ball. Made me realize I had to be cold and ruthless to survive, like him.

speaker: Ice
text: And now he's dead. There's probably a lesson in there somewhere. Something for me to think about, at least. Congratulations again, Stranger... and goodbye.

speaker: Ice
text: I heard you're going to fight Bendak Starkiller, Stranger. I'm not one to mince words, so let me just say this: you're dead. He'll kill you, end of story.

speaker: Ice
text: You think I'm cold and hard, wait until you step into the ring with him. He's a natural born killer. You had great potential, Stranger. Too bad you're going to throw it all away.

speaker: Ice
text: I've never been one to shy away from the cold, hard truth so I'll just come right out and say it: I can't compete with the likes of you, Stranger. I know when I'm overmatched.

speaker: Ice
text: You're good - very good. But you're wrong if you think that means I'm suddenly going to warm up to you. Truth is, I really don't have anything more to say, so you might as well move on.

speaker: Ice
text: What do you want? Wait, let me guess - now that you're a duelist you figure we have something in common? Something to chat about, right?

speaker: Ice
text: Wrong! Just because we're both duelists doesn't mean we're suddenly friends. So give me some space, Stranger. I've got nothing more to say to you.

speaker: Ice
text: Back again? Didn't you get the message last time - I'm not here to make friends. Talk to the Duel Organizer if you want a match, otherwise leave me alone.

speaker: Ice
text: Wait, I know what you're going to say: I'm so beautiful, I'm so attractive, how can someone who looks so hot with a weapon in her hand be called Ice? Well, I've heard it all before.

speaker: Ice
text: I'm here to take care of business in the dueling ring, not to have some slack-jawed, goggle-eyed man slobber all over me. So back off!

speaker: Player
text: Wow - that was cold!

speaker: Ice
text: Now you know why they call me Ice. If you're looking for a match, go talk to the Ajuur. He's that big Hutt over there in the corner. Otherwise, just go away.

speaker: Player
text: Dueling ring? What are you talking about?

speaker: Ice
text: You don't know about the dueling ring? This is unbelievable! Then why are you even here? Wait - never mind. I don't really care.

speaker: Ice
text: You know what? I'm not one for friendly chit-chat, so I'm just going to deliver the cold, hard facts: I don't want to waste anymore time with you.

speaker: Player
text: I just want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Ice
text: Wait, I know what you're going to say: it's great to see a woman in the duel ring, strike a blow for equality, I'm a credit to my gender, blah, blah, blah. Just save it, okay?

speaker: Ice
text: I'm just here to take care of business in the dueling ring. For some reason every woman who comes in here thinks we should have some kind of female bond. Guess what? We don't!

speaker: Elise
text: Oh, thank you! Thank you!

speaker: Elise
text: I don't know what I would have done if I had lost him!

speaker: Player
text: It's...

speaker: Elise
text: It's just soo great to have him back!

speaker: Elise
text: We're just going to go right home, right now, and celebrate, aren't we, my lovely little droid?

speaker: Elise
text: Don't worry, I'm going to hug you and oil you and care for you and make sure you never ever get away again.

speaker: C8-42
text: Please kill me...

speaker: Carth
text: I don't think I've ever felt so bad for a droid before.

speaker: T3M4
text: [sadly] Beep boop-oop.

speaker: Player
text: I agree. Completely.

speaker: Cand
text: Ha! Better get used to it, droid!

speaker: Player
text: No...

speaker: Elise
text: Greetings, young Jedi, I wonder if you could assist me. I seem to have lost my... companion, you see.

speaker: Player
text: Your companion?

speaker: Elise
text: We were working on my farm to the north of here. I was working in the garden outside, and he was working inside.

speaker: Elise
text: I heard the door to the house open, but not close. I went to see and found it wide open!

speaker: Elise
text: I searched everywhere, and could not find him! I worry so much. I need him back so badly. I wonder if he... Could he have been kidnapped?

speaker: Player
text: It is possible...

speaker: Elise
text: Maybe it was the Mandalorians... or maybe kath hounds. But... no...

speaker: Elise
text: Kath hounds are not intelligent enough to open doors. Although they have been more vicious lately...

speaker: Elise
text: No, it must have been someone who could open the door by himself. Come to think of it, the door was locked!

speaker: Player
text: Did someone break it down?

speaker: Elise
text: No, the door was undamaged and showed no signs of tampering...

speaker: Player
text: Could it have been opened from the inside?

speaker: Elise
text: Well... Yes, it could have. But he had no reason to run away! His programming...

speaker: Player
text: Your missing companion is a droid??
