speaker: Elise
text: Well... yes... he is a droid.

speaker: Elise
text: But he is very valuable to me all the same! He is the last piece of my poor, passed-away husband that I have left.

speaker: Elise
text: He is very dear to me, my precious is. I don't know what I'd do without him!

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep-beep boople boop!

speaker: Player
text: Yes, Teethree, I understand that you're concerned about him, too...

speaker: Elise
text: He's the only companionship I have on all of Dantooine!

speaker: Player
text: You live alone with this... droid?

speaker: Elise
text: He is a personal assistance droid. My husband was a genius at constructing droids. He made this one capable of taking care of me for the rest of my life.

speaker: Elise
text: As the last legacy of my husband, for my own personal ease of mind, I need him back! His absence gnaws at me like a gaping wound.

speaker: Carth
text: Wow. She really misses her droid, doesn't she?

speaker: Bastila
text: There is no need for you to make fun of her. She is obviously desperate.

speaker: Carth
text: I'll say.

speaker: Bastila
text: Carth! Enough!

speaker: Elise
text: Please, I beg of you, return my droid to me!

speaker: Player
text: I will help you find your droid.

speaker: Elise
text: Thank you! Thank you, master Jedi! If you find him, please send him home to me. I need him so much!

speaker: Player
text: If I happen to see him, I will send him back to you.

speaker: Player
text: I am not interested.

speaker: Elise
text: Please! Should you find him, send him home to me!

speaker: Player
text: What exactly did you use him for again?

speaker: Player
text: A droid?!?
comment: if the player has not heard the history before

speaker: Player
text: You expect me to run off to find some stupid droid??
comment: if the player has not heard the history before

speaker: Elise
text: He was supposed to be completely loyal! To serve me after my husband died!

speaker: Elise
text: Please, if you come across my droid, bring him to me. I need him so much...

speaker: Player
text: Could someone have bypassed the lock?

speaker: Player
text: Could it have been kath hounds?

speaker: Player
text: Does anyone hold a grudge against him?

speaker: Elise
text: Not that I know of... Er... *ahem* None of my neighbors really know he's there.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Elise
text: Oh, I'm sorry, master Jedi, I did not give you a proper introduction. I am Elise Montagne. I own the farm to the north of here.

speaker: Elise
text: But I really am in need of your assistance. Time may be critical with so many kath hounds about. Oh, and those Mandalorians! Please, will you help me find him?

speaker: Player
text: Alright, I will help you. Tell what happened.

speaker: Player
text: I am sorry, I have no time for this.

speaker: Elise
text: Please, I beg of you, I must find him. How can you leave him out there with so many dangerous beasts and predators? Have you no humanity?

speaker: Player
text: No means no.

speaker: Elise
text: Please, if you do see him, return him to me. He is so far from home... He is a C8 model droid about a meter and a half tall...

speaker: Elise
text: My droid is still missing. I can feel him like a hole in my aching heart.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I found your droid... but he had been destroyed by kath hounds.

speaker: Elise
text: [Success] My droid... destroyed? No, no! This cannot be happening! I can't bear to live without him!

speaker: Player
text: I am afraid your droid had to be destroyed.

speaker: Elise
text: My droid... destroyed? No, no! This cannot be happening! I cannot bear to live without him!

speaker: Player
text: Your droid escaped and is nowhere to be found. He's still out there somewhere.

speaker: Elise
text: He is out there still? I must find him!

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, why'd you have to do that? That was just mean!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Your actions disturb me. Among my kind, those who take pleasure in the suffering of others are considered dangerously unstable.

speaker: Juhani
text: The dark side dwells in us all, but you cannot give in to your baser instincts like this!

speaker: Jolee
text: Nice. Real nice. Maybe later we could find some insects to pull the legs off, huh?

speaker: Bastila
text: It troubles me to see you behaving this way. Such acts can lead to the dark side.

speaker: Carth
text: Why did you do that? Sometimes... sometimes I just can't understand how you can be so cruel.

speaker: Player
text: Could you tell me what happened to him?

speaker: Player
text: Do not worry, I will find him.

speaker: Player
text: I am sorry, I must be going.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Want to take an unofficial run around the track? You've beat everyone, I know, but it's good to keep your skills sharp. 20 credits.

speaker: Player
text: I'll pay for a recreational run.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Very good. We'll have your bike put in position for the next time trial. Get ready, it won't take long.

speaker: Player
text: Why is there a fee?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Well, Motta pays for timing on official runs, but rec-runs are staffed by volunteers. They deserve a little something.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Besides, paying for runs keeps usage down. That way we don't crowd the pros off the track.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to try an officially timed race.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: You'll have to go through Motta for that. He keeps track of all official standings at this track.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: There's money in it too. He pays riders for good times to encourage competition.

speaker: Player
text: No thanks. Goodbye.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: All right. Anyone else want to step up?

speaker: Player
text: Can I hear what the track records are?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: We keep tabs on all active racers. Currently we have information on you, Garm Totryl, Yuka Rill, and Zoriis Bafka. Nico has withdrawn for the time being.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have on me?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Nothing yet. You'll have to put in some track time before we can record your results.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have on Zoriis?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: She is the current track leader with a time of <CUSTOM29>.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have on Yuka Rill?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: His best time was <CUSTOM28>, which you have beaten.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have on Garm?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: You have made short work of his best time of <CUSTOM27>.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my other questions.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Just don't keep me too long. Other racers might want to have a run down the track. Do you want a race?

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: His current best time is <CUSTOM27>.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Yuka Rill's best time is currently <CUSTOM28>.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Her best time is <CUSTOM29>, which you have beaten.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Your best time is <CUSTOM25>. Your first time was <CUSTOM24> and the last time we have for you is <CUSTOM26>.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: You are the current track leader. Your best time was <CUSTOM25>. Your first time was <CUSTOM24> and the last time we have for you is <CUSTOM26>.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Well, another swoop-jock come to give the track a try? It's just a 20 credit timing fee for recreational runs.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Sorry, the track is only for racers that Motta has accepted and signed up. He pays for track upkeep, so it's his choice.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Go talk to him and we'll see about setting you up.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: Well raced. You would do well in our local tournament. Did you want to have another go? The fee is 20 credits, as you know.
comment: Initiated after player races recreational run, player has not defeated everyone yet.

speaker: Track Coordinator
text: A good result. I can see how you beat everyone in the official races. Did you want to have another go? The fee is 20 credits, as you know.
comment: Initiated after player races recreational run, player has defeated everyone already.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: I heard you challenged Bendak Starkiller. I'll probably watch the fight... but forgive me if I don't go to your funeral.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: This is great! You beat Bendak - you're a legend! Whenever anyone asks I can say I was the first duelist the Mysterious Stranger ever beat in the ring! I'm going to be famous!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Wow - you're the new champ. Congratulations, I guess. You know, when you started out I actually thought I'd be able to crawl up from my last place ranking for a while.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Shows what I know. Enjoy your time at the top, Stranger. Sooner or later someone will come along to knock you down here with the rest of us grinders!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: You beat Ice! I've been trying to beat her for years, and you do it just like that! Heh. I can't believe how lucky you are!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: That's right - I said lucky! Lucky to be born with the kind of talent I've spent a life time trying to build. It isn't fair, I tell you!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: What do you want? Oh, let me guess - you beat me in the dueling ring and now you're here to rub it in my face! Yeah well, I'm used to it. So pardon me if I ignore your gloating.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Questions? I don't have to answer your questions just because you beat me in the ring!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Look, I admit it - you're better than me. Everyone is better than me! A blindfolded, one-legged tach with a rusty knife could probably beat me, okay?

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Is that what you wanted to hear? You satisfied yet? Are you happy now that you've taken the last shred of dignity I have?

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I'm happy now.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Slime-rat.

speaker: Player
text: Uh... I'll just be going now.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Oh. Well... okay. Goodbye, then.

speaker: Player
text: Wow - you sure have a bad attitude.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Gee, I wonder why? Couldn't have anything to do with being the WORST duelist on Taris, could it? Even a rookie like you got the better of me!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Back for more, eh? I thought you would have learned your lesson by now: don't step into the dueling ring with Deadeye Duncan!

speaker: Player
text: I want a rematch!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: I may have lost 54 consecutive matches before I beat you, but I figure I've got your number! You want to step into the ring again, just tell the duel organizer to set it up!

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Yeah yeah, off you go. Run away like the coward you are!

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: What are you looking at, fresh meat? You want a piece of me? You want to step into the dueling chambers with me?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: I'm Deadeye Duncan, the number five ranked duelist in this cantina. You must have seen me in the dueling chambers, right?

speaker: Player
text: Dueling chambers?

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: You know - the dueling chambers: two people in combat, loser gets carried out unconscious on a stretcher. It's the only reason people come into this part of the cantina.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Look, I'm the number five ranked duelist around here; I don't have time to explain all this. Go talk to the Duel Organizer if you're interested. He's that Hutt over there in the corner.

speaker: Player
text: You're the number five ranked duelist? Out of how many?

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Uh... five. But it's an elite group, okay? It's not like just anyone can step into the dueling chamber! Well, actually anyone can... but not many do!

speaker: Player
text: You don't look so tough. I think I could beat you in a duel.

speaker: Deadeye Duncan
text: Big talk. Go speak with the Hutt in the corner to back it up - he's the Duel Organizer. I'll look forward to our match. Fresh meat is just what I need to end my losing streak!

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Yeah, what do you...? Oh, I apologize Master Jedi, I should not have been rude.

speaker: Player
text: It is alright.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: No really, I should apologize. I should try to control myself... as you Jedi do.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Is there anything I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: Why do the Sith upset you so much?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: These damn Sith are everywhere on Manaan, pushing us Republic citizens around, trying to goad us into breaking the law somewhere.

speaker: Player
text: Breaking the law?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: The Selkath want to maintain their neutrality in this war we're fighting with the Sith and they enforce it VERY strictly.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: So we have to sit here and let the Sith insult us and we can't raise a hand against them otherwise the Republic will face severe kolto export restrictions. That could lose us the war altogether.

speaker: Player
text: What is kolto?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: You're joking... right?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Sorry, but everyone knows what kolto is. The most powerful healing agent in the galaxy. I would've died several times myself if we didn't have this stuff handy.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: But the reason it's important here is that kolto is only found naturally on Manaan, and all of our attempts to synthesize it have failed miserably.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: So we sit here on the surface, the Selkath harvesting what kolto bubbles up from the bottom of the ocean, and we buy it from them.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Us and the Sith of course. The Selkath don't want to play favorites.

speaker: Player
text: The Republic and Sith both stay here?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: The Selkath think that by staying neutral they can play both sides, selling kolto to everyone that needs it, and making themselves too valuable to be worth conquering.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Well, that, and they threatened to destroy the only natural source of kolto on the planet if anyone tries to attack them.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: But I think they're underestimating the lengths the Sith will go to get what they want... They're probably planning something already.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Is there anything else you require?

speaker: Player
text: Have you seen an ancient Star Map?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: A Star Map? Like an ancient artifact or something?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: No, sorry, never heard of it.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Is there anything else I can do for you?

speaker: Player
text: Why are there Sith on Manaan?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Well, for the kolto, of course. Really that's the only reason anyone would want to be here. It's the only reason the Selkath built Ahto City in the first place: to export kolto.

speaker: Player
text: Why haven't they joined the Republic?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Ahto City.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Um... It's big. Real big. Actually it's pretty much the only real city on the entire world. The only place for us air-breathers anyway.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Manaan is a water world - which you may have noticed on your way down to land here - inhabited natively by a species of fish-people called the Selkath.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: They built this city to cater to us off-worlders and as a base of operations to export kolto, which is the only real thing they have to trade here.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind, I must go.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Of course. If you have any other questions you should probably see Roland Wann, he's the Republic diplomat here. He's by the Republic enclave near the visitor residences.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: If you don't know where that is, go north from here, then south past the port official and the first courtyard, east into the second courtyard, then north then east again. You got that?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Have a pleasant stay, Master Jedi.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you run them off Manaan?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: There's nothing we can do, though. The Selkath want to maintain their neutrality and they enforce it VERY strictly.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith and the Republic coexisting peacefully? Well... relatively...

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Peacefully? Not hardly. Just look in their eyes. You can see they'd like nothing more than to kill each and every one of us, personal-like.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I know the feeling...

speaker: Player
text: They mean well, but are misguided.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: You're... you're joking, right? The smug Hutt-spawn push us every chance they can get and enjoy it.

speaker: Player
text: It is the work of the dark side.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: If you say so, Master Jedi. It's very aggravating. Sometimes I just want to take one of them and... *grrr*

speaker: Player
text: I would like to ask a few questions.

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: Of course, I'm always willing to help a Jedi. What do you require?

speaker: Player
text: Who are the Selkath?

speaker: Republic Soldier
text: If you have any other questions you should probably see Roland Wann, he's the Republic diplomat here. He's by the Republic enclave near the visitor residences. Have a pleasant stay, Master Jedi.

speaker: Dia
text: Another Sith patrol? I'm telling you, you're wasting your time here.

speaker: Dia
text: Go ahead and search my apartment again, if you want. You'll find the same thing as last time... nothing.

speaker: Dia
text: Who are you? What are you doing in here? You can't just come barging into someone's home!

speaker: Player
text: I spoke to Holdan, Dia. He'll remove the bounty on your head if you pay him off.

speaker: Dia
text: I have nothing... I barely make enough credits to get by. I can't afford to pay that pig off!

speaker: Dia
text: I guess I have no choice but to stay here and hope Holdan cools down. With that bounty on my head it's too dangerous to go outside.

speaker: Player
text: I spoke with Holdan. I convinced him to remove the bounty on your head.

speaker: Dia
text: He... he called the bounty off? That's wonderful! I only wish I had something to give you as a reward.

speaker: Dia
text: Wait a minute... I know! I don't have many credits, but there is something I can give you. It's a family heirloom. It's not much, but it's something.

speaker: Player
text: Keep your reward, Dia. Helping you was thanks enough.

speaker: Dia
text: I can never truly repay you for helping me, but you'll always have my thanks for what you did.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you, Dia. This reward will be fine.

speaker: Player
text: I save your life and all I get is some family trinket?

speaker: Dia
text: If I had more I'd gladly give it to you, but this is all I've got. I'm sorry.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to collect the bounty on your head, Dia!

speaker: Dia
text: Wait! Think about what you're doing. If that pig had just kept his hands to himself, I wouldn't have had to give him that scar with my vibroblade.

speaker: Dia
text: He gets drunk and tries to force himself on me, and I get a bounty put on my head for defending myself? Where's the justice in that? Holdan's the one to blame, not me.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything I can do to help?

speaker: Dia
text: I doubt it. Holdan is one of Davik's men. When you work for the local crime lord the authorities tend to turn a blind eye. I'm afraid this is between me and Holdan now.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I could speak to Holdan for you.

speaker: Dia
text: You could try, I guess. He usually hangs out at the cantina in the Lower City. It probably won't do any good. Holdan's used to getting his own way.

speaker: Dia
text: That's one of the fringe benefits of being a goon for Davik. Working for the local crime lord lets you get away with things. Still, I appreciate the offer.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Dia
text: I can't help you there. Since this thing with Holdan I've been scared to leave my apartment. I don't know anything about what's going on in the outside world anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Holdan? Who's that?

speaker: Dia
text: Just one of Davik's men who can't keep his hands to himself. But all he got for his trouble was a nasty scar from my vibroblade! Too bad I'm the one still paying the price.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Dia
text: I... I don't want to talk about it. I'm in enough trouble already. Besides, I don't know if I can trust you.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] You can trust me. Maybe I can help.

speaker: Dia
text: [Success] Well, I suppose you seem like an alright sort. When I cut Holdan it made him back off, but it also embarrassed him in front of his friends.

speaker: Dia
text: Holdan's a spiteful little Hutt-slug. He went and put out a bounty on my head for what I did! That's why I'm hiding out here.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll just collect that bounty on your head!

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Dia
text: Goodbye. Thank you again for all your help. I don't know what I would have done without you.

speaker: Dia
text: Goodbye, and good luck. I hope you can talk some sense into Holdan.

speaker: Dia
text: Good. I don't much like strangers in my home.

speaker: Dia
text: [Failure] No, I don't think so. I can't afford to trust anybody right now. Please, just leave me alone.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me what's going on or I'll end all your problems... permanently!

speaker: Dia
text: Okay, I'll tell you... just try and stay calm. The last thing I need is trouble with you and Holdan.

speaker: Player
text: I don't care about justice. I just want the credits!

speaker: Carth
text: What's wrong with you? She doesn't deserve this!

speaker: Player
text: She sliced that guy up. She's only getting what she deserves!

speaker: Dia022
text: Then you're going to learn the same lesson I taught Holdan: I'm not as helpless as I look!

speaker: Player
text: Fine, this is between you and Holdan. I don't want to get involved.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I guess Carth's right. Maybe we could help you out.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not getting involved in this. What you do now is your concern, not mine.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry. I was just investigating the area.

speaker: Dia
text: That's no excuse. You can't just go around barging into people's apartments because you're curious! But at least you're more polite than that pig, Holdan.

speaker: Player
text: I'm just looking for something to steal. Stay out of my way and you won't get hurt.

speaker: Dia
text: You're as bad as that pig Holdan! I'll stay out of your way, but you're wasting your time. I don't have anything worth stealing.

speaker: Dia
text: You're back. Did you... did you manage to get Holdan to withdraw the price on my head?

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I've decided to collect that bounty myself!

speaker: Player
text: No, not yet.

speaker: Dia
text: You again? Why do you keep bothering me?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I welcome you back. Czerka Corporation would like to extend its thanks to you for representing its interests so thoroughly.
comment: Initial initiation following return to 22aa after Chuundar wins

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Chuundar is very interested in furthering our exchange of labor for weapons. We've begun expanding our operations, as I'm sure you've seen.

speaker: Player
text: I think Zaalbar will have something to say about this.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: The time for objections is long since passed, if there ever was one. You brought about this change. You have no one to blame.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have no objections. Chuundar showed me the way things must be. There is nothing for me here. The old ways are dead.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Er, the tone of your Wookiee's muttering seems agreable. He likely agrees that this was the gentlest outcome possible.

speaker: Player
text: What are your plans for Kashyyyk?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka Corporation will begin an extensive examination of the commercial potential of this world. The Wookiees will aid us in this.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I'm certain there are ample resources for us to export. I doubt we will encounter much more resistance. We will be here for quite some time.

speaker: Player
text: I need supplies. What do you have available?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka Corporation maintains a well-stocked armory, although for general goods you will need to speak with the vendor in the docking area.

speaker: Player
text: Can I expect a reward for what I have done?
comment: This should only be able to be selected once.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I would think that the thanks of Czerka Corporation would be enough, especially after your previous actions. You have caused us significant difficulty.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I have reports about you meddling with our operations in the Shadowlands. I think we will consider this agrement with Chuundar to be fair compensation. Yes, that is what we will do.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps I could persuade you otherwise?

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Perhaps that is exactly why I have instructed the guards to watch your every action, and how I react to you. I have taken precautions reagrding your... capabilities.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: No, I don't believe we will be extending any financial compensation to you today. Thank you for your assistance.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: I have no information about that. You appear to have explored deeper than any of our current expeditions. I certainly can't expand on what you've seen.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Very well. Thank you again for your assistance.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Czerka will be operating here for quite some time. All things considered, this was the gentlest outcome possible.

speaker: Player
text: I don't approve of this.

speaker: Player
text: It's not my concern.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: It was the gentlest outcome possible. I am sure that everyone will come to see this in time.

speaker: Player
text: It was the only outcome possible.

speaker: Janos Wertka
text: Thank you again for your assistance. Is there anything further you need?
comment: Secondary selection after returning to 22aa aftere Chuundar wins

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hey - this street is for Sith only. You got to pay a 20 credit toll to walk down this street.
comment: scripted ancounter,  when player enters alley, if he hasnt stood up to the bully

speaker: Player
text: Fine, here's your 20 credits.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Thanks for the credits, nerf-herder!

speaker: Player
text: This is a public street!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hiding behind the Selkath laws - typical Republic cowardice!

speaker: Player
text: You can have your credits when you take them from my cold, dead hand.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You talk big - but remember what we did to Taris. Maybe you're next on our list.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hey, you working for the Republic? You look like a Republic agent - I can see the cowardice in your eyes.

speaker: Player
text: Your taunts are nothing to me. There is no emotion, there is peace.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You think you can impress me by spouting a bunch of Jedi garbage? If it wasn't for the Selkath neutrality laws, I'd add your name to the list of Jedi I've killed.

speaker: Player
text: You better change your attitude, or the Selkath might find your body floating in the ocean!

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Are you threatening me? It's illegal to try to start a fight in Ahto City! Constable - over here! This Republic scum is trying to break the peace!

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Is this true human? Are you threatening this woman with violence?

speaker: Player
text: She started it! She's insulting me.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Insults are one thing, human. Threats of physical violence are quite another. They are expressly forbidden by the laws of Ahto City.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm sorry, constable. It won't happen again.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: [Success] Very well, I shall overlook this infraction. But you would be wise to watch your words in the future, human.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: The Selkath claim neutrality, but you're always giving preferential treatment to the Republic! I'm going to report this incident to the Sith Embassy!

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: [Failure] Apologies are not sufficient. The law must be upheld.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] This argument was the fault of the Sith. She should be arrested.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: [Success] Yes - you are correct, human. The Sith is the one at fault.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Me? I didn't do anything! This is an outrage! A travesty of justice!

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Come with me to the Ahto City prisons. We will alert your Embassy and you shall be released when they pay the fine.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Though I've known the Sith to let their people languish in the prison for many months before securing their release.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I'll get you for this, Jedi! The Sith won't stand for this!
comment: selkath takes sith from the area  other sith leave

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: [Failure] A strange interpretation of these events, human. One I do not share. Clearly you are the one at fault here.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Human, you are fined 100 credits for disturbing the Manaan peace. If you do not pay, you will be taken to the Manaan prisons.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have that much.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Then you shall be imprisoned until you can pay the fine.
comment: cut scene showing the player stunned and waking in jail

speaker: Player
text: Here are your credits.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Further disturbances will be dealt with in a similar manner.

speaker: Player
text: Your laws are nothing to me!

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: Perhaps a 500 credit fine and a stint in the Ahto City jails will teach you to respect our laws.
comment: cut scene player is stunned and fades to black.  Wakes up in the jail.

speaker: Player
text: What are you going to do?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith and I are exchanging meaningless taunts.

speaker: Selkath Guard
text: I am not deaf, human. I heard your words, and threatening physical violence is not permitted in Ahto City.

speaker: Player
text: ... And? You want a piece of me, too?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Out of my way - unless you want to feel the wrath of the Sith!

speaker: Player
text: Your words are all sound and fury, signifying nothing.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You dare mock me? If it wasn't for the Selkath laws I'd teach you proper respect!

speaker: Player
text: I've seen the wrath of the Sith. I wasn't impressed.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: The wrath of the Sith is a terrible thing! Remember Taris! You'll see - you'll all see!

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I should just split you open from head to toe! How's that for wrath?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: You're back. The Council said you might return to Dantooine... I'm glad you did. I wanted to thank you.

speaker: Player
text: Do I know you?

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Maybe you don't remember me? I'm Kel... Kel Algwinn. We, uh, met in the academy on Korriban.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: You told me I should leave the Sith and seek out the Jedi. Well, I did. Everyone's been very nice... much nicer than I thought they would be.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I almost didn't think the Jedi Council would give me a chance, but they said everyone was welcome to return to the light side.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I guess I never *really* believed in the dark side. This just feels so right. I can't remember the last time I felt at peace like this.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: They said I have a long road ahead of me, but they made me a proper Padawan and I have a Master, now. I... I just can't thank you enough.

speaker: Player
text: You were too weak to be a Sith anyway.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I... guess, if that's how you want to look at it. The Sith don't support each other like the Jedi do... and I don't think that's a weakness at all.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Well, at any rate, I wish you well. May... may the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: The decision was yours, Kel.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I guess so. You pointed me in the right direction, though, and I have to be grateful for that. The Sith certainly didn't have my best interest at heart.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad I could help.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: I'm glad you were there. I don't think I ever would have made it through the academy alive. And now I might actually become a Jedi someday.

speaker: Player
text: Thank me for what?

speaker: Player
text: You're certainly welcome.

speaker: Kel Algwinn
text: Thank you again. I hope your mission for the Council goes well.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Your destiny does not lie with the Sith... at least, not yet. The academy is mine, now... I trust you won't be remaining long, correct?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Ah, there you are... my favorite prospect for the year.
comment: Yuthura will approach the PC when he passes her quarters

speaker: Player
text: Your favorite prospect?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Absolutely. By my estimation, you are far more likely to achieve the prestige necessary to join the Sith than any of the others.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As a matter of fact, I am so certain of that that I'm willing to offer you an opportunity of the once-in-a-lifetime variety. Would you like to hear it?

speaker: Player
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Good. I do so adore someone who's willing to take a chance.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As I said, you're no doubt going to be the one whom Uthar chooses to become a Sith. With my help, of course.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Once that occurs, he will take you into the Valley of the Dark Lords to the tomb of Naga Sadow to administer the final test.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: There you and I will be alone with him. The perfect time to, shall we say, arrange for a change in the academy's leadership?

speaker: Player
text: What's so important about this tomb?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The tomb is an ancient ruin on the surface that was visited years ago by Darth Revan and Darth Malak. They discovered a Star Map there of great importance.

speaker: Bastila
text: That --

speaker: Player
text: Quiet!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Reaching that map, as they did, is part of the final test. At any rate, it is not the tomb that is important. That Uthar will be alone is what is important.

speaker: Player
text: You want me to kill Master Uthar?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Is that such a daunting prospect? It is not as if I am asking you to perform the task alone, or as if you will get nothing out of it.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Master Uthar cannot prevail against us both. That's all there is to it. It is a very simple matter.

speaker: Player
text: Pupil against master. Sounds familiar.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: And so it should. It is central to our beliefs. It is my responsibility to replace my master when I am strong enough.

speaker: Player
text: What's to stop me from telling him about this?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I suppose you could do that. Even the hint of betrayal from his pupil and Uthar would move to eliminate me.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: But this is a very good opportunity for you... you can start off your Sith career as the right hand of the head of the academy: me. Uthar will not offer you that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Do you believe Uthar would not be aware of this? He would quickly figure out what you have to gain by betraying him... and would never believe someone would pass that up.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Tell Master Uthar what you wish. Were I you, I would think first of what the consequences of such an action might be.

speaker: Player
text: And what's your part in this?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: My 'part' in this is to help you gain enough prestige... and slow down the progress of the other hopefuls. I want you in that tomb when the time is right.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: We destroy Master Uthar together and I take his place... and you take your place at my side. A beautiful plan in its sheer simplicity.

speaker: Player
text: How do I know this isn't some test?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: *chuckle* You must not know much about the Sith, yet. If Uthar were to even suspect that I might be trying to supplant him, true or not...

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Well, let's just say that he wouldn't likely stop to ask too many questions before ensuring I was dealt with.

speaker: Player
text: Very well. I agree.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I'm so glad you see it my way.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I will begin to make preparations for your final test. Your only worry now is to get there... don't disappoint me.

speaker: Player
text: How do I get more prestige?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You must impress Master Uthar... go to him with news of your deeds or artifacts you have discovered.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The first and easiest way would be for you to learn the Code of the Sith and speak it to him. I can teach you that, if you like.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Shall I go on?

speaker: Player
text: Can you tell me about the Code of the Sith?
comment: if the Code is not known

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I can help you to understand it. Would you like to hear it?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: "Peace is a lie, there is only passion. Through passion, I gain strength. Through strength, I gain power.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Through power, I gain victory. Through victory, my chains are broken. The Force shall free me."

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Simple words, yet easily misunderstood. Would you care for me to explain anything?

speaker: Player
text: 'Peace is a lie, there is only passion'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The Jedi would have you believe that peace is a desirable goal. That peace of the spirit is the way the Force is mastered, that a lack of conflict betters man.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: We know different. It is our passion... our hate and our desire... that fuels the Force. It is conflict that improves the lot of civilization and single being both.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Conflict forces one to better oneself. It forces change, growth, adaption... evolution... or death. These are not our laws, but the universe's. Without conflict you have only stagnation.

speaker: Player
text: 'Through passion, I gain strength'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What fuels your power with the Force but your passion? The stronger, darker emotions. Anger, hatred, fear... these passions empower us.

speaker: Player
text: What about love?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Love is more dangerous than all those things. Love leads to anger and hatred more often that not... but it also leads to mercy, which is far worse. That, however, is a lesson for another time.

speaker: Player
text: Those seem like awfully negative passions.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Negative? Compared to what? What keeps even the most rudimentary creature alive? Fear to run, anger to fight... without it a creature would most surely die.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying we aren't anything more than a rudimentary creature?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: We are far more than them, perhaps, but in some ways we are little different. To think us creatures beyond the need of simple passions is a delusion.

speaker: Player
text: The Jedi say the opposite. How can both be right?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The Force gives us all power, even the Jedi. It is our mastery of our passion that gives us the strength they lack.

speaker: Player
text: I see.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: It is our goal to be stronger, to achieve our potential and not rest upon our laurels. We are the seekers, not the shepherds.

speaker: Player
text: 'Through strength, I gain power'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The stronger you become in the Force, the more power you will achieve. But always must you fight for your power.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Without strife, your victory has no meaning. Without strife, you do not advance. Without strife, there is only stagnation.

speaker: Player
text: 'Through power, I gain victory'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: How many sorts of victories can you imagine? Peaceful victory? Victory by sacrifice? A truce, an achievement?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Unless the victory is achieved by demonstrating that your power is superior, it is only an illusion. Temporary at best. We seek more.

speaker: Player
text: 'Through victory, my chains are broken'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: This... has been argued over, and often. The chains represent our restrictions, both those placed upon us and those we place upon ourselves.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Ultimately the goal of any Sith is to free herself from such restrictions. In a way, it is so we may do whatever we wish... but it is much more than that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: One who has freed themselves from all restrictions has reached perfection. Their potential fulfilled. Perfect strength, perfect power, perfect destiny. Imagine it.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: That is our ideal, at any rate. It is said in Sith legend that the 'Sith'ari'... the perfect being... will one day lead us. But perhaps that is just a legend.

speaker: Player
text: You don't think the Sith'ari can exist?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... wonder what a being would be like. The legends say the Sith'ari will destroy us... and make us stronger than ever.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: But perhaps that is just a legend. Perfection is... a goal, I think, rather than a state of being. The Jedi would argue that, no doubt.

speaker: Player
text: 'The Force shall free me'?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The Force is our servant and our master. Our teacher and our companion. A weapon and a tool.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Know it and you know the universe. Master it and you master the universe. Strive for perfection and the Force shall reward you.

speaker: Player
text: I think I got it.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I am not surprised. The Force is strong with you... master it and it shall serve you well.

speaker: Player
text: I have some news about Uthar...
comment: the player has already gone to Uthar

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What? What's happened? Our plan is still intact, I hope.

speaker: Player
text: He plans to have me fight you in the final test.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Ahhh. How very clever of him. Normally you would face some other student in the tomb, preferably one of the failed ones.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Obviously Uthar has decided to get rid of me. But why...? Did you say something to him?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, I did.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What?! You fool! While I respect your attempt to play both sides of the fence, you are playing a dangerous game.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: If you think Uthar will truly be so grateful to you for double-crossing me, think again. Your only chance lies with me.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: In the end, it works out better that it is only the two of us in the tomb with him. So long as we refuse to fight. Is there anything else I should know?

speaker: Player
text: He wants you poisoned. I'm supposed to give this pad to Andrenas.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Let me see that. Hmm... so it's true. Thank you for bringing this to me... now I will be far stronger than Uthar expects.
comment: Yuthura takes the pad, destroys it.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Here... this passcard will allow you access to Uthar's quarters. It's at the far end of the passages with the other quarters.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Take this device as well and put it inside his cot. No-one should see you do it. Then Uthar will be too weak to stand up against us.
comment: Yuthura gives the passcard and the device to the PC set the betrayal global to 3

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Don't even think of failing me. You and I are too far into this now to back out.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] He wants you poisoned. I don't know how, though.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Hah! He's a fool. I can make preparations to resist any poisons. Thank you for telling me... now I will be far stronger than Uthar expects.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] No. I don't know anything else.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Good. I'm not about to rest on my laurels, however.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] No, that's it.
comment: Yuthura has not already been poisoned

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] No, of course not.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Success] Then how could he suspect? Unless one of the others... never mind. It is not important, now.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Failure] Hmph. I truly doubt that. You are attempting to play both sides of the fence, I think. I respect that. You are playing a dangerous game, however.

speaker: Player
text: It's nothing. Our plan is fine.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Good. Let's keep it that way.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask more about the Code.
comment: if the Code is known but the test not completed

speaker: Player
text: I want to know more about these ruins on the surface.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I have been involved in the work there over the last couple of years, but not often. Most of the excavating is left to the students. What did you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: Is there any way into the tomb of Naga Sadow?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Not unless you are accompanied by Master Uthar, no. It is strictly forbidden... and I truly doubt you could bypass the doors to the tomb with anything less than ship blasters. Even then, perhaps.

speaker: Player
text: There's no other way inside?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: None. I do not even know how Master Uthar gains entrance, to tell the truth, though I look forward to discovering that fact.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I have searched many times, so do not bother... there is no other way. Do not fret, however. Simply get the prestige you need and you will see the tomb soon enough.

speaker: Player
text: Why are the Sith so interested in these ruins?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: We could learn much about the history of the ancient Sith... why they were on Korriban and why they left.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Perhaps we could learn more about the origin of the Force, itself. With that knowledge could come great power.

speaker: Player
text: I've heard enough.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As you wish.
comment: player has passed the second test

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about Darth Revan?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Revan? You mean Darth Malak's former master?

speaker: Player
text: That's the one.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Very little. I never met him personally, though I hear he was a powerful man. Very charismatic.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: In the end, Revan was outshone by his pupil. Such is the way of the Sith. Why? Is this dead man of importance to you?

speaker: Player
text: Do you think it's possible Revan might be alive?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Anything is possible. Uthar's former master still lives... though he is in no condition to challenge his former pupil for leadership.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Perhaps the same is true for Revan. Perhaps Revan is out there, somewhere, waiting to take revenge upon Malak.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: More likely what we were told is the truth: Revan is dead. Malak would be foolish to leave his old master alive, considering all the knowledge Revan held.

speaker: Player
text: So you wouldn't recognize Revan if the two of you met?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Is there any reason I should? Beside the fact that I did not know Revan in life, Revan was known for wearing a full helmet and cape.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Perhaps Revan's body had been disfigured by the power of the Force... it is not unheard of. Regardless, I doubt I shall be meeting Revan anytime soon.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned that Revan came here before?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Both Revan and Malak came to Korriban when they discovered the tomb of Naga Sadow. That was before my time.

speaker: Player
text: That's all I have to ask.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Fair enough.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know a student named Kel?
comment: Kel has told the player his secret plot not resolved yet

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Yes... vaguely. The boy burdens himself with doubts and anxieties. It is sad to watch, really, for he does possess a certain flair with the Force.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Kel will not survive long. Someone will betray him soon enough, and he will be dead. If you are smart and you know something, that person should be you.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about yourself.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: About myself? I am originally from Sleheyron, if you must know. I was a slave to a cruel master, Omeesh the Hutt. I am sure you don't need to know more.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I hope to see you again.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Come back soon... my friend.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are very close to succeeding... work quickly!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You have had an excellent start... go, gain more prestige!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You have much to do.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned you were from Sleheyron...

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I did. I also said that you didn't need to know more. Why are you asking?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I just would like to know more about you, that's all.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Success] I... see. Very well. I suppose there's no harm in the tale.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: As I said, I was originally a slave to one of the Hutts. The Hutts control everything on Sleheyron, and a slave is nothing to them.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I was determined not to be 'nothing'. One night when the drunken worm had me alone in his chambers I stabbed him and escaped the compound.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I stole onto a cargo ship and was not discovered by the crew until they reached the next system. They left me for dead on a desolate planetoid, alone... but that was fine by me. I was glad to be anywhere other than Sleheyron.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: It was not luck that I was eventually rescued, of course. The Force was strong with me, though I didn't know that at the time. Not until the Jedi told me, that is.

speaker: Player
text: The Jedi found you? What happened?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I'd... rather not discuss it. Perhaps another time.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Is there something else you needed?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Failure] You know all that you need to. We can exchange niceties once Uthar is gone, if you desire.

speaker: Player
text: Alright, forget I asked.

speaker: Player
text: How did you become a Sith?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... would prefer not to discuss that.

speaker: Player
text: I'd really like to hear the tale.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Why? There is no point. Have I asked you about your past?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I just thought we could become friends, is all.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Success] You... have odd notions for someone hoping to become a Sith.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Let's see... after escaping from Sleheyron I was found by the Jedi. They took me in and trained me even though I was a bit older than most Padawans.

speaker: Player
text: You were a Jedi?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Not really, no. I never progressed beyond Padawan. I had discipline, but no peace... and after my treatment at the hands of the Hutts there was little room in me for the ways of the Jedi.

speaker: Bastila
text: You sound much like... someone I know.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Yes, well... I imagine I am not unique. Things very easily could have been very different for me.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I wanted to use the Force to free the other slaves I knew, to fight for what I knew was right. The Jedi restrained me until I couldn't stand it any more.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: They claim the dark side is evil, but that isn't so. Sometimes anger and hatred are deserved and right. Sometimes things change because of it.

speaker: Player
text: But not always. Mostly it makes things worse.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Any failure to get the results I want is due to a lack of power on my part. That can change, in time. As a Sith, my mettle is tested far more than when I was a Padawan.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I know this may sound strange, but only my compassion stands in my way, now. Once that is gone let the slavers beware.

speaker: Player
text: But... if you lose your compassion, will you still care about those slaves?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... yes, of course. I mean losing my compassion as in... holding back...

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: But enough of that. I've talked about myself too much, surely you are tired of it.

speaker: Player
text: How long before you begin this fight, do you think?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I... well, there is much training to do. I... may be a long time...

speaker: Player
text: It's a commendable goal. I admire your spirit.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Thank you. I only wish I was as strong with the Force as you are. You could change much, yourself, if you wanted to.

speaker: Player
text: I find it hard to think of any Sith with compassion.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I suppose I shouldn't be telling you these things... sharing my weaknesses with you. Being a Sith doesn't make me a monster, however.

speaker: Player
text: But has anything changed?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: No... not yet. But my anger has not diminished, nor my desire to see change. The more time I spend with the Sith the more I am certain that one day I will be able to fight as I must.

speaker: Player
text: I agree.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: There is suffering and injustice in the universe. I am surprised the Jedi can even stand the stench of it, much less stand by and do nothing.

speaker: Jolee
text: You sound very much like... someone I used to know.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Failure] Friends? We can be friends once Uthar is dead. Until then, a 'friend' is a weakness.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I just thought we could become friends... or maybe something more.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Success] I see. You... certainly have odd notions for one hoping to become a Sith. I'll play along... for now.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Is there any harm in telling me?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: [Failure] There is always harm in becoming too vulnerable. I will not be as weak as you desire.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Very little. I never met her personally, though I hear she was a powerful woman. Very charismatic.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: In the end, Revan was outshone by her pupil. Such is the way of the Sith. Why? Is this dead woman of importance to you?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, go on.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: There are a group of students who refused an order by Master Uthar to execute a group of civilians in the colony.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Uthar declared that they were to be executed, themselves, but the students escaped and fled before the order could be carried out.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: We are certain that they have not left Korriban. No doubt they have not gotten far and are simply in hiding... we just do not know where, exactly.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: If you were to locate them and carry out Uthar's order, I am sure he would be most appreciative.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The rebel students I told you about must still be found and dealt with... Master Uthar would be greatly impressed by their deaths, I am sure.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I would suggest you talk to the other prospective Sith and find one that you can gain an advantage with.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I believe Lashowe would be an excellent choice. She is too trusting. I have little doubt you could talk her into letting you 'help' her somehow.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Just make sure that it is you who gains the advantage, not her. Be ruthless, if you must. That is the only thing that will impress Uthar.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The only other idea I can suggest to you is that you head into the Valley of the Dark Lords on the surface. There are ancient ruins there which can be explored.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: It's possible you might find some artifacts or information in them which would please Uthar... it's difficult to say for certain.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I still think that approaching Lashowe would be your best move. She is too trusting and can no doubt be talked into aiding your cause.

speaker: Player
text: No, I've heard enough.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: The Code of the Sith is the easiest way, to start. I have told you all that you need to know of it, already.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I don't want to be a part of this.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You are already a part of this. Don't be a fool.

speaker: Jolee
text: You don't say? Well, the master loves tombs, don't you master?

speaker: Carth
text: Darth Malak went there? Very interesting... isn't it, master?

speaker: Player
text: Do I have a choice?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Not really. Oh, don't worry... what I have in mind will benefit us both, you can be sure of that.

speaker: Player
text: But I don't even have any prestige, yet!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: 'Yet' being the operative term. As I said, you have my utmost confidence.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What are you doing here? Go back to Uthar and tell him you're ready to take your final test! Our moment is at hand, go!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Hmmm. You're a rather tricky human, aren't you? However did you manage to convince Kel Algwinn to reveal himself to you?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: No matter. I applaud you for the maneuver, at any rate. An act worthy of a Sith, surely.

speaker: Player
text: I rather enjoyed it. He was a fool.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Now that's what I like to see... the flash of ambition in a young human's eyes. Your species has such remarkable retinal coloring, did you know that?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You have other things to turn your attention to, however, I'm sure. What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: He wouldn't have lasted. I just put him out of his misery.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Yes, I... suppose so. The weak can surprise you sometimes with their strength, however. He could have surprised us.

speaker: Player
text: I... suppose so.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What's this? Regrets? Not to worry, dear pupil, it... gets easier with time.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I understand you managed to kill Lashowe. Well done! She was devious, but I knew her trust could be turned against her!

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: One less opponent is an excellent result regardless of how it occurs, correct? Now, then... something you needed?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: So... you managed to kill Shaardan, did you? Good news travels quickly. Well done... he wouldn't have made a good Sith, anyway.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You killed Mekel, I hear? Well... I suppose it is just as well. He was far too devious to be allowed to live.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: You've been doing well... I hear you've almost enough prestige to be declared the victor. Somehow I just knew you were the one who would succeed.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I hear that you have gained even more prestige. You are closing in on victory... this is good.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Were I you, I would not get too excited just yet. You still have plenty left to do.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: I understand you have impressed Master Uthar at least a little. That is good... we are one step closer towards completing my plan.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Greetings, my friend. *chuckle* I do rather enjoy saying that.

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: Hello, again. I trust all is going smoothly?

speaker: Yuthura Ban
text: What do you wish? I am eager to get this over with.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I have heard a disturbing rumor, <FullName>. A hunter matching your description is reported to have slain a Krayt dragon on Tatooine. Please, tell me it wasn't you.

text: It was me. Why?

text: I do not mean to pry, <FullName>. But the Krayt dragon is a fierce and deadly beast, a monster even one of your power would be smart to avoid!

text: If something should happen to you - if you are injured or even slain by such a beast - then Malak will never be toppled!

speaker: Player
text: I can look after myself.

text: I suppose if there is anyone in the galaxy who could reasonably expect to survive such an encounter, it would be you, <FullName>.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: But if you are going to continue with such reckless escapades, I would strongly recommend you stock up with weapons and armor from my inventory.

speaker: Player
text: Let me see your premium items.

speaker: Player
text: I have some questions for you.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know a lot about the Ebon Hawk and its previous owners?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I know very little about the owners of the Ebon Hawk. Most were affiliated with the Exchange, and they only revealed enough to enable us to do business with them.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: But the ship itself is very well known, especially here on Korriban. Some say it is the finest smuggling vessel in this sector. Others say it is a cursed vessel, bringing doom to its owners.

speaker: Player
text: Cursed? What do you mean?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: None deny the Hawk is a fine vessel with a long history of successful smuggling runs to its credit. But the owners have not fared nearly as well the ship itself.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Take Davik Kang. He was the last owner I know of before you. His home world was the planet Taris - a world the Sith utterly destroyed. Few would call that a fortunate occurence.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: And even if Taris hadn't been destroyed, would Davik still be around? It seems doubtful he *sold* the ship to you. And I know Davik didn't *buy* it from the previous owner.

speaker: Player
text: These events have more to do with the type of owner than the Hawk itself.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Yes, I suppose a Sith Lord has little time for curses. You are probably far beyond such things. In any case, I meant no offense. I am only telling you what I know of the Hawk's reputation.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Is there anything else you are needing from me?

speaker: Player
text: Ziagrom says you sell... special items.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Yes, to the right buyer. Traditionally, the owner of the Ebon Hawk has been the contact for all my transactons. But in the past, the owner was always affiliated with the Exchange.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: That was why Ziagrom did not approach you earlier. We had no idea who you were, or if we wanted to do business with you. Of course that has all changed now, Lord Revan.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad you've seen the light.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: The light? A fine jest, though it contains a crystal of truth. We have allied with you in this conflict, and we trust you will remember us once victory is yours, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: What kinds of things do you have for sale?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Yes, let's get right to business. I carry only the rarest of items. Expensive, yes - but worth every credit! Weapons, armor, equipment: I carry a little of everything.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: The previous owners of the Ebon Hawk would often resell the items they purchased, but in your case I imagine you might find more than a few of them quite useful against your old apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Of course. Remember to return whenever you desire to see my inventory of permium items. We are eager to help you against your old apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: Your motives seem very self-serving.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Of course. How else are we to survive? Now, do you wish to see the premium items I have for sale? Or is there something else you need?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not who you think I am. I'm not Revan anymore.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: No? Ziagrom's information is never wrong. Are you saying that you don't want to revenge on your former apprentice? Are you saying you don't plan to kill Malak?

speaker: Player
text: I will stop Malak and his Sith, but not for revenge.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: In truth, your reasons matter little to me or my partner. But we do believe in your power. We believe you will bring Malak down - and we want to help you, in our own small fashion.

speaker: Player
text: Anything interesting going on here?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Since Malak stole the Order from you, the Academy here on Korriban has become all but impossible to deal with. The Sith there care for nothing but their own plots and schemes.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I hope that once you destroy your old apprentice things will return to the way they were before. The Sith and the Exchange should work together: it could benefit both sides.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Sith academy?

speaker: Mika Dorin

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: The Sith built their academy here to train students. Many go to train there, though I know not why. Most are not permitted to train and many die in their attempt to be admitted.

speaker: Mika Dorin

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Sith's excavations?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Very little. None are allowed in their ruins other than the Sith themselves, as I understand it.

speaker: Player
text: Surely there must be some way to go there.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: The Sith do have a passage that leads to their valley from within the monastery. Only they may use it, however.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I doubt they would let you in, even if you could somehow convince them of your true identity. Most of the Sith at the Academy are loyal to Malak, now. They see him as the true Master.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I am afraid not. The Sith have a passage that leads to their valley from within their monastery, but only they may use it.

text: Do you know anything about a Star Map on Korriban?

speaker: Player

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: There is a place on the surface of this planet called the Valley of the Dark Lords, I believe, where the Sith dig amongst such ruins. Perhaps what you seek is there.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Ebon Hawk?

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: Only what I hear from rumors, sentient. The Hawk has been a frequent visitor to Korriban in the past, though often with a different owner.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: In all fairness, I should tell you that many of the past owners were suspected of being smugglers, slavers and pirates. It was even whispered that some worked for the Exchange.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: But I always found the Hawk's owners to be excellent citizens of fine character. The kind of people I prefer to do business with. Much better than the Sith, at least.

speaker: Player
text: That's all for now.

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: As you desire, sentient.

speaker: Player
text: The very old kind. Perhaps the Sith's excavations involve something like it?

speaker: Mika Dorin

speaker: Player

speaker: Mika Dorin
text: I only hope your actions don't draw the attention of your old apprentice. I'd suggest you stock up from my inventory in anticipation of your next meeting with Malak.

text: People are saying the Kolto supply on Manaan has been destroyed. Of course when I heard the news I immediately thought of you, <FullName>.

text: Who else could have caused such a catastrophic change? You are a force of destiny, <FullName>. The galaxy is changed forever by even your slightest of actions.

text: But such actions have consequences, including drawing the attention of old enemies. You should probably look at my stock, <FullName>. It might come in useful in the coming battles.
