text: Well, you picked a real stinkhole to stop at. Republic soldiers are everywhere, those arrogant Selkath treating us Sith like we're second-class citizens.

speaker: Viglo
text: I wish we could bomb this ocean world into a desert, but we need that kolto for our Sith troops. Man, I hate this place.

speaker: Viglo
text: Oh, you're back. You going to stick around this time? Or did I offend you?
comment: subsequent conversations, not drunk, not asleep

speaker: Viglo
text: I probably should cut back on the drinking, but it's a good way to relax. There's a lot of tension here on Manaan.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Malak will show you Republics how a war is really waged!

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: You! You're the one! You beat Zoriis Bafka's time? I have to get your autoprint.
comment: Fade in, Initiates with the player after they win the Swoop race championship.

speaker: Player
text: What? My autoprint? Are you serious?

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: Sure I am! You are fast for a human, and once the races are running regular again, you'll be famous. Well, maybe you will.

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: If you start winning on the real tour, I want to be able to say I saw you when you were just starting out. How about it?

speaker: Player
text: Sure, why not? Scan away.

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: Really? That is great of you. You will be a fan favorite. Some of the racers sell their prints, but that is just rude.

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: Here, just put your hand on this pad. Thanks again. I know I'll be seeing more of you, human.

speaker: Player
text: Go away, I don't have time for you.

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: No? Why not? I just wanted to get a mark from the best new racer on the circuit. What is wrong with that?

speaker: Ganda Kaitoova
text: If you are so full of yourself now, I would hate to see what you would be like if the pro tour was back up. Keep your print, then.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Do you... do you have the cure, up-worlder? Have you come to save us from the horrible fate of the others?
comment: Dialog Mission Statement: If player initiates dialog infected outcasts beg for player to help them. Player can refuse to help or player can get the Rakghoul serum and cure them. If cured they will give player info about the downed escape pod. Exit Points: 1. Player has cured the infected ones and they have already returned to village, player reinitiates dialog. Thank player, don't perform any other actions. 2. Player gives cure to outcasts. They play animation of taking the cure, they give player info about downed escape pod, thank player then return to the village. The plot is marked as done. 3 and 4. Generic goodbyes. Player has not saved infected ones. No action needed.

speaker: Player
text: I have brought you a serum to cure the rakghoul disease.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: You... you have a cure? Please, give it to me. Please. Quickly, before it's too late.

speaker: Player
text: Here, take this rakghoul serum. I have enough for both of you.
comment: animation of handing something to the speaker??

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Quickly - I must inject it before it is too late. Yes... I feel it working!
comment: injection animation on both outcasts, and a glowing effect

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: I feel the disease burning away! It... it is like a miracle! I am cured!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Thank you, up-worlder. You have saved us from a fate worse than death. I only wish I had some reward to give you. Maybe you can find something worthwhile in the wreckage of that Republic escape pod.

speaker: Player
text: Republic escape pod? What are you talking about?

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Not long ago an escape pod crashed in the Undercity, far to the northeast of the village. We were going to try and salvage equipment from it but we were attacked by the rakghouls and infected.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: I'd tell you more if I could, but our salvage team never reached the pod. It's probably still there, unless some of the other up-worlders already found it and picked it clean.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We should go now, up-worlder. We're anxious to return to the village and see our families again. Thank you once again for everything you have done.

speaker: Player
text: I was just happy to help.

speaker: Player
text: What will you give me in exchange for this cure?

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We... we have nothing, up-worlder. We are Outcasts. All we have are the clothes on our backs.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please, up-worlder. Show us mercy. Give us the cure out of the goodness of your heart!

speaker: Player
text: Forget it. I'm not wasting the cure on an Outcast!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Go then, up-worlder. Leave us here to die, abandoned by everyone!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry - I'm here to help you.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: You... you will help us? Bless you, up-worlder! Bless you. But... you must hurry!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: We have the rakghoul disease. It is only a matter of time until we are transformed into terrible creatures like those who attacked you when you first came into the pen.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: It is too late for them. Soon it will be too late for us and we will transform into those horrible rakghouls ourselves!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry... I'll be back when I find a cure for you!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please hurry, up-worlder. We don't have much time until the transformation.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Don't forget about us, up-worlder. If you find any way to cure this disease, please come back and help us.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll kill you so you don't infect anybody else!

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Why have you come back, up-worlder? Do you come to mock us in our suffering as the disease destroys us?

speaker: Player
text: Get away from me you diseased mongrels!

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: When the rakghouls infected me I never thought I'd see my family again. Thank you for all your help, up-worlder.

speaker: Infected Outcast
text: Please... you have to help us. We beg you. We don't want to end up like the others. Please help us. We can't end up like them.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? Why are you locked away from the rest of the village?

speaker: Zeena
text: Hey, you're not bad... maybe if you win a couple races, I might be glad to have talked to you.

speaker: Zeena
text: Wow! You're, like, sooo great! I can't believe you actually spoke to me. Like, wow!

speaker: Zeena
text: What do YOU want? If you aren't a racer, you're nobody, so just leave me alone.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I shall answer questions pertaining to the case and those questions only.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of Sunry?

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I find the idea that some half-human cripple could murder someone as obviously competent as the Sith Elassa questionable at best.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: A man who can barely walk killed a Sith warrior in her prime? Preposterous!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: But I wouldn't put it past the Republic to try and arrange such circumstances to see her dead. The Sith are much more straight forward about their intentions.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Is that all?

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything suspicious about this case?

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I find it presumptuous to assume that the cripple Sunry could kill Elassa. I think that there must have been another there who killed her. Perhaps one of the 'witnesses'.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I do not know the reason for the medal clutched in Elassa's hand either, but it may have been that she fought them off even as she died.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I think this may be the work of some Republic conspiracy and I am not afraid to say so! If the only means I have of hurting the Republic is through Sunry, then so be it!

speaker: Player
text: What do you think of the Republic and the Sith Empire?

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I think the Republic is an institution in sore need of change. It has gone on too long and the Sith are the fresh wind of change blowing across the galaxy.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I do not believe in the false stories of the evils of the Sith Empire. They are nothing compared to the oppression and stagnation that the Republic represents at its core.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: If I was given the power to decide, Manaan would join with the Sith, forcing the Republic to accept the new face of the future.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: But sadly, it would appear that I am wiser and more farsighted than my immediate superiors. I am relegated to civil judicial matters.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I will judge this case. And I will find Sunry as guilty as he is charged to be.

speaker: Jolee
text: So nice to meet an impartial judge, for a change.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Impartiality is one thing. Blindness is another entirely.

speaker: Jolee
text: You said it, not I.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Are you finished?

speaker: Player
text: I have no more questions for now.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Do not bring frivilous topics to discuss. I deal only with trial information.

speaker: Carth
text: Hey! I thought you Selkath judges were supposed to follow the law! You can't already have decided that Sunry is guilty!

speaker: Bastila
text: If you had listened, Carth, you would know that that *is* the law. Sunry is guilty until proven innocent.

speaker: Carth
text: That's a stupid law for any civilized world to have.

speaker: Bastila
text: Angering the judge won't get us a more impartial decision, Carth.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: It is up to you off-worlders to prove the human's innocence. I simply doubt that you will be capable of doing so.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: I don't waste time on individuals who are not involved in my legal jurisdiction. Do not disturb me.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: We were watching you on the cameras, and I want you to know that you did the right thing. Killing that shark probably saved us all.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I'm sure the kolto will be fine. A few impurities that may have got in should be flushed out in no time.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Just hurry up and get back to the surface and get the Republic to send down a real rescue team. We'll be waiting here for you.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I saw what happened on the camera... and I can't believe what you did.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: How could you willfully destroy the kolto harvesting machinery?! That will set us back years!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I will have you know that when we get back to the surface I'll have the Republic do a full inquiry into your actions!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Now go back to the surface and get the Republic to send a REAL rescue team down for us.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: No - no, you can't come in here! You'll let the firaxa and the Selkath in! No - stay out! Stay out!
comment: on radio when the player first enters the room

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I won't let you open the door for those monsters to get in! I'll stop you! I'll suck all the pressure out of the chamber! That'll stop you!

speaker: Sami
text: Kill them! Kill them now!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: What - what do you want? Go away! You'll let the firaxa and the Selkath in! They'll get us like they got all the others!
comment: if the player talks over radio

speaker: Player
text: No - I'm <FullName> and I'm here to help you. But first you have to stop the depressurization sequence.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: No... the firaxa... the... the Selkath... I... I can't let you in. They'll get us!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'll keep you safe. I promise. But you have to let me in.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: [Success] I... I don't want to hurt you. I don't want to hurt anyone.
comment: Persuasion successful, she hits buttons to stop depressurization sequence

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I'll unlock the door, but you have to come in quickly!
comment: opens the door for the player

speaker: Sami
text: No, no, no. Don't do it!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: [Failure] No... I can't. The Selkath will get me! The firaxa will eat us! I can't! I can't!
comment: continue depressurization, she disconnects communicator and disables it by blasting it (all visible through the window)

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I'm a friend. You want to let me in. You want to stop the depressurization sequence.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: [Success] Yes. You are a friend. You'll protect us. You won't let the firaxa eat us. You'll keep the Selkath away.
comment: stops the pressurization sequence and unlocks the door

speaker: Player
text: Open this door or you'll wish the Selkath had got you!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: No... I can't. The Selkath will get me! The Firaxa will eat us! I can't! I can't!

speaker: Player
text: Please - we're going to die if you don't stop the sequence!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I... I'm sorry for what I did. I don't know what came over me. I... I just panicked when I heard someone outside the door. *Sigh* Please, forgive me. I'm just so scared.
comment: first conversation if the party calmed her

speaker: Sami
text: We're both just scared.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: When the Selkath went crazy I thought everyone else except me and Sami went mad. We had a few people outside the station when it happened...

speaker: Sami
text: The... firaxan sharks just tore them apart... It was like they were frenzied...

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: The next thing we knew our Selkath researchers started screaming and... and clawing at everything around them. My team... my team was torn apart and eaten before my eyes!

speaker: Bastila
text: How horrible! I can only imagine how frightened you were.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Sami and me... I... I thought we were the only ones left. We heard the Selkath outside at the doors every once in a while... and those strange noises echoing through the base.

speaker: Sami
text: We... thought everyone was dead... dead or insane.

speaker: Sami
text: I must have been hysterical, I... I don't know what I can say... I truly apologize for the horrible mistake I was making.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I am Kono Nolan, and this is Sami. We were scientists working here on the Hrakert Rift project.

speaker: Player
text: You have a lot to answer for!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Look, I'm sorry! I've just been under a LOT of strain recently. You know, the whole thing about having my entire research team DEVOURED BEFORE MY EYES!!

speaker: Sami
text: Kono. Kono, calm down.

speaker: Sami
text: Don't talk to him like that! We've gone through a lot, and we said we're sorry for the mistake we made!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Just... I am sorry for my actions. But... but what are you doing here?

speaker: Player
text: I'm on a mission for the Jedi Council to find pieces of a Star Map.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: A Star Map? I don't know of anything about a Star Map down here.

speaker: Sami
text: But... there were some ruins that were excavated when we were digging the foundations for the last section of the kolto harvesting machine.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: But we can't go anywhere near those now! Maybe... maybe that's why it all happened in the first place...

speaker: Player
text: What happened?

speaker: Sami
text: We don't know! Not for sure...

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: The work teams were outside in the Rift near the vent. Then there was this rumbling and my head felt like it was splitting open...

speaker: Sami
text: This... this monster rose up from the Rift...

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: It was a firaxa shark I think... bigger than any I'd ever seen before. Bigger than our submersibles.

speaker: Sami
text: It was like it was screaming inside my head...

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Then all the Selkath started screaming too... and they turned on us.

speaker: Player
text: Turned on you?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: It was like they couldn't control themselves... like the sound that the monster was making in our heads drove them insane.

speaker: Sami
text: Well... maybe it was protecting the ruins by the Rift.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: It could have been. It might have a lair in the Hrakert Rift near the kolto vent. Hm... that may explain a few things, too...

speaker: Player
text: Like what?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Like why it reacted so violently when our construction efforts got closer to the vent.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: And also why it is so large. It must be feeding off the kolto. It would have to be ancient indeed for it to reach that size. But with kolto as a food source...

speaker: Sami
text: And all those other firaxan sharks! Those might be its offspring!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Which would be why they all swarmed when it called out to them... Children coming to protect their mother.

speaker: Player
text: So what can I do about it?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: The firaxan sharks have always been a serious problem. We had some blasters and projectile cannons to defend against them, but they still got some of our workers from time to time.

speaker: Sami
text: We were working on a soluble chemical compound that would drive them away. Something that smelled or tasted repulsive to them, but we never got it working right.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Oh, I think not! Even flawed like it is, it should be ideal for this situation.

speaker: Sami
text: No! It's not working right! You don't know what it will do!

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Sami
text: The repellant we made was supposed to drive firaxan sharks away, but we never got very far in its development.

speaker: Sami
text: The one we tested instead was violently toxic to them, rupturing their outer skin in seconds and preventing them from drawing oxygen from the water by clogging their intakes.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Which is exactly what we need in this situation! Something to kill that monster shark that destroyed our station!

speaker: Sami
text: But we don't know how else the chemical reacts! We only tried it in a controlled environment. In the open ocean, who knows what it could do... it could even affect the kolto.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: We know exactly what it will do: it will kill the shark. That's what we designed it to do.

speaker: Player
text: How would I poison the shark?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You can take this cannister of toxin. We were working on it just before the giant shark drove all the Selkath insane.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: All you need to do is insert it into the main kolto harvester and have it vent it.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Get away as soon as you can. We don't know how much worse it will affect the giant firaxan shark.

speaker: Player
text: OK. I'll vent the toxin into the Rift to kill the giant shark.

speaker: Sami
text: Wait! Don't! We don't know what effect the toxin will have on the ocean environment around the Rift!

speaker: Sami
text: It could poison the water against all life. It could poison the kolto itself, even! There is another way...

speaker: Sami
text: Well, the monster seems to have been driven out by the machinery we installed at the edge of the Rift. We've seen it out there on the cameras bashing itself against the machines.

speaker: Sami
text: I think if you could destroy the machinery we installed, the shark would calm down and retreat back into its lair inside the Rift.

speaker: Player
text: How would I do that?

speaker: Sami
text: You can reprogram the harvesting machines to overpressure their self-oxidizing fuel, so that the fuel tank cannisters will rupture and the entire machine will destroy itself.

speaker: Sami
text: The Hydrolium gas we use is a gas at 1 to 3 million sangen, a liquid at about 4 million sangen, and a solid above that. When it's a liquid it's VERY explosive.

speaker: Sami
text: If you inject enough of the Hydrolium gas into the tank, the pressure will be so great that it will turn to liquid form and start a chain reaction inside the machine.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: But we'll lose everything we've built here! All those years of work!

speaker: Sami
text: It's better than whatever your chemical will do to the water!

speaker: Player
text: I will try to poison the shark.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You know it's the right thing to do. It can't go wrong.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Just put the cannister into the machine and have it vent it into the Rift. The firaxan shark should die in no time.

speaker: Sami
text: No! You shouldn't do that! It could poison everything!

speaker: Sami
text: Just reprogram the harvesting machine's computer to overpressure the fuel tanks. Once it's destroyed, the shark should just leave.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You know what you have to do.

speaker: Sami
text: I just hope you make the right choice.

speaker: Player
text: I will try to destroy the harvesting machine.

speaker: Sami
text: Good! Destroying the machinery will be better in the long run. We can't risk damaging the environment or the kolto.

speaker: Sami
text: You'll have to break into the computer on the harvesting machine and fiddle with the fuel injectors to get the tank pressure up to the point where the Hydrolium will liquidize.

speaker: Sami
text: Once the machinery is gone, the shark should leave.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: That won't work and you know it! We have to vent the toxin from the harvesting machine. Once the shark is dead, we can get back to mining the kolto.

speaker: Player
text: I'll do what I want... and kill both of you as well!

speaker: Sami
text: What? No!

speaker: Sami
text: Run, Kono! He's one of them!

speaker: Sami
text: Run, Kono! She's one of them!

speaker: Player
text: I am not so sure...

speaker: Sami
text: I AM sure.

speaker: Player
text: What other choice do I have, though?

speaker: Player
text: What else could I do?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You don't need to do anything else. We have a cannister of the toxin here right now. We were working on it before the giant firaxan drove all the Selkath insane.

speaker: Player
text: What compound?

speaker: Player
text: What does this compound do?

speaker: Player
text: Where is this monster firaxan now?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I don't know. It must still be out there.

speaker: Sami
text: Out there waiting for us...

speaker: Player
text: I have to get to the kolto machinery.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: That would be suicide... It's out there still.

speaker: Player
text: The Star Map I'm looking for is out there. I need to get past.

speaker: Player
text: How could you miss something that big living there?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: I don't know. It seems impossible, but...

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Maybe what ever sort of power it used to drive the Selkath insane masked it from us somehow... or maybe it was lying dormant deeper in the Rift.

speaker: Sami
text: I think it might live there. Live there because of the kolto.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Hm... maybe. That would explain more...

speaker: Player
text: And no one knew about this thing?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: We had no clue at all... until it came out.

speaker: Player
text: What did the shark have to do with that?

speaker: Player
text: It was protecting something?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: It may... It may have been. Maybe it was protecting the ruins by the Rift.

speaker: Player
text: Something happened in the ruins?

speaker: Player
text: What are you babbling about?

speaker: Player
text: The Republic wants me to find out what happened here.

speaker: Sami
text: Well, we're not too clear ourselves just exactly what happened...

speaker: Player
text: How about I ask the questions.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Oh.... okay. What is it you want to know?

speaker: Player
text: What was the Republic doing here?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: We had a secret agreement with moderates in the Selkath government. They knew that Manaan could not survive independently if the Sith were victorious.

speaker: Sami
text: Those thugs would wipe out the whole damn planet just to get at the kolto.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: So the Republic approached them about making this secret installation to harvest more kolto where the Sith couldn't see us.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: But that all went horribly, horribly wrong...

speaker: Player
text: Did this have something to do with a Star Map?

speaker: Player
text: Did the Sith do something?

speaker: Player
text: Have you seen a Star Map?

speaker: Player
text: Why did the Selkath all go crazy?

speaker: Player
text: You tried to kill me!

speaker: Carth
text: I suppose that explains a lot. You've been under a lot of strain, here.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: No! No! The firaxa will get us! No! The Selkath are coming! No!
comment: first time conversation if the party didnt calm her

speaker: Sami
text: No! No!

speaker: Player
text: Calm down... everything will be okay.

speaker: Player
text: I'm a friend. I'll protect you. You're both safe now.

speaker: Player
text: Stop screaming!

speaker: Sami
text: Eeeee! No!

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You... Sami! Sami, calm down! I don't think they're here to kill us.

speaker: Sami
text: Eee... Kono.... Are... are they?

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: Yes. I think they're here to help us.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: We're not leaving this room. We're safe here, and there's plenty of food and water. If you manage to reach the kolto harvesting machinery you can put the poison cannister in it and trigger it to release it into the Rift.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: After you've made it past the monster safely you can look for this Star Map of yours and unlock the door to the submersible docking bay.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: You can use the submersibles to get back to the surface and report what happened. The Republic will send down a proper rescue crew for us.

speaker: Kono Nolan
text: No offense, but we'd rather wait for them than go with you - even if we're stuck here a few more days. Just get back to the surface afterwards, and the Republic will take care of us.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Ah, greetings. You must be assisting Master Bolook in his investigation.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I am Handon Guld, perhaps you've heard of me?

speaker: Player
text: No.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Well, I presume you wish to hear my story then? I shall tell you, of course, but there is not much to it. I am sure that you'll agree that Rickard is quite obviously guilty of murder.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: You see, I was out here running earlier today - yes, running, I do that a lot. Can't stand speeders, never use them. Keeps me in shape too, you know! Anyway, I was out running on the other side of that bridge there...

speaker: Handon Guld
text: When all of a sudden I heard a shot coming from over here. I ran over and found this man Calder lying on the ground dead!

speaker: Player
text: Did you see the killer?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I saw Rickard come skulking out of the shadows of the rocks south of the river, and I knew something was wrong. I hit my emergency button and called the Enclave right away.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Well... there, that's my story. Now please hurry this up and arrest Rickard so I can get on with my day!

speaker: Player
text: Go on.

speaker: Player
text: Should I have?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Um... I guess, under the circumstances, no.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Ah, yes of course, Mr. Guld.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: [Success] Really? *Ahem* Well, then, I assure you on my reputation I had nothing to do with the killing. I will help you with the case as best I can, though.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: How can I be of further assistance?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the weapon found by the body?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: That blaster was stolen from my house last week! I never knew what happened to it.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I hardly have enough money to afford a single blaster, let alone another. I can't tell you how important it is to have a weapon on hand with all these ravenous kath hounds around.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Even an iriaz can take a man down if it gets in the mood. Every settler has a weapon. It's our most prized possession.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I would most appreciate it if I could have that back after you determine that Rickard is the killer.

speaker: Player
text: You knew Calder better than you admit. You rented a speeder with him!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: But I... I realize this must seem like a motive to you, but I assure you it isn't. I dislike Calder, true. I would punch his face in, given the opportunity. But I would not kill him!

speaker: Player
text: Punch his face in? Why?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: My wife was cheating on me with him. They slept in my own bed while I was in the next room!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: But... as much as I may hate him for that, I could not kill him.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: It may have been my own fault for driving my wife away. I must try not to take the law in my own hands.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I was just out running, trying to clear my head for the divorce proceedings, not stalking him to kill him. Running is not a crime.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: That's all for now.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Of course, of course. Listen, if you need anything I shall be glad to assist.

speaker: Player
text: You better come clean!

speaker: Player
text: I want the truth - now!

speaker: Player
text: You wanted to kill Calder for having an affair with your wife!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Knock his block off, sure, but not kill him! Oh my... I hope you don't find that incriminating...

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Normally I am not prone to outbursts like that, but Calder... Mr. Nettic, he was not a very nice person. Not a very nice person to me or my family.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I had had my suspicions for several weeks, but had no proof until two days ago. It seems Calder was seeing my wife. Right under my nose, no less!

speaker: Cand
text: Well, if you can't keep her, it's your own fault.

speaker: Juhani
text: She may have had her reasons, Mandalorian!

speaker: Player
text: Did you know the victim?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I knew him a little bit, but I was not any sort of great friend to him or anything.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I never really associated with him that much. In truth, I didn't really want to. He had a... reputation. Very inconsiderate of family, I heard.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: But merely having heard unkind things about someone wouldn't make me want to kill him!

speaker: Player
text: Liar! You wanted to kill him for having an affair with your wife!

speaker: Player
text: No one says you killed him... yet.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I'm sorry, I'm... I'm getting a bit agitated. Why must we remain here? Can't... Can't you see that Rickard must have shot him?

speaker: Player
text: What did you see happen?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Actually, I didn't see anything. I was over across the bridge, I heard a shot and came over. I can tell you I was sure surprised to see Calder's body lying there!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I just got here when I saw Rickard coming out of the rocks, holding his blaster! I was terrified!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I had no idea what he was going to do so I hit my emergency button and called the Enclave.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Master Bolook came out here with his droid and started questioning us. I think he really doesn't understand what's going on.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I hope that you'll be able to make a more informed decision and get me out of here soon. I have things I have to do!

speaker: Player
text: Why would someone want to kill him?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Um... well, you see, Calder was involved in some pretty sordid business from time to time. More often than not, I've heard.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Disreputable business practices, even more disreputable clients. I've even heard he had dealings with... a Hutt! A Hutt here on Dantooine!

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Now I bet you're wondering if I had any reasons to kill the man, but I tell you I hardly knew him! Saw him once or twice, yes, and I have heard some pretty unkind things about him, but...

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Certainly nothing that would make me want to kill him!

speaker: Player
text: Why were you out here?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: I was taking my daily constitutional. I just happened to be running by when I heard a shot. I ran over and found Calder's body lying there.

speaker: Player
text: Do you often run around the plains?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: Yes, quite often. I generally prefer running to anything else. Can't stand speeders.

speaker: Handon Guld
text: A healthy body will breed a healthy mind, as I always say! Ha ha!

speaker: Player
text: You're holding your side. Are you injured?

speaker: Handon Guld
text: In... injured? No, of course not! Why would I have been? Fit as a bantha! Har har! Yes... I run. I don't know if I mentioned that.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing more right now.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Hold here, spacer. Czerka Corporation doesn't recommend traveling in wild Edean. Katarn attacks are especially bad right now.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Wookiee hunters usually keep numbers down, but I think they leave certain areas infested, just hoping a Czerka guard will get killed.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Wookiees?

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: You're the Wookiee-lover, why don't you tell me about them? I'm sure you're real close friends.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Grraarrr!

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Keep your pet on a leash or you'll be wearing him. I've no love for these animals. I've seen guards ripped to shreds.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe I should just let him rip your arms off.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: I don't take kindly to threats. Don't test me, spacer, we've more than enough firepower to bury you here.
comment: Only appears if player has not threatened the guard before (state 0, nothing set yet). Set guard threat state to 1 from 0

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm just trying to get my bearings. I don't mean any harm.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: [Success] Ah, you ain't so bad. Was there anything else you needed?
comment: Success SET THREAT THING BACK TO 0

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Czerka Corporation?

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: I don't talk to Wookiee-lovers. Get rid of your rug and maybe I won't have you shot.

speaker: Player
text: Don't get in my way. You'll wind up dead.

speaker: Player
text: I'm going past you. I paid the landing fee.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: I won't stop you, but you leave this area at your own risk. We're here to protect the company, not you.

speaker: Player
text: That's all. Goodbye.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Watch yourself out there. There won't be any rescue missions if you go missing.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Go to Janos for company policy. I just man the gate to make sure people like you know you're on your own on the other side.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: [Failure] What are you doing? Are you making fun of me? Don't push your luck, fool.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You haven't warned me. I'm a nice person. You like me.

speaker: Player
text: I meant nothing by it. Could you answer my questions?

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Make it quick. I'm getting tired of you.

speaker: Player
text: Should I care? You are nothing to me.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, yes, you're big and tough. I'll leave.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: That's right you will. Now get moving.

speaker: Player
text: So the Wookiees are fighting back?

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Not anymore. Look, you want to know why the Wookiees are acting compliant, you go ask them.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: When they rip your head off, we'll fish it out of the Shadowlands and give it a proper burial. How about that?

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: What's to tell? They're big, powerful, difficult, and worth the most when caged and shipped off this forest-covered rock.

speaker: Mission
text: That's horrible! You wouldn't talk like that if Big Z was here!

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: You're not some anti-slaver, are you? If so, go talk your crud somewhere else. I've seen guards ripped to shreds. They're animals.

speaker: Bastila
text: Shipped as slaves to work as soldiers and heavy laborers in Czerka camps, no doubt.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Still here? Why do you keep bothering me? All our services are up near the docking area.

speaker: Player
text: I have questions for you.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Make it quick. I'm no information booth. Talk to Janos in the Czerka office.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. I'm leaving.

speaker: Czerka Guard Captain
text: Fine then, move along.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: [Focused on the nearby enemy, Zaalbar is in no mood to talk right now.]

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Is there something you want?

speaker: Player
text: How do you feel about me being Revan?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You rescued me from the Gammorean slavers. It does not matter to me if you are called <FullName> or Revan: I have sworn a life debt to you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will stay with you to the end, <FullName>. And I will judge you on your actions as I see them, not on a history I have never known.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the planet we're on?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have been away from Kashyyyk a long time, but things look the same as I left them. Slavers still hold my people prisoner.
comment: before Kashyyyk plot done,  ON Kashyyyk Freyyr alive AND Chuundar alive

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I'm not sure what I could tell you. Or even what I would want to. You are an outsider here too. It angers me.

speaker: Player
text: I wonder if you could help me with a problem.
comment: Zaalbar will have little in the way of input, unless physical strength is required.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Unless you want someone threatened or a door bashed in, you should ask someone else.

speaker: Player
text: I want you to make me a grenade.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You've got a bunch already. You really don't want these things banging around together. Use some up first.
comment: player has too many grenades at the moment

speaker: Player
text: I want to know a little more about you, Zaalbar.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You have seen more than I would have allowed, and taught me some things too. I am grateful for that.
comment: Visited Kashyyyk, plot done Freyyr alive, Chuundar dead

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It will be a while before I know what my role will be in making Kashyyyk truly free. I have a lot to learn.

speaker: Player
text: Why did you request to take Bacca's Sword?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I'm not sure I really know. Father expects much of me... I guess I do as well.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I think, when I've learned enough, I'll bring it back to Kashyyyk. What happens then... we'll see.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry we can't stay on Kashyyyk longer.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You and I have important things to do, and I don't feel bad about leaving this time. I know I'll be welcomed back.

speaker: Player
text: This nostalgia won't interfere with your service to me, I hope.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I should get mad, but I won't. Your comment was callous, but you have shown you respect my people.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: And it is that harshness of you outsiders that I must try to understand. I will follow undistracted while I observe.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. Let's just get moving.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will follow.

speaker: Player
text: I wish you well. Let's get going.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will fulfill my life debt with you, but I don't think outsiders are worthy of knowing about me or my people.
comment: Visited Kashyyyk, plot done Freyyr dead, Chuundar alive

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I don't think I have to explain why. You witnessed what happened on Kashyyyk, what is still going on.

speaker: Player
text: The slavers are responsible for what happened, not me.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Chuundar showed me that you are all the same, all greedy, but I also learned that outsiders can be used.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: As long as you think you are leading, you don't care what those beneath you do. I will use this to my advantage.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I owe you a life debt, and I will honor it, but I will also serve myself. That is all I have to say.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps the outsiders are to blame, but your people are complicit.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Did we ask to be enslaved? Suffer like we have and then you can criticize how we dealt with this.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Chuundar has done what he must to ensure we survive. I see it now. He has shown me you can be used.

speaker: Player
text: Your attitude better not interfere with your service to me.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am only a slave to you, just like my people are slaves. Well, Chuundar has shown me how to use you anyway.

speaker: Player
text: Then I will leave you be.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Thank you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am sorry, but I don't feel like talking. All I have seen tells me that my home is just as I left it. We are still enslaved.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: For now, just let me think of what must be done. When I learn something new I will comment.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I will honor my life debt, but I don't feel we share more than that. Mission may say more, but I will not.

speaker: Player
text: You don't trust me?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It is nothing personal, but I just don't feel you could understand anything about me.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: The ways of my people are not for outsiders to know. You'll have to be content with that.

speaker: Player
text: You'll have to tell me more eventually.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: That may be, but not today.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe we'll talk later.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Very well.

speaker: Player
text: I saved you. I deserve respect.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: A life debt is the greatest respect. I just don't think you could understand anything about me.

speaker: Player
text: Have anything more to say about yourself, Zaalbar?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have said all I am going to. I will follow you as my life debt commands, but you are just another outsider to me.
comment: Pissed off. Set on the "I owe you a life debt, and I will honor it, but I will also serve myself. That is all I have to say." line

speaker: Zaalbar
text: All right, let's see what I can do. I think I have enough parts for something. Just a moment.
comment: player does not have too many greanades all ready Player has not just asked for one.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: There you are. One grenade. Careful with it.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: So many things have changed on Kashyyyk. I'm not sure what my place is. I must learn more about you outsiders.
comment: After Kashyyyk plot done,  ON Kashyyyk Freyyr dead OR Chuundar dead

speaker: Zaalbar
text: When I know enough, I will understand how to best serve my people. I will travel with eyes open this time.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: But, I leave with good feelings. My father will do what is right until I can return. And I will, when my life-debt is paid.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Chuundar has told me much about our failures here. I think learning how to really live elsewhere will help.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: And maybe... maybe I'll come back to fight... but not now.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I know that it isn't my homeworld. That is all I care about. There is nothing here to interest me.
comment: before Kashyyyk plot done,  not on Kashyyyk Freyyr alive AND Chuundar alive

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I don't know much about the planets we visit, but... I suppose I should learn.
comment: After Kashyyyk plot done,  not on Kashyyyk Freyyr dead OR Chuundar dead

speaker: Zaalbar
text: When you ask someone else, I will listen as well.

speaker: Player
text: I have a little stowaway problem, actually.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I cannot help you with that.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about dealing with gizka?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I know nothing of what you speak.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing. Never mind.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Your actions disturb me. Among my kind, those who take pleasure in the suffering of others are considered dangerously unstable.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Had I known you were so cruel, I might have thought twice before swearing my life-debt to you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am proud to call you my friend, <FullName>. You have a noble and generous spirit.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I know you. You're the Arbiter in the murder trial. Elassa was a friend of mine. If there's any justice in the galaxy, they'll feed Sunry to the firaxans.
comment: first time conversation, during sunry trial

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Shouldn't you be preparing for the trial? What are you doing here?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: You can ask - but I doubt you'll get many answers you'll like.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about the Sunry case?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I know he'd already be tried, convicted and executed if the Selkath knew anything about justice! But the fish people are as weak as the Republic when it comes to such matters.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Is there anything else?

speaker: Player
text: Why is the Republic hiring so many mercenaries?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Who knows? Some scheming plot, no doubt. Hopefully the Selkath uncover it and ban the Republic from the planet.

speaker: Player
text: Why have the Sith taken such an interest in the Selkath youth?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I haven't the faintest clue as to what you're talking about.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Go. Stay. Doesn't matter to me. If you want to, you can even wander up to the embassy gates. Heh. But don't expect to get inside.

speaker: Player
text: I have business with the Sith.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Ha! We know who we have business with. If you don't know how to get in, then we don't want anything to do with you. Now back off!

speaker: Player
text: I have this passcard.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: If you have a pass, why are you bothering me with it? Just go in.

speaker: Player
text: I know the pass code.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Oh, really? You mean someone like you actually has some real purpose inside? Well, then, what is it?

speaker: Player
text: Zeta 245698 Alpha.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Hmph. Yes, well, I suppose you really do have some business here. Head on in.

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: I can't believe you let that murderer Sunry go free! If the Selkath are so neutral and unbiased, why can't the Sith find any justice on this planet?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: But we Sith have long memories. Soon there will be a day of reckoning - very soon. So what are you doing here?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Allow me to thank you for helping put that killer Sunry in prison. Elassa was a friend of mine, and the thought of her murderer going free enraged me!

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: But thanks to you, justice was served. So what can I do for you?

speaker: Sith Diplomat
text: Only people who have business with the Sith are allowed inside the Embassy.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I am not for hire. Perhaps the Mandalorian or the Echani can help you - though they lack the stomach for certain jobs.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Ask whatever you wish - though you may find some of my answers distasteful.

speaker: Player
text: Why is the Republic hiring so many mercenaries?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Perhaps you should ask them. The Republic prefers not to deal with my kind... though maybe they need an Iridorian to finish the job.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: The mercenaries they hire must be failing, as they are never heard from again. That is all I know. Is there more you wish to ask?

speaker: Player
text: Have you heard anything about young Selkath going missing?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Perhaps - but my business with the Selkath is my own.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] But I am your friend. You want to tell me what's going on.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: [Success] An Iridorian has no friends! Though I feel a strange kinship with you - you do not seem like the others of this world. Even the Sith here do not understand our kind.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: The Sith sought to buy my loyalty with credits... as if wealth could somehow quench my burning bloodlust! They would have been better off hiring an Echani for the errands they had me running.

speaker: Player
text: What were you doing for the Sith?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: The task paid well, but was boring and beneath me. I was told to lure the Selkath youth to the Sith Embassy, nothing more. I lied, I threatened, I promised... and I brought the most promising youth of the fish people to the Sith.

speaker: Carth
text: What then? What happened to the youths?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: And there I left them. To what purpose I neither know, nor care. Perhaps when the Sith learn I have betrayed their secret they will try to kill me. I would welcome the excitement.

speaker: Cand
text: Sounds like a recruiting drive to me. We used to use it on planets we had conquered. Get 'em while they're young and impressionable.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Is there more you would ask of me, human?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know about the murder of Elassa?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: On my world those too weak to defend themselves deserve to die. A murder is justified if you have the strength to kill your victim. Is there anything else you would know?

speaker: Player
text: I am seeking an ancient Star Map or some alien ruins.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Manaan has no such things, unless the Selkath have them hidden away at the bottom of the ocean. Is there more you would know?

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I am not surprised. There are few on this watery world who feel comfortable in my presence.

speaker: Jolee
text: Sounds like the Sith are trying to win this planet by corrupting the Selkath youth. Much more subtle than their usual methods.

speaker: Mission
text: I bet they're twisting the minds of those Selkath youth, trying to trick them into joining the Sith!

speaker: Bastila
text: So you brought these youths to the Sith. And then what did you do to them?

speaker: Juhani
text: So you tricked these innocents into going to the Sith base. And then what did you do with them?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe the Selkath would be interested in your activities?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I have no fear of the fish people or their laws. There is no evidence I have done anything wrong. You will not learn my business this way.

speaker: Player
text: How many credits would it take to make your business my business?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: This is the way of this water world, is it not? Pathetic creatures bargaining with credits for what they cannot seize through strength. My people are warriors, not snivelling merchants.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: But perhaps this world has made me soft. I will play this role, distasteful as it is. For 500 credits, I will tell you what you wish to know.

speaker: Player
text: Here are the credits. Tell me who hired you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have that much.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I humble myself to change information for mere credits, and you insult me with this game of offers and counter offers? On my home world such insult would result in death!

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I tire of this conversation and I tire of your company, human. In fact, I tire of this entire weakling world - the air reeks of sea salt and the fawning cowardice of the fish people!
comment: Leaves area, doesn't open up recruitment plot.

speaker: Player
text: Make it 200 and we have a deal.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Maybe I'll just gut you like a Selkath preparing an Orchana ray for lunch.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: [Success] You speak the blunt and brutal language of my people. We share the love of death and bloodshed. But we are a rare breed on this planet. Even the Sith here are as weak as the cowardly fish people.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: [Failure] Your threats are mere words, nothing more. Here on Manaan such bloodshed is not permitted - as I have been told time and time again.
comment: Persuasion fails.  Gets up and leaves area.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Force Persuade] But we are not your enemies... we are your friends. Tell us what you know.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: I am of sterner stuff, human. I seek blood and death and my reward is the taste of my enemy's fear. Take your credits elsewhere... my price is too high for the likes of you.
comment: Bump each persuasion up one category.

speaker: Player
text: On second thought, I don't really want to talk to you.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have against the Echani and the Mandalorians?

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: They lack the resolve to do what needs to be done. The Echani believe in a non-existent warrior code of honor, and the Mandalorians prize credits above bloodshed.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: But I am Iridorian. Honor comes from slaying your opponent, and the true reward of any job is the taste of your foe's dying blood on your tongue.

speaker: Player
text: A mercenary who's not for hire. That's strange.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Why do you care? There are other mercenaries you can hire. Though I suggest you act quickly - the Republic seems to be in desperate need of mercenaries right now.

speaker: Iridorian Mercenary
text: Though not so desperate they have asked for my help as of yet. They prefer the simpering, submissive type - like the Mandalorian and the Echani.

speaker: Sith Patron
text: I'm not here to chat. I just finished a long shift at the military base and now I'm just looking to relax.

speaker: Sith Patron
text: Let me enjoy my drink in peace, and I won't have to run you in for questioning.

speaker: Sith Patron
text: If you're here to complain about the quarantine don't waste your breath. There's nothing I can do about it. I just follow the orders I'm given.

speaker: Zelka Forn
text: What are you doing? Don't go in there! That door is for employees only!

speaker: Player
text: What's going on here?

speaker: Zelka Forn
text: The Sith governor said I could keep this medical facility open. I have the proper permits. Please... I don't want any trouble.

speaker: Zelka Forn
text: N-nothing. This... this isn't your concern. Just... just forget you saw anything, okay?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm a friend of the Republic. You can trust me.

speaker: Zelka Forn
text: [Success] I guess... I guess I better tell you what's going on. I only hope the Sith don't find out what I've done.

text: This murder is much more complicated than it may first appear. Sunry and Elassa are proxies for their governments and both sides want the other to fail.

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: You can see the journey, heh, by the footprints. You understand, yes?

speaker: Player
text: Um... I think so... kinda...

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: Hmm, dear dear. I'm saying they both had something to do with it! They've both kept their hands in this from the start!

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: If you want to get to the bottom of this murder, you might seek information from both the Sith and the Republic, likely in their Embassies.

speaker: Player
text: They'd just give it to me?

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: No, of course not! You think state secrets are for sale on the common market?

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: You would have to be, heh, devious to get what you want.

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: Heed my advice, Jedi, and you may yet find the truths in this murder.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I believe you?

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: Because you have no one else to trust? Not Sunry, not the witnesses, and certainly not the judges!

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: And if you take my advice, what have you to lose?

speaker: Player
text: I've heard enough of you!

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: And I've been seen speaking to you for far too long.

speaker: Player
text: Huh?

speaker: Player
text: You're talking crazy talk.

speaker: Player
text: Why are you telling me this?

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: Let us just say that I am an interested party, and that I have, heh heh... concerns.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this!

speaker: Mysterious Man
text: Oh, but I think that you do!

speaker: Adrenas
text: Greetings, student.

speaker: Player
text: I'm no student. I'm Darth Revan!

speaker: Adrenas
text: I have heard you have gained much prestige, student. Why you would want to throw it away by making ridiculous claims is beyond me.

speaker: Adrenas
text: The Sith aren't big on such jokes, human. You would do well to remember that. Now, if your sorry attempt at humor is over, is there anything else you need?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Adrenas
text: My name is Adrenas. I am the chamberlain of the academy... generally I look after maintenance and supply, here.

speaker: Player
text: Master Uthar gave me this datapad for you.
comment: if the player has the datapad

speaker: Adrenas
text: He did? Allow me to see that for a moment...

speaker: Adrenas
text: Ah, yes, I see. I will do as Master Uthar requests, of course. Thank you for bringing this to me.

speaker: Player
text: So you aren't a Sith?

speaker: Adrenas
text: No, not truly. I serve the Sith, but I do not study and train in the Force as you do.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Adrenas
text: I am sure there is nothing I can help you with. I am only a servant to the academy.

speaker: Player
text: How come you don't speak Galactic Basic?

speaker: Adrenas
text: Galactic Basic is the language of the Republic, but I come from a world beyond the edges of Republic space. There the Twi'lek language of interstellar trade and commerce is the most common dialect.

speaker: Adrenas
text: I can speak your language, but my accent is still very pronounced. Some at the Academy would mock me for this, and I am not eager to become the subject of ridicule.

speaker: Adrenas
text: There are many humans here who come from worlds beyond Republic space. We seem to be more sympathetic to the Sith cause. Some of them are even training at the Academy, unlike me.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Adrenas
text: May the Force serve you well.

speaker: Adrenas
text: If you wish. Good luck with your training.

speaker: Adrenas
text: You are one of the hopefuls who look to gain prestige, yes? I am afraid there is little that I could help you with.

speaker: Adrenas
text: I am sure you would prefer to speak to one of the students, here, or perhaps the trainers.

speaker: Adrenas
text: Darth Revan? Remarkable, considering Lord Revan was killed. If this is a joke, student, it is one I do not understand at all.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Bendak Starkiller's dead! I don't believe it! Bendak never loses... that was an amazing duel! Best duel I've ever seen!

speaker: Player
text: Glad you enjoyed it. Now where's my share of the purse?

speaker: Ajuur
text: You've done well, Stranger. I'm pleased. Very pleased. Here are your credits. Plus, I'll give you Bendak's blaster pistol as bonus as a sign of my appreciation.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you Ajuur. That's very generous of you.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Everyone will be talking about you now, Stranger. They're all going to know you were the one who killed Bendak Starkiller. You're famous now.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I think I deserve a little extra for putting my life on the line.

speaker: Ajuur
text: [Success] Very well, Stranger. I like you, and this was a special fight. Biggest purse I've ever handled! I'll give you a little bonus this one time only.

speaker: Ajuur
text: [Failure] I always pay my debts, but if you get more then all the duelists will want more. We had a deal - ten percent. I expect you to honor it.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, I'll take the ten percent.

speaker: Player
text: Pay up, you overgrown slug, or I'll tell people you went back on our deal! Your reputation will be ruined!

speaker: Ajuur
text: You'd lie about me? Maybe it would have been better if Bendak had killed you in that ring. But you're still alive, and I can't afford to have a new legend disparaging my reputation.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Okay, you win. Here's another 200 credits... more than fair. Now don't be accusing me of not paying my fighters; I've got a reputation to protect!

speaker: Player
text: I know, I know - I'm a living legend. Now, what about my cut?

speaker: Player
text: Cut the flattery - just get to my credits.

speaker: Ajuur
text: I've heard the news, Mysterious Stranger. You and Bendak are planning a death match. This is excellent news... people will bet a fortune on this fight!

speaker: Ajuur
text: Not too many people want to fight a death match anymore. Some are scared, others think it's wrong to kill someone else for credits. I guess that's why they're illegal now.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe it is wrong to take a life just for credits.

speaker: Ajuur
text: What? What are you talking about? No, no, no. I was just making idle chatter, it doesn't mean anything! Bendak is an evil, evil man. Killing him would be a good thing.

speaker: Player
text: You're right - let's do this!

speaker: Ajuur
text: This fight is different than most, of course. We'll turn off the energy suppressor, so weapons won't be limited - they can kill. Anything goes. So, you ready to fight this match now?

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready!

speaker: Ajuur
text: Good. Excellent. High wagering means lots of credits for the winner on this match. Come see me after the fight to collect your credits - if you're still alive.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not ready yet.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You're not ready? What are you waiting for? Are you scared? Look, don't worry about it. I'll wait. You just come back when you're ready to fight.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like your just trying to rationalize this. I need to think this over.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Why don't you think this over? Think about all those credits you'll get if you kill Bendak. Then come back and talk to me. I'm confident you'll want to step into the ring.

speaker: Player
text: Let's get on with the match!

speaker: Ajuur
text: But why are you here now? A death match takes time to get ready. I have to bribe officials so they don't break it up. You might as well leave the cantina for now and come back later.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Congratulations, Mysterious Stranger. You're the new duel champion. Twitch had a good run, but you took him down! Here's the purse for beating Twitch.

speaker: Ajuur
text: The bad news is that I don't have anyone left who wants to fight you - you're too good for your own good. Nobody wants to go in the ring with you.

speaker: Ajuur
text: The only one who'd fight you was Bendak Starkiller, but you killed him. Now I'll never find anyone to fight you. I'm sorry to say, but your dueling career is over, Stranger.

speaker: Ajuur
text: The only one left who'll fight you is Bendak Starkiller, but he's retired. Too bad. People would pay a fortune to see you fight Bendak.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Mysterious Stranger - why are you here? I don't have anyone who wants to fight you - you're too good for your own good. Nobody wants to go in the ring with you.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Good fight, good fight. People like you, Mysterious Stranger. They bet a lot when you fight. It makes me happy... and rich.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Too bad you lost, though. I don't pay you for losing. But I'll give you a rematch if you want one. What do you say?

speaker: Player
text: Give me a rematch.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Yes - rematch! People always bet lots on a rematch! And who knows, Stranger... maybe you'll even win this time.

speaker: Player
text: No - not right now.
