speaker: Ajuur
text: I hope you're not giving up, Stranger. You lost this time, but maybe next time you'll win. You come speak to me if you ever want a rematch.

speaker: Ajuur
text: I always pay my debts. You won, so you get paid. Ten percent of the purse - that was the deal. Here's your credits. You come see me when you're ready to fight again.

speaker: Ajuur
text: I'm sorry, human - the betting window's closed. No more fights right now. People are sick of seeing the same duelists all the time. It's bad for business. Unless...

speaker: Ajuur
text: My name is Ajuur. I organize all the duels here. We need a new face in the dueling game, human. Maybe you want step into the duel ring? It can be a highly profitable venture.

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Ajuur
text: I can arrange for you to fight in the duel ring. If you win, you get the standard contract: 10% of all wagers. And don't worry, nobody dies in the duel ring anymore. Death matches are illegal now.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Most fighters in the duel ring use vibroblades or stun sticks because the ring's pretty small, but a few of the duelists use blasters. Use whichever you prefer.

speaker: Carth
text: Vibroblades and blasters? And nobody ever dies? How come I get the feeling you're trying to take us for a ride?

speaker: Ajuur
text: The duel ring has energy suppressor fields to make sure nobody dies. Weapons are limited so they hurt, but don't kill. And we've got a medic droid in case of serious injuries. Are you interested?

speaker: Player
text: Okay, I'll do it.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Good - new blood for the ring! But you need a nickname, like Ice or Deadeye or Twitch. Good nicknames make people bet more. Hmmm... what's a good name for you?

speaker: Ajuur
text: You're an off-worlder. You're new here, people won't recognize you... I know! From now on in the duel ring you'll be the Mysterious Stranger!

speaker: Player
text: The Mysterious Stranger. I like it.

speaker: Ajuur
text: The Mysterious Stranger is a perfect name for you. You've got no past, no history... it makes you seem like you have some big, dark secret. People like that. Makes them bet more.

speaker: Carth
text: This is for the best. We could use the credits from these duels, but using your real name is too risky. The Sith might have come across a crew manifest back on the Endar Spire.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You ready for a duel now? You want step into the ring right away? I'll set you up with Deadeye Duncan to start. I'll tell you the rules if you're ready.

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready for a duel.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You lost last time, but maybe this time fortune will smile on you. I'll give you a you rematch and a chance to redeem yourself.

speaker: Player
text: Let's do it.

speaker: Player
text: I've changed my mind.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You say you're ready, then you change your mind? Is this a joke to you? I don't have time for jokes - they don't make me any money! Come back when you'r ready to fight.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Yes! You fight and people bet and I make money! It's all good. Only one rule - nobody dies. Your opponent goes down, you don't finish them off. Death matches are illegal now.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You new at this, so I'll start you off easy. You get to fight Deadeye Duncan. Are you ready to go into the ring now?

speaker: Ajuur
text: You handled Duncan pretty well. I think you're ready to fight Gerlon Two-Fingers. Just remember - Gerlon uses blasters in the ring sometimes. You ready to step into the arena?

speaker: Ajuur
text: I think you're ready to go against Ice, human. She's tough, but so are you. There'll be lots action on this fight... a huge purse! You ready?

speaker: Ajuur
text: You've got a real talent for this game, Stranger. I think it's time you fought Marl. He's getting up there in years, but he's still very, very good. He used to be the duel champion.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You've beaten almost everyone, human. I think you ready to fight Twitch. Twitch might be crazy, but he's the best in the game. If you can beat him, you'll be the new champion.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not ready for the match yet.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Not ready? You look ready to me! Why are you here if you don't want to fight? You don't get paid if you don't fight! Come on... are you sure you don't want to step into the ring?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Questions? Bah - I don't have time for questions. They don't make me any credits! I want you to fight, not to ask questions. So, are you ready to step into the ring?

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Ajuur
text: I have big plans for you next match, tiny human. You come back when you want to fight.

speaker: Player
text: That's a terrible name!

speaker: Ajuur
text: Bah - what do you know about nicknames? I've been giving names for twenty years! Mysterious Stranger - that's your name now.

speaker: Player
text: My name is <FullName>. I think that sounds better than a nickname.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'll do it, but I want more than ten percent.

speaker: Ajuur
text: [Failure] Ha-ha-ha! You're joking, right? If I pay you more, then everyone wants more.

speaker: Ajuur
text: No, you get the same as all the others - ten percent. That's my final offer.

speaker: Player
text: Sorry, I'm not interested.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Don't pass this opportunity up, human. You fight for me and I'll make you rich. If you change your mind you come back and talk to me again.

speaker: Player
text: I might be interested - what's in this for me?

speaker: Player
text: I just want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Ajuur
text: Questions? Bah - questions don't make me money! But if you want to fight, it would could be very profitable for both of us. You interested?

speaker: Ajuur
text: Ah, Mysterious Stranger... I knew you'd be back. They all come back.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You fought well last time. People like you, Stranger. They bet lots on your last fight. They'll be more on your next fight. You get ten percent, same as always.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You want to step into the ring now? Are you ready to prove yourself against the best duelists on Taris?

speaker: Ajuur
text: You want to set up another fight, right? The ring is in your blood now, like a virus. You need to hear the cheers of the crowd; you need the rush of battle... you need to fight again.

speaker: Ajuur
text: My latest find; my new rising star. We make good team. I'm making money, you're getting famous... it's all good.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You're getting quite the reputation, Stranger. Everyone's excited, they all want to bet on your next match. I'm excited, too... more bets means more credits for me!

speaker: Ajuur
text: You've come for a duel, right? I can set up a match and we'll make some money, yes? You get ten percent of the purse if you win.

speaker: Ajuur
text: You're back, human. Does this mean you want to step into the duel ring? It could be very profitable for both of us. Ask around - everyone knows Ajuur treats his fighters well.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Greetings once again. I trust you have been discrete concerning the events at the Hrakert Rift.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Should the Selkath obtain proof of what occured down there the consequences for the Republic would be severe. For both our sakes, I hope you are smart enough to keep silent on this matter.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Truth be told, I am uncomfortable even with us being seen together. The rumors are already plentiful enough among the Selkath about the Republic's role in this.

speaker: Player
text: I have some questions about Ahto city.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: A beautiful place, Ahto city - a paradise on the water. But remember, within the city itself the Selkath have absolute authority. They are a tough race, but fair.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Obey the Selkath laws, keep the peace and you should encounter no problems. I assume you received a visitor guide to the city when you docked your ship.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I regret there is little I can tell you that is not in the visitor guide, my good Jedi. My duties rarely permit me to venture beyond the walls of the Republic Embassy.

speaker: Player
text: Why are your soldiers loading so much kolto?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Kolto is a precious resource - it's healing powers are near miraculous. During times of war, kolto becomes even more valuable.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: As long as we have the permits, we will continue to harvest kolto and ship it to our Republic soldiers battling against the Sith. Of course, the Sith enjoy the very same privileges.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: If there was some way we could gain an edge over the Sith in our kolto supply...

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But the Selkath are fiercely protective of their neutrality in this conflict. They do not want to grant either side an advantage.

speaker: Player
text: I am on a mission from the Jedi Council, perhaps you can help me with it.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Uh... of course, of course. I will do whatever I can. But I am only a simple diplomatic representative of the Republic. I doubt I can be of any use to the Jedi Council.

speaker: Player
text: I seek a Star Map, the remnant of an ancient and forgotten race.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: An ancient and forgotten race... and you think it may be here on Manaan? Hm...

speaker: Player
text: You know something?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Well... perhaps. But if you want to get information about that, you'll have to do something for me first.

speaker: Player
text: What do you want me to do?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We were using a submersible reconnaissance droid in the ocean surrounding Ahto City and it was... damaged. It took a data recording of the outside of the city before being driven off by the firaxan sharks.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But while it was returning to the surface it encountered difficulties and was disabled. Its automatic systems floated it to the surface, but we could not retrieve it in time.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Sith were applying subtle pressure to the Selkath authorities for some reason we have not determined, and were able to delay us long enough that they could retrieve the droid before we did.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The droid's data centers are heavily encrypted, so it will take the Sith several days, we believe, to get to its data. It was captured 12 hours ago. It is imperative that we get it back!

speaker: Player
text: Where is the droid?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: It is heavily guarded, we are sure, in the Sith Embassy here on Manaan. Since we have no remaining soldiers to spare, and certainly not our elite ones, we have no one capable of entering the Sith base and retrieving it.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: That is what we would ask you to do.

speaker: Player
text: How do I get in the Sith base?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: There are several leads we have been working on to get into the Sith base. Any of them should work for you, although it might be wise to concentrate your efforts on just one.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The first method that's possible is to help us interrogate a Sith prisoner we managed to catch after he tried to infiltrate our base. He is being held just inside our enclave.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We think he may be able to give us the passcode that the Sith give their informers to enter the base.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: He has proved most resilient so far...

speaker: Player
text: Interrogating the prisoner sounds good.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good. It's a logical place to start. But you should also hear about the other options available to you.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We managed to pick up a crate of blank Sith data cards the type they use for passcards.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The encryption system to unlock them is very difficult however, but if you are more skilled than our technicians, you may be able to gain access that way.

speaker: Player
text: Decrypting the passcard sounds good.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good. It is a very intelligent and skilled individual who can crack the matrices of a Sith encryption system.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But there is one last method you should know about in case all other options fail.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Sith have got the Selkath to give them exclusive use of one of the main hangar bays.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Visiting Sith masters use this bay to land, then take a speeder over the water to an external entrance to the Sith enclave.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The luckless spy we mentioned earlier had a passcard to that hangar on him. While it is surely well guarded, it may prove to be the most direct route. Here is the card.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Sith base itself is very heavily guarded. If they became aware of your presence, I fear you would be quickly outnumbered and killed.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Here is a passcard to get you inside our facility. You should find all you need to get started in there.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: You can choose whichever of the methods you want as long as you get in the base and get the data recording back. Which method do you think you would like to try first?

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll interrogate the prisoner.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good call, just make sure you don't push him too hard or we might lose him.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I wish you luck in your task. Should you retrieve the data recording from the droid, return it here to me and we can see about getting you that information.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll decrypt the passcard.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good choice. We've been working at that for a while, but it's been too difficult so far. Maybe you'll have better luck.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll raid the landing bay.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: You'll need luck for that one - odds are they have some pretty strong guards in there. But it's also the way most likely to succeed.

speaker: Player
text: Is there another way?

speaker: Player
text: Can I get back to you on this?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: If you want to find information about ancient ruins or your 'Star Map' or whatever it is, I think this is your best choice.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But you will have time to consider your options. And when you come to the only conclusion possible, I will be here to tell you how we can work together.

speaker: Player
text: I do not want to get involved.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not your errand runner!

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But you need our information, and I guarantee you that you will never be able to get it unless we have our secrecy guaranteed against the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: What is this recording?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: It's intelligence information about Sith activities on Manaan, as well as some oceanographic reports on the local marine life.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Come on, tell me.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: [Failure] No, no. You do what I want and maybe I can help you out. Until then: nothing.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You want to tell me.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: [Failure] Don't think you can manipulate me, Jedi! The Republic Diplomatic Corps has to deal with the Sith all the time, so we are very resistant to mental influence.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Your only real choice is to help me, so I can help you.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Then I shall wish you good day. On behalf of the Republic, I hope you enjoy your time here on Manaan.

speaker: Player
text: I'm investigating the Sunry case.
comment: Player has been appointed Sunry arbiter

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I don't know much about the facts of the case, but I find it hard to believe. I never met Sunry, but he's a hero of the Republic - not a murderer.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The so called evidence against him is an obvious frame up - it has to be! The Sith must have plotted Sunry's downfall to embarass and discredit the Republic!

speaker: Player
text: That's one possibility.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: If you want to solve this mess, I would focus on the Sith. That, or check out the murder scene at the hotel. Talk to the other guests - maybe they know something.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I regret I could not be of more assistance in your investigation. Is there anything else?

speaker: Player
text: I found this recording in your computers.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: You mean you sliced into our... That is a very serious crime! We could have you executed for treason if that information caused any harm!

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But... I may just be willing to overlook this transgression if you NEVER EVER TELL ANOTHER LIVING BEING ABOUT IT.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: And that is all I will ever tell you on the matter.

speaker: Player
text: Are you so sure it was the Sith?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Who else? Sunry's conviction will be a blow to Republic-Selkath relations. Who would benefit from this other than the Sith?

speaker: Player
text: Any chance the Republic is involved?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Republic? That makes no sense. Sunry has no enemies in the Republic, and his conviction will make all of our jobs more difficult.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe a bribe would ensure my silence.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Don't be foolish! If the Republic's role in this is discovered, I will be sure the blame rests on your shoulders as well. We share a secret - and we will share the consequences if the secret is revealed.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: For both our sakes you should move on. Our conversation attracts undue attention.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: You have returned! I was beginning to fear that you, too, might have been lost. Did you find out what had happened down there at the facility?

speaker: Player
text: The Selkath went insane.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Insane? What did they do? And why?

speaker: Player
text: They killed almost everyone on the Station.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: They killed... everyone? And the mercenaries we sent later? That is... horrible. What caused them to all go insane at once like that?

speaker: Player
text: Your construction woke something up.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Something was down there? Living in the Rift by the kolto?

speaker: Player
text: A gigantic firaxan shark that drove all the Selkath insane.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: That's... horrible. The entire operation wasted by a disaster we could never in a thousand years have foreseen.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: What has happened to the facility itself? Were there any survivors?

speaker: Player
text: A few scientists have survived.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Well, that is good to know. Good to know indeed. But... What has happened to the facility? Was it damaged?

speaker: Player
text: The harvesting machine was destroyed.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: No! That is terrible. That will set our work back years... *sigh* It may even cost us the war.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: While I am glad that you were able to solve our problems, the cost may have ended up being much too high.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But you have done your job and helped us in our time of need, and for that I thank you.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Oh, and did you end up finding your Star Map?

speaker: Player
text: Yes I did.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: As you can see, by helping us you helped yourself. Perhaps we can work together again in the future.

speaker: Player
text: None of your business!

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I'll assume that means yes. As you can see, by helping us you helped yourself. Perhaps we can work together in the future.

speaker: Player
text: The kolto seems to have been contaminated.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Contaminated? That's... That's much worse than I would ever have thought possible. It might have been better to lose the entire facility rather than damage the kolto supply.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: This must remain entirely secret. We cannot allow anyone to find out that we damaged the kolto production or we would be banned permanently from the planet.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We can only hope that the damage that was caused will go away in time.

speaker: Player
text: I haven't finished my investigation.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Please, continue your investigations and find out what happened to our facility.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: When you are ready to explore the Hrakert Rift, enter the Republic base. In the kolto packing room there is a door leading to the Republic submarines.
comment: after player has player has been given access to the submarines

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The sub will have a course to the Hrakert Scientific Research facility charted in. It will take you to the Hrakert Rift.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I wish you luck on your quest. Hopefully a Jedi can succeed where so many others have failed.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Ah, you're back. Have you decided to assist us and, at the same time, yourself?

speaker: Player
text: I'll get your recording for you.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good. I'm glad that you have come to accept the inevitable. Now we can really get down to work.

speaker: Player
text: Not right now.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Very well.

speaker: Player
text: Quit bothering me, imbecile.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: There is no need to be so rude.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Have you managed to retrieve the data from our droid in the Sith base?
comment: after acceptance, but before having data

speaker: Player
text: Yes, here it is.
comment: if the player has the data in his possession

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Excellent! It does not appear to have been tampered with, so the Sith did not manage to copy its contents yet.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: And now for your information... We are not supposed to speak of this, but since you are a Jedi, and we have exhausted all the other options, I think I can entrust you with this.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: As you know, the Republic is fighting for its very existence against the evil of the Sith Empire. As you also undoubtedly know, we are doing very poorly.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We need much in the way of supplies and material to stem the tide of battle and bring us victory.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Manaan is the sole source of kolto, the most powerful medical substance in the galaxy. Frankly, we need as much of it as we can get.

speaker: Player
text: What has the Republic done?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Selkath conservatives with their neutrality treaties seek to treat the Sith and the Republic equally. This includes kolto exports.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But a few more far-sighted Selkath see that if the Sith are ever allowed to win, the galaxy will be plunged into darkness and there would be nothing to stop them from taking Manaan anyway.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: So we made a deal...

speaker: Player
text: What sort of deal?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We recently began construction of a secret underground facility to harvest kolto directly at its source. We also hope to one day be able to synthesize it effectively.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Current techniques are insufficient for the task, so we must mine it for now. The amount we take would hardly be noticed, since most is lost naturally before it reaches the surface anyway.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We were nearing completion of the base when the digging teams reported some sort of obstruction... an ancient building or artifact. Possibly your 'Star Map'.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Transmissions from the base were cut off abruptly after that, and we haven't heard from the station since.

speaker: Player
text: Why have you not investigated?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: As you may have noticed, we are hiring a lot of mercenaries around here. Ostensibly they're to be shipped off-world to aid in our fight against the Sith, but they are really for another purpose.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: When we lost contact with the station in the Hrakert Rift, we sent our contingent of Republic soldiers down to investigate. None returned...

speaker: Roland Wann
text: We have tried hiring mercenaries and sending them down as well, but none of those expeditions have returned either.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The reason we really sent that droid underwater - and the reason we needed its data back so badly - was to find out what had happened to the Hrakert Rift station.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: But now that we have the data back, our operation is in no danger of exposure to the Sith. And now I must live up to my end of the bargain.

speaker: Player
text: How will I get down there?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I took the liberty of having a submarine prepared for your departure. Merely use this card to get past the door behind our kolto packing room and enter the sub therein.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: It has been programmed to take you down to the station, and also to take you back up should you need something.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I would send soldiers to assist you, but we have lost many of ours, and nearly exhausted the mercenary population of this planet. The soldiers we have are barely enough to keep this base secure!

speaker: Roland Wann
text: The Sith have also noted our interest and begun to bribe mercenaries away from us...

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Please, find out what happened to the facility. There may be some survivors left down there, perhaps even the head scientist - Kono Nolan.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Good luck in your efforts.

speaker: Player
text: What will you do for me?

speaker: Player
text: What happened down there?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: *Sigh* We don't know. We just don't know.

speaker: Player
text: What does this have to do with me?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Please, just let me explain.

speaker: Player
text: You violated the treaty?!?

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Shhh! Not so loud! Yes, it is a technical violation of the treaty, but it is sanctioned by elements of the Selkath government. We need only keep it hidden from the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: This is dangerous...

speaker: Roland Wann
text: I know... but to the senators, it seemed to outweigh the risks.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, yeah, get to the point.

speaker: Player
text: No I have not.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Time is a critical factor. We cannot allow the Sith to decode that data recording or our operations on Manaan would be compromised.

speaker: Roland Wann
text: Welcome to Manaan. I am Roland Wann. As the official representative of the Republic Embassy on this planet, I am here to help all citizens of the Republic should they require aid.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: The droid is actively engaged in its patrol route. You cannot reprogram it anymore.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: The droid is now active. It will attack any enemies that come in range.

speaker: Player
text: Optimize droid's weaponry. (<CUSTOM42> repair part(s))

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Success] The droid is now set for maximum firepower.

speaker: Player
text: Optimize droid's targeting systems. (<CUSTOM43> repair part(s))

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Success] The droid is now set for maximum accuracy.

speaker: Player
text: Activate droid's shields. (<CUSTOM44> repair part(s))

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Success] The droid's shields are now active.

speaker: Player
text: Engage droid in patrol mode. (<CUSTOM45> repair part(s))

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Success] Patrol mode engaged. Once you end this session the droid will begin patrol and destroy any enemies it encounters.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: WARNING: Once you end this session the droid's program will be locked in. You will not be able to modifiy the droid anymore.

speaker: Player
text: Leave it alone.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: The droid engages its patrol mode and moves off to carry out your programmed instructions.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Failure] You do not have enough repair parts.

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: This is an old, broken down bartender droid. It has been deactivated in preparation for disposal.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid. (1 repair part)

speaker: Disabled Sentry
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Wookiees settle down a lot once they're caged.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: You know, every Czerka outpost is expected to double the number of Wookiees they take in the next year.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Hey, we just got word that shipments will be increasing. This Chuundar really knows how to do business.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Hey, business is better than ever. These animals will pay our way for years.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: I hear the Wookiees seem to be cooperating even more than usual now. Czerka can pretty much do whatever it wants.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: I heard the Wookiee leader is saying we can increase the number of slaves we take. I think Czerka will be here a long time.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: You know, I hear Czerka has negotiated to increase its presence here by six more outposts.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Hey! Don't get too close to the cages. Even these cowed Wookiees will take your arm off if they get the chance.

speaker: Czerka Guard
text: Don't bother me, now. I've got twice as many Wookiees to process as usual.

speaker: Mechanic
text: Still around the starport, I see. Heading off, soon?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Mechanic
text: Oh, nobody special. I just do the routine maintenance work for the ships that come in. I used to see the Hawk here all the time.

speaker: Player
text: How do you know about the Ebon Hawk?

speaker: Mechanic
text: Oh, I've seen this little ship before plenty of times. Used to make runs for the Exchange, didn't it? Korriban's nice and remote, the kind of place the Exchange likes.

speaker: Mission
text: I knew we'd run into some of Davik's old associates sooner or later. No matter where you go somebody's working for the Exchange!

speaker: Mechanic
text: You don't need to worry about me saying anything. I don't give a whit what you do with your ship. Smuggling's what the Hawk was made for, though.

speaker: Player
text: Can I ask you some questions?

speaker: Mechanic
text: You sure can.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about Korriban?

speaker: Mechanic
text: Not much. It's a pretty barren planet, to tell the truth. Not of much interest to anyone. Unless you're a Sith, I guess... they seem to think this place is something special.

speaker: Player
text: Why do the Sith think Korriban is special?

speaker: Mechanic
text: Probably all them ruins they found on the surface. That's the reason they built their academy here, I guess, to dig all them ruins up.

speaker: Player
text: There's a Sith academy here?

speaker: Mechanic
text: There's people that come here from all over Sith space to try and join the academy. Most of them die, I hear. Pretty gruesome business, that.

speaker: Player
text: How does someone get to the ruins?

speaker: Mechanic
text: You don't. Not unless you're a Sith in the academy. They're the only ones allowed on the surface. They pay Czerka to ship things in and out, I guess, but that's all closely monitored.

speaker: Player
text: So how does someone get into the academy?

speaker: Mechanic
text: I don't know. There's all kinds of hopefuls in the colony trying to get in... why don't you ask one of them?

speaker: Player
text: Have you ever heard of a Star Map?

speaker: Mechanic
text: A Star Map? You mean like a navigation chart?

speaker: Player
text: Yes, but much older. Perhaps in the ruins?

speaker: Mechanic
text: If them Sith found a Star Map in those ruins, nobody's ever mentioned it.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Sith Academy?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know how to reach the ruins on the surface?

speaker: Player
text: Thanks, I'll be going.

speaker: Mechanic
text: Yep. Take care, now.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, but much older. Are there ruins on Korriban?

speaker: Mechanic
text: There's a whole bunch of old Sith ruins up on the surface of the planet. That's why they put one of their academies here, to dig them all up.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go.

speaker: Mechanic
text: Nice to see the Hawk's still in one piece. Beauty of a ship, that.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: This job is not fair trade.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: You were not here first, yet Jawas serve.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Better here than with People of Sand.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Jawas will dig the sand for you one day.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: Move to the sides, out of serving way.

speaker: Jawa Server
text: [Unintelligible]
comment: Standard Jawa Utinni exclamation, or the equivalent of a Jawa swear.

speaker: Carth
text: The Star Forge... I've never seen anything like it.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm transmitting these coordinates to Admiral Dodonna.  Maybe a quick strike by the Republic can cripple the Sith fleet.

speaker: Carth
text: Message is away. Now we can just wait for the Republic to show up. We should be safe here - we're outside their sensor range.

speaker: WookieF
text: What's that?

speaker: Carth
text: A small vanguard of Sith fighters, coming in hard!  Someone needs to get on those gun turrets. ## Take those fighters out before they report our position to the main fleet!

speaker: Carth
text: ALARM

speaker: The Storyteller
text: [Compared to the warriors that you have encountered, the Sand People Storyteller is relatively calm in his movements and speech, but he still regards you coldly.]

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: He identifies himself as the Storyteller, master. He has been told of your warrior skills and will speak the history to you.

speaker: Player
text: I am honored. Ask him what he records.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: [Unintelligible]

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: There is only one accepted history, passed orally to each successive generation.

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: A book or datapad can be taken away, cheapening the value of what it contains. To commit it to paper or storage is to remove it from the people.

speaker: Player
text: Continue the history from where we left off.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask questions about what I've heard.

speaker: HK47
text: Cautionary: Remember my warning, master. They may consider certain questions to be "speaking the words in error," a blasphemy they would attempt to kill you for.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about the outsiders.

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: They appear to hate humanity with a passion only rivaled by their hatred of the Builders. For some reason, you resemble what they once were.

speaker: HK47
text: Perhaps there is a lingering fear that you are their tainted selves returning from exile among the stars.

speaker: Player
text: Is it a physical or societal similarity?

speaker: HK47
text: Cautionary: Master, if you mean to suggest that humanity is ancestrally linked to ancient Tatooine, you will strain his belief system to its pitiful meat-bag maximum.

speaker: Player
text: Just pose the question.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about a different part of the history.

speaker: HK47
text: Cautionary: I should warn you, master, that any questioning of their interpretation may be seen as trying to change the meaning of what was said.

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: They may consider this to be "speaking the words in error," a blasphemy they would attempt to kill you for.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about the long walk.

speaker: HK47
text: Impatience: Master, I refuse to inconvenience you with this. He spouted names of petty tribal fights in deserts so distant they might as well be across the galaxy.

speaker: HK47
text: Really, master, I'm sure it's important to him, but it has nothing of value that you could ever put to use.

speaker: Player
text: We'll have to discuss this impudence, HK-47.

speaker: HK47
text: Agreement: Of course, master. Just no more of their inane wandering.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about the great war.

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: The occupying force suffered some sort of species-wide plague that lowered their numbers over time. His people used this extended weakness to sabotage their larger ships.

speaker: HK47
text: The response of the Builders appears to have been to lay waste to the entire surface of Tatooine.

speaker: Player
text: How could they repel such a powerful species?

speaker: HK47
text: Doubting: They didn't, master. They struck a blow, but the Storyteller only believes they won because the Builders were gone when they emerged from their caves.

speaker: HK47
text: That does not mean they defeated anyone. It seems clear that the Builders simply sterilized their problem and left. The enemy judged them not worthy to fight.

speaker: Player
text: Ask him if that is a possibility.

speaker: HK47
text: Cautionary: Master, this line of questioning may be interpreted as attempting to change the story. He may react poorly.

speaker: Player
text: Just do it.

speaker: Player
text: What kind of weapon could do so much damage?

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: I may not have properly conveyed how long they fought with the Builders. Given time, any number of armaments could destroy a world.

speaker: HK47
text: Hypothesis: Perhaps this is another distortion. Their climate may have begun to fail due to their unrestrained development even before the Builders arrived.

speaker: HK47
text: Looking back thousands of years later, such a shift could easily be attributed to the much-hated conquerors.

speaker: Player
text: Suggest that possibility to him.

speaker: Player
text: How could they survive such an attack?

speaker: HK47
text: Hypothesis: If his people were moving away from technology for a long time under the Builders, they may have had extensive cave systems that could grant shelter.

speaker: HK47
text: I would also suggest that, given the evidence of the massive shift in the nature of their society, most of them did not survive.

speaker: Player
text: Let's return to my other questions.

speaker: HK47
text: Obedient: I will ask whatever you wish, master.

speaker: Player
text: Begin the history.

speaker: Player
text: Oral histories are often inaccurate.

speaker: Player
text: I'll return later.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about the time of enslavement.

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: I believe they were occupied by this technologically superior species for a substantial period. Stripping an entire planet of useable resources would have taken generations.

speaker: Player
text: How many of his people were taken off-world?

speaker: Player
text: Why would the invaders have done this?

speaker: HK47
text: Obvious: The same reason Czerka Corporation is attempting it now. Expanding empires need tremendous amounts of resources.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask something about the ancient times.

speaker: HK47
text: Clarification: It would appear that they once had a thriving technologically advanced society, but were wiped out by a much more sophisticated alien species.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything in the galactic record that would verify this?

speaker: HK47
text: Negative: I am no library, but since there is no Republic record of this planet having sentient life before Czerka colonization, I doubt you will find such evidence.

speaker: Player
text: Ask him if these "Builders" resemble any modern species.

speaker: Player
text: Can he clarify how long ago Tatooine was "green with life"?

speaker: HK47
text: Doubting: I don't believe he can, master. Even if their stories are exact and unchanged, it is likely they were first told thousands of years after these events occured.

speaker: HK47
text: This has become very much like a creation myth for his people. There is no date; it simply was.

speaker: Player
text: What topics can I choose from?

speaker: Player
text: He will speak it? They don't write it down?

speaker: Player
text: What good will these histories be to me?

speaker: The Storyteller
text: [You have no chance of understanding him without HK-47 present. He senses this and dismisses you, not wanting to waste his time.]

speaker: The Storyteller
text: [The Sand People Storyteller regards you as he did before; as an outsider. He is obviously used to being the most important figure in the tribe.]

speaker: HK47
text: Translation: The Storyteller waits for your questions, master.

speaker: Freyyr
text: We have done it... I am saddened that it had to come to this, but I couldn't let it continue.
comment: Initial after Chuundar dead. Freyyr initiates.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Zaalbar, my son. I am truly sorry. You have suffered a great shame. I was blind. I have no excuse.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I can forgive, father. I have learned a lot over the years.

speaker: Player
text: I have a few questions about Kashyyyk, Freyyr.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Could they wait? I will answer what I can later, but we need to settle our current business. There is much that needs to be done.

speaker: Player
text: What will you do about the slavers?

speaker: Freyyr
text: We will fight them. It will be difficult, but I swear they won't take another one of my people without bloodshed.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I'll send quick-climbers to other villages and try to rally a defense. We must guard against this ever happening again.

speaker: Freyyr
text: You will be the last outsider welcome here for a very long time. That is a change for the better, I think.

speaker: Player
text: What will you do now, Zaalbar?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Returning home has lifted a great weight from my mind... but it has been painful as well.

speaker: Freyyr
text: You have a place by my side, Zaalbar. I would be honored if you would take it.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I... I can't. Not yet. I'm just getting used to being free... and not just from the slavers.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: And I have a life-debt. Now that my life is truly my own again, honoring that agreement is all the more important.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Listen to my son! His insight humbles me. Take that good judgment with you and all the planets will come to revere Wookiee wisdom.

speaker: Player
text: I think it's time I was leaving.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Perhaps, but before you go, <FullName>, I must see to your reward. You have done us a great service. Kashyyyk will remember you well past your lifetime.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Because of you, I am reinstated as Chieftain. We will return to the old ways, when honor and trust of kin ruled above all else.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I'm not sure there is a reward that accurately reflects the value of what you have done. Our world is changed because of you.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have a request, father. I have thought about it a great deal. I would like Bacca's Sword.

speaker: Player
text: That would be fitting, I think.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Well... That is quite a request. I am tempted to say no but... perhaps I should consider it an investment.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Zaalbar, do you understand what this will mean? It is the legacy of our people, held by chieftains... and future chieftains.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I understand. I want this, father. I'll bring it back one day.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I have no doubt. Let the two halves of the blade be made one. My son shall hold Bacca's Sword.
comment: Give player Bacca's sword. Boot them out to the main village area. They can re-enter if they want.

speaker: Player
text: Zaalbar, shut up. I want some credits.

speaker: Mission
text: Look, Big Z may owe you a life-debt but you've got to cut him some slack!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have gone through a lot here. I don't think it's too much to ask that I choose the reward.

speaker: Jolee
text: Now, you just close your hole, child. It's a shock, I'm sure, but this isn't about you.

speaker: Juhani
text: You should not be so self-serving, lest you fall to the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Enough. I want my reward and then I'm leaving.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I have not forgotten you, <FullName>. You don't need to make demands. You have done us a great service. Kashyyyk will remember you well past your lifetime.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I believe you have taken advantage of my good will. If you wish to talk, bring my son with you. I will speak out of respect for him, not you.
comment: After player has pissed off Freyyr, Zaalbar NOT in party.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Welcome back, <FullName>. Much is happening, but I can spare a moment. Our fight against the slavers will be a long one.
comment: Selected after Chuundar dead and player has gone through initial dialogue. Special: Do not display if player has pissed off Freyyr and Zaalbar is NOT in the party.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Greetings father. It is good to see you again.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask about the reward you gave.
comment: Tricky thing: Do not display this question if: It is set to 1 AND Zaalbar is in the party (Player asked the question and Zaalbar took offense, preventing him from asking again) OR It is set to 2 (Player asked the question to it's rude conclusion.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Yes, Bacca's Sword. It promises a great future for my people in my son's hands.

speaker: Player
text: Yes, sure, but I've got bills to pay.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: What? Wait, I won't have you demean the gift of Bacca's Sword by asking for money as well.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I mean it, I don't want to hear you ask my father about this again.
comment: Set the state of this question to 1, meaning that it will not display while it is set to 1 AND Zaalbar is in the party. Check is made on the "I want to ask about the reward you gave.' question.

speaker: Player
text: I saw a strange computer in the Shadowlands.
comment: Player HAS spoken to the computer Do not display if the player has asked the second part of this question, the "It's older than the forest. It created the trees." line.

speaker: Freyyr
text: Yes, I remember seeing it during my exile. It wouldn't do much for me. I imagine it's some Czerka cast-off.

speaker: Player
text: It's older than the forest. It created the trees.
comment: Set local so the "I encountered a strange computer in the Shadowlands." question cannot be asked again.

speaker: Freyyr
text: You are saying nonsense. I'm not sure why you have made this jest but I would ask that you stop.

speaker: Freyyr
text: These are difficult times. I don't want you threatening our traditions while I am trying to unite my people under them.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I will investigate your claims at a more appropriate time. Until then, don't speak of this again.

speaker: Player
text: I encountered some Mandalorian hunters in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Freyyr
text: I am surprised that such a thing escaped my attention. Was their camouflage so great, or was I simply too struck by grief to see anything?

speaker: Freyyr
text: If more are encountered, we will deal with them in short order. My people will never be weak again.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.
comment: Player has not talked to the Computer

speaker: Freyyr
text: I have no knowledge of anything like that. Wait... there was something...

speaker: Freyyr
text: In my exile I encountered a strange computer in the depths of the Shadowlands. I thought it was a Czerka cast-off.

speaker: Freyyr

speaker: Dorak
text: As a chronicler of the Academy here on Dantooine, I feel it is my duty to share the history of our Order with the newly initiated. Unfortunately, our recent history is one of tragedy and bloodshed.

speaker: Dorak
text: The Mandalorian Wars, the fall of Revan and Malak, the rise of the Sith: there are important lessons to be learned from these events if we do not wish to repeat the mistakes of our past.

speaker: Player
text: I am eager to learn, Master Dorak.

speaker: Dorak
text: Of course I could not tell you the entire history of our Order; the Jedi have existed for thousands upon thousands of years. We are as old as the Republic itself.

speaker: Dorak
text: Instead, I will begin forty years ago with the war of Exar Kun. Like Malak and Revan, Exar Kun was a Jedi who fell to the dark side and led an army against the Jedi and the Republic.

speaker: Dorak
text: Exar Kun was defeated, but the war left both the Republic and our own Order severely weakened. For twenty years we struggled to rebuild, trying to erase the scars of the terrible conflict.

speaker: Player
text: What does this have to do with Revan and Malak?

speaker: Dorak
text: All things in time. You shall learn that history is an intricate weaving of many events. No one thing can be understood without the proper context.

speaker: Dorak
text: Twenty years ago the Mandalorians, aware the Republic was in a weakened state, began conquering small worlds on the Outer Rim. They were careful to choose only planets outside the Republic's jurisdiction.

speaker: Dorak
text: After much debate, the Senate chose not to intervene. As long as the Mandalorians avoided planets that were members of the Republic itself, there would be no retaliation.

speaker: Player
text: That sounds like a big mistake.

speaker: Dorak
text: Well, you can hardly blame the Republic. The memory of war was fresh in everyone's mind, nobody was eager to relive the horrors in a campaign against the Mandalorians. But in the end it was unavoidable.

speaker: Dorak
text: The Mandalorians stockpiled resources from their conquered worlds, preparing for a massive assault. Seven years ago they launched a simultaneous attack in three separate sectors of Republic space.

speaker: Dorak
text: The Senate had no choice but to retaliate with the entire Republic fleet. The Mandalorian Wars had begun.

speaker: Player
text: Did the Jedi join in?

speaker: Dorak
text: The Republic petitioned the Jedi Council for aid, but there were many factors to consider before we allowed ourselves to be drawn into another conflict so soon after the war with Exar Kun.

speaker: Dorak
text: While the Jedi Council preached patience, there were many among our Order who were eager for us to join the battle. Two young Knights in particular demanded immediate action: Revan and Malak.

speaker: Dorak
text: They rallied many of the Jedi to their cause and, against the wishes of their Masters, joined the Republic fleet battling the Mandalorians.

speaker: Dorak
text: Revan was a brilliant military leader, and the Republic fleet began to win victory after victory. Four years ago the Mandalorians surrendered unconditionally.

speaker: Player
text: So Revan did the right thing.

speaker: Dorak
text: No one is denying that Revan was one of the keys to defeating the Mandalorians... but something happened out there on the Outer Rim.

speaker: Dorak
text: Instead of returning after the war's end, the ships under Revan's command went deep into unexplored space. They claimed to be searching for the last remnants of the Mandalorian fleet.

speaker: Dorak
text: All contact was lost. For many months it was assumed some great disaster had befallen the entire fleet. Everyone thought they were dead.

speaker: Dorak
text: There were unsubstantiated rumors of Revan and Malak being seen on a number of different planets during these months - scattered sightings that were never confirmed.

speaker: Player
text: Where did they disappear to?

speaker: Dorak
text: Perhaps they simply went far beyond the edges of Republic space. Maybe they found previously undiscovered hyperspace routes to the ends of the galaxy. Nobody knows for certain.

speaker: Dorak
text: Three years ago, Revan and Malak returned at the head of a massive invasion fleet. Revan had assumed the title of Sith Lord; the hero had become a conqueror.

speaker: Player
text: Where did Revan get the ships for the Sith fleet?

speaker: Dorak
text: Some of the ships in the Sith fleet are those that were under Revan's command during the Mandalorian Wars. But many more are of an alien design we have never seen before.

speaker: Dorak
text: The source of this massive fleet is one of the many things about the Sith we cannot explain. It seems impossible to have created it in such a short time, yet we cannot deny its existence.

speaker: Dorak
text: The source of the Sith soldiers is, unfortunately, much easier to understand. Initially the bulk of the force were former Republic soldiers who had served under Revan.

speaker: Dorak
text: With each conquest thousands more flocked to join the invaders, swelling their numbers. Even many of our own Order have betrayed us, lured by Sith promises of riches and power.

speaker: Player
text: So what happened next?

speaker: Dorak
text: For two years the Sith were all but invincible. Fortunately, Bastila and her Battle Meditation allowed the Republic to win a few key victories and kept the Sith from total triumph.

speaker: Dorak
text: In desperation we set a trap for the Dark Lord. Bastila was with the strike team that tried to capture Revan, as you probably know. She was there at Revan's end.

speaker: Dorak
text: That was nearly a year ago, but things have not improved. Malak has stepped in and assumed the mantle of Dark Lord for himself, though he is far from Revan's equal in strategy or tactics.

speaker: Dorak
text: Still, his fleet continues to grow in both ships and soldiers. If we do not find some way to stop the Sith soon, Malak will overwhelm us with sheer numbers.

text: You will have to disable the energy shield around this temple before we can leave. There is a computer here on the Temple summit that has access to the power generators.

text: I've been watching you. I've seen how you have resisted great temptations and continue to walk the path of the light side. Very commendable.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Greetings, fellow sentient! I notice that you are not heavily armed... or at least, not heavily armed, enough!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Please allow my self to introduce myself. I am Adum, a simple merchant with a much noble purpose!

speaker: Player
text: Purpose?

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Yes! Purpose!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: The settlers and noble humans of Dantooine have been plagued by kath hounds, raiders and other fearsome troubles of late.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: It is much, much too sad to see these things happen to such people as this. Therefore, I have made this my mission to be!

speaker: Player
text: Er.. mission?

speaker: Adum Larp
text: To overcome their troubles, they must be able to defend themselves. Therefore, I shall offer the highest of quality of weapons at the lowest of low of prices for them!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: I am here, offering you much in the way of weaponry at low, low prices! How can any sentient pass up such a bargain? They cannot!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Weaponry it is, and weaponry I have! What is it you would like from me this fine day?

speaker: Player
text: Let me see what you're selling.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Yes, yes! Here is the best you can find anywhere on this world!

speaker: Player
text: Do you happen to have any maps of the area?

text: Maps? Why yes, yes I have.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: What areas would you like a map to? I am afraid I do not have all areas of maps, though.

speaker: Player
text: I would like a map to this area.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Maps for little, maps for cheap! Only 2 credits for this fine, fine map.

speaker: Player
text: I'll take it.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Here then, is that map I have. Is there anything else you would like?

speaker: Player
text: I would like to ask you some questions.

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Of course I shall endeavor to be of service to whatever endeavor you are on. What is it you wish to ask?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know of the Mandalorian raiders?

speaker: Adum Larp
text: A plague on this world... a plague that must be cleansed with fire!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Fire generated from a sterling example of weaponcraft such as this fine Blaster Rifle right here. Can't do better, you know!

text: Um... yeah, hold it. I'd like to ask something else.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to take a closer look at your weapons.

speaker: Player

speaker: Adum Larp
text: Is there something else you wish to ask?

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the kath hounds?

text: Fearsome beasts! Predators! A danger that the settlers of this world must constantly face and do battle with!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: And what better way to battle them than with this handy Blaster Pistol! Crafted from the finest, sturdiest materials, it can stop a kath hound dead in its tracks at fifty paces!

speaker: Adum Larp
text: I am sorry, but I have not been on this world long. I am not familiar with any specific locales in this area.
