speaker: Bastila
text: Revan - I knew you'd come for me. Malak thought you might be afraid to enter the Temple again, but he doesn't know you like I do. Not anymore. Not since you've changed.

speaker: Juhani
text: Quickly, Bastila - come with us! We have to escape before Malak arrives!

speaker: Bastila
text: Escape? You don't understand. I have sworn allegiance to Lord Malak and the Sith; I am no longer a pawn of the Jedi Council.

speaker: Player
text: No, Bastila! Don't go over to the dark side!

speaker: Bastila
text: You say that as if the dark side is some terrible entity. The Jedi Council has brainwashed you like all the others. Like they once did with me.

speaker: Bastila
text: They speak of the dark side as if it something to be feared. But in reality their only goal is to manipulate those who are strong in the Force. The fear of the dark side is a tool to maintain control.

speaker: Bastila
text: Why do you think the Jedi forbid you and Malak from joining the Mandalorian Wars? They knew you would realize your true potential and break free of their domination.

speaker: Bastila
text: Malak has shown me how the Jedi Council have been using me the same way they once tried to use you. They've been holding me back because they knew one day I would surpass them all.

speaker: Player
text: No - I don't believe it! How could you betray us like this, Bastila?

speaker: Bastila
text: I resisted at first. I endured the Sith torments with the passionless serenity of a true Jedi, emptying my mind. But after a week of endless tortures I finally saw the truth.

speaker: Bastila
text: Malak forced me to acknowledge my anger and pain. He showed me the liberating power of these emotions. Then he made me see how the Jedi Council has denied me what is mine by right!

speaker: Bastila
text: The Jedi Council gladly used my Battle Meditation in their wars, but they still treated me like a child - like an inferior. They were jealous of my power... of what I could become!

speaker: Bastila
text: They wanted me to bow and call them Master and follow their Code and obey their every order. But all the while they were exploiting my Battle Meditation for their own use!

speaker: Player
text: Don't do this, Bastila! Fight it! I'll help you!

speaker: Bastila
text: You are a sad little fool. You speak as if I were the same Bastila that you've known all along. But freed from the control of the Jedi Council I've become much, much more.

speaker: Bastila
text: I almost wish you could see things as I do now. I wish you could join me and taste true power once again. Sadly, I doubt you are even capable any longer.

speaker: Bastila
text: With the power of the Star Forge Malak will destroy the Republic and conquer the galaxy. And I will be the apprentice at his side - after I prove my worth by killing you!

speaker: Player
text: I like this side of you, Bastila. Now we can truly be together.

speaker: Bastila
text: You think so, do you? You style yourself the Master of the Sith that you once were? To think I once envied you your passion, your power.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be lured in by these Sith lies, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: Lies? You are the one living a lie, Revan. The Jedi Council made you into something you are not; they programmed you to be their slave.

speaker: Bastila
text: You used to be Revan, Master of the Sith, but no longer. You are simply a pawn of the Jedi Council and the Republic they serve... like I was until Malak freed me from their shackles!

speaker: Bastila
text: A pity the power you once had is so diluted in you. You could have been strong as I am now... stronger, even. But that will never happen, now.

speaker: Player
text: I am Revan, the Dark Lord! Bow down to me, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: If you've fallen under Malak's control you must die!

speaker: Player
text: It's not too late, Bastila! You can still turn away from the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: It didn't take long to convert you, did it? I always knew you were weak!

speaker: Player
text: A pawn of the Jedi Council? What are you talking about?

speaker: Bastila
text: Surely you know what I mean, Revan. Look at what the Council did to you; they turned you into their puppet. The same thing they do to all who are truly strong in the Force.

speaker: Jolee
text: Come on, Bastila. We have to escape before Malak shows up!

speaker: Bastila
text: You are stronger than I would have thought possible, after what the Jedi Council did to you. Seems that Malak was wrong - the power of the dark side is not lost to you after all, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: I draw my power from the light now, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: You can deny what you are, Revan, but you are only fooling yourself. I know the truth. I have seen the shadows inside your mind.

speaker: Bastila
text: Remember: I was there when you nearly died in the trap set by the Jedi Council. I used the Force to preserve your life, Revan. We are forever linked by my actions on that bridge!

speaker: Player
text: That is how I know you will come back to the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: These are not your true feelings, Revan. You are speaking as a tool of the Jedi Council - as I once did. But now I see how the Jedi used us both!

speaker: Bastila
text: The Council tried to exploit the bond between us. They hoped I would draw out your memories to lead them to the Star Forge. We were slaves to their will - like all who follow the Jedi Code!

speaker: Bastila
text: But in our shared visions of the Star Maps I also felt the so called taint within you. I resisted it at first, but now I embrace the power of the dark side - your dark side!

speaker: Player
text: Learn from my mistakes. It is not too late to come back to the light!

speaker: Bastila
text: Mistakes? No, Revan - the only mistake you are making is the one you are making now! You deny yourself the power that is yours by right! Only now do I realize how strong you are.

speaker: Bastila
text: You deserve to be the true Master of the Sith, not Malak. I see this now. Together we can destroy your old apprentice. Join with me and reclaim your lost identity!

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore. I don't even remember those days.

speaker: Bastila
text: Your mind was too badly damaged to ever fully restore your memories, Revan. But your power, your strength of will, the essence of who and what you are: these things still remain!

speaker: Bastila
text: Once long ago you defied the Jedi Council, freeing yourself from their control. You claimed your rightful title of Dark Lord of the Sith. Together we can defeat Malak and take back what is yours!

speaker: Player
text: Please, Bastila... if you feel anything for me, you won't do this!

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I don't. The only Revan I could respect is one who would break free of the Council's slavery. One who would grasp the power that lies before him... not the weak fool I see.

speaker: Juhani
text: Bastila, it is not too late for you to be saved. The teachings of the Jedi can lead you from the dark side back into the light and a true understanding of the Force.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are beneath my contempt, Juhani. When you felt the power of the dark side you fled to a cave like some cowering animal! You know nothing of the Force or its true potential!

speaker: Bastila
text: But you, Revan - the power of the dark side is yours to command! You can use it to destroy Malak! With my help you could rule over the entire galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to rule the galaxy. I want you to return to the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are a pathetic fool, Revan! Together we could have defeated Malak and ruled over an Empire, but now I will be at Lord Malak's side instead!

speaker: Bastila
text: You will be crushed with the Republic and all the fools who bow down to the Jedi Council! No one can stand against the power of the Star Forge and the Sith fleet!

speaker: Player
text: The Dark Lord Revan is dead. I am a servant of the light now.

speaker: Player
text: Yes! Together we can rule the galaxy!

speaker: Jolee
text: Listen to me... the dark side leads to death and destruction. I've seen the horrors the Sith have unleashed on the galaxy. Turn away from this path.

speaker: Bastila
text: Shut up, old man. Your time is over! The age of the Jedi and the Republic is no more! This is the age of Darth Revan and the Sith!

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't do this, kid. I don't want to, but I'll fight you if I have to. Even if it costs me my life.

speaker: Player
text: I am the Lord of the Sith! Bow down before me!

speaker: Juhani
text: A true Jedi will never bow down to the Sith. If this is your decision I have no choice but to do battle against you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Kill her! Rend her flesh! Show her the fate of all who dare stand against us! Embrace the power of the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: No, I will not kill my friend. I reject the power of the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Death to the Jedi!

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes! The sacrificial blood will consecrate this ancient temple in the name of the Sith! With the death of the Jedi the rebirth of Darth Revan will be complete!

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm a Jedi... I'll never bow down to the Sith. If you go through with this I have no choice but to do battle against you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Kill him! Grind his old bones to dust! Show him the fate of all who dare stand against us! Embrace the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: Then you must die!

speaker: Player
text: You... you're right. I cannot do this. I reject the dark side!

speaker: Juhani
text: No! Do not walk down this path... it can only lead to destruction! I know of what I speak!

speaker: Bastila
text: Shut up, Juhani! You know nothing of the dark side's true potential! When you felt its touch you fled to a cave and cowered in terror!

speaker: Juhani
text: I have no wish to fight you and Bastila, but if you choose to walk down this path you know I must stand against you... even at the cost of my life.

speaker: Player
text: How do I know you won't betray me?

speaker: Bastila
text: I need deny my passions no longer, Revan. I would stand by your side gladly, as your lover and apprentice!

speaker: Bastila
text: I swore allegiance to Malak only because I thought you had lost the power you had once wielded. But this... this would be much better.

speaker: Bastila
text: I would be utterly yours, master! Together we would destroy Malak and you would reclaim the mantle of Dark Lord!

speaker: Player
text: No, I... don't want you like this. I want the woman I knew.

speaker: Player
text: Turn away from this path, Bastila. The dark side leads only to destruction.

speaker: Jolee
text: It's not to late for you, Bastila. The dark side is evil but it isn't all powerful. You can still fight against it. Don't let it consume you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are beneath my contempt, old man! You hid like a coward for decades on Kashyyyk! You know nothing about the true potential of the Force!

speaker: Player
text: I don't trust you. I think I'll just kill you instead!

speaker: Juhani
text: No! This is the way of the dark side! Do not give in to the anger and hatred!

speaker: Jolee
text: No! Don't give into your anger. Remain calm, remain focused. Don't let her twist your mind like this!

speaker: Bastila
text: It is your power that will keep me as your loyal apprentice, Revan. I swore allegiance to Malak only because I thought you had lost the power you once wielded.

speaker: Bastila
text: But you have proven yourself in our battle; I see you possess the strength to destroy Malak and reclaim the mantle of Dark Lord. Now I see you will make a worthy Sith Master.

speaker: Player
text: How can I reclaim my identity if I can't even remember it?

speaker: Player
text: No! This isn't the Bastila I knew!

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course not! I have been reborn in the wake of destiny... *your* destiny! The power of the dark side is yours by right!

speaker: Player
text: What are you saying, Bastila?

speaker: Player
text: If I am so powerful, then why do you serve another master?

speaker: Player
text: Then why don't we join our power together, as it was meant to be?

speaker: Player
text: There is no link between us, Bastila! Not anymore!

speaker: Bastila
text: Our bond is not easily broken, Revan. Even when your mind was destroyed and reprogrammed with a new identity the bond between us endured.

speaker: Player
text: We are linked by more than just a bond, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: Do not mistake the power of the Force for love, Revan. It does not exist. Power is what forged our bond, and power is what made us both tools of the Jedi Council!

speaker: Player
text: Don't call me that. I'm not Revan anymore. I'm <FullName> now.

speaker: Player
text: Now you see the power of the true Dark Lord!

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, Revan! I was there when you almost died in the trap set by the Jedi Council; I used the Force to preserve your life. We are forever linked by my actions on that bridge.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Council tried to exploit our bond. They hoped your memories would lead me to the Star Forge. But in our shared visions of the Star Maps I also tasted the power of the taint within you!

speaker: Maintenance Droid
text: Beep beep beep-oop!

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: You have returned at last, Revan. I was beginning to wonder what had happened to you in the Temple.

speaker: Player
text: You know me?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We had met previously when last you entered our enclave, many years ago. You inquired as to my research then as well.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: You came here and gained access to the Temple, and were never heard from again. Some thought you might have betrayed us to the others, but they were never able to penetrate our defenses.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: But if you will help us now, then the time taken is nothing. Is there anything else you require?

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: What am I doing? You mean, the purpose of my research here?

speaker: Player
text: What is your research?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: As you may have heard from our historians, in our distant past we melded technology and the Force to create truly wondrous effects.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We guided ships across the galaxy using our power, and incorporated its use into all aspects of our society.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: But... something happened somewhere.

speaker: Player
text: What happened?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: There are a variety of theories on what happened. Perhaps we became immune to the effects of the Force from overuse. Perhaps our breeding habits rendered our species insensitive to it over time. None truly know.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: The only discernable result was that we could no longer command the Force as we had. Its power had escaped us.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: With its loss, our technologies could no longer hold us as far above the subjugated races we ruled, and our empire began to crumble. The races we subjugated rose up, plagues swept our worlds... we could do nothing against all these calamities.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: In the end, only the members of our race left here, on our homeworld, survived.

speaker: Player
text: So what is your research then?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Every once in a while, there is an individual born who has an affinity for the Force. Maybe not the ability to use it directly, but at least the ability to remain open to it.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: I believe this is a sign that whatever genes our species had that gave us the ability to use the Force are not completely gone. Perhaps when the ancestors of the current tribes fled beneath the surface, some retained this trait.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We have been working for years to isolate this gene in an attempt to resurrect it in our species as well.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We of the Elders do not have Force sensitivity ourselves, but by harnessing the genetic structure of other tribes, we hope to be able to breed the gene back into our species.

speaker: Player
text: You're capturing prisoners... for their genes?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: You make us seem like monsters... Truly we are not.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We capture them, yes, but only because the tribes have become extremely xenophobic in their millenia trapped on this world. They would not aid us willingly, and killed our messengers when we asked.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We believe that if we get a large enough genetic sample, we can reintroduce the recessive Force sensitive genes back into our people, allowing us to once again access the heritage of our past.

speaker: Player
text: Heritage... You mean the Temple?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Yes, the Temple. It can only be entered by those sensitive to the Force, so it has been barred to us for ages.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: What we may find inside will allow us to lift the other tribes out of the barbarism into which they have fallen and restore us as a productive force in the galaxy.

speaker: Player
text: You're trying to restore your empire, aren't you!

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: No! We do not want to fall down the path that so twisted our people before.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: This time, perhaps we can redeem ourselves in the eyes of the galaxy, and become a force of good.

speaker: Player
text: How close are you to finishing your research?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We are quite far along, having had centuries to work already, but with the arrival of another tribe on our island, we have been restricted in our movements to just our enclave.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We have captured a few of their warriors, but the one that really interests us is their leader... the One.

speaker: Player
text: The One? What's special about him?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Those with the genes we seek seem to be marked... Marked with a destiny that causes them to rise above others as we did as a species early on.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: In hearing the stories his warriors tell of the One, we believe that he may hold some of the genes we seek. He may be nearing Force sensitivity.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Unfortunately, he and his people are much too aggressive and violent for us to ever get close enough to study him. His corpse would not do either, as only a living, working body is of use to us.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Maybe in time, though, the differences between our peoples will lessen enough that we may study one another and gain the information we need.

speaker: Player
text: What kind of information do you need?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Genetic data on drifts and changes over the many millenia we have been here. Specific data on exceptional individuals.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: If only we had access to the knowledge of our ancestors... They must have known much, much more than us. They had a much greater population sample to work with.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: I believe that in the Temple there may be the information we seek. Perhaps in old archives or scrolls... maybe even in an ancient computer if any is still functioning.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: This information would help us greatly in our work, and we would be very grateful to you for it.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about your research again.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Temple?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: It is ancient, that we know. And it is guarded by advanced technology that only Force sensitive races can penetrate.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Recently we have seen ships coming and going from it, similar in design to ones that came at about the same time you did many years ago.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Other than that, we do not know... although we would dearly like to find out.

speaker: Player
text: I have to go now.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Very well then. Come and go as you please.

speaker: Player
text: How could I help with your research?

speaker: Player
text: I don't know if your eugenics program is a good thing...

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: We would not revert to our old ways, rest assured, Revan. We merely seek data on genetic drifts and changes in the millenia of our imprisonment here.

speaker: Player
text: How can you find these genes?

speaker: Player
text: Do any of these warriors have what you're looking for?

speaker: Player
text: You want to reunite the tribes?

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Unite the tribes and take our place in the galaxy at large.

speaker: Player
text: I don't know how the Republic and the Sith would see you...

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: That is a worry, but we hope that our good intentions will let them accept us...

speaker: Player
text: You're trying to rebuild your genetic structure?

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you just ask them for help?

speaker: Player
text: No Rakata can use the Force?

speaker: Player
text: I don't need to hear this.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Perhaps not, but it is critical to my explanation of my work.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: When my species began to lose control over the Force, the power we had held over the subject races began to decay, along with our empire. The races we subjugated rose up, plagues swept our worlds... we could do nothing against all these calamities.

speaker: Player
text: I've heard this before.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Yes, likely you have.

speaker: Player
text: Why do you have these prisoners?

speaker: Player
text: You know damn well what I'm asking!

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Yes, yes, my research.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time to talk.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing much happened...

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Indeed... Nothing much happened for many years it seems.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: You have done our people a great service here, Revan, but your destiny lies elsewhere. May the blessings of the Elders go with you.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: Yes, Revan? Is there anything I can help you with?

speaker: Player
text: I have found data on the genetic structure of your species.

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: You... you have! Thank you! Thank you, Revan!

speaker: Researcher Ll'awa
text: This data will aid us greatly in our research.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: I demand justice! The Sandral family is a blight upon Dantooine! They must be punished!
comment: SCRIPTED  when ahlan is confronting the jedi council Dialog Mission Statement   These dialogs are the conversation files for Ahlan Matale in the Jedi Enclave. Before the player becomes a Padawan, Ahlan is sitting in a waiting room in the Enclave. Once the player does become a Padawan (see zhar13 for more details) Ahlan is moved fromthe waiting room to the council chambers. The next time the player enters the Council chambers, Ahlan, Vandar and Vrook will be there and the first dialog will initiate. Exit point in conversation: Exit stream 1: No matter what choice the player makes they are given this quest and told to do it. DAN_PLOT_ROMANCE is set to 1 to show that the quest has been activated. Upon saying his final line, Ahlan exits the room and is removed from Module 13. Exit stream 2: The line is said and the dialog ends.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Council will look into this matter, Mr. Matale. You must be patient. Your accusations have no proof, and we do not want you stirring up trouble with the Sandrals if there is some mistake.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Mistake? My son Shen is missing! How can there be any doubt the Sandrals are to blame?

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: There are other possible explanations for your son's disappearance.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Bah! You Jedi are good for nothing but talk! I shall only wait so long before I take action on my own!

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: As dangerous as the threat from Darth Malak and the Sith may be, we Jedi cannot simply abandon our other responsibilities. The Council has promised Alhan Matale we will look into his son's disappearance.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Should you have time, Padawan, you may want to investigate this matter.

speaker: Player
text: I shall look into it at once.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: If Shen Matale is not returned to his father it may ignite a savage and bloody feud between the Matale and Sandral estates. We must not allow that to happen.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Your study and training are important, of course. But the Jedi are not a cloistered Order. Our influence and teachings must spread beyond the walls of our Academies.

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: It is in the real world that we truly prove ourselves worthy of the title Jedi. You would do well to remember this, young Padawan.

speaker: Carth
text: Not to mention that I wouldn't mind getting out of this enclave for a bit. I mean, come on, how bad could it be?

speaker: Bastila
text: This task has its own importance. It may also serve to divert our minds for a short time... something which carries its own rewards.

speaker: Player
text: But what about my Jedi training?

speaker: Player
text: I have more important things to do!

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything else I should know?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: These two families have been settled here for some years now...

speaker: Vrook Lamar
text: And causing me no end of trouble!

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Indeed. They have been settled here for some time and feuding ever since.

speaker: Player
text: What caused this feud?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: I do not know how the original feud started, but they want nothing to do with each other.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: As you may have heard, Ahlan Matale believes that his son, Shen, has been kidnapped by Nurik Sandral.

speaker: Dorak
text: Curiously, Nurik's son Casus has been missing for some time as well... I fear Nurik may suspect Ahlan in this...

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: Which families are involved?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Sandral and Matale families are involved.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: The Sandrals live far to the south. The head of that family is Nurik Sandral. He is a stern man, but I believe him fair. Under the present circumstances, though... who knows?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Ahlan Matale can be much more unstable. He is convinced of his own importance and can be a most... oppressive individual at times. He lives closer to the enclave, but still to the south.

speaker: Player
text: Where are they settled?

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Both families have settled to the south of this enclave. The Matales are the closer of the two.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Both have similar estates, but Ahlan is much more paranoid about his and guards it quite heavily.

speaker: Vandar Tokare
text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

speaker: Player
text: I shall investigate this immediately.

speaker: Player
text: I will investigate if there is time.

speaker: Player
text: I must continue on my main mission.

speaker: Ahlan Matale
text: Why are you bothering me? I am here to speak with the Council, not some servant! Please leave or I shall be forced to tell the Council of your rude behavior!

speaker: Merchant
text: Greetings human, and welcome to the Ahto City Visitor's Provisional Stand. We are here to provide visitors with all manner of indigenous treats and products produced right here on Manaan.

speaker: Merchant
text: We carry all manner of foods and provisions, and have contacts with resellers across the world to provide you, the customer, with the best shopping experience possible.

speaker: Merchant
text: How is it that the Ahto City Provisional Company can help you today?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Ahto City.

speaker: Merchant
text: Ahto City is the center of trade and commerce for all of Manaan. Indeed, for this entire sector! It is the only known source of kolto in the galaxy, and thus one of its most important worlds.

speaker: Merchant
text: This city was constructed by we Selkath so that other races and cultures could experience the wonders that Manaan has to offer.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Manaan.

speaker: Merchant
text: Manaan is the homeworld of we Selkath. It is here that our race has lived and thrived for uncounted millenia. With our valuable supply of kolto, we have become an important player in intragalactic politics.

speaker: Merchant
text: We have taken a neutral stance in the current galactic war between the Sith and the Republic as we believe that violence is not a permanent solution.

speaker: Merchant
text: Is there another way in which I can assist you?

speaker: Player
text: Let me see your inventory.

speaker: Merchant
text: Of course. The Ahto City Visitor's Provisional Stand is here to service you, the customer.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing for now.

speaker: Merchant
text: Rest assured that as long as Manaan is here, the Ahto City Provisional Company will be here to serve your needs. Good day to you, sentient.

speaker: Player
text: I will be leaving now.

speaker: Merchant
text: You are not welcome in this city anymore, human, but we cannot deny you entry either.  Therefore, I am obliged to treat you as I do my other customers.

speaker: Greeta Holda

speaker: Gar
text: Is there anything else you require?

speaker: Player

speaker: Gar

speaker: Cand

speaker: Gar
text: With the Sith invasion, the Republic doesn't have the manpower to hunt them down.

speaker: Gar
text: The Jedi are even worse off because Malak has been hunting them specifically.

speaker: Gar
text: They're worried that he might even be supporting these raiders, so don't want to face them directly. That puts us in a kind of hard situation.

speaker: Gar
text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

speaker: Gar

text: I would like to ask you something else.

speaker: Player

speaker: Gar

speaker: Damaged Sentry Droid
text: This droid is damaged and inactive.

speaker: Player
text: Reactivate the droid. (1 repair part)

speaker: Damaged Sentry Droid
text: [Failure] You don't have any repair parts. You leave the droid alone for now.

speaker: Pilot
text: Our ship will be ready soon. Then it's off to Coruscant for a week or so.

speaker: Pilot
text: You own the Ebon Hawk, don't you? Wish I could fly a bird like that.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Greetings, human. I am called Bwa'lass, and I have been selected as your Arbiter for the duration of your trial.

speaker: Player
text: Arbiter?

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Yes, Arbiter. The one who defends you before the judges of the Selkath people.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I will endeavor to prove to them that you are not guilty of the heinous crimes that you are accused of, off-worlder.

speaker: Player
text: I don't need anyone to represent me!

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: While it is true that you do have that right, I would recommend against it. Due to your confinement, you have not had much of a chance to build up evidence to pursue your case.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Also, I do not believe you off-worlders truly understand the minds of we Selkath. It would be best if you left your defence up to me.

speaker: Player
text: How will you get me free?

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I would first like to ask you a few questions regarding the events that led up to your arrest.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I have already been given all relevant data on you and your companions, so that can be disregarded. For what reason did you enter the Sith Embassy?

speaker: Player
text: I was invited.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Indeed... That would explain the reason a passcard for entry was found on your person.
comment: if the player has the passcard

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: What is your prior association with the Sith?

speaker: Player
text: I have no prior association.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Indeed... Since you have a passcard to their base, I can only assume you believe taking this route would lessen your sentence... Very well.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: That should be all the information I require of you, for now. If you wish, we can begin the trial whenever you are ready.

speaker: Player
text: Um... Don't you need to ask more questions?

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I have all the information I need. We should proceed now, the judges are waiting.

speaker: Player
text: How can you expect to defend me without getting more information?

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I think this trial is relatively straight forward. It should be obvious to the judges what has transpired.

speaker: Player
text: Let's get the trial started.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Very well, we shall proceed to the courtroom.
comment: player released  walk away with arbiter  fadeout

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: While your... special position bears heavily on our minds, we cannot ignore the blatancy with which you have violated our laws.
comment: player has completed the hrakert rift trial

speaker: Judge Duula
text: You stand accused of the grievous murder of many Sith, and extensive property damage to their Embassy here.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: How do you plead?

speaker: Player
text: Not guilty.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Let the record show that this trial has commenced. Presiding are judges Shelkar...

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Jhosa...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Naleshekan...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Kota...

speaker: Judge Duula
text: and Duula.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This trial is to determine the culpability and punishment of this individual in the recent assault on the Sith Embassy.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Given the severity of this trial, we can dispense with the normal formalities of the court and proceed directly.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: You have pleaded not guilty, yet there were reports of weaponsfire and detonations from within the Sith Embassy.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You were seen entering and leaving the Embassy. The Sith have not conferred with the authorities about this matter, but from all available evidence, it would seem that you are the source of the disturbance.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: What is your explanation for being in the Sith Embassy?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith lured me inside.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Indeed. I am most skeptical of this statement.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: But it may be true... How was it they lured you inside? What bait did they use?

speaker: Player
text: I was there for diplomatic negotiations.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: I am skeptical of this assertion... but it does seem in the character of the Sith to reneg on their commitments.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: There have been many provocations before this! Their character is well known!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Indeed, but that is not an issue for outsiders to hear.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We will adjourn to debate your story and the charges brought against you.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We have reviewed your case and decided that there is not enough evidence to convict you of this crime.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: The provocations of the Sith are well known, and we will be issuing a memo of censure against them. Their Embassy is considered off-limits to all Ahto City Security personnel.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: No calls or incidents from their base will be attended to until this matter is dealt with, as they are no longer subject to the protections of Selkath law.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You have been found innocent, and may leave as you desire. This trial is now over.

speaker: Player
text: They were secretly trying to lure me to the darkside.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: This mystical darkside you Jedi keep speaking of is a convenient excuse. Basically, they wished to hire you away from the Republic.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: How, then, did the fighting start?

speaker: Player
text: I refused and they attacked.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Preposterous!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: That does sound like something the Sith would do...

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: I am inclined to believe the off-worlder.

speaker: Player
text: They tried to double-cross me.

speaker: Player
text: I felt like showing them who was boss.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: You... attacked them?!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I knew the off-worlder was a danger!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: You have willfully and blatantly broken our laws, and for that you shall be sentenced accordingly!

speaker: Player
text: No! I am a Republic citizen!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: For the crimes you have committed against the Sith and against the laws of the Ahto City Civil Authority, this court finds no alternative: We hereby sentence you to death.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You will be executed immediately. This court has spoken.

speaker: Player
text: I'm innocent!

speaker: Player
text: I have this datapad as proof that the Sith are up to no good!
comment: if the player has the Sith Master's datapad

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Let it be noted that the court has taken this new evidence into consideration.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Hm... This is... most disturbing.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The court will adjourn for a brief period to verify this evidence and discuss its importance.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: We have verified that this is indeed a Sith datapad indicating their complicity in a plot to overthrow the lawful government of Manaan.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: In gratitude for having discovered this heinous offense, all charges against you regarding this incident will be dropped.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Pending a suitable penalty against the Sith, their Embassy is considered off-limits to all Ahto City Security personnel.

speaker: Player
text: If you try to punish me, I'll let everyone know that the kolto is gone.
comment: if the player has already threatened the selkath

speaker: Judge Duula
text: You wouldn't!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: I wouldn't doubt the human... they are known for these double-dealings...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Kolto is the lifeblood of Manaan. Our entire economy and independence rests upon it. Now that it is gone we must maintain a perilous pact secrecy with your Republic.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: We can NOT afford to jeporadize that secrecy. Not for anything.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: If we allow you to leave, you are a threat and a liability to the Selkath people. Therefore we cannot.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Your secret will die with you, off-worlder.

speaker: Player
text: They offered me a job.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Offered you a job? To a Jedi?

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Unlikely... but possible. How then, did the fighting start?

speaker: Player
text: I was working for the Republic.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: You were working for the Republic? So the Republic had you break in and kill the Sith? It is as I suspected...

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Do not jump to conclusions.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Why did the Republic have you enter the Sith Embassy?

speaker: Player
text: To steal information.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You admit that you enetered the Sith base illegally and attempted to commit crimes there!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: It is obvious that they tried to stop you and that you initiated hostilities!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: So like an off-worlder...

speaker: Player
text: To retrieve data the Sith had stolen.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: One crime does not permit the use of another to set it right!

speaker: Player
text: To stop them from learning about the secret base by the Hrakert Rift.
comment: if the player has learned of the rift

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It is good that you are looking out for the joint interests of the Republic and Manaan in this issue, but was is really necessary to take such extreme measures?

speaker: Player
text: They had almost found out about the station.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: The secret must be kept from the Sith, no matter the cost!
comment: if the player has spoken about the hrakert rift already

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Indeed. We will adjourn to discuss the situation and the charges brought against you.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Station? What station?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: This is a internal matter for Selkath alone! We will adjourn immediately to discuss these things without the interference of outsiders!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Upon review of this case, we find that there is no basis for a case against the defendant.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Additionally, the Sith will receive a censure for provoking combat within Ahto City.

speaker: Player
text: They needed killing.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You admit to your crime!

speaker: Player
text: I was investigating the disappearances of young Selkath.
comment: if the player has been given the plot by Shaelas  if this option has not been selected already

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: You believe that the Sith have had something to do with those disappearance?

speaker: Judge Duula
text: The off-worlder has probably been listening to Shaelas and his rumor-mongering.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Most likely. Do you have any proof to back up your assumption, human? Have the Sith been implicated?

speaker: Player
text: I found this token on a dead Selkath inside the Sith base.
comment: if the player has the token

speaker: Judge Kota
text: I recognize that token! It is from Galas, one of the youths who went missing!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You found that in their Embassy?!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: The Sith HAVE been taking them!

speaker: Player
text: Er... well, no...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You will need to come up with a better excuse than that, off-worlder!

speaker: Player
text: I was killing Sith. See? Simple.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: See! I knew that the off-worlder was guilty! They all are!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: What... what possible reason could you have to justify your actions?

speaker: Player
text: The Sith are a blight upon the galaxy!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: That does not excuse your actions! The neutrality and laws of Manaan WILL be upheld!

speaker: Player
text: The Republic ordered me to go into their base.

speaker: Player
text: It was just a coincidence.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You were clearly seen entering the Sith base. You cannot deny this fact!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You must have had some reason for entering. What was it, human?

speaker: Player
text: Guilty.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: You... You are guilty? You admit to your crime?

speaker: Player
text: Yes.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Well... Then I suppose we have no choice but to sentence you for your crimes.

speaker: Player
text: Er... no... I was just kidding.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: This court will not be mocked!

speaker: Player
text: It was a lot of fun, really.

speaker: Player
text: I don't plead! I tell!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: We will not tolerate insolence! You will obey the rules of our court, or you will be summarily found guilty!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The Sith have been using and manipulating the young among our race; we know this. It is up to us to decide what actions we should take, not vigilante justice by some human.
comment: player has saved the selkath youths (talked to shaelas)

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: While you have proven the Sith to manipulative and deceitful in their activities here on Manaan, I believe you will have a much harder time defending your actions now. Some things go too far, off-worlder.
comment: player has saved sunry and sith blamed

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The familiarity you gained in your successful defence of Sunry will aid you here, human. But the charges you are faced with are far more grave.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Your past experience as Arbiter in the Sunry case may aid in your defence now, human, but you must do a better job yourself, given the crimes you are faced with.
comment: player has failed to save sunry

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: While your high standing among the off-worlders on Manaan may bring you some leniency from them, being a successful swoop rider brings you no credit here, human.
comment: player is a famous swoop rider

speaker: Player
text: I think I'd rather represent myself.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: While that is your right, I strongly recommend against it. I am versed in all the necessary particulars of this case and Selkath law, off-worlder. You would do well to heed my advice.

speaker: Player
text: No, I'll represent myself.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: You off-worlders are not known for your mental prowess. I shall leave your demise up to you.

speaker: Player
text: Fine, represent me.

speaker: Player
text: I said no, fish-head!

speaker: Player
text: I have proof that the Sith are evil.
comment: if the player has the Sith Master's datapad

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Indeed? And what is that?

speaker: Player
text: This datapad proving they are kidnapping young Selkath.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: This is most... disturbing. We should take this evidence and present it before the court right away.

speaker: Player
text: I'll show it to the judges, or no one!

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: You must share the evidence with me before I can release you and we can proceed to the courtroom.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I am skeptical of that, as will be the judges. You off-worlders tend to congregate much amongst yourself. I see no inherent differences between your two groups.

speaker: Player
text: I'm on a mission to stop them from taking over the galaxy.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: The Sith are an expansionistic power, true, and at war with the Republic. You may make it your personal mission to foil them, but the authorities take a dim view of it taking place here.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I think you will need a more thorough explanation in order to convince the judges.

speaker: Player
text: I kill them wherever I can find them.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: I am... humbled by your candor. While I'm sure that you yourself see that as a noble sentiment, I doubt that those assigning your sentence will be so generous.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Indeed. I find that unlikely, off-worlder, but perhaps the judges will be more sympathetic to your view.

speaker: Player
text: I had authorization to enter.

speaker: Player
text: I... er... broke in.

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Illegal acts seem to be a common occurance among you off-worlders. I am not terribly surprised by your actions, but the judges will want to hear a little more convincing reason.

speaker: Player
text: What have I been charged with?

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: You have been charged with initiating violence within the Sith Embassy, murdering members of the Ambassadorial Commission of the Sith Empire, and disregarding our own laws regarding violence in Ahto City.

speaker: Player
text: What can I do?

speaker: Player
text: It's all the Sith's fault!

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: Be that as it may, I doubt the judges share your view. I will endeavor, however, to make them see your point, off-worlder.

speaker: Player
text: Get me out of here!

speaker: Bwa'lass
text: The question of your freedom will be up to the court to decide. All I can do as Arbiter is attempt to sway their decision in your favor.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Go away. You would regret the only other option.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: What do you want, rail-rat? I don't have the time or desire to bother speaking with wandering idiots.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Go talk with your adoring fans over at the swoop races. I'm sure they fawn all over their beloved Sector Champion.

speaker: Player
text: Could I ask you a few questions?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I will get tired of your voice in short order, so make it quick.

speaker: Player
text: You mentioned the races.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You're the Sector Champion; you know the races inside and out. Why ask me? Are you trying to worm a compliment out of me?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Nothing about the current state of the races make me want to watch. Especially if it means associating with the cattle grouped in there now.

speaker: Player
text: There are no racers you like?

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I admire the mercenary spirit of Casandra Mateil. Other than that, no one.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Her mercenary spirit isn't what's selling the autoprints.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: She does have... other qualities as well.

speaker: Player
text: Let's go back to my first questions.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hurry it up. This is a poor use of my time. You should know not to annoy one of my kind.

speaker: Player
text: I have some questions about Manaan.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Grow some gills and swim the planet yourself. There's no substitute for personal experience. I have nothing else to say on the subject.

speaker: Player
text: I don't like how hostile you are.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Hostile? I would consider this the height of calm for dealing with insects like yourself. If I were hostile, you'd be dead.

speaker: Player
text: A pity we can't test the theory now.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Yes, Manaan is a very unsatisfying world for settling disagreements. The Selkath are very insistant that even words are not used as weapons.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Since we both refuse to initiate a violent event, you'll have to accept my contempt-filled dismissal, and hope we don't meet again.

speaker: Player
text: I won't take that chance. Goodbye.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Wisely played. Go away.

speaker: Player
text: I have to leave. Goodbye.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Good. This visit was dragging on.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Our Taris campaign killed the giants of the sport. The current racers are hardly inspiring. An Aqualish champion? Hmph. Laughable.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: You're probably another race fan in a fool's stupor after that big win by local whelp Queedle Molta.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Go join the other transients in the swoop race area. At least you'll all be contained.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Why are you back again? I didn't show enough disinterest the first time around? You really shouldn't pester a soldier of the Sith.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: Go look for fans over at the swoop races, Sector Champion. I'm sure they'll give you what your looking for.

speaker: Sith Soldier
text: I shouldn't expect you to listen. You're probably just another open-mouthed fool here for the swoop races.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: Hey - you can't come in here! This is a restricted area! You better tell me what you're doing or I'm going to hit the alarm!
comment: Dialog Mission Statement: She initiates when player enters Republic base. Player either persuades her and she leaves, or fails to persuade and she triggers alarm.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I'm here for a meeting. Don't worry - I know where I have to go.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: [Failure] Nice try. What - you think that just because I'm pretty I'm also stupid?

speaker: Receptioni091
text: You better tell me why you're here or I'll hit this alarm and you'll have about three seconds before this office is swarming with Sith soldiers!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Look, here's 50 credits - just don't hit that alarm.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: [Success] 50 credits? You've got a deal! The Sith have made my life a living hell ever since they took over this base.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: You know, it's about time someone stood up to these Sith! Just do me a favor and wait until I'm out of here before you start blasting the place up.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: [Failure] You must think I'm pretty stupid! If I take your bribe the Sith will have me executed!

speaker: Receptioni091
text: I don't know what you're up to, but I have the feeling it might get me in a lot of trouble. I hate to do this, but you'll have to explain yourself to the guards.

speaker: Player
text: Don't hit the alarm. I don't want to have to hurt you.

speaker: Receptioni091
text: Don't shoot! I just work here - I never wanted any part of this! I would have quit when the Sith took over, but they wouldn't let me!

speaker: Player
text: Okay - get out of here and I'll let you live!

speaker: Player
text: You're in the wrong place at the wrong time. It's bad luck, but I still have to kill you!

speaker: Receptioni091
text: You shouldn't threaten a girl who's got an alarm right at her desk!

speaker: Player
text: Touch that alarm and you're dead!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I work here - look, I've got an access card.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Greetings, human. A word, if I may. It concerns the Dark Lord of the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: You mean Malak?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: No, human. I mean the *true* Lord of the Sith. I am speaking of Darth Revan. Of you.

speaker: Player
text: How do you know who I am?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Listen to me, and all will be made clear. My name is Ziagrom. I am a... a businessman. I and my partner deal in rare items of extraordinary value and power.

speaker: Player
text: You're with the Exchange!

speaker: Ziagrom
text: No, we are not. We are independant operators, though often our transactions involve those who represent the Exchange.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Traditionally, we have always done business with the owner of the Ebon Hawk: Davik Kang, most recently. Ahita Othar before him. Forii Haxa before her. But we were reluctant to approach you.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: You had no ties to the Exchange, which was a problem. Even worse, you were a Jedi! Not the sort of person we normally associate with.

speaker: Player
text: Get to the point - how do you know my true identity?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: There were reports of the Ebon Hawk traveling to many different planets. We wanted to know what you were up to. At your last port, I placed a small tracking device on your ship.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: The tracking device reported back to us that you had been captured by the Leviathan. Once we had that information, we began digging into our sources within the Sith fleet.

speaker: Player
text: Sources? What sources?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: There are millions of soldiers in the Sith fleet. Surely you aren't surprised that some of them will sell information? Even high ranking officers aren't immune to the lure of easy credits.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Your escapades on the Leviathan created quite a stir in the Sith fleet. Of course Malak tried to suppress the truth about your identity: there were more than a few summary executions.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: But even if security footage is destroyed and witnesses silenced, some bits of information always slip through. Spend enough credits to gather the tiny pieces and the puzzle becomes clear.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: We know what happened on the Leviathan. At least, we know enough. You are Darth Revan, and you are going to kill Malak for daring to claim dominion over the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: How does this involve you?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: My partner and I deal in very rare and powerful items. Weapons, armor: things you could use in your battles against Malak and the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: And you're just going to give these items to me?

speaker: Ziagrom
text: I don't carry these items with me, of course. They're with my partner. But they're yours, if you've got the credits to buy them. We do want to make a profit on this, after all.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Just go to the Cantina here in Dreshdae. There's a Rodian there named Mika Dorin. Tell Mika that Ziagrom sent you to look at the premium items.

speaker: Player
text: I'll go check it out.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Mika already knows to expect you. Like I said, just tell him you want to look at the premium items.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: I guess my work here is done. Goodbye, Revan. And once Malak is beaten, don't forget who helped you to victory.

speaker: Player
text: I can't be bothered with this.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: It's up to you, I guess. But you'll be missing out on the best equipment in the galaxy! Sooner or later you'll realize this deal is to good to pass up.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Just go to the Dreshdae Cantina on Korriban. There's a Rodian in there named Mika Dorin. Tell Mika that Ziagrom sent you to look at the premium items.

speaker: Player
text: I'll check it out next time on Korriban.

speaker: Player
text: Let me see these items.

speaker: Player
text: You're wrong. I'm not in this for revenge.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Maybe, maybe not. But whatever your motivation may be, you *do* intend to stop Malak and his followers - of that we are sure. And we want to help.

speaker: Player
text: Go on.

speaker: Player
text: So why are you approaching me now?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Player
text: If you tell anyone who I am, I'll kill you!

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Your secret is safe with me, Lord Revan. At least until you chose to reveal yourself. But I have come here with an offer of aid. I want to help you defeat your old apprentice.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore.

speaker: Ziagrom
text: You are what you are, human. You cannot deny that you were once the Lord of the Sith. And you cannot deny that you wish to defeat Malak!

speaker: Player
text: *I* am the Dark Lord of the Sith!

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Yes, human. I know. That is why I have approached you.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for this!

speaker: Ziagrom
text: Please, human - this is of importance to us both! I know who you are... Revan!

speaker: Matton Dasol
text: Thanks for your help, friend. I'm getting off this planet as soon as I can. I'll pay my own way, too. No more debts to anyone.

speaker: Matton Dasol
text: No more trusting anyone, either. I've learned what that gets you.

speaker: Matton Dasol
text: Hello again. Welcom back to Eli Gand's outpost, now under new management. What do you need?

speaker: Player
text: Let's see what you have for sale.

text: I suppose that closes his little outpost here.

text: How do I equip a weapon?

speaker: Trask
text: Use the EQUIP screen to equip the armor and weapons from your inventory. You can access this screen by selecting the EQUIP menu icon in the upper right corner of the screen.

speaker: Trask
text: Use the mouse to look through your inventory slots. The menu on the right displays items you can equip in each slot.

text: Combat uses a pause and play system. At any time you can press the Pause button to pause the game and issue commands to your characters.

speaker: Trask
text: While the game is paused you can use the mouse to select a target or select icons from the TARGET and ACTION MENUs. You can switch characters by left-clicking on their portrait in the lower left corner of the screen.
