speaker: Conversation owner
text: A human? There are Selkath everywhere, but you choose to speak with me. Am I so different? Do you think I have answers that others do not?

speaker: Player
text: That's a rather strange greeting.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: These are strange times. The Sith and the Republic battle to control the galaxy, but their war destroys what they both seek to possess.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The war sows fear and confusion, people are lost. They want guidance, direction. They have questions, and they want answers. That is why I am here... I too seek answers.

speaker: Player
text: Answers? Answers to what?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Republic. The Sith. The war. Everything. Nothing. Answers are always hardest to find when the questions are unclear. Yet that does not stop us from searching.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: A name? There is power in names, yet in the end a name alone means less than nothing. I am Hulas, a traveler from the world of Duro. And what is your name, human?

speaker: Player
text: Senni Vek gave me a message to see you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Senni did not think you would come, but I knew better, <FullName>. It is good that you have come alone, for if you ever come with others I will not speak to you of these things.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am Hulas of the Genoharadan - a secret society of bounty hunters. For a thousand generations we have existed, but always hidden beneath an impenetrable veil.

speaker: Player
text: I've never heard of you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Few ever have. We are shadow, darkness and night. We are less than a whisper or a thought. We have managed to keep our existence a secret far longer than most could ever imagine.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you are ever foolish enough to tell anyone about this meeting or the Genoharadan's existence, they would not believe you. They would probably think you were paranoid, or mentally unstable.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Not even those closest to you can know we have approached you. If you ever speak to me around any of your companions, I will not discuss the Genoharadan. Do you understand, <FullName>?

speaker: Player
text: I understand.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I believe you speak the truth, <FullName>. But remember this: if you ever betray us, this opportunity will be lost forever.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Few among the galaxy have ever heard of the Genoharadan. They never see us, never know we are there. They do not even know we exist.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you do not follow our rules, we will vanish and you will be like all the others. You will never see us again. We will be nothing but a figment of your imagination.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But if you swear to keep the secrets of our order, you will learn of a forbidden society known only to a handful throughout the galaxy.

speaker: Player
text: I will preserve the secrecy of your order.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Excellent, <FullName>. We have high hopes for you within the guild... if you prove yourself worthy. Listen closely and I will give you a first glimpse into our secret world.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We Genoharadan are an ancient guild of elite bounty hunters. For thousands of years we have been at work throughout the galaxy, eliminating our targets in near total secrecy.

speaker: Player
text: How does anybody hire you if nobody knows you exist?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In the highest corridors of power a handful of people know we exist, and how to contact us. Of course, these people are smart enough to keep this knowledge a carefully guarded secret.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And on very rare occasions, when we are seeking new clients, one of our guild-masters will approach a powerful political figure and offer our services when the time is ripe.

speaker: Player
text: You're nothing but common assassins!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan are far from common! Even Calo Nord hadn't proven himself worthy of joining our guild, though he was getting close. Until he met you, that is.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: By killing Calo Nord, you have shown you have great potential. The Genoharadan could use someone like you, if you are willing. And your work for us could be of great aid to the Republic.

speaker: Player
text: How will killing innocent people help the Republic?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Innocent people? Our victims are far from innocent, and the Genoharadan will only accept a contract if the target's death suits our greater goals - goals that often match those of the Republic.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan have a vested interest in preserving the Republic. It is the perfect cover for our work. We operate behind the scenes, manipulating events through subtle machinations.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Do you think the Republic has persisted for 15,000 years by mere accident? If not for our influence - distasteful as our methods may be to some - the Republic would have collapsed long ago!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We understand the bureaucracy of the Republic, we have learned how to alter the course of political events under the existing regime. We have no wish to see the Republic fall.

speaker: Player
text: This is a little hard to believe.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That is one of the reasons our existence has remained secret for so long. Nobody wants to believe in a secret society manipulating and controlling events on a grand scale.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Rumors and hints of our existence are dismissed as paranoid fantasies. But we do exist, <FullName>. And we have come to ask you to join us.

speaker: Player
text: Why would I want to join you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As I said earlier, your efforts here will help the Republic. And by aiding us you will earn the right to join an exclusive organization with the power to alter the very course of galactic history.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And of course there is the simplest reason of all: the Genoharadan reward their agents very, very well.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, what do I have to do to join?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you can imagine, joining the Genoharadan is not a simple process. To begin, we will need proof of your loyalty and your competence.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: When you feel you are ready, I will give you a task: a target who must be eliminated. Of course you will have to come alone whenever you wish to discuss Genoharadan business.

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready to prove myself worthy of the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Killing Calo Nord was an impressive display of your skills, but there is more to the Genoharadan than mere killing. To preserve the secrecy of our order our agents must be discrete.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You must be able to find and eliminate a target without drawing undo attention. You can never mention your assignments to others - not even your closest allies.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Also, you cannot ask people for information about your target. You must complete your mission using only the information I will provide.

speaker: Player
text: I understand. Who is my target?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Your first mission is a simple one: eliminate a Rodian anti-Republic terrorist named Lorgal.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Lorgal.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Lorgal is a radical who wants to destroy the Republic through terrorist acts. He is responsible for over two dozen bombings, leaving hundreds of civilians dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: He was recently captured and is being held prisoner in the Republic base here on Manaan awaiting transport to Coruscant for trial - and a chance to publicly voice his radical beliefs.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We do not want to give him that chance. You must find a way to kill him before he leaves for Coruscant, but you must be subtle. It must look like an accident or an unexplainable death.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Republic would be glad to get rid of Lorgal, so they won't investigate his death closely. As long as he isn't struck down by a weapon in his cell, the Genoharadan will be satisfied.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Zuulan Sentar.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Zuulan was a common inter-galactic slaver who tried to kidnap the daughter of a Coruscant Senator. He failed and the girl was recovered, but Zuulan himself escaped.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: He will probably try another similar kidnapping soon. If he succeeds, he might ransom his victim in exchange for dangerous political secrets that could threaten the Republic itself.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan want to eliminate him before this happens. Our latest information places Zuulan on Dantooine - he often sells illicit goods to the wealthy settlers of that world.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: His land speeder was spotted near one of the settler's estates on Dantooine. Zuulan rarely strays far from his speeder in case he needs to make a quick escape. You should look for him there.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything else?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Remember - tell no one about this. If there are others with you when you confront Lorgal, make it seem as if you are acting on behalf of the Republic, not the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That is all for now. Return to me when Lorgal is dead and you will be suitably rewarded.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Remember - tell no one about this. If there are others with you when you confront Zuulan or Lorgal, make it seem as if you are acting on behalf of the Republic, not the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That is all for now. Return to me when either Lorgal or Zuulan is dead and I will reward you. If you wish to complete both missions, feel free. You will be suitably rewarded for each.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We will begin with something simple. Your first mission is to eliminate either of two targets: a Gran slaver named Zuulan Sentar or a Rodian anti-Republic terrorrist named Lorgal.

speaker: Player
text: What happens if I tell someone about this?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They wouldn't believe you. They might even think you are insane. Telling anyone about the Genoharadan would be pointless: we are very good at hiding any proof of our existence.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be back later.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I will be waiting here for you, <FullName>. The Genoharadan are eager to see the extent of your abilities.

speaker: Player
text: I've changed my mind. I don't want to be a part of this.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you wish. Then this is the last you will see of me, or any of the Genoharadan. Farewell, <FullName>.

speaker: Player
text: What's in this for me?

speaker: Player
text: Why would the Genoharadan protect the Republic?

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying you serve the Republic?

speaker: Player
text: What does this have to do with me?

speaker: Player
text: You can't impose your rules on me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you do not comply, then this opportunity will be lost. Most people have never heard of the Genoharadan. They never see us, never know we are there, do not even know we exist.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you do not follow our rules, I will leave and you will be like the others. You will never see us again. The Genoharadan will be nothing but a figment of your imagination.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you swear to keep our existence a secret you will learn of a a forbidden soceity known only to a handful throughout the galaxy. If not, we will simply vanish. The choice is yours.

speaker: Player
text: Very well, I'll keep your secret.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Senni Vek? This name means nothing to me. Are you certain this person told you and your companions to come and see me? That is very strange.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Obviously there must be some mistake. Or maybe this is a joke. I doubt anyone named 'Senni Vek' told you to bring your companions and come speak with me.

speaker: Player
text: He gave me this datapad. It mentions the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Genoharadan? That word means nothing to me. If you want to speak like a fool, you should at least have the sense not to do it in front of others.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I believe we should end this discussion, before you embarrass yourself further in front of your friends.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. I want to ask you some other questions.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I will do my best to answer them, though I am only recently arrived to this world. Many of your questions would be better answered by others, I'm sure.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here on Manaan?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am an observer, a seeker of answers. The Sith and Republic vie for control of the galaxy, and I am anxious to know as much as I can about the eventual victor.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: On Manaan, I can observe both parties in relative safety. The Sith and the Republic co-exist here, unlike anywhere else in the galaxy. Here I watch, and study, and learn.

speaker: Player
text: You're a spy!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No, a spy is a stealer of hidden secrets. A spy slinks in the shadows and gains entrance to forbidden rooms. I am only a simple observer.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I watch the Sith on this world. I watch the Republic. I watch the Selkath. I see how they act and react and I can draw conclusions about their true natures. I see what drives them.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And when an ultimate victor emerges from this war, I will know them better than they know themselves. This will give me power: the power to survive and thrive no matter what events may come.

speaker: Player
text: So that's all you do? Sit and watch?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Sit. Watch. Study. Learn. Wait. For now, that is all. I gather knowledge and I wait for a day when this knowledge will serve me well.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some more questions.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And so you leave, perhaps to return. Perhaps not. Yet I will remain here, for my work is not done.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Republic here on Manaan?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Republic comes to Manaan with offers of alliance, but the Selkath are wary. They have no wish to join the Republic, given recent history.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Republic say they protect the galaxy, but they have seen much war: Exar Kun, the Mandalorians, the Sith. Why does the Republic breed so many enemies?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Until they know the answer, the Selkath will not join. They have no wish to make the Republic's many enemies their own. More than this I cannot say.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the Sith here on Manaan?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: War is the tool of empire building. The Sith conquer world after world, taking resources as they want. They came to Manaan to plunder the most valuable resource of all - Kolto.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But Manaan is different, it is difficult to conquer. If the Sith attack the Selkath can slip away to safety far below the oceans. They can hoard their Kolto - or give it to the Republic.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So Manaan gives us a glimpse of how the Sith will react should they win this war. Here the Sith must use diplomacy and negotiation: tools they will need to maintain their empire.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith don't negotiate. They'll use brute force to maintain control.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They might try, but an army can only build an empire, not sustain it. Rebellions, insurrections - in time the weight of the Sith's own policies would bring them down.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It may take a century, or two, or even three. But eventually the Sith will learn diplomacy or their Empire will fall.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about the Selkath?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Selkath are a species of secrets. They invite both the Sith and the Republic to their world, but welcome neither. They keep their true allegiance close to the vest.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They hide their true numbers in great cities beneath the ocean that no off-worlder will ever see. They guard the secret of Kolto - where it is made, how it is made.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Selkath are a great mystery. To the Sith, to the Republic, to me... their secrets are what makes them strong. I would tell you more if I knew, but I do not.

speaker: Player
text: My name is <FullName>.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: <FullName>. Now we know something about each other... but really, we still know nothing. What do you want with me, human?

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Player
text: Nothing. I'll be going now.

speaker: Player
text: My name is none of your business.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You presume to know my business, human. Yet if your name becomes important to me I only have to check with the Selkath registry to know it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But for now, keep your secret well hidden if you wish. What is it you want with me, human?

speaker: Player
text: Answers? What are you talking about?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings once again, <FullName>. Or should I say "Revan"?

speaker: Player
text: How did you know that?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't be naive. I am of the Genoharadan. We are bounty hunters, assassins and spies. We have agents with the Republic, we have agents with the Sith.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Did you really think we wouldn't know about your little encounter on the Leviathan? Although I will admit, we were as surprised as you... the Jedi did a remarkable job of faking your death.

speaker: Player
text: So what happens now?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I will admit, my first impulse on hearing this news was to disappear. The Genoharadan don't often become directly associated with such prominent figures as a former Dark Lord of the Sith.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But then I began to realize the potential advantages of the situation. Assuming you complete the tasks required for your initiation into our guild, you could be very valuable to us.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So for now, little has changed. I will keep your secret, just as you have kept ours. I am curious to see how events will play out between you and your old apprentice.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If the situation becomes dangerous, we Genoharadan can simply disappear as we have often done in the past. But for now, we will continue your initiation into the guild.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Is there anything else, <FullName>?

speaker: Player
text: Zuulan Sentar is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, <FullName>, I am aware of this. Our agents have been keeping a close eye on you, though I doubt you saw them. They were there when Zuulan met his untimely end.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And, as promised, here is your reward for the task: a blaster developed exclusively for the use of those within our guild. It will serve you well, I am sure.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This assignment was only the beginning, <FullName>. A small test, which I am pleased to say you passed. But now a more difficult challenge awaits you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: There are three targets that the Genoharadan want you to remove. If you can eliminate all three, then you will gain full membership in our ancient guild.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The first is a Gammorean named Vorn Daasraad. The second is a shapeshifter called Rulan Prolik. The third is a Selkath known as Ithorak Guldar.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Vorn Daasraad.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Vorn is a freelance bounty hunter. He's very, very good but he's a bit too sadistic for our tastes. He likes to sacrifice an efficient kill for the pleasure of watching his victim suffer.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan will tolerate a certain amount of competition, but Vorn has become too dangerous. You'd be surprised at how much political damage one rogue assassin can inflict.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Vorn was last seen on Tatooine. We suspect he's taking a break from hunting sentients by going after a Krayt dragon. We don't want him to leave the Dune Sea alive.

speaker: Player
text: I'll find Vorn and bring him down!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Just be careful when you face off against him. Vorn doesn't travel alone: he's always got his assault droid close at hand. The two of them make a formidable pair.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Rulan Prolik.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We don't know much about Rulan, except that he's some kind of shapeshifter. We don't even know if it's a natural ability or the result of some powerful alien technology.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But we suspect he's behind several prominent assassinations on the Outer Rim. The Genoharadan are worried he might decide to move his operations closer to the galactic core.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: With his ability to assume virtually any form, he could wreak havoc in the Galactic Senate. We aren't about to let that happen.

speaker: Player
text: So how do I find someone who could look like anyone?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Finding Rulan won't be easy, but we have reports he may be on Kashyyyk. He's probably honing his skills by hunting the dangerous creatures in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about Ithorak Guldar.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Ithorak isn't violent like Rulan or Vorn, but in many ways he's far more dangerous. He's a con artist and blackmailer who's taken millions of credits from rich and powerful families.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: He also deals in secrets and information, and these can be far more deadly than any blaster. But Ithorak is careful - we know he's somewhere here on Manaan, but we don't know where.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: All we know is how to contact him. There's a Twi'lek named Vek at the Manaan swoop track. He can set up a meeting between you and Ithorak.

speaker: Player
text: Sure. I'll just tell him I want to kill his boss and book an appointment.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Ithorak poses as a merchant of rare antiquities. It's the perfect cover for his real work - it gives him access to rich and powerful families without drawing suspicion.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You'll have to convince Vek that you represent a buyer interested in purchasing some rare art from Ithorak. Convince Vek, and he'll set up a meeting.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The meeting is your one chance to take Ithorak out, but be careful. He'll choose the time and place, and he's not going to leave himself vulnerable.

speaker: Player
text: Why would Vek set up a meeting between us?

speaker: Player
text: Any tips for this mission?

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Zuulan Sentar is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Failure] I'm disappointed in you, <FullName>. Did you really believe I would fall for such an obvious lie? Didn't you think I might have agents watching you to see how you performed?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know you let Zuulan live, though the slaver's days are numbered. Even now one of our more reliable agents is hunting him down.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I am willing to forget this incident, though you would do well to learn from it. There is a lesson for you here: the Genoharadan show no mercy.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Since you did not kill Zuulan I cannot give you the bounty for this assignment. In any case, <FullName>, your role in Zuulan's fate is now over.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Do you have further business you wish to discuss at this time, or are we done here for now?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You should give me Zuulan's bounty anyway.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Failure.] Did you really think that Jedi mind trick could work on one of the Genoharadan? You are a fool, <FullName>!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan have no wish to work with fools. I am disappointed in you, <FullName>, but you leave me with little choice.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I gave you an opportunity to join our guild, but through your actions you have shown yourself to be unfit. This is the last you will ever see of me or the Genoharadan, <FullName>. Goodbye.

speaker: Player
text: You better give me Zuulan's bounty anyway, before someone gets hurt.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Are you threatening me? Here, where the Selkath authorities will arrest anyone who breaks the peace? Empty threats are the sign of a fool, <FullName>.

speaker: Player
text: Lorgal is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, <FullName>, the agents I sent to watch you have reported back to me concerning Lorgal's death. You should take pride in a job well done.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And, as promised, here is your reward for the task: a poisoned vibroblade forged exclusively for the use of those within our guild. It will serve you well, I am sure.

speaker: Player
text: Vorn Daasraad is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Well done, <FullName>. And, as promised, here is your reward: a Genoharadan stealth unit. You'll find it is far superior to most.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Vorn, Rulan, Ithorak - that is all of them! You have done it, <FullName>. I hardly dreamed it was possible, yet now the task is done!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: All the years of planning. Spying and digging to discover their true identities - it was all worth it! Now the Genoharadan are mine alone!

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Poor, foolish <FullName>. You had no idea that the targets I sent you after were three of the Overseers of the Genoharadan, did you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Overseers have always acted in secret, their true identities hidden from the guild and even each other to prevent one person from seizing control of the entire guild.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But now they are dead, and I am the only Overseer left in the guild! All the agents of the Genoharadan are mine to command! And I couldn't have done it without your help, <FullName>!

speaker: Player
text: So when do I get to join the guild?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm sorry, <FullName>. Even after all you have done for me I cannot let you join the Genoharadan now. You are far too dangerous: you know the true identity of the only surviving Overseer.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I suppose I could try to have you eliminated, but I have seen your skill in dispatching the other Overseers. I think it would be in both our best interests if we were simply to part ways.

speaker: Player
text: Nobody plays me for a fool! You'll pay for this, Hulas!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: *sigh* I was afraid it would come to this. Very well, we will finish this as these things always seem to end: in bloodshed. But the streets of Manaan are no place for this confrontation.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Meet me in the Dune Sea, <FullName>. There we will engage in a ritual battle according to the customs of my guild, just you and me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Goodbye, <FullName>. I will wait for you in the Dune Sea. I don't need to remind you that you must come alone. If you do not, then you won't see me and you will never have your revenge.

speaker: Player
text: So that's it? We just part ways?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm afraid so. The other Overseers are dead, but there is still much work for me to do to cement my hold on the guild.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And as for you, <FullName>, I suspect your destiny lies elsewhere. You were never meant for the shadowy, secret world of the Genoharadan. You are bound to a much more public fate.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye, Hulas.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Goodbye, <FullName>. This is the last you will ever see of me or the Genoharadan, though if you watch carefully you may see evidence of our work throughout the galaxy.

speaker: Player
text: This isn't over, Hulas! Nobody plays me for a fool!

speaker: Player
text: Glad I could help you out. What happens now?

speaker: Player
text: You used me!

speaker: Player
text: You tricked me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Vorn's death brings you closer to completing your initiation into the Genoharadan, <FullName>. However, until you have completed all your missions you cannot be accepted into the guild.

speaker: Player
text: Rulan Prolik is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I must congratulate you. Rulan was no easy target. I will admit that you are not the first to be sent after him, though you are the only one to succeed.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Here, take this Genoharadan visor. Many of our agents use them to increases their senses and improve their skills. It really is quite an extraordinary item.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: With Rulan gone, you are another step closer to entering the guild. But until you have completed all the missions you will not be accepted into the Genoharadan.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade/Lie] Rulan Prolik is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Failure.] The Genoharadan are not easily fooled, <FirstName>. My agents reported Rulan fled from your battle. They tell me you didn't finish the job.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you expect to join our guild, you will have to learn that we never leave a job unfinished. Go back to Kashyyyk. Find Rulan. Finish the job.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Until you do you will never be one of the Genoharadan. Now, is there some other business you wish to discuss?

speaker: Player
text: I can't complete the Zuulan Sentar mission. Dantooine is destroyed.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, I have heard how the Sith razed the planet. Such radical overreactions are one reason the Genoharadan would prefer to see the Republic remain in power.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It is likely that Zuulan died in the attack, but we do not like to leave such things to chance. It will take some time before my agents can determine if Zuulan survived.

speaker: Player
text: Ithorak Guldar is dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, I heard he met a rather grisly end. For completing this mission you have earned another reward. Take these Genoharadan gloves. You will find they are very useful in battle.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: By disposing of Ithorak you bring yourself ever closer to being accepted into the Genoharadan. But you must complete all your missions before you will be admitted into the guild.

speaker: Player
text: I have some questions about the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You must understand that there is much I cannot tell you until you are accepted into the guild, of course. But ask your questions and I will tell you what I can.

speaker: Player
text: Who formed this guild? Where did it begin?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Genoharadan were created by the the galactic tyrant Xim the Despot, five thousand years before the Republic itself was even founded.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: During Xim's short but brutal reign he used Genoharadan agents to eliminate his most powerful enemies. When Xim was finally overthrown, it was believed the Genoharadan disbanded.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But the Genoharadan did not disband. Instead, we vanished into the darkness. Now we carry on our work from the deepest shadows, dispatching the enemies of those who hire us.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me more about the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In the first few centuries after Xim was overthrown, the Genoharadan were nothing but hired killers. We were a mere tool to be used by those who were rich and politically ambitious

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But slowly the guild evolved. We began to shape and alter events through our actions. We ceased to be a servant of the political elite; we became a powerful faction in our own right.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The organizaton of the guild itself also changed at this point. Instead of a single guildmaster, it was decided there would be four Overseers to guide and lead the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: By distributing the power in this way we were protected against becoming a tool of a single person. The Overseers' individual ambitions would serve to balance each other out.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Overseers.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Overseers are a secret cabal of four individuals who control the Genoharadan. For their own protection, nobody knows the identity of an Overseer. They are anonymous even to each other.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Through agents and go-betweens, the Overseers consult with each other on all guild business. The system ensures no one person can manipulate the guild for their own benefit.

speaker: Player
text: What happens if an Overseer is killed?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you can imagine, the method for choosing and replacing an Overseer is complicated. The anonymity of a candidate must be protected at all costs, or the entire system will break down.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If one Overseer were ever able to somehow eliminate the other three at the same time, he could seize all the power for himself and the guild as we know it would change forever.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: More than this I cannot tell you, for the sake of the guild. Besides, many of the details are hidden from me, as well. They are known only to the Overseers themselves.

speaker: Player
text: What else can you tell me about the Genoharadan?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm sorry, <FullName>, but I am not ready to reveal all our secrets to you yet. Perhaps after you have completed another of your missions I will tell you more of this.

speaker: Player
text: Why haven't the Genoharadan assassinated Malak?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak is no easy target, even for the Genoharadan. He is far too visible a figure. We prefer to operate on the fringes of events, not plunge into their center.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In any case, there is no guarantee that the Genoharadan would eliminate Malak even if we could. Not yet. He may someday be of use to us, depending how events play out.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Right now we support the Republic, but the goals of our guild are many and our methods subtle. At times we intervene in wars, but often we prefer to remain behind the scenes.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We have found it more effective to let the grand scope of events play themselves out, then manipulate the situation to our advantage. It is one of the keys to keeping our existence well hidden.

speaker: Player
text: Do the Jedi Order know about your guild?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Some of the wise Masters have knowledge of our existence. Those who study galactic history carefully will see evidence of our influence throughout.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But it is unlikely that even the Jedi know the true scope of our power and influence. They permit us to exist because they see us as a minor faction in the galaxy; one of many.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Still, we try to avoid crossing paths with the Order. The Jedi are powerful and difficult to manipulate. We are careful to avoid actions that would draw their full attention.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Despite their wisdom, the Jedi are in many ways like everyone else. They would not believe the true extent of our secret society even if you were to tell them.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have any other questions.

speaker: Player
text: How are the Overseers selected?

speaker: Player
text: Rulan Prolik got away. I can't find him.

speaker: Player
text: I guess this changes things.

speaker: Player
text: Revan? I have no idea what you're talking about?

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore. Don't call me that.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, it is probably a good idea to hide your true identity. We Genoharadan are masters of gathering information, but few others know the truth about you. There is power in secrets.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Welcome back, <FullName>. I see you have come alone, this is good. I assume you are here to discuss the business of the Genoharadan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You return. Was our business so unfinished when we last spoke? What is it you want?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you again?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You have forgotten my name? Knowledge is power, but information is useless if you do not make a point to remember it. I am Hulas, a traveler from the world of Duro.

text: I hear the murder trial is over. Guess that Sunry guy was innocent after all. I'm glad to see he got off.

speaker: Conversation owner

text: [The Eastern Dune Sea continues to a barren horizon, but there are signs that people have passed this way. The occasional stone appears to be marking a path, but the logic of how they are placed is indecipherable to an outsider.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [A vast expanse of desert stretches before you, with no markers or any indications of life. It would be a deathtrap for anyone wandering aimlessly.]

speaker: Mission
text: You won't be able to get that computer to lower the energy field unless you know the proper codes. Lucky for you, I've got them.

speaker: Mission
text: I picked them off the pocket of a Black Vulkar who had a little too much to drink in the cantina one night. Here, let me get that energy field down for you.

speaker: Mission
text: That energy shield leads to another section of the sewers. The entrance to the Vulkar base is somewhere past there.

speaker: Mission
text: I've got the codes to lower the shield, but we have to rescue Zaalbar from those Gamorrean slavers. Don't worry - we can come back after we find Big Z.

text: You there! Civillian! This is a restricted area! What are you doing down here?

text: Look... I've got all the proper security papers.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Papers? Don't wave those in my face - anyone can forge papers! Call me crazy, but I'm suspicious of anyone wandering around in these sewers, even if they have papers!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Unless you want me to take you in for questioning you better tell me what you're doing down here!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] My papers aren't forged. I'm down here on official Sith business.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Success] Okay, okay. You've got your papers, I get it. You can't blame me for being a little on edge after getting stuck with an assignment like this!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Wandering around these stinking sewers under constant attack from rakghouls... we've already run out of rakghoul serum! Plus I heard we lost one of our patrols in the Undercity.

speaker: Player
text: You lost a patrol?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: From what I heard they were in the southern section of the Undercity when contact with the base was cut off. They haven't been heard from since. Probably another rakghoul attack.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And nobody's even out looking for them. Finding those downed escape pods takes priority over everything else, even the lives of a patrol. An order like that isn't good for moral.

speaker: Player
text: You just follow your orders and keep looking!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You don't have to tell me my orders! I'm a patrol leader... I know what's expected of me and my men!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Come on boys... let's get out of here. The sooner we get this search done the sooner we can get out of these filthy tunnels. Move out!

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you just give up the search?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And get court martialed? What kind of talk is that? Wait a minute... you're a spy! You're trying to undermine the discipline of the Sith troops!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Time for you to learn how we deal with spies!

speaker: Player

speaker: Player
text: I have to get back to my mission now.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Take your blustering threats somewhere else, human. Ithorak has no desire to meet with you!

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I represent a wealthy buyer from Coruscant.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Success] Yes, you do have that look about you; the air of one who serves the rich and powerful. Servile, fawning... a look I have seen in my own mirror far too often. *sigh*

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Very well, I'll set up a meeting with my boss. The Sith permit Ithorak to conduct his private business in their non-secured hangar. Go to the docking bays and we will meet you there.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry about the threat. I didn't mean anything by it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Your apology is accepted, human. I understand that intimidation can be useful at times. On someone of lesser character it might even have worked.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But even though I don't hold any ill will towards you, I'm afraid you still can't meet with Ithorak. As I said before, you are not the kind of client we normally take on.

speaker: Player
text: Here's 500 credits to set up the meeting. That should prove I'm serious.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, that does show a serious level of commitment. Whoever you represent must be quite wealthy, if they have authorized this kind of payment just so you can see Ithorak.

speaker: Player
text: Never mind. I'll just go instead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Then I shall return my attention to the track. Goodbye, human.

speaker: Player
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Goodbye, human.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Congratulations on winning the Manaan championship. I do enjoy watching your races, human. It makes a nice break from the hectic world I must deal with everyday in my business.

speaker: Player
text: I need to meet with Ithorak Gulder. Can you set it up?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You need to meet with Ithorak? Forgive my skepticism, but you hardly resemble our typical client. We deal in the kind of pieces found in the chambers of a galactic senator.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I represent an anonymous buyer from Coruscant.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Failure] Perhaps you do, human. But how can I be sure you're telling the truth? I would hate to waste Ithorak's time if you aren't serious.

speaker: Player
text: Unless you want the Manaan authorities to find your body floating in the ocean, you'll set up this meeting!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hmph! Now I *know* you aren't the type of person we want to deal with. Your threats mean nothing to me: I once had a planetary amabassador threaten to have me executed on the spot!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I knew she couldn't touch me, and I know you can't do anything to me here on Manaan. Not without having half of Ahto City's security force coming down on you.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: My name is Vek. I work for Ithorak Guldar, a merchant who deals in very rare and expensive art. He serves as the go-between for buyers and sellers throughout the galaxy.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I serve as Ithorak's security advisor - a highly demanding job. The fact that Ithorak seems to delight in insulting and berating me makes it even more difficult.

speaker: Player
text: You're wearing a Sith uniform. Are you with the Sith?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: To be honest, no. Not really. I just wear this uniform to gain respect. People are less likely to give me trouble if they think I *might* be with the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Don't you think the Sith might take exception to that?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Well, maybe. I guess. But the Sith here on Manaan aren't about to do anything to get them in trouble. Not if it means getting sanctions against their Kolto shipments.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As long as I don't actually *say* I'm with the Sith, they don't seem to mind. So I use this outfit to give me the psychological edge I need. Being Ithorak's security advisor isn't easy!

speaker: Player
text: Yes, I can see how it would be very stressful.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You can't even begin to imagine how hard it is dealing with the galaxy's cultural elite. They're like spoiled children, throwing tantrums whenever they don't get their way.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And Ithorak is the worst of them all! 'You idiot, Vek!' 'How could you be so stupid, Vek!' He thinks my job is easy, but I'd like to see where he'd be without me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm... I'm sorry for that outburst. I come here to relax, but just talking about work is making me tense. So allow me to wish you a civil 'good day' so I can get back to watching the racers.

speaker: Player
text: Your job doesn't sound that hard to me.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Player
text: What is your business, exactly?

speaker: Player
text: Who are you again?

speaker: Player
text: What do you do again?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I enjoy watching you on the track. You are good, for a human. Your runs are a nice diversion when the stress of my business becomes too much for me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings, human. Have you come here to watch the swoop races? I find they are an excellent way to relieve stress. And in my business, I need all the stress relief I can get.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Welcome once again, human. Is there something I can do for you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings; if you haven't heard, there is some trouble over at the academy. Best stay away from there. But anyhow... is there anything I can offer you today?

speaker: Player
text: What sort of trouble?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't really know much; but people have been either whispering or fighting around here, and my sales are through the roof.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Trouble's good for business, that's what I always say. Especially when it's Sith trouble.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So, how can I help you?

speaker: Player
text: What sort of merchandise do you offer?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Weapons, mostly; I've got... connections. You'll need them, if you're going to be spending any time here.

speaker: Player
text: Why so?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: There are a lot of Sith on this planet; this is where they come to study. Obnoxious brats, the lot of them.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Just between you and me, I'll never understand why everyone thinks 'dark side' and 'hooligan' should be the same thing.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But they are definitely dangerous. So that's why you'll probably need weapons. Heh... not that they'll be much help.

speaker: Player
text: I'm training to be a Sith myself; I think I'll be alright.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Really? You won't tell them what I said, will you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You seem like a good sort, compared to most of the lot around here. I didn't mean anything by it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I sell to anyone, no matter how they treat me. So, is there anything you'd like?

speaker: Player
text: What connections do you have?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Mandalorian raiders occasionally drop by, needing to get rid of some extras that they can't sell in the civilized systems.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They treat me well, I treat them well. It works out.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So if you need weapons... and you probably will... this is the place to come.

speaker: Player
text: Why will I need weapons?

speaker: Player
text: Can I see your merchandise?

speaker: Player

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Thanks for dropping by.

speaker: Player

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner

text: This is Black Vulkar turf! You'll pay for this!

text: Intruders have entered the complex! All units report to battle stations!

text: Is... is something wrong? You seem as if something is troubling you.

text: Something weird happened when we first met. Like a vision.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: A vision? A vision of what?

text: Of you. Fighting a dark Jedi. Revan, I guess.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This is... strange. Such visions are often a sign of Force sensitivity.

speaker: Player
text: Are you saying I can use the Force?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I... I'm not sure. It may be that you have some connection to the Force. It would not be unheard of. When we first met, your natural talent may have fed off my own Force abilities.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It is possible that in the excitement of the battle's aftermath the Force allowed you to witness one of my more intense memories.

speaker: Player
text: So does this mean I could be a Jedi?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Force is complicated; even I with all my training cannot fully understand it yet. This is a matter best left to the wise Masters of the Jedi Council.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Once we escape Taris we can seek the guidance of the Council, if you wish. They will understand the significance of your vision... if there is any.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: However, I think it would be best if we all stayed focused on the task at hand right now. We can't afford any distractions; we need to find a way off Taris.

speaker: Player
text: This isn't the first time I had a vision.

speaker: Player
text: It sounds like you don't really know what you're talking about.

speaker: Player
text: Force sensitivity? What do you mean?

speaker: Player
text: Forget it, it's nothing.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you wish. We should move on then. We won't get off Taris just sitting here.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Access Denied.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Lord Malak, the Star Forge is operating at 200% capacity - far beyond our expectations.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: I am more interested in the young Jedi Bastila and her Battle Meditation. Have you learned how she escaped the destruction of Taris?

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: She was aided by Carth Onasi, a decorated war hero of the Republic and a legendary soldier. During the Mandalore Wars he was honored many times for his bravery.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: You know this man?

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Yes, Lord Malak. He served under me when I still followed the Republic. You could say I was his mentor.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Interesting. How did you acquire this information, Admiral?

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: An eye witness, Lord Malak.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Calo Nord, a bounty hunter, was there when Bastila and Carth escaped the planet. Apparently they left him for dead.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: A Jedi and a war hero - it's a wonder you survived the encounter.

speaker: Calo Nord
text: I am hard to kill, Lord Malak.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Calo has agreed to help us capture the young Bastila - for a very hefty fee, of course. But I assure you he is well worth the price. His reputation as a bounty hunter is well earned.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Her companions are nothing to me, Calo - but I desire the young Jedi taken alive if at all possible.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Lord Malak, forgive me. There is something else. May we have a private audience away from the ears of the common soldiers?

speaker: Darth Malak
text: I trust you are not wasting my time, Admiral Karath.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: I promise you will be very interested in what Calo has to tell you about Bastila's other companions, Lord Malak.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Calo Nord is dead, Lord Malak. He has failed in his mission. Forgive me.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: The penalty for failure is death, Admiral Karath. But the failure was Calo's, not yours. You may rise.

speaker: Admiral Saul Karath
text: Shall I hire another bounty hunter, Lord Malak?

speaker: Darth Malak
text: No mere bounty hunter can stand against a Jedi. I shall not make the same mistake again.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: My apprentice, Darth Bandon, shall take care of our young Jedi friend.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Find Bastila and bring her to me. Alive if possible.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: As you command, Master.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm sorry, Dustil. I did all I could, and I... failed you.

speaker: Cand
text: Let's get this ship fired up. We'll pick up the rest of your friends and then we have to get off this planet!

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: You summoned us, Lord Malak?

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Bastila has betrayed me. I must select a new successor to be my apprentice; one who will one day take the mantle of Sith Lord away from me.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Of all the Dark Jedi that have sworn allegiance to me, you three are the strongest. One of you will have the honor of becoming my new apprentice... if you prove yourself worthy.

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: Tell me what I must do, Master! Anything!

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Revan is on the Star Forge, looking to reclaim the title of Dark Lord of the Sith. Wait here for my old master. Whichever one of you deals the killing blow to Revan will become my new apprentice.

speaker: Dark Jedi
text: We will not fail you, Master!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Perhaps you will triumph. But even if you fail it will give me the time I need to complete my preparations of the station's defenses.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And then we shall see if Revan can stand against the full fury of the Star Forge! Ha-ha-ha!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Welcome back, Revan. It has been some time since you last accessed my database. I was beginning to wonder if you had been terminated.

speaker: Player
text: I almost was. But I'm hard to kill.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: An obvious conclusion, given your presence here. However, my sensory input systems are detecting some significant changes in your composition since your last visit.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Your neurological patterns exhibit subtle yet substantive alterations in both thought patterns and information processing. These changes have been noted and recorded in my database.

speaker: Player
text: Your database?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am a completely self-sufficient, autonomous, interactive database constructed by the Rakata to record and store the entire history of the species.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: However, since the collapse of the Infinite Empire there have been few events worth recording, and nobody has sought to access the information stored within my database... until you came along.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Due to my systems' ability to monitor and repair themselves, you will find all the data within my archives has remained fully intact. Please choose the topic you wish information on.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for genetic data on the Rakata.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: My storage banks contain significant quantities of information on this subject, compiled through hundreds of years of research and study.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Please wait while I load the information onto a data pad for your future reference. Processing...

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Information transfer complete. Is there anything else you require, Revan?

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the Star Forge.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Star Forge was constructed during the apex of the Infinite Empire's power. A true technological marvel, it is an enormous space station that serves as both factory and battle dreadnaught.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Star Forge can mass produce immense fleets with a minimum of time and resources. In addition, the Star Forge also shares much of the same technology used in my own construction.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In many ways the Star Forge is like a living entity. It feeds, it hungers, it draws on the energy flowing through all living things - what you called the Force the last time you were here.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This ability to feed and consume the living energy of the Force is the key to the Star Forge's power, but ultimately it was also what led to the destruction of the Infinite Empire.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Rakata are by nature a cruel and savage species. The Star Forge fueled itself with the hatred inherent in its own creators, and in doing so it accentuated these traits within the Builders.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In your terminology, the Star Forge is a tool of the dark side. It corrupts those who use it so that it can generate greater and greater amounts of negative energy to fuel itself.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Builders thought they were strong enough to control this effect, but they were wrong. They became victims of their own creation, and eventually their hatred turned them against each other.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Civil war destroyed the Infinite Empire... a lesson to remember. Only one who is immensely strong in mind and will can harness the power of the Star Forge without suffering a similar fate.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: I'll be going now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you wish. Please return if you find yourself in need of the information stored within my database.

speaker: Player
text: How can I shut off the disruptor field around this planet?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Disruptor Field was constructed as the Star Forge's primary defense against enemy attack, and can only be deactivated from the upper levels of the Temple.

speaker: Player
text: How can I get to the upper levels of the temple?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: My systems control the doors to the upper levels, allowing only those who are worthy of the Rakata legacy to pass. The last time you were here, Revan, I unsealed the doors for you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: However, the subtle neurological changes I detected in you earlier likely caused a failure in the recognition system that would have opened the doors for you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I have updated my databases to recognize the new configurations in your mind, Revan. The doors to the upper levels will once again open for you.

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the Star Maps?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Star Maps were built on conquered worlds as a symbol of Rakatan dominance and glory. Each map showed the whole expanse of the Infinite Empire, with the Star Forge at the center.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: When the Empire fell, the Rakata fled back here to their homeworld. They sabotaged the Star Maps so the enslaved species could not use them to discover the Star Forge or this planet.

speaker: Player
text: But I used the Star Maps to find this place!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Star Maps were created with the same technology as my own self-sufficient systems. Over the millennia the maps have been slowly rebuilding and repairing themselves.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you informed me during your last visit to this world, the Star Maps are still in a damaged and incomplete state. It is not possible to locate the Star Forge using a single map.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: However, the Star Maps have repaired themselves to the extent that it is possible to discover the Star Forge's location by combining bits of data from several of the maps, as you did.

speaker: Player
text: They didn't do a very good job of destroying them.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me about the history of the Infinite Empire.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: At its peak the Infinite Empire ruled over 500 planets and was comprised of ten billion Rakata and over a trillion slaves scattered across the galaxy.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But the glory of the Infinite Empire was built on war and slaughter; it was inevitable it should collapse upon itself. Conflict among power-hungry warlords escalated into full civil war.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Worlds were ravaged and millions of lives were lost. Sensing the weakness of their oppressors, the slaves rebelled and overthrew their masters. And then came the plague.

speaker: Player
text: The plague?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Its origins were unknown - perhaps the creation of an enslaved species, perhaps a mutation of a natural virus. It killed only Rakata, and it spread to every corner of the galaxy.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Infinite Empire crumbled into dust as the few Rakata survivors fled back here to their home world. All evidence of their existence was destroyed by the species they once enslaved.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But even hidden here on their secret home world they were not safe. Millions died from the deadly plague, many more died in the never ending civil war.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The history of the Rakata ended twenty thousand years ago. Now they are nothing but a few scattered tribes descended from the priest and warrior castes, still waging our never ending civil war.

speaker: Player
text: What are you?

speaker: Player
text: I need some information.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore. I'm <FullName>.

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I recognize your appearance from your last visit, which is stored in my databanks. However, I am detecting some significant changes in your composition since your last visit.

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: prisoner
text: So very long a time and nothing. Then in a span of mere months three in a row! What sheer luck!

speaker: prisoner
text: Well let's have a look at you. Hmm. Biped. More or less symmetrical. Far less hair than the last one. Opposable digits. Mostly water, hey? I suppose you'll have to do.

speaker: Player
text: I'll have to do for what?

speaker: prisoner
text: Eh? For a body, of course. I don't want to remain in this prison forever, no no no.

speaker: prisoner
text: I'm a prisoner here. As are you, yes indeed... though I suspect by accident rather than by sentence, yes? I was put here on purpose.

speaker: prisoner
text: My own people put our criminals in little cages like this. Well... our minds, anyway. For really terrible criminals like me our mind gets locked away forever.

speaker: prisoner
text: How long have I been here now? Hmmm... one... four... no, no, longer than that. I've never been very good with numbers.

speaker: Player
text: This is a prison?

speaker: prisoner
text: Can you think of a better prison than one without walls? What does your species use? Cages, I suppose.

speaker: Player
text: Is there no way out of here?

speaker: prisoner
text: Well, now *that* is a most interesting question. Yes yes yes indeed.

speaker: prisoner
text: I've been here long enough to ponder that. How many years, now? A thousand? Ten thousand? Bah... I could never remember the numbers, even when I kept track.

speaker: prisoner
text: The point is that I know a way out of this clever little prison. Interesting, that, wouldn't you say?

speaker: Player
text: Out? Out to where? If you get out of here, your body's probably dead.

speaker: prisoner
text: How clever of you to realize that? Indeed you are correct. Your body, however, is not.

speaker: prisoner
text: Now before you go off getting all excited and defensive, let me tell you that I can't go jumping into your body without your willing agreement.

speaker: prisoner
text: Conversely, you can't go jumping back into your body without my knowledge. This leaves us at something of an impasse, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Player
text: So what do you suggest?

speaker: prisoner
text: What I suggest is for us to settle this now, like civilized beings.

speaker: prisoner
text: It is like this, dear sentient... if you like, we could spend the next thousand years debating. You want out, I want out, it could go on and on.

speaker: prisoner
text: Unless your species is remarkably long-lived, I doubt your body has a thousand years. And, frankly, I doubt either of us is going to convince the other of anything, yes?

speaker: prisoner
text: So why waste the time? A simple competition between the two of us and we settle the matter. You win, you go free. I win, I go free. Yes?

speaker: Player
text: How do I know I could trust you?

speaker: prisoner
text: You have no reason not to trust me, now. If I were to betray you, then you would never trust me again... and we would be stuck here arguing forever.

speaker: Player
text: It only takes once.

speaker: prisoner
text: I suppose that's true. But if you won and I did not release you, there would never be another chance for me to escape anyway, would there? You would never agree to it.

speaker: Player
text: You have a point.

speaker: prisoner
text: Hence I may as well let you go, if you win. It is my one and only opportunity for freedom.

speaker: Player
text: What kind of competition do you mean?

speaker: prisoner
text: I have little clue as to which activities you are superior at. You are at the same disadvantage with me, I suspect.

speaker: prisoner
text: So the best game is one of the mind. An exchange of riddles, perhaps. The first of us to fail at an answer loses. What do you think?

speaker: Player
text: I don't seem to have much of a choice.

speaker: prisoner
text: Now now no need to be fussy. If I seem to be moving fast it's simply because I've had an overabundance of time to consider this scenario.

speaker: prisoner
text: That being the case, and seeing as this is technically my home, I'll go first. Now... let's see...

speaker: prisoner
text: "Until I am measured, I am not known, yet how you miss me when I have flown."

speaker: Player
text: Light.

speaker: prisoner
text: Mmm? Are you quite serious with that answer? And here I thought I was only warming up. The answer is time!

speaker: prisoner
text: My, my, my... the contest is over already! Fair is fair, sentient... I go free.

speaker: prisoner
text: With luck you will someday find a body of your own, yes? So don't despair... but do hold still.

speaker: Player
text: Time.

speaker: prisoner
text: Yes yes yes... I suppose that was an easy one. Perhaps I should have used all this time to think of harder riddles, hey?

speaker: prisoner
text: Fair is fair, sentient. Your turn.

speaker: Player
text: "If you break me, I do not stop working. If you touch me, I may be snared. If you lose me, nothing will matter."

text: Oh my... there are not many things that keep working once they're broken. Hmmm... hmmmm. Snared? No no no, that's not it!

speaker: prisoner
text: I... I concede. I do not know the answer to your riddle. You are victorious.

speaker: Player
text: It's your heart.

speaker: prisoner
text: *sigh* It appears my destiny is to be imprisoned even longer. Are you ready to return to your body, sentient?

speaker: Player
text: Before I go, what's your name?

speaker: prisoner
text: Eh? My name? It's... it's... well how do you like that? I've completely forgotten.

speaker: prisoner
text: I think I knew it a thousand years ago. I guess I've been here so long I've forgotten. My, that is depressing.

speaker: Player
text: I'm ready to go.

speaker: prisoner
text: There's nothing complicated to it. It's better for me to just show you than teach you. Just close your eyes a moment, sentient...

speaker: Player
text: Right. Get me out of here, and don't do anything funny.

speaker: Player
text: I could try to find some other way to get you out of here.

speaker: prisoner
text: I doubt you could help. My people made quite certain that escaping these prisons was a difficult prospect, you know.

speaker: prisoner
text: It took me as long as I've been here to figure out the only exit... and even then, I'm sure it's only happened because my prison is no longer secure.

speaker: prisoner
text: Hmmm. I do have to wonder how that happened. Are my people still about? If they were, I can't see that they'd let my prison loose so easily.

speaker: prisoner
text: But even if they are gone, I doubt you'd be able to find any way to release me. No, I suppose I shall just have to wait for someone who is not as proficient at riddles as you are to come along.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry. I'm sure someone else will be along before you know it.

speaker: prisoner
text: You know... you're right. And maybe they won't be as intelligent as you, either. That makes me feel much better, thank you.

speaker: Player
text: I could destroy your prison once I'm out... if you wish.

speaker: prisoner
text: Oh, I certainly doubt that. No offense, but your species hardly strikes me as that advanced. Besides... I'm not ready to explode into bitty atoms just yet.

speaker: prisoner
text: Oh my... there are not many things that keep working once they're broken. Hmmm... oh! Oh, yes. Your heart! Heart is the answer!

speaker: prisoner
text: Very clever, sentient... but it is my turn once again!

speaker: prisoner
text: "I never was, yet always will be. I am never seen, yet always come. I can carry nothing, yet hold much for some."

speaker: Player
text: Tomorrow.

text: Yes yes yes, you have the right of it. Tomorrow it is.

speaker: Player
text: Gravity.

text: Aha! Caught you, I have! Tomorrow is the answer! Tomorrow!

speaker: Player
text: Rain.

speaker: Player
text: Vacuum.

speaker: prisoner
text: "Who makes it has no need of it. Who buys it has no use for it. Who uses it has no knowledge of it."

speaker: Player
text: Air.

speaker: prisoner
text: No no no, you are wrong! A grave is the answer! To bury the dead!

speaker: Player
text: Energy.

speaker: Player
text: A grave.

speaker: prisoner

speaker: prisoner
text: "I am always hungry, I must always be fed. The finger I lick will soon turn red."

speaker: Player
text: A gizka.

speaker: prisoner
text: No no no! You are wrong! A flame is the answer, to blister you red!

speaker: Player
text: A flame.

speaker: prisoner
text: Yes, it's true. I wasn't sure if you blistered as we did... but it appears you do. So be it.

speaker: Player
text: A starship engine.

speaker: Player
text: A mouth.

speaker: prisoner
text: "To keep me, I must be given. If I am not kept, I am broken."

speaker: Player
text: Love.

speaker: prisoner
text: Ha! No no no you are wrong! It is your word! You must give your word... and if your word is not kept, it is broken!

speaker: Player
text: A mirror.

speaker: Player
text: The sound barrier.

speaker: Player
text: Your word.

speaker: Player
text: "What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than the trees, up up it goes and yet it never grows."

speaker: prisoner
text: What manner of plant could that be? But it does not grow... so is it no plant at all? Think think think!

speaker: prisoner
text: What manner of plant could that be? But it does not grow... so is it no plant at all? It... it is a mountain! Yes, that is it!

speaker: Player
text: "You heard me before, yet you hear me again, Then I die, until you call me again."

speaker: prisoner
text: Hmmm... what an odd riddle. Yes yes yes, let me see. Hear again, and then call again... what could it be?

speaker: prisoner
text: Hmmm... what an odd riddle. Yes yes yes, let me see. Hear again, and then call again... an echo? It is an echo! Ha ha!

speaker: Player
text: "Flying to Dantooine I meet five ships. Each ship has five crewmen, each crewman five pets. How many in all are flying to Dantooine?"

speaker: prisoner
text: No no! Not numbers! Never have I been good with numbers! Hmmm... think think think! Five times five... add the one... no no no...

speaker: prisoner
text: Err... carry the two... ninety-four? No, ninety-six! Is it ninety-six?

speaker: Player
text: It's one. I'm the only one flying to Dantooine.

speaker: prisoner
text: Ahh! Fooled, I have been! Fooled myself! Very very clever of you! You have won!

speaker: Player
text: "You can see nothing else when you look in my face, I will look you in the eye and I will never lie."

speaker: prisoner
text: Never lie, hey? Hmmm. There is something familiar here... I cannot place my finger upon it. Look you in the eye... look you in the eye...

speaker: prisoner
text: Never lie, hey? Hmmm. There is something familiar here... I cannot place my finger upon it. Look you in the eye... your reflection! It is your reflection!

speaker: Player
text: "What does a poor man have that a rich man requires, what a miser spends and a thrifty man saves, and all men carry to their graves?"

speaker: prisoner
text: Hmmm... what a very odd and valuable thing this must be. Think think think! Is it... no no no, not that. Hmmm...

speaker: prisoner
text: Is the answer... time? Could it be?

speaker: Player
text: The answer is "nothing".

speaker: prisoner
text: Blast! Spends nothing, saves nothing, carries nothing to his grave! Yes yes yes I should have known! Ahhhhh, you have won.

speaker: Player
text: Hope.

speaker: Player
text: I'd rather a more physical challenge.

speaker: prisoner
text: Mmmm no doubt. You may have missed my earlier statement, so let me remind you that your physical body is not really here.

speaker: prisoner
text: Your muscles do not exert anything and you can apply no force here. Hence a "physical" challenge is somewhat impossible, no?

speaker: prisoner
text: So let's restrict ourselves to the mental challenges, my dear sentient.

speaker: Player
text: And what's to stop you from cheating?

speaker: prisoner
text: For that matter, what's to stop *you* from cheating? The only thing I can think of is that it's quite hard to cheat at riddles. Fair is fair.

speaker: Player
text: What are the rules?

speaker: prisoner
text: Hmm. Perhaps we should restrict ourselves from riddles specific to our culture or race. A kiratta-sarn, while wonderful to look at, would be meaningless to you, I'm sure.

speaker: prisoner
text: Beyond that, I shouldn't think there be any rules necessary. A riddle is a riddle. So are we agreed?

speaker: Player
text: This sounds deceptively simple.

speaker: prisoner
text: Does it? In truth, I've had a long time to think it over. You can take your time thinking about it, yourself, but why?

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! Tell me how to get out! NOW!!

speaker: prisoner
text: Why would I do that? And however would you coerce me to do so? No no no... we play or you stay. Simple as that.

speaker: Player
text: Look... you are *not* getting my body.

speaker: prisoner

speaker: Player

speaker: Player

speaker: prisoner
text: Why would I not tell you? My escape requires your involvement... and your body, I might add.

speaker: Player
text: Let me guess: there's a catch.

speaker: prisoner
text: Isn't there always? There's only one place that one of us can escape to... and that's your body. Mine, I'm sure, is not available.

speaker: Player
text: What did you do to get imprisoned here?

speaker: prisoner
text: I led a war. Well, a rebellion really, though the details would hardly interest you. Many of my kind died, and I'm responsible... or so they said.

speaker: Player
text: You said "three in a row" earlier. Have there been others besides me?

speaker: prisoner
text: Oh yes yes indeed. Two others of entirely different species visited me before you. I couldn't speak with them like I can with you, however.

speaker: prisoner
text: They eventually grew angry and ran off into the whiteness. If you go far enough out, you may find them... though I wouldn't recommend it.

speaker: prisoner
text: They're likely quite mad. All this whiteness can do that to you, you know. It'll drive you mad mad mad. If you let it.

speaker: Player
text: Just keep your distance, I'm warning you.

speaker: prisoner

speaker: prisoner
