text: I... I love you. And I...I can't wait until all of this is over with.

speaker: Player
text: I love you, too.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey! Sheesh... get a room, will ya?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: That two spirits have found each other amidst such turmoil is a good omen, Mission. Does it not please you to see?

speaker: Mission
text: Oh, sure. Even a good omen can get itself a room, though, don't ya think?

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, I'm an old man and I know you should take love when you can find it. Good for you two, I say.

speaker: T3M3
text: Beep! Beep-beep boop!!

speaker: HK47
text: Answer: I have no idea what they speak of, droid. Organic meatbags are an eternal mystery to me.

speaker: Juhani
text: Confidence is all well and good, Carth, but if we are going to catch up to Bastila we should leave soon, don't you think?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Okay - let's get moving. The longer we wait the harder this is going to be!

speaker: Player
text: Hey, cool your engines there.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Right. Sorry. I just... can't remember the last time I felt this happy. I can wait until the Star Forge is destroyed.

speaker: Mission
text: You make that sound so easy. Just fly over and boom, one less Star Forge in the universe, huh?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I feel more confident now than I ever did before. The Force is with us, Mission.

speaker: Player
text: We've got a long way to go yet, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: I could never do what Bastila did.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know. I can't blame Bastila for being turned, however... she's...she's just so young and doesn't deserve this kind of fate.

speaker: Player
text: Thank you. I appreciate the support.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Always. I'm not certain any one of us wouldn't have been tempted by Bastila's offer.

speaker: Player
text: I chose the light side. It's true.

speaker: Player
text: Once and for all? What are you talking about?

speaker: Jolee
text: Bastila tried to tempt her to the dark side, to reclaim Revan's heritage. She failed.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No doubt. Let's go, then, before she has time to organize a bigger welcoming committee.

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm not sure what's in store for us, but I sense Bastila still has a role to play. I have no doubt she'll be waiting for us on the Star Forge.

speaker: Player
text: It took the whole Jedi Council and a mind wipe to save me. What chance does she have?

speaker: Player
text: It's too late for her. Just accept it.

speaker: Player
text: I can't help but feel this is partly my fault.

speaker: Jolee
text: In the end we all choose our own path, but keep in mind the role that you played in her downfall. You and the task assigned to her by the Jedi Council.

speaker: Player
text: Malak corrupted Bastila because she was weak.

speaker: Jolee
text: Weakness has nothing to do with the corruption of the dark side. A Jedi must always guard against pride and the desire for power. Especially you.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila is lost to us now. She deserves to die.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila is dead, Carth. Malak killed her.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Dead? I... I can't believe it.

speaker: Juhani
text: She is not dead, Carth - though maybe that might have been easier for you to accept. She has fallen to the dark side and fled to the Star Forge.

speaker: Jolee
text: She's not dead, Carth - though that might have been easier for you to accept. She's fallen to the dark side and fled to the Star Forge.

speaker: Player
text: No time! We have to get off this planet and get to the Star Forge!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hold on a second! What about Bastila? Wasn't she in the Temple? Wh...what happened?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Bastila - you're alive! I was worried about you. For a minute there I was sure we'd never see you again once Malak got his... w... wait a minute.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Where are Juhani and Jolee Bindo? Are they okay? What happened inside that temple?

speaker: Player
text: I have reclaimed the title of Darth Revan! Bow before me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What... what are you talking about?

speaker: Bastila
text: The Jedi Council has failed, Carth - Darth Revan has been reborn! Together we will destroy Malak and seize control of his fleet, then use it to crush the Republic!

speaker: Bastila
text: Juhani and Jolee would not swear loyalty to the new ruler of the Sith. They died for their foolishness. Now swear loyalty to Darth Revan, or face your own death!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No, you can't mean that! This... this isn't you! You're not Revan, I know it!

speaker: Player
text: I am Revan, Carth. Now and forever.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You've got to resist it! Th... this isn't you talking... we... we can help you, we can find a way --

speaker: Bastila
text: My, my. I think the sad fool may actually be in love with you, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: This is my choice, Carth, whether you like it or not.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I refuse to believe that! We'll...we'll stop you if we have to, all of us. We'll save you from yourselves!

speaker: Player
text: Don't resist me, Carth, or I'll be forced to destroy you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Wait, Lord Revan. Carth speaks only for himself - he does not speak for the others. He may find he stands alone here!

speaker: Bastila
text: The droids will continue to serve you Revan - they are programmed to obey their master. And there may be others who will choose to join us.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Republic is doomed, Revan has returned! Who will now swear loyalty to the second coming of the Dark Lord?

speaker: Cand
text: You're Revan and I'll follow you anywhere. It doesn't matter who you're fighting against, I'll be at your side. Mandalorians don't have any great love for the Republic anyway.

speaker: Cand
text: Light side, dark side - it doesn't make any difference to me, Revan. I'll stick by you no matter what comes.

speaker: Player
text: Mission, what about you?

speaker: Mission
text: I saw what the Sith did to Taris - anyone who serves the dark side is evil! Big Z and I are with Carth on this one!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: No, Mission. I am bound by the oath of my life debt. I... I must stand with Revan.

speaker: Mission
text: Zaalbar - Revan's a Sith! Just like Malak! It's not a betrayal if you break your life debt now!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: If I go back on my vow I am betraying myself, my people and my ancestors. I cannot do that. Please, Mission - join us.

speaker: Mission
text: No, Zaalbar. I don't care! I won't help the Sith against the Republic! Not for anything! Not even for you!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You don't have to help the Sith, Mission. Not while I'm here.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I see now it was a mistake to let you go into that Temple. I of all people should have seen this coming. First Saul Karath, and now you... I mean, I should be an expert on betrayal by now!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But nothing you can say or do can make me betray the Republic. I won't join you, and I won't just stand aside and let you become ruler of the Sith again, Revan!

speaker: Player
text: You don't stand a chance against all of us, Carth.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I... I'll find a way to save you, I swear! I won't give up on you... no matter what!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Run for it, Mission! Go! Go!

speaker: Bastila
text: Let him go! We have more important things to worry about. We have to get to the Star Forge and kill Malak. Then we can turn our attention to the Republic.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Run for it, Mission! Go! Go!

speaker: Mission
text: No, Carth! Don't do it!

speaker: Player
text: Then I guess it's time for you to die!

speaker: Player
text: It's too bad it had to come to this, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: Zaalbar, what about you?

speaker: Player
text: Not everyone is willing to throw their life away for the Republic, Carth!

speaker: Player
text: Not everyone is as foolish as you are, Carth!

speaker: Player
text: All of you? Are you sure of that?

speaker: Player
text: I guess I'll just have to kill you all, then.

speaker: Player
text: Join me, Carth. You can rule at my side, it's not too late.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No, never! You're not the woman I love. We'll stop you if we have to, all of us.

speaker: Player
text: How sad. I guess there's no future for us after all, is there?

speaker: Player
text: Does it matter who I am? I have joined the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be a blind fool, Carth. Open your eyes.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Wh... what? No! We serve the Republic! You're no better than Malak! We'll never swear allegiance to one who serves the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: If you resist me, I'll destroy you all!

speaker: Player
text: Only you serve the Republic, Carth. You don't speak for the others.

speaker: Bastila
text: Jolee would not swear loyalty to the new ruler of the Sith. He died for his foolishness. Now swear loyalty to Darth Revan, or face your own death!

speaker: Player
text: They didn't make it.

speaker: Player
text: I went over to the dark side, Carth. That's what happened.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Where's Jolee Bindo? Is he okay? What happened inside that temple?

speaker: Player
text: He didn't make it.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Kashyyyk... my home. I should have prepared you for coming here... but I don't know if I've prepared myself.

speaker: Player
text: Prepared me? What do you mean?

text: I am an exile. The slavers on Kashyyyk only took me after I was forced to leave my village home, 20 years ago.

text: Why were you forced to leave?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: My brother made deals with the slavers and allowed them to get a foothold. I found out and attacked him.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: The fight was stopped, but my father did not believe me when I told him about my brother's actions.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I was made an exile, disowned by my home and people. I should not be here. They will not accept me back.

speaker: Player
text: Why didn't your father believe you?

text: When I attacked my brother I was so mad... I used my claws. You don't understand what that means to a Wookiee.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Our claws are tools, not weapons. To use them in battle is to become an animal. It is madness without honor.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I am forever a madclaw in the eyes of my people. Nothing I say is to be trusted. They were right to cast me out.

speaker: Player
text: We'll deal with that if we have to. Let's go.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I don't have much hope.

speaker: Player
text: Time has passed. Things will have changed.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: The slavers are still here... this dock is theirs. I doubt anyone has risen to try and fight. Nothing has changed.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I just hope I can prove myself to my people. It will be difficult to make them listen. I just don't know.

speaker: Player
text: That's enough. I'll learn the rest on my own.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Then stumble blindly. I won't speak of it again until it is in your face.

speaker: Player
text: I don't care, I'll learn what I need myself.

speaker: Player
text: It's a little late for warnings, fur ball.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Don't mock me, this is hard. Mission may have told you I was taken from here by slavers... but there is more.

speaker: Mission
text: Zaalbar should be here. He shouldn't miss this. He needs to know he can come back here.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Mission
text: I can't talk for Big Z, but believe me, he should be with us. He's got... unfinished business here.

speaker: Player
text: I decide who comes or stays on the ship.

speaker: Mission
text: I'm not saying that I know better than you, but this is Zaalbar's home. Don't you think he'd know some things?

speaker: Mission
text: Besides, he's got things here he needs to take care of.

speaker: Carth
text: The Wookiee was looking pretty agitated back in the ship. You think it's wise to leave him unattended?

speaker: Bastila
text: Perhaps you should reconsider leaving Zaalbar behind. This is, after all, his homeworld.

speaker: Juhani
text: It is always good to know as much as possible about a world, and to have a reliable guide. Perhaps we should get Zaalbar to accompany us.

speaker: Cand
text: Hmph. Maybe we should have brought the Wookiee out. This place looks... untamed.

speaker: Juhani
text: Are you afraid of the wild, Mandalore? Are you a coward?

speaker: Cand
text: Mandalorians are not cowards! We're just practical.

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: You should have brought the Wookiee Zaalbar, despite the smell. He would have knowledge of this place, master.

speaker: Player
text: He has been away a long time.

speaker: HK47
text: Retort: "A long time" is still more frequent than "never," which is how many times the rest of us have been here, master.

speaker: Wookiee Rebel
text: Raargh!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This unsavory looking man appears to be looking for someone... maybe even one of your companions back on the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: *grunt* What the hell is your kind doing here? Bad enough I have to deal with all these other idiots, but now there's a stinkin' Cathar on this world too?

speaker: Juhani
text: I have as much right to be here as you do, SIR!

speaker: Player
text: Do not seek to aggravate us.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Ooooo! Big man, the Jedi, shooting his mouth off from behind a lightsaber, or whatever you're carrying.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hiding behind your pet Cathar... And a woman at that!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We should have exterminated all you Cathar when we had the chance.

speaker: Juhani
text: Wha... What do you know about my world?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know enough that... Hey, wait a minute... you look familiar somehow...

speaker: Juhani
text: What? You...

speaker: Player
text: Do you two know each other?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This doesn't concern you, Jedi trash.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hm... now where could I have... No, he's dead and she likely is too. I...

speaker: Juhani
text: What are you talking about??

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Maybe I was wrong. Still, I think a specimen like you would be a nice addition to my collection.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So what would it take, Jedi, for you to sell your pet here to me?

speaker: Player
text: She is not for sale!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Now don't be so selfish. We both know Cathar aren't real people anyway.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The females make amusing pets, but males should be put down like the animals they are. I remember one time on Taris...

speaker: Juhani
text: What?! WHAT DID YOU SAY?!

speaker: Player
text: What are you saying?

speaker: Juhani
text: WHAT DID YOU DO ON TARIS, YOU SCUM?!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Put one of you down like the animals you are. So easy... then I saw one of the females on the auction block, but those darn Jedi...

speaker: Juhani
text: It was you!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What? Me? Oh ho! Now I recognize where I've seen that face before.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You were the little Cathar I was going to purchase. But those Jedi came and stole my pet away from me!

speaker: Player
text: You bought Juhani?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: When I was fighting with the Mandalorians against the Cathar, I developed an appreciation for these creatures. They make excellent servants if properly trained.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You Jedi act all prim and proper, but inside you must feel the same way I do about the lesser, non-human species. The Sith at least let their feelings show on the outside.

speaker: Juhani
text: You... My homeworld...

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Come now, will you let your pet go? I'm sure we can come up with a price we both think is fair.

speaker: Player
text: You'll only hurt her if I let her go.

speaker: Juhani
text: NO, I WILL NOT BE SOLD!

speaker: Juhani
text: And I will see you dead for what you have done to my people!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Uh... hold on a second! Don't be hasty!

speaker: Player
text: Do not fall to the dark side again, Juhani.

speaker: Juhani
text: I... I will remain calm. I am a Jedi now.

speaker: Juhani
text: My lust for vegeance must be curbed.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, yes... Say no to the dark side...

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I will have you yet! Heh.

text: Just ignore him, Juhani.

text: A big mouth like that can get you killed.

text: What do you mean?

text: You... you animal! You wretch!

text: I will not give him the satisfaction of seeing me give in to the dark side.

speaker: Xor

text: I killed your people on Cathar in the sky, on the ground, in their homes. I hunted them down like the animals they were, just to see them burn.

speaker: Xor
text: But the treacherous beasts fought back and left me with injuries that meant I could never fight again... or so they thought!

speaker: Player
text: Stop trying to provoke her!

speaker: Juhani
text: No, I will not give in to him.

speaker: Xor
text: I ended up in the Lower City of Taris, and what did I find? A few of those stinking beasts living there!

speaker: Xor
text: The male was easy enough to best, but the females proved elusive. I didn't know what happened to them after I killed the male, until I saw this cursed woman on the auction block.

speaker: Xor

speaker: Player
text: Just step away.

speaker: Player
text: Reunion? What are you talking about?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What? Ha-ha-ha! You mean you don't know? Ha-ha-ha! All this time, and you still haven't figured it out? Ha-ha-ha!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I wonder how long you would have stayed blind to the truth? Surely some of what you once were must have surfaced by now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Even the combined power of the Jedi Council couldn't keep your true identity buried forever, could it?

speaker: Player
text: Why did the Jedi spare me? I don't understand...

speaker: Player
text: This meeting was inevitable, Malak!

text: As is the outcome. I am actually surprised this confrontation did not happen sooner, given how powerful your mind once was.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You cannot hide from what you once were, Revan! Recognize that you were once the Dark Lord - and know that I have taken your place!

speaker: Player
text: No... this is some type of trick! A Sith lie!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You do not yet remember, Revan? The Jedi set a trap. They lured us into battle against a small Republic fleet. During the attack a team of Jedi knights boarded your ship.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Jedi strike team captured you and the Council used the Force to reprogram your mind; they wiped away your identity and turned you against your own followers.

speaker: Player
text: No, I don't believe you, Malak!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You must have seen flashes of your old life in your dreams, Revan; memories bubbling up to the surface? Surely you must remember the battle in which you were captured?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: How you survived the final battle is a mystery to me. Perhaps you should ask Bastila; after all, she was part of the Jedi strike team that captured you!

speaker: Player
text: Bastila, is this true?

speaker: Bastila
text: It's true. I was part of the team sent to capture Revan... to capture you. When Malak fired on the ship you were badly injured. We thought you were dead.

speaker: Bastila
text: Your mind was destroyed, but I used the Force to preserve the flicker of life in your body. I brought you to the Jedi Council. They were the ones who healed your damaged mind.

speaker: Player
text: Then why don't I remember being Revan?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Jedi Council didn't restore your wounded mind, Revan! They merely programmed it with a new identity - one loyal to the Republic! They tried to make you their slave!

speaker: Player
text: You've been lying to me this whole time, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: I wanted to tell you, but the Council forbid it! They were afraid you might return to the dark side if you discovered your real identity!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But now you know the truth, Revan! The Council has failed in their attempt to make you their pawn! The will of a Sith Lord is not so easily manipulated!

speaker: Player
text: Why not just let me die?

speaker: Bastila
text: The Jedi hold all life sacred, even that of a Sith Lord. I could not just let you die, Revan. Not if it was possible to save you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Bastila hides the truth behind noble words, Revan! The Jedi needed the memories buried deep in your wounded mind; there was no other way to bring them out. They had to keep you alive!

speaker: Player
text: But why program me with another identity?

speaker: Bastila
text: We couldn't simply restore your true identity; Revan was too dangerous. But locked inside your mind was information the Republic needed: the secrets of the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Council created an identity for you: a soldier under my command. Your subconscious memories were supposed to lead me to the Star Forge; there was no other way to get the information.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They made you their puppet, Revan - and Bastila was the handler pulling your strings!

speaker: Player
text: Why you, Bastila? Why did the Council choose you?

speaker: Bastila
text: When I used my Force powers to keep you alive on that bridge it created our bond. I convinced the Council that I could use that bond to draw out your memories and lead us to the Star Forge.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Tell the truth, Bastila, you wanted to taste the dark side for yourself! You knew the only way the Council would permit you to explore the Sith's power was through Revan's lost memories!

speaker: Bastila
text: NO! I wanted to help you, Revan. I thought this mission would redeem you; that it would atone for your past crimes. How else could you be saved?

speaker: Player
text: But what if I remembered who I really was?

speaker: Bastila
text: You had to be healed so I could try and draw out the secrets of the Star Forge - it was our only hope of stopping the Sith! It was a risk the Council chose to take.

speaker: Player
text: I understand, Bastila. You had no other choice.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Forgiveness, Revan? You are weak; I was right to betray you. You are not fit to rule the Sith!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: A small part of me has always regretted betraying you from afar. I always knew there were some who would think I acted out of fear, that I did not want to face you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But now fate has given me a second chance to prove myself. Once I defeat you in combat no one will question my claim to the Sith throne; my triumph will be complete!

speaker: Player
text: Your power is no match for the light!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Jedi Council were foolish to let you live. I won't make the same mistake. We shall finish this alone in the ancient Sith tradition: master versus apprentice, as it was meant to be!

speaker: Player
text: Triumph, Malak? You seem to forget that I'm still alive!

text: You have returned! I was beginning to fear that you, too, might have been lost. Did you find out what had happened down there at the facility?

text: The Selkath went insane.

text: Insane? What did they do? And why?

text: They killed almost everyone on the Station.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They killed... everyone? And the mercenaries we sent later? That is... horrible. What caused them to all go insane at once like that?

speaker: Player
text: Your construction woke something up.

text: Something was down there? Living in the Rift by the kolto?

text: A gigantic firaxan shark that drove all the Selkath insane.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That's... horrible. The entire operation wasted by a disaster we could never in a thousand years have foreseen.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What has happened to the facility itself? Were there any survivors?

speaker: Player
text: A few scientists have survived.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Well, that is good to know. Good to know indeed. But... What has happened to the facility? Was it damaged?

speaker: Player
text: The harvesting machine was destroyed.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No! That is terrible. That will set our work back years... *sigh* It may even cost us the war.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: While I am glad that you were able to solve our problems, the cost may have ended up being much too high.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But you have done your job and helped us in our time of need, and for that I thank you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Oh, and did you end up finding your Star Map?

speaker: Player
text: Yes I did.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you can see, by helping us you helped yourself. Perhaps we can work together again in the future.

speaker: Player
text: None of your business!

text: I'll assume that means yes. As you can see, by helping us you helped yourself. Perhaps we can work together in the future.

text: The kolto seems to have been contaminated.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This must remain entirely secret. We cannot allow anyone to find out that we damaged the kolto production or we would be banned permanently from the planet.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We can only hope that the damage that was caused will go away in time.

text: Thank you for destroying the tribe of the One. We do not believe in needless violence, but they could not be reasoned with.

text: With the death of the One the terrible secrets of our ancestors are once again safe. Thank you, Revan.

text: I have to give you credit... you've led me on quite a chase. But nobody gets away from Calo Nord in the end!

speaker: Player
text: How did you get down here?

speaker: CaloNord

speaker: Duros
text: You have defeated the murderous animals! We thank you, human, for saving us!

speaker: Player
text: Er... No problem!

speaker: Duros
text: If your arrival had not been so fortuitously timed, we would have been in great danger. We thank you again for saving us.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here?

speaker: Duros
text: We had crashed here when our mining survey vessel encountered some strange sort of energy field. It disrupted our engine and power system and forced us to make a crash landing on this world.

speaker: Duros
text: Our ship sank far out to sea, but a handful of us were able to make it to this island... more than you see here, though.

speaker: Player
text: Where are the rest of your companions?

speaker: Duros
text: Many have been killed at the hands of the locals. A few tried to swim to one of the closer islands, but we have not heard from them in many days.

speaker: Duros
text: Of the 10 of us who remained here, we two are the only remaining survivors...

speaker: Player
text: The native creatures killed the others?

speaker: Duros
text: They attack any they come across. They are barbaric savages who feast upon the bodies of the dead!

speaker: Duros
text: The only beings who crash here that can hold them off are the Mandalorians, and we dare not go near them... we know of their depredations too well.

speaker: Player
text: There are Mandalorians here??

speaker: Duros
text: Yes, there are. More than you might think, although that may just be because they aren't killed as easily as we are.

speaker: Duros
text: With their weapons they raid and kill other survivors, and can fight off the natives as well. They seem to have some sort of invisibility or light cloaking shield that hides them until they strike.

speaker: Player
text: Where are they?

speaker: Duros
text: They are north of here by a large temple structure. We dare not approach it, for they would surely kill us.

speaker: Duros
text: But we cannot delay here much longer... The longer we stay, the more likely either the Mandalorians or the natives will find us and kill us.

speaker: Player
text: Why don't you try to get to one of the other islands?

speaker: Duros
text: I believe that would be the best choice... The others have not returned, but it may be because they could find no way to.

speaker: Duros
text: It would be worth the risk, rather than stay here and face certain death...

speaker: Duros
text: I thank you one last time, human, for saving us. We shall remember you, and hope that, should you escape, you will tell the Republic of those of us stranded here.

speaker: Player
text: You could stay in our ship if you want.

speaker: Duros
text: No, we dare not. If we remain here, it will only be a matter of time before the natives or the Mandalorians find us and kill us.

speaker: Player
text: Tell me of the natives.

speaker: Duros
text: We know little beyond what we have told you already... savages who eat the dead and attack anyone on sight. If it were not for them, this world might almost be habitable...

speaker: Player
text: Has anyone found a way off this world?

speaker: Duros
text: The Sith... we have seen Sith interceptors in the sky once or twice... They appear to be able to fly unimpeded through the field which forced us to crash. If we could somehow find a ship of theirs...

speaker: Duros
text: But it is too much to hope for. The Sith would surely kill us on sight if we were found. Much better to hide and hope the Republic finds us here eventually.

speaker: Duros
text: We believe they may have something to do with the large temple structure to the north of here. We have been suspicious of that structure since we landed, but we cannot approach it... the Mandalorians hunt in that area.

speaker: Player
text: What happened?

speaker: Player
text: It's not like me to crush insects like you, but I'm bored, so...

speaker: Duros
text: What?! You... No!

speaker: Player
text: Why would they have attacked you?

speaker: Player
text: How do you know I'm friendly to you?

speaker: Duros
text: Why... why would you not be? All we survivors on this strange world must band together, else the marauding inhabitants would slaughter us all!

speaker: Player
text: Actually, I'm not here to save you.

speaker: Duros
text: You... you are not? Then what are you here for?

speaker: Player
text: I have to find a way off this world.

speaker: Duros
text: As do we all.

speaker: Duros
text: We have seen little in the short time we have been on this world that would indicate a way off... except...

speaker: Player
text: Except?

speaker: Player
text: Spill it!

speaker: Player
text: It's not like I had a choice...

speaker: Duros
text: None of us are here by choice... and all seek a way to escape.

speaker: Player
text: I'm here to finish the job they started!

speaker: Player
text: Well, they attacked me first...

speaker: Player
text: If I had known you were there, I would have waited a couple minutes...

speaker: Duros
text: If you had... had waited for a better opportunity, yes! But then we would have been in danger... but I can see your point!

speaker: Duros
text: You are smart as well as valorous. We thank you again for saving us.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You will find my prices have increased dramatically, human. Kolto production is faltering, and the Manaan government has raised all taxes on goods sold to foreigners.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to see what's in stock.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am certain you will see that all of my inventory is of superior quality.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am far too busy to spend my time conversing, human. I must reserve my time for paying customers, not idle gossip.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll be going now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Until next time, human.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings, human. In these troubled times with difficulties between the Republic and our government here, know that you can always find the goods you need with me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings, human. While the Sith have suffered setbacks here on Manaan and their goods are in short supply, you can rest assured that I will always have what you need.

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greetings, human. There are few places in Ahto City where off-worlders are welcome, but here they are at least tolerated.

text: You there! Human! You are placed under the arrest of the Ahto City Civil Authority!

speaker: Player
text: What? Why?

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Though the Sith Embassy here is considered sovereign territory of the Sith Empire, we have been monitoring an alarming number of weapon discharges and detonations from within the base.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Inquiries to the staff of the Embassy yielded no response. It would seem that contact had been cut.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Our cameras recorded you entering the base shortly before contact was lost and fighting apparently began.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: It is the conclusion of the Ahto City Civil Authority that you are responsible for the disturbance here, and you are hereby placed under arrest. You will come with us to await your trial.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: As material witnesses, the individuals who accompany you will be detained at your vessel, and the vessel itself prohibited from leaving Manaan.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: We will leave. Now. Do not attempt to resist, or we shall resort to overwhelming force.

speaker: Selkath Officer

speaker: Player
text: You'll never take me alive!

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Do not be foolish, human! We have the entire armed forces of Manaan at our disposal. You WILL submit to our authority!

speaker: Bastila
text: Dantooine... it seems like a lifetime since I last set foot on her surface, though in truth it has only been a few months. We should be safe from Malak here... for now, at least.

speaker: Carth
text: Safe? You saw what his fleet did to Taris: there wasn't a building over two stories high left standing! They...they turned the planet into one big pile of rubble.

speaker: Bastila
text: Even the Sith would think twice before attacking Dantooine. There are many Jedi here, including several of the most powerful Masters of the Order. There is great strength within this place.

speaker: Player
text: I agree with Bastila. We should be safe here.

speaker: Bastila
text: We can get supplies here and recuperate. The Academy is a place of mental and spiritual healing; something we could all use after what we've been through.

speaker: Carth
text: Maybe you're right. It isn't easy to witness the annihilation of an entire planet. I know Mission must be taking it pretty hard.

speaker: Bastila
text: She will find a way to come to terms with her grief. She is stronger than she appears. We just need to give her time.

speaker: Bastila
text: Now I must go speak with the Council. I need their advice on... recent developments. After I have met with them I will meet you outside the ship.

speaker: Player
text: I think Carth has a point. We should keep moving.

speaker: Bastila
text: We can't just keep running; Malak will find us eventually. We need to regroup; we need a plan.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Force has given us a... a vision. Like the one we shared on Dantooine. Did you see it? Of course... you must have. The Force is strong with us both.

speaker: Bastila
text: There are some who believe Korriban is the birth place of the Sith... this planet is an evil place. There are secrets here best left uncovered.

speaker: Player
text: It looked like the Star Map was in some sort of cave.

speaker: Bastila
text: During the vision I felt cold and trapped; almost as if I was buried alive. It felt... it felt like we were in some kind of tomb.

speaker: Bastila
text: No doubt things will become more clear once we discover the Star Map's location.

speaker: Player
text: Won't the Sith recognize you?

speaker: Bastila
text: Hmmm... maybe you're right. Most of the dark Jedi would only know me by name, but there are a few among them who might recognize my face.

speaker: Bastila
text: For the safety of our mission I must remain on the Ebon Hawk while we are on this planet.

speaker: Player
text: It would be safer if you stayed hidden on the ship.

speaker: Player
text: We have to uncover those secrets if we want to stop Malak.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are right, of course. We cannot turn away from the path we have started on... no matter where it may lead.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for your visions, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: The visions are as much yours as mine - and they are the key to finding the Star Forge and stopping Malak!

speaker: Bastila
text: The Wookiees of Kashyyyk make their home high among the wroshyr branches; only their bravest warriors dare to descend into the forbidding depths of the forest.

speaker: Bastila
text: If the Star Map is located far beneath us on the planet's surface, as our vision seems to suggest, it is unlikely the Wookiees even know of its existence.

speaker: Bastila
text: The Star Map would likely have to be within some kind of shelter to protect it against dust and sandstorms.

speaker: Bastila
text: I suspect there are many such caves and caverns hidden in the sands of the Dune Sea. The creatures of this world probably use them as their lairs.

speaker: Bastila
text: The ocean floor is vast and much of it is uncharted, even by the native Selkath. But how could Revan and Malak have found their way down?

speaker: Bastila
text: Kashyyyk is a lush but simple and undeveloped world. I would not have expected to find the alien technology of a Star Map here.

speaker: Player
text: It looked like the Star Map was on the forest floor.

speaker: Player
text: Do you think the Wookiees are involved?

speaker: Bastila
text: Tatooine is known for little but blowing sand. I find it surprising that there would be a Star Map somewhere in its desolate wastes.

speaker: Player
text: It looked like it was inside some kind of cave.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe Tatooine wasn't always a desert.

speaker: Bastila
text: Perhaps, though that would have been tens of thousands of years in the past. Now there is nothing but the howling emptiness of the Dune Sea.

speaker: Bastila
text: It is strange that anyone would have built a Star Map here; the entire surface of Manaan is covered by nothing but vast oceans.

speaker: Player
text: It looked like the Star Map was underwater.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe the land was once above the surface.

speaker: Bastila
text: It is possible. The melting of polar caps or a cataclysmic earthquake could have buried the land beneath the waves eons ago. Records from that time are incomplete.

speaker: Bastila
text: Another vision. The Force is guiding us, helping us retrace the steps of Malak and his old Master. Leading us ever closer to the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: You felt it, yes? Another vision? The Force continues to work through us; showing us the Star Maps unearthed by Revan and Malak.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Can you sense it? The wind... the sound... the smells? I feel it all now that we are away from the spaceport.
comment: This dialogue is launched by the player crossing a trigger in 22ab, halfway between the exit and the village If Zaalbar ISN'T in the party, the dialogue fires ONCE for some other party member to say something. If Zaalbar is in the party later and croses the trigger, but the plot has not been completed, then this dialogue would launch again for him and him only (this would happen if the player left the Ebon Hawk, explored a bit of Kashyyyk but DID NOT talk to Chuundar, then returned to the ship and picked up Zaalbar)

speaker: Zaalbar
text: This walkway is new, probably built by the slavers, but I remember the trees. My village is not far from here.

speaker: Player
text: What can I expect to encounter?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I'm sorry, I don't know. It has been so long since I left. I only know the way things were, and many things may have changed.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I must warn you of one thing... I don't know if I will be a help or hindrance to you here. My father was very powerful... a chieftain.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Perhaps his feelings have mellowed, but if my brother had his ear all this time... I may be very unwelcome.

speaker: Player
text: We'll deal with that when the time comes.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: That is what I am dreading. My shame was meant to be forgotten on some far away world. I never thought I'd come back.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I'm sorry, I've taken enough of your time. We should press on.

speaker: Player
text: I don't have time for your family squabbles.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I'm not asking you to deal with anything. I just wanted you to know about potential problems.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Bah, do what you want with this information. I won't say any more about it.

speaker: Player
text: Is there anything I can help you with?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It is kind of you to offer, but my problems are very personal. I'm not sure if I am ready to deal with them.

speaker: Player
text: We're here for the Star Map. Nothing else, understand?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Yes, your outsider concerns must always come first. Just remember that this was my home. You are the stranger here.

speaker: Mission
text: I never thought I'd see the big trees. Zaalbar's stories didn't do it justice. This is incredible.

speaker: Mission
text: I wish he was here to see this. He'd want to see this, you know?

speaker: Carth
text: This planet is incredible! It's too bad Zaalbar isn't with us. It would be nice to have a guide who's familiar with this place.

speaker: Juhani
text: This place is wild and untamed. It stirs the blood and makes one feel alive. It is a shame the Wookiee is not here with us; I have no doubt he would feel the same way.

speaker: Bastila
text: This place is so wonderful, yet so strange. Maybe we should have Zaalbar with us. A guide with local knowledge could be invaluable.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If you are not a student here, then your questions should be addressed to the Jedi Council.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am afraid that I am too busy to answer you questions.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You have done well in bringing Juhani back into the light. I am sure that once she gets past her remorse, she will be a model Jedi.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It was most regrettable that you could not save Juhani. She was an endearing, if rash, pupil.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Do not let the lessons she has given us all elude you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, apprentice? What is it you require?

speaker: Player
text: I wish to know about the Jedi Code.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: There is much to learn of the Jedi Code, and much subtlety in what is there.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You would do well to learn from the example of my student, Garrum: There is no ignorance, there is knowledge.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Know this, and you can never fail.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: For the rest of the Code, I suggest you ask some of the other Jedi here. Know your peers as well.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Is there anything else you require?

speaker: Player
text: Do you know anything about the corrupted grove?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The dark side holds great sway over people, places and things. It is not always obvious from where this dark power comes.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If the Council has told you to investigate, perhaps you should do just that.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about the Mandalorian raiders?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Mandalorians have been scattered across the Outer Rim since their defeat by the Republic years ago. They have managed to survive by raiding for food and credits.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I have not heard much about any activities of theirs on Dantooine. I spend much of my time in seclusion meditating. Perhaps another may help you.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am Master Tar'eelok. I train here with, and under, Master Zhar Lestin.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: A Jedi's training is never over, even when one has a padawan of their own.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Knowledge will be the key to our eventual victory over the Sith. Knowledge of our weaknesses and theirs.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Knowing yourself is the key to any great battle.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know of the Council?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They are great and powerful Jedi, all. Do not be intimidated by them, however. If there is something you wish to know from them, merely ask.

speaker: Player
text: What is this Cortosis ore you mentioned?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Cortosis mineral is a rare and unique substance that has the property of being able to deflect the beam of a lightsaber.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Although the process for forging it into blades was developed by the Echani for their dueling culture, it has since spread across the galaxy.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Sith have taken to providing blades of this type to their mercenaries and pawns, so that they would prove more effective against us.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It does raise the possibility of those same mercenaries being effective against their Sith masters in turn, but given the overpowering military might of the Sith at the moment, it is unlikely.

speaker: Player
text: I must go now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As you will.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I hope that the Force guides you well on your quest, Padawan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, Padawan? What is it you require?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Greeting, young human. You are welcome in my humble abode, as are all others who deign to visit this poor, outcast Hutt.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I am known as Shuma. I am one of the many who have been made poor and disadvantaged by this cruel, cruel war.

speaker: Player
text: What are you doing here?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Alas, even a poor Hutt businessman is not exempt from the fires of the conflict that now rage between the Sith and the Republic.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The world my business was based on, Neka, was subject to a most unexpected and unfortunate attack by the Sith armada.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The space lanes were clear one day, then the next they were filled with Sith interceptors and closed to traffic.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I had under my employ - quite unwittingly, of course - certain transport pilots who knew ways to slip me past the blockade above that world.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That is the only means by which I managed to escape Neka before the Sith commander deemed it worthless and virus-bombed all intelligent life from it...

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It gives one a new appreciation of the value of the... sometimes troubling Jedi Order.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Is there anything else you wish?

speaker: Player
text: You're a Hutt!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hahaha! You are most perceptive, I see! Not many people can tell that at first glance.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I know that is not what you meant. I labor under the misconceptions and biases against my species.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We have the unfortunate reputation, you see, of being criminals and murderers and worse...

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I am merely a businessman who has been cast out from his home in this most cruel war. Your Council has seen fit to grant me asylum here away from the dangers in this sector.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But enough about my troubles. What more would you have of me?

speaker: Player
text: I must be going now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Good luck to you then, in all your endeavors. Should you come back to me, I would be grateful for any conversation.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Welcome back, young Jedi. You are kind to spend time with a poor, old Hutt.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Welcome back, young apprentice. You are kind to spend time with a poor, old Hutt.

text: Oh... uh... hello, officer. Making another patrol, are you? Well, I won't get in your way.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't hurt me! Just... just take what you want. I won't try to stop you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Before the Sith arrived there was talk of changing Taris' alien restriction laws. But I guess that probably won't happen now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know some Twi'leks who've been given special permission to live in the Upper City. They don't have to hide out in a dump like this.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I hate this world. They treat us aliens like scum. As soon as the Sith quarantine is over, I'm leaving for good!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Anchorhead

speaker: Bastila
text: No, this is not possible! You have rejected the dark side, you are a weak and pathetic servant of the light! How can you still stand against me? Why can't I defeat you?
comment: Fourth dialog (init when dropped to 1 hit point)

speaker: Player
text: Now you see the dark side is not stronger than the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, I see you speak the truth. I am no match for you. Please, for the sake of what we once shared, do not make me suffer. End my life quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: I could never kill you, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: What other choice do you have? I have fallen to the dark side, I am the apprentice to the Dark Lord himself. You cannot let me live.

speaker: Player
text: You can reject the dark side, Bastila. Return to the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: No... I'm not strong enough. There is too much anger inside me now. Too much hatred and fear. I can no longer find peace in the Force.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Use our bond, then. Take your strength from me.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] You... always had more strength than I did. I told you that. I felt so... helpless before your destiny.

speaker: Bastila
text: You were Revan and I couldn't tell you... it was agonizing! Even worse when I began to... feel closer to you. I despised myself for it.

speaker: Bastila
text: And even now I... feel your strength. It... does help me. Thank you, I think I can face the end, now. If you are the one to end it for me.

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] I love you, Bastila. I can't abandon you, ever.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] You... love me? Heh. I... there was a time I yearned for and yet dreaded to hear those words. I loved you, too, but I could never... face who you were.

speaker: Bastila
text: Malak knew how I felt. Any part of the light that was within me would be extinguished when I killed you.

speaker: Bastila
text: But what good is love? It cannot save me from the sea of blackness I am drowning in. I have betrayed everything I ever believed in! How can I atone for that?

speaker: Player
text: Help us defeat the Sith, Bastila. This will atone for what you have done.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, I... could join you in your battle against the Dark Lord. That alone would not make up for all I have done, yet... it would be a step in the right direction.

speaker: Bastila
text: But how would you be able to trust me? How do you know I wouldn't turn on you when you faced Darth Malak? How do you know the dark side wouldn't make me betray you again?

speaker: Player
text: I trust you enough to leave myself open to your attack, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: You play a dangerous game. Are you certain you wish to take this risk? I could end your life and gain Malak's favor with a single stroke of my lightsaber.

speaker: Player
text: You won't, Bastila. Because I love you and I believe in you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are brave... and some would say foolish. But you are also right. The dark side has not wholly consumed me. I cannot raise my blade against you.
comment: Player has high enough conversion score from dialog

speaker: Bastila
text: You will go on to defeat Malak, of this I have little doubt. You will have gone from being the Sith Lord, himself, to the savior of our galaxy.

speaker: Bastila
text: And... and you said you loved me. This may not be the best time to say it, but...

speaker: Bastila
text: I love you, too. With all my heart.

speaker: Player
text: You aren't afraid to love anymore?

speaker: Bastila
text: After this? No, nothing could make me feel safer than to be loved by you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You should go. Malak awaits. This isn't over, yet... for any of us.

speaker: Bastila
text: I should stay here, though. If we face Malak I am afraid his dark presence will overwhelm me. It would not be wise to expose myself to such temptation.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila, I want you at my side when I face the Dark Lord.

speaker: Bastila
text: I'm sorry, but the risk is too great. I am not wholly free of the dark side's shadow. Not yet. But you are more than a match for the Dark Lord. I understand that now.

speaker: Bastila
text: I will stay here in this chamber and use my Battle Meditation to aid the Republic fleet. I am their only hope of destroying the Star Forge and ending the Sith menace.
comment: After converted, but Malak not dead and player speaks to her

speaker: Bastila
text: You must go and face Malak, but you have to hurry. Once I turn the battle in the Republic's favor we won't have much time to escape the Star Forge before it is destroyed.

speaker: Bastila
text: Good luck, my love... and may the Force be with you.

speaker: Bastila
text: Good luck... and may the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: You could use your Battle Meditation to aid the Republic fleet.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, that would be for the best. You don't need me to defeat Malak, anyway. Now I understand that a true Jedi is a match for any Sith. Even the Dark Lord himself.

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I must know something, first, before that happens. I must ask you something.

speaker: Bastila
text: Will there be a place for me in your future? Do you... do you love me?

speaker: Player
text: I do love you, Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I love you, Bastila, but after everything that's happened...

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. Thank you for your honesty. It's probably for the best that it goes no further. You saved me and I will always be grateful.

speaker: Player
text: No. I'm sorry, Bastila, but I don't love you.

speaker: Bastila
text: You are brave... and foolish. The dark side has wholly consumed me, and you will suffer for failing to see that!

speaker: Player
text: You won't, Bastila. I know you still serve the light side.

speaker: Player
text: You're right. I suppose I can't trust you, after all.

speaker: Bastila
text: A wise decision. You cannot trust me, and you cannot bring yourself to execute me. I see now there is only one way this can end. The time for words is done! Defend yourself!

speaker: Player
text: You're right. Don't worry, you won't feel a thing.

speaker: Bastila
text: Do it. Quickly...

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure] There is nothing in my heart but the blackness of the dark side! I am sick of your preaching, Revan!

speaker: Bastila
text: I ask you for an honorable death, but you are too weak to even grant me that! No more words! This must end with blood!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Look into your heart, Bastila, and you will find the light.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] I... I know a flicker of the light still burns within me. Malak felt it too. He knew it could only be extinguished if I killed you.

speaker: Bastila
text: But what good is a single flicker of light against the sea of darkness I am drowning in? I can never atone for my betrayal.

speaker: Player
text: I was redeemed, Bastila. You can be, too.

speaker: Bastila
text: You were a special case. The Council had no other choice. They needed you alive so they could discover the location of the Star Forge. It was an act of desperation.

speaker: Bastila
text: It was my responsibility to watch over you, to make sure you did not slip back into your evil ways. I was supposed to protect you from the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: You did protect me, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: But at what cost? In protecting you, I fell to the dark side myself. Is that the price of a Jedi's redemption? Must another of the Order fall to save me?

speaker: Bastila
text: I cannot allow that to happen. Please, this is too painful. Strike me down. End this now, quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: You can't protect someone from the dark side. Each individual must choose their own path.

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I suppose you are right. Yet the path I have chosen is that of the dark side. I don't see any way I could atone for what I have done. I deserve to die.

speaker: Player
text: You did more than protect me, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: It's true I possess... feelings for you. But was it only an illusion brought about by our bond? And what was the cost?

speaker: Bastila
text: Please... this is too painful. End it now, quickly. There is no other way.

speaker: Player
text: I was the Dark Lord, Bastila, and the Jedi Council let me live.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure!] No! That bond is what took me down this path to begin with! It poisoned me... I hated myself for loving you and now I have betrayed everything!

speaker: Player
text: [Persuade] Turn to the Jedi code, Bastila. It can help you.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Success] I doubt mere words can help me now, but to appease you I will recite them:

speaker: Bastila
text: There is no emotion: there is peace. There is no ignorance: there is knowledge. There is no passion: there is serenity. There is no chaos: there is harmony...

speaker: Bastila
text: Strange, but even now I find comfort in these words. I... suppose old habits die hard.

speaker: Bastila
text: There is no death: there is the Force. Thank you, Revan. I am ready to face my fate now.

speaker: Bastila
text: [Failure] The Jedi code is nothing but words, the babblings of senile old Masters! The code cannot help me now!

speaker: Player
text: There's no need for me to kill you, Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I am stronger than you could ever be, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: You can't win, Bastila. Now you must die!

speaker: Mission
text: Hmmm... look at this. This is one of those old style manual locks. No computer codes or nothing. The sewers is the only place you'll see one of these on Taris.

speaker: Mission
text: You can't use conventional security spikes on these old locks, but don't worry. I've come across them before. I've rigged up a little device that should do the trick.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: You're a sight for sore eyes, Mission.

speaker: Mission
text: I'm glad to see you too, Big Z! You didn't think I'd forget about you - Mission and Zaalbar, together forever!

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: Who's that with you?

speaker: Mission
text: These are my new friends, Big Z. Without them I never could have got you out.

speaker: Player
text: Good to meet you, Zaalbar. I'm <FullName>.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: You know the language of my people? That is rare among your species; I am impressed.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: You have saved me from a life of servitude and slavery. There is only one way I can ever repay such an act: I will swear a lifedebt to you.

speaker: Mission
text: A lifedebt? Are you sure about that, Big Z? Think about it carefully. You better be sure about this.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: I am sure, Mission. This is an issue of great importance to me. Because of our great physical strength, Wookiees are being used as slave labor on our own homeworld.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: They see us as brutes and animals to be exploited. Over the years slavers have taken many of my people; we must always be on guard against raids against our villages.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: When the Gamorreans captured me, I thought I was doomed to a life of servitude. I have been saved from such a fate, and the only way I can repay that is through a lifedebt.

speaker: Mission
text: Big Z swearing a Wookiee lifedebt to you. Wow - this is major. Do you realize what this means?

speaker: Player
text: It's some kind of loyalty vow, isn't it?

speaker: Mission
text: A lifedebt is the most solemn vow a Wookiee can make. It means he'll stay by your side for the rest of your life - wherever you go, whatever you do, Zaalbar will be with you.

speaker: Tar05_Zaalbar
text: In the presence of you all I swear my lifedebt. Forever after I will be by your side, <FullName>. May my vow be as strong as the roots of the great Wroshyr trees of Kashyyyk.

speaker: Player
text: I'm honored to accept his vow.

speaker: Mission
text: I guess this means you're stuck with me too. Wherever Big Z goes, I'm going. I almost lost him once - it's not going to happen again.

speaker: Player
text: I'm glad to have you aboard, Mission.

speaker: Mission

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: At last, my search is over! I was beginning to fear someone else had killed you and deprived me of the pleasure.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: You may have defeated the pathetic bounty hunter my Master sent after you, but you are no match for me! I have studied at the foot of the Dark Lord himself!

speaker: Player
text: How did you get down here?

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: Do you think those Republic subs are the only way to reach the ocean floor? Malak and Revan found a way down here long before the Hrakert station was built.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: I acquired a ship and followed the same route Revan and my Master used on their own journey. Then it was simply a matter of waiting for you to return for the Star Map.

speaker: Player
text: You're Malak's apprentice? Can't say I'm impressed.

speaker: Darth Bandon
text: Your words mean nothing to me... unless you wish to beg for your life. No? Then I shall try to make this both quick and painful!

speaker: Player
text: When will Malak learn? I'll kill you just like I killed Calo Nord!

speaker: Player
text: You're a fool if you think you can defeat me.

speaker: Player
text: You were on the Endar Spire! You killed Trask. You'll pay for that!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hey - I saw you in the big swoop race! I'm glad someone finally gave Brejik what he deserves - the guy was nothing but a thug!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I wonder if there'll be any female riders on the swoop circuit this season. I thought about taking it up myself, but I blew my knee out in a training run. Those things are dangerous!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This Cantina used to be packed every night, but since the Vulkars started shooting people in the streets the crowds have been pretty thin.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I wish the Sith would lift this quarantine; I was supposed to visit my sister in the core worlds! I hear Davik has a ship that can get off the planet.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Everyone says Zax is on Davik's payroll. Maybe I should talk to him and see what it would cost to hire out that ship.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Those bounty hunters make me nervous when they come in here. I always feel like they're trying to guess what my head would be worth if they brought it in.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What... what do you want? I'm not doing anything wrong. I'm just standing here... please, don't take me in for questioning!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Did you hear what happened at the swoop race? They say Brejik didn't pay up his wager, and a brawl broke out!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They say Brejik was killed in the fight! I wonder what's going to happen to the Black Vulkars now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Swoop season is almost here. I hope I do better than last season - I lost a bundle betting on all the longshots!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: None of the Beks or Vulkars come into the cantina anymore. I guess that's one good thing about the gang war - it's not so crowded in here.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This quarantine is making my life miserable! I bet Davik isn't stuck here like the rest of us - everyone says he's got a ship so fast the Sith can't catch him!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't mind this place, but I wish it wasn't so close to the bounty office. Those guys are hired killers - I don't like it when they come in here for a drink.

speaker: Mission
text: No - this isn't happening! It can't be happening!

speaker: Player
text: You're all alone now, Mission. Swear your loyalty to me!

speaker: Mission
text: No! I'm not going to just stand aside and do nothing! You'll... you'll just have to kill me. But I don't think you will.

speaker: Mission
text: I don't believe you've gone over to the dark side. Not totally. I don't think you'll kill me. Not if I don't attack you, first.

speaker: Player
text: I won't kill you. But Zaalbar will, if I tell him to.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have sworn a life debt to you, Revan. I will serve you as long as I draw breath. I will not break my vow. But you cannot ask me to turn on my best friend.

speaker: Mission
text: Looks like you'll have to do your own dirty work, Revan - if you've got the guts!

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] You swore a life debt to me, Zaalbar! You'll do as I say!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: [Success] I... I have no choice. The life debt is greater than any single life, it is a solemn vow of all my people. I cannot break it, not even for you. Forgive me, Mission.

speaker: Mission
text: Zaalbar, what are you saying? Revan can't force you to do anything you don't want to! It's me, Big Z - Mission!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Mission, forgive me!!!

speaker: Mission
text: Please, Zaalbar - don't do this! Please! NO!!!

speaker: Bastila
text: Well done, Lord Revan. You are as ruthless as Malak ever was! Quickly, now. We have to get to the Star Forge and destroy the Usurper!

speaker: Player
text: Fine - I'll just kill you myself.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: No! I won't let you hurt Mission!

speaker: Player
text: Then I'll just kill you both!

speaker: Player
text: You're wrong Mission - I'm the Dark Lord now! Taste my wrath!

speaker: Player
text: Go on, Mission - get out of here. We don't want you anymore.

speaker: Player
text: You should have run when you had the chance, Mission.

speaker: Player
text: Now it's time for you to die, Mission.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This droid is beyond repair.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm not looking for any trouble with you Sith. Please, just leave me alone.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: People complain about the Sith, but this quarantine is good for all the businesses on Taris. Look at Javyar's cantina. That place has never been busier!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: If the Sith wanted to get on everyone's good side, they'd go clean up the swoop gangs in the Lower City.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What's this, another off-worlder? I didn't realize how many of you there were on Taris until this Sith quarantine.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I heard a bunch of wreckage from the battle overhead crashed into the Undercity. Think of the damage it could have caused if it had landed here!

speaker: Calo Nord
text: I have to give you credit... you've led me on quite a chase. But nobody gets away from Calo Nord in the end!

speaker: Cand
text: I see you brought some back up, Calo. Realized we were a bit much to handle on your own, eh?

speaker: Calo Nord
text: You got lucky on Taris; the Sith attack saved you from a quick and gruesome death. But I promise you, the Sith won't be getting in my way this time!

speaker: Player
text: How did you get down here?

speaker: Calo Nord
text: You underestimate me; there's other ways down here besides the Republic subs. A small vessel with the right weapons can blast a path right through those firaxian sharks.

speaker: Calo Nord
text: Once I got down to the ocean floor all I had to do was come here and wait. I knew you'd come back this way eventually.

speaker: Player
text: Hold on, Calo... maybe we can work out a deal here.

speaker: Calo Nord
text: Sorry, I'm not in this for the credits. You're the only ones who've ever gotten away from me - I've got a rep to protect!

speaker: Calo Nord
text: Let's go, boys... it's show time!

speaker: Player
text: You think I got lucky last time? Okay, let's do it again!

speaker: Player

text: Why have you disturbed me?

speaker: SithMaster
text: I have news, Lord Malak. About the Jedi.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Ah, the Jedi. Did my droids pass their test? Did they destroy our enemies?

speaker: SithMaster
text: N-no, Lord Malak. The droids could not stop them.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Strange. I did not think there were any among the Order who could survive an attack by an army of the Star Forge's battle droids.

speaker: SithMaster

speaker: Darth Malak

speaker: SithMaster
text: Do you... do you think they can stop Revan, Lord Malak?

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Of course not! But they will slow Revan down. That will give me the time I need to fully prepare the Star Forge's defenses.

speaker: Darth Malak

speaker: Conversation owner

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: We have detected a number of underwater detonations coming from the vicinity of the Hrakert Rift.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: You have been known to have asked questions about this, and our spy monitors in the Republic Embassy recorded you leaving in a submersible that descended to the Hrakert Rift.

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: You will come with us immediately to answer for your actions, or we will be forced to take you by force!

speaker: Player
text: You'll never take me alive!

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Do not be foolish, little human! We have the entire armed forces of Manaan at our disposal. Should you attempt to resist, you would be overwhelmed before you ever reached your ship!

speaker: Selkath Officer
text: Now come with us!

speaker: Player

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Chuundar is very interested in furthering our exchange of labor for weapons. We've begun expanding our operations, as I'm sure you've seen.

speaker: Player
text: I think Zaalbar will have something to say about this.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The time for objections is long since passed, if there ever was one. You brought about this change. You have no one to blame.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I have no objections. Chuundar showed me the way things must be. There is nothing for me here. The old ways are dead.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Er, the tone of your Wookiee's muttering seems agreable. He likely agrees that this was the gentlest outcome possible.

speaker: Player
text: What are your plans for Kashyyyk?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Czerka Corporation will begin an extensive examination of the commercial potential of this world. The Wookiees will aid us in this.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm certain there are ample resources for us to export. I doubt we will encounter much more resistance. We will be here for quite some time.

speaker: Player

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Czerka Corporation maintains a well-stocked armory, although for general goods you will need to speak with the vendor in the docking area.

speaker: Player
text: Can I expect a reward for what I have done?
comment: This should only be able to be selected once.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I would think that the thanks of Czerka Corporation would be enough, especially after your previous actions. You have caused us significant difficulty.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I have reports about you meddling with our operations in the Shadowlands. I think we will consider this agrement with Chuundar to be fair compensation. Yes, that is what we will do.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps I could persuade you otherwise?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Perhaps that is exactly why I have instructed the guards to watch your every action, and how I react to you. I have taken precautions reagrding your... capabilities.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No, I don't believe we will be extending any financial compensation to you today. Thank you for your assistance.

speaker: Player
text: I'm looking for something called a Star Map.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I have no information about that. You appear to have explored deeper than any of our current expeditions. I certainly can't expand on what you've seen.

speaker: Player

speaker: Conversation owner
