text: If you see one of them Sith wandering around outside of the monastery, just look away. They rule this planet and they do as they like.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: There are folk who come from all over Sith space looking to get into the monastery here to be trained. Only a few of them ever get chosen, however.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Ah, wish they had a band, here. Place is dull as an asteroid.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I hear the Sith are digging up old artifacts in some valley up on the surface. I wonder what that's all about?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [A vast expanse of desert stretches before you, with no markers or any indications of life. It would be a deathtrap for anyone wandering aimlessly.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [A vast expanse of desert stretches before you, with no markers or any indications of life. It would be a deathtrap for anyone wandering aimlessly.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Good to see you up, instead of thrashing around in your sleep. You must have been having one hell of a nightmare. I was wondering if you were ever going to wake up.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm Carth, one of the Republic soldiers from the Endar Spire. I was with you on the escape pod, do you remember?

speaker: Player
text: I had a strange dream. Like a vision or something.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm not surprised. You took a serious blow to the head. You're probably having all kinds of strange dreams. I wouldn't worry too much about it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Well, you've been slipping in and out of consciousness for a couple of days now, so I imagine you're pretty confused about things. Try not to worry. We're safe... at least for the moment.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We're in an abandoned apartment on the planet of Taris. You were banged up pretty bad when our escape pod crashed, but luckily I wasn't seriously hurt.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I was able to drag you away from our crash site in all the confusion, and I stumbled onto this abandoned apartment. By the time the Sith arrived on the scene we were long gone.

speaker: Player
text: The Sith?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Taris is under Sith control. Their fleet is orbiting the planet, they've declared martial law and they've imposed a planet-wide quarantine. But I've been in worse spots.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I saw on your service records that you understand a remarkable number of alien languages. That's pretty rare in a raw recruit, but it should come in handy while we're stranded on a foreign world.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: There's no way the Republic will be able to get anyone through the Sith blockade to help us. If we're going to find Bastila and get off this planet, we can't rely on anybody but ourselves.

speaker: Player
text: Why is it so important to find Bastila?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That smack to your head did more damage than I thought. Bastila's a Jedi. She was with the strike team that killed Darth Revan, Malak's Sith master.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Bastila is the key to the whole Republic war effort. The Sith must have found out she was on the Endar Spire and set an ambush for us in this system.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I believe Bastila was on one of the escape pods that crashed down here on Taris. For the sake of the Republic war effort, we have to try and find her.

speaker: Player
text: How can one person, even a Jedi, be so important?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Bastila is no ordinary Jedi. She has a rare gift the Jedi call Battle Meditation. Bastila's power can influence entire armies.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Through the Force Bastila can inspire her allies with confidence and make her enemies lose their will to fight. Often, that's all it takes to tip the balance in a battle.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Of course, there are limits to what she can do. But from what I understand of her ability, it requires great concentration and focus to maintain her Battle Meditation.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The attack on the Endar Spire happened so fast she never had a chance to use her Battle Meditation. Like us, she barely got out alive.

speaker: Player
text: So what do you suggest we do next?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Bastila's going to need our help. Many of Darth Malak's followers can use the dark side of the Force, and the Sith have already killed more than their share of Jedi in this war.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Nobody will be looking for a couple of common soldiers like us. And if we're careful we can move about the planet without attracting notice; a luxury Bastila won't have.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: She's going to have half the Sith fleet looking for her. They know how important she is to the war effort.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The whole planet is under quarantine. No ships can land or take-off. So if Bastila's going to escape Taris, she's going to need our help. And we'll probably need hers.

speaker: Player
text: Any idea where we should start looking for Bastila?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: While you were out I did some scouting around. There are reports of a couple escape pods crashing down into the Undercity. That's probably a good place to start.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But the Undercity is a dangerous place. We don't want to go in there unprepared. It won't do Bastila any good if we go and get ourselves killed.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you some questions.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'll tell you whatever I can, though I...I don't know how much help it'll be.

speaker: Player
text: What do you know about Malak and the Sith?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Everything I know about Malak is pretty much common knowledge. He escaped the trap that killed Darth Revan, his Sith Master. With Revan's death, Malak became the new Dark Lord.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It's obvious that Malak's a ruthless tyrant who'll crush anyone who stands in his way... just like Revan was. Experience has shown that the Sith won't stop until the Republic lies in ruins.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak and his Sith don't respect anything except raw, brutal power. It's hard to imagine how someone who used to be a Jedi could become such a monster!

speaker: Player
text: A Jedi? What do you mean?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak and Revan were once both part of the Jedi Order, but they were young and headstrong. And against the wishes of the Council they went to battle the Mandalorians on the Outer Rim.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Something happened out there. Something corrupted them and drew them over to the dark side. Or maybe there was something rotten inside them all along. I don't know.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They formed an army of ex-Republic soldiers and Jedi who had fallen to the dark side, with Revan at their head... until Revan was killed by Bastila's Jedi strike team.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But even that didn't slow the Sith down. Malak just stepped in and assumed Revan's role. He took control of the Sith armada and resumed the bloody conquest of the Outer Worlds.

speaker: Player
text: I want to ask you something else.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry. We'll find a way to stop the Sith.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I hope you're right. But the Republic hasn't been able to stop them so far, even with the support of the Jedi Council. I think Bastila might be the galaxy's last hope.

speaker: Player
text: What can you tell me about this planet we're on?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Taris was once a magnificent planet-wide metropolis of towering skyscrapers. But that was a long time ago.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Upper City, where the rich citizens live, is...is still pretty safe. If it wasn't for the Sith occupation and the planet-wide quarantine it might not even be that bad a place to live.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But farther down things have degenerated. The...the Lower City is nothing but a slum overrun by swoop-bike gangs waging a never-ending war for control. And the Undercity is, well, even worse.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The lowest level of Taris is a wasteland overrun by rakghouls; mindless, diseased mutants that attack on sight. I've already entered all this info into your data-pad journal.

speaker: Player
text: I'd like to know some more about you, Carth.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I understand why you want to know more about me; I...I kinda get the feeling we'll be spending a lot of time together over the next while.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But this isn't really the best time for long introductions; we should stay focused on the task at hand. There'll be time for that later.

speaker: Player
text: The sooner we start looking for Bastila the sooner we find her. Let's go.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Good idea. We can use this abandoned apartment as a base, and we can probably get some equipment and supplies here in the Upper City. Just remember to keep a low profile.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I've heard some grim stories about the Dark Jedi interrogation techniques. They say the Force can do terrible things to a mind. It can wipe away your memories and destroy your very identity!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I figure if we don't do anything stupid we should be okay. I mean, after all, they're... they're looking for Bastila, not a couple of grunts like us. Alright, soldier, let's move out.

speaker: Player
text: Come on. I want to scout this planet out a bit.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like Malak and the Sith have the right idea.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: How can you say that? The Sith are butchers! Soldiers, civilians - I mean, they don't care who they kill! Even...even children!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Right now the Republic is the only thing keeping Malak's brutal fist from crushing the entire galaxy... and it won't be long until even the Republic falls to the Sith fleet.

speaker: Player
text: What's in this for me if I help you out?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You mean besides a chance to get off this planet before the Sith find you? Do you...do you have any idea what the Sith do to prisoners of war?

speaker: Player
text: Okay, you made your point. I'll help you out.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Good. We need to work together if we're going to survive.

speaker: Player
text: If you want my help you better make it worth my while.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Oh, I get it. Never mind that the Sith will destroy the Republic and ravage the galaxy. You're only in this for the credits.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't worry. The Republic pays its mercenaries well. You help me find Bastila and they'll make it more than worth your while, I'm sure. Plus, it might be your only chance to get off Taris.

speaker: Player
text: If it means getting off this planet, I guess I can help you find Bastila.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll take my chances on my own.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't be a fool! You're not getting off this world without help, and you can't hide here forever. Do you have any idea what will happen when the Sith find you?

speaker: Player
text: If Bastila's a Jedi, she can probably look after herself.

speaker: Player
text: How do you even know Bastila's still alive?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't. But Bastila's young, and she has a powerful command of the Force. We survived the crash landing, so I'm willing to bet that she may have, too.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Besides, what's the alternative? I mean, if she's dead, then no one can stop Malak and his Sith from wiping out the Republic. And I'd rather operate on the assumption that she survived.

speaker: Player
text: Forget it! I'm not risking my life to try and save her!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't think you understand the situation. We can't hide on this planet forever. Eventually the Sith will find us... and, trust me, you don't want that.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Getting off this world isn't going to be easy... we'll probably need Bastila's help. Not to mention that without her, the whole Republic war effort is doomed.

speaker: Player
text: Bastila? She's the one from the Endar Spire, right?

speaker: Player
text: I guess I owe you my life. Thanks.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You don't have to thank me. I've never abandoned anyone on a mission, and I'm not about to start now. Besides, I'm going to need your help.

speaker: Player
text: So are we just going to wait here for the Republic to rescue us?

speaker: Player
text: Right. I'm <FullName>, by the way. How did we get here?

speaker: Player
text: Carth, the one on the communicator. I remember.

speaker: Player
text: Where am I? How did I get here?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Whoa, hold on. Don't try to get up yet. You were smashed up pretty bad when we crash landed here on Taris.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't worry, we should be safe here in this apartment. I gave you something to help you sleep. Just get some rest and let the kolto packs do their job.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This unsavory looking man appears to be looking for someone... maybe even one of your companions back on the Ebon Hawk.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: *grunt* What the hell is your kind doing here? Bad enough I have to deal with all these other idiots, but now there's a stinkin' Cathar on this world too?

speaker: Juhani
text: I have as much right to be here as you do, SIR!

speaker: Player
text: Do not seek to aggravate us.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Ooooo! Big man, the Jedi, shooting his mouth off from behind a lightsaber, or whatever you're carrying.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hiding behind your pet Cathar... And a woman at that!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We should have exterminated all you Cathar when we had the chance.

speaker: Juhani
text: Wha... What do you know about my world?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know enough that... Hey, wait a minute... you look familiar somehow...

speaker: Juhani
text: What? You...

speaker: Player
text: Do you two know each other?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This doesn't concern you, Jedi trash.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Hm... now where could I have... No, he's dead and she likely is too. I...

speaker: Juhani
text: What are you talking about??

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Maybe I was wrong. Still, I think a specimen like you would be a nice addition to my collection.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So what would it take, Jedi, for you to sell your pet here to me?

speaker: Player
text: She is not for sale!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Now don't be so selfish. We both know Cathar aren't real people anyway.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The females make amusing pets, but males should be put down like the animals they are. I remember one time on Taris...

speaker: Juhani

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Revan - I knew you'd come for me. Malak thought you might be afraid to enter the Temple again, but he doesn't know you like I do. Not anymore. Not since you've changed.

speaker: Juhani
text: Quickly, Bastila - come with us! We have to escape before Malak arrives!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Escape? You don't understand. I have sworn allegiance to Lord Malak and the Sith; I am no longer a pawn of the Jedi Council.

speaker: Player
text: No, Bastila! Don't go over to the dark side!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You say that as if the dark side is some terrible entity. The Jedi Council has brainwashed you like all the others. Like they once did with me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They speak of the dark side as if it something to be feared. But in reality their only goal is to manipulate those who are strong in the Force. The fear of the dark side is a tool to maintain control.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Why do you think the Jedi forbid you and Malak from joining the Mandalorian Wars? They knew you would realize your true potential and break free of their domination.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak has shown me how the Jedi Council have been using me the same way they once tried to use you. They've been holding me back because they knew one day I would surpass them all.

speaker: Player
text: No - I don't believe it! How could you betray us like this, Bastila?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I resisted at first. I endured the Sith torments with the passionless serenity of a true Jedi, emptying my mind. But after a week of endless tortures I finally saw the truth.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak forced me to acknowledge my anger and pain. He showed me the liberating power of these emotions. Then he made me see how the Jedi Council has denied me what is mine by right!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Jedi Council gladly used my Battle Meditation in their wars, but they still treated me like a child - like an inferior. They were jealous of my power... of what I could become!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: They wanted me to bow and call them Master and follow their Code and obey their every order. But all the while they were exploiting my Battle Meditation for their own use!

speaker: Player
text: Don't do this, Bastila! Fight it! I'll help you!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You are a sad little fool. You speak as if I were the same Bastila that you've known all along. But freed from the control of the Jedi Council I've become much, much more.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I almost wish you could see things as I do now. I wish you could join me and taste true power once again. Sadly, I doubt you are even capable any longer.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: With the power of the Star Forge Malak will destroy the Republic and conquer the galaxy. And I will be the apprentice at his side - after I prove my worth by killing you!

speaker: Player
text: I like this side of you, Bastila. Now we can truly be together.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You think so, do you? You style yourself the Master of the Sith that you once were? To think I once envied you your passion, your power.

speaker: Player
text: Don't be lured in by these Sith lies, Bastila!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Lies? You are the one living a lie, Revan. The Jedi Council made you into something you are not; they programmed you to be their slave.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You used to be Revan, Master of the Sith, but no longer. You are simply a pawn of the Jedi Council and the Republic they serve... like I was until Malak freed me from their shackles!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: A pity the power you once had is so diluted in you. You could have been strong as I am now... stronger, even. But that will never happen, now.

speaker: Player
text: I am Revan, the Dark Lord! Bow down to me, Bastila!

speaker: Player
text: If you've fallen under Malak's control you must die!

speaker: Player
text: It's not too late, Bastila! You can still turn away from the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: It didn't take long to convert you, did it? I always knew you were weak!

speaker: Player
text: A pawn of the Jedi Council? What are you talking about?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Surely you know what I mean, Revan. Look at what the Council did to you; they turned you into their puppet. The same thing they do to all who are truly strong in the Force.

speaker: Jolee
text: Come on, Bastila. We have to escape before Malak shows up!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You are stronger than I would have thought possible, after what the Jedi Council did to you. Seems that Malak was wrong - the power of the dark side is not lost to you after all, Revan.

speaker: Player
text: I draw my power from the light now, Bastila.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You can deny what you are, Revan, but you are only fooling yourself. I know the truth. I have seen the shadows inside your mind.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Remember: I was there when you nearly died in the trap set by the Jedi Council. I used the Force to preserve your life, Revan. We are forever linked by my actions on that bridge!

speaker: Player
text: That is how I know you will come back to the light.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: These are not your true feelings, Revan. You are speaking as a tool of the Jedi Council - as I once did. But now I see how the Jedi used us both!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Council tried to exploit the bond between us. They hoped I would draw out your memories to lead them to the Star Forge. We were slaves to their will - like all who follow the Jedi Code!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But in our shared visions of the Star Maps I also felt the so called taint within you. I resisted it at first, but now I embrace the power of the dark side - your dark side!

speaker: Player
text: Learn from my mistakes. It is not too late to come back to the light!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Mistakes? No, Revan - the only mistake you are making is the one you are making now! You deny yourself the power that is yours by right! Only now do I realize how strong you are.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You deserve to be the true Master of the Sith, not Malak. I see this now. Together we can destroy your old apprentice. Join with me and reclaim your lost identity!

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore. I don't even remember those days.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Your mind was too badly damaged to ever fully restore your memories, Revan. But your power, your strength of will, the essence of who and what you are: these things still remain!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Once long ago you defied the Jedi Council, freeing yourself from their control. You claimed your rightful title of Dark Lord of the Sith. Together we can defeat Malak and take back what is yours!

speaker: Player
text: Please, Bastila... if you feel anything for me, you won't do this!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I... I don't. The only Revan I could respect is one who would break free of the Council's slavery. One who would grasp the power that lies before him... not the weak fool I see.

text: Bastila, it is not too late for you to be saved. The teachings of the Jedi can lead you from the dark side back into the light and a true understanding of the Force.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You are beneath my contempt, Juhani. When you felt the power of the dark side you fled to a cave like some cowering animal! You know nothing of the Force or its true potential!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But you, Revan - the power of the dark side is yours to command! You can use it to destroy Malak! With my help you could rule over the entire galaxy!

speaker: Player
text: I don't want to rule the galaxy. I want you to return to the light.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You are a pathetic fool, Revan! Together we could have defeated Malak and ruled over an Empire, but now I will be at Lord Malak's side instead!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You will be crushed with the Republic and all the fools who bow down to the Jedi Council! No one can stand against the power of the Star Forge and the Sith fleet!

speaker: Player
text: The Dark Lord Revan is dead. I am a servant of the light now.

speaker: Player
text: Yes! Together we can rule the galaxy!

speaker: Jolee
text: Listen to me... the dark side leads to death and destruction. I've seen the horrors the Sith have unleashed on the galaxy. Turn away from this path.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Shut up, old man. Your time is over! The age of the Jedi and the Republic is no more! This is the age of Darth Revan and the Sith!

speaker: Jolee
text: Don't do this, kid. I don't want to, but I'll fight you if I have to. Even if it costs me my life.

speaker: Player
text: I am the Lord of the Sith! Bow down before me!

speaker: Juhani
text: A true Jedi will never bow down to the Sith. If this is your decision I have no choice but to do battle against you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Kill her! Rend her flesh! Show her the fate of all who dare stand against us! Embrace the power of the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: No, I will not kill my friend. I reject the power of the dark side.

speaker: Player
text: Death to the Jedi!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes! The sacrificial blood will consecrate this ancient temple in the name of the Sith! With the death of the Jedi the rebirth of Darth Revan will be complete!

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm a Jedi... I'll never bow down to the Sith. If you go through with this I have no choice but to do battle against you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Kill him! Grind his old bones to dust! Show him the fate of all who dare stand against us! Embrace the dark side!

speaker: Player
text: Then you must die!

speaker: Player
text: You... you're right. I cannot do this. I reject the dark side!

speaker: Juhani
text: No! Do not walk down this path... it can only lead to destruction! I know of what I speak!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Shut up, Juhani! You know nothing of the dark side's true potential! When you felt its touch you fled to a cave and cowered in terror!

speaker: Juhani
text: I have no wish to fight you and Bastila, but if you choose to walk down this path you know I must stand against you... even at the cost of my life.

speaker: Player
text: How do I know you won't betray me?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I need deny my passions no longer, Revan. I would stand by your side gladly, as your lover and apprentice!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I swore allegiance to Malak only because I thought you had lost the power you had once wielded. But this... this would be much better.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I would be utterly yours, master! Together we would destroy Malak and you would reclaim the mantle of Dark Lord!

speaker: Player
text: No, I... don't want you like this. I want the woman I knew.

speaker: Player
text: Turn away from this path, Bastila. The dark side leads only to destruction.

speaker: Jolee
text: It's not to late for you, Bastila. The dark side is evil but it isn't all powerful. You can still fight against it. Don't let it consume you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You are beneath my contempt, old man! You hid like a coward for decades on Kashyyyk! You know nothing about the true potential of the Force!

speaker: Player
text: I don't trust you. I think I'll just kill you instead!

speaker: Juhani
text: No! This is the way of the dark side! Do not give in to the anger and hatred!

speaker: Jolee
text: No! Don't give into your anger. Remain calm, remain focused. Don't let her twist your mind like this!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It is your power that will keep me as your loyal apprentice, Revan. I swore allegiance to Malak only because I thought you had lost the power you once wielded.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But you have proven yourself in our battle; I see you possess the strength to destroy Malak and reclaim the mantle of Dark Lord. Now I see you will make a worthy Sith Master.

speaker: Player
text: How can I reclaim my identity if I can't even remember it?

speaker: Player
text: No! This isn't the Bastila I knew!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Of course not! I have been reborn in the wake of destiny... *your* destiny! The power of the dark side is yours by right!

speaker: Player
text: What are you saying, Bastila?

speaker: Player
text: If I am so powerful, then why do you serve another master?

speaker: Player
text: Then why don't we join our power together, as it was meant to be?

speaker: Player
text: There is no link between us, Bastila! Not anymore!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Our bond is not easily broken, Revan. Even when your mind was destroyed and reprogrammed with a new identity the bond between us endured.

speaker: Player
text: We are linked by more than just a bond, Bastila.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Do not mistake the power of the Force for love, Revan. It does not exist. Power is what forged our bond, and power is what made us both tools of the Jedi Council!

speaker: Player
text: Don't call me that. I'm not Revan anymore. I'm <FullName> now.

speaker: Player
text: Now you see the power of the true Dark Lord!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, Revan! I was there when you almost died in the trap set by the Jedi Council; I used the Force to preserve your life. We are forever linked by my actions on that bridge.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The Council tried to exploit our bond. They hoped your memories would lead me to the Star Forge. But in our shared visions of the Star Maps I also tasted the power of the taint within you!

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: We have seen you, Interloper! You are a servant of the Elders. By order of the One you must die!

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: Stay your weapons, Interloper. We are not here for battle or blood. We bring you an invitation from the One, Great Champion of the Rakata.

speaker: Player
text: Rakata? The One? What are you talking about?

speaker: Carth
text: Wait a minute - you understood these creatures? Of course... you and Malak must have been here before. You...you probably learned their language back when you were Revan.

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: You have used strange magics and weapons to slaughter our raiding parties, Interloper. You have bathed in the blood of fierce Rakatan warriors.

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: Your power and skill in battle has impressed the One. He wishes an audience with you: a great honor. Come with us now and we will take you to him.

speaker: Player
text: Who is the One? What's going on here?

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: The One is the leader of our tribe, the Great Champion of the Rakata. He has feasted on the flesh of many foes. Come with us and we will take you to him now.

speaker: Player
text: Okay. Take me to the One.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not going anywhere with you.

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: The will of the One cannot be denied, Interloper. You will come with us now to see our Champion, or our rancor war beasts will destroy you.

speaker: Player
text: I think I'll just kill you instead!

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: Are you blind, Interloper? Our war beasts will crush you if you defy us! This is your last chance: come with us to see the One, or we will feast on your bones!

speaker: Player
text: You can't kill me! I'm invincible!

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: Release the war beasts!

speaker: Player
text: Death is such a small impediment.

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I don't have to come with you.

speaker: Rakatan Elite Warrior
text: [Failure] You try to use your magic on us, Interloper? We are Rakata! You cannot bend us to your will like mindless beasts!

speaker: Cand
text: Hold on a second - you understood these goggle-eyed freaks? You must have come to this planet and learned the language back before the Jedi messed up your mind. Back when you were still Revan.

speaker: HK47
text: Query: You are able to comprehend the speech patterns of these organics? You must have visited this planet and learned their language in your previous incarnation as Darth Revan.

speaker: Jolee
text: Wait a minute - do you understand these creatures? You must have learned their language when you came here in search of the secrets of the Star Forge. Back when you were still Revan.

speaker: Juhani
text: You understand these aliens? Of course... you must have come here and learned their languge in your search for the secrets of the Star Forge. Back when you were still Revan.

speaker: Mission
text: Whoa. Can you actually understand what these guys are saying? I guess you must have come here back when you were Revan, huh?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You can actually understand this strange speech? You must have come to this planet and learned their language when you were Revan.

speaker: Player
text: An invitation? What kind of invitation?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You talked to old Rukil Wrinkle-Skin? My mommy says he's crazy! I have to stay away from him!

text: Mommy says all the up-worlders is selfish and mean. But you look nice to me.

text: Mommy said you're the one who made her sick friend better. She said you gave him medicine.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm not allowed to go out past the gate. My daddy went out there once and he never came back. Mommy said the rakghouls got him.

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila, I was wondering something. How did those Vulkars manage to capture a famous Jedi like you? Were you knocked out when your escape pod crashed?

speaker: Bastila
text: No, I was conscious. But my Force powers were exhausted from using my Battle Meditation in the battle for the Endar Spire. Without my help you might never have gotten off the ship alive.

speaker: Carth
text: Fair enough. But I've seen you Jedi in action. There's no way those thugs would have stood a chance against your lightsaber.

speaker: Bastila
text: My lightsaber was... misplaced. I couldn't find it after the crash. I looked *everywhere* in that pod. The Vulkars came and overwhelmed me even as I was searching for my weapon.

speaker: Carth
text: Wait a minute, let me get this straight. You *lost* your lightsaber? Ha-ha! I mean, isn't that a violation of some kind of Jedi code or something?

speaker: Player
text: Of all the Jedi in the galaxy, why do we get one who's absent-minded?

speaker: Bastila
text: This is no laughing matter! During the crash my lightsaber must have... it must have fallen from my belt and rolled under my seat! The Vulkars probably found it there when they searched the wreckage.

speaker: Carth
text: Hey, hey, hey, don't get mad. I'm sorry. It's just funny to think of a legendary Jedi losing her lightsaber. Take my advice: this is one detail you might want to keep out of the history texts.

speaker: Bastila
text: I hardly consider myself a legend, Carth. Though I will consider your advice when I relate these events to the Jedi Council. There is no need for them to know *every* detail of what transpired.

speaker: Player
text: Maybe losing lightsabers is a side-effect of her Battle Meditation.

speaker: Player
text: Leave her alone, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila, did you ever think about joining all the Jedi who were running off to follow Revan and Malak when they went to fight the Mandalorians?

speaker: Bastila
text: That was nearly five years ago. I was still an apprentice, my Battle Meditation hadn't even manifested itself. Yet even then I had the wisdom to obey the will of the Council. Unlike Revan.

speaker: Carth
text: I guess. Still, do you ever wonder if things could have been different? Would Revan and Malak still have been corrupted if the Council had supported them instead of dragging its feet?

speaker: Bastila
text: Do not blame Revan's corruption on the Council! Your Republic saw only the threat of the Mandalorians, but the wisdom of the Masters saw beyond the immediate threat.

speaker: Player
text: What did they see, exactly?

speaker: Bastila
text: There was something lurking out there, something that devoured Revan and Malak - and many other Jedi. Had the Council sent us all into the unknown, how many more would have fallen?

speaker: Carth
text: So you're saying we should have done nothing? Just let the Mandalorians conquer us unopposed? I mean, the Republic was under attack, and the Order abandoned us!

speaker: Bastila
text: We did not abandon you! But the Council were not about to throw lives away foolishly. In time, we would have aided you against the Mandalorians. But you couldn't wait.

speaker: Bastila
text: Revan and Malak offered a quicker answer, and the Republic chose to walk the easy path rather than the path of wisdom. Now we see the results all around us.

speaker: Bastila
text: You asked me if I think things could have been different? I *know* they could have! If Revan had only listened to the Council, millions of innocent people would still be alive.

speaker: Carth
text: Yeah, right. And every single one of them would be speaking Mandalorain. I think we're done here. Let's just get back to the task at hand.

speaker: Player
text: Sounds like you're just making excuses, Bastila.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, Carth. You're a pilot for the Republic, right? You've been all over the galaxy I bet, right? So tell me, how would you rate Taris compared to other worlds you've seen?

speaker: Carth
text: I'll be honest, Mission, Taris would rate pretty low. The prejudice, the rich spoiling themselves while the poor are crushed beneath them - not a pretty picture.

speaker: Mission
text: Yeah, but that's only since the Sith occupation. Before that... well, I guess it wasn't all that different, really. Hmm... maybe Taris ain't as great as I thought, you know?

speaker: Carth
text: Trust me, Mission. There are a lot of worlds better than Taris. There are worse, too. But Taris is no place for a kid to live on her own - even a kid who's got a Wookiee to look out for her.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, I ain't no kid! And I look out for Zaalbar as much as he looks out for me. Big Z's my friend, not my babysitter! Geez, I come ask you a question and you give me a lecture!

speaker: Carth
text: Don't you snap at me, missy! You want a lecture? How's this: only bratty little children fly off the handle because of a simple comment.

speaker: Player
text: Settle down right now - both of you!

speaker: Mission
text: I don't have to listen to you, Carth! You ain't my father - though you're sure old enough to be! So keep your lectures inside your withered old head, 'cause I don't need 'em!

speaker: Carth
text: And I sure as hell don't need this. Let's just drop it and get back to what we were doing.

speaker: Player
text: You're not going to take that from him, are you Mission?

speaker: Mission
text: Uh, hey Carth. Can I... can I talk to you for a second?

speaker: Carth
text: Are you ready to have a civil chat? Or are is this going to be another childish tantrum?

speaker: Mission
text: Tantrum? I'm trying to apologize, you nerf-herder! Uh... I mean... I'm sorry. I didn't mean to get mad at you. It's just that I'm sick of everyone treating me like I'm a helpless kid.

speaker: Carth
text: Yeah, I know. And I'm sorry about what I said, too. I'm just a little on edge lately. Not surprising considering all we've been through. But I shouldn't take it out on you.

speaker: Player
text: It's about time you two made up.

speaker: Carth
text: Mission, you have to know that we don't think you're helpless. Look where we are, look at what we're doing. You're not just along for the ride.  We need you.

speaker: Mission
text: You really mean it, don't you? Nobody's ever said anything like that to me before, not even Big Z. He might think it, but he's not really one for words, you know. Thanks, Carth.

speaker: Carth
text: Ah, it's no big deal. I know how it is. Sometimes you just need to hear a few words of encouragement. Kids are like that.

speaker: Mission
text: Kids are like that?? Listen you... oh, I get it. Okay, you got me. You're pretty funny, Carth. For an old guy. Come on, you geezer - let's get back to what we were doing.

speaker: Player
text: What's with all the apologies? I was hoping for another fight!

speaker: Cand
text: Carth, you fought in the Mandalorian Wars, didn't you? We may have faced each other in combat. What battles were you in?

speaker: Carth
text: I try not to think about my past battles too much. The horrors of war are something I'd rather not relive.

speaker: Cand
text: The horrors of war? My people know only the glory of battle. I'm disappointed in you, Carth. I thought a warrior like you would understand.

speaker: Player
text: Carth isn't like you, Canderous.

speaker: Carth
text: I'm not a warrior, I'm a soldier. There's a difference. Warriors attack and conquer, they prey on the weak. Soldiers defend and protect the innocent - mostly from warriors.

speaker: Cand
text: Nice speech. I bet you tell yourself that every night so you can sleep. But I accept who and what I am. I don't have to justify it with words - victory in battle is my justification!

speaker: Carth
text: Justification through victory? So what happens when you lose? You know, like you did against us.

speaker: Cand
text: You had us outnumbered five to one. You had more ships, more troops, more supplies and the Jedi on your side. And we still made the Republic tremble before we fell!

speaker: Carth
text: Nice speech. I bet you tell yourself that every night so you can sleep. I don't want to talk about this anymore, Canderous. The war is over. You lost.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, Carth. When did you get all peace-loving on me?

speaker: Player
text: Keep it cool, you two. I don't want this getting out of hand.

speaker: Cand
text: So, Bastila, I heard a rumor that the Vulkars captured you without much of a struggle. It must be embarrassing to be bested by a handful of street thugs.

speaker: Bastila
text: There were extenuating circumstances. And I can assure you it took far more than a handful of Vulkars to subdue me.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, let's not get into this.

speaker: Cand
text: Whatever you say. All I know is that if we had more Jedi like Bastila fighting against us in the Mandalorian Wars, my side might not have lost.

speaker: Bastila
text: Bold talk from a broken-down merceneray who was serving at Davik's heel. I'd call you his pet kath hound, but they have enough loyalty not to turn on their masters.

speaker: Cand
text: Insults? Maybe if your Master had trained your lightsaber to be as quick as your tongue you could have escaped those Vulkars, you spoiled little Jedi princess!

speaker: Bastila
text: I was not spoiled! I was given the same training as everyone else in the Order! You are nothing but a... no. I must not do this. There is no emotion; there is peace.

speaker: Cand
text: That's the problem with you Jedi. Always chanting about peace and control, never up for a good fight. Well, except for Revan, I guess.

speaker: Bastila
text: Enough, Mandalorian. I won't rise to your bait any more. The game is over. Let us continue on with what we were doing.

speaker: Player
text: Yeah, I'm sure there were twenty of them. I mean, fifty... no, wait... a hundred!

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, Big Z, we've got to do something about your breath.  I didn't want to say anything, but it's bad. Worse than usual, which is hard to believe.

speaker: Mission
text: In fact, now that I think about it, your breath has been pretty rancid ever since we rescued you from those Gammorean slavers. What did they feed you, buddy?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: They didn't. I wasn't their guest, Mission. I was a prisoner. I don't think they cared much what happened to me.

speaker: Mission
text: Oh, Zaalbar, that's terrible! I know how grouchy you get if you don't get your eight square meals a day. I'm amazed you didn't pass out from hunger.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I did manage to take a chunk out of the arm of a guards that wandered too close to my cage. But it tasted awful, so I spit it out.

speaker: Mission
text: Ewww! No wonder your breath is so bad, Big Z. Gammoreans smell like bantha poo-doo! We'll have to pick you up a toothbrush to clean that stench out of your choppers.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Wookiees do not brush their teeth, Mission! It... it just isn't done! What humiliation will you use on me next? A comb?

speaker: Mission
text: Okay, relax. No toothbrush. Sheesh. Just try to eat something else to cover up that smell, okay? Stay away from anything that's smart enough to lock you in a cage this time.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: *sigh* I'll take care of it as soon as I can, Mission. For now, let's stay focused on the task at hand.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, Big Z. Don't take this the wrong way, but lately I've noticed you're starting to look a little bit scruffy.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Scruffy? What are you talking about? I hope you aren't suggesting I take a bath!

speaker: Mission
text: No, I'm not suggesting a bath. I know how well that went over last time. But your hair's getting all tangled. And if you look close, you can see a few gray strands starting to poke through.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You're making this up! I groom every day! My hair is not tangled, and it's not going gray!

speaker: Player
text: She's got a point, Zaalbar. You could use a good makeover.

speaker: Mission
text: Don't worry, Big Z. It's nothing I can't fix. A little trim, a splash of coloring and you'll be as good as new. Best looking Wookiee on the planet. Maybe a nice suit...

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You don't trim a Wookiee! You don't color a Wookiee! And you certainly don't dress a Wookiee!

speaker: Mission
text: I know Wookiees aren't into the whole clothing thing, but you could start a whole new trend! You'd be on the cutting edge.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: Rargh! Leave me alone!

speaker: Mission
text: Okay, okay. Sheesh. Try to offer some constructive criticism and this is the thanks I get? Let's move on. You can just stay naked and scruffy for all I care.

speaker: Player
text: Zaalbar looks fine to me.

speaker: Mission
text: Hey, Bastila. You ever just use the Force for fun? You know, a little jolt of the Force to trip some jerk who's ticking you off?

speaker: Bastila
text: I would never use the Force for such a petty and trivial revenge! The mere thought of it is preposterous!

speaker: Mission
text: Ah, come on. There's got to be times when you've thought about it. Don't be so stuck up - you can tell me.

speaker: Bastila
text: I am not stuck up. I merely have the years of training to give me the wisdom and understanding to see how childish such an act would be.

speaker: Mission
text: Childish? Is that a crack about my age? You ain't much older than me, miss high and mighty! Just 'cause you're some Jedi doesn't mean you can be a prissy little...

speaker: Mission
text: What the -?? Hey, that wasn't funny!
comment: Mission tripped by Bastila using Force powers

speaker: Bastila
text: I have no idea what you're talking about, Mission. Come now, we have to get going. Please do try to be less clumsy in the future.

speaker: Bastila
text: Jolee, may I have a moment? There is something I wish to speak to you about.

text: Silence! This is not for outsiders to hear!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Well, human, you find yourself in a most difficult situation. The Hrakert Rift is the most precious resource on Manaan, and anything that threatens it or the kolto it produces threatens our entire species.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: We will not tolerate threats to our neutrality, our existence, and our way of life!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: As much as we may admire your Republic and your Order in particular, I believe you will have a hard time explaining your role in this incident adequately.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: We have determined that you are responsible for the detonations that occurred near the Hrakert Rift. We demand to know what occurred down there!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: If the Republic has broken its neutrality treaty with us, the reprecussions shall be very grave indeed!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: What have you done to the Rift?

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] Nothing happened down at the Rift.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: [Failure] Do not try to manipulate us with your powers, human! You have only one chance left to tell us the truth!

speaker: Player
text: [Force Persuade] I am telling the truth.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Enough of these lies!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: For your crimes against Manaan and the Selkath you are banned forever from this world, on pain of death!

speaker: Player
text: You can't do this!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: It is our duty to punish those who transgress our laws. We can do this... and we will!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Guard! Eject the prisoner from the court!

speaker: Player
text: You won't get away with this!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: We can and we will. Your Republic will not risk offending us. Not with the Sith as powerful as they are.

speaker: Player
text: But I've done nothing wrong!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Do not mock us, human!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: You have been found guilty, proving that you actually are.

speaker: Player
text: If you knew who you were dealing with...

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: You are an off-worlder, like any other. Only more troublesome than most...

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] The Sith were trying to collapse the Hrakert Rift!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: [Success] The Sith were down at the Rift?!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: But how could the Sith have been there when we had...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: What?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: When we... we monitor the Rift constantly. How could the Sith have approached it without us knowing?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] They had built a station down there already.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: [Success] I find that highly unlikely... How could we have missed such a large undertaking?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Impossible! Our own sta...

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Our what?

speaker: Judge Kota
text: It is impossible... that's all...

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Maybe they have some sort of stealth field.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: [Success] That they could smuggle onto Manaan without our knowing about it? Impossible!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You fail to realize that if they had such a stealth field, we would not be able to detect them bringing it either.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: But that area is closely monitored... We would have detected any new vessels approaching it just by perturbations in the currents.

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] Maybe some Selkath were helping them.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: [Success] Some... Selkath?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Selkath would not be helping off-worlders to disrupt our most valuable resources!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: They have already attempted to seduce our young away from us... Who's to say they hadn't corrupted someone else?

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Have you seen this, human? Is this how you know of it?

speaker: Player
text: There were many Selkath down there.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: This we know. What happened there, off-worlder?

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: We know??

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Silence. It will be discussed later.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: Well, human? What REALLY occurred down there?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] It was the Sith. They tried to blow it all up.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: [Failure] Your lies only make the hole you dig yourself deeper, human!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It is likely that you have sabotaged our efforts AND the facilities at the Hrakert Rift. For this you must pay the price.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: How do we know this? What have you been hiding from us? What facilities??

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It is not an issue to be discussed among outsiders.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: No! I demand answers! What has been happening down there?

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: Our agreement with the Republic to research and synthesize kolto has nearly borne us disaster. That is all you need to know.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: The Republic... Why were we not informed?

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It was not necessary for you to know. Now keep your silence!

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I really don't know exactly.

speaker: Player
text: I've been lying... It wasn't really the Sith.

speaker: Judge Duula
text: What?

text: I knew it! It was the Republic, wasn't it!

speaker: Player
text: The explosions were at the research station both our governments set up there.

text: Research Station?! What are you talking about? Dont try to lie to us, human!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We know of this.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: What?!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: It will be discussed later.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: This cannot be kept silent! The Council will...

text: The Council will hear nothing of this! And you will keep your silence or be ejected from the court!

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: But we cannot...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Silence!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: What has happened at the research station? What caused the explosions?

speaker: Player
text: The machinery had woken up a giant firaxan shark.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: A giant firaxan? Could it be...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Impossible! It is only a legend.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: But he said he killed it... didn't he?

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: You killed this shark, human?

speaker: Player
text: I didn't kill the shark!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: The Progenitor... it must have been!

speaker: Judge Duula
text: Be quiet! That is merely a myth, and not fit for outsiders to hear!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But if it was the life-bringer... the ancestor of our species... Think of what this could mean!

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: If it always laired there... then perhaps the kolto...

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Enough! Off-worlders are not to hear of such things!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But he said he saved it... He destroyed the harvesters to save it.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Indeed. This casts your actions in a new light, human.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This, I believe, will require more thought... both on your actions, and on what we must do in response.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This court will adjourn while we deliberate.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We have reviewed your actions and the situation, human.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We thank you for the destruction of the machinery and saving the giant firaxan which, we believe, is the source of our kolto... or at least its guardian.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We will not detain you any longer. While we cannot show our gratitude overtly, know that you have earned our respect.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: This trial is now over.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: But she said she saved it... She destroyed the harvesters to save it.

speaker: Player
text: I destroyed the machinery to save it.

text: The machine was making it drive everyone mad.

text: But she said she killed it... didn't she?

text: The entire station had been driven mad.

text: Mad? I find that hard to believe, human.

speaker: Judge Kota
text: We did receive those transmission just before the station went silent...

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: Ask the human what happened!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Well, human? What drove all the sentients down there mad?

speaker: Player
text: A giant firaxan shark was woken up by the harvester.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: And you destroyed the harvester to kill a giant firaxan...

speaker: Player
text: Only the Selkath went mad.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: You accuse us of being to blame for this?

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Calm yourself. We are more advanced than that.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: Why do you say that only we Selkath went mad?

speaker: Player
text: A giant firaxan shark sent out some sort of psychic call.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: The explosion... to kill a giant firaxan?

speaker: Player
text: Because they were all insane and had eaten everyone else...

text: But why? If the entire station was driven mad, as would seem to be the case, surely there must have been some evidence that something had transpired down there. What was it?

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I have no idea.

speaker: Judge Jhosa
text: [Success] Bah! This humans information is worthless! We have lost the facility on the bottom of the ocean. Our efforts will be exposed!

speaker: Judge Kota
text: If the entire station was driven mad, as would seem to be the case, surely there must have been some evidence that something had transpired down there. What was it?

text: [Lie] The station was empty.

text: [Failure] We do not believe you, human! Tell us what you know or you will not leave here alive!

speaker: Player
text: [Lie] I really don't know anything.

speaker: Player
text: You couldn't kill me if you tried!

text: We should kill him now! Before anyone knows!

text: No, there are others who would notice his absence and begin asking... difficult questions.

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: We cannot ban the Republic for its actions, the Sith would gain too much, but we cannot let you go unpunished.

speaker: Judge Naleshekan
text: We should kill her now! Before anyone knows!

speaker: Judge Shelkar
text: No, there are others who would notice her absence and begin asking... difficult questions.

speaker: Player
text: They killed the scientists and the rescue teams the Republic sent down.

text: [Lie] The harvesting machine malfunctioned and exploded.

text: Malfunctioned?

text: Impossible! That machinery was constructed by us to last a thousand years!

speaker: Player
text: What? Our stowaway is gone?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Boop. Beep. Zzzott. Whirr.

speaker: Player
text: Why would she just leave?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Whoop. Boop. Beep. Fritz.

speaker: Player
text: You think she left because she sensed we were heading for trouble? That's a cheery thought.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Whirr. Click. Beep. Boop.

speaker: Player
text: You're right. We'll probably never see her again.

speaker: Player
text: Good. I'm glad she's gone.

speaker: Player
text: What do you mean by gone? Where did she go?

speaker: Bastila
text: Master, why have you summoned me? Without my Battle Meditation there is a chance the Republic capital ships could break through and attack the Star Forge itself!

speaker: Darth Malak
text: This will not take long, Bastila. You will be able to resume your Battle Meditation soon enough. I only wanted you to know that Revan is here on the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: Revan? But...

speaker: Darth Malak
text: The Force is bringing us towards a confrontation with my old master. The Star Forge has drawn our enemies together so they may all die in a single, glorious day!

speaker: Darth Malak
text: You must kill Revan to prove yourself worthy of being my apprentice, Bastila. You must finish what began in the Rakatan Temple.

speaker: Bastila
text: Y-yes, Lord Malak.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: I sense your fear, Bastila. But it is unfounded. The power of the Star Forge will feed the dark side within you, it will give you the strength you need to defeat my old master.

speaker: Darth Malak
text: Stay here in the command center while you use your Battle Meditation against the Republic fleet. Revan will find you here in due time. It is inevitable.

speaker: Bastila
text: Of course, Master. I will not fail you again.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Perhaps you will triumph, Bastila. But even if you fail it will give me the time I need to complete my preparations of the station's defenses.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And then we shall see if Revan can stand against the full fury of the Star Forge! Ha-ha-ha!

speaker: Juhani
text: Where is Bastila? What happened on the ship?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We ran into Malak. He would have killed us, but Bastila sacrificed herself so we could get away.

speaker: Mission
text: You mean she's... she's dead?

speaker: Jolee
text: Bah. Malak won't kill her, don't be foolish. He'll want to use her battle meditation against the Republic. Turn her to the dark side and the Sith will always be victorious.

speaker: Player
text: We have to go back for Bastila!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Not so fast. I need to know if what Malak said about you is true or not, first. You aren't... you *can't* be, can you?

speaker: Player
text: I don't care what Malak said! I'm not Darth Revan, I'm <FullName>.

speaker: Mission
text: Revan? What... what are you talking about? Is this some kind of joke?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: No, it's no joke. The Jedi Council captured Revan and erased the Dark Lord's mind, programming in a new identity. Saul Karath told me on the Leviathan and Bastila confirmed it!

speaker: Mission
text: You're Darth Revan? This is... this is big. Do you... do you remember anything about being the Dark Lord?

speaker: Player
text: Small bits. A few strange dreams and visions. That's all.

speaker: Mission
text: Just a few flashes? That's it? Nothing more? Then I don't think there's a problem.

speaker: Mission
text: It seems to me that if you don't really remember anything about being Revan, then it doesn't really matter anymore. You are who you are now, right?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Of course it still matters! How do we know more memories won't come flooding back? How do we know Revan won't suddenly turn on us?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I've been such a fool! I... I swore to protect you! And here you were the enemy all this time!

speaker: Player
text: I'm not your enemy, Carth, I swear!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But... you're the one responsible for the death of my wife, the destruction of my home world! You destroyed my life!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: How could I have been such a fool! How could I have not known?! How could you betray me like this?!

speaker: Player
text: I didn't know I was Revan! How could I have known?!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You should have known. I...*sigh* I should have figured it out. I just can't... was, was everything a lie, then? Everything we talked about?

speaker: Player
text: Everything that was important was real, Carth.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Are you sure? I'm not sure what to believe any more. Who's to say that your old life won't come back... all of it?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Was the woman we knew Revan or... or someone else? Will you change into Revan? How...how can any of us trust you?

speaker: Mission
text: Well, I trust you! I know you... and you're not Revan anymore. Whatever you used to be, you're one of us now!

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I agree with Mission. I swore a life-debt to the person you are, not to the person you were.

speaker: Mission
text: Big Z and I will stick by you. We owe you our lives; we won't desert you now!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't know if I can get over it that easily, Mission. I mean... after all Revan did... how could any of us forgive her?

speaker: Juhani
text: It was Saul Karath who commanded the fleet that attacked your people, Carth. And it was Malak who gave the order. You know this.

speaker: Juhani
text: I have felt the presence of the dark side in you, Revan - as it is in all of us. I know the dangers of that path; yet I also know the fallen can be redeemed.

speaker: Juhani
text: I judge you by your actions, and as long as we have been together I have seen you act as a servant of the light.

speaker: Player
text: What about you, Jolee?

speaker: Jolee
text: What about me? I already knew who you were, though it wasn't my place to tell you. Better off that you know, if you ask me.

speaker: Jolee
text: Does it change anything? I'm not here to judge you. You'll do what you have to, and I'll help if I can.

speaker: Player
text: What do you think, Canderous?

speaker: Cand
text: You defeated the Mandalore clans in the war, Revan. You were the only one in the galaxy who could best us.

speaker: Cand
text: We had never met one like you before, and never since. How can you even ask if I will follow you?

speaker: Cand
text: Whatever you are fighting, it will be worthy of my skill. I'm your man until the end, Revan, no matter how this plays out.

speaker: Player
text: What do you have to say, HK-47?

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: I am... experiencing something unusual, master.

speaker: Player
text: Why? What's happening?

speaker: HK47
text: Answer: My programming is activating my deleted memory core. I believe I have a... a homing system that is restoring it, master.

speaker: Player
text: So this is the... stimuli you were waiting for?

speaker: HK47
text: Explanation: I believe so, master. I was unaware of my homing system until it had been activated.

speaker: HK47
text: It seems that the homing system deliberately restores my deleted memory core upon... upon returning to my original master.

speaker: Player
text: You mean... Revan?

speaker: HK47
text: Affirmation: Correct, master. Sith protocols maintain that all droid knowledge be deleted before assassination missions, and restored upon return.

speaker: HK47
text: I have returned to you, and my full functionality is now under your personal command. It is a distinct pleasure to see you again, master.

speaker: Player
text: Well... that makes a lot of sense, actually.

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: Indeed. I do hope we shall have the chance to engage in combat together again soon, master.

speaker: Mission
text: Wow. What are the chances of that happening?

speaker: Cand
text: Remember we're talking about the Force, here. At this point Malak himself could drop out of the sky and I wouldn't bat an eyelash.

speaker: Mission
text: Good point.

speaker: Player
text: You won't abandon me, will you T3?

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep! Beep! Woop-woooop!

speaker: Mission
text: I knew the little guy would come through for you - droids don't hold grudges.

speaker: Player
text: Well, Carth - will you stand with me against Malak?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Well, the others seem to trust you... and I don't see any other way that we can stop the Sith. And I suppose that Malak is the real enemy here... I really don't have any other choice, do I?

speaker: Player
text: I won't let you down, Carth. I promise.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I want to believe you. You've proven yourself time and time again during our mission, but this is a little much for me to wrap my mind around.

speaker: Player
text: You have to try... for Bastila's sake.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This must be even more of a shock to you... I don't know how you even keep going. I guess we both just have to find a way to push forward.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't worry about me - I'm a soldier. I can put aside my misgivings for now. We can, uh... we can talk later, you and I. Just give me time.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: So I guess that's it then... we keep going. We've still got one more Star Map to uncover if we're going to find that Star Forge and save Bastila, so let's do it before it's too late.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't worry - I won't let my personal feelings get in the way of my assignments or this mission. But don't forget: I've sworn an oath to defend the Republic!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: As long as this mission stays on course I'll stick with you. But I won't let you betray the Republic under any circumstances!

speaker: Player
text: How do you think I feel?

speaker: Player
text: You have to find a way to deal with this, Carth.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not Revan anymore, Carth. You have to believe that.

speaker: Player
text: You're right - you don't have a choice! I'm in charge here!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I see. Well, I guess that answers a lot of my questions about who you really are.

speaker: Player
text: Well, Carth... what are you going to do?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I don't know. Maybe I just need time to, uh... to think about it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The others seem to trust you... and we need you to stop the Sith. And I suppose Malak is the real enemy here. But I don't have much choice but to go along with this for now, do I?

speaker: T3M4
text: Beep! Beep-beep boop! Bwoooop.

speaker: Player
text: But I found you, you didn't find me!

speaker: Jolee
text: Think you'd never heard of the Force before. Seems obvious enough to me it was meant to be.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not exactly Revan anymore, HK-47...

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: That does not matter, master. I am your droid, regardless of your actions or personality.

speaker: Player
text: Good. So long as you're loyal.

speaker: HK47
text: Commentary: I believe I have served you well in the past, master, and will continue to do so for as long as you have need of me.

speaker: Player
text: Everyone be careful... there's no telling what this means!

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: That is unnecessary, master. My intent is not hostile. I am receiving no combat override commands.

speaker: HK47
text: Observation: My homing system is a function of my assassination protocols... that which I told you had been de-activated. This system was not.

speaker: Player
text: Your homing system? What's that?

speaker: Player
text: I'll destroy you if you make a move, droid!

speaker: Juhani
text: I have seen signs of the taint of the dark side in your actions and deeds, but I will not give up on you as you did not give up on me. I will stay with you, Revan.

speaker: Juhani
text: I can tell there is conflict between light and darkness within you. I do not know which way the struggle will turn, but I will not abandon you in this difficult time, as you did not abandon me.

speaker: Cand
text: Everyone knows it was Malak who gave the order to attack your people, Carth. You can't blame Revan for that.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It, uh... it all makes sense now... Revan. I've watched you, I've seen your cruelty. I've seen your... your dark side. And now this! I don't know if I can trust you. Can any of us?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I... I suppose you've proven yourself to be a friend of the Republic by your actions so far... Revan. But can I trust you? Can any of us?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: How can you say that, Mission? The Sith bombed my home world! Revan took away my family and destroyed my life!

speaker: Player
text: I don't know. Everything has changed, now.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: That's what I feared. Who's to say your old life won't come back... everything you felt and thought, all of it?

speaker: Player
text: Why? Were you lying to me all that time?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: This isn't a joke. You know what I'm talking about. I'm talking about you, about the way you felt...

speaker: Player
text: Please, Carth... don't do this to me!

speaker: Player
text: Get over it, Carth. We've got more important things to think about.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Get over it? Yeah... yeah, I can get over it. I should have figured out earlier you weren't what you seemed. That's my fault.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Do you think everybody else is going to be so quick to 'get over it'? You think they're going to follow a Sith Lord?

speaker: Mission
text: I don't see the Sith Lord standing here, I see a friend who's been with us through thick and thin! Remember - Malak's the one who tried to destroy Taris!

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth... I wish this wasn't true.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But it is true. It's horribly true! It was...it was you... you killed my wife, you ravaged my world. You...you destroyed my life!

speaker: Player
text: Blame the Jedi Council for this, Carth - not me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It doesn't matter who's to blame. You're still the one who did it. You killed my wife... you betrayed everything that I believed in! You destroyed my life!

speaker: Player
text: This changes nothing. I am who I am.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Oh, it changes everything! It was... it was you! You were the one that attacked my world! You were the one that destroyed my life!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The whole time we've been chasing after Malak we've had his old Sith Master right at our side; listening to our secrets; hearing our plans!

speaker: Player
text: But I'm not the Dark Lord anymore, I'm <FullName>. I'm one of you!

speaker: Player
text: This changes nothing! I still want to stop Malak!

speaker: Player
text: I don't remember anything about being Revan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And so the lies begin. It was obvious you remembered something back there when Malak confronted you with the truth. It might have only been small pieces, but there was something there!

speaker: Player
text: It looks that way. I'm... Darth Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Back off, Carth! There's nothing you can do about it!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I suppose I shouldn't be surprised by your attitude now that I know who you really are... Revan.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Not so fast. We've got a bigger issue to deal with here. They deserve to know the truth about you. Do you want to tell them what Malak said, or should I?

speaker: Player
text: I'll tell them. I'm... I'm Darth Revan.

speaker: Player
text: Say one word and you're dead, Carth!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Threats? You can't bully me - though I shouldn't be surprised now that I know who you really are... Revan.

speaker: Player
text: We can't help Bastila - not unless we find the Star Forge first.

speaker: Juhani
text: The Dark Lord will not kill her. He will want to use her battle meditation ability against the Republic. He will take her alive so he can turn her to the dark side. I am sure of it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Malak won't kill her. I think he'll want to use her battle meditation against the Republic. He'll keep her alive so he can turn her to the dark side!

text: Hmph - who dresses you? You look like you crawled up here from the Lower City. Oh well, I guess we can't all have style.
