speaker: Carth
text: Good job, Mission! I knew you wouldn't let us down. When we get out of this I'm going to see you get a medal from the Republic for everything you've done!

speaker: Carth
text: If I remember the layout of this ship our equipment should be in a storage chamber just through the north doors. After we grab our stuff we need to get to the main bridge controls.

speaker: Carth
text: The bridge is the only place we can open the docking gates of the hangar where they've got the Ebon Hawk. We have to open those gates before we can fly out of here!

speaker: Bastila
text: We better get moving. I can feel the darkness of Malak's presence approaching, and I don't want to be here when he arrives. None of us is a match for the Sith Lord.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not afraid of Malak!

speaker: Bastila
text: Then you are a fool! The power of the Dark Lord is strong enough to destroy any of us... even you. It would be suicide to face Malak here! We need to get away before he arrives.

speaker: Player
text: We need some type of plan.

speaker: Bastila
text: Surprise and secrecy will serve us best. A small group might have a better chance of sneaking onto the bridge undetected while the others make their way down to the Ebon Hawk.
comment: Init after party is rescued by NPC

speaker: Carth
text: Count me in, then. I've got a score to settle with the Admiral before we get off this ship, and I have a feeling I'm gonna find him on the Leviathan's bridge!

speaker: Player
text: I'm coming, too!

speaker: Bastila
text: That's a good idea. The others can get to the Ebon Hawk on their own, but Carth and I might need your help.

speaker: Bastila
text: The three of us will get our equipment and make our way to the bridge. The rest of you head down to the docking hangar where they've got the Ebon Hawk. You'll have to find a way to deal with guards.
comment: Carth, Bastila and PC form party, everyone else escapes area and appears back in the ship

speaker: Cand
text: Don't you worry about that. I know how to deal with the guards. They won't know what hit them!

speaker: Player
text: Good. Get to the equipment room, grab what you need, and get going.

speaker: Bastila
text: We'll meet you there as soon as we get those docking bay doors open. Just make sure the Hawk is ready to fly when we get there. And may the Force be with you.

speaker: Player
text: We still have to get our equipment.  Let's go.

speaker: Player
text: Careful, Carth, there's more at stake here than personal revenge.

speaker: Bastila
text: That's true, Carth. You can come, but don't let your hatred of Saul Karath jeopardize our true mission: getting the Ebon Hawk safely off the Leviathan.

speaker: Bastila
text: You better come with me and Carth. The others can find their way on their own, but we might run into trouble. We'll need you and your powerful Force abilities to deal with it.

speaker: Player
text: I'll go with the others back to the Ebon Hawk.

speaker: Player
text: Let's get our equipment and blast our way to those bridge controls!

speaker: Bastila
text: Well done, Jolee. I knew we could count on you. A Jedi never fails to get the task done!

speaker: Carth
text: Nice job, Canderous. You keep getting us out of jams like this and there might be a place for you in the Republic army, even if you are a Mandalorian!

speaker: Bastila
text: Well done, Juhani. In freeing us from the cell you have proven yourself truly worthy of the title of Jedi.

speaker: Carth
text: You may be a droid, but when this is all over I'm going to see the Republic gives you a medal for your part in this!

speaker: Bastila
text: Don't try to move too quickly, you might not be fully recovered yet. Admiral Karath had his guards continue to torture you even after you passed out.

speaker: Carth
text: They tortured all of us, though you got the worst of it by far. Saul wanted them to make us suffer. He's become some sort of sadistic monster.

speaker: Bastila
text: The dark side has perverted him, Carth. Once you start down the tainted path it leads you ever further into the depths of evil. I fear he is forever lost.

speaker: Player
text: No one is without hope of redemption, Bastila.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes, hmm, I suppose you are correct. Sometimes it is easy to lose sight of that hope in the face of such unbridled cruelty, but you speak the truth.

speaker: Bastila
text: I suppose I'm taking the news of Dantooine's destruction quite hard. First Taris, now the Academy... is there no end to the killing?

speaker: Player
text: Maybe Admiral Karath was lying.

speaker: Bastila
text: I'd like to believe that Saul was lying to us, but even as he said the words I knew they were true. The Academy is gone.

speaker: Bastila
text: We should have felt a disturbance in the Force when the attack came. The fact that we did not is a bad sign. I fear the dark side is growing stronger, casting shadows our vision cannot pierce.

speaker: Bastila
text: I can only hope that some of the Jedi escaped. Vrook, Vandar, Zhar... I cannot imagine all of them being gone. In any case, we have lost our one place of refuge in the galaxy.

speaker: Carth
text: None of this will matter if we don't get out of this prison before Saul gets back!

speaker: Player
text: Where is Saul Karath now?

speaker: Carth
text: Saul mentioned that Lord Malak was on his way. I think the Admiral left to prepare for his arrival... and to report the results of our interrogation.

speaker: Bastila
text: I only wish you had been able to resist the Admiral's questioning. I hope the information you revealed does not bring the entire galaxy under the dominion of the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Bastila, but I couldn't just let you be tortured!

speaker: Bastila
text: I appreciate your... feelings... for me. But you can't let your feelings override your judgment. Remember the Jedi code: There is no emotion, there is peace.

speaker: Bastila
text: Your efforts were well intentioned but poorly thought out; Saul tortured us all anyway. There is too much at stake to let reckless passion rule our actions.

speaker: Player
text: How dare you judge me? You have no idea what it's like to be put into that kind of position!

speaker: Bastila
text: I know if I had been in that position I would not have betrayed the Order and the Republic!

speaker: Player
text: No, you would have just left someone you care about screaming in agony!

speaker: Carth
text: Stop it, both of you! Bastila, you... you can't honestly say how you would have reacted in that situation - nobody can! Besides, Saul already had all the information. I could tell.

speaker: Carth
text: The interrogation was a sham. Saul was toying with us. He didn't care what we told him. I think it was just an excuse to torture us before Malak arrived.

speaker: Bastila
text: Did you feel that? A disturbance in the Force. The Admiral has sent his message, the Dark Lord knows we are here now. Malak is coming.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope Mission busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope T3-M4 busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope Jolee busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope Canderous busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope Juhani busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Carth
text: Well, then we better hope HK-47 busts us out of here before he arrives.

speaker: Player
text: I'm... I'm sorry I failed you. I didn't know what else to do.

speaker: Carth
text: Don't be so hard on yourself. I've known the Admiral a long time. I could see that he already knew the answers to the questions he was asking.

speaker: Player
text: Saul already knew the answers to the questions he was asking.

speaker: Carth
text: I've known Admiral Karath a long time and I think you're right.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Bastila, but I couldn't just let Carth be tortured!

speaker: Bastila
text: I appreciate your... feelings... for Carth. But you can't let your feelings override your judgment. Remember the Jedi code: There is no emotion, there is peace.

speaker: Player
text: Why should I endure torture just to protect the Republic and the Jedi?

speaker: Bastila
text: Your attitude disturbs me. Such selfishness is a sign of the dark side's taint, and it does little to fill me with confidence in you.

speaker: Carth
text: Forget about it, Bastila. It doesn't matter anyway. I've known the Admiral a long time. I could see that he already knew the answers to the questions he was asking.

speaker: Bastila
text: It is fortunate you were able to resist the Admiral's questioning. The fate of the galaxy could be changed by revealing the slightest piece of vital information.

speaker: Bastila
text: I have to confess something. There was a moment - just a moment - when part of me was hoping you would tell him what he wanted to know. Just to make the horrible pain stop.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Bastila. Watching you suffer tore me apart.

speaker: Bastila
text: I know you wouldn't ever do anything to intentionally cause me pain. But you did the right thing.

speaker: Bastila
text: I don't honestly know if I could have been as strong in your position. To watch you suffer like that... it might have been too much for me to bear.

speaker: Player
text: Saul would have tortured us no matter what I told him.

speaker: Player
text: The only reason I stayed silent was to watch you suffer.

speaker: Bastila
text: You wanted me to suffer? You enjoyed my torment? I don't know what to say. I thought there was a bond between us.

speaker: Bastila
text: Maybe... maybe you're not the man I thought you were.

speaker: Carth
text: I, uh... I have to confess something. There was a... there was a moment - just a moment - when part of me was hoping that you would tell him what he wanted to know. Just to make the horrible pain stop.

speaker: Player
text: I'm sorry, Carth. Watching you suffer tore me apart.

speaker: Carth
text: No, I know you wouldn't ever do anything to intentionally cause me pain. But you had no other choice. You couldn't betray our cause.

speaker: Carth
text: I... I don't honestly know if I could have been as strong in your position. To watch you suffer like that I... I might have cracked.

speaker: Player
text: I'm not afraid of him!

speaker: Player
text: I know... it's hard to believe they're all gone.

speaker: Player
text: It's their own fault. They should have seen the attack coming.

speaker: Player
text: Blah, blah, blah. Don't you ever get tired of being so preachy?

speaker: Bastila
text: This is not a matter to joke about! If there is one thing we can learn from Saul it is how the power of the dark side can corrupt even the bravest of heroes!

speaker: Bastila
text: I'm sorry. Forgive me. Snapping at you like that won't help our situation.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Yes, I promised you an answer when we reached the Ebon Hawk, didn't I? But I'm afraid you won't like it. We should have some privacy for this.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I can't deny that there are parts of you I am drawn to. Your power, your will. You are so much stronger than I am.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: In some ways you make me feel weak, like I am caught up in the wake of our destiny. But at the same time, you make me feel stronger, more alive.

speaker: Player
text: So what does this mean for us?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I realize now these feelings are part of the bond we share. The Jedi Council surely realized this; they knew my loyalty to the doctrines of our Order would be tested on this mission.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: By facing and overcoming my feelings for you I have learned a valuable lesson about control and the dangers of emotion. This is an important step in understanding the Force.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm sorry if this is not what you wanted to hear. But I felt it was important you know our... infatuation... was nothing more than a result of our powerful bond.

speaker: Player
text: So I was just a stepping stone to you becoming a Master?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Please, don't say it like that. You make it sound like I was using you! Don't you realize how difficult this was for me?

speaker: Player
text: Difficult for you? What about me?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Why do you think I came to this decision? I know how hard this is for both of us! You just kept pressing forward, so I had to be the one to step up and do the right thing!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You're the one who can't face the truth! Malak has to be stopped. How can I do that if I let myself be blinded by my feelings for you?

speaker: Player
text: I'm going to stop Malak, Bastila. But I want to do it with you at my side.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You... you mean it, don't you? But how can I be sure you aren't making a mistake. I... I have to resist. I have to be strong for both of us.

speaker: Player
text: You know I'm right, Bastila.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But I don't... I mean, I can't... Malak will...

speaker: Player
text: Shut up and kiss me, you babbling fool.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Oh, my!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We... we shouldn't have done that. It was wrong. The Jedi aren't allowed to fall in love.

speaker: Player
text: It didn't feel wrong to me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: It was... it was a moment of weakness. When I kissed you... we shouldn't have... no, I'm sorry.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I know we both wanted it, but we shouldn't have given in to our desire. We're Jedi! We can't act like this. Not now, not while we still have to deal with Malak!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm... I'm sorry. I don't blame you, but... it was a mistake. I have to get out of here before somebody sees us together!

speaker: Player
text: We're not going back to this again, are we?

speaker: Player
text: I love you Bastila. And I know you love me.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Okay, you've made your point. Now shut up and kiss me, you fool!

speaker: Player
text: You don't always have to be strong, Bastila. Give in just this once.

speaker: Player
text: That's okay - I never felt anything for you anyway.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Oh, I thought... No, this is good. I'm glad you told me. This makes everything much easier.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Don't worry - I can put this behind me. Let's just continue on with what we must do. It is better this way.

speaker: Player
text: I... I understand, Bastila.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I hope you can put this behind you. You need to focus on stopping Malak, as difficult as that may be. Come, we should continue our mission.

speaker: Player
text: This is nothing but an excuse! You're afraid to face your feelings!

speaker: Player
text: You're rationalizing, Bastila. You're just scared to face the truth!

speaker: Player
text: So that's it? It's all over?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I'm... afraid so. Although I suppose I should thank you for all you've done. For the lessons you helped me learn.

speaker: Player
text: Great - you learn a lesson and I get dumped!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: I wish it could be otherwise, but you have to understand that this is the way it must be. I am a Jedi, after all.

speaker: Player
text: And I feel more alive when I'm with you.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: You're stronger than I am, and there's no point in telling me otherwise. You will be a great Jedi, I think. I hope.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Thank you for freeing us! You will eternally have the gratitude of the Rakata!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: But... I can't help but wonder, off-worlder... Why have you freed us?

speaker: Player
text: I work for the One.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: The One! He sent someone back for us as I knew he would!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: We shall return to the One and tell of what you have done.

speaker: Player
text: I have no love for the Elders.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: And neither do we. We thank you for what you have done for us.

speaker: Player
text: Shut up and accept it!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: Er... yes... yes! Thank you!

speaker: Player
text: Actually I just wanted a moving target.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: What?? You shall never kill me!

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This door is held closed by some great power, and cannot be opened at the moment.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This door is locked and must be opened by some other means.]

speaker: Carth
text: Bastila - you're alive! Finally, things are looking up. Now we just need to figure out a way to get off this planet.

speaker: Bastila
text: You mean you don't have a plan to get off Taris yet? What have you been doing all this time?

speaker: Player
text: We were trying to find you, remember?

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. Now that I'm back in charge of this mission, perhaps we can start doing things properly. Hopefully our escape from Taris will go more smoothly than when you "rescued" me from Brejik.

speaker: Carth
text: I know you're new at this, Bastila, but a leader doesn't berate her troops just because things aren't going as planned. Don't let your ego get in the way of the real issues here.

speaker: Bastila
text: That hardly strikes me as an appropriate way of addressing your commander, Carth. I am a member of the Jedi Order and this is my mission. Don't forget that!

speaker: Bastila
text: My Battle Meditation ability has helped the Republic many times in this war, and it will serve us well here I am sure.

speaker: Carth
text: Your talents might win us a few battles, but that doesn't make you a good leader! A good leader would at least listen to the advice of those who have seen more combat than she ever will!

speaker: Player
text: Both of you settle down! This isn't helping.

speaker: Bastila
text: Yes... You're right, of course. I apologize, Carth. This has been a difficult time for me. Of course I'm happy to listen to your advice. What do you suggest we do?

speaker: Carth
text: First off we can't get hung up on who's in charge; we all need to work together if we want to get off this rock. The answer's out there, we just have to find it.

speaker: Bastila
text: Well said, Carth. And the sooner we start looking the better; I've already been a prisoner of the Vulkars and I don't plan on being captured by the Sith.

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry. I won't let that happen!

speaker: Bastila
text: I think we'll need some help getting off Taris. Maybe if we ask around one of the locals can help us out. We should probably start by asking around in the cantinas.

speaker: Player
text: Okay, so what now?

speaker: Player
text: Let's go find a way off this planet.

speaker: Player
text: He's right. You aren't showing much leadership ability right now, Bastila.

speaker: Carth
text: You know, I had my doubts about this mission but I figured the Jedi Council wouldn't put you in charge if you weren't prepared. But here you are, acting like a spoiled child!

speaker: Bastila
text: I see. It's true I that don't have much military experience; perhaps I should not be so quick to judge. Very well, Carth: what do you suggest we do?

speaker: Player
text: Carth! You can't talk to your commanding officer like that!

speaker: Player
text: Don't worry. We'll figure something out.

speaker: Player
text: I'm getting a little sick of your attitude, Bastila!

speaker: Bastila
text: My attitude? It strikes me that you're the one in sore need of an attitude adjustment. I happen to be in charge of this mission, if you'll recall.

speaker: Jolee
text: Ah, the damnable racket of battle! Watch yourself, even more of these crawling beasts are hiding in the underbrush.
comment: Initiates part-way through the battle as he appears. Pause combat for dialogue, then resume and spawn a few more creatures to fight. Jolee should help with the battle meditation that he does. Jolee should not have his saber.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you? What are you doing here?

speaker: Jolee
text: I'm Jolee. Jolee Bindo. Follow me to my camp and we'll talk a bit.

speaker: Player
text: I will, but explain what you are doing here.

speaker: Jolee
text: Why am I here? Hmph. Well it isn't because I like the stink of dead kinrath. Let's move this talk to my camp where the air is better.

speaker: Jolee
text: Keep close. It's nearby, under a log. Yeah, I live like some burrowing rodent. I fought the Sith... now look at me. Hmph!
comment: Moves to his camp area. Correct this line for proper directions

speaker: Player
text: You use a lightsaber in battle. Are you a Jedi?

speaker: Jolee
text: Ah, don't start fawning just yet, I'm too old for it. *Sigh* I...I know a few things, but we can talk about it at my camp.

speaker: Player
text: Who are you to give me orders, old man?

speaker: Jolee
text: Look, you can follow now or stumble around on your own, but I'm too old to care whether you think I'm babysitting you.

speaker: Player
text: What, do I have to fight you as well now?

speaker: Player
text: Help or don't, just stay out of my way.

speaker: Jolee
text: That's the way! Now prove that wasn't blind luck, you baby!

speaker: Jolee
text: Quit your yapping for now. We'll talk when the company is better. Get to fightin'!
comment: Battle commences again, more creatures spawn. Jolee helps with his battle meditation stuff.

speaker: Jolee
text: Well, that was acceptable. You're not quite the commander I'd have accompanied in my youth, but you managed to walk away.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [This submersible can be used to descend to the deep ocean Hrakert research station.]

speaker: Player
text: [Use the submersible.]

speaker: Player
text: [Step away from the submersible.]

speaker: Bastila
text: If the droid is correct, then we must complete the tasks in the proving grounds to the east and west before these doors will open.
comment: SCRIPTED  when the player first approaches the huge circular door to the star map  LINKED

speaker: Bastila
text: This... this must be what Revan and Malak found when they entered this temple. This must be where their journey down the dark side began.

speaker: Player
text: What is it?

speaker: Bastila
text: This is a... a map. Some sort of intergalactic navigational chart. Revan and Malak must have used this to lead them to the Star Forge.

speaker: Bastila
text: We could use this map to follow their path and find the Star Forge ourselves. But we must be wary... they may have laid traps or concealed what they found.

speaker: Player
text: So what is the Star Forge, exactly?

speaker: Bastila
text: I... I don't know, but Revan and Malak were very interested in finding it. It must be a tool of some type... or maybe a weapon. Perhaps the Council can tell us more.

speaker: Bastila
text: But I think this map might be the key to finding the Star Forge, whatever it is.

speaker: Bastila
text: See this world here? This looks like Korriban, a Sith world. And if that's Korriban, then this is... Kashyyyk... and Tatooine... and here's Manaan.

speaker: Bastila
text: But there are pieces missing: incomplete hyperspace coordinates, corrupted data... and there doesn't seem to be anything indicating where the Star Forge itself might be.

speaker: Player
text: Perhaps those worlds have more clues.

speaker: Bastila
text: I was thinking that, too. This map can't take us to the Star Forge, but I know that Revan and Malak visited Korriban at least once. Perhaps they discovered something more there.

speaker: Bastila
text: They may have found something on each of the other worlds that completed this map. Maybe if we find all the pieces they will lead us to the Star Forge... and some way to destroy it.

speaker: Carth
text: That sounds like quite a supposition. What if you're wrong?

speaker: Bastila
text: What if I'm right? We can't ignore this. Finding the Star Forge might very well be the key to defeating the Sith!

speaker: Bastila
text: We must inform the Council of what we have discovered. They must decide our next course of action, though I suspect our task has only just begun.

speaker: Player
text: What good is an incomplete map?

speaker: Player
text: I still don't understand about the Star Forge. What does it do?

speaker: Player
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Player
text: I don't get it. Is this the Star Forge?

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [There are ancient symbols here, worn as though traced by generations of Wookiee claws. Layers of moss and dirt suggest that no one has been here in many years.]
comment: This should be on a stone or metal plate on the ground near the ritual place.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [The beast comes when summoned, if you are generous. It comes to battle, if you are worthy and wise. It grants you glory, if you are fearsome and brave.]

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Feed the beast and it will heed your call. Take vipers from their lair and hang them from above. Let blood scent the ground of our ancestors.]

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I remember this. I remember the tales of the hunters that would prove themselves in the Shadowlands.

speaker: Player
text: Can you shed any light on this?

speaker: Zaalbar
text: It is a description of the ritual you have already completed. We need not concern ourselves with it.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: I never went to the Shadowlands to prove myself. I was cast out before I could reach the proper age. I don't know anything about the rituals.

speaker: Zaalbar
text: You will have to follow whatever your instincts tell you. These were tests for individual warriors. I am sorry I can't be of more help.

speaker: Player
text: Whatever. Just tell me what you know about it.

speaker: Conversation owner
text: [Obviously this was once a place of great ritual importance.]
